I've been feeling really overwhelmed and frustrated lately because of the difficulties I'm having with my relative. My wife just last week said she wants a divorce and it's all sudden. I understand that marriages have their ups and downs but I don't understand why she can't tell me why she wants a divorce. Should I fight for my family (daughter and wife)?

My partner's passing has been incredibly difficult for me. He was not only my love but also my support system. Lately, I've been feeling really down and lonely. I have this belief that no one would ever want to be with me or be my friend because of who I am. It's weird because on one hand, I crave love and connection, but on the other hand, I'm afraid of being hurt because I've experienced a lot of loss in the past.

Lately, I've been experiencing a lot of stress at work. My coworkers have been making false statements about me to our boss, saying that I have mood swings. I've been struggling with my gender identity lately. I feel like I would be more comfortable identifying as a girl, even though I am still attracted to girls. Recently, my cousin has been staying with me in the city and I've been feeling really belittled, insecure, and frustrated by her behavior. Lately, I've been experiencing some extreme mood swings and changes in my behavior. Sometimes I feel really happy, energetic, and talk really fast. I recently started dating a man I met online. He disclosed to me that he is a registered sex offender, but he insists that he didn't actually commit any offenses. For the past three years, I have been struggling with body image issues. Despite being thin, I still feel ugly. I want to know how I can stop thinking about their comments and prevent them from affecting my self-esteem. I've expressed my need for therapy to my parents, but they don't seem to take it seriously and think I'm okay.

A few nights ago, I opened up to a friend about my self-esteem issues. We had a long conversation where she reassured me that I am a great person, attractive, and have a wonderful personality. It really boosted my self-confidence and I felt much better the next morning.

I'm feeling really overwhelmed and confused about a recent argument with my friends. It seems like they're all against me and I'm questioning if I'm overreacting. I feel attacked and like I'm playing the victim, but I can't help but wonder if I'm actually being unreasonable and annoying my friends. On the other hand, maybe they're being insensitive and not respecting me in our friendship. Can you help me make sense of all this?

I am feeling incredibly distressed and heartbroken about the current state of my marriage. My wife and I have a beautiful family together - we have three boys and I have a daughter from a previous marriage. We are also blessed with three grandchildren. My wife wants to leave, but I love her deeply and I don't want that to happen. Even our three boys are urging us to work it out because they love both of us and want our family to stay intact. Is there any advice or hope you can offer me in this difficult situation?

My wife and I have been married for about two months, but we're already experiencing some challenges in our sex life. I'm worried that we won't be able to have an honest conversation about this, and it will further impact our sex life. Can you help me navigate this situation?

Patient: I feel like no matter how hard I try, I'm always being criticized and told that I'm not good enough. I put in so much effort into everything I do. Patient: I've noticed a pattern in my relationships where I tend to be attracted to men who are unavailable or only interested in intimacy without commitment. I've been reflecting on my past actions and I deeply regret hurting her. She means the world to me, yet it seems like my efforts to make things right are not effective. Despite this, my love for her remains unwavering. When I am with her, nothing else matters. I love her more than anything and the thought of another man raising our kids is difficult for me to accept.

I've been diagnosed with dog obsession disorder, and it's causing conflicts in my relationship with my girlfriend. I find myself prioritizing my two dogs over her. I want to know how I can overcome this problem and start prioritizing my girlfriend over my dogs.

Lately, I've noticed that I have a tendency to lie about insignificant things in my daily life. It's become a habit and I want to understand why this happens and how I can change it. I really want to become a more honest and open person, regardless of the situation.

Over the course of 8 months, I engaged in an inappropriate relationship with a mutual friend while our spouses were not present. I have always believed that cheating is completely unacceptable in a relationship, but when I found out about my partner's infidelity, I made the difficult decision to stay for the sake of our two daughters. However, now I am struggling with the pain, and I find it hard to trust him again. Trust is crucial for me to continue in this relationship, but I also don't want my children to be hurt. I feel stuck and unsure of how to move forward.

I have been in a long-distance relationship for seven years, and recently I have been feeling like it's not meeting my needs. My partner lives three hours away and we only see each other once or twice a month. He likes having someone to talk to throughout the day, but I want someone who is more present and can be a true life companion. Lately, his busy work schedule has made it even harder for us to spend time together, and I've been feeling frustrated and angry about it. I've tried discussing my concerns with him, but I still feel like the relationship isn't a priority for him. It's starting to hold me back from finding the kind of relationship I truly want. However, every time we try to break up, I panic and feel overwhelming anxiety and depression at the thought of him being with someone else. I also worry that I'll never find someone else that I like. This cycle of breaking up and getting back together has happened multiple times, and I recognize that it's unhealthy, but my fear of the anxiety and depression keeps me from fully ending things.

I've been in a relationship for a while now, but I've noticed that I'm always the one putting in more effort and not getting it in return. It's starting to bother me, and what my ex said about never finding anyone else is constantly on my mind.

I am currently struggling to find employment due to the challenges I face in my relationship with my bipolar mother. I currently live with her, which causes me significant stress. Unfortunately, I am unable to afford therapy at the moment, but I believe it would be beneficial for me to receive therapy before pursuing employment.

I've been struggling with my eating habits, specifically when it comes to self-control. It seems like most people are able to stop eating when they feel satisfied, but for some reason, I find myself continuing to eat purely for the enjoyment of it. This is especially true with desserts - I never feel like I've had enough.

I have a friend who seems to be highly sensitive to stress and negative tones of voice. Whenever we have a disagreement, he tells me that my communication is harming him. Can you offer any advice on how to handle this situation?

Lately, I've been noticing that my partner talks to someone when I ask them who they are talking to, but they insist that they aren't talking to anyone. Is my partner trying to make me doubt my own mental stability, or are they talking to themselves?

I recently had a romantic relationship with someone and it felt really good. However, they suddenly expressed a desire to just be friends, and I've been struggling to move on. Thoughts of them constantly occupy my mind, and I find myself wanting them back.

Lately, I've been feeling really down about myself. I constantly doubt that anyone would want to be in a relationship with me or be my friend. It's like I have this fear of being loved because I always end up losing in the end.

I have been in a relationship with someone for the past five months. Despite our age difference (he is in his late thirties and I am in my mid-twenties), I really like him. I'm unsure if I should give him a second chance.

Lately, I've noticed that my partner seems to be having conversations with someone else, even when no one else is around. I've even confronted them about it, suspecting that they might be hiding a secret phone. It's making me question my own sanity. Are they deliberately trying to drive me crazy, or is there something else going on?

I have a pattern of entering relationships with men who are going through difficult times. Despite my best efforts to support and assist them, the relationships always end in failure. I constantly find myself drawn to individuals who need help, but it's leaving me feeling alone, sad, and frustrated. How can I break this cycle and avoid getting into relationships with men in bad situations?

My girlfriend's grandmother passed away 5 months ago and they had a close relationship. She took care of her until she passed away. Initially, things seemed to return to normal a few weeks later. I'm feeling insecure about our relationship and have thoughts of her cheating, even though she says otherwise. It just feels like something is really off.

Patient: I have been diagnosed with bipolar disorder and last summer was a particularly difficult time for me. I experienced recurring nightmares and now I find myself avoiding anything that might trigger similar feelings to what I went through during that summer.

Lately, I've been struggling with my thoughts and emotions. I find myself constantly trying to convince myself that everything is okay, even when it's not. Patient: I've been feeling really overwhelmed lately. I find myself constantly trying to convince myself that everything is okay, even when deep down I know it's not. Patient: Recently, I discovered that my boyfriend takes anti-depression medication. He has been expressing that he feels overwhelmed and needs space to contemplate our relationship. We have only been dating for three weeks, but I have developed strong feelings for him.

I have been in a relationship with my best friend for over a year now, and we recently welcomed a beautiful baby girl into our lives. We were deeply in love, and I still have strong feelings for her. However, she has mentioned that she feels a disconnect between us. She has started talking to a random guy, claiming that he is just someone to talk to. He also has rules about me using his phone because of past issues with his ex. Although I don't believe he is cheating, he sometimes lies about when he leaves her place or goes to see them. I think my partner may not have fully let go of his past relationship, which is causing some of these issues. Other than this, he is a wonderful boyfriend.

Over the past six years, my therapist and I have developed a close relationship. He has always paid me back when I loaned him money, and I felt like we were friends. I'm feeling confused and unsure about what to do.

I still love him deeply, but this situation has shattered my self-esteem, leaving me feeling unattractive and inadequate. It feels like my world has been turned upside down and I'm trying to find my footing again.

I made the decision to stop because I wanted to save our marriage, but he did not share the same commitment. I still have strong feelings for him, despite everything that has happened. Patient: I've recently been diagnosed with ADHD and I've been having episodes of manic depression. On top of that, I struggle with anger management. I've also been told that I have ODD, bipolar disorder, and a split personality. It feels like a lot to handle. How can I find true happiness?

I’m a senior high school student who is five months pregnant. I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for three years, but my parents don't want us to communicate with each other. I have been struggling with gender dysphoria for the past 10 years and have always felt a strong desire to transition from male to female. However, I feel overwhelmed and unsure about where to start. I also lack the necessary information to make an informed decision.

My friends have also made comments about how I would make a beautiful woman, which has made me think about this even more. I've been struggling to connect with my parents, who are in their sixties, while I'm a teenager. Although I care about them, I find their personalities difficult to handle. It seems like they don't take me seriously when I try to discuss important events in my life. Even if my dad doesn't believe me, my mom follows suit and acts like she doesn't believe me either. On top of that, I identify as pansexual, but I don't feel comfortable trusting my own parents with this information. I've battled depression in the past and overcame it, but now I'm being overwhelmed by stress and anxiety. I feel like my friends don't listen to me. I understand that they have their own problems, and I always try to support them, but it hurts when they don't reciprocate the support when I really need it. It feels like my childhood has been stolen from me, and I feel like I have no one I can truly trust.

I'm going through a really tough time right now. My wife and I are getting a divorce after being together for seven years, and we just had a baby seven months ago. I had to move back in with my mother because I don't have anywhere else to go. I've been feeling really down lately and it's been affecting my sleep - I've been having both good and bad dreams. I also feel like everyone hates me. Can you help me? Can you intervene? Is there someone I can talk to about all of this?

Lately, I've been experiencing frequent bouts of anger. It seems like even the slightest miscommunication can trigger a strong reaction from me. This is a new behavior for me, and I believe it started after getting into a relationship with my soon-to-be husband. His own issues with mood swings and anger seem to have influenced me. Although I don't get as extreme as he does, I find myself constantly yelling and unable to control my emotions. It's concerning because I have two young children who are exposed to this behavior, and I don't want them to grow up with a mother who acts this way. I really want to find a way to regain control and return to my old self.

I have been in a committed relationship with my boyfriend for over a year now. Recently, he started a new job that requires him to travel frequently. I'm finding it difficult to adjust to him being away all the time. It feels like he has forgotten about me because he doesn't communicate with me as much or keep me updated on his day like he used to. I'm feeling lost, sad, and unwanted. This is a new challenge for me, and I'm considering breaking up with him even though I still love him deeply. I think I might be experiencing separation anxiety. Is there anything I can do to help cope with these feelings while he is out of town?

As a teenager, I have been experiencing intense bursts of anger that feel uncontrollable. I initially thought it was just hormonal, but others have noticed it too. When I get angry, I engage in self-destructive behaviors like biting my arms and fingers, pulling my hair, scratching my face, or punching my thighs. I do these things to avoid damaging my surroundings and having to explain it to my mom. It's important to note that I come from a loving family, have a great relationship with my boyfriend, and a good job. I'm confused about why this is happening and how to manage it. It seems to happen over minor things, like tonight when I couldn't get my earrings out. On a good week, this happens about two to three times, and it's always triggered by insignificant matters.

It has been a challenging nine months since my partner said he would try to support me, but he hasn't followed through. This situation is worsening my mental health. Today, he mentioned that I should respect whatever decision he makes. I'm feeling confused - should I really respect his decision to leave me alone, constantly crying and worried every night, just because he can't handle what I'm going through? It feels like he keeps changing his mind about whether he wants to work things out.

I recently found out that my daughter-in-law has been smoking marijuana while pregnant due to her morning sickness. I'm feeling quite shocked and unsure of how to handle this situation. Adding to my distress, I recently lost my mother who was always there to offer guidance and advice during difficult times.

It's been a challenging nine months since my partner said they would try, but haven't followed through. This situation has taken a toll on my mental well-being. Today, they mentioned that I need to respect whatever decision they make. Is it really necessary for me to respect their decision to leave me, knowing that they can't handle what I'm going through? It's distressing to be left here, feeling upset and anxious every night, especially when my partner keeps changing their mind about working things out.

I've been struggling with my mental health for some time now. I was hospitalized twice, with the most recent admission being last month for psychiatric help. Currently, I am taking medication, but I'm finding it difficult to combat the negative thoughts, irrational fears, and feelings of loneliness that still persist. The people in my life aren't providing much support either.

Lately, I've noticed that I have moments where I struggle to find the right words to say, even though I'm usually outgoing. It's like I have this fear that people won't like what I say or that they're talking about me behind my back. This self-consciousness makes me withdraw and avoid conversations altogether.

I've been struggling a lot lately, and I feel really overwhelmed and depressed. My parents are going through a divorce, and it seems like everything in my life is falling apart. Sometimes, I even have thoughts of wanting to harm myself.

My toddler is struggling with toilet training. He has developed a strong aversion to his own poop and gets nauseous whenever he sees it. Despite our attempts with a toilet chair and a ring for the big-boy toilet, he refuses to use them. He will sit on the toilet for long periods of time but only ends up peeing. He holds his poop until he gets up and then goes in his diaper. I've tried dumping the diaper in the toilet to show him where it belongs, but it hasn't helped. How can I support him in overcoming this fear and reducing his stress?

I experienced a traumatic event where I was sexually assaulted by multiple individuals. As a result, I've been struggling with a distorted self-image and it's affecting my intimate relationship with my wife. I find myself relying on lingerie to try and regain a sense of sexual excitement.

My husband and I have been married for almost five years now, and recently he dropped a bombshell on me by expressing his desire for a divorce. This revelation came just before our infant daughter's birthday. I've noticed a pattern in his behavior, as he did something similar in his previous marriages when his children were infants. It seems like he easily detaches from relationships at that stage but wants to reconnect with the children when they are older. Additionally, he has a history of ending relationships with women who have children when the children are infants. I've tried researching online, but I haven't found any answers. He also has an unhealthy dependence on alcohol and strongly denies the existence of mental health disorders like depression and bipolar disorder. He refuses to seek therapy or any professional help. Is there a possibility that he has a detachment disorder or some form of mental block? Where can I find more information on this?

I have been feeling a lot of conflict in my relationship with my sister. While I don't wish her any harm, I can't help but feel that I would prefer if we weren't related. It feels cruel to admit this, but I wonder why blood ties automatically mean we have to be friends. Am I being unreasonable in feeling this way? Is there a way to improve our relationship?

Lately, I've been struggling with intrusive thoughts about life after death. I was raised in a religious upbringing that emphasized the concept of eternal life in either heaven or hell. However, the idea of living forever, even in a positive place like heaven, overwhelms me. These thoughts consume my mind and trigger feelings of panic and anxiety. I worry that these thoughts are abnormal and wonder if I'm going crazy.

Patient: I experienced a traumatic event where I was sexually assaulted by multiple individuals. As a result, I have been struggling with a negative body image and low self-esteem. I have been feeling a lot of conflict and confusion about my relationship with my sister. While I don't wish her harm, I can't deny that I don't feel a strong bond or love towards her. I find myself preferring to spend time with my friends instead. It's not just a phase, as I still have a loving relationship with my parents. Is it wrong to feel this way?

I've been dealing with a difficult situation involving my ex-boyfriend who has been harassing and stalking me. It's been really challenging because we work together, and I can't seem to escape him. I believe he needs some kind of professional help to move on from our past relationship. He constantly accuses me of things that are not true, and it seems like he genuinely believes them. It's taking a toll on my mental health.

I had a complicated relationship with my ex-boyfriend. We met over a year ago and quickly fell in love, but he had trust issues and accused me of cheating. Unfortunately, we broke up right before I found out I was pregnant. I lost the baby five months later, and we didn't speak for a while. Now we're talking again, and he says he loves me but is afraid of getting hurt again. I really love him and want to rebuild our relationship and create a happy family together. Can you guide me on what steps to take? I want to make it work.

Over a year ago, I entered into a relationship with my ex-boyfriend. We quickly fell in love, but his trust issues caused him to assume I was cheating on him. Unfortunately, we broke up right around the time I found out I was pregnant. Five months later, I experienced a miscarriage and we didn't communicate for a few weeks. Now we are talking again, and he says he still loves me but is afraid of being hurt once more. I want to know how to navigate this situation because I still love him deeply and want to rebuild our happiness and create a family together.

Patient: It's been really difficult for me lately. My mother seems to ignore me and yells at me for things that I haven't done. I feel like she treats my brothers with more respect, even though I'm the one who shows her respect by not fighting with her.

After being single for 25 years, I recently experienced falling in love for the first time. However, the person I fell for abruptly ended things after just one week without any explanation or farewell. I am in so much pain and my heart feels like it's on fire.

Patient: I've been feeling a lot of internal conflict lately. I constantly find myself trying to convince myself that everything is okay, even though deep down I know it's not. I have this habit of blocking out negative experiences and memories, which I think is contributing to my struggle. On top of that, I feel like nobody cares about me. I feel completely alone.

I have been experiencing erectile dysfunction and have been trying various medications like Viagra and Cialis, but nothing seems to be working. This is causing a lot of frustration in my relationship with my girlfriend of 3 years. I told her that it is okay for her to have sex with other men. Is that really an acceptable solution?

I recently experienced a heartbreak after falling in love for the first time in 25 years. The person I fell for suddenly ended things after just a week, without any explanation or closure. It has left me feeling an intense burning pain in my heart, and I'm struggling to cope with this emotional distress.

It seems like I can't move on from my past relationship with my ex-boyfriend from four years ago, even though I'm currently in a happy relationship with my boyfriend. We had to end things back then due to parental intervention, but now we're friends and I feel a strong sexual tension between us. We never had sex when we were together, but we did have a casual thing two summers ago. Since then, he's gotten back together with his girlfriend on and off, and they're planning to move in together soon. I feel conflicted and I need closure to move forward. I'm worried about the potential consequences of talking to my ex-boyfriend about my feelings, as it could affect my current relationship and cause problems with his girlfriend. I don't know what to do, please help me.

Lately, I've noticed that whenever I try to communicate with my spouse, he becomes angry and says that I make him angry. It's not just about our conversations though, whenever he's upset about something else, like work, he takes it out on me. Our relationship feels so distant now, and it's a far cry from the laughter we used to share. I feel like he allows too much negativity to affect our relationship. What should I do? We've been married for two years, but we've been together for seven.

Over the past year, I've been experiencing a lot of frustration and stress due to my adolescent son and daughter constantly fighting. It's gotten to the point where I feel overwhelmed and don't know what to do anymore. Is there any advice you can give me on how to improve their relationship and reduce the conflicts between them?

Since my husband took a job out of state, I've noticed a significant change in his behavior. He used to just work and sleep, and on his days off, he preferred staying home. But now, he's going out with friends several nights a week while I'm left at home taking care of our two kids and working a demanding 50-hour job. He suddenly tells me he misses me and wants me to be his adored wife, but I can't help but feel emotionally neglected after years of feeling starved for affection.

I've been in a long-distance relationship with my girlfriend who is in a sorority. Lately, I've noticed that she has been changing and it's been affecting our relationship. I feel like I'm not as important to her anymore and it really hurts. She constantly asks me to support her sorority, but it's been difficult for me. I try my best every day to show her that she is the most important thing to me, but it seems like she doesn't reciprocate. For instance, she can't even stay relatively sober at fraternity parties, which worries me and makes me feel like she doesn't care about my feelings. We still love each other, but we're going through a rough patch.

My husband's work schedule has been causing a strain in our family life. He works from home, but he constantly works from morning until night, leaving little time for our family. It feels like he is neglecting us. I have to find a babysitter if I want to do anything for myself, while he gets to do whatever he wants. He rarely comes to bed when I do, and we never have date nights.

Lately, I've been feeling really guilty and anxious whenever I choose not to share certain details about my life with my friends or anyone else. It's like there's this overwhelming feeling of emptiness in my stomach that only goes away when I engage in self-harm.

I've been feeling really frustrated and neglected in my marriage lately. My husband works from home, but he seems to be working all the time, from morning until night. It feels like he's neglecting our family because I have to find a babysitter whenever I want to do something, but he can do whatever he wants. It's also been really difficult for us to spend quality time together because he rarely comes to bed when I do and we never have date nights.

Lately, I've been feeling a deep sense of guilt and emptiness when I choose not to share insignificant details or actions with my friends or others. It's as if there's a constant discomfort in my stomach that only dissipates when I engage in self-harming behaviors.

I've been in a long-distance relationship with a man who seems perfect in every way, but I'm struggling with my level of attraction towards him. While everything else is great, I find myself being drawn to more physically attractive men. We're at a point where marriage is the next step, but I want to marry someone who I have a strong physical and emotional connection with. I don't want to throw away a good relationship over what might just be temporary lust. Am I expecting too much from the "perfect guy"? Is there such a thing? Do I truly love him?

I've been feeling really isolated and alone lately. I have a girlfriend, but our relationship has become strained. I find myself pushing her away, and she also distances herself from me. We're currently going through a breakup, and I feel like I have nobody to turn to.

During my high school years, my friend and I engaged in sexual activities together. Looking back, I find it uncomfortable to even discuss because it feels strange to me now. At the time, we didn't fully grasp the implications of our actions. There was one occasion when things escalated, and we ended up engaging in sexual acts for each other. Initially, it was not intended to be a homosexual experience, but reflecting on it now, it seems that way. I buried these memories until they resurfaced recently, and it's causing a great deal of distress for me.

Lately, I've been feeling really inadequate compared to everyone else around me. It seems like everyone is more intelligent and confident than I am. I also feel a lot of pressure to have a certain body type and I've been struggling with disordered eating behaviors. I constantly feel like I'm doing everything wrong and that I can't seem to get anything right. I haven't met anyone else at school who feels this way, so I'm wondering if these feelings are normal for teenage girls. I don't think they are, and it's starting to really worry me.

I've been in a long-distance relationship with my partner, who I consider to be my ideal man. However, I'm struggling with a lack of attraction towards him compared to other men who I find more physically appealing. While everything else in our relationship is perfect, I have doubts about whether I should proceed to marriage without feeling that intense attraction. I don't want to dismiss a great relationship based solely on fleeting feelings of lust. Am I being unrealistic in my expectations of finding the "perfect guy"? Can true love exist without intense physical attraction?

Lately, I've been feeling really down and unmotivated. I don't have the energy to do the things I used to enjoy, and I feel like I'm just going through the motions. It's hard for me to find joy in anything anymore.

I have been struggling with an eating disorder characterized by episodes of binging. To address my weight, I underwent gastric sleeve surgery. However, I believe there are underlying issues related to my childhood abuse, addiction, and experiences with abusive men that need to be addressed. I have been in therapy for five months, but I feel like I am not receiving any feedback from my therapist. Can you help me?

As an international student, I recently started my first semester in graduate school in the United States. It has been quite an adjustment for me, and I experienced a cultural shock upon arrival. Thankfully, the counselor at my university has been a great source of support and has helped me navigate through this challenging period. I am now planning to return to my home country for a vacation, and I wanted to express my gratitude to my counselor. I thought about getting him something special that represents my country, and since he enjoys wine, I thought of gifting him a bottle from my country, as we are known for our wine. However, I am not sure if this would be an appropriate gift to give him after Christmas.

Ever since then, my wife struggles emotionally during this time of year and questions her love for me. Recently, another man came into her life and gave her attention, which led to infidelity. I'm willing to forgive her if she comes home.

I come from a family where my dad cheated on my mom for 13 years. This has caused me a lot of distress and insecurity in my current relationship. This obsession is causing strain in our relationship. How can I break free from this cycle?

I've been struggling with feelings of insecurity and fear when it comes to talking to others, regardless of their gender. Even when I'm just walking around, I find myself fixating on my appearance and facial expressions.

Since I was a child, I have struggled with binge-eating. It has been particularly challenging for me since I had gastric sleeve surgery. I recently spoke to a friend who is studying psychology, and they suggested that I see my doctor to check if I might have major depressive disorder. I'm feeling anxious about the potential consequences of seeking a diagnosis. If I am diagnosed with major depressive disorder, will that information be added to my medical records? I'm concerned that it could hinder my career aspirations, such as becoming a counselor, and potentially limit other opportunities. People I know who have taken antidepressants have warned me against it, suggesting that there are better treatment options available. I'm worried that if I seek help, I might be forced to go to a clinic and be compelled to take medication because others think I am incapable of making decisions for myself. While I'm not actively suicidal, I have noticed that I am neglecting self-care. I've also heard rumors about electroshock therapy still being used, and I'm not comfortable with that idea. So, I wonder if it's better for me to focus on self-help and try to work through my issues independently. It's worth noting that I have struggled with emotional difficulties since elementary school, and although I've graduated now, I still haven't been able to fully improve my mental well-being.

I had a spiritual mentor for a few years, but the experience was a mixed bag. Sometimes it was fine, but other times it felt strange. I'm concerned because this person holds a position of leadership that others trust, and nobody suspects anything. It feels like I'm being portrayed as the one attacking their character. I've been in a long-distance relationship with my partner for a while now, and everything seems perfect about him except for one thing - I'm not as physically attracted to him as I think I should be. Is it possible to have it all?

I'm currently in the process of applying to private high schools. Basketball is a big part of my life, and I currently play on my school team, which I love. Today, I had to go to the emergency room to get an X-ray of my spine. My boyfriend didn't want to sit there and wait with me. Instead, he wanted to go do things for his friends while I waited. This lack of support has left me feeling trapped in a constant state of extreme rage. It's gotten to the point where I can't even leave my living space because I'm afraid I'll lose control and harm someone.

This year has been really tough for me. My parents got divorced, even though I know they still care about each other and me. It's just hard to accept that they're no longer together. It's been really difficult for me to focus on my school work because of this.

I've had a difficult time forming connections with people. Growing up, my parents had frequent explosive fights that sometimes turned physical. While they were good parents to my brother and me, I never witnessed any love or affection between them. They often separated, leaving my brother and me to bounce between different relatives' homes while our parents were in different countries.

My friend is experiencing feelings of sadness and low self-worth due to her perceived lack of a romantic partner. She often belittles herself and expresses a belief that she is not good enough. Initially, I advised her to be patient and focus on self-improvement, hoping that she would find someone soon. However, I now realize that she is seeking external validation and relying on another person to be her primary source of happiness. After discussing this with her, she expressed that she does not know how to love herself. How can I support her in this journey?

I have been a member of a Facebook group that supports women who were born with a congenital disease that prevents conception. Lately, I've noticed that many of the women in the group, although well-intentioned, have a very negative and discouraging attitude. They often talk about the importance of being strong, but it seems like they don't take any steps to actually feel good about themselves. Instead, they seem to dwell in self-pity and have a sense of entitlement. Additionally, there are some individuals in the group who seem to think it's acceptable to ostracize women in their lives who become pregnant.

I'm a 21-year-old who currently lives at home with my parents. I've been dating my boyfriend for the past 7 months, but my parents don't approve of our relationship. They believe that because I live under their roof, they can control my decisions. My boyfriend has had a troubled past, but he has changed for the better. However, my parents think he will never change and that he's holding me back. I disagree with them because he supports me in everything I do, he's there for me during difficult times, and he knows how to help me calm down during panic attacks. Recently, my parents forced me to break up with him, but I'm not ready to let him go. Unfortunately, they won't allow me to see him as long as I live at home, and I don't have the financial means to move out. My boyfriend has offered for me to move in with him, with me covering the food and utilities while he pays the rent. I'm scared that my parents will disown me if I make that choice, but I can't imagine my life without him. Is there any way I can convince my parents to change their mind? I understand their concerns, but I want them to trust me and recognize that I'm capable of making my own choices. What should I do?

When I was in the 9th grade, my family got a puppy. Whenever the puppy was put in a box that he couldn't climb out of, he would panic and cry until someone rescued him. My mother found amusement in this and would purposely put him in the box to see his reaction, allowing him to panic and cry until I couldn't bear it anymore and intervened.

As a teenager in India, I often experience racing thoughts when I wake up. It's like my mind jumps from one thing to another, without any specific worries or concerns. These thoughts can be about anything, not necessarily negative. It's different from the usual morning thoughts that we all have.

I'm really concerned about my significant other. They have bipolar disorder and have been exhibiting strong suicidal tendencies and extreme anxiety. Every night, regardless of whether I'm home or not, we have a conversation that lasts at least an hour, where my partner goes into graphic detail about wanting to end their life. I was also hiding my depression and therapy sessions from her because I was afraid she wouldn't understand and would criticize me. Her past comments about me being overly dramatic and playing the victim have made it difficult for me to open up to her.

Patient: I live with my dad and his long-term girlfriend, who has become more of a mother figure to me than my own mother. Over time, I've noticed that my relationship with my parents has been deteriorating, especially with my dad. It feels like there's a power struggle happening, mainly initiated by him. I'm unsure if I'm to blame for this or if there are steps I can take to improve our relationship, aside from avoiding him or blindly following his rules. He has a very aggressive and controlling nature, using respect as a weapon to manipulate situations and make me feel like I'm always in the wrong. While I understand the importance of respecting parents, I've never had much respect for my birth mother due to her lack of empathy. However, I have always respected my dad, although there has been an underlying fear. The stress of living in this toxic environment has become overwhelming. My dad refuses to acknowledge his mistakes and instead blames me, which makes me feel depressed and question if there's something wrong with me. I'm at a loss for what to do.

I'm a 13-year-old from the U.S. and I've noticed something about myself that I find confusing. I can control my levels of apathy. It's like I can turn it on or off depending on the situation. For example, when something happens to a friend, I can turn off my apathy and feel worried, but it also feels kind of fake.

I've been feeling overwhelmed, anxious, and stressed lately. I've been having panic attacks sometimes, and there are times when I just don't feel like doing anything. I find comfort in being alone, but I also have this urge to punish myself, although I've never seriously hurt myself. I often insult myself and have negative thoughts, as if there's another voice in my head. While I haven't engaged in self-harm or cutting, I frequently have thoughts of suicide, even in situations like driving. These dark thoughts are really haunting me.

Hi, I'm a 16-year-old girl from the U.S. Recently, I've been experiencing these unsettling daydreams that seem to be getting worse. It all started when my older sister moved in with my stepmom and dad. We didn't have a great relationship growing up because I was raised separately, living with my aunt and cousin until I was 10.

Two years ago, I discovered that one of my closest friends was being physically and potentially mentally abused by her stepfather. Despite her dismissive explanations, I could sense her fear and resentment towards him. Recently, she has been showing up to school with cuts on her face, which she attributes to being sick and her stepdad's disapproval of her missing school. I am torn between reporting the abuse and potentially having her taken away from her mom, or continuing to support her as a friend. What should I do?

I have found myself in a complicated and distressing situation. I have developed romantic feelings for my brother's wife, despite our friendship predating their marriage. It has been 15 years and I am still unable to move on from these emotions. I feel a mix of anger, confusion, and love towards her, but I don't want to jeopardize my brother's marriage. I'm feeling lost and in desperate need of guidance.

I have been feeling really hurt and left out when it comes to my family dynamics. My sister seems to receive more attention and support from our mom, especially when it comes to her children. Even though we live closer to our mom, she only attends a few of my kids' birthdays, whereas she never misses any of my sister's kids' events, despite her living farther away. It's frustrating because I'm the one who puts in the effort to maintain communication and make plans. Whenever I try to talk to my sister about my feelings, she accuses me of starting a fight. I recently invited her to Thanksgiving, but she declined because she didn't want to take her child away from her grandparents and her boyfriend's kids away from their family. This has been going on for a long time and it's really taking a toll on me emotionally. I find myself continually subjecting myself to these hurtful situations.

I'm concerned about my mom's recent behavior. She had a difficult childhood, but lately, she's been acting strangely. It's almost like she's trying to relive her childhood. I worry about her every day because there seems to be something new going wrong. This started about a year ago when she turned 38.

I have been experiencing some troubling symptoms that I think might be related to Antisocial Personality Disorder (ASPD). However, I have already been diagnosed with Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD) and I haven't mentioned these ASPD symptoms to my therapist. I'm not sure if they will believe me or understand what I'm going through. I have a tendency to lie and lack empathy at times. I also find myself manipulating others for my own benefit, and I have a strong desire for attention and control. While BPD explains some of these behaviors, it doesn't account for my obsession with blood, constant thoughts of harming others, lack of remorse, and dreams of violently killing people I know and strangers. I'm not sure if it's safe to share these thoughts with my therapist. Can you provide guidance on this?

I have been engaging in several behaviors that I realize may not be healthy or beneficial for my relationships. Some examples include speaking negatively about someone's past to a stranger, ignoring my friend's girlfriend when they first meet, calling her irrational, boasting about my achievements, pretending to have another mental illness, taking on a high-responsibility role, excluding newcomers from groups, using sarcasm towards my friend's girlfriend, publicly belittling others, and manipulating my friend's boyfriend to lie and call her irrational based on my advice.

I'm really struggling with the situation involving my mother-in-law. After I wrote a blog post about dealing with toxic people, mentioning her as an example, she completely banned me from her life. My husband claims to be on my side, but he continues to see and talk to his parents as if nothing happened.

Since moving to Canada two years ago, I've been feeling a lot of anxiety about my 23-year-old sister. Our parents are back home, and I feel a strong sense of responsibility for her well-being. She relies on me for everything, from tasks to making decisions. Her eating habits are concerning, as she either doesn't eat at all or eats unhealthy fast food, which has led to her being overweight. She also has trouble sleeping, feels depressed, and doesn't have any friends. I constantly worry that something bad will happen to her due to her poor eating habits. I've tried talking to her about seeing a nutritionist or psychologist, but she never listens and says she wants to change but can't. I just want to stop worrying so much and focus on living my own life.

Lately, I've been experiencing intrusive thoughts of dangerous situations like getting into a car accident or being a victim of violence. These thoughts have been persistent, occurring both while I'm driving and when I'm at home. I've even had thoughts about harming myself, although I don't always act on them. It's strange because the intensity of my motivation to carry out these thoughts fluctuates and sometimes fades away. It doesn't matter to me whether these thoughts end in my death or not, and my preference varies. The recent suicide of a friend has had a profound impact on me, but I must clarify that these thoughts started before their tragic incident. While I am deeply saddened by my friend's loss, I also struggle with conflicting feelings of guilt and envy because he ultimately did what I've always contemplated.

I'm a 26-year-old disabled man living in the United States. I have been dealing with depression, anxiety, and PTSD. My mother has complete control over my life and she constantly lies to me. I feel like I have no freedom because she won't let me go anywhere without her, have anyone over at my house, or even drive anywhere. I feel trapped and I need help.

It seems like my struggles with anxiety and depression started in 8th grade, but looking back, I realize that I've always had difficulties with social connections. I used to engage in maladaptive daydreaming as a coping mechanism and seek out depressing content. I also had unhealthy attachments to others, which drove them away. When I moved in 5th grade, things seemed fine until 7th grade ended and my anxiety peaked. I stopped caring about everything and everyone, which helped alleviate some physical symptoms but left me feeling empty. Now, in high school, I feel isolated and fearful of the future. I don't have any interests or goals, and I often retreat to my own fantasy world. I recognize that my thoughts may be distorted by anxiety, but I still don't feel any different. I just hope to someday be "normal" and have fulfilling experiences, although I often shy away from them in the moment. Sometimes, I wonder if this is all karma for being a bad person or a narcissist suffering the consequences of my actions.

As a teenager in the Philippines, I have noticed a pattern of narcissistic behavior in my father's side of the family, and it deeply disgusts me. However, recently I have started to question my own sense of self. While I was preparing to argue against this behavior, I suddenly had a realization that made me question everything. This is the first time I am being truly honest with myself, and it's overwhelming.

I'm really struggling with a difficult situation. I am currently engaged to be married, but I've been feeling conflicted because I think I may be in love with an old friend. I care deeply about both of them and I don't know what to do. Can you please guide me in figuring out the right choice? Kind regards.

I have a family member who is chronically angry and verbally abusive towards me. Even though I have stood up to them in the past and they haven't physically attacked me since, they still engage in aggressive behavior like yelling, swearing, and slamming doors. I find their cursing offensive and degrading. Is there any way I can avoid letting their behavior affect my mood?

Throughout my life, I have always enjoyed being alone. However, as I've gotten older and entered the adult world, I've noticed that this preference is starting to have a negative impact on me. Whenever I'm with friends, I feel uncomfortable and awkward. It feels like I'm constantly putting on a facade and I can only truly relax when I'm at home by myself. When I'm alone, I find myself lost in my thoughts for hours, imagining a different life and various scenarios. Is this normal?

Hi, my name is Lillyan. I'm 19 years old and I've been experiencing symptoms of Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) for the past six months. It came on suddenly and has been incredibly debilitating. My family and I were unsure how to handle it, and I'm still struggling to cope. I have severe tremors and haven't been able to return to work. Sometimes I have intrusive thoughts, like imagining there's a shooter in the house when I hear a sound. I don't actually see anything, but the image pops into my head. I constantly need background noise to distract myself. Is it normal to have these thoughts and images? I'm really scared that I might be going crazy or developing schizophrenia. I've never actually seen or heard anything other than my own anxiety-induced perceptions, like mistaking a lamp for something else. It's difficult to talk to my family about it because they don't believe me. I have an appointment with a therapist next week, but I'd appreciate some clarity in the meantime.

I’ve been experiencing these symptoms for over 7 years now. It started with increased irritability and anger, which escalated to destructive behaviors like breaking things and ripping up clothing. I also started isolating myself from loved ones. Over time, I developed a belief that I am being watched and that people are trying to harm me through poisoning or even murder. Presently, I struggle to form relationships due to my unpredictable behavior like laughing in inappropriate situations or showing no emotion at all. I also believe that people are reading my thoughts and trying to steal them, and I hear voices commanding me to do terrible things. This has had a significant impact on my ability to maintain employment, as there are days when I can't even leave my house due to fear. Despite all this, I have never sought professional help because I've been told that having strong faith in God is enough.

I have been experiencing symptoms that align with depression or a depressive disorder. However, when I try to explain it to others, they don't believe me. In March of this year, I was hospitalized due to extreme exhaustion, dehydration despite drinking water, loss of appetite, constant feelings of sadness, and difficulty sleeping. I was diagnosed with insomnia, but my parents made jokes about it instead of taking it seriously.

Lately, I've been experiencing occasional suicidal thoughts, although I have no intention of acting on them. While they may not be too serious, they still concern me. I've noticed that I do things at a slower pace, which I've heard could be a sign of depression. Additionally, a few activities that used to bring me joy don't have the same effect anymore. I often feel like a failure, although there are moments when I feel overly confident. Another issue I've been facing is difficulty sleeping. I've been ignoring the possibility of having depression because I sometimes think that people fake it. Could this be depression? And if it is, should I consider seeking professional help?

It seems like I have always been highly observant and intellectually gifted, but I struggle with understanding people's motivations and emotions. As a result, I have developed a skill for charming others and being able to quickly assess their inner thoughts and beliefs. However, this ability has left me feeling weary and disillusioned. I often find myself frustrated with people's lack of self-awareness and their seemingly slow and foolish actions. I feel like I am surrounded by individuals who are unaware of the consequences of their actions, and it's disheartening to manipulate them so easily. I long for genuine human connection, but sometimes I feel like an outsider in my own understanding of people.

I've been really worried about these thoughts I've been having lately. They seem to come up whenever I read or hear about people who are abusive or cruel, especially parents who harm their children. I can't help but think that it would be better for their victims if these people were no longer alive, and I feel guilty for having these thoughts.

I've been struggling with understanding why my friend S consistently chooses someone who treats him poorly over me, even though I've always been there for him and tried to make him happy. No matter what this other person, C, does to S, he forgives them instantly, whereas he never forgives me if I do something similar.

Patient's statement (background): The patient is a young woman from Canada who recently went through a breakup with her partner. They had been dating for 2 years and lived together. The patient had difficulties adjusting to a new city, which caused her to experience unhappiness and anxiety. The strain of these challenges became too much for her partner, leading to the breakup. They attempted to reconcile but her partner's mixed signals and inconsistent commitment made the situation even more confusing for the patient.
Sometimes, when I am feeling sexually aroused, I find myself fantasizing about girls between the ages of 14 and 19. These fantasies involve sexual scenarios with myself.

Lately, I've been experiencing a significant change in my behavior and emotions. I've noticed that I no longer enjoy activities that I used to, and I find myself avoiding social interactions with my friends. It has become challenging for me to hold conversations with my grandparents and dad due to social anxiety, which is something I didn't struggle with before. When I'm at school, I might initially feel positive, but as soon as I come home, I suddenly feel overwhelmingly sad, without any apparent reason. I've heard about bipolar disorder, but I'm not sure if that's what I'm experiencing, or if it's all just social anxiety.

As a teenager in Canada, my boyfriend and I have been in a relationship for 1.7 years. Despite having arguments and taking a 4-month break to figure things out, our relationship is generally good. We're both 18 years old and we feel like the decisions we make now will have a lasting impact on our lives.

I have been struggling with severe body dysmorphic disorder, generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), bipolar disorder, and severe depression. My body dysmorphic disorder started when I was also battling anorexia. During this time, I also had to come to terms with my sexual orientation, which has been a source of great distress for me. It's something that I deeply dislike and it has contributed to my feelings of worthlessness. The reason I am reaching out is because I feel like I am losing touch with reality more and more each day. However, I am hesitant to pursue therapy because I have convinced myself that it won't make any difference. Online, I receive hurtful messages from gay men who criticize my appearance and tell me that I shouldn't be gay because of how I look. Some even suggest that I end my own life. There isn't a single thing that anyone could say to make me like myself, and being gay isn't something that can be changed, so why waste time and money on therapy that can't fix these issues? I have had negative experiences with therapy in the past, and I'm tired of people suggesting it as a solution when it hasn't worked for me. How can I explain to others that cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) may not be effective for everyone? Not everyone has the financial means to afford therapy, and it feels like the situation is only getting worse. Why do therapists feel the need to oversell the effectiveness of treatment at the expense of their patients' well-being? It seems like many therapists are only interested in money and use their patients as a way to figure out their own problems. I even studied Psychology myself, and it feels like a joke. It's all about the money (from the USA).

I have been living with my family friend, who I consider to be like an aunt, and three other roommates. Initially, we planned to stay together for a few months until we could save enough money to move closer to where my aunt wants to live and where I'll be attending college. However, the living situation has become increasingly challenging. The other roommates don't clean, neglect their cat, and leave waste out, causing a lot of unpleasantness. When I confronted them about it, two roommates decided to move out, but the remaining ones started to say mean things about me, making me uncomfortable. On top of that, my aunt ate my separate food despite agreeing not to, and she responded angrily when I asked her to replace it. I feel like everyone is picking on me, and it's becoming difficult to handle this situation on a daily basis.

I'm only 13 years old and sometimes I feel like I'm just being dramatic like other kids my age who want attention. But I really want to be honest about what I'm going through because I genuinely want to know if I should reach out for help or make changes in my life. Can you please guide me?

As a teenager in the United States, I didn't experience direct bullying or name-calling about my appearance. However, as I transitioned into young adulthood, I've noticed that I have developed an unhealthy obsession with how I look. I constantly find myself scrutinizing my appearance, fixating on perceived flaws. It's become a compulsion, as I can't seem to stop looking at myself in reflective surfaces like mirrors, windows, and even my phone screen. It's starting to make me feel conceited and trapped in this cycle.

I feel trapped and emotionally abused by my family. I don't have any other options because I'm unemployed, have no money or friends, and rarely leave my home. When I try to express how their treatment affects me, they dismiss or snap at me, making it hard for me to communicate. I'm reaching a breaking point and fear I might resort to drastic measures (not suicide) if things don't change.

I'm really concerned about my 14-year-old brother. Our family understands that teenagers can go through difficult phases where they may become angry and distant from the family. However, our main concern is that he spends all his time playing violent video games on his laptop and neglects his homework and household responsibilities. His grades are suffering, he refuses to make friends, and he isolates himself.

Recently, I had a dream that was part of a series of unrelated dreams. In this dream, I found myself at my grandmother's house and came across a picture of myself as a child with my now-deceased grandfather. In the picture, it seemed like he was kissing me with his tongue. I was initially alarmed and confused, but didn't mention it directly. Instead, I focused on trying to determine the year the photo was taken, as I believed I was two years old in the picture. My grandmother and father looked at the back of the photo to find the date, but they didn't seem to notice or acknowledge what I was seeing. They even tried to distract me with trivial things, though I'm not sure if that was intentional. We couldn't find the date, and they didn't seem concerned. When I saw my grandfather kiss me, I immediately felt that it was molestation and that it was wrong. However, I didn't make a big deal out of it. It was so out of character for my grandfather and so disturbing that I didn't really feel anything at the time, just a bit of disbelief. After we couldn't find the date, I let the rest of my paternal family distract me and didn't bring it up again or care. In fact, I had completely unrelated dreams afterwards, and when I woke up, I remembered thinking that every dream except that one was significant. It later dawned on me that I had witnessed something incredibly disturbing, but I still didn't have a big reaction. None of my sister, mom, or maternal family members were in the dream. It was just one dream, and I'm wondering if it might indicate that I was actually molested as a child.

I follow these girls on social media and often fantasize about having a sexual relationship with them or seeing them engage in sexual activities. I also have an attraction towards adult women, but my preference leans more towards teenage girls, about 80%.

I have been dealing with a difficult family situation involving my mother, who has been diagnosed with several personality disorders such as Narcissistic Personality Disorder (NPD), Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD), and Dissociative Disorder. She is very judgmental and disrespectful towards me, and I'm not sure if we can rebuild our relationship as long as my mother is involved.

Last year, my parents and boyfriend had a heated argument about my cat. They accused me of abusing her because she has separation anxiety and I spend time with my boyfriend once a week. My boyfriend has been supportive and even helped out financially, but my parents are constantly negative towards him. They think he will cheat on me and abuse me. We had an agreement that they would help with rent and bills, but now they want me to pay everything on my own. I tried to find a roommate, but my parents didn't approve. I'm considering getting a foster for my cat and staying with my boyfriend until we can find our own place. I can't afford to live on my own, and finding a room seems risky. My boyfriend is planning to join the Air Force, so he wants to wait until he returns to find a place together. I'm not sure if this is the right decision, but I feel like I need to get away for the sake of my mental health.

Since May, I've been experiencing difficulties with sleep. It started when I returned home and began sleeping in my own room after having a roommate. I've been feeling extremely anxious at night, constantly perceiving things that make me fearful. For example, I see flickering lights by my window and hear sounds coming from under my desk, both of which make me believe that someone is present. These fears have become so overwhelming that I am unable to sleep unless I take benadryl. Due to my lack of sleep, I have also started to experience minor hallucinations, primarily auditory ones such as hearing the microwave running or dishes breaking. Additionally, I often feel like there are bugs on me when I am feeling particularly paranoid. How can I cope with these fears?

When I was around 10 years old, my 3 or 4-year-old brother used to sleep over in my room frequently. One night, after watching a movie where people kissed, I became curious and kissed my brother on the lips for a longer duration than usual. I didn't understand the sexual or romantic connotations at that time, but I felt it was strange. It lasted for about 5 seconds, and I believe my brother asked me to stop.

I have noticed some concerning traits in myself. I lack empathy, constantly believe I am superior to others, and have a big ego. I also tend to think negatively and assume the worst in situations. I enjoy having power and get easily bored when my friends share their problems with me. I am a teenager in the United States. I have been diagnosed with depression, anxiety, ADD, and Type 1 diabetes. But I'm scared it will ruin my relationships and I want to know how to improve myself or find the root of this problem.
