However, during my first visit to her place, I discovered that she had been lying about her communication with a male friend, whom she had a one-night stand with last summer.

I experienced severe trauma in my childhood, including sexual abuse by my father and being victimized by other men. These experiences have left me feeling worthless and questioning my own morality. I have engaged in harmful behaviors, such as harming my pets and exhibiting cruelty towards my cat. I worry about the potential for hurting others, including a hypothetical girlfriend. I wonder if I am a predator or prey, and if my actions make me evil. I have even contemplated isolating myself or ending my life to protect others. Can you help me understand what is happening?

Throughout my life, I have struggled with a significant lack of memory, especially when it comes to my past. I only have a few memories from my entire childhood, none from junior high school, and very few from high school. It seems that as soon as an event is over, I can only recall a small fraction of what I experienced. However, it is particularly challenging for me to cope with the fact that my memories of my childhood and early teenage years are essentially non-existent.

Patient: I’m a 17-year-old Indian with ADHD and I have aspirations to pursue medicine and a post-graduate degree in forensic medicine. However, I'm struggling to concentrate for more than a couple of minutes and I'm worried about how it will impact my future career. I received my 12th-grade results yesterday and they were disappointing. My mom is extremely upset with me. I have an entrance exam in two days, but I haven't prepared enough to achieve a good score, and I feel ashamed about it. There's another exam a month later that I'm interested in, but my mom wants me to have other options. I'm scared of disappointing my family and relatives if I don't perform well in the first exam. I also feel guilty for not living up to my parents' expectations. They are unaware of my ADHD and I'm afraid to tell them. I constantly struggle with distractions and find it hard to focus on anything, which has greatly affected my productivity. I don't know how to handle this situation and I don't want to let my parents down. Please help me.

I've noticed that whenever something happens that I don't like or disagree with, I suddenly feel a lot of pressure in my head. It's like my head is going to burst, and it happens without any warning. I think it might be an anxiety attack.

My brother, who is 40 years old, has been consistently quitting jobs for the past 20 years. He initially worked as a lecturer but quit because he felt uncomfortable with teenagers. He then took a gap year and eventually joined a school to teach primary kids. However, he resigned from that job as well, stating that he didn't get along with the principal. Since then, he has been repeating this pattern of joining different schools every six months to a year. He refuses to take advice from anyone and cuts off contact with those who criticize him. He keeps making excuses, saying he will start fresh once he recovers.

I recently discovered that my partner is liking a large number of half-naked women's pictures on Instagram. This has made me feel insecure and questioning our relationship. It seems like he prioritizes his activity on Instagram over acknowledging our relationship there. Additionally, these women are very different from me in terms of appearance. I can't help but feel like he wants someone else and is only with me because he can't have those other women.

Lately, I've been experiencing some troubling thoughts and feelings. I find myself consumed by certain fantasies and lacking empathy. I have thoughts about harming people, particularly through poison or engineering a suicide, although I don't believe I would actually act on these thoughts. I've noticed that I've become socially withdrawn and my relationships feel superficial. However, I also have the capacity to deeply care for certain individuals and enjoy helping them. I recently took the Hare psychopathy checklist and scored 29, but I'm not sure if that accurately reflects my ability to feel empathy. I don't think I need professional help, but I would appreciate your thoughts and any advice you may have.

I grew up in a secular family. Both of my parents never mentioned religion and they never expressed any religious beliefs. In fact, my dad always made it clear that he disapproved of religion. It's interesting because neither of my parents had any religion in their own upbringing either. It's just not something that was ever a part of our family culture.

My girlfriend and I have been in a relationship for over 9 months. Initially, we had sex after three weeks of dating, and she was the one who initiated it. However, around the three-month mark, she started showing a decreased interest in having sex, and there have been times when we've gone a whole month without being intimate. It's worth noting that she started taking birth control pills around the same time. I wonder if this could be influencing her behavior.

My sister is a 33-year-old woman who is married and has three children, ages 7, 4, and 8 months. Her youngest child was recently diagnosed with a rare genetic condition, which has understandably caused her a lot of stress. However, she has always had anger issues that she has never acknowledged. Whenever she is upset or angry with one person, she tends to shut off and be angry with everyone around her. Our family has learned to tiptoe around her during these moods, but we know that this isn't a healthy way for her to cope. We want to help her, but she refuses to talk about it or seek therapy. We don't want her to become isolated, as she doesn't have relationships outside the family. How can we approach this situation without pushing her away?

I have been struggling with depression and anxiety since I was about 10 years old. Recently, I experienced a significant loss of a loved one, which has exacerbated my symptoms. I feel trapped in a constant state of anxiety and it's becoming overwhelming. Unfortunately, I am unable to find an available therapist to see me in the near future. Can you provide any resources for free or Medicaid-covered mental health help that I can access quickly?

I've noticed that I tend to be a very expressive and passionate person. Whether I'm angry or excited, I have a tendency to become loud and argumentative. I have been told that I have the potential to be a leader, but I personally feel uncomfortable with that idea. I actually despise the idea of being seen as a potential leader because of my traits. It really bothers me.

Patient: I just wanted everything to go away. I'm 14 years old and currently in high school. As a child, my mother used to teach me, but if I got a question wrong, she would hit me with a rolling pin. There were times when she would get angry and physically drag and throw me into my bedroom. I wasn't allowed to cry, otherwise, she would punish me even more. Although this happened more when I was younger, these memories still haunt me. Sometimes, I would get bruises. However, my mother would try to make it up to me by saying she loved me and buying me snacks. It's confusing because I still don't know if this is considered abuse. My father did help me a lot, but he was often working. There have always been two sides, my mother's side and my father's side. I always had to choose, but I don't want to anymore. My parents always fight and then make up, but it's a never-ending cycle. I just want it all to go away. I've considered running away, but I'm scared my mother will find me and punish me. I don't know what to do.

I'm really concerned about my preteen son's behavior. He often seeks attention and doesn't seem to care about following rules or respecting authority. He has gotten detentions at school for being disrespectful to his teachers and has even acted out during scout activities. We've tried taking away privileges, grounding him, and even tried neurotherapy, but nothing seems to be working. I'm at a loss and don't know what to do next. Any suggestions?

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for the past two years. Our first year was okay, but it felt like he was more focused on himself than our relationship. However, things changed when he experienced a significant loss and began relying on me for support. Since then, I've noticed that he's become excessively attached to me, and it's starting to become unhealthy. I'm not sure how to handle the situation.

Hello, I am a 34-year-old male and I am happily married with children. I have always had a fondness for kids and infants in general. However, in the past few years, I have been experiencing a troubling urge to hurt specific infants. This urge is limited to three infants from my wife's sister, two infants from my wife's brother, and one infant from an old female friend's brother. I don't feel this way towards any other infants. It's important to note that I have a good relationship with my wife's sister and her husband, but I don't feel the same way towards my wife's brother.

Lately, I've been finding it increasingly difficult to deal with a very close friend of mine. They exhibit several concerning symptoms such as compulsive talking, defensiveness, physical restlessness when standing, a need to always be right and seek agreement, frequent anger outbursts, trouble with speech fluency, interrupting conversations to bring up past grievances, and repeating themselves until acknowledged.

Since my recent childbirth, my in-laws have started becoming more involved in our lives. They visit more frequently, constantly text me, and have even crossed some boundaries. Despite telling them "no," they still show up uninvited, make plans without asking me, and change those plans when I assert myself.

I have been struggling with a lack of hope for my own future for the past six years. While I can still find moments of joy, I feel like I have lost almost everything. I am frustrated with the mental healthcare system and feel that it prioritizes cheap imported drugs over providing proper care for individuals who are passionate or who identify as white, straight, and conservative. I am tired of being associated with opioid addicts when I am dealing with depression and PTSD, which are not choices. Additionally, I feel frustrated with the privileges given to certain groups in society, such as illegal immigrants and minorities, while I work hard and feel like what I earn is being taken away from me and given to freeloaders. The cost of my corporate health insurance has skyrocketed, and it only covers the same low-quality providers that Medicaid recipients can access. I believe that Obamacare has compromised our private medical data, and I am concerned about the cures act and the potential risks it poses to human subjects. The generic medications I've tried have had terrible side effects, and I am dissatisfied with the quality of non-MD providers in the healthcare industry. All of these factors have left me feeling hopeless about the future and concerned about the treatment of citizens in our country.

I have been in therapy for almost 4 years to address childhood trauma and general mental health concerns. Initially, everything felt fine and my therapist asked the right questions. But lately, things have become intense. She knows that I struggle with forming friendships, so she asked if we could consider ourselves friends. Two weeks ago, I started sitting on the floor during sessions for comfort, and she followed suit, sitting across from me with her shoes off. I found her sitting position a bit uncomfortable, as she had her legs open. During our conversation, she mentioned her own feelings and said she would share them with me. I'm unsure if I'm overthinking this or if I'm just feeling emotionally sensitive. I mentioned this to my sister and she suggested that my therapist may have feelings for me and that I should consider finding a new therapist.

Hi. I've been in a relationship for over a year now with someone who was my friend for 2 years before that. Around 4-5 months into our relationship, he expressed concern about how I prioritize taking care of myself. It hurt me deeply because I've struggled with low self-esteem and insecurity. Since then, our relationship has felt disconnected and awkward, which has worsened my insecurities and anxiety. I've even accused him of cheating, despite knowing deep down that I love him. I've lost trust in everything and question our relationship every day, leading to heightened anxiety and avoidance of seeing or talking to him. I hate feeling this way.

I went through a difficult divorce after being in an abusive marriage. My children also suffered a lot during that time. However, I am grateful that after years of hard work, my two children have come out of it incredibly well. I have a lot of positive things in my life, such as financial stability, a successful career, and a supportive family. But what truly brings me the most happiness and fulfillment is seeing my children thriving and happy. I am deeply grateful for that every day.

Patient: Since moving in together, my boyfriend has been getting angry with me every day. It usually centers around me being too quiet. The first time he yelled at me for being quiet, I became even more quiet as a defense mechanism from a previous abusive relationship. Then he started calling me names and I had a panic attack due to my anxiety. He apologizes afterward and blames his behavior on needing time to adjust to our living situation, but it's starting to make me feel like there's something wrong with me. I'm constantly walking on eggshells at home and dread being home when he's there. I know he has a history of sexual abuse and a "fuck everyone else" mindset, but he's never been this way with me before. I shake every time he yells at me and he gets even angrier when I try to talk to him about it. I've asked him to stop calling me names, but he hasn't. He even says hurtful things about my past and makes me feel lucky that he's not worse. I'm a detective who has worked in domestic violence, but I'm struggling to recognize if this is going down a dangerous path. I've never called him names and I don't know if things will improve.

Throughout my life, I have noticed that I have been attracted to older men, even as early as the age of 4. However, I have also been attracted to people closer to my own age, and I am currently in a relationship with someone who is around the same age as me.

It seems like my boyfriend has made significant changes in his life to be with me, but he is still holding on to aspects of his past. We've been living together for over two and a half years, yet he hasn't finalized his divorce from his ex-wife. He also keeps old pictures of them on his social media profiles and has not returned a sentimental item she asked for. It feels like he's struggling to fully let go. Why would someone make such big changes but still hold on to the past?

As a teenager in the U.S., I am feeling genuinely scared for myself and others. I am currently serving as a soldier in the Army and have aspirations of becoming an Officer in the coming years. Additionally, I am a freshman at university. Last summer, during Basic Training, I experienced stress fractures that led to a break in my left hip. While physically healed now, I am concerned about the impact this may have had on my mental health.

Since I was around 10 years old, I've been feeling this constant pressure of anxiety in my mind. It started off as a faint presence in the background, but now it feels like it's taking over every moment of my life, whether I'm aware of it or not.

As a teenager in Thailand, I often find joy in making others happy. I am known as the funny one in my friend group and I bring a lot of positive energy to those around me. However, lately I've been struggling. I've experienced panic attacks, sought medical advice from a heart doctor, and have been dealing with short-term memory issues.
I have been in a long-term relationship with someone who started out as a friend about ten years ago. We have grown together and been through a lot.

I have concerns about my fiancé's behavior towards my 18-year-old daughter. He does things that make me question his intentions. We have been together for over a year and have a 9-month-old baby. We are planning to get married soon. He has disclosed to me that he had a past incident where he molested his younger sister when they were younger. He has received help for it and was in a youth program until he became an adult. He also faced legal charges for the incident. I have accepted him and have been dealing with it because he is mostly a great guy and has never harmed me.

Last week, I noticed that I was smelling things that weren't actually there. Although I didn't experience any strong or unpleasant smells like rotten fish or eggs, it still worried me. I read online that this could be an early sign of developing Schizophrenia, which scared me. I went to the doctor on Friday for bloating and headaches, and he did a neuro test which came back normal. However, I did smell some things in my room, but I attributed it to the messiness. Despite not having the smell issues anymore, I can't help but worry that it might be Schizophrenia.
I've recently started dating this girl who had a year of being single and enjoying herself, hooking up on Tinder and partying. It's been on my mind and I'm not sure how to handle it.

Lately, I've noticed that my speech has become slower and I struggle to find the right words sometimes. It's frustrating because I used to be able to speak quickly and effortlessly. People often finish my sentences for me or respond before I can finish. Is there anything I can do, like tongue and mouth exercises, to help improve my speech speed? Additionally, I've been experiencing frequent word-finding difficulties. For example, I might say "I put the paper down on the table" when I actually meant to say "chair." I also mix up my children's names often. Is this a problem with my brain or am I just being lazy?

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for about 8 months, but things have been difficult due to my past traumas. In the last half of our relationship, I've acted emotionally abusive, responding with anger and insults out of jealousy and insecurity. My boyfriend wants to leave, but I don't want to split. I've started counseling and I'm promising him that I'll change because I truly love him, despite my actions suggesting otherwise.

I've been feeling really down lately. I've been dealing with self-hate and feeling disconnected from my friends. But lately, I've noticed that one of the main causes of my depression is that I don't feel safe in my own mind.

Lately, I've been feeling a significant change in myself. I used to have a lot of curiosity about life and many interests. I had dreams and everything seemed bright. But now, suddenly, I feel dumb. I don't have any opinions and I'm slow in my studies. I struggle to concentrate in class and even forget things I've heard multiple times. It's like my brain isn't working properly. Nothing seems to go inside my head and I forget most of what I hear or read.

When I was around 5 or 6 years old, I had a friend named Jackie who engaged in sexually inappropriate behavior in front of me. At the time, I didn't understand that it was wrong, so I participated as well. This continued until I moved away and lost contact with Jackie. I feel a lot of shame and embarrassment about this, but I've recently started wondering if it could have caused trauma or PTSD. I already struggle with anxiety and depression, and I've been experiencing symptoms like insomnia and nightmares. I never thought much about it before, but it suddenly came back to me this year. Can you help me understand if this event has affected me?

When I was 11 years old, I discovered that my brother was struggling with depression and even had thoughts of suicide. At that young age, I didn't know how to handle it, and my parents seemed angry with me for not knowing what to do. That night, I cried myself to sleep out of fear and confusion about my brother's situation. I blamed myself and thought I was somehow responsible for his changed behavior. Sometimes, when my brother says he doesn't want to be alive anymore or resorts to smoking as a coping mechanism, I feel helpless. It makes me question if he loves me because if he doesn't value his own life, does that mean he doesn't value any life? Last week, I watched a documentary on the Jonestown massacre and it made me question the value of life even more. I feel conflicted because my brother is the one with depression, but it affects me deeply. Am I wrong for feeling this way?

I have been dating a guy for the past 6 months. We met online and both live very busy lives where our careers are very important to us. He currently travels for work to another state Monday-Thursday every week. I am his first serious girlfriend and the only girlfriend he’s introduced to his parents (that don’t even live in the same state as we do). Throughout our 6-month relationship he has taken many steps to show how committed he is to me. For example, when I had received an interview for school in Colorado, he began interviewing for jobs there. For the past couple months, he’s been looking for jobs back in the city that we live in. Despite all the great things he’s done, and despite how much I know he loves me, I have severe trust/jealously issues. My last boyfriend had lied to me and was dating a “friend” while he was dating me. My first love whom I dated for 2.5 years broke up with me because he developed feelings for someone else. Needless to say, I let past experiences and my insecurities get the best of me in my current relationship. I have gotten jealous about his female friends and have admittedly over-reacted many times. However, I have had (what I fear) legitimate reasons to be concerned about his new friendship with a female coworker. Like I said he works out of state during the week. On the phone one night, he mentioned he met a girl at work who’s parents live where his parents live and that she invited him to get together for drinks with her and her brother during Christmas. Fast forward to Christmas, after not responding to my text for hours, he tells me he and his sister were having drinks and playing games at his coworker’s parents house. I got very upset and asked if they had hung out before. He admitted that they spent two hours together ALONE on the beach two days prior. I was distraught and did not speak to him until the next day. He insists they are just friends and I have nothing to worry about. I let it go until I recently saw that they became friends on Facebook. I again got very upset with him and expressed how much it bothered me. He was hurt that I didn’t trust him despite saying time and time again that I had nothing to worry about and that she was just a friend. He isn’t friends with anyone else on Facebook from work other than her and he even works with a guy that went to the same college as him. To me, this situation does not seem right. As I have told him, I fear he has developed feelings for this person and doesn’t want to admit it to himself, let alone me. I don’t want to be with someone who has feelings for someone else and I wish he would just admit it to me if that’s the case. My question is: Am I letting my extreme jealous nature get the best of me and I need to learn to take my boyfriend at his word? Or do I need to interpret my feelings as instinct and walk away from the relationship?

Counselor's response: It sounds like you have been experiencing a vivid and imaginative way of engaging with music and creating stories since you were 9 years old. This is known as musical imagery or musical fantasizing, and it is actually quite common. It seems that this behavior has become more frequent and time-consuming for you as you've gotten older. While music may have initially triggered these stories, it seems that they now occur even without music. It's important to note that this is not necessarily a problem or abnormal, but it is understandable that you find it bothersome and distracting, particularly when it interferes with your studying.

Hello, I've been dealing with depression for as long as I can remember. I find myself using the internet as a way to escape and distract myself from the pain. It all started when I left the Jehovah Witness religion at the age of 15 because I didn't agree with their beliefs. My mom doesn't understand and insists that I'm unhappy because I don't believe in God.

Over the past few weeks, I've been experiencing this overwhelming sense of emptiness that I haven't felt in years. It feels like I've lost control over my emotions. It's as if my emotions have become like a switch, where I have no say in whether it's on or off. Sometimes, it's on and I experience a range of emotions, and then suddenly it's turned off and I feel nothing. I've noticed that even when I watch videos that are meant to evoke emotions like sadness, anger, happiness, or motivation, I don't feel anything. It's frustrating because I don't even feel frustrated about it. I'm just really concerned about what this means for me.

Since 2004, I've noticed some interesting changes in my sister-in-law's appearance and lifestyle. I have a unique pin-up style with platinum blonde hair and tattoos, while she used to have a more ordinary style. However, she has recently started dyeing her hair blonde and wearing flower clips, as well as purchasing pin-up style purses from the same brand as me. Additionally, she and my brother have bought cars and trucks that are the same make and model as ours, just different colors (mine is black, theirs is white). It's starting to feel like she's trying to imitate me.

I've been experiencing some troubling thoughts and behaviors lately. I find myself fantasizing about killing others and I've even abused animals in the past as a way to cope with my anger. My childhood was very traumatic, as I was given up by my mother and went in and out of foster care. I was also subjected to sexual abuse. I feel like this has destroyed me and I don't feel any guilt for the harm I've caused. I've even gone so far as to plan out the details of killing my adoptive parents. I've attempted suicide multiple times, but without success. I feel this deep anger towards the world and I challenge authority. I've been diagnosed with mild depression and emotionally unstable personality disorder, but I'm concerned that I may have traits of a psychopath. I worry that one day I may actually harm someone. What is wrong with me?

I'm concerned about my sister's behavior. She has been constantly blaming our upbringing for all of her problems and has been fabricating stories about our childhood. It's become more noticeable since she pursued a degree in early childhood development. During her studies, she started criticizing how she was raised and discussing her own childhood experiences. I'm not sure how to approach this situation.

During my childhood, I experienced both mental and physical abuse. Although I have made efforts to overcome these experiences and find closure, I still feel their lingering effects. Despite ending the toxic relationships with my abusers and considering myself a healthy individual, I have noticed some negative habits that stem from that time, such as dissociation. I find myself daydreaming frequently and constantly needing external sounds, like music or TV, even if I'm not actively engaging with them. Every few days, I also feel empty and disconnected, almost like a zombie. While I can identify these symptoms and occasional waves of depression, I'm struggling to understand the root cause. Previous experiences with psychologists and psychiatrists have not been helpful, and I'm unsure of what steps to take. I don't necessarily want to focus on discussing the abuse, but rather on becoming emotionally and mentally healthy. I'm tired of letting the effects of the abuse control my life, and I'm eager to find a solution.

Patient's statement (rewritten): I am a 28-year-old gay man from Spain. Before coming out, I used a dating app in secret. During that time, I made a mistake that I deeply regret now. I came from a loving and supportive family, but what I did would definitely shock them. I met a 70-year-old man who offered me a large sum of money to meet him. Despite initially declining, I eventually agreed and we met multiple times over a period of three months. While we never engaged in sexual intercourse, I did allow him to engage in other acts with me.

Lately, I've been fixated on my mental health. I'm currently in Secondary School with Asperger's and considering pursuing A Levels and studying psychology and mental health in university. However, I can't seem to stop obsessing over my own mental health. One of my main issues is this constant urge and desire to have a serious mental health disorder. It's like I want to experience disorders ranging from schizophrenia to dissociative identity disorder. I know it sounds terrible, but I can't seem to get my mind off of it. I overanalyze every little thing that happens in my day, searching for any sign or symptom of a disorder. I've researched different disorders out of curiosity, so I don't think I'm a hypochondriac. I'm currently seeing someone for possible anxiety disorder, and I believe I'm showing early signs of a dissociative disorder and some form of psychosis. But I also worry about not being diagnosed with a disorder. I often imagine myself in a mental hospital in the future or developing alternate personalities. It's fascinating to me, and I even had a dream recently where I lived with dissociative identity disorder, although I can't recall all the details. I've also been more on edge than usual, constantly flinching and questioning if noises are real. I've been experiencing depersonalization for a few years now, which has started to blend with derealization and keeps me on edge. One thing that might help is hearing the thoughts and experiences of someone who actually has the disorders I'm paranoid about. I would appreciate your opinion to help calm these obsessive thoughts.

I met this friend on the first day of college freshman year (we are soon to be juniors) and it has become increasingly apparent that something is not right. My other friends actually sat me down to tell me they thought she was genuinely in love with me, but I thought they were just being dramatic. She has always been a little nuts (yelling at guys she doesn’t like, getting belligerently drunk, etc). I thought she was just a lot of fun and I didn’t mind be friends with someone a little out there. Everything changed when 4 of my best friends (including her, who was my best friend at the time) got an apartment together. It’s too hard to explain so let me just list things that have happened and are happening: – she screamed at guests we had over for being too loud and insulted them when she could have just asked for quiet (by the way she is the loudest person I know) – Recently, we had to take her to the emergency room when I got a call from my friend saying she was unresponsive and needed to go to the ER. When I showed up she started yelling to everyone to fuck off and to only let me near her when I wasn’t even the one at the time helping her – We went out one night and she got so angry at me for not wanting to go to the same club as her that she yelled at me in public – Every time I go out with her she drinks so much that I have to follow around and take care of her ALL night – she tells every person she meets that I am her best friend and that we are attached at the hip – She spent over 1k on me both my birthdays even though anyone who knows me knows I would NEVER want that – she constantly talks about how we will be each others bridesmaids – she follows me around for entire days and nags me constantly to hang out with her – she gets very jealous and angry when I have other friends. She has straight up bullied my new roommate since she moved in She has had an extremely hard life and I feel so guilty but I can’t do it anymore, help?

As a child, I experienced severe physical and emotional abuse from my mother on a daily basis. I endured beatings with various objects and constant verbal insults that made me feel worthless. Additionally, I was sexually abused by a family friend, a secret I have kept hidden until now. During my teenage years, I experienced panic attacks, which eventually subsided on their own. Currently, at 38 years old, I feel like a failure. I am homeless, unemployed, and struggling with depression. I have had opportunities to improve my situation but somehow find myself gravitating towards destructive circumstances. It almost feels like I am addicted to sadness, poverty, and allowing others to mistreat me. I struggle to express my thoughts and needs because I fear inconveniencing others. Is it possible that I have developed an addiction to failure?

Lately, I've been feeling really confused and scared. I don't know if the things I'm experiencing are real or if I'm just making them up in my head. It's been really overwhelming trying to figure myself out.

I've been experiencing distressing memories and flashbacks from my childhood. When I was around 7 years old, I had a traumatic experience where a boy who was four years older than me touched me inappropriately during a sleepover. I remember waking up to his actions and feeling scared and confused, but I didn't know what to do or say at the time.

As a teenager in Germany, I've become increasingly aware of my weight issue. While my peers are gaining muscle and bone mass, I seem unable to gain any weight at all. Over the years, it has become more noticeable that I am underweight. My body has become extremely thin, with a thigh gap, visible ribs, and arms that resemble twigs.

I have been diagnosed with Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD) and experience intrusive thoughts related to my condition. However, I have also been struggling with a persistent fear of someone being in my house and intending to harm me. This fear is constant, and I find myself constantly checking closets and around corners. It feels like I am always on edge, fearing that a random person could be in my house and that my life is in danger. I am unsure if this fear is related to my OCD or if it is something separate. Thank you for taking the time to read my message and for offering your assistance.

My brother was diagnosed with severe depression a few months ago. He has been taking medication and it seems to be helping him. However, he refuses to see a therapist, even though I believe it would greatly benefit him. I recently signed up for Mental Health First Aid Training to better support him. Do you think it would be a good idea to invite my brother to attend this training with me? I'm hoping that by learning how to help others, he may also help himself. But I'm worried that he might feel pressured or uncomfortable, which could potentially worsen his depression.

Since 7th grade, I have been experiencing extreme irritability towards certain sounds, particularly those made by other people such as breathing loudly, clearing their throat, or tapping pens. Lately, it has gotten worse and has started triggering panic attacks. I find myself having to leave the classroom multiple times and I am unable to make eye contact with anyone. It's impacting my ability to focus in class as my heart races and I struggle to breathe. I often end up crying in the bathroom and missing a lot of class.

I've noticed a pattern of behavior that has been going on since I was around 12 years old. Sometimes, when I'm in class, I find myself pretending to be a fictional character and having conversations with made-up characters in my head. Although I don't speak out loud, it can be distracting and interrupts my ability to focus on my schoolwork.
