However, I struggle to accept that I was born this way, especially because it is not linked to traditional notions of sex. Sexual encounters and explicit scenes do not arouse me at all. I have even started to wonder if I experienced sexual assault or abuse as a child, although my parents were loving and normal. On top of this, I have experienced depression since childhood, engaged in self-harming behaviors unrelated to masochism, and have been reckless with my own safety. In fifth grade, I even attempted suicide by ingesting pills for what now seems like a trivial reason. Recently, I have been trying to recall my childhood memories. We had a nanny when I was around 6 or 7, and I remember despising her to the point where I once threatened to harm myself with a knife if she didn't stop bothering me. However, I cannot recall specific details about what she did, and I find it odd that I can remember other people and events from an earlier stage in my life. Additionally, I experienced bullying from my peers as a child, although it was not physical in nature. I know it may sound foolish, but I am desperate for an explanation. Can you help me understand these experiences better?

Patient's statement (rewritten): I have been seeing a therapist for the past three years and he has been incredibly helpful. However, I am struggling to discuss my concerns about sex with him. Due to past childhood abuse, I have carried feelings of guilt and shame for over three decades. Now, I feel ready to pursue an intimate relationship, but my lack of confidence and experience is causing me anxiety. I want to address these fears and anxieties by discussing the details of my abuse with my therapist, but I don't know how to initiate that conversation. The thought of talking about sex with him has been so embarrassing that I have even had sessions where I couldn't speak at all. How should I approach this?

I've been experiencing intense and disturbing dreams that feel very real. They often involve multiple personalities and I feel like I am not alone. These personalities communicate with me through my dreams. I've also been engaging in self-harm rituals and smearing blood on myself. I spend a lot of time in the dark, twitching, and although I don't hear voices, I feel their presence within me. I feel disconnected from others and don't know what's wrong with me. I'm terrified that I'm going insane and I cry after hurting myself. The impact of these dreams affects my mental state throughout the day and I constantly feel panicked. It doesn't seem like a typical nightmare disorder. Despite the harm they cause, I have a strange attachment to these dreams and I can't let go of my past. Please help me understand what's happening to me.

I've been in a relationship since the second semester of 9th grade, and now it's been 5 years. But things have changed and it's not the same anymore. I've been wanting to break up for the past 2 years, but every time I try, she tells me that she can't handle it and that everyone else in her life is leaving her, and I'm the only one she has left.

I feel like my life is stuck in a never-ending cycle, where I keep going in circles with no way out. I've decided to try and make the best of it by focusing on becoming perfect within this limited scope.

I come from a very dysfunctional family. There is a history of alcoholism, sexual deviancy, and abuse on both sides of my parents' lineage. I'm concerned about how it has affected me and my mental well-being.

Over the past year, I've been experiencing distressing thoughts that originate from within me. Lately, these thoughts have become increasingly violent, resulting in me hitting myself or involuntarily jerking my head and screaming "no" when the voice bothers me. Sometimes, the voice compels me to do things or else it threatens that something bad will happen. These thoughts cause me immense anxiety, but I haven't sought professional help before. My brother is already in therapy due to our shared traumatic experiences, but my parents dismiss my struggles as mere imitation. I don't want to self-diagnose, but I also don't want to appear selfish if I ask for help. What are these voices and what steps should I take?

I've been feeling really down lately. It seems like my mood swings from feeling sad and hopeless to feeling numb and empty. I've lost interest in things I used to enjoy and I'm having trouble sleeping and eating. I just don't know what to do anymore.

I've been in an on-and-off relationship with a man for almost 6 years. Recently, he admitted that he sees potential in me, but he can't envision a future together. He's honest and kind, but he struggles with intimacy and avoids discussing his feelings. Our relationship has been unconventional - more like friends with benefits mixed with deep conversations. Whenever we end things, he disappears and then comes back. He's able to pursue other casual relationships and introduce those women to his friends and family, but he won't do the same with me. My counselor believes that he's afraid of the depth of our connection and what it could mean if we were to date. Do you think that's accurate? I don't know anyone else who has gone through something like this. I've tried to move on, but I still long for our connection. I don't understand why he won't fully commit to me. Am I not important enough to him?

My daughter has been in a tumultuous marriage for the past decade. Both her and her husband engage in verbal and emotional abuse towards each other, leaving us feeling helpless to intervene. Lately, she has been displaying extreme volatility and anger towards not only her spouse but also towards me and other family members. This level of behavior is unusual for our close-knit family. It seems like she is reflecting on her life and placing blame on everyone else. I am deeply concerned for her well-being as her anger and attacks are escalating, causing her to shut us all out. She is saying hurtful and hateful things through text messages, expressing that she wants nothing to do with any of us. It seems like she has developed a victim mentality, feeling alienated and abused by everyone around her. I am devastated by this situation, and I want to find a way to help her.

My boyfriend and I have been together for almost 4 years and have been living together for a little over 3 years. About a year ago, while we were on vacation, my boyfriend's friend stayed over at our house. I had never met this friend before, but I trusted my boyfriend's judgment. However, I later discovered that his friend had brought over a female coworker without informing us. I found an eyeliner that belonged to the coworker, and it upset me. I asked my boyfriend to talk to his friend about the situation, as I didn't want to confront him directly.

Over the past 3 months, my husband has been engaging in excessive partying and coming home drunk at 4 am on multiple occasions. I have expressed my concerns to him and asked him to stop, but he continues to disregard my feelings. The last time he went out, he didn't even inform me about his whereabouts or who he was with. I called him multiple times, but he only responded via text at 4:11 am, claiming he didn't see my calls. He eventually came home at 4:45 am, intoxicated.

Over the past year, I have noticed that I have been partying more than usual. Although I don't drink every day or use alcohol to cope with my anxiety (which I have a history of), I do tend to drink on either Fridays or Saturdays (never both). However, I have been drinking more than is healthy overall. In fact, there have been very few weekends in the last 6 months where I have remained sober throughout. Additionally, I have noticed that my hangovers are quite severe. Interestingly, I have also observed that the day after a hangover, my anxiety tends to worsen and can last for up to a week.

I recently got married to someone from India. I have been experiencing difficulty in my relationship because my husband often misleads me and leaves me feeling confused. He hurts me emotionally by doing this.

I have been struggling with OCD, an eating disorder, depression, and anxiety. My best friend, who also has depression and anxiety, suddenly stopped talking to me two weeks ago. I apologized repeatedly, thinking I had done something wrong. However, she clarified that I hadn't done anything, but she didn't like my personality and felt uncomfortable around me.

Recently, my daughter moved into my home and shortly after, I started experiencing problems in my relationship with my boyfriend. I suspected that he was cheating on me and then he contracted an STD, which thankfully I did not get as we were not intimate during that time. He constantly rejects me and I feel hurt. One morning, I left my phone recording while I took my other kids to school. To my surprise, I heard him engaging in intimate activities with a girl and he even mentioned her name as I walked in. She was the only one present. I confronted both of them, but they deny any wrongdoing. Now, I find it difficult to trust them alone.

I am an 18-year-old teenager from Turkey. I come from a Turkish family that is not very open-minded. I have been in a relationship with my non-Muslim boyfriend for over a year now. He lives in Europe, while I live in Turkey. The problem I am facing is that my parents do not accept our relationship and do not want me to be with him. However, I believe that it is my life and that our relationship can work, regardless of their support. They have even refused to let me go to Istanbul with him for New Year's, using harsh words that make me feel like I am doing something terribly wrong. I love my parents, but I also love my boyfriend. Can you please help me figure out what to do?

As a young man in Nepal, I find that my mind is constantly active. It seems to be constantly processing subtle noises around me or replaying memories and sounds on a loop. This can be overwhelming at times, and it causes me to feel irritated with my family members, even though I truly love and admire them. Can you help me understand why I experience this and how to manage it better?

Last year, right before Christmas, I felt the need to have a one-on-one conversation with my mother to share some important news about a 21-year-old grandchild she didn't know about. However, I had a strong sense that my request would be ignored or dismissed by her. So, I reached out to her closest friend of 40 years and shared the situation, asking if she could talk to my mom and help arrange a meeting between us in the coming month.

I recently met someone special in August, a girl from the USA, and we quickly developed strong feelings for each other. However, since we started communicating through Skype, I've noticed that I am having difficulty expressing myself verbally. It's been three months now, and I'm still struggling to find my voice, which is causing frustration for both of us.

I'm currently at my grandparent's house in Alabama because my grandfather recently passed away. I decided to reach out because I'm struggling with how I'm handling this situation. This year has been quite overwhelming for me, and it feels like everything started to unravel when I turned 20. I've been through a series of events that have had a lasting impact on me, and I haven't had the chance to gain a different perspective. I believe my unhealthy obsession with J.D. Salinger's The Catcher in the Rye during this time has had a negative effect on me, despite my initial love for the book.

I have been in a relationship for the past 8 months and overall, I've been happy. However, I've been struggling with my boyfriend's reaction to my past relationships. I mentioned them briefly in the beginning, but he seems to be haunted by the fact that I've been with others before him. He's been experiencing severe retroactive jealousy and finds it difficult to accept me as I am. We both love each other and have tried to break up, but we can't seem to let go. How can we overcome this?

I have been struggling with ongoing conflicts with my mom. It seems like we are constantly at odds, with her criticizing and belittling me and my choices. She also makes hurtful remarks about my husband. Whenever I try to address the issue, it just escalates into yelling and she accuses me of being disrespectful.

I have been in a relationship for over a year, and I am starting to feel overwhelmed and unhappy. One of the main issues is my partner's inconsistent discipline with his child. He can be both too harsh and too lenient, which I find concerning. When I express my disagreement through facial expressions, he becomes defensive and expects me to agree with him. There is also a jealousy issue where my partner constantly compares the gifts he gives to his child with the gifts I give. We have had major arguments, and his go-to response is that he is the parent and I should stay in my lane. I feel emotionally alienated and resentful, and it seems like my partner is afraid of his ex-partner using their child as leverage. I'm not sure how to handle this situation.

It sounds like you and your husband had a friendly relationship with your neighbors, including a woman who has a traumatic brain injury. For a while, she seemed calm around you, but you were aware that she would scream and berate her husband on a daily basis. However, one day she directed that same volatile behavior towards you because she didn't like that you were doing your MBA homework. As a result, you decided not to return to that environment. How has this experience been affecting you?

Lately, I've been struggling with managing my patience and emotions when it comes to waiting for replies to my text messages and emails. A few months ago, I reached out to a friend to discuss my self-esteem issues and asked for her opinion on my positive qualities, but she didn't respond. Another instance was when I wished a former crush a happy birthday and tried to reconnect, but again, there was no response. These situations have been triggering intrusive thoughts and increasing my anxiety. I find myself feeling like a burden and questioning my interactions with others, especially with friends of the opposite gender.

I've been experiencing a lot of anxiety lately and it's starting to affect my daily life. I constantly overthink things and it's causing me to become really on edge and lose focus. I've even started shaking from the anxiety and I've snapped at people unintentionally. Sometimes it gets so bad that I have panic attacks and end up missing out on important events. My friends have suggested therapy, but I'm not sure if my issues are really that serious. I don't want to waste anyone's time or money if I can just handle it on my own.

As a child, I experienced a disability which had a significant impact on my life. During that time, I found comfort in wearing cloth diapers. Even as an adult, I still find solace and pleasure in wearing a double cloth diaper and plastic pants at night or when I am alone at home. However, I am facing a dilemma now because I don't know how to address this with the people closest to me if they were to discover my secret. I have been asked questions about the baby powder scent in my room, and I feel the need to be honest next time, but I don't know what to say. Additionally, I struggle with washing the diapers as it feels like I am hiding and being dishonest. Despite these conflicting emotions, this particular comfort brings me joy and I'm unsure of what steps to take.

Over the summer, I had a really intense argument with my mother that escalated into hours of yelling and crying. It felt really overwhelming and I couldn't handle it anymore, so I ended up hurting myself in the bathroom, which is something I've been doing for months now.

I'm a woman from the Philippines and I'm facing a difficult situation with my parents and my boyfriend. They strongly disapprove of my relationship with him for a few reasons. Firstly, they are upset about his past relationships, where he has been involved with multiple girls and even lived with two of them. This makes my parents uncomfortable and they have expressed their strong dislike for him. Secondly, my boyfriend comes from a broken family, with his father having cheated on his mother. My parents believe that this means he is likely to follow in his father's footsteps. Lastly, there is a difference in our professional backgrounds, as I am a professional and my boyfriend is not.

My stepson is 17 years old and I have been in his life since he was 6. Throughout the years, he has consistently lied and exhibited spiteful behavior. His academic performance has also been a concern, with frequent trouble at school and barely passing each year. Currently, he is attending school online with only a few in-person days, but his grades have plummeted to all F's. His mother has struggled with addressing his behavior, but I have been more proactive. Despite this, his lying has persisted and he has become more skilled at being convincing.

I have been dealing with anxiety for as long as I can remember. My childhood was difficult, as I experienced sexual and mental abuse. Despite these challenges, I have managed to cope well for the most part. However, about 5 years ago, I started experiencing severe body aches, chronic fatigue, and other symptoms. This coincided with starting a high-stress job. I have since been diagnosed with Fibromyalgia, Chronic Fatigue Syndrome, a paralyzed vocal cord, 100% loss of smell, Anxiety, Depression, and ADHD (diagnosed in my early 30s).

Hi, I'm here to talk about what I've been going through. I was diagnosed with Major Depressive Disorder and OCD during my recent hospitalization. I've been hospitalized twice in the past due to suicidal thoughts and depression. One year and five months ago, when I was 12, I lost my dad to a stroke and long-term sickness from diabetes and kidney failure. It was a very difficult time for me, and I experienced deep grief and intrusive thoughts. People would bully me and make hurtful comments about my dad. I attempted suicide three times during that period. Right now, I'm feeling incredibly hopeless and pessimistic. I don't believe things will get better, and I feel like the evil in the world outweighs any good. I'm just going through the motions of fulfilling obligations to my peers and teachers. I don't enjoy going to high school, even though I'm just a freshman. I have goals of becoming an animator and starting a family in the U.K., but I'm not sure if those are truly what I want. I have a fear of having different goals because I worry it will lead to depression. Currently, I feel numb, and I've been self-harming as a way to feel something. When I was suicidal, at least I felt pain and worthlessness, which felt better than this numbness. I also miss being depressed because it felt like my safety blanket and part of my identity. Occasionally, I get extremely angry and have thoughts of doing something terrible to myself, but it has only happened once. I've been on medication, but I want to get off it because I don't want to rely on drugs to be happy. Can you give me any advice?

My son was always considered bright in high school and was a source of help to his friends in various subjects. However, since starting at an elite school, he has been struggling with his academics. He often avoids hard work, repeats courses, and has even been on academic probation. He seems to escape into video games and binge-watching TV shows. We don't suspect substance abuse, but he lies about his coursework and struggles to build strong relationships. How can we help him? Is there a mental health issue? We are unsure if he's been seeing a counselor.

My 7-year-old daughter has a habit of constantly moving her fingers. She does it while eating, watching TV, and even at school. She has mentioned to me that she can't stop doing it, but insists that it doesn't bother her. However, I am concerned that there may be an underlying issue that she is not aware of. When she moves her fingers, it seems like she is counting, as she follows a specific sequence - touching her pinky with her ring finger, then her ring finger with her middle finger, and so on. Sometimes she even does it backwards. I would appreciate any insights or advice you may have. Thank you.

When I was 11 years old, my parents got separated. It was a difficult time for me because I felt a lot of pressure from everyone, except my dad, to fix the situation. I was told that my close relationship with my dad meant he would listen to me. However, I struggled to come to terms with the separation and didn't handle it well. While I was in boarding school, I spent most of my time crying and even engaged in self-harm by cutting. I didn't know who to talk to about what I was going through, so I've kept my feelings to myself until now.

I remember browsing a psychology website out of curiosity, looking at the characteristics of narcissism. I didn't think much about it until I started relating to the symptoms I was reading about. It made me wonder if I might be a narcissist myself.

My girlfriend and I have been in a relationship for 5 months. She has been a member of a Baptist church for the past 5 years. However, she is also bisexual, which she believes is a sin. Another issue is her past and the insecurities she carries from previous experiences with infidelity in same-sex relationships. She has turned to religion as a way to find healing, growth, and become a better person. While she believes Jesus has been her savior, she also acknowledges the role that supportive people in the church have played in her recovery. She has chosen to abstain from sex until marriage due to her religious beliefs, but I suspect her insecurities may also be a factor. It's challenging for both of us because we love each other and I'm willing to wait, but I'm unsure how to navigate these complexities.

Counselor: It's clear that you are reflecting on the influence of upbringing, past experiences, and past ideologies on a person's current reasoning. It's important to recognize that our upbringing and past experiences can shape our beliefs and perspectives to some extent. However, as individuals, we also have the capacity for growth, change, and the ability to challenge our beliefs.

My loved one and her boyfriend have been in a tumultuous relationship since high school, and they recently became parents to a baby girl. However, their relationship is filled with instability and threats of suicide whenever he tries to leave. It's important to note that my loved one has a history of childhood trauma and comes from a family with a background of mental health issues. She struggles with commitment, used to have a sleep disorder, and tends to hold grudges. On the other hand, her boyfriend is younger and feels restricted in the relationship due to his own health issues and a dysfunctional family. He has expressed his desire to leave and even tries to reach out to others, but my loved one refuses to let him go. It seems like they are both in a difficult situation and searching for a new place to live. I'm concerned about how to approach this without risking their privacy or making the situation worse.

These past few days have been incredibly difficult for me. My son's mother and I were together for about three years. I've always struggled with expressing my emotions in a sensitive way, but recently I told her that I didn't want to be with her anymore. At the time, I believed it to be true, but now that she's moved on and found someone new just two weeks later, I'm feeling hurt and confused.

I'm feeling really overwhelmed and frustrated with my boyfriend's behavior lately. When we first met, we used to have these amazing 6-8 hour conversations where we really clicked and connected like never before.

It sounds like you're going through a lot right now. It's important to recognize that your past experiences, such as the trauma of being molested, can impact your ability to trust others. It's understandable that these experiences have contributed to your feelings of insecurity and suspicion in your relationship. It's also clear that you are struggling with low self-esteem and negative body image, which can further contribute to your anxiety and difficulty in social situations.

I recently started dating someone I met on a dating app and things were going well. However, he recently confessed that he is a recovering alcoholic and has been struggling to stay sober for the past 10 years. He also admitted that he lied about the length of his sobriety when we first met.

Patient's Statement: I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for 3 years now. We initially met online and after a year, we finally met in person. Although we've had our fair share of issues, we've always managed to work through them. However, I've noticed that ever since we met, I'm always the one going to his house and he has never made the effort to come to mine. We've made plans for him to visit, but there's always some reason preventing him from doing so. I'm unsure if these reasons are legitimate or if he simply doesn't want to make the effort. Recently, my parents invited him to spend New Year's Eve with us, and when I asked him, he seemed enthusiastic and said he would ask his mom. However, it's been two weeks and he hasn't mentioned anything about it, which makes me think he doesn't want to come. I'm feeling confused and unsure about what to do. I love him a lot, but I'm unsure of what this means for our relationship.

As an 18-year-old professional/competitive athlete in Russia, I have been feeling increasingly empty over the past few months. Although I am skilled at communicating and do not experience anxiety, I find solace in the intense feelings I have after training. The only other thing that brings me any sense of fulfillment are dogs, but unfortunately, I cannot own one due to European regulations. I apologize for reaching out on an American forum, but I don't know where else to turn for support.

My boyfriend has been struggling with hypochondria for quite some time now. Before we got together, he was dealing with severe delusions and firmly believed that he had nonexistent medical issues. While he has improved since then, he occasionally projects his delusions onto me, accusing me of having an eating disorder and other issues. He refuses to seek professional help or counseling due to fear of humiliation, and he is also resistant to taking medication. I'm not sure how to support him through this.

I've been experiencing a disturbing pattern of thoughts that I find hard to put into words. It's like there's a constant undercurrent of violent thoughts in my mind, even when I'm engaged in everyday activities like talking, eating, or relaxing. It's really distressing to have these thoughts about harming the people around me.

As a teenager in the U.S., I have had a difficult upbringing. I was adopted from a family with a history of drug abuse, and my adoptive family has struggled with alcoholism. I have always felt criticized and put down by my parents, which has made it difficult for me to love them. I recently lost my grandmother, but I didn't feel much sadness. I have also noticed that I have hurt my parents emotionally and physically, mirroring the pain they have caused me. My father's recent hospitalization didn't elicit much of an emotional response from me either. In my romantic relationship of 3 years, I love my boyfriend, but he has expressed that he doesn't feel loved by me. He says I rarely compliment him and I struggle to show affection. Additionally, since starting birth control, I have lost my sexual feelings towards him, although I used to enjoy being intimate with him. I want to keep our relationship, but I am not sure how to improve things.

I recently realized that since I was around 8 years old, I have engaged in behaviors that harm my body on a micro level. These behaviors include biting my lips, biting/clipping off my cuticles, flossing too hard to make my gums bleed, and picking at my scalp to create scabs. I am curious as to why I am doing this. Could it be a nervous release? It may be relevant to note that my parents got divorced when I was 8 years old.

I've been feeling really down lately and I don't see a happy future for myself. There are several reasons contributing to this. Firstly, I don't find any joy in my current job. Additionally, since I stopped drinking and using drugs, I've lost most of my friends. I constantly worry about things that don't really matter and I can't seem to let go of the heartbreak from a past relationship over ten years ago. On top of that, my beloved brother lives far away and it's difficult to see him often. I'm also struggling with finding a decent partner and starting a family. I've lost my motivation to engage in conversations or pursue my hobbies. I'm genuinely concerned that I'll end up alone without a family. Despite having a good life on the surface, with loving parents and basic necessities, I can't shake this feeling of hopelessness for the future. I try to stay positive, but I often wake up feeling low and unmotivated. I've become very quiet at work because I simply lack the energy to socialize. People might misunderstand my behavior and think I'm aloof, when in reality, I just lack the drive to engage with others like I used to. I feel much older than my actual age of 27. Can you please help me make sense of all this?

My adult son, who is 23 years old, has been struggling with depression for a number of years. Despite our efforts to support him, he seems to be stuck and unable to move forward in his life. My husband and I recently completed a 12-week NAMI class, which has shed some light on his symptoms, and we suspect that he may be dealing with bipolar II disorder. However, he vehemently refuses to seek help from psychologists or psychiatrists, believing that they cannot offer any assistance. He is also consumed by political events, constantly checking his phone for updates, and identifies as a nihilist. He feels that moving forward has no purpose. He currently lives with us, his parents, and is struggling with a lack of friends, boredom, excessive sleeping, and unemployment. He plans to enroll in classes in January, but this will be his third attempt, as he has become too depressed to complete his previous attempts despite having good grades. He believes that pursuing education is his only hope. I feel hopeless and unsure of how to help him, as he engages in self-sabotaging behaviors and is too depressed to help himself. Are there any online counseling options available? The challenge is that he is highly intelligent and has been able to manipulate previous counselors into thinking that he is fine when he is not. Any suggestions would be greatly appreciated. Thank you.

My son is 15 years old and a freshman in high school. He has been involved in wrestling since he was 5 years old and has excelled at the national level. However, he recently expressed a desire to not participate in wrestling during high school and instead pursue boxing. My husband and his coach believe that he should continue wrestling due to his talent. I am torn on whether or not to force him to wrestle at least for one year. Additionally, he doesn't have a ride home from practice unless I pick him up, but my husband suggests having his older brother bring him home. I feel conflicted and unsure about what to do. Is it appropriate for me to insist that he continues wrestling for one more year?

Lately, I've been feeling really unsettled by my friend's love for horror movies. It's not that I'm scared or grossed out by them, but the fact that she can enjoy watching people die in such horrific ways really bothers me. It has gotten to the point where I've stopped watching any movies or shows, playing games, or engaging in anything that involves violence or death. It's affecting my ability to enjoy things I used to love.

"Hello. I’ve known about this site for awhile but it wasn’t until now that I’ve finally decided to ask a question. Basically, like the title suggests, I’m afraid my depression is a personality and that there’s no hope for recovery. I’ll do a rundown because I didn’t just come up with this randomly. I was diagnosed with depression when I was 6 and honestly I don’t think I’ve ever been okay."

I've been in 5 relationships and I'm currently in one. We've only been dating for about a month, but I've gotten really depressed. I've stopped enjoying things I used to like, and I have no motivation to get up in the morning. I've gone from feeling happy with this guy to dreading the mention of his name. I don't want to see him anymore, and every time he talks to me or texts me, I feel nauseous. I don't understand why I've developed this sudden hatred towards him when just a few weeks ago, I couldn't stop talking about him. This has happened before in my past relationships too. I become obsessed with these guys, and then suddenly, I become depressed and develop a strong dislike towards them. But once I break up with them, it's like nothing ever happened, and I instantly feel refreshed and back to normal.

I've been best friends with David for three years now, and he has been diagnosed with anxiety and depression. Our friendship started after he ended his friendship with Alex, who was a terrible friend to him. Alex would ignore David, lie to him, say mean things, and even sabotage other relationships to get closer to him. I think these experiences have really traumatized David, as he constantly puts himself down for every little thing he does. It's also affecting our relationship because he puts me on a pedestal and I can't be comfortable with that. I know it's important to compromise in a healthy relationship, but it feels like I'm always the one in the right. I'm feeling overwhelmed and not sure what to do because I don't want to say anything that will make him feel worse about himself. Whenever I bring up an issue, he shuts down and can't respond. I feel like I'm causing him to have a mental breakdown, which he has had before. He does have a therapist, whom he has been seeing for two years. I apologize if my thoughts are scattered, that's just how I feel right now. Thank you for listening.

Patient: I'm a 16-year-old who has been struggling with maintaining interest in girls I'm involved with. Over the past three years, I've had numerous girlfriends and have been talking to even more. The problem is that after a few weeks, I start losing interest in the girl. Even though they have great qualities and I feel attached to them, I can't help but be drawn to other girls. Additionally, I've noticed that once things become sexual, my interest diminishes once we're no longer together. This has been bothering me for about 7-8 months now, and I'm starting to feel emotionally and psychologically drained. Currently, I have a girlfriend who is amazing, but I'm experiencing this same pattern of wanting to leave her. I want to have a serious relationship, but I'm unsure of what to do. Thank you for listening.

I have been friends with this person for a long time and I have noticed a significant decline in her mental health over the past few years. Last year, she was hospitalized for severe depression and anxiety. Although she was prescribed medication, she had to stop taking it due to financial constraints. I feel that her condition has worsened since then. She recently returned to school but is facing extreme anxiety. She has developed negative thoughts about her appearance and body, which has led to her avoiding social events. I believe that her home environment exacerbates her condition, as she spends a lot of time in her room and her father is not affectionate. Additionally, there may have been instances of abuse in her past. Unfortunately, her family cannot afford any form of treatment for her. I try to support her as much as I can, but I am concerned about her worsening condition. She has tremendous potential and intelligence, and I want to find ways to help her. What can I do to support her?

I recently ended a relationship with someone who I now realize was a covert narcissist. I expected them to discard me after the idealization and devaluation phases, but that didn't happen. Instead, I had to be the one to distance myself from them.

I am a 15-year-old male who has been diagnosed with OCD. My psychiatrist initially thought it was related to intrusive thoughts about harming children, but I believe there's more to it. I feel guilty because when I masturbate, I often think about little kids and look at cartoons online. Recently, I've noticed that I find girls between 9 and 12 years old attractive, although I am mostly attracted to guys my age. Am I a pedophile?

I'm a 20-year-old man from Sri Lanka. Since my childhood, I have always been very shy and have struggled to make friends. Lately, I have been experiencing a lot of anger and violent thoughts that I can't seem to control. It's really distressing because I feel like I'm losing my mind. When I was 13, I started having troubling thoughts about God and religion, and at 15, I had my first violent thought. Now, all I can think about are these harmful thoughts.

Patient: I am wondering what stage of breakup I am in. The breakup occurred three weeks ago after being in a five-year relationship. At first, I was devastated and desperately wanted my ex-boyfriend to reach out and express regret. But lately, I find myself starting to accept the reality that he is gone. However, I'm not sure if I'm still in denial and have yet to go through the other stages of grief.

I have been struggling with self-harm for a while now. Whenever I cut my skin, I feel a strange sense of relief, even though the sight of blood makes me feel sick and I sometimes faint. I can't seem to understand why I am so addicted to this behavior. I have sought help from psychologists before, but it hasn't been effective in stopping this. Can you offer any guidance on why this is happening and what steps I can take to prevent it?

When I was 16, I started smoking weed heavily every day for about a year and a half. I turned to smoking as a way to cope with a difficult breakup. The girl I deeply loved at that time left me for someone else. However, I had to stop after having a bad trip on acid. During the trip, I experienced intense anxiety and constant fears of developing schizophrenia, which lasted for 12 hours. This happened about 7 months ago. Since then, I've had to quit weed because it triggers panic attacks. I've had a total of 3 panic attacks since then - one while on weed, one that I think was caused by nicotine, and the last one occurred when I was sober.

Hello. Last year, my fiance's mother passed away from cancer, and as a result, we decided to take in his 8-year-old brother into foster care. Initially, everything was going well, but we've been facing some challenges with his behavior. He has been lying a lot, and when we confronted him about it, he said he does it to avoid getting into trouble. We've tried explaining to him that lying will lead to bigger consequences, but he continues to do it. Recently, he has also been using foul language and swearing at older kids in school. When I asked him about it, he lied about the words he used and who he directed them towards.

I have been experiencing a lot of emotional distress lately due to the way my mom treats me when she's angry. She often mocks my appearance, making hurtful comments about my acne and weight. It feels unfair because whenever I make a mistake, she forces me to apologize to her and my dad, even for minor things. My two sisters, on the other hand, seem to get away with their misbehavior without facing the same consequences. I always find myself apologizing, while they don't have to.

I have been dealing with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) and anxiety for the past 6 months. It has been a challenging time for me, and despite my efforts to engage in coping strategies, I still struggle on a daily basis. Recently, I experienced a fear of going insane and losing control. I had watched a movie about involuntary time travel, and for a couple of days, I was consumed by the irrational thought of it happening to me. Looking back, I now realize how unrealistic and laughable that fear was. However, I am concerned about the fact that I even entertained such a ridiculous idea, as it triggered anxiety and made me question my sanity. I read online that people who are "crazy" have difficulty distinguishing reality from fiction, which added to my fear. Am I losing my mind? I'm really scared. Thank you for your response.

I've been feeling really overwhelmed and disconnected lately. I've been isolating myself, skipping school, and avoiding my friends. It's like I want to disappear and not deal with anything anymore. It's hard for me to put into words exactly how I feel, but it's chaotic and confusing. I tend to bottle up my stress until it becomes too much, and then I start acting irrationally. I've been using recreational drugs occasionally to cope with these feelings, but I don't think I'm dependent on them. My life feels like it's spiraling out of control and I don't know what to do.

Hi, Doctor. I've been feeling really down lately and it feels like my depression is getting worse. I can't seem to shake off the negative thoughts that keep popping up in my mind. It's hard for me to focus on my work because all I can think about is what might go wrong or what if I can't achieve anything in life. It's a constant struggle to live a normal and happy life. I'm 24 years old and I feel like I have no direction or purpose. Whenever I try to take a step towards my career or anything else, I feel overwhelming fear that I can't explain. This fear consumes me throughout the day. Another big issue for me is that I'm not happy with my physique. I'm very skinny and I just want to change that. Please help me, I don't know what to do. I'm eagerly awaiting your response. Thank you. (From India)

I'm a 16-year-old boy in my second-to-last year of school. I've always struggled with time management, but it hasn't affected my grades because I'm naturally gifted. However, things have started to change this year. My grades are dropping because I haven't been putting in the effort. I think playing games may be contributing to this issue.

I'm really struggling right now. I used to see a therapist during difficult times, but my therapist retired a few years ago. I'm experiencing a lot of grief, isolation, and anxiety and depression. I feel like I can't handle it on my own anymore, but I can't afford to see a therapist. I feel so alone, even when I reach out to people for support, they don't seem to understand the importance of it in my life.

I have been struggling with a secret that has been weighing heavily on me. Since I was around 8 years old, I have had a deep fascination with women's lingerie and panties. It started when I would look at JC Penney's catalog and be drawn to the lingerie section, wondering what it would feel like to wear those garments. Over the years, I have occasionally tried on my mom's panties and sometimes even my sister's. I feel a great deal of shame and guilt about this, and I can't seem to accept or stop this behavior. I'm a 28-year-old married male with a new 8-month-old son, and I really wish this part of my life never existed.

I am a 56 year old female and my partner is 57. We have a friends-with-benefits arrangement, where we engage in a physical relationship without any commitment. However, I've noticed that my partner's behavior changes when we are intimate. He becomes aggressive and does not engage in any foreplay. When I mentioned it, he simply kissed my neck and proceeded without addressing my concerns.

Over the past year, my brother's behavior has become increasingly concerning. It started with him randomly throwing away all of his clothes for no apparent reason. He started coming to my room at night, asking about my day, but then saying things that didn't make sense. For example, he would mention receiving calls that didn't happen. Recently, he has been isolating himself in his room, only eating at night and staying awake until the early hours of the morning.

I have been experiencing difficulties in speaking languages other than my native language. Even though I have knowledge of these languages, I find it hard to communicate with people. Sometimes, I feel a lack of desire to engage in conversation, even though I know it is important for work and school. I feel like everything has changed and I am not the active person I used to be. I had a lot of friends, a good job, and a perfect body, but now I am overweight and struggling to lose weight. My weight seems to fluctuate every day. I am also having trouble focusing on my studies and I have no desire to meet new people. I am afraid to go to the cinema because I am scared of meeting new people due to my language difficulties. I feel very numb and disconnected from my emotions. I often reminisce about my past life and wish I could go back to it. I feel like I don't have enough time to rebuild my life. I am 29 years old and I moved to America two years ago. I had a college degree, a job, and friends, but it all seems to have changed now. I am scared and filled with regret, even though I know I shouldn't be. I have tried to change my way of thinking, but it hasn't been successful.

Patient: Lately, I've been experiencing distressing thoughts and hearing a voice that urges me to harm myself and others. Initially, it was focused on self-harm, but recently it's been directing me towards hurting others as well.

I am 22 years old and have been in a relationship with my partner, who is 38 years old, for nearly 6 years. He has a 16-year-old daughter who has always disliked me and has been trying to undermine our relationship. Lately, her behavior has become even more concerning. She displays a disturbing obsession with her father and engages in inappropriate conversations with him about her sexual experiences. She also attempts to replace me and has crossed boundaries that make me uncomfortable. I am already dealing with various mental health challenges, and I feel overwhelmed by this situation. I'm reaching out for help because I don't know how to handle it.

I've been seeing my school therapist every two weeks. It seems like every time I go, it's after a good week where I feel fine. I end up not having much to say or work towards because I genuinely feel like I'm already doing okay.

I've noticed that my wife has been maintaining friendships with other men, and it's been causing some concerns for me. In the past, she has sent inappropriate texts to men, but she claims to have stopped. However, I've noticed that she still messages or snap-chats other men and becomes defensive and angry when I try to discuss it with her.

Over the past three months, my husband's behavior has drastically changed. He has been lashing out at me almost every night, even over the smallest things. I believe the stressors in his life, such as my health crisis, his medication-induced weight gain, and the emotional rollercoaster of connecting with his biological family, have contributed to his anger. I try to be supportive and ask how I can help, but he either dismisses my offers or gets angry when I don't anticipate his needs. He accuses me of not caring about him and even suggests that I married him for his money. Additionally, he is resentful of my close relationship with my family and insists that I must have been molested as a child and brainwashed. These episodes are happening almost every night, and though he apologizes and acknowledges his mistakes, the cycle continues. He refuses to go to counseling, claiming it hasn't worked for him in the past. He does see a psychiatrist and takes mood stabilizing medication. I'm at a loss for what else I can do to help him and restore our relationship to its previous happiness.

I have been struggling with my mental health for a while now. It all began when I started training seriously in ballet at a young age. I was passionate about ballet and it became a big part of my life. However, my mother put a lot of pressure on me, making it seem like ballet was the only option for me and that I had no other choices. This started to take a toll on my self-esteem, as I constantly felt like I wasn't good enough. Even my teachers reinforced this belief. Eventually, I made the difficult decision to quit ballet, and things started spiraling downhill from there. Around six months ago, I made a mistake that many teenagers make - I went out with friends without telling my parents, and they reacted with extreme verbal abuse, calling me horrible names and making me feel worthless. Since then, I've been subjected to this kind of treatment on a daily basis. It feels like my life has been a series of unfortunate events, and I feel completely alone with no one to talk to about how I'm feeling. I've lost all hope that things will ever get better, and I'm starting to believe the negative things my mother tells me. I spend hours crying every day, struggle to sleep at night, and find solace in junk food. The only thing keeping me going is my focus on school and achieving good grades, because I know that will bring me closer to being able to leave my parents and find my own happiness. However, these past six months have been the lowest point of my life, and I feel like there's no way out except for ending my own life. I've attempted suicide before, but fear has always stopped me. I did see a therapist once, but my parents didn't allow me to continue. I'm desperate for something worth living for, as all of my happiness has been taken away. I don't understand why my parents don't love me like I love them.

As a teenager living in the United States, I've been struggling with disturbing thoughts of death, harming others, and hurting myself on a daily basis. It's overwhelming and I feel like I have no control over these thoughts. Sometimes, I even end up hurting myself without even realizing it until it's already done. I've been diagnosed with ADHD, depression, anxiety, and PTSD. My thoughts are all jumbled up, ranging from wanting to save people to wanting to harm them. I also tend to see everything in cycles. Failing is something I really hate, and when it happens, it sends me into a deep depression, which leads to even more failures.

I've always been perceived as intelligent by others, but I constantly feel stupid and incapable. Despite my love for learning and my ability to obtain any degree, I struggle with applying my knowledge in real-life situations and solving problems. This has led to feelings of depression and a string of failures. I'm even considering a career change. Will this solve my issues or will I always be stuck in a cycle of studying without being able to work effectively? Maybe I'm in the wrong field altogether?

Background: A teenager in the U.S. is seeking advice on how to cope with their mother's fluctuating emotions. The patient is currently in 11th grade and is working towards obtaining their associates degree. The patient's mother is a single parent.

It sounds like you've been carrying a lot of conflicting emotions and beliefs about your father and your upbringing. It can be really difficult when our perceptions and memories start to shift as we grow older. It's important to remember that healing and understanding are a process, and it's okay to question and reevaluate what you've been taught. Would you like to explore these feelings further and discuss how they're impacting you?

Lately, I've been feeling really isolated and unable to connect with others. I struggle to form lasting friendships or have a stable romantic relationship. The only relationships I feel comfortable maintaining are with my family members.

Patient: Lately, my friend has shared with me that they've been experiencing unsettling thoughts about wanting to harm random people they don't know. They mentioned having a strange desire to hurt strangers, as well as having dreams about causing harm. I reassured them that I'm here to support them and that they can stop answering my questions anytime they feel uncomfortable.

I've been feeling really down lately. I've been experiencing a lot of regret and it's affecting my ability to enjoy life. I also struggle with social anxiety and I suspect I may have Asperger's. My low self-esteem is holding me back and I feel like I wasted my 20s. I feel stuck and frustrated, and I don't even know where to begin.

Last night, I ended a relationship with a man for various reasons. We had been friends for 8 years and then started dating for the past 10 months. We initially met while working in Cape Town, where he is from. When I moved back to Scotland, we stayed in touch and decided to give our relationship a try when I returned to Cape Town earlier this year. However, from the beginning, things were difficult and I perceived his behavior as verbally abusive. I've allowed this terrible behavior from him, and I can't help but wonder if his jealous nature is what led to him being cheated on in the past.

I have been experiencing disturbing thoughts and behaviors since I was a child, and they have become worse since I had my daughter. For example, I have intrusive thoughts about eating dirty napkins and I avoid using dishes or going into my own kitchen. I also have distressing sexual thoughts. However, what really bothers me is the repetitive popping sound I make with my lips before falling asleep, which I cannot control. Additionally, I have a history of obsessive-compulsive behaviors such as excessive hand-washing and praying for extended periods of time. I suspect that I may have OCD, and I feel anxious and depressed about things that haven't even happened. At times, I engage in self-harm by excessively clipping the skin around my fingers and toes. I also experience jitteriness and a sense of detachment or impending doom. I want to seek help, but I feel like nobody understands me. These issues were particularly severe when I was younger, but they have resurfaced since I became postpartum. Some of my symptoms are too distressing to even disclose anonymously. I just want to find happiness, but it feels impossible.

Over the past year, I've been experiencing a lack of motivation and interest in things. I constantly feel tired and find it difficult to manage my final years of school. I also get overwhelmed easily. Besides that, I don't really know how I feel. It's like I'm just going through the motions of life without really thinking about it. My mom says this is just who I am, but I'm not so sure.

As a teenager in the UK, I recently had a disturbing realization about something I experienced when I was around 9 years old. I came across a newspaper article describing a sadistic event, and I remember feeling a strange sense of enjoyment while reading it. I knew it was wrong, but it shocked me that I could have felt that way. I forgot about it until someone mentioned the story recently, and it all came rushing back, including the fact that I had enjoyed reading it.

I have been diagnosed with Bipolar Disorder and I am currently taking celexa (Citalopram) as prescribed. Lately, I've been struggling with medication compliance. About a month ago, I started feeling a low mood and stopped taking my medication for about a week. It was a terrible experience - I felt tearful, agitated, exhausted, and even became aggressive. I called in sick for work multiple times. When I resumed taking my medication, I felt a significant improvement. However, recently I've been feeling like I'm entering another depressive episode, and I find myself wanting to stop taking the medication. It's like I miss the familiar feeling of being depressed, as if it was my comforting best friend. I know life is unbearable without the medication, but I crave feeling something, even if it's pain. The medication makes me feel numb. I know it sounds strange, but I'm unsure of what to do. I'm looking for answers as to why I feel this way and if there are other medications that might allow me to experience emotions without spiraling into deep depression.

When I was 18, I experienced a traumatic event that has had a lasting impact on my life. I feel like I'm detached from reality and not fully present in my own life. It's been overwhelming and sometimes I worry that it sounds crazy.

Since my parents' divorce, I have experienced mistreatment from my relatives on my mother's side. It seems that they disapproved of my maintaining a relationship with my father. They would say hurtful things about him in front of me and mock me for talking to him. They even called me anorexic, even though I was a healthy weight for my age. I remember confronting my mom about this when I was around 14, but she always told me to be patient and that family is family. I shared my concerns with my dad once, but his reaction frightened me, so I turned to my sister for support, even though she was quite reserved. It has been years now, and it seems that every year we face criticism from these relatives, despite my mom raising us on her own. They neither offer help nor support, only criticism. As I've grown up, I've felt a lack of belonging and a strong desire to distance myself from them. My mom, however, continues to tolerate their behavior because she loves them. Unfortunately, I still have to hear about their mistreatment of her, even though I no longer live with her. I'm worried that if this continues, I might lose my need for my mom in my life, which makes me feel guilty.

My father has been diagnosed with OCD (Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder), but I believe there may be more going on than just obsessions and compulsions. He exhibits behavior such as emotional manipulation, intense reactions, exaggerations, and even some paranoia. He constantly calls my mother and secretly follows her to work. He demands access to her passwords and threatens self-harm. He also exhibits delusions of my mother cheating on him and takes extreme measures to monitor her activities. He refuses to see a psychologist and dismisses the idea as a waste of money. How can I help him?

I have been struggling with the presence of a toxic family member in my life. We have shared familial responsibilities, which means I have to interact with this person on a daily basis. In the past, this family member was physically and verbally abusive towards me until I reached my thirties. Although the physical abuse has stopped, they now engage in toxic rants and swearing tantrums. It feels like they have substituted their previous bullying behavior with these harmful outbursts.

My fiancé and I have been together for 4 and a half years. We got engaged a year and a half ago and our wedding is in 18 days. We've always been a strong couple and I've been proud of how well we functioned compared to others around us.

Hi, I'm a teenage girl from Turkey. Lately, I've been questioning whether I might be a sociopath, but it seems a bit irrational to me. I'm hesitant to seek help from an expert in person, so I'm reaching out here. English is not my first language, just so you know. I consider myself intelligent, but I'm not sure if I'm overly intelligent or just a narcissistic idiot. I haven't taken any tests yet. Everything feels so abstract to me, like words in my mind are just combinations of letters that manipulate people's perceptions. The word itself doesn't hold any real meaning. It's all very confusing.

When I was 13 years old, my stepdad molested me. It happened when I was sick with a stomach bug and he offered to help me take a bath. I agreed, but I did not consent to him undressing me and bathing me. I felt terrified and violated. I did tell my guidance counselor at school about the bath, but I didn't mention the other things he had done. Child Protective Services came to our house, but nothing came of it. It wasn't until I was 19 that I found the courage to tell my mother everything, including the molestation and the other inappropriate things he had said and done over the years. The most disturbing thing he said was when I was 12, a year before the molestation, he told me that if I were 18, he would leave my mom for me. I nervously laughed it off at the time. Despite telling my mother everything, she chose to stay with him and showed little concern for what I went through. Three months ago, I decided to come forward to all of my family members and my stepdad's family. My mother said she wanted to speak with a professional before making any decisions. However, when my older brother spoke to her last month, she lied and said that I had spoken to the professional she supposedly saw. She even claimed that this "professional" said I may have a delusional disorder. I am devastated and don't know how to handle this situation. My mother and my stepfather's family have all sided with him, which is incredibly soul-crushing. I desperately need guidance.

Lately, I've been receiving feedback from two friends that I come across as patronizing and condescending at times. It's confusing because in my mind, I don't sound that way, and I genuinely try to avoid it. However, my efforts seem to be in vain. I've started to wonder if I have a different understanding of these terms, which is why I don't realize when I sound that way. It's frustrating because I feel like my true intentions get lost in translation from my thoughts to my speech.

I'm really concerned about my boyfriend's temper issues. He's 31 years old and he's aware that he has a problem. He saw a therapist before, but they didn't provide a diagnosis, just recommended therapy sessions. Unfortunately, he wasn't able to attend due to his frequent business trips. His temper problem is quite severe. Even small things that don't meet his expectations cause him to become extremely angry. He admits that he becomes a completely different person during these episodes. He says hurtful things and emotionally abuses the other person. He also sometimes hits objects, like walls. It takes him a while to recover from these episodes, and he often doesn't remember what he said or did. He tends to blame others for his behavior and acknowledges that it's not fair to expect people to tolerate it. He feels guilty and wants to change. He mentioned that his temper has always been an issue, but it seems to be getting worse as he gets older. I want to help and support him. What should I do?

I am graduating in May with a degree in Psychology. My family is going through a difficult time because of my Aunt's behavior. I suspect that she may be experiencing untreated symptoms of schizophrenia or a personality disorder. Her actions, such as taking control of my great grandmother's finances and forcing my grandmother to move, are causing a lot of distress. It's worth mentioning that schizophrenia can be hereditary, as my great grandfather on my mom's side also had it. My mother is seeking guidance on how to handle this situation for the benefit of the whole family. We are planning to move my grandparents into our home this weekend to protect them from my Aunt. However, we are unsure of how to help my Aunt as she is deceitful and has not responded to previous attempts for intervention. We have considered involving DSS, the police, or a mental health facility, but we need guidance on the best course of action. Any suggestions would be greatly appreciated.

I've been feeling really isolated lately. I don't have any close friends and I struggle to form connections with others, whether they're men or women. I often feel like I'm boring and have nothing interesting to say. On top of that, my voice is extremely quiet, almost to the point where it's not audible. When I try to speak up, it feels like I'm shouting and I can't think clearly. This makes me hesitant to speak in group settings because my voice gets drowned out and people talk over me.

About a year ago, I noticed a repetitive behavior in my sister. Every few days, she would put on her headphones and start running down the hallway. After reaching the end, she would go back to the start and sometimes linger there for a few moments before starting the running cycle again. This behavior lasts for several minutes.

Patient: Dear Therapist, I am a 15-year-old who feels mature for my age, but I am struggling with excessive worry and obsessive thoughts. I believe I have Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (OCD). It has been ongoing for about two years and has been getting worse. I have specific rituals and behaviors that I feel compelled to do, such as sitting up a certain way, blinking a certain number of times, and avoiding touching doorknobs. My friends have noticed my strange behavior, but I usually make excuses to cover it up. It's really impacting my life and I'm frustrated. I also have anger towards my mother and I'm not sure if medication, sleep, or stress relief would help. Am I going crazy?

I've been in a relationship with this guy for a year and a half now, and today he dropped a bomb on me. He told me that his parents want him to break up with me because he was diagnosed with Anti-social Personality Disorder (ASPD) a couple of years ago. They don't think it's fair to me. He mentioned his ASPD before, and I remember reading about it and seeing some symptoms that could apply to him, but also to many other people.

Patient: I've been struggling with some insecurities and feelings of inadequacy in my relationship. Before I met my fiancée, she had some encounters with famous individuals, including a child actor and a singer from a band she idolizes. It's been difficult for me to process and I find myself comparing myself to these individuals. I feel like I'll never be the type of man she truly adores, someone talented and famous. It's been eating me up inside and I need help with overcoming these thoughts.

I'm concerned about my 89-year-old father. He seems to have a consistent lack of trust in others, including me and my brother. He becomes suspicious in various situations, such as misplacing his ID and insurance cards and suspecting the nurse of taking them. He also suspected the visiting nurse of taking his blood pressure measuring device. He even believes that the hospital, rehab, and I are conspiring to keep him in the hospital to make money, despite the doctors wanting to discharge him. Additionally, he accuses me of taking my 86-year-old mother away from him when she moved in with me after he had a stroke. She has late-stage Parkinson's disease, dementia, and is blind in one eye. I'm wondering if these behaviors indicate a mental health problem or if it's more of a personality issue. Thank you.

As a medical student, I often feel overwhelmed and stressed. I find that going out and spending time with friends helps me relax and recharge. Unfortunately, since finishing school, I haven't been able to see my friends as often as I'd like, and it's been a bit depressing for me. My parents, who are more conservative, believe I shouldn't go out as frequently as I do. We've reached a point where we can't seem to agree, so I thought seeking professional advice might help resolve this issue. Personally, I believe that these outings are crucial for maintaining my mental well-being, but the constant debates with my parents have become mentally draining. I hope your input will bring some clarity to this situation and help us find a resolution. Thank you.

I've been experiencing ongoing conflicts with my mother and we're both exhausted from all the fighting. She constantly criticizes me, making me feel like I can never do anything right. I've tried expressing my feelings to her, but she never listens. Recently, I've discovered that I might have bulimia, but I haven't told her because I anticipate that she'll dismiss it as something imaginary. It's frustrating because I feel like I can't open up to her about anything.

I've noticed that I have intense emotions when it comes to certain things, like passion and empathy. However, I struggle to feel anger, even in situations where it seems natural to. Additionally, I find it difficult to fully understand and experience other emotions like sadness, happiness, and love. It's like I only feel them partially, never fully. I constantly question if I even feel anything at all or why I can't experience emotions to the fullest. I apologize if my explanation is confusing.

Lately, I've been struggling with intense feelings of anger towards my stepchildren. It's gotten to the point where I can't control my anger even when they haven't done anything wrong. I've been trying to understand why I'm holding onto this anger, but I haven't been successful so far.

I have a long history of mental health issues, and it seems to be a recurring pattern in my family as well. Unfortunately, when I was younger, I wasn't able to access the care I needed because my parents didn't allow it. This led to me resorting to self-harm and experiencing suicidal thoughts. In contrast, my brother faced his own mental health struggles and ended up with substance abuse issues and a delinquent record, which eventually led to court-ordered counseling. Now, as an adult, I've faced additional challenges such as unreliable access to food and shelter, as well as being sexually assaulted. I am unable to afford college and struggle to make ends meet even with financial aid, let alone being able to afford doctors or therapy. On the other hand, my brother's criminal record has continued to grow, and he was fortunate enough to receive support in a fancy rehabilitation facility for 6 months to avoid prison. While I am glad to see him getting the help he needs, it has always been painful to witness his problems being acknowledged and healed because of his violent and criminal behavior, while I struggle to take care of myself and even get out of bed. It feels like the available programs and resources are only designed for criminals or those who have severely damaged their lives in some way. I don't want to follow in my brother's footsteps or hurt anyone, but it feels like that's the only way to get people to notice and help me. If I don't find some drastic way to prove that I am suffering, I fear I won't receive the assistance I desperately need. How can I navigate this situation and find the help I need?

Throughout my school years, I've developed a habit of not putting much effort into my school work. I would rely on completing some homework and performing well on tests to pass my grades. I rarely study and often find it difficult to pay attention to the teacher during lessons. As a result, my handwriting has become quite sloppy and I experience discomfort when writing for extended periods of time.

From a young teen in Israel: I've been feeling really strange lately. I struggle with reaching out to people and it makes me feel depressed. I find myself saying things like "I want to die" to my new classmates, who I think are pretty cool. I feel like they're annoyed with me because I'm not popular and I didn't really have any friends before. I wish I had someone to talk to about life, but my parents never listen or understand. I was also bullied in middle school because I was different and didn't have any friends.

I am concerned about my husband's sexual behavior and its impact on our relationship. He has OCD, ADHD, and a mild form of Tourette's syndrome. He seems to have aversions to wetness and is uninterested in engaging with my genitals. Instead, he is focused on discussing my thong and creating scenarios involving violence. He requires constant talking during sex and is only able to maintain an erection with these specific stimuli. This leaves me feeling unfulfilled and unable to fully enjoy the experience. I believe there may be underlying factors contributing to his behavior, such as genetics or past experiences. Over the course of 5 years, I worked in an industry that had a reputation for having a toxic work environment. I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for almost three years now. About three months ago, we decided to take the next step and move in together. We are also planning to get married soon. Over the past five years, I've noticed a significant change in myself. I used to be a high-achieving student, but now I feel like a different person. I find it difficult to experience any emotions other than anger, and everything else feels muted. I even find myself laughing at my own misfortunes, which seems strange to me. I want to understand what's happening to me and how I can become the person I should be. Can you help me figure out what's wrong and what steps I should take?

I have been dealing with my unique quirks and tendencies since I was a young girl. Initially, I thought it was just me being particular or slightly obsessive. However, after becoming a parent, I've noticed that these "sensitivities" have become much more intense. My skin has always been hypersensitive, to the point where individual hairs touching it can drive me to frustration and anger. Certain sounds also have a strong impact on me, making me want to either curl up in a ball or scream. I'm concerned about how these things might affect my child's ability to cope with their emotions. Additionally, I have specific ways that everything needs to be done, and when those systems are disrupted, it feels like the end of the world. This includes organizing cabinets, the fridge, and even loading the dishwasher. The thought of things being out of order while raising a child triggers panic attacks and leaves me feeling exhausted. Socially, I struggle with severe apprehension, although I am able to hide it. Growing up in an abusive household with many siblings, I had to develop qualities that could protect my siblings and establish support networks outside of our home. It's a daily challenge for me to leave the house, go to noisy places like bars, and engage in conversations with people all night long.

Three years ago, I ended a six-year relationship with my boyfriend. Our relationship was intense and complicated due to our 13-year age difference, with him being older. He was my first serious relationship, and we essentially grew up together. The reason for our separation was his fear of commitment and refusal to move in with me, even though our relationship was his longest one thus far.

During my childhood, around the age of 7, my father entered into a serious relationship with my now step-mother. Around the same time, I began to experience sexual curiosity. Unfortunately, my step-siblings and I engaged in inappropriate games, such as spin the bottle, as a way to explore this curiosity. Over the years, this curiosity turned into a sexual attraction towards my youngest step-brother. By the time I was 13, we started engaging in oral sex, and by age 16, we had intercourse.

Recently, I've been experiencing a lot of fluctuation in my feelings towards the people around me, including my family and friends. It's causing problems in my relationships and I'm unsure of why I go through these changes. Sometimes, I feel a deep love for them, but other times I can't stand to be around them. When I become irritated with certain friends, I tend to cut them off completely, but I feel guilty because I can't pinpoint a valid reason for these emotions. Despite my efforts to stay positive, something always ends up triggering negative feelings again.

I believe that I may meet the criteria for Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD) based on my research and self-assessments. Although BPD is not typically diagnosed in adolescents, there are studies suggesting that symptoms can manifest during this age.

I am an 18-year-old heterosexual male and I have been struggling with distressing thoughts for the past two years. It all started when I accidentally had a brief sexual thought about my mom's breast, which made me feel disgusted and led me to question my worthiness of living. My doctor reassured me that it was a normal reaction, but then I started having thoughts about being attracted to a child anime character. I constantly check if I get turned on by looking at pictures of this character, even though I don't actually feel sexually attracted to them. I recently had a split-second turn-on when I purposely looked at pictures of the anime character and thought about having sex with my mom. This has left me feeling extremely distressed and confused about my identity. Am I a pedophile and incestuous or is this a symptom of POCD?

I've been struggling with what I think might be Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder. It's really hard for me to focus and my mind is always wandering. I'm only 14 and I want to get professional help, but I don't know how to approach this with my parents. Can you give me some advice?

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for almost 2 years. Recently, I found out that he has a child with his previous girlfriend.
