The only friends I have are from school, and since I don't go anywhere else, I feel really lonely when I'm by myself. I appreciate your help and guidance.

I'm really struggling with my boyfriend's sexual history. He's been with a lot of women, and it's hard for me to wrap my mind around it. He's told me that he feels ashamed of his past and that he's been intimate with friends, married friends, and even had one night stands. He's also admitted to not using a condom with three of his partners out of a total of fifteen. He has since gotten tested for STDs.

Hi, I've been experiencing a lot of anxiety and distress lately because I've become obsessed with understanding how the mind works. I find myself constantly thinking about how I produce my inner voice, how I memorize things, how I calculate, and how I imagine things. It's overwhelming and I feel trapped in this hyper-awareness of my consciousness. I want to escape from it, but I can't seem to stop thinking about it. It's like a never-ending cycle. It feels like hell right now and I'm afraid I'll never be able to forget this feeling. Can you please help me?

Hi, I'm a 20-year-old who recently moved to Chile with my mother after my parents' separation. I've been dealing with depression for a while and have been taking medication, but it doesn't seem to be effective. Lately, my symptoms have worsened. I constantly feel down on myself and never believe that I'm good enough. It's been so long since I've truly felt happy. I find myself getting angry over what my mother considers small issues, although to me, they feel significant. I'm always on an emotional rollercoaster, where even the smallest thing can bring me down and ruin my entire day.

I want to discuss an experience I had before my wedding that has been weighing on me. About 17 years ago, my wife had her last bridal shower at the church she was attending at the time. On that day, I had an argument with my father before attending the shower. I was feeling upset and distant during the event, and didn't engage much with anyone there.

I have a long-standing friendship with my best friend who is 50 years old, while I am 36. She has two grown-up daughters and tends to worry a lot, often taking things too seriously, even when her husband teases her. Due to her husband's overseas residence, she currently lives in her mother's house. She has experienced many challenges in her relationship with her husband, and despite him being the general manager of an estate, she chooses to continue living with her mother instead of moving in with him.

Patient: I've noticed that whenever I'm in public, especially at school, I feel extremely uncomfortable when people touch me. It could be something as simple as someone resting their arm on my shoulder, and it immediately grosses me out. I end up getting angry and yelling at them to remove their touch. I have noticed that I have a tendency to lie about things, even when it's unnecessary. I find myself making up stories and telling people that they are true. I'm wondering if there is a specific name for this behavior and if there are any steps I can take to address it. I'm not sure why I do it.

Hi, I've been married for a year now and we had a love marriage after being in a relationship for 9 years. However, we faced some challenges due to our different religions and I had to convert to my husband's religion for the marriage to be approved by his family. Currently, my husband is working abroad while I am staying with my in-laws. Initially, my in-laws were nice to me, but they seemed hesitant to spend money on my needs compared to my sister-in-law. They are unemployed, and my husband supports them financially, while I have a low-paying job. When I raised this issue with my husband, he admitted to giving a significant amount of money to his parents every month, while I struggle financially. How can I get him to help me?

I've noticed a pattern in my dating history where I seem to be attracted to men who are unavailable. For example, in high school, I was drawn to a guy who later came out as gay. In college, I pursued guys who were off-limits due to their roles as resident advisors or leaders of organizations. I also had a fling with a man who was married and another who lived in a different state. Recently, I found myself involved with a man who had no relationship experience and another who was recently divorced and didn't want to remarry or have more children. I even entertained the idea of being with a man who lives in a different country and doesn't speak English. I'm starting to question why I keep repeating this pattern.

It seems like my mother's behavior has taken a troubling turn. She has always been critical, but lately, she has become more bold in her actions. For example, she will say hurtful things to people in public and then claim to forget or accuse others of misinterpreting her. She also demands that I constantly tell her I love her, even when I have just said it, and then spreads false information about me refusing to do so. It's not just her behavior that concerns me, but also the fact that she keeps repeating the same stories every time we talk on the phone, without any coherence or relevance.

I'm a teenager living in the United Arab Emirates. I've been struggling with a difficult situation involving my girlfriend. She cheated on me with three of my friends, and it's been really hard for me to move on from it. This is especially challenging because I have never had any sexual experiences before, while my friends are more experienced. It's been two years since it happened, and I feel stuck. I don't know what to do, so I'm seeking help.

Since I was around 8 or 10 years old, I have developed a habit of biting my nails and picking the skin around them. Although I used to also pick at my acne, I have resolved the acne issue and my face has cleared up. However, I find it difficult to quit this nail-biting habit despite numerous attempts. While I have made some progress, my husband is now actively involved in supporting me to overcome this habit.

Patient's statement (revised): My boyfriend recently shared with me the painful experiences of physical abuse he endured at the hands of his father during his childhood. Learning about this has helped me understand some of the insecurities he had expressed before. I tried my best to create a safe and supportive environment for him to open up, knowing how difficult it must have been for him to share his story.

I've noticed some concerning behaviors in my mom that I can't quite pinpoint. Initially, I thought she might be narcissistic, but while researching sensory integration disorder for myself, I came across the term "thought disorders" in a forum. The symptoms mentioned, like blocking, circumferential speech, derailment, distractible speech, loss of goal, and semantic paraphasia, seem to align with what I observe in my mom. She is mostly coherent but frequently exhibits these symptoms. For instance, she tends to ramble on about various topics, frequently switches subjects, and experiences moments of blocking where she forgets what she was just talking about. She also substitutes words in sentences with random words. It's been challenging to have a coherent conversation with her. She often confuses my name with one of my brother's names and vice versa.

It seems that the current issue I am facing is closely tied to my experiences during childhood. To provide some background, my parents separated when I was quite young, leading me to grow up in a single-parent household. Surprisingly, that aspect isn't the source of my current problems. However, my mother has OCD and struggles with other emotional difficulties. Growing up, expressing any emotions other than happiness was discouraged. If my siblings or I showed any signs of sadness or anger, my mother would become angry herself and question us in a disparaging tone. She yelled frequently.

I have been struggling with severe OCD since my diagnosis in 2009. I have been in therapy for it since then. However, I had to stop going to therapy recently because I was helping take care of my mother who unfortunately passed away from uterine cancer last December.

I recently went on holiday with my girlfriend in the UK. Towards the end of the trip, I noticed that she was being secretive with her phone, hiding notifications whenever they popped up. I was thinking about confronting her about it, but I ultimately chose to let it go and try to move past it.

I'm really overwhelmed and don't know what to do. My fiance of 6 years is an alcoholic and he is mentally and verbally abusive to me every night. Additionally, my 18-year-old son works with him and relies on him for transportation and job opportunities. I feel trapped and don't know where to turn for help. Any advice would be appreciated.

I've been married to my husband for about a year now. Before getting married, we dated for seven years but didn't spend much time together or live together. We had discussed doing things 50/50, including household chores and finances. However, it seems like we're on different pages. I've been feeling exhausted and overwhelmed, often crying at night. I understand that things can't always be exactly equal, but I need some support from my husband. For example, when I can't make it home by 8, I would appreciate it if he could cook dinner or get something for us to eat. Unfortunately, he doesn't do anything until I get home. Additionally, I had a lot of debt from our wedding that I had to pay back on my own. Despite it being our wedding, my husband made me feel guilty about the expenses and hasn't been helping with household chores either, even though I've been contributing financially now.

I've been struggling with this issue for quite some time now. It seems that whenever I start something, whether it's a puzzle, a game, or even a social relationship, I can't seem to follow through. I'm a 16-year-old with no friends and no hobbies. I'm currently seeing a psychologist and a psychiatrist because I have social phobia. It's strange because people at school are actually trying to befriend me, but I consistently push them away unintentionally. I really want to do something meaningful with my life, but I have no idea where to start. When I asked my psychologist what I can do about it, they told me there is no solution. I used to play guitar and violin, but I quit both. What can I do to finish the things I start?

I've been attending therapy for several months now, and recently I've noticed that my therapist has been consistently coming in about 20 minutes late and ending the session early. I find it frustrating because a 50-minute session ends up being only 20 minutes. I'm wondering if this is her way of trying to communicate something to me.

I have been talking to myself and creating elaborate stories in my mind for as long as I can remember. It starts with me creating different characters and plotlines, and then I act them out aloud, playing the role of each character I've created. These stories can last for weeks and seem to evolve as I age. When I was younger, they were more childlike with talking animals and miniature people. Now, as an adult, they revolve around couples, family issues, and friendships.

I've been feeling a lack of interest and emotional detachment from everything lately. It's like my brain is turned off and I'm just going through the motions. I'm 20 years old and I've been reading about depression, specifically Code F32.2, which seems to match my symptoms.

I'm concerned about my older sister's lack of motivation and financial independence. Our childhood was difficult due to our alcoholic mother and our father's early death. Unlike my brother and me, she never worked as a teenager and instead engaged in problematic behaviors like stealing our mother's credit cards. It seems like she has never taken any initiative to support herself. She is now approaching 60 and has only worked for about 12 years in her entire life.

I recently started a new job as the director of a software company. I've developed a close relationship with one of my team leaders, and we often find ourselves discussing topics that go beyond work, like our personal lives and philosophical ideas.

Lately, I've been feeling like there's no point to life and my thoughts are constantly scattered. At home, I'm dealing with an abusive older sister whom I used to be close with. Now, my parents blame me for the abuse and it's causing a lot of tension. I've been having panic attacks and even vomited recently after a traumatic event. I also find it difficult to disconnect from technology. At school, I feel like my closest friends don't trust or rely on me, and I often question if I can rely on them either.

Nine years ago, at the age of 30, I was diagnosed with severe obstructive sleep apnea. Looking back, I believe this condition has affected me since childhood, causing various emotional, cognitive, social, and personality difficulties. I was always seen as a peculiar child, but no one ever pinpointed the root cause. Some people even speculated that I had Asperger's, but that diagnosis didn't quite fit.

I've been feeling really overwhelmed lately. It's like I have so much going on in my life and I can't seem to find a way to handle it all. I've been feeling anxious and stressed all the time, and it's starting to affect my sleep and my ability to focus.

I've been reading about this character, let's call him A. A seems to possess a carefree and reckless attitude, not giving much thought to the consequences of his actions. He lives in the moment and adopts a "do what you feel, YOLO" mindset. A is also quite materialistic and indulgent, spending a significant amount of money on clothes and possessions. His time is mainly dedicated to partying and having fun.

Lately, I've been struggling with understanding and interpreting my own emotions and the emotions of others. It's been going on for a few years now, and I've realized that it's becoming a hindrance in my daily life. While I can recognize emotions like anger and happiness in theory, when it comes to real-life situations, I find it difficult to comprehend them and why people express them so easily. It's frustrating because it seems like a skill that others have naturally, but I struggle with it. Should I seek help or talk to someone about this?

Recently, I have been experiencing intrusive thoughts when I pray. Even though I'm unsure of my belief in God, I find myself asking for things I am afraid of to not happen to me. However, there's a voice in my head that responds with the opposite, asking for those things to happen. This has been going on for the past four years, particularly with my fear of losing my arms. I have to repeatedly beg in my head for God to not take them and to ignore the voice. It triggers panic attacks, even though I know these thoughts are irrational. It's affecting my daily life, making it hard to focus on anything else because my mind is consumed with this fear. I feel helpless and terrified. Could this be caused by trauma or rejection? Is this a normal anxiety experience? I would appreciate any information or if someone has gone through something similar. It's really frightening me.

I've been struggling with social phobia and depression on and off since I was a young child. Despite these challenges, I come from a loving and non-violent family. Growing up, we had pets like a rabbit when I was seven, a cat at ten, another cat at twelve, and several fish in between.

Last year, I woke my wife up for sex. This has happened multiple times throughout our marriage, and there was never an issue raised. There were times when I didn't want to have sex but didn't say anything because I didn't want to disappoint her. On that particular night, I unknowingly triggered a traumatic flashback related to a past experience she had never shared with me. She didn't ask me to stop, and I only found out months later that it was unwanted. I felt hurt and betrayed by her during the assault. I realize now that I should have communicated my feelings to her instead of trying to replace negative emotions with providing her pleasure.

My husband has been diagnosed with Antisocial Personality Disorder (APD). I have been struggling to find a psychotherapist in Las Vegas who specializes in working with individuals with sociopathy. I have been feeling frustrated and discouraged, as the regular psychiatrist I have been seeing doesn't seem to fully understand the specific issues related to sociopathy. Can you please recommend a qualified psychotherapist in the area who can provide the specialized help we need?

I have a client who has been diagnosed with schizophrenia, PTSD, and borderline personality disorder. I was recently told that it isn't possible to have both schizophrenia and borderline personality disorder. Is this true, and if so, what is the reasoning behind it?

Lately, I've been noticing that I have been reacting strangely to some really distressing news. When I found out that my cousin had passed away, I didn't really know how to process it, so I just went back to bed and fell asleep. Then, when I found out that my grandma had a seizure, instead of feeling worried or upset, I just kept eating my lunch like nothing happened. And recently, when I learned that a friend of mine has a brain tumor, I found myself just mindlessly eating candy while lost in deep thought. I'm not sure why I'm reacting this way, but it's starting to concern me.

I've been struggling with intense jealousy towards my sister-in-law. She seems to possess qualities that I feel I lack, such as physical attractiveness, intelligence, and a sense of independence. I find myself constantly comparing myself to her and feeling the need to imitate her style and choices. I've even developed obsessive behaviors, like saving pictures of her and regularly checking her online profiles. It's affecting my self-esteem and causing me distress.

I recently found out that my dad has been diagnosed with Asperger Syndrome, which has made me reflect on my own experiences. Throughout the years, I've struggled to make friends and have kept a journal where I initially blamed others for not understanding me. However, I've started to realize that maybe it's me who doesn't understand them. I often find myself getting frustrated when people don't explain things clearly or when I ask for further clarification. This has been weighing heavily on me and I've been feeling increasingly depressed. I'm not sure if I need help or how to go about getting it. I just want to understand why I am the way I am.

I'm from the UK and I'm really concerned about my aunt's situation. She has severe bipolar disorder and takes Risperidone to manage her symptoms. She lives with a caretaker who also has another job, but he has a drinking problem and is often abusive. He even has suicidal tendencies and engages in disruptive behavior at night. Despite all of this, my aunt seems to have developed a close relationship with him and doesn't want him to leave.

For the past 15 years, I believe I have been dealing with severe depression. Unfortunately, I am unable to seek counseling or therapy at the moment due to certain reasons. Recently, I faced a problem at work where my manager harassed me repeatedly, and although I wasn't afraid, I found myself unable to stand up for myself. Eventually, I left the job, but now I am constantly filled with fear and anxiety. I worry that if a similar situation arises, I will react in the same way. I am desperate for help, and I am willing to do anything to feel better. I just need some guidance. Thank you in advance.

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for almost 9 months now, but we've only been on one date. I feel like he's not really putting in the effort to make our relationship meaningful. He admitted to pleasing another woman in the beginning, and he's not sincere with gifts or important dates. He's lied to me and let me down multiple times.

My best friend and I have been close since we were in grade 2, and now we're in grade 11. Lately, she's been showing signs of depression and pushing everyone away. She's stopped eating but won't admit it, and her school grades have taken a significant hit. She mentioned feeling sad and depressed, but when I asked if she had talked to someone else about it, she said she had. However, I found out from her mom that she hadn't. Her mom also expressed her concern, and my other friend and I share that worry.

Over the past 8 months, I have been dealing with severe anxiety. Despite trying various approaches like dietary changes and meditation, my symptoms have persisted. I experienced a prolonged period of numbness for about 4 months, and for the past 3 months, I have been struggling with difficulty breathing. I have seen multiple doctors who have attributed these symptoms to anxiety. Recently, a psychologist recommended that I try taking Praxil, but I haven't started it yet. Can you share your experience with Praxil or any other antidepressant?

I've been feeling really neglected by my parents lately. My sister is always the center of attention because she excels academically and in swimming competitions. It seems like my parents only talk about her and my life revolves around her schedule. I feel forgotten and like my worth is tied to her success.

I have been in a homosexual relationship with a man who has two children from a previous heterosexual relationship. When we first got together, it was clear that his children were not fully accepting of me joining the family. Despite their reservations, my partner chose to continue our relationship. We've now been together for 9 years, but I constantly feel unwanted by his children. It's becoming increasingly difficult for me to feel like I belong in this family.

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for almost six months. We were really close friends before we started dating, so I thought it would make the transition easier. However, I find myself feeling constantly annoyed and angry with him as a boyfriend, whereas he says he feels the same way.

I have been struggling with mood issues that resemble depression, but my reactions to medication have been quite concerning. My psychiatrist mentioned that I had a reaction similar to bipolar disorder, but I don't meet all the criteria for a bipolar diagnosis. The medications, both antidepressants and a mood stabilizer, have actually made me feel more suicidal. I find it strange because I don't consistently experience these symptoms, but rather go through periods of good mental health followed by depressive episodes or breakdowns. It seems to last longer than just a reaction to a specific event, so I think it's related to my mood. My doctor acknowledges that my reactions are unusual, and we're both struggling to understand what's happening. I think therapy might be a good option, but I tried CBT and I can't concentrate when I feel this low. I believe I can eventually overcome this, but it feels like it will keep happening, and it's disheartening to feel so lost without anyone who understands or can help me. I know you can't diagnose me, but I'm wondering if it's possible for someone to not fit into any specific category and not find relief through professional help? Does that mean I have to navigate my mental health journey alone?

I've been thinking about the psychological effects of making someone feel guilty. Why do people do this to others? And how does it impact the person who experiences this guilt in the long run, especially if they grew up in an environment where guilt was frequently used?

Counselor: I'm really sorry to hear about the distressing situation you and your daughter have experienced. It's understandable that you're feeling devastated and concerned about the future of your family. It's positive that your husband has moved out and is willing to seek counseling. Rebuilding trust and healing from such an incident can be a long and challenging process. However, with the right support, it is possible for families to come back from such situations.

I have a history of PTSD, anxiety, depression, and OCD. I've been pregnant twice before, once resulting in a miscarriage and the other resulting in the birth of my son who is now almost 3 months old. During both pregnancies, I experienced a strange sensation in my head that made me feel sick, nervous, and gross. This feeling continued throughout my pregnancies but stopped after giving birth. However, whenever I think back to my pregnancies, I still feel that weird sensation and it makes me anxious. Lately, I've been feeling sick, tired, having headaches, and experiencing nausea. I don't think I'm pregnant, but the feeling is causing me a lot of anxiety.

Over the past six months, I've been experiencing intrusive thoughts about death. These thoughts occur multiple times a day and seem to pop into my head regardless of what I'm doing. It's becoming distressing and I can't seem to stop them.

Hello. I have a friend who is experiencing conflicts in his relationship with his girlfriend. While she is generally sweet and successful, her behavior in certain situations has caused problems. I was wondering if they should consider couples counseling or individual therapy to address these issues. Can you provide some guidance on how they should proceed?

I recently ended a long-term relationship with my partner of 4 years. Over time, the relationship became abusive and I felt it was necessary to leave. He would occasionally choke me, although not to the point of losing consciousness, and he caused damage to my belongings and our home. Recently, I had a challenging experience with my dad. He was upset with me for having three late assignments and made me stay up until midnight to complete them. After finishing, I went to my bedroom but passed through the kitchen. In that moment, I noticed the knife set and felt a strong urge to harm myself. I picked up a knife and held it to my wrist, contemplating adding to my collection of cuts. However, my dad unexpectedly woke up and entered the kitchen. He grabbed the knife, but instead of expressing concern, he got angry and yelled at me, calling me a failure and saying he wished I could be more like my younger sister, who excels academically and is a star basketball player.

About a week ago, I had a realization that I am mortal and will eventually die. Since then, I have been consumed by thoughts of my own mortality. It's affecting my ability to enjoy life and I experience intense emotional distress whenever the thought resurfaces. I'm desperate to find a way to cope with this and return to a sense of normalcy. Can you please help me?

Patient: Hi, I just found out that my mom is cheating on my dad and I don't know what to do. I discovered a letter in her bag from another man, stating that they have been seeing each other for the past four years.

I've been noticing that my relationship with my mom has been strained lately, especially when her boyfriend is around. We all live together in the same house, and her boyfriend has never seemed to like me. He constantly says negative things about me, and while some of it may be true, I feel like it's not helping our situation. It's concerning to me that my mom's mood changes when he's around. We can have a great day together, but as soon as he's in the picture, she becomes hateful towards me. I had a fun day with my mom and my son, but when I left to take my son to practice and came back, my mom was in full-on "hate mode" towards me. When I asked her what was wrong, she said something about me giving her attitude. I'm starting to wonder if her boyfriend's constant negative talk about me when they're alone is fueling her negative feelings towards me. It's like he's reminding her of all my mistakes and failures. I'm just not sure if this dynamic is making our situation any better. Any insight would be greatly appreciated.

Lately, I've been struggling with holding onto things mentally and moving on from them. For instance, just yesterday, I was at a book store and as I was approaching the counter, I felt something hit my back. I looked down and it turned out to be a children's rubber toy. There was a stand nearby that it could have fallen off of if I accidentally bumped into it. However, I didn't notice anything on the stand and it landed on my back.

Since I was a teenager, I've been deeply interested in psychopathy and Antisocial Personality Disorder (ASPD). I've noticed certain traits in myself, such as my ability to manipulate and influence others, my lack of empathy (unless it directly affects me), and my intelligence and awareness of my choices. I've managed to avoid getting in trouble by being clever and finding alternative solutions, even if it means convincing others to join me. I am fully aware of how people express empathy, concern, and helpfulness, and I can portray these traits if the situation requires it. For instance, I cheat, exchange sex for money, and make up sob stories to get people to do tasks like yard work.

I wanted to share some background information about myself, as it may be relevant to my current struggles. Firstly, my eating habits are not very healthy, and I find it difficult to trust others. There isn't a single person in the world whom I fully trust. Additionally, I have a strained relationship with my family and we don't get along well.

My son, who is 27 years old, has recently been experiencing what appears to be symptoms of schizophrenia. He has been struggling with social skills and sleep issues for years. Despite graduating from law school, he has developed a fear of being around people, hears voices, neglects personal hygiene, and engages in compulsive spending. He bought multiple identical jackets, still in the package, despite not having the budget for it. The challenge we are facing is that every time he seeks help, healthcare providers accuse him of seeking drugs, even though he has a strong aversion to taking medication. He also fails to acknowledge the severity of his issues, believing that his sleep problem is the only concern. He maintains that everything will be fine if he can just get a good night's sleep, even though that doesn't seem to resolve his other symptoms. How can we convince healthcare providers that there is a more significant problem at hand, especially when he can come across as quite normal in certain situations, only revealing his struggles through off-the-wall comments?

I have noticed an interesting pattern in my romantic attractions. While I used to have crushes on straight celebrities as a child, as I've gotten older and started pursuing relationships, I find that I am only attracted to homosexual men. I can appreciate the physical attractiveness of heterosexual men, but once I get to know them, I lose interest. This has happened repeatedly and I find that I am particularly drawn to gay men, even if they don't fit the stereotypical flamboyant image.

I'm currently feeling concerned about the impact my mom's boyfriend is having on our household. In the past, my mom and I used to have intense arguments, but now that we all live together - me, my son, my mom, and her boyfriend - I'm wondering if his presence is causing more harm than good.

When I was nine years old, my family and I went through a traumatic experience with scabies. It was an isolating and distressing time for me, and I have been dealing with mild but persistent symptoms of PTSD ever since. The depression I have been experiencing since then has completely taken over my life, and in the middle of 7th grade, my general feelings of anxiety escalated into a full-blown disorder.

I come from a family where my father is narcissistic, closed-minded, and frequently angry. He often plays the victim role and used to have daily fights with my mom. My mom, on the other hand, also tends to play the victim role, and she is quite sensitive, pessimistic, and lonely. Both of my parents have been overprotective, judgmental, and critical, which has had a significant impact on my upbringing. Growing up in a lower-class neighborhood, I felt shy and introverted, as my family was from a middle-class background. I relied on my mom for buying clothes and my father for handling important paperwork. As a result, I have limited life experiences and feel scared to be myself or make independent choices, fearing my father's judgment. I don't have any real friends to share life experiences with, which only adds to my feelings of isolation. I find it exhausting to constantly hide my purchases from my parents, as they judge and criticize me whenever they find out. It's frustrating to not be able to freely express myself around them. I want to break free from this cycle, stop worrying about what my parents or others think of me, and live an independent life.

I am a 17-year-old female from the U.S. Lately, I have been struggling with my social interactions. I find it difficult to connect with others and I tend to avoid appearing needy. However, when someone shows interest in me, I become vulnerable and share my secrets, which often leads to them leaving. I feel lonely but also too arrogant to pursue relationships.

As an American teenager, I've been feeling ashamed and jealous of couples who engage in public displays of affection. I'm 18 years old, single, and I've never had a girlfriend, apart from online relationships that were distant and inaccessible. I've never been kissed and it's been weighing heavily on my mind. On one hand, I try to remind myself that I'm young and that it will happen eventually, but on the other hand, I can't help but compare myself to others who had their first kisses in middle school. Seeing couples kissing in school and in public spaces has become exhausting for me, especially since I've never been a part of that. It's made me realize that my desire for physical intimacy has been a major factor in my failed attempts to be with someone I like. I've even started having dreams about making out. In my waking life, I find it difficult to watch kissing scenes in movies or on TV, as it brings up feelings of jealousy and awkwardness. My patience is running thin and I'm desperate to have the experience of kissing a girl in real life. It seems so easy for other guys, even younger ones, and I can't help but attribute my struggles to my ongoing shyness. I'm just wondering why I have such a strong desire to make out with someone.

Over the past two years, I have been regularly seeing a psychologist to address my ongoing struggle with depression. Two years ago, I experienced a traumatic event where I attempted to take my own life. While I have physically recovered, I still find that every day is a challenge for me. I have become increasingly isolated and rarely leave my home, except for work. I have an adult son who has treated me poorly and been both physically and psychologically abusive since he was a teenager. I also have three grandchildren, but unfortunately, I only get to see one of them now. My psychologist believes that I am dealing with complex trauma, stemming from childhood abuse by my mother and sexual abuse by my brother. Additionally, I was in a domestic violence situation with my son until he tragically ended his own life. To make matters even more difficult, I lost my closest friend to suicide as well. It feels like the pain just keeps piling up. How can I begin to recover from all of this?

Over the past few weeks, my best friend (24 m) came to visit me for the weekend. My family has always had a close bond with him, considering him like another son. They even gave him keys to my mother's house, although I live with my Dad. On the first night, nothing happened. However, on Sunday morning, I woke up to find his hand in my pants, which made me feel uncomfortable. I didn't know how to react, so I moved his hand away and kept a pillow between us for the rest of the night. The following weekend, he came over again, but just for Saturday. This time, I woke up to discover that both his pants and mine were missing. Additionally, my panties had been removed, which is not something I do, regardless of how hot it gets under the covers.

I've been feeling really overwhelmed lately and I don't know who else to talk to. My parents don't seem to understand and just tell me to get over it. But I've been having this intense fear of aging and it's been getting worse.

I am reaching out because I am concerned about the dynamics between my 2-year-old son and my 5-year-old stepson. The older child often humiliates the younger one by calling him names and making hurtful comments about his toys. It's really distressing to witness. I'm not sure how to address this issue and help them develop a more positive relationship.

I have just completed my third year of college and I am feeling overwhelmed by the pressure to maintain good grades. My current GPA is 2.614, which is lower than what my mom expects from me. She is a high school counselor with high academic standards and she wants me to have at least a 3.25 GPA. I have been avoiding showing her my final grades in the past, but she always finds out and confronts me, making me feel ashamed and threatened to pull me out of school.

I've been experiencing some concerns about repressed memories lately. It's something that I know can happen to people, but I can't quite figure out why I'm having these issues. I'm a twenty-one-year-old female. When I was really young, around the age of four or five, I remember having sexual dreams or images in my head. These would involve characters from movies or shows that I had watched, and they were in nonconsensual situations. The antagonist would be doing something to the protagonist, and I always identified with the victim. I'm not sure how I had this understanding of sex at such a young age, especially something non-consensual. I don't recall ever seeing it or having it explained to me, but I did know about anatomy and where things should go.

Two years ago, I experienced a sudden onset of severe anxiety and depression. It became so overwhelming that I made three suicide attempts, the last one occurring while I was in the hospital. I consider myself fortunate to have survived such a dangerous attempt, especially since I had no prior history of psychiatric issues.

I have been involved in an extramarital affair for the past 10 years. Both myself and the person I am having an affair with are married. We initially met 12 years ago, and if it weren't for me getting pregnant with my son, I would have left my husband for him. However, I ultimately went back to my husband after finding out about the pregnancy. Now, we are both feeling miserable and want to leave our spouses. We know our actions are wrong, but we are concerned about the impact on our children, who are the same ages - two boys aged 7 and two girls aged 5. I have tried expressing my unhappiness to my husband, but he doesn't seem to understand and believes we can work through it. We have attempted counseling together and individually, but my husband is very co-dependent while I am not. This situation is causing me a lot of distress and I don't know what to do. Any guidance would be greatly appreciated.

Three years ago, when I was 19 and working as a landscaper, I began to have strange episodes. During this time, I was also experimenting with MDMA on a semi-regular basis. These episodes were characterized by a sudden onset of feeling as if I was experiencing someone else's trapped, frightened, and desperate emotions. Although I remained in control of myself and my emotions, I had a persistent bubble of these intense emotions. Additionally, whenever I performed a simple action like picking up or putting down an object, I would have vivid images in my mind of myself throwing or smashing the object, or engaging in a more violent and desperate version of the action.

I've been feeling empty and hollow lately. It's not quite depression, but I've noticed that I don't experience many emotions, except for two specific situations. Firstly, when I'm provoked multiple times, I become extremely angry. Secondly, there have been two instances in my life where I've felt a strong attraction towards a girl my age, even though I know very little about them. Looking at their pictures and being around them makes me feel happy. Throughout the day, I find myself wearing different masks to interact with others, and it seems like no one notices that I'm not being genuine. I also experienced intense physical bullying during my childhood, as well as instances of sexual assault from a parent of one of my elementary school peers. The thing is, I don't seem to react to anything. Whether it's winning or losing, watching movies, jump scares, death, surprises, birthdays, or anything else that would typically elicit a response from a person, I feel nothing. Can you help me understand what's happening in my brain? Thank you.

I have been feeling overwhelmed lately. There are a few things on my mind. Firstly, I am really struggling with living in a small apartment with my parents. They are always at home and tend to argue or talk loudly, which creates a lot of tension. Additionally, I recently broke up with my boyfriend because of the distance between us and the fact that we are both still early in our careers. The idea of getting married seems overwhelming right now. Another issue is that I lack confidence at work and worry that people question my ambition. Lastly, I have trouble opening up to people because I'm afraid of being judged for my language skills or lack of knowledge. At night, I have trouble sleeping peacefully and often wake up with scary dreams or feelings.

Lately, I've been intentionally trying to impair my hearing over a long period of time. It's become a way for me to escape from what I perceive as the social "norms" and the madness of modern society. However, my best friend seems to think that I may be teetering on the edge of insanity. I tried explaining to him that it's not about being unaware or blind to the messed-up aspects of the world, no matter where you go.

I have been struggling with depression and anxiety since I was 6 years old. It has greatly impacted my life. I have difficulty enjoying things and tend to push away the people I care about. This has led me to drop out of high school and quit multiple jobs. I constantly feel the need to be alone and lack motivation. On top of that, I also experience bipolar disorder, frequent panic attacks, and body dysmorphia.

I've been dealing with agoraphobia for the past 3.5 years, which has caused me to become homebound. Unfortunately, I am unable to afford traditional therapy due to my financial situation and lack of support from my family. My only option seems to be online treatment, but I haven't found any resources that address my specific needs. I feel stuck and don't know what to do.

I've recently gone through a breakup and I'm feeling really confused and hurt. I met this guy in January and we started dating, even though we live in different countries. He seemed really interested in me and would reach out to me every day. But suddenly, a few days ago, he ended things out of nowhere. I'm just not sure what happened or how to deal with it.

My sister experienced sexual abuse as a child. She has chosen not to disclose the specific details, but she has shared that it was perpetrated by a 17-year-old son of a family friend. Despite what happened, she maintains a relationship with him and refers to him as her brother. She also blames herself for the abuse, even going as far as calling herself a prostitute. She recalls not recognizing his behavior as sexual at the time and believed it to be normal due to our father's affectionate gestures towards her. It's important to note that our father has bipolar disorder. Now, I am starting to have suspicions about our father, although he has never molested us and has always shown love towards our sister and myself. I feel confused and unsure about what to think.

Throughout most of my life, starting from puberty, I have relied on hobbies and people to fill a void in my life. One example is my obsession with dance. As I became more skilled than my peers in the dance studio, I started to feel a sense of importance and validation from others. This led me to put immense pressure on myself to always succeed and outperform others, as I wanted to maintain that image of being good at something and special to others.

Throughout my life, I have been pretending to have specific mental disorders to gain attention and validation from my friends. Lately, I have been trying to convince myself not to feel remorse, so I can label myself as a sociopath. I used to hate myself to fit the criteria for depression. Now, I feel like I am going down a dangerous path and developing psychopathic tendencies. I have been engaging in harmful behaviors such as killing things, breaking laws, manipulating others, and even becoming narcissistic. I have a strong desire to have a mental disorder, and it feels like a matter of life and death. I am hesitant to admit that this is for attention because I am young and feel ashamed. Can you help me understand what is going on and if this could be classified as Munchausen Syndrome?

Hello, I’m an 18-year-old female from the UK. Over the past year, I have been facing significant challenges. Unfortunately, I do not currently have access to professional help, but I am in desperate need of guidance. My main struggles include self-diagnosed Pure OCD and the ongoing impact of growing up with emotionally and physically abusive parents, whom I am still living with. Additionally, I have also experienced bullying at school. With regards to my OCD, I have gone through various obsessions that have led me to feel deeply depressed and even contemplate suicide. I have managed to overcome fears related to cancer, paraphilia, schizophrenia, and existential concerns, among others.

It sounds like you had a challenging upbringing with a family that was critical and not very encouraging. It must have been particularly difficult for you when your parents separated during a crucial time when you were trying to get into college. And then, to add to that, your father's diagnosis of mesothelioma and his passing must have been incredibly tough for you to go through at such a young age. It's understandable that you may be feeling overwhelmed. How are you coping with all of this?

I have been seeking help for my mental health, but I feel confused and frustrated because each psychiatrist I've seen has given me a different diagnosis. This has made it difficult for me to understand what is really going on. I have also tried various medications, attended an Intensive Outpatient Program (IOP), and engaged in different therapies, but I haven't found much relief. I'm feeling really depressed and lost, not knowing what my next steps should be or where to turn to for help.

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for nearly two years. He's a really kind, caring person who always listens to me and supports me, even when I'm being unreasonable. However, he also has a close friend that he spends a lot of time with.

I've been feeling what I believe to be depressed lately. It's not a new feeling, but it keeps coming back. I have a difficult relationship with my mother, which makes me feel unloved and even more depressed. I recently tried opening up, but I'm not sure if it was the right decision. I wonder if I stopped talking because I didn't want to burden others or because I genuinely felt like a bother.

I've been feeling really down lately. I just can't seem to find joy in anything anymore. I used to love going out with friends and pursuing my hobbies, but now everything feels empty and meaningless. I'm worried that I might be depressed.

Lately, I've been noticing that my behavior and mood swings have been becoming more intense and it's really starting to frighten me. I've always considered myself to be overly emotional, overly sensitive, and prone to having tantrums, but now I'm starting to wonder if there might be something more going on.

As a teenager in New Zealand, I have been feeling extremely unhealthy and lacking energy. I have a deep dislike for myself and feel like I am destroying my own life. I have never really engaged in physical activities and now I feel stuck.

As a 63-year-old male, I have endured a history of physical and emotional abuse from my father since I was very young. He would often use a thin pigskin belt to whip me as hard as he could, all while screaming at me. Whenever I cried, he would continue to whip me until I stopped. I vividly remember the overwhelming sensation of collapsing inward when I had to endure these beatings. My mother did try to intervene, but my father would lock us in the bathroom during the abuse.

Over the past three years, I have been experiencing symptoms of depression, and it has been difficult for me to find someone to confide in. I feel like my family wouldn't understand or truly listen, no matter how important it is for me to share. My friends often offer the same advice of "it's going to be okay," but I no longer find it comforting.

I recently got married at the age of 20 and I'm struggling with my relationship with my husband's 4-year-old daughter. She displays spoiled behavior and has a difficult attitude. She frequently throws extreme tantrums and refuses to listen to us. She often responds to our requests with a defiant "no" or even yells it.

Patient: I have been experiencing running thoughts that I can't seem to control. This has been happening on and off for about a year now. Additionally, I have this strange feeling like what's happening to me isn't real, almost like I'm detaching from reality. I've also been having bizarre dreams, like being chased by zombies and feeling trapped in certain situations. It's starting to affect my daily life as I struggle with concentration, forgetfulness, and increased sensitivity. I experience this weird feeling almost every day now, and it's becoming overwhelming, especially upon waking up. It's really scaring me.

Patient: I'm originally from Indonesia. Last month, I started taking an antidepressant medication, but I only took it for 8 days before stopping. It wasn't because I couldn't handle the side effects, but rather because my parents no longer permit me to take it.

In October, my girlfriend experienced a manic/psychotic episode for the first time. During this episode, she exhibited impulsive behaviors like excessive spending, drinking, lack of sleep, engaging in risky sexual behaviors, and having grandiose beliefs. She sought treatment and was prescribed medication while also attending therapy. However, she discontinued group therapy because she felt that everyone else in the group had their own issues. She did continue individual therapy for a while but eventually stopped because she felt it wasn't helpful. During this time, we broke up but remained in contact. Recently, we decided to give our relationship another chance and take things slowly.

I've been feeling really down lately and it's been affecting my daily life. I've been isolating myself, having trouble sleeping, and feeling irritable. I've also been having frequent thoughts of suicide. I don't know how to approach my parents about this because I'm afraid they won't take me seriously or make fun of me. Can you please guide me on how to have this conversation with them?

Lately, I've been experiencing some troubling thoughts and feelings. It feels like there is another presence in my mind that controls my imagination and inserts thoughts into my head. This entity also makes me paranoid and impulsive at times. When someone gets too close to me, I feel a strong urge to punch them and run away. I've come to realize that this presence is not me, but it still makes me feel stalked. I've even started covering my phone's camera and checking behind the bathroom curtain out of fear. Physically, I may appear fine, but mentally I feel like my mind is deteriorating.

I’ve been living with my aunt for over 6 years now, but the past 4 years have been really difficult. She constantly yells at me and sometimes even resorts to physical violence. It's been really hard for me to cope with these situations, and sometimes I find myself having thoughts of harming her. I've managed to stop myself from acting on these urges, but I'm worried about my own well-being. Additionally, I have a close friend who has confided in me about her adopted dad behaving inappropriately towards her. I'm unsure about how to handle these situations and how to talk to my friends about it.

As I reflect on my childhood, I've realized that my perception of my mother has changed over time. When I was younger, I saw her as funny and kind, although she was strict about my studies. However, as I've grown older and become more mature, I've noticed some behavior that concerns me. For example, when she needs help, she speaks in a high-pitched voice and makes indirect statements rather than asking directly. Sometimes I understand the hint and help, but other times I don't, and she reacts with a tantrum. Additionally, she makes insensitive comments about our weight and seems to compete with us. She also tends to dismiss my problems and make them about herself. I've been reading about narcissism, but I know I shouldn't diagnose her based solely on that.

Hello, I'm a teenager from Slovakia. I apologize for my English, it is not my first language. I am currently facing a difficult situation in my life. I recently underwent heart surgery and I am now in the process of recovering. However, I have another serious issue that requires me to take hormone pills in order to preserve my fertility for the future. Unfortunately, I am unable to take these pills due to my heart condition.

It has been a very challenging experience for me over the past 8 years. I was denied contact with my two children and had to give up my parental rights. Recently, I came across my now 21-year-old daughter on Instagram. To my surprise, she mentioned that her father had told her that I forced him to let me terminate my parental rights and that I only wanted my son, not her. She also shared that they were subjected to terrible stories of abuse during their first 13 years of life with me.

Lately, my husband and I have been experiencing frequent conflicts. We have been married for almost 3 years and have a blended family with four daughters and a 1-year-old son. I love my husband, but his behavior has become increasingly hurtful. He often cusses at me, calls me names, and says hurtful things. While things eventually go back to normal after a few days, he never apologizes or takes back his hurtful words. He claims that I am mean and rude "all the time," but can't provide any examples to support this. He uses this as an excuse for his own behavior.

I've been feeling really isolated lately and I think it's because I've been distancing myself from everyone. It's almost like a defense mechanism. When I was younger, my father emotionally abused me and constantly lied, which has made it hard for me to trust others. I've always felt alone, especially because I'm an older child and my parents aren't very attentive to me. When they do pay attention to me, I feel uncomfortable and like I don't deserve it.

Recently, I've been reflecting on my behavior and I've come to realize that I exhibit many traits commonly associated with sociopathy. I find myself lying frequently, occasionally stealing money, and lacking guilt or remorse for my actions. I believe these traits may have developed as a result of my difficult childhood. My father has been absent for the past 8 years and used to manipulate me into relaying messages and asking for money. I felt like a puppet and it made me angry that my feelings were disregarded. My father was a manipulative and generally negative influence. Although I'm not exactly like him, I struggle to feel empathy or concern for others. I've even found myself watching violent videos without feeling any emotional response, sometimes even laughing at the suffering of others. I become easily annoyed by people who bother me and have thoughts of causing harm to them. I also struggle with impulsivity and have difficulty thinking ahead. Fear and distress are rare for me, except when it comes to physical pain. I've caught myself intentionally thinking of terrible things happening to my loved ones without any emotional reaction. My kindness towards others is often motivated by what I can gain from them. I've noticed that I can't comprehend love when I see my brother and his girlfriend expressing affection. I used to be a caring and understanding person, but now I find myself becoming impatient and rude. I wear a facade of sociopathy to hide my true emotions and I've noticed that my empty gaze tends to make people uncomfortable. Recently, I developed an interest in a girl and attempted to manipulate her into breaking up with her boyfriend while pretending to be friendly. Although it didn't work out, the heartbreak I experienced caused me to shut down my emotions even further. While I'm not actively seeking help because I somewhat enjoy my mindset, I do want to know definitively if I exhibit sociopathic tendencies. Thank you for taking the time to read this.

I've been struggling with communication issues for as long as I can remember. I often find myself unintentionally hurting others' feelings because I take things too literally. It's like I don't always pick up on the emotional context behind certain words or phrases. For example, I might say something is "irrelevant" without realizing that it carries a negative connotation. I constantly have to remind myself to be mindful of how my words might come across.

I'm in a relationship with a man who shares a bed with his 5-year-old daughter. Despite putting her in her own bed every night, she consistently ends up in his bed. When I sleep over, it becomes challenging for me because I don't get a restful sleep and sometimes end up on the couch. One night, she became upset that she couldn't be next to her dad because I was there, and she even hit me until I left. I'm concerned that this situation may be harming my relationship with my boyfriend, as we don't get any alone time even in bed. Additionally, I wonder if she has learned that making enough noise and causing a scene will allow her to get what she wants. Is it selfish of me to desire some alone time with my boyfriend? Is she perceiving that her dad's relationship with me is not important if she can easily remove me from our time together?

From the beginning of our relationship, it feels like my husband prioritizes his mother's feelings over mine. For our wedding, we initially planned to have just the two of us and two witnesses, but my husband was afraid to tell his mother, so I ended up telling mine. I received a bit of a cold shoulder from my mother, but my husband wouldn't budge. He was worried about his mother being upset, so we ended up having a wedding that didn't reflect our true desires. I can't seem to let go of this resentment, and it keeps resurfacing in our relationship.

I have been experiencing persistent delusions for quite some time now. I constantly feel like people can read my thoughts, there are surveillance cameras everywhere watching me, and that everyone I encounter is reporting on me. The confusing part is that I am aware that these beliefs are false, but they still persist most of the time. However, there are moments when I have some clarity and realize that these delusions are not true.

I'm really concerned about my younger brother's behavior. He recently got into a heated argument with our mom in the kitchen, and things escalated when he pulled out two knives. My brother has a history of having outbursts, but this is the first time he has ever used a weapon. I'm also worried because during these episodes, he often says things like he's going to harm people, although he later apologizes and claims he doesn't mean it. I've secretly recorded some of these instances because I don't want him to legally purchase a gun. I'm unsure of what to do because if I involve the police, he might get arrested and it could ruin his future.

"From the U.S.: My husband and I have been together for 9 years, married 5 of those years. When we first got together, my boys were 7 and 5 years old, and they got along. A year later, we moved in together and my boys could do nothing right in his eyes. It wasn't THAT bad, so I told myself it would take time. Every year got worse and not better! I still tell myself it will get better someday, but I think now it will only get worse."

Throughout my life, I have struggled with extreme shyness and difficulties in social interactions. I have very few friends, and I rarely see them, leading me to question whether they can truly be considered friends. I spend most of my time alone, from going to school to sitting in the cafeteria, even during weekends.

A few months ago, I started seeing a counselor for the first time at my college. I should have sought counseling earlier, but I was always reluctant until I had a recent breakdown. Throughout my life, I've struggled with social anxiety, feeling extremely shy and finding it difficult to make friends. I often assume that people think negatively of me and won't like me, which makes me distant and hard to get to know. This affects my job and professional performance due to a lack of self-confidence and fear of judgment. The counselor mentioned that my experiences align with social anxiety. However, even after multiple sessions, I still felt anxious and shy. It's challenging for me to warm up to people, even if I've known them for years. I found therapy difficult and became frustrated, leading me to quit after several sessions. Although I made some progress and learned a lot, I felt hopeless that things would ever change. I've researched avoidant personality disorder (APD), which seems similar to social anxiety. It made me wonder if I have APD and if treating personality disorders is difficult. I'm not a fan of labels, but I'm curious if my therapist would diagnose me. They did mention that the therapy we did was CBT.

As an Iraq war veteran, I've been experiencing a sense of not belonging anywhere. It's hard to describe, but it's not necessarily depression. These feelings used to come and go, lasting only a few days or a week. However, now I feel stuck. It's as if a part of me is missing and I desperately want to find a place where I belong, but I don't know where that is.

I've been struggling with my mental health for the past two years and it's only getting worse. I'm a 16-year-old girl and I'm not sure if what I'm experiencing is normal for someone my age. While I know that adolescence can be challenging, I feel like I'm dealing with more problems than my friends, or at least they don't seem to be showing it.

Lately, I've been noticing that things I used to enjoy are making me feel sad and empty. I've been dealing with depression and anxiety for a few years now, and although I can't afford therapy right now, I try to take care of my mental health by staying busy with hobbies and spending time with friends. However, instead of feeling happy when I engage in activities like reading, watching TV shows, or listening to music, I just feel more depressed. It's frustrating because I can't understand why this is happening, and if I can't understand it, I don't know how to fix it. Can you help me understand why the things I love don't make me happy anymore?

Patient: I'm 25 weeks pregnant with my first child, but I'm unsure if I'm making the right choices. Prior to getting pregnant, my partner and I led a fast-paced lifestyle involving alcohol, weed, and clubbing. However, I have made the decision to change my life for the better, cutting off negative influences and becoming a sober parent. Unfortunately, my child's father hasn't made any changes and doesn't seem interested in doing so, even for the sake of our son. He doesn't trust the changes I've made and believes it's all an act. He shows little interest in me, texts other women in my presence, and makes me feel unappreciated. I grew up without a father, so I've been trying to keep him around for my baby's sake, but now I'm questioning if it's more harmful than beneficial. I'm unsure of what to do, but I want to make the best decision for my son.

Throughout my life, I've always felt like I didn't fit in with people my age. I've often viewed them as immature, which created a sense of disconnect. As I've grown older, I've become more accustomed to the changes in my body, and so have others. Despite this, my perception of my peers has remained the same over the years. I can't help but notice that they seem to be "growing up faster" than me, particularly in terms of their sexual experiences.

I'm a seventeen-year-old who recently went through a breakup with my boyfriend of six months. We had a great relationship and enjoyed spending time together. Unfortunately, our relationship ended because of a lie that was spread about us. After the breakup, we both wanted to get back together, but my mom is preventing it. She has some sort of issue with him and won't even allow me to talk to him. I still have strong feelings for him and feel like my mom is keeping us apart. I'm not even allowed to interact with him at school.

Last month was a bit of a rollercoaster for me. Despite feeling a little depressed due to some ongoing challenges, I managed to secure a job which initially brought me joy and excitement. However, on my first day, I started experiencing dizziness and lightheadedness. After visiting the doctor, I learned that I had a sinus infection. Things took a turn for the worse as I started having panic attacks and intense anxiety over the next few days. It got to the point where I woke up one day feeling incredibly anxious and unable to think clearly. I felt like I was walking around in a fog and didn't recognize myself. This continued for three weeks.

Lately, I've been feeling really down. I've been experiencing intense sadness and find myself crying a lot, especially when it comes to things like school work and stress. Even small things, like overhearing classmates making fun of my weight, really get to me. I never thought I would consider suicide, but lately, it's been crossing my mind. It's just so difficult. I've tried looking up the symptoms of depression online, but I don't have all of them, so I'm worried that I might be overreacting and just being dramatic about my weight and emotions. Can you help me determine if I am depressed?

I'm a 22-year-old who has been struggling with depression. I've been trying to understand the cause of my depression, but I haven't been able to pinpoint anything specific. However, during my self-reflection, I've noticed that I have some strange dreams and nightmares. One recurring nightmare involves being intimate with my father, not necessarily sexually, but in an intimate way. When I have this dream, I feel guilty and scared. It always feels like the first time, but then I remember that I've had the dream before and I try to ignore it. I've never talked to anyone about this dream because I'm scared. I'm afraid that it's just a dream, but I'm even more afraid that it might be based on a real experience. I also struggle with trust issues, especially with men, and I'm wondering if there's any connection to these dreams. Lately, I've been feeling awkward around my father. How can I stop having this dream, and how can I determine if it's more than just a dream?

I'm an 18-year-old from the U.S. and I'm really struggling right now. I feel like I need professional help, but I don't know where to turn. My parents don't believe in therapy and have even discouraged me from seeking it in the past. On top of that, I'm currently unemployed and can't afford therapy without them finding out. I feel completely lost and don't know what to do.

I've been struggling with this ongoing dilemma about my female friend. We tried dating but it didn't work out, and now we're just friends. However, I've had doubts about whether she genuinely cares about me for quite some time.

Patient: I've recently started therapy again after struggling with my fear of opening up and being judged for years. However, I've discovered that the counseling service I've chosen is affiliated with a Baptist church, and my therapist is openly religious. It's evident from her Facebook posts and the presence of Bible verse plaques in her office.

When I was 15 years old, my older brother passed away due to a long-term heroin addiction. He was not only my brother but also my best friend, and I had to witness his death. I coped with the pain by partying, as it provided a temporary escape. However, the pain eventually caught up with me, and I had to face the grief I had been avoiding.

I've noticed that my cousin, who is around the same age as me, has been inventing stories about her childhood. She tells people, including myself, false narratives about growing up in Virginia, even though she actually lived just two miles away from me her whole life. She also claims to have been in an abusive marriage for over 15 years, where her husband controlled and isolated her, preventing her from contacting her parents. However, the problem is that she lived in the same house as her mom and dad. She also contradicts herself by saying that her husband never allowed her to work, but then mentions working at a nearby factory for 15 years. It seems like she has completely recreated her past to portray herself as a victim. Because of this behavior, people are starting to distance themselves from her. While she seems normal in the present, whenever she talks about her past, it's all fiction. It's really strange how she contradicts herself within just a few minutes of talking. The common thread in her stories is that she positions herself as a victim.

I've been struggling with the end of my relationship with my ex for the past two years. We met when I was 18 and he was 21, and we were together for a while before he had to move to Chicago for a job. He broke up with me a couple of months before he left because he didn't want to hurt me more in the long run. Since then, I've been feeling incredibly depressed and even had thoughts of suicide. I can't stop thinking about him and it's affecting my daily life. I've tried everything to move on, but nothing seems to work. I need help to overcome this pain.

I've noticed that I have a tendency to get easily upset and hurt by other people, even over small or trivial things. Sometimes, I can take a step back from the situation, think about it, and eventually feel better. However, there are other times when I find myself becoming irrationally angry and acting in a mean and hurtful way.

I have noticed this for quite some time. I can't feel empathy or sympathy towards people. An example of this is when my best friend was crying in front of me because she was getting death threats, I couldn't bring myself to actually care. Another example is when my uncle died, and my dad was crying in front of me. I found it hilarious.

Since I was 12 years old, I have been experiencing symptoms of depression. Throughout my childhood, I struggled with behavioral issues and endured bullying. Thoughts of suicide occupy my mind daily, although I have never acted on them. I feel completely worthless and believe that there is no future for me. I lack any sense of purpose or enjoyment in life, and each day, must summon more and more willpower just to focus on my studies.

Over the years, I've noticed a pattern with the people I've helped. I genuinely enjoy supporting my friends and loved ones through their challenges, but it seems like they either distance themselves from me or don't appreciate my efforts. It hurts to see them disregard my advice and then come back later admitting I was right, only to repeat the same mistakes. I've also experienced situations where they leave me in the dark and ignore my attempts to communicate. It's really difficult for me, and I question whether I should have even tried to help them. I feel used and discarded, which makes me question my own worth. I apologize for rambling, and I appreciate your time.

I feel overwhelmed by the multitude of issues I'm facing and I'm unsure of what steps to take. It feels challenging to articulate my problems in a concise manner, but I understand the importance of providing thorough information for a better understanding. I live with my single mother and younger sister. Unfortunately, my father left us when I was just three years old, and I've struggled to come to terms with that. My mother has tried to fill that void with individuals who have addiction issues, alcoholism, and even pedophilia. As a young and vulnerable person, I found myself caught up in those dynamics.

I have a female friend whom I've been friends with for about 8 years. We are very close, but we never engage in any physical contact like hugging or touching each other's shoulder. I'm starting to develop feelings for her, and I'm wondering if it's normal for friends to have physical contact or if our lack of it is due to fear of sexual arousal. Could it be a sign that she might be interested in me but doesn't want to ruin our friendship?

Patient's statement (rewritten): I've realized that I have been experiencing rapid changes in my mood, thoughts, and feelings for as long as I can remember. It feels like I'm constantly lost in my thoughts, struggling to focus on the present or plan for the future. I have so many ideas and realizations, but they fade away quickly, and I struggle to identify my moods because they change so frequently. It's like I have no control over my mind, and nothing about myself feels permanent. Even my feelings towards my loved ones fluctuate without any clear reason. I haven't experienced any trauma and have a loving support system, so I'm not sure why I feel this way.

As a teenager in Egypt, I experienced childhood sexual abuse. Unfortunately, when my father found out, he did not take any action. I have tried to move on from this trauma, but I still engage in behaviors that make me question if it has truly affected me. Recently, I was diagnosed with a rare form of cancer and just completed chemotherapy. While I am getting better physically, I am filled with fear about what the future holds. If my childhood was filled with pain and now, at 18, I am dealing with cancer, what will happen when I turn 21? Will I lose a limb or someone I love? I just want to know how to heal from this trauma and manage the anxiety attacks I experience.

I have a friend who I consider my best friend, but she is not open with me. I have invited her to meet my family multiple times, but she always rejects the invitations and makes excuses. I invited her one more time to meet my cousin and sister at a restaurant, just the four of us. She responded with a sad voice message, saying she feels anxious, her heart is racing, and she's shaking. She mentioned that there will be too many people, even though it's just the four of us. I tried to reassure her by pointing out that she goes to restaurants and meets people all the time, but she wouldn't explain what's really bothering her. We ended up arguing, and she told me to look it up online. I searched for answers and came across social anxiety, but she denied it. I'm really confused about what the issue is. Can anyone offer any insights? By the way, we've been friends for about a year.

Last week, my partner called me because he was stuck at work and asked if I could pick him up. I had just finished my own work and was feeling exhausted, so I initially hesitated and suggested that someone at his workplace could give him a ride. However, after a minute, I realized that I felt awful about my hesitation and called him back to apologize and offer to pick him up. Now I'm struggling with the idea that my initial reaction reflects my true self, despite ultimately making the right choice. I've searched online for answers, but haven't found anything satisfying. I feel guilty about my initial selfish reaction and worry that it's indicative of who I really am. Can you help me understand if it's my initial reaction or my subsequent response that defines my values and morals? Thank you.

Hello. I am a 21-year-old from Argentina, and I'm struggling with a lot of anxiety. It feels like my life is stagnant because I can't seem to move forward. My parents constantly make me feel miserable and depressed, and I don't have any family members who can offer me support. It's really difficult for me right now.

I have noticed that whenever I spend time with my friends, even for a short while, my long distance girlfriend struggles with it. She doesn't have any friends of her own and feels very lonely. Even though I try to keep in touch with her through texting, she emotionally shuts down and only gives me one-word responses. As a result, I have started distancing myself from my friends because I don't want her to shut down on me. She has been dealing with severe depression for a long time, and I believe it might be a contributing factor. She describes this feeling as her brain shutting her down, and she feels helpless. I would like to understand what might be causing her to feel this way and how I can support her. She also has anxiety, separation anxiety, and depression, which I think could be playing a role. I just want to learn how to help her work through these challenges so that I can spend time with my friends without feeling guilty and sad when she shuts down. It's frustrating, and I don't know what to do.

I have been dealing with family issues for most of my life. I was born as a result of an affair between my mother and a man who was already married. He promised to divorce his wife, but never followed through. Now my brother and I are left feeling like love children. It's been a source of pain and confusion for me.

I've been noticing a pattern in my behavior where I tend to procrastinate or avoid doing things, even simple tasks like checking my email, paying rent (even when I have the money), doing homework, and studying. I've also noticed that I do the same thing with things that I actually enjoy doing. For example, I tend to procrastinate doing homework until the last hour, but once I start, I really enjoy it. The same goes for studying for a class - I put it off, but when I finally do it, I find that I really enjoy the process.

When I was 13 years old, I engaged in harmful behavior towards my family's pit-bull puppy, resulting in its death. I tied a rope to its collar, hung it from a tree, and witnessed its suffering until its neck snapped. I then disposed of its body and kept its canine teeth as a memento. I also brought my sister to see the dog's head, pretending it was a coyote's. I frequently have thoughts and fantasies about harming and torturing animals. I'm concerned about what this means.

I'm 58 and I've recently started dating a man who is 4 years younger than me. He has a young daughter and three older adult children from his previous marriage. He was married for 25 years and is originally from Europe. He is also quite wealthy.
