We have a strong and magnetic connection and spend a lot of time together, including evenings and even a whole weekend. He seems to have a hard time being away from me for too long.

I recently moved to Prague with my husband and two young sons after experiencing a period of emotional distress. Prior to the move, I was working full-time in a highly stressful job while also caring for my children. I returned to work shortly after giving birth to each of my sons, despite facing complications and the sudden loss of my mother when my second son was just a few months old. During this time, my husband was frequently away on business, which made it difficult for me to properly grieve.

My father is a 75-year-old man who has been unemployed for the past 25 years. He spends most of his time alone at home, and I believe this has affected his self-worth. When he is in larger groups of family or friends, he seems to behave normally. However, when it's just me or my mom, he exhibits attention-seeking behavior and doesn't seem to care about his reputation or how his actions reflect on him. Could he have a psychological issue, and is there anything my mom and I can do to help him?

I have been struggling with various mental health issues for a long time, including depression, anxiety, low self-esteem, and social issues. However, there are thoughts and concerns that I haven't been able to fully understand or express. It's difficult for me to talk about these things, even though I've seen counselors in the past. I feel like there must be something wrong with me, but I can't quite pinpoint it.

As a teenager in the United States, I have experienced a history of physical abuse from my father and emotional abuse from my mother. Additionally, I have faced challenges with abandonment after my parents' separation and the people who were supposed to care for me also left. These experiences have contributed to feelings of depersonalization and derealization, causing me to frequently feel disconnected from myself and the world around me. I have also heard voices and seen shadows, which I have come to perceive as my friends.

I am a 52-year-old individual from the U.S. I have an adult child and a younger child who is on the autism spectrum and defiant. Late in life, I became a parent again. I am disabled due to multiple medical issues, including bipolar depression, fibromyalgia, severe arthritis, chronic fatigue, as well as neck and back pain.

I've been experiencing some distressing thoughts and beliefs lately. I've started to believe that I have the ability to cause deaths and control electronics across the globe. I had an experience where someone claimed I turned off their lights in their room, but when I tried to test it on other people, they said I couldn't do it. However, I'm still unsure if that person was lying or not. These thoughts and beliefs are causing me a lot of distress, and I also feel paranoid when I go for a walk, thinking that people are being hostile and know who I am.

Recently, I've noticed that I have a tendency to avoid making eye contact with others, whether they are close friends or family members. Whenever I try to maintain eye contact, my eyes become watery and irritated. As a result, I struggle to engage in normal conversations and often feel like I lack concentration or fail to give others the attention they deserve. Additionally, I frequently wake up feeling sad and have a strong desire to isolate myself from others. I used to attribute these feelings to being shy, but now I'm starting to think there might be something more to it. It's frustrating because I'm 19 years old, and I feel like socializing should come more naturally to me.

I'm concerned about my girlfriend's relationship with her mom. They have a very dysfunctional dynamic and it's causing a lot of conflict. About a year and 6 months ago, my girlfriend had to move out because the fights between them were getting out of hand, sometimes even turning violent. Her mom is verbally abusive, often calling her hurtful names. She ended up moving in with her grandparents, which her mom resents. It's been a difficult situation for her.

Since I started college in a different state than my home, I isolated myself to focus on school; I decided that I would just focus on academics and not socialize. As a result, I have made no friends in college and there are days, and sometimes weeks, that go by where I don’t talk to a single person. What drove me to continue isolating myself like this was the fact that I was doing well academically. However, I started realizing that all this time in isolation forced me to constantly focus on negative thoughts and I saw a significant decrease in my cognitive ability; things I could previously do quickly in high school took a lot longer now. When I entered the fall semester of my sophomore year in college, the coursework really picked up and I saw myself doing poorly on one exam after another; it really took a toll on me and I just became more and more discouraged after each failure. The day I got a 27/100 on an organic chemistry exam was the day that it all went downhill. From this day onward, I don’t feel stress anymore; stress is what previously drove me to get my work done and do well on exams. My brain is preventing me from focusing now because of how discouraged I have become. I spend hours upon hours studying, but I’m never efficient because I don’t feel stress; this has become a cycle and is really taking a toll on me. I can’t seem to figure out what’s wrong with me.

Lately, I've been feeling really isolated from my friends and classmates. It's like we've all grown apart and don't even acknowledge each other anymore. I find it hard to muster up the motivation to connect with others and I often feel sad. This loneliness has been going on for several months now. The only person I feel comfortable talking to is my boyfriend.

I was in a serious relationship for 3 years. We started off as best friends and eventually fell in love. Our relationship was strong and mature, especially considering that it was the first serious relationship for both of us. We faced a lot of challenges and came close to breaking up multiple times, but we always managed to work through it.

Patient: I have been diagnosed with Borderline Personality Disorder and Bipolar Disorder Type II. Recently, my psychiatrist prescribed me a new anti-psychotic called Invega (3 mgs.) to address my distorted thinking, intensified emotions, and daily crying spells. Compared to other more recent anti-psychotics like Seroquel, I am tolerating Invega well, except for the weight gain. Despite my efforts to diet and exercise, I have already gained 5 pounds. Will this side effect lessen as my body adjusts to the medication? If not, should I consider trying older anti-psychotics like Haldol? Do they also cause weight gain? Will these other medications be effective in managing my symptoms? I would appreciate your opinion, as my psychiatrist is unsure about my concerns due to the newness of the medication. Thank you in advance.

Lately, I've been feeling overwhelmed by my friend's depression. I've been trying to support her, but my own anxiety has been getting worse. I've been experiencing self-harming thoughts and feeling suicidal. It's hard for me when she talks about negative things because it triggers something in me. I've tried suggesting that we talk about other topics, but she finds it helpful to discuss her depression. I feel guilty for wanting to distance myself from her, even though I know it's not fair to her. Another important detail is that when I asked for space, she asked me to help her instead of herself. I accepted her apology, but I still haven't fully forgiven her. I'm feeling so conflicted and broken, and I don't know what to do.

I am a single mother from the U.S. who has been raising my 9-year-old son with ADHD on my own since he was born. His father has been largely absent and uninvolved in his life, despite my attempts to get him to help with discipline and teaching responsibility. Two years ago, I met my boyfriend who unfortunately has terminal cancer. While we have a great relationship, we struggle to see eye to eye on how I should raise my son.

I have been struggling with intense feelings of anxiety. Whenever I'm in social situations and people are talking, I can't help but believe that they are discussing and judging me. This constant worry is overwhelming. Additionally, I have difficulty expressing myself verbally, often freezing up when others ask me questions. Making eye contact is also a challenge for me, to the point where I have to consciously force myself to do it.

I hope you can help me understand my self-harming behavior. I'm a 16-year-old girl and I don't really have a reason for doing it. I don't want anyone to find out because it would cause a lot of problems in my family. I do feel insecure about my body, but that's not why I self-harm. I want to know what a professional thinks because I want help, but I can't ask my parents. My older sister and biological father have cluster B personality disorder, but I don't think I have it. Any thoughts from a professional would be great.

I'm a 14-year-old who has been dealing with some concerns lately. I've been feeling guilty and blaming myself for some things that have happened. When I was 13, I had an experience with my dog that lasted only a few seconds before I realized it was wrong and never did it again. I also find myself sometimes looking at people's private parts, but I know it's not right and I try to avoid it because I don't want to harm anyone. I understand that it's normal to be curious during adolescence, but I can't shake off the guilt. Do I have a problem? Should I seek help for these experiences?

I've been feeling really anxious lately. I constantly worry about things going wrong in my life, even when there's no evidence to support those thoughts. It's taking a toll on my daily functioning and I don't know how to stop these anxious thoughts.

As a 3rd year animation student, I've been experiencing some concerning shifts in my mood. Over the past few weeks, I've noticed that I've been going back and forth between severe depression and a kind of mania. While I may have experienced this "high" before, it has never been to this extent, especially during finals season when most people are feeling stressed and down. Instead of feeling the usual depression or stress about my work, I find myself not caring at all. I've been falling behind on assignments and showing up late to class, but it doesn't seem to bother me.
Patient: I've been struggling with a habit of constantly picking at my face. It's become a problem because I do it without even realizing it. I don't understand why I do it or how it started.

I've been feeling really overwhelmed lately. There's so much going on at work and in my personal life, and I just can't seem to keep up. I feel like I'm constantly stressed and on edge. I'm not sure what to do.

As a teenager living in Wales, I've been struggling with constantly imagining a different life that I don't have. This issue has been going on for about five years and it's becoming more noticeable. I find myself daydreaming about being in situations with real-life celebrities or social figures that I admire.

Six months ago, I entered into a relationship with a man who I believe is the man of my dreams. However, there is one challenge - he has a two-year-old daughter. We are living together now and I am struggling to accept his daughter into my life. Before meeting me, he had a brief dating period with his daughter's mother and she became pregnant. Although they tried to make it work, it didn't. My partner is fully committed to his daughter and has assured me that he will always be there for her. However, I feel resentment towards him and his past mistake. Whenever his daughter is around, I become physically ill and it reminds me of him and his ex. I worry about what it means for our future if I can't fully accept his daughter and fear that I will always hold onto this resentment. I feel a mix of emotions - hurt, frustration, sadness, anger, and overwhelm. My partner is supportive and listens to me, but I know that my feelings are hurting him and he wishes I felt differently. I want to be able to embrace his daughter and be more understanding, but I am constantly angry.

Over the past 4 years, I have been in a relationship with my fiancé who has been previously married and has a child from his previous marriage. We also have a child together and function well as a family unit. However, we are facing escalating issues in our relationship. I feel that he lacks respect for me and becomes verbally abusive when our children are not around. He has attributed his behavior to dissatisfaction with our sex life, but even when I make an effort to improve it, his behavior reverts back to the same pattern. I love him and value his role as a father, but I'm starting to feel resentful and avoid him to avoid confrontation. I don't want to break up our family, but I'm unsure of what to do.

I was raised in a religious household and have been struggling with a belief that I am being possessed. It may sound strange, but this feeling feels very real to me. Starting from my early adolescence, I frequently experience visits from an evil presence while I am asleep. During these episodes, I feel frozen in fear as the presence tries to enter me and speaks to me, threatening me with unspeakable things. As a child, my mother would take me to church for deliverance prayers, but unfortunately, the experiences persisted even though I eventually told her they stopped. Recently, I shared with my psychologist about the sexual contact I had with three men between the ages of 6 and 15. He believes that these possession episodes are actually flashbacks to those traumatic experiences. I want to believe him, but I'm scared. It has been incredibly challenging for me to process the memories of those childhood experiences due to the shame and guilt I feel for being so needy and even enjoying the attention. I can't help but feel like God is punishing me.

I have been diagnosed with panic disorder and have been managing it through various techniques such as kundalini yoga and self-talk during panic attacks. However, recently I have been experiencing increased fear about developing a psychotic illness, specifically during a panic attack. I am worried about having a psychotic break.

My mom has been experiencing bipolar mania for several years, with episodes occurring 1-3 times per year. We've tried setting up doctor appointments, but she always cancels them and is in major denial about her condition. Given her age of 71, we're concerned about the toll these episodes are taking on her body. Is there any way to compel her to seek help? How should we approach her about it, especially when she's in denial? Should we wait until she's not in a manic state to have the conversation? We're feeling desperate and don't know what to do anymore.

I recently found myself in a unique situation where I developed romantic feelings for my therapist after completing therapy. We both have carefully considered and consensual intentions, but I'm struggling to find resources or guidelines for navigating this rare scenario. Do you have any recommendations or insights?

The other day my family and I were out at a restaurant, and this child in the booth behind us kept screaming and yelling and wouldn’t stop. Around the third time he yelled I had an image flash in my head of me strangling and then cutting up the child. I felt an immense anger for some 5 seconds. Then after that, the thought faded and I was very emotionally detached for the rest of the dinner. I felt no emotion whatsoever and said nothing. I had no urges to do anything but sit and stare at the table. I don’t know why I had such a violent thought, or strange feeling after. I did not act on my thought (just to be clear). (From the USA)

I've been feeling really preoccupied with my boyfriend's past. Recently, I found out that he was married before and he never told me about it. Instead of discussing it with him, I kept my feelings to myself and bottled them up. Now, it seems like this issue comes up constantly - either in conversations or when he mentions something related to his past. I also find myself ruminating about it in my mind.

I'm a 15-year-old dealing with depression, and it's starting to impact my school performance and daily functioning. My parents are divorced, and currently, I spend more time with my mom, who has more control over my life. I tried talking to her about my depression a few months ago, but she dismissed it as typical teenage behavior. She believes I should solve my problems on my own and not rely on therapy. I feel trapped and unable to seek help. My grades are suffering, and the only thing keeping me going is my friends who need me. I'm reaching a breaking point, and I truly believe that therapy or medication is necessary for me to continue. Unfortunately, I can't access either of them because of my current situation. I don't know what to do, please help.

I've been in a relationship with a woman for the past few months. However, before we started dating, she was in a relationship with another woman for about two years. We actually dated briefly before she got together with her previous partner, but things didn't work out at the time.

Recently, I confessed to my parents that I used to play Grand Theft Auto V (GTAV) at a friend's house without their permission for three years. They didn't get too angry, but they told me I couldn't play it anymore. The problem is, now that I've stopped playing, I feel a strong need to play it again. No other game can replace it, and I feel unhappy and unfulfilled. Video games used to be an easy way for me to cope with life. I'm not interested in the mature content of GTAV, but I can't find the same enjoyment in other games. I've done research and believe I'm not a psychopath or narcissist. However, there was one scene in the game involving torture that I found difficult to get through. I've already completed everything in the game and seen similar content in movies and TV shows, so I feel like I've seen it all. My parents are worried about potential negative effects, but I'm experiencing feelings of depression and sadness since I stopped playing. I would really appreciate your help. Thank you! (From Sweden)

When I was a child, I experienced multiple instances of sexual abuse by my older brother who is six years older than me. These incidents occurred when I was six, ten, and sixteen years old. I have no other siblings, and my parents did not seek therapy or support for me following these traumatic experiences.

I'm really struggling with my sister. It seems like she has some underlying mental issues because she acts completely irrational and doesn't accept any rational help. She becomes extremely rude and vile if she doesn't get immediate solutions to her problems. I've tried different approaches, from being angry and yelling to being calmer. But no matter what, she responds with rude remarks and doesn't seem to understand that her behavior affects my ability to help her. She also doesn't seem to learn from her experiences, repeating the same actions despite being punished. I'm worried about her and unsure of how to handle the situation.

I've been receiving feedback from people about my depression for as long as I can remember. Back in my teenage years, I tried counseling because I was concerned about my inability to make friends and establish emotional connections with others. Despite being on medication for depression now, I still struggle with these issues. The only change I've noticed is that I'm now able to put into words what feels off.

I'm a seventeen-year-old student who has been struggling with self-harm and depression for the past two years. It's been really difficult for me, and both my parents and friends are concerned about my well-being. Recently, I was diagnosed with major depression, and it's been overwhelming. My therapist has recommended inpatient treatment because I'm having trouble taking care of myself. I'm scared of being locked away forever and don't fully understand how inpatient treatment works. I'm also hesitant about starting medication since I've never been on it before.

Patient: I've recently had my first child, and my relationship with the baby's father has been a roller coaster. We're currently spending time apart, but he keeps trying to get me and our son to spend time with him and his daughter from a previous relationship. I'm struggling with this and finding myself resenting his daughter. I feel horrible about it, but I feel like he's there for her more than he is for me and our 5-month-old. He provides financial support to her mother as ordered by the court and buys everything she needs, while her mother parties. On the other hand, I have to constantly beg and complain to get his support. I even had to ask him to pay me back for money I lent him in the past. My feelings about him and our relationship are unclear, and I also find myself not wanting anything to do with his daughter. It tears me up inside to feel this way. Additionally, I might be pregnant with his second child, but I'm scared because I had a difficult experience with my first pregnancy and had a c-section. I'm not sure if I'm mentally strong enough to go through another pregnancy. I'm doing a lot of this on my own with minimal support from the father and only my family's support. Despite his infidelity, destruction of my belongings, name-calling, and sending me pictures of other women, he acts like nothing is wrong. I'm currently living with my family, and I feel guilty for not making an effort for my son to spend time with his sister when she's with her father. However, I also find myself resentful towards his daughter. I'm also worried about our living situation. My son is growing so fast, and we don't have a suitable environment for him to have his own room and be in a kid-friendly space. I would have looked for a place sooner, but I thought we were going to live with the father. However, his house is unsafe with broken glass and no heat. I'm tired of cleaning up after him.

I've been feeling really frustrated and defeated lately. It seems like no matter what I do, my parents never believe in me or support my relationship. I've put so much effort into gaining their approval, but it's always the opposite of what I hoped for.

Over the past year, I have been experiencing intense emotions and difficulties in regulating my emotions. I am feeling scared of other people and have a fear of abandonment. I have always felt different, but recently I have become more isolated and disengaged from others. I find myself going to school and coming straight home, unable to be myself at school and pretending to be an asocial and isolated person. I hate living like this, but I feel like I have no other choice. I constantly feel empty and impulsive, sometimes making expensive purchases without thinking. My life feels purposeless now that my teacher is no longer my teacher, and I have closed myself off from both boys and girls. I really need to talk to someone, but I fear that they will despise me. I don't understand why I am behaving this way. What is wrong with me?

I have been married to a woman for thirty-two years, and I have been struggling with some serious issues in our relationship. One major concern is her lack of empathy, sympathy, and understanding towards not only me but also her friends. She tends to be a fair-weather friend, only there for people when it's convenient for her. I've witnessed her abandoning friends in need without any explanation or support. Additionally, when I was ill for nine months and unable to work, she consulted a lawyer and tried to have me thrown out of the house. Whenever I try to address marital issues, she becomes defensive, angry, and even vicious. It feels like I can't bring up any problems without facing her wrath. Lastly, she displayed a disturbing lack of remorse and was cruel to our little dog.

As a teenager in the U.S., I have been struggling with emotional difficulties since I was in third grade. At that time, I started attending a new school and found it challenging to fit in. I began experiencing frequent breakdowns and felt isolated from my peers. As a coping mechanism, I engaged in questionable behaviors, like sacrificing worms, which I now understand may have been influenced by my childhood nature.

Lately, I've been feeling really lonely and ignored by people. It seems like no matter how friendly I try to be at work or in social situations, people just ignore me. Even when I say hello to someone in the hallway at work, they look right through me and continue walking. It's really taking a toll on my self-esteem and making me feel incredibly isolated.

Lately, I've been feeling incredibly overwhelmed and down, especially when it comes to myself. Whenever someone says something negative about me, I feel an overwhelming sense of guilt and end up bursting into tears either in the moment or later when I'm alone. I find myself constantly worrying about everything, even things that are beyond my control. Last night, I resorted to self-harm for the first time. I had been thinking about it for a while and, to be honest, it provided some relief. I'm concerned, but I don't feel comfortable discussing this with my mom. She already has a lot on her plate with my two brothers, who both have their own issues and are seeing therapists, which is a financial strain for us. Additionally, she is seeing a therapist herself. On top of all this, my dad is getting remarried to a woman who has strong Catholic beliefs, while I consider myself agnostic and my brothers are atheists. They have four other children, and we recently moved into their house. Now, my mom is fighting for full custody, which has only escalated the tension. I'm also in a demanding school program, and I constantly worry about my grades and whether I've completed all my assignments, even when I know I have. I just feel lost and don't know what to do anymore.

Hello. Lately, I've been feeling concerned about my mental state and wondering if I might be experiencing symptoms of psychosis. I've been diagnosed with Borderline Personality Disorder, but the symptoms I'm currently experiencing don't seem to align with the usual signs of that disorder.

For the past 10 years, I have been struggling with panic attacks, but recently they have become much worse. I find it increasingly difficult to cope with them. On top of that, I have severe health anxiety. My heart seems to beat fast for no apparent reason, which has led me to believe that I have A fib. Despite undergoing various medical tests like a month-long heart monitor, stress echo, and EKGs, the results only show premature beats. However, I can't seem to let go of my belief and it's really impacting my life. Now, I'm unable to distinguish if my heart is racing first or if I'm experiencing anxiety first. I've been trying to get an appointment with a mental health professional, but haven't been successful yet. Any advice on what I should do? I'm constantly obsessing over this, checking my pulse repeatedly, and any slight increase in heart rate triggers a state of panic. I feel like I'm living in misery.

Patient: I'm feeling overwhelmed and unsure of where to start. My everyday life feels like a long story, and I think it all begins with my family. There's been neglect and emotional and physical abuse from my siblings.
I am really worried about my mother's mental health. She's only 36 years old and I'm 19, the oldest of her children. I've noticed some concerning behavior from her lately and I'm not sure what to do.

I've been feeling incredibly overwhelmed and isolated lately. My friends and family are too emotionally involved to provide unbiased support. I'm supposed to get married in 11 days, but I've had doubts and dread throughout my entire relationship. It feels like I'm planning my own death instead of my wedding. The thought of the wedding makes me physically sick. I mustered up the courage to suggest postponing the wedding due to the immense stress and pressure I'm feeling, but my fiance responded by saying if I have doubts, we should end the relationship altogether.

For years, I have felt a strong dislike towards my sister. There are certain behaviors of hers that really bother me. My parents went through a divorce, and my sister and I live with our mother. My mother had surgery a few years ago due to stress. I take on a lot of responsibilities at home, such as fixing things around the house and being there for my family. I work hard and don't ask for much, and I try to show respect to others. However, my mother has asked me not to yell at my sister or tell her what to do, and she can't discipline her either because she's afraid it will negatively impact her health. I feel stuck because I don't want to add more stress to my mother's life, so my sister gets away with doing whatever she wants.

I've been experiencing some concerning changes in my emotions lately. Over the past year, I've noticed that my feelings have become duller. I don't seem to feel remorse when I hurt others emotionally or physically, and recently I had an intense urge to harm my sister with a hammer. Instead of feeling guilty, I felt a rush of adrenaline. I've also noticed that the line between fear and excitement has become blurred for me. I'm also a sadomasochist, finding pleasure in both giving and receiving pain. While I do experience emotions like crying, anger, and laughter, they often seem to be self-centered. I can also put on a facade of being nice, and it's difficult for others to see my true intentions. Although I'm still a teenager, I'm worried that these aspects of myself will consume me as I approach 18.

I am a 16-year-old who is struggling with intense feelings of guilt and regret surrounding three incidents from my childhood. When I was 9 years old, I engaged in some inappropriate behavior with my cousin sister, who was 6 at the time. We were playing doctor and I inspected her private parts. Then, when I was 10 or 11, we played a game where we pretended to breastfeed as part of a mother-child roleplay. I am worried that she might tell her mom and blame me, leading to potential legal consequences and being labeled as an abuser.

My former step-son has been exhibiting concerning behaviors and I'm worried about his mental health. He has a borderline developmental delay, ADHD (although he's currently not taking medication for it), and is bipolar. He has been experiencing hallucinations but chooses to ignore them. He is currently on probation for a crime that I believe he didn't commit. During a recent polygraph, he admitted to something that I know didn't happen. Why does he keep admitting to things he didn't do and imagining scenarios that never occurred?

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for a couple of years now, and recently we started dating. However, my mom seems to think that being with him has made me depressed, even though I am actually really happy. It has become a problem because she doesn't want me spending time with him or attending his family activities. She doesn't seem to be happy for me and refuses to accept our relationship. She has imposed restrictions on when my boyfriend can come over, unlike my friends who can visit at any time. My boyfriend doesn't want to come to my house anymore because of how my mom treats him. I've reached a point where I am considering moving out because of her controlling behavior, but I don't know how to talk to her about it. I'm afraid she will react negatively and try to take away my belongings. I feel torn between my family and my boyfriend, but I see a future with him. I'm really unsure about what is the right decision.

Over the past three years, I have been working closely with an incredibly supportive therapist who has been instrumental in helping me navigate my journey as a transgender and gay individual. He has provided guidance and support as I came out and gained the confidence to explore dating and relationships. Recently, I started seeing a wonderful person who is also transgender and gay, only to discover that we share the same therapist. Given that my therapist is open about his queer identity and works with many queer clients, it's not entirely surprising. However, as I become more socially active and encounter new people in bars and parties, I anticipate running into my therapist more frequently.

Lately, I've been noticing some concerning symptoms that resemble those of schizophrenia. I've been having hallucinations and mainly delusions. I frequently see a figure following me and shadows around me. My delusions include the belief that nothing around me is real, that everyone hates me, and that something or someone is out to harm me, even if it's not alive. I also experience thoughts that feel like they're coming from someone else, and I have no control over my thoughts or my own actions. My thoughts are disorganized, and I have difficulty speaking coherently, even though I don't have any speech problems. Expressing my emotions is also a struggle, and at times, it feels like I can't even feel them. Performing even simple tasks feels overwhelming, and there are many more symptoms I could mention. I have been diagnosed with depression, but I'm also concerned that I may have anxiety. I apologize for any language errors and the disorganization of my message.

I want to start by acknowledging that my parents are genuinely good people who have always had my best interests at heart. They have always been there for me during my struggles with depression and anxiety, and I am grateful for their support. However, recently their efforts to help me have inadvertently been making things worse for me. It feels like they don't truly understand me, despite their best intentions.

I have been experiencing some concerning thoughts and feelings lately. Sometimes I feel like I have two different sides to me, and it's starting to worry me. I have moments where I feel a strong urge to harm someone, and it feels like something takes control of me. I don't want to act on these urges, but I'm afraid that I may lose control someday. I've also noticed that I don't feel empathy or guilt, which I've read is similar to psychopaths. However, I do experience fear, particularly about how my family will react if they find out who I truly am. I've been pretending to be someone I'm not for a long time, and I'm scared to see a therapist because I don't know if I can keep up the facade. I don't want to end up in a mental hospital for the rest of my life. I hoped these feelings would go away on their own, but they seem to be getting stronger the more I ignore them. Can you please assure me that I'm not crazy?

Hi, I’ve been experiencing some issues with my perception of time and emotions for the past 4 months. It feels like everything is moving too quickly and I struggle to comprehend things, like words on boards. I also feel emotionally numb, where I can laugh but not really feel anything. I've been diagnosed with depersonalization, but I'm not sure if these other symptoms are related to that or something else. Can you help?
I have been struggling with my romantic connections with women and find myself more attracted to men, even though it may not be a sexual attraction. I'm unsure about my sexual orientation.

Over the past six months, I have been working with my therapist to address the trauma I experienced from sexual abuse during my childhood, teenage years, and adulthood. I have never had a strong interest in sex and recently ended an abusive relationship. Since I first met my therapist, I have felt a deep connection with her and have found her attractive. However, I understand that there are professional boundaries and laws in place. Lately, I have been having sexual fantasies about her, where initially she resists my advances but then it turns into a consensual encounter. These fantasies have become intense and I have even masturbated to them. I realize that this is not a real relationship and it feels strange to have these fantasies, but at the same time, they provide me with some comfort and a break from my current circumstances. I am unsure of what to do with these feelings and whether it is healthy to continue having these fantasies.

I've been struggling with depression for as long as I can remember. It began long before I sought help at the age of 16. Currently, I am in a committed relationship with my fiancée of six and a half years. We own a house together.

Lately, I've been experiencing a lot of anger. It seems like every day I wake up already feeling angry, and even if nothing major happens, something small can set me off for the entire day. Sometimes, I find myself getting upset about things that happened years ago. It's like I'm constantly on edge and irritated by every little thing.

Hello, I'm a 17-year-old girl living in Hong Kong. Last year, I was feeling extremely stressed, so I decided to seek help from a psychologist who diagnosed me with adjustment disorder. I've been taking medication and have noticed some improvements, such as experiencing fewer headaches. However, I've started to suspect that I may also have dependent personality disorder. I feel helpless and believe that I will never be able to overcome these feelings. I did some research on Wikipedia and found that dependent personality disorder is often linked to adjustment disorder. I struggle with decision making and always rely on others to make choices for me, like my mom deciding which school and college I should attend, as well as which subjects to study. Since primary school, I've always leaned on one friend and feel anxious and helpless when I'm alone. I find it difficult to say no or be independent because I constantly need to rely on others. I feel lost and unsure about what to do with my life. Additionally, I still live with my mom, and she tends to make decisions and define my life for me. I feel trapped and unable to break free from her influence.

I've been feeling really down lately and it's hard for me to determine if it's just normal teenage moodiness or if I might actually have depression. I've taken some online surveys, like the SanityScore one, and they all indicate that I have "Severe Depression." But I'm still skeptical because sometimes I think I'm just overreacting. I have extreme mood swings, feelings of hopelessness and worthlessness, and a sense of being out of control in my life. But then I also feel guilty because I think there are people who have it worse than I do. I want to talk to my mom about it, but I'm afraid of her judgment. I wrote her a letter but haven't given it to her yet. Any advice?

I have been experiencing disturbing thoughts of harming others and myself for a while now. These thoughts have become more intense since I turned 14. I feel scared and overwhelmed because I find myself wanting to inflict harm on others, even thinking about torturing them. I also have thoughts of hurting myself in painful ways. I understand that these thoughts are not normal or right, but they are becoming harder to ignore. I tried talking to my parents about it, but they are afraid of the consequences and won't let me see a therapist. I'm feeling lost and don't know what to do.

I recently met someone on an online gaming platform, Playstation 3. We've been chatting and connecting on a personal level. However, when I searched for information about him online, I discovered several newspaper articles describing his involvement in car thefts and other offenses. Despite this, I chose to ignore these red flags because his words and our connection made me feel really good.

My family and I have noticed concerning behavior in our mother that leads us to believe she may be experiencing bipolar disorder. She exhibits combative behavior and seems emotionally unstable. Additionally, she has been excessively spending money, leading to financial difficulties, including a past bankruptcy. Currently, they are living in a small mobile home that my brothers and I purchased for them, relying on my stepfather's Social Security checks. Unfortunately, they do not have medical insurance, which poses a problem. She is inconsistently taking her medications, including those for other health issues like gout, blood pressure, cholesterol, and Polymyositis.

Since I was young, I have always struggled with feeling comfortable with giving and receiving affection. It hasn't been an issue for me until recently, when I started dating my girlfriend. She is a very affectionate and supportive person, and while I appreciate her affection, I worry that I'm not reciprocating it enough.

Lately, I've been experiencing some distressing symptoms. I've been having visual and auditory hallucinations that others around me don't seem to perceive. Additionally, I've been struggling with memory loss, finding it difficult to recall even simple details like what I ate for breakfast or my test grades. I've also noticed that I lack motivation to complete everyday tasks. The most concerning aspect is that I've been having intrusive thoughts that don't feel like they originate from me. These concerns have made me worried about my mental well-being. However, the biggest obstacle I face is not knowing how to approach my parents about these issues. I fear that my dad would belittle me and not take me seriously, as he often does when I seek his help. I'm at a loss as to who to turn to or how to access professional help without involving my dad.

I began therapy about 9 months ago due to my struggles with anxiety. Through therapy, my anxiety has improved significantly. However, a few months ago, I experienced a severe bout of depression. I reached a point where I made specific plans for suicide. Although I am feeling better now, I still have a consistently low mood, lack energy, and have gained weight. I'm concerned that I may not fully recover from this depressive episode and that it has caused irreversible damage to my brain. Therapy doesn't seem to be helping with my current mood, and sometimes analyzing things in therapy actually makes things worse.

I was in a relationship for two years that had its challenges but also had moments of fulfillment. In the second year, my partner was diagnosed with severe depression, which had likely been present for some time. This diagnosis led to a breakdown, where he became emotionally aggressive and cruel towards me. I felt abused and ended up experiencing my own health problems as a result. I sought therapy for myself, and after 10 months, I decided to leave our shared living space to focus on my own recovery. Surprisingly, he chose to end the relationship and cut off all contact, which brought me relief despite my love for him. I spent a year living without him, focusing on my own healing, and found happiness through dating and a fulfilling job. However, I can't shake the feeling that I've lost the opportunity to grow old with someone I truly loved.

Lately, I've been experiencing some disturbing thoughts and fantasies that involve violence and sexual desires. These thoughts have become more intense and I find myself imagining scenarios that involve harm to others. I've also been feeling a strong urge to commit murder, especially when someone angers me. As a result, I've distanced myself from people and I struggle to be around them at work, even though my job requires interaction.

I don’t think I have the right to be sad because my life is great compared to most but I don’t feel happy. I have no one to talk to and I feel like my mind is just full with different problems. I don’t go to regular school because I constantly feel like I don’t fit in or my self esteem gets in the way.. I’m confused with what is wrong with me or if there is even anything wrong with me. I have almost no friends and keep alienating myself from others even when I feel sad and lonely after. I have tried to talk to my mom about it but she brushed it off. what do you think?
I'm a teenage female and when I'm at home, I always wear shorts. A while ago, I noticed that my father used to stare at my legs, particularly my thighs. However, lately, he doesn't do that anymore.

I'm a teenager in Indonesia and I'm really concerned about my sister who is turning 21 this year. She has been displaying some strange behavior. For example, when she is upset about something, she becomes quiet and avoids talking to anyone for a couple of days. Then, out of nowhere, she starts laughing and then crying. I don't know how to handle this because she won't open up to me. It's starting to affect my own mental health because her actions are confusing and frustrating me. I suggested to my mom that we should see a psychiatrist, but she didn't take it seriously. This is making me feel depressed. Thank you for listening to me.

Hello, I'm a 12-year-old from the United States. Lately, I've been experiencing intense interests that last longer than my previous ones, which usually only last a few days or months. I'm not sure if this is related to Asperger's or something else. I don't mean to offend or diagnose myself, but I think I may have Asperger's. While it doesn't bother me too much, I would like to get a proper diagnosis.

I recently had a heated argument with my teenage son, and I must admit that I didn't handle it well. I allowed my anger to get the best of me, and I ended up shouting at him. In the heat of the moment, I told him to stay at his grandmother's house until he learned some manners. However, I'm finding it difficult to cope with the fact that his grandmother and my brother have taken his side and are spoiling him by taking him on shopping sprees, spending a significant amount of money on him.

I've been in a relationship with my now husband for the past 15 years, and it has been quite tumultuous due to his trust issues. However, we recently got back together and are now engaged. We also have a child together.

I have been experiencing intense internal turmoil and uncontrollable urges to engage in bizarre movements, nonsensical language, and grimaces when I am alone. Despite my efforts to maintain control in public, there are times when I cannot hold back and it feels like something else is taking over my body. I am fully aware of my actions and my surroundings, but I am unable to regain control. Unfortunately, my therapists and psychiatrist do not believe me and dismiss my concerns. It's frustrating because I don't know how to convince them to take me seriously. Lately, I have even considered hurting myself just to prove the seriousness of my situation, although I recognize that it seems irrational. Can you offer any insight into what might be happening and provide advice on how to address this?

I have been experiencing distressing daydreams lately that involve me being physically punished by an authority figure and forced into sexual situations. These daydreams have become obsessive and have caused me to lose interest in my hobbies. What concerns me is that I actually enjoy these daydreams and sometimes even wish they would happen in real life. They are starting to affect my ability to focus at work and while driving. I am 45 years old and have been diagnosed with Schizoaffective disorder since my 20s. I've noticed that these daydreams often precede the onset of auditory hallucinations, which usually occur about 1 or 2 weeks later. I am currently taking my medication as prescribed. Additionally, I am dealing with increased stress due to a bankruptcy. My question is, why do I experience these daydreams and how can I prevent them from escalating to the point of needing hospitalization? Thank you for taking the time to address my concerns.

Ever since I was about eight or nine, I've always had this intense desire to have a mental disorder. It's like a constant need for validation or attention. I find myself trying to convince myself and others that I have a mental disorder. I spend hours researching and analyzing every little symptom, hoping to find something that fits. It's becoming overwhelming and it's starting to hurt.

I'm really concerned about my half-brother. He's 46 years old and has always been a sensitive and caring person since we were kids. However, in the past seven years or so, he has developed a problem with alcohol. I think he drinks every day, maybe a six-pack each night. He also smokes marijuana.

I've been experiencing some intense and disturbing thoughts lately, and I'm not sure how to categorize them. I don't have any diagnosed mental illnesses, and I come from a loving and stable family. But for about a year now, I've had this curiosity or desire to experience pure hatred directed towards me. I have thoughts of wanting to kill someone just to witness their family grieving, and I even have thoughts of wanting to torture someone, although I can't imagine myself actually doing it. It's like a strong craving that lingers in the back of my mind. I don't know what to do about it or if I should be concerned. I'm seeking advice on how to handle this.

Hi, I am 19 years old and my girlfriend is 17 years old. We have been in a committed relationship for over a year and have recently encountered a serious issue. We were sexually active for about five months, but three months ago, we stopped having sex because my girlfriend became scared. We always practiced safe sex, using condoms and withdrawal. She was worried about a possible pregnancy and even though we took two home pregnancy tests which came out negative, she still believes she might be pregnant despite having no pregnancy symptoms.

During a conversation with my long-term girlfriend, who is also 23 years old, we started discussing our experiences and knowledge about sex. She shared that her mother had a unique approach to discussing sex education with her and her brother. Instead of having separate conversations, her mom chose to have "the talk" with both of them at the same time.

My husband and I are both nurses. We have two sons. Our oldest will turn five in May and our second son will turn one in April. My husband works full time while I stay home with the kids. Tonight, I caught our 4-year-old wearing my thong underwear under his pajamas. It turns out, he stashed some of my underwear in his room along with two of my Victoria’s Secret catalogs. We talked to him about this. I have always noticed evidence of what Freud calls the oedipal complex in my son. He is a smart boy and has adapted quite well to his new role as big brother. He has said “why did God not make me into a girl” but when I explore this, it turns out that what he really means is that he likes girls, including mommy because girls are pretty. I have never seen any other “feminine” tendencies in him (he’ll say pink is for girls and refuse to ride a Barbie bike) but I just want to make sure that this is just a normal phase for him and we shouldn’t be thinking about gender issues here. I imagine a 4 year old won’t see this as a social taboo although it would be a different situation in an older kid. Please share your views about this situation. Thank you very much.

Lately, I've been experiencing a lot of distressing emotions and thoughts. I feel guilty, depressed, and overwhelmed. I find myself doubting everyone, including myself, and I fear losing control. Sometimes I have intrusive thoughts that make me feel even more guilty. It's gotten to the point where I question the reality of the world and wonder if I'm dreaming. I'm constantly paranoid, thinking people are talking about me and staring at me. Trusting others has become really difficult. My moods are all over the place, going from happy and cheerful to angry and depressed. I even have moments where I feel hateful and dislike everyone. I've started to believe that pain is a way to alleviate my guilt. On top of that, I feel like there's someone living inside my mind, watching and judging me. It terrifies me because I can't act normally, thinking this person is mocking me. I'm exhausted and desperate for rest, but I can't seem to find it. I love my family so much, but because of my mood swings and mental state, I've been mean to them. It fills me with guilt to the point where I've had thoughts of suicide. I don't know what to do to get better.

I have been going through a difficult time in my relationship. My boyfriend and I have decided to break up next week, and we want to end things on good terms. However, there have been some concerning incidents that have made me question his feelings for me. One day, while discussing our breakup, he suddenly mentioned that he still loves the girl he was courting before me. He initially said it seriously, but then claimed it was a joke. I'm unsure if I should believe him, especially because I've had dreams about him cheating on me. It's been bothering me a lot lately.

My daughter used to excel in competitive Irish dance, consistently winning from ages 8-12. However, as she reached the highest level in the sport, her performance has declined. This has affected her confidence and she no longer has the drive to compete. While she has the natural talent to succeed, she is reluctant to put in the necessary effort to compete against girls at her level. I'm unsure if it's due to laziness or fear of putting in the work and still not achieving top results. Presently, she still performs well but doesn't place within the top 3 as she used to.

I'm currently in a very happy and otherwise healthy, long-term romantic relationship for the first time in my life. It took me until I was 19 to find my first best friend. I'm an ENFP and she's an INFJ. We come from very different backgrounds.
