I would never, ever consider doing anything like that in real life, but is this something I should be concerned about?

I experienced sexual abuse during my childhood, and about a year ago, I was diagnosed with clinical depression. I used to struggle with intense anger issues, often snapping or having emotional breakdowns. While these outbursts have become less frequent, I still engage in self-harm when I'm in a depressive state.

I've been struggling with my body image and eating habits. I feel really sensitive about my weight and how much I eat. There are times when I end up binge eating. Even though I'm within a "healthy" weight range, I have this desire to be thinner because my husband prefers slim women.

"I've been feeling really down lately. I constantly have this empty and numb feeling inside of me. It's like I've lost interest in everything and everyone. I've even started cutting myself, but I'm trying to stop."

I recently went through a highly contentious divorce with an abusive spouse. Throughout the marriage, I experienced emotional abuse, manipulation, and control tactics. My ex-spouse even took our son away for a period of time, using my mental health as an excuse. I have decided to cut off contact with my parents because they have been supportive of my ex-spouse. The abuse escalated during the divorce process, with my ex-spouse using tracking devices and invading my privacy. I was constantly gaslighted and berated.

Last night something really alarming happened to me that I've never experienced before. My boyfriend and I were in my car and I was feeling extremely angry and frustrated with him. It's important to note that the day before, I had a really difficult time and almost broke up with him. As my stress and agitation escalated, he tried to calm me down and I suddenly started feeling lightheaded. Eventually, I lost the ability to move and felt completely devoid of any emotions. I couldn't even speak. Even my boyfriend commented that I looked lifeless. It took me about two hours to slowly regain movement and speech. I remember being able to see and hear everything, but I felt completely paralyzed. I became really scared and started crying, and my boyfriend suggested that perhaps my body shut down as a way to protect me from feeling any more emotional distress. I can't help but wonder if there's a deeper meaning to this experience, like if it was a sign from a higher power to finally find some peace. Can you provide some insight or answers?

I'm really concerned about my dad. He's been showing signs of severe depression and has been making alarming statements about wanting to end his life. He's become very isolated and refuses to seek help. He constantly belittles himself and spends most of his time alone or complaining about life. I feel lost and unsure of how to help him. Can you please provide some guidance?

I've been struggling with my relationship with my mom lately. I find myself blaming her for a lot of our problems. She tends to overwhelm me by constantly relying on me to take care of my younger siblings and using me as a source of advice and support. It's become exhausting and I feel like she doesn't fully recognize or appreciate the responsibilities I've taken on. Furthermore, she often makes accusations and claims that I find hurtful and untrue. It's difficult for me to navigate these dynamics and I'm not sure how to handle my emotions.

I'm not really sure if I will get a response, but I need some sort of answer and I refuse to go to a clinic. Ever since my 16th birthday, I've developed strange urges. These urges range from wanting to hurt people and animals to wanting to convince everyone that they are wrong about everything and that nothing they do is worth their time. Now I know this might seem harmless, but I'm 20 now, and slowly but surely the urges have gotten worse. I usually have one episode per year, and I'm concerned. Last year, I actively went searching for an animal to kill and bludgeoned an opossum to death with a pipe. I'm not sure if I should seek help or if I should convince myself that it's all in my head. Please, I need an answer.

I decided to see a private therapist for the first time today because I have been feeling overwhelmed and struggling with my mental health. After the session, I couldn't help but feel like it was pointless. This made me question today's experience because my previous sessions with a school psychologist were incredibly helpful and professional.
I have been dealing with depression for as long as I can remember. However, at the beginning of this year, I experienced a traumatic event that intensified my symptoms and made my anxiety unbearable.

Patient's Statement (Rewritten): I have two sons, one who is 17 and another who is 19. My younger son has been struggling with learning disabilities throughout school and had to attend a school far away from our town. He is now a senior in high school and doesn't have many friends locally. On the other hand, my older son has always excelled in school and has a strong social circle. He spends a lot of time with his friends, which makes my younger son feel lonely and depressed. We have talked to my older son about spending time with his brother, but he hasn't made the effort. I don't want to force him and create animosity between them. How should we approach this situation?

Lately, I've been feeling lost and overwhelmed in life. I've noticed that I often experience intense emotions like rage, anger, and hatred towards others, even when there doesn't seem to be a specific reason. It's a stark contrast to how I used to be as a child - someone who was light-hearted and always willing to help others. Now, when I look at myself in the mirror, I see a monster filled with so much rage that it feels like I could spit fire. I really want to find a way to stop feeling this way.

I have been struggling to find effective treatment for my PTSD, and I have started to question if my lack of progress is due to my own beliefs. While I trust and respect my therapist, I have serious doubts about the effectiveness of EMDR. I have tried it multiple times, done extensive research, and it feels like a secular form of confession with rituals. As a scientist, I wonder why we don't compare fMRI scans of EMDR and REM sleep if it simulates REM. I have been trying to stay open-minded, but it has been disappointing to not experience the miraculous results I've read about.

Before this incident, I considered myself mentally healthy. I was facing challenges with my libido, erectile dysfunction, and sexual arousal. In an attempt to address these issues, I decided to try a small dose of Bremelanotide (PT-141), which is not approved by the FDA.

Over the past few months, I've been struggling with a lot of difficult experiences. I've had arguments with my mom, had to say goodbye to my beloved dog, and ended up in a class with a really challenging teacher. These things have taken a toll on my mental health and I've noticed that I've been feeling worse than ever before. I've even started having thoughts about self-harm, which I used to find ridiculous. My emotions have been all over the place, with frequent breakdowns and sudden bouts of crying. I've also been through two terrible relationships, one involving sexual coercion and the other where my partner left me for someone else and blamed me for the relationship failing. On top of that, my mom's behavior towards me has been inconsistent, going from being nice to ridiculing and ignoring me. It has really affected my already low self-esteem. To make matters worse, my teacher at school is not supportive and makes me feel anxious and unwanted. I've been trying to drop the class, but my principal hasn't responded to my emails. I want to seek help, but part of me feels like I don't deserve it. I've been trying to resist the urges to harm myself, but they've been getting stronger. I haven't been experiencing any positive emotions lately, but I find myself smiling when others are around, even when I don't want to. I'm really unhappy with the way I am right now and I want to get better, but I'm worried about causing trouble for others.

Since getting married in July, my husband has been struggling with alcohol issues. Although we have addressed his drinking in the past, it has caused me severe anxiety. Just four months ago, he drove home drunk from a co-worker's house, which has made it difficult for me to trust that he has truly changed.

Hello, I'm really struggling with my feelings towards my stepdaughter and I need help. I've been with my husband for 5 years and my stepdaughter is now 11 years old. Over the past couple of years, she has been displaying disrespectful and lazy behavior. We tried various approaches to discipline and teach her empathy, but nothing seems to work. We even had her tested and she was diagnosed with Oppositional Defiant Disorder (ODD), but her mom is resistant to considering medication or alternative treatments. My husband has no legal say in her medical treatment until she is 16. Recently, she has been coming between my husband and me when he shows me affection, and we had to address this behavior. She also told her grandma that she is scared of me, which caused a big argument. When we confronted her about it, she said she was joking. She has a history of making cruel remarks about her stepdad as well. Her behavior has been challenging and she often competes with me for her father's attention. I find myself hating and detesting her, which is difficult for me because I generally love children. Therapy is not an option due to her mom's disapproval. How can I overcome these negative feelings towards my stepdaughter?

Lately, I've been experiencing intrusive thoughts about physically harming others. These thoughts involve graphic details and urges to inflict pain on random people. I also hear voices urging me to kill and have brief delusions of acting on these thoughts. I'm also reflecting on my childhood, where I would become angry and hurt others without remorse, almost like I was experimenting on them. I'm feeling concerned and in need of help.
I've been with my girlfriend for a while now and we recently moved in together. Despite some mistakes I made in the past, our relationship has been improving and we've been doing better than ever.

I'm a 35-year-old mother of two children. Throughout my childhood, I had to cope with difficult circumstances, including having a narcissistic mother and an absent father. I experienced emotional neglect, physical and sexual abuse, and was also bullied during elementary school. As an adult, I sought cognitive therapy and believed I was making progress.

I have been dealing with major depression and chronic insomnia for as long as I can remember. Throughout my life, I have always found solace in reaching milestones and going through the motions. Even during the darkest times, I would convince myself that things would improve after high school, college, or getting my first job. However, lately, I have been feeling worse as I have run out of milestones to look forward to. It got to the point where I had to quit my job because I would frequently break down in tears while at work. I feel completely unmotivated and like I have given up.

My loved one has been experiencing mutism ever since a traumatic event. She hasn't spoken a word to anyone, including her family. I've done some research and it seems like she might be suffering from selective mutism, which is often linked to anxiety. She has also become listless, lost interest in activities she used to enjoy, and her eating and sleeping patterns have been disrupted. Additionally, she becomes distressed when she has to leave the house or be alone without a family member. I'm wondering what the best course of action is to help her return to her normal self and overcome this issue. I think therapy could be beneficial, but I'm concerned about her not being able to speak. I don't want to force her to talk if she's not ready, but this situation doesn't seem normal. Thank you for your time.

Lately, I've been experiencing a deep sense of depression and emptiness when I'm at home. It feels like I'm trapped in a dark box with no way out. I used to find solace in my hobbies of drawing and writing stories, but now I've lost interest in them. Additionally, I constantly feel low on energy and have a decreased appetite.

From an 18-year-old girl in Sweden: I've noticed that I have a pattern of getting into relationships and then intentionally hurting the other person later on. It's not something I do because I enjoy causing pain, but in the moment, it gives me a sense of excitement and satisfaction. I worry that a life without hurting others would be boring and unfulfilling.

After my breakup with a girl, I was feeling anxious and depressed. I decided to join a healing group and have one-on-one sessions with a healer where I shared my feelings, fears, and hopes about the relationship. It was initially helpful, so I invited the girl to join the healing sessions as well, hoping it would benefit her. However, I later found out that the healer had divulged confidential information to her and showed her a lot of attention. I stopped attending for a while but eventually asked the healer if he was involved with her. He denied it, but I couldn't ask her directly because she kept urging me to move on. After five agonizing months, she finally confessed that she had been pursued by the healer and gave in. However, their relationship didn't last long, and he moved on to someone else from the group. I feel angry and betrayed, as it seems like he used the information I shared about her to pursue her for himself. I also feel conflicted about whether to expose him publicly or let it go. What should I do?

Several years ago, I was admitted to a psychiatric hospital for treatment of an eating disorder. During the first three months of my stay, I experienced episodes where I would lose control of my arm in the dining room, making it impossible for me to pick up a fork and eat. I would have to rely on the staff to move my arm for me. What struck me as strange is that I wasn't resisting their help, and yet I couldn't move my arm on my own. It took three months before I regained control and could move my arm to eat. I've tried to find answers online, but I couldn't find any information about this experience. Is there a name for this behavior? Am I the only one who has experienced this?

For about 9 months now, I've been experiencing a lack of motivation in the mornings. It takes me up to 40 minutes to gather enough motivation to get out of bed. Once I'm at school, I start to feel a bit better, but then I get these intense waves of sadness for no reason. I think it might be related to how much I dislike myself, including my appearance and behavior. I haven't talked to anyone about this because I don't want anyone close to me to know what I'm going through. I've been keeping it to myself, thinking it's just a phase that teenagers go through. However, it's getting worse and I'm tired of feeling this way. I haven't been diagnosed with anything because I haven't spoken to a doctor about it. I've also lost interest in things I used to love. I spend about 3 hours a day on the computer talking to online friends, and I think it's a way for me to escape from how I feel. I'm scared that one day I'll reach a breaking point and everyone will see the real me. I appreciate you taking the time to read this and I hope you can provide some guidance. Thank you.

I've been experiencing a challenging situation for the past six months. Due to my mother's sudden interest in card readings and crystals, she started to believe that our house was haunted. She would scream Jesus quotes in the middle of the night and cover the floors and furniture with salt. She even started sleeping on the sofa. I became concerned when she began coming into my room and pouring salt in my bed, causing me to switch rooms with her. Then, out of nowhere, she announced that we were moving to LA, leaving behind all our belongings because she believed they were tainted by evil entities. After waiting for hours in Leeds, she finally arranged for a taxi to take us to my grandparents' house. She then left to stay with a friend and got married. I decided to stay with my grandparents, which meant changing schools and starting over. When I went back to our old house to retrieve some electronics, my mother lied to me about the condition of my brother's 2DS and claimed there was a devil pit under the sink.

I've been having a lot of difficulties with my mom. Our relationship has always been rocky and it feels like any kindness between us is forced. She constantly blames me for our conflicts and accuses me of disrespecting her. She dismisses anything I say because she sees me as just a "teenager". Her overprotectiveness is suffocating and I can't handle it anymore. Despite never giving her a reason not to trust me, she treats me like I'm a terrible person. It's like she has these imaginary ideas about who I am and it's starting to worry me. One of her obsessions is taking away my phone every night at 8:00 without fail. Lately, she even tried to limit my phone access to just one hour after school. I mean, I'm a teenager, shouldn't I have some independence? It's like she has a mental disorder because she becomes a completely different person every night. Just last Friday, she called me while I was out with friends to make sure my friend's mom was bringing me home. It may seem like she's just being protective, but when I gave her the mom's number, she accused me of giving her the wrong number and even threatened to call the mom's workplace to complain about my friend. I'm really struggling here. How do I make her understand that I'm just a teenager?

Lately, I've been feeling really isolated and alone, despite having plenty of friends. I also have this constant sense of disappointment from my parents, and it's been really hard for me to feel comfortable around them. On top of that, I've been eating really poorly and have been dealing with a stomach ache for a few days. My procrastination has gotten so bad that I hardly ever do my homework. And even though I love theater, I've been struggling to get into the mindset of memorizing lines. I'm starting to wonder if there's something wrong with me or if this is just a phase in my growing up.

Throughout my life, I've struggled with the frustration of being unable to complete tasks. Despite my efforts to learn and adapt, I find that my motivation often dissipates, making it difficult to manage this aspect of my personality.

From a 13-year-old boy in the U.S.: "So I started talking to myself when I was about 6 or 7. I’ve always felt a little bit psychic. Which has nothing to do with this, I think. But every time, a week before a loved one of mine dies, without notice, I get a dream which I wake up crying and the dream tells me I should start treating this person right, and outta nowhere. EXACTLY a week later, the person dies. On top of that, I have always talked to myself."

I have been married to my husband for 5 years, and we have 2 kids together. Recently, I discovered that he was on the computer looking up his ex-girlfriend's web page. He was engaged to his ex-girlfriend for 3 years, but they split up when he found out she was cheating on him. Despite that, they continued emailing each other even while my husband and I were dating. Now she is married to someone else, but my husband still had her web page saved in his favorites. I feel really upset and I don't trust him anymore. He insists that he didn't contact her, but I find it hard to believe. I am considering leaving him. What do you think?

Patient: It took me a very long time to learn to trust my therapist. Recently my trust has been shaken. It’s complicated but I feel like I have trouble making myself understood, and sometimes I feel like my therapist is patronizing me, and that my therapist is tolerating me rather than appreciating me. I got into the habit of emailing my therapist between appointments when I became anxious or melancholy, and my therapist would tell me that we could talk about it at my next appointment. I recognize that I have issues and things to work through, but when these issues come up I feel crowded, and I feel like I’m being pressed to change my viewpoint when I think I would like have room to think. Part of me doesn’t want to return to therapy. Part of me wants to go back, but if I did return I think I would like to tell my therapist: I think I need to be more careful about what I share. I recognize that I shouldn’t email my therapist between appointments, because it's asking her to work for free and I should be able to deal with things myself. I want to take things slowly and ease back into therapy. What do you think?

I have been married for 2 1/2 years. I love my husband very much; however I don’t like having sex with him. I like sex and think about it all the time. When my husband and I are apart, I fantasize about things we can try but, as soon as he comes around, I don’t want to anymore. When he tries to touch me I push his hands away. He feels as though I want someone else and that is not true.

My 9-year-old daughter has been displaying challenging behaviors lately. She often refuses to listen and when things don't go her way, she becomes convinced that everyone hates her. I've tried various strategies such as taking away privileges and using positive reinforcement, but nothing seems to be working. Her behavior is also affecting her performance at school, as she frequently acts out and even talks back to adults. I feel like I've lost control and I'm not sure what to do next.

Recently, my girlfriend shared with me that she has a preference for kinkier activities in the bedroom. She enjoys being dominated and has expressed her desire for me to be more assertive and even use force. She's mentioned being influenced by the "Fifty Shades of Grey" series and finds being choked and slapped to be pleasurable. I'm struggling to understand why she wants me to engage in this kind of behavior, as I consider myself a kind person. It's particularly concerning that she wants me to say hurtful things about her, especially in public. She's only 18, and I worry about the psychological implications of engaging in such a fetish at a young age. Additionally, she has a strained relationship with her father due to a broken marriage, and she feels unwanted by him. I've read that these kinds of experiences can contribute to sexual problems in females. What are your thoughts on this? It's also worth noting that she has a history of self-harm.

Recently, I had a really difficult experience at my therapy session. I had written down the appointment on my calendar, but when I arrived, I was told that I wasn't actually scheduled for that day. I was already feeling down and this just made things worse. The receptionist suggested that I wait to see if the next appointment didn't show up, but while I was waiting, I started having really negative thoughts and blamed myself for everything. I even had thoughts of wanting to die. It was a really emotional state for me.

I'm a 29-year-old woman with a degree in psychology. Lately, I've been struggling with my thoughts and feelings about my physical appearance. I find myself obsessing internally about wanting to be seen as attractive by others. I know that societal pressures around beauty can affect many women, but I feel like my obsession is stronger and more intense than what is considered normal. I've had a history of both bulimia and anorexia since I was 15, but for me, it's not about control, it's solely about wanting to be physically desirable. I've even considered getting plastic surgery and have met with a surgeon, but my husband was not supportive, so I didn't go through with it. The only thing that sexually arouses me is receiving compliments on my physical appearance, even from strangers online. While I consider myself a feminist, I feel conflicted about enjoying catcalling because it satisfies my deep yearning for physical praise. I used to hate myself, but now I feel more neutral about my appearance on most days. I just can't shake this desire to be praised for my physical beauty. Can you help me understand why I feel this way?

I've been experiencing an ongoing sense of emptiness and detachment for as long as I can remember. It's not the typical feeling of losing purpose in life, but more like a numbness in my mind. While I don't feel sad or depressed, I wonder if depersonalization could be a possible explanation. I haven't been tested for an anxiety disorder, though.

My wife and I have been married for about two years now. Before getting married, we had many discussions about our plans for having children. It became clear that having children was more important to me than it was to her. We eventually reached a compromise and agreed that we would have one child, but only after we both completed graduate school and found stable jobs. I was happy with this agreement and thought it was responsible and reasonable.

I have been diagnosed with Paranoid Schizophrenia and OCD, but I feel that the symptoms of bipolar disorder align more with my life experiences and struggles. After experiencing a period of Great Depression, I came to the USA for my master's program. Initially, I was doing well with a GPA of 3.5 and 3.24 in my first two semesters. However, suddenly I lost all emotions, desire, and motivation. I have no career goals and I am failing in my subjects without feeling any emotional impact. This is different from my previous experiences where failing exams would break my heart. Currently, I am facing termination of my masters program, but I don't feel any emotional difference no matter how bad the situation gets. Additionally, I feel no difference in emotions when talking to different people. The real world and events seem very dead and useless to me, while the scenarios and events in my mind, which are purely imagination, feel real and make me happy. What is wrong with me?

I've been struggling with my weight and have a strained relationship with my mother. She is highly regarded by others, while I often feel like the less attractive and less interesting daughter. Although she does offer some support when it comes to my weight, she also frequently belittles me, calling me disgusting and saying she can't bear to look at me. These hurtful comments often escalate into intense arguments, and even if she sees me crying, she dismisses my emotions as being overly dramatic. It's really taking a toll on me.

As a teenager living in the Channel Islands, I've been observing my sister's behavior and I can't help but wonder if she might be sociopathic. I've researched the signs extensively, but I haven't been able to come to a conclusion after years of observation.

Over the past two weeks, I've noticed a significant improvement in my relationship with my ex-girlfriend of 27 years. We've been getting along well, and she has been friendly and polite whenever I visit her. She also responds quickly to my phone calls and texts, and is always available for me. However, she recently expressed feeling sad when I leave her to go home, and suggested that I should stay at her apartment. I feel like I've let her down too many times before.

Patient: I've been feeling really overwhelmed lately. My oldest brother was diagnosed with schizophrenia about a year ago, and his condition has been deteriorating rapidly. It's been difficult for me to witness his struggles. On top of that, I have a maternal grandmother who also had schizophrenia.

My wife and I are almost 30. We’ve been married for two years, and I can count on my fingers the amount of times I have had a peaceful time with my wife. Here again are the holidays and all hell is breaking loose, evidenced by the finger scratch marks on the side of my neck from a fight last night. I have been faithful to my wife, I have tried to take care of things around the house to the best of my ability but she is constantly unhappy- says "I'm not happy."

I met this guy while he was on exchange at my university in Malaysia. We spent a few weeks together and eventually decided to officially date, knowing that he would have to go back to his home country eventually. After he left, we didn't have much communication until one day he told me he was seeing someone else. I expressed that it was unhealthy for me to keep in contact and cut off communication. Surprisingly, he ended things with the other person and started texting me every day.

I've been with my boyfriend for one and a half years now. We moved to a new city together a couple of months ago because we both got jobs at the same place. However, ever since we started living together, he has been consistently getting angrier. He shouts out of anger at least once a day now. I've tried talking to him about it and suggested that he seeks help, but he refuses to acknowledge that there is a problem. He dismisses my concerns and claims that I'm just too sensitive. While I do consider myself a sensitive person, his anger seems excessive and not normal. He becomes mean and insults me, and then later feels upset because I'm affected by his words. I feel trapped and controlled in this relationship. Additionally, I've started developing feelings for a coworker, which confuses me even more. I'm torn between staying with my boyfriend, who alternates between being sweet and angry, and exploring these new feelings. I fear being alone, as my depression might worsen if I break up with him. I'm also worried about the financial implications, my dad's reaction, judgment from friends and family, and having to see him every day at work. I just don't know what to do. I feel like I'm losing my sense of self and freedom. Can you help me figure out what to do?

"I'm a young woman from Ireland and I've been in a committed relationship for three years. We've always been faithful and loved each other deeply. However, I recently discovered that my partner has been using drugs, something he's kept hidden from me. This is not something I'm okay with."

My parents have been married for 18 years, but over the past year, they have been experiencing conflict. My dad, who is a teacher, tries to maintain a positive attitude in life, but my mom tends to be pessimistic and self-centered. She often blames others for things that go wrong and rarely takes responsibility herself. Additionally, my mom is resistant to change, possessive of her belongings, and always wants to be in control. This behavior is similar to her father's. I'm concerned about their relationship and worried about how things will turn out. My mom has promised to change, but I haven't seen any progress. What should they do, or what can I do to help?

Over the past 8 years, I have experienced a range of mood episodes, starting with my first depressive episode at age 18. After using antidepressants, I experienced a hypomanic episode. Two years ago, I was diagnosed with Bipolar 2 and began taking medication. For the past year, I have been in a long-lasting depressive episode, but recently experienced a shift in my mood due to a medication change. Currently, I am feeling stable.

I've been struggling with depression for as long as I can remember. I've also noticed some physical symptoms, like an underactive thyroid. I've tried to be happy and work hard, but I always feel like I'm falling short. I've been relying on alcohol to cope, but I'm trying to quit. I worry about ending up like my agoraphobic mother and I don't want to rely on medication either. I just want to know if it's possible for me to be happy without feeling overwhelmed and scattered all the time.

I recently received a diagnosis of OCD from my doctor, but I believe I may also have symptoms of bipolar disorder. My doctor mentioned that there can be a connection between OCD and bipolar disorder, especially in more advanced cases. Can you please listen to my additional symptoms and help me determine if they may be related to bipolar disorder or not?

I have been seeing my psychologist for the past couple of months (10 sessions) and we had been working on cognitive behavioural therapy techniques. Now it seems that I’ve grasped the concept of changing my thoughts and challenging my anxiety but I somehow feel more depressed than when I went into this treatment. My anxiety is still something that bothers me pretty frequently but dealing with it seems much more manageable.

I'm a 13-year-old girl living in the United States. I'm really struggling with my stepdad's behavior. While he hasn't physically harmed me, he said some hurtful things today, like wishing I would weigh over 300 pounds. It's not the first time he's insulted me, calling me ignorant and criticizing my choices. It's hard to feel safe when he's around, especially considering his own unhealthy habits like smoking and drinking excessively.

I've been in a relationship with someone I care about, but there are some concerning behaviors that have been causing me distress. From the very beginning, he expressed love for me and became overly attached and obsessed. He would exhibit extreme jealousy and accuse me of cheating if I didn't immediately respond to his texts while I was out with friends. However, I have noticed that his jealousy has lessened after about two months into the relationship, which I appreciate.

I've been noticing that my husband has been reacting poorly to stress lately. He works from home, and when I try to reach out to him, he often responds with anger and yells at me. Even simple questions are met with hostility. It's becoming really difficult for me to communicate with him.

Lately, I've been feeling a constant sense of emptiness and like there's something wrong with me. It's like I'm stuck in this cycle of self-doubt and self-criticism that I can't escape from. And recently, I've started to realize that some of my behaviors might actually be sociopathic. I've tried to justify them, but deep down, I know it's not right. It feels futile and dishonest to lie to myself.

From a teenage girl in the Philippines: I am struggling to understand my own behavior. I find myself lying frequently and people believe me, but I fear that they will leave me if they discover who I truly am. Sometimes when I try to tell the truth, it comes across as a lie. In my senior year of high school, my friends perceive me as socially awkward with claustrophobia, although I don't actually have claustrophobia. I enjoy the extra attention and care they give me in tight spaces. I also have a tendency to manipulate people for no reason and sabotage my relationships when someone gets too close. Additionally, I experienced sexual abuse, but my family denies it and claims it was just a dream. I am troubled by these memories at night and struggle to determine their truth. Sometimes, I even desire punishment, but not verbally. My parents constantly fight and physically harm each other, and I sometimes have thoughts of wanting them to die, although I understand this is not right. I also have thoughts of hurting, torturing, and killing someone involuntarily, especially when I am angry. I harm myself instead of acting on these thoughts. I have urges to engage in destructive behavior, like smoking, and I often resort to self-harm to suppress these cravings. I feel like I always ruin things and I long for someone to truly know and accept me, although I am unsure how to make that happen. I was bullied in junior years, and the memories sometimes trigger panic attacks. I find myself crying for no apparent reason, overwhelmed by the constant thoughts in my mind. I have a strong desire to die, and although my family is aware of my self-harm, I struggle to communicate my feelings to them because I don't fully understand them myself. How can I explain something that I don't understand?

Patient's statement (revised): Throughout my childhood, I experienced severe abuse from both my father and mother. My father sexually abused me until I was placed in foster care at the age of 9. I am an only child of parents that are both ‘mentally ill’. My Dad (deceased since 1991, and Mother, still living in Arizona have schizophrenia. Over the past year, I've been struggling with self-harm. It started when I felt overwhelmed and full of self-hatred, so I began cutting my wrist. Over the past two years, I've been experiencing some new and unusual sexual desires. It started with enjoying masturbating on video chat for anyone who wanted to watch, regardless of their gender. Patient: I believe, and my family members also believe, that I was suffering from serious paranoid delusions for years. I also had repetitive physical movements that I couldn’t control, and some hallucinations. I came out of it spontaneously, without medication two and a half years ago.

I am a 34-year-old woman and I’ve been married for 5 years, but we don't have any children. About 3 years ago, I experienced some stressful events in my life which caused me to become somewhat depressed. During that time, I also noticed that I lost my libido and couldn't feel any sexual attraction towards anyone. Despite this, I continued to have intimate relations with my husband for about a year, but it brought me little pleasure and our encounters became less frequent until they stopped altogether. My husband has been understanding and supportive, and we've maintained a platonic relationship while he focused on his career and hobbies. However, over the past 6-8 months, I've started feeling sexual desire again and I've begun to imagine having sex. I've been hesitant to initiate anything because we've become so accustomed to acting as just friends. Finally, I gathered the courage to propose sex to my husband, but he kept finding excuses. This eventually led to a big fight where he revealed that he no longer loves me as a woman, doesn't find me attractive anymore, and wants to split up and see other women. I'm devastated because I love him and feel guilty for causing this problem. Is there anything I can do about it? Thank you very much!

Over the past month, I've been seeing a therapist and while I've experienced personal growth, I'm unsure if I'm making progress. This year has been challenging for me - I dropped out of college due to stress, experienced mood swings, anxiety, and had a difficult breakup. I also had a manic episode followed by depression. My therapist initially mentioned bipolar disorder but later diagnosed me with an anxiety disorder. I'm feeling lost and lacking direction for my future.

I'm a 17-year-old female who has been experiencing a variety of symptoms and feelings. I often find myself wanting to have a mental illness because I get bored with normal things. I've been having obsessive thoughts about having borderline personality disorder (BPD) because I believe it would make me feel special. I have many of the symptoms, such as feeling empty and struggling with social anxiety, but I don't experience impulsivity, extreme fear of abandonment, or anger issues. I've also had a history of self-harm, suicidal thoughts, and childhood sexual abuse. Additionally, I used to see things that may or may not have been real, and I often feel like I'm hiding my true self from others and can switch off my emotions. My paranoia sometimes prevents me from functioning, and I'm easily hurt by words, even though I don't show it. I'm not particularly interested in getting better because I feel more comfortable being in pain or sadness, and being stable seems boring to me. I just want to know if I might have BPD. Thank you for listening.

I used to love everything about life. I was so happy and ready to show the world who I was. I started college and during my junior year everything changed in one night. I got home from work and started feeling terrible. I felt like nothing mattered and that life had no point. Since then I have had difficulty with suicidal thoughts, depersonalization and derealization. Sometimes I feel like part of me is watching over me, and that it wants me to join it in heaven. Other times I get scared when I’m around loved ones because I know they are going to die one day, and that I’ll be left without them. I also get scared that I’m going to die, that I could end my life without realizing I’m doing it. How I feel seems to vary by the day, but they are not mood swings from high to low, just low to lower. When I’m walking around sometimes I feel like I may be in heaven already, especially when I’m walking through scenic environments. If I see something especially pretty or out of place I feel like I may be imagining it. Even going to the lake is enough to make me wonder if I’m real. This feeling doesn’t ever go away. I get overwhelmed extremely easily, and sometimes feel like I’m in a fog. Situations as simple as having a conversation at work or going to the store can make me feel like there’s too much going on, and that I’m about to wake up from a coma or a dream. I always feel like I’m about to hear my alarm clock go off and I’ll wake up. I’ve seen several therapists, talk therapy hasn’t been very helpful. I’ve been on and off Lexapro a few times. I’m on it now and this has been the only successful time. My dad, his parents and my other grandpa are alcoholics and my sister and aunt are bipolar type 1. I feel like a freak and honestly don’t understand why this is happening to me. I have never had real issues in my entire life. (From the USA)

I'm a 16-year-old girl from the United States. My stepdad recently made some inappropriate comments towards me. He told me that he liked me and wanted to kiss me because I am his first "daddy's girl." He commented on my physical appearance, saying that my ass is nice, I'm cute, I have nice legs, and that I'm sexy. He later clarified that it wasn't meant in a sexual way, just that he wanted to kiss me because of our father-daughter relationship.

Patient's statement (rewritten): My son is 14 years old and he has been displaying certain behaviors that make me wonder if he may have Asperger's. He excels academically and is generally a good kid, but he has a strong need to "run" and spends a lot of time alone. He struggles with criticism, dislikes socializing, and is sensitive to the texture of clothes. While he has friends at school, I worry about his social life as he gets older and how these behaviors may affect his relationships and work. I'm torn between seeking a diagnosis to help him navigate life or just letting things be.

I am experiencing a very difficult situation with my husband. He can be unpredictable, violent, and uses abusive language towards me. He even spat on my face. It's confusing because he has a good professional and personal reputation. He is highly educated and works as a journalist in the press media. Recently, we were out for a walk with some family members when he playfully slapped me on the shoulder. I playfully slapped him back, but he reacted aggressively and forcefully grabbed my neck. It was a terrifying experience and everyone present thought it was just a joke.

Over the past couple of years, I have been experiencing difficulties with controlling my emotions. I often feel panicked and scared about thoughts and ideas that are unlikely to happen. Specifically, I have been dealing with social anxiety and general anxiety, which has led to panic attacks when I am in unfamiliar social situations or new environments.

Since I was young, I've struggled with overwhelming negative thoughts that seem to consume my mind. These thoughts make it difficult for me to envision a happy or peaceful future for myself. I often imagine my loved ones, including my parents, siblings, and friends, turning against me. These thoughts even extend to contemplating leaving my home, family, and studies to start anew in a different country where no one knows me. While I recognize that these thoughts may sound typical for a teenager, they feel more intense and persistent for me. I want to emphasize that I would never want to cause harm to my parents, but there have been moments in the past where I've had thoughts of hurting them myself.

Patient: I'm a 20-year-old woman with two children, both boys, and I'm engaged to be married. Lately, our relationship has been unstable for the past 8 months. I find myself having uncontrollable outbursts towards my fiance, saying hurtful things that I don't mean. Our relationship is currently on edge, and I've been reflecting on why I react this way, wondering if it could be related to my birth control. I'm currently taking Yaz.

I am currently in a blended family situation, where my wife and I have been married for 2 years. We both have children from previous marriages, and we have shared custody with her ex-husband. The children stay with us occasionally during the school year and spend the summers with us. I have a good relationship with both of the children. However, when the son is in our home, he often expresses a strong preference for sleeping in our bed or on the floor next to us, rather than in his own bed.

Three years ago, I had a sudden and intense panic attack. I didn't understand what was happening to me, so I went to the emergency room. They assured me that it was just due to stress, but it was hard for me to believe that such intense symptoms could be caused by stress alone. As a mother of two young children, I do experience stress, but I couldn't wrap my head around the idea that stress could cause these physical sensations. I started experiencing depersonalization and derealization, and it caused me to worry about having a brain tumor or a stroke. Even though the doctors reassured me that I was physically fine, the feelings of depersonalization persisted. These feelings made me fear that I might harm my children because it felt like I was losing touch with reality. I made the mistake of doing a lot of research online, which only intensified my fear of developing schizophrenia.

I'm an 18-year-old guy who has been struggling with a lot of anxiety lately. Ever since I moved to a new place, I've been hearing voices. Sometimes they're in my head and they say really negative things about me. Other times, I hear them outside of my head, like in large crowds or whispers. These voices are constantly distracting me and it's hard for me to understand what people are saying or comprehend what I'm reading. I've tried to make them stop, but I can't, and this conflicting idea of making it up and not being able to control it is causing me a lot of confusion and distress.

I've been feeling really down lately and I'm wondering if there might be something more serious going on with my mental health. I've never reached out for help before because I didn't want to burden anyone and I always felt like my issues weren't important enough.

When I was around 7 years old, I had an uncomfortable experience with my grandmother. She made me sit in her lap and suck on her breast. I can't recall if it happened more than once, but I remember feeling alone in the room with her and her smiling at me during the incident. Over the years, I have occasionally thought about this experience, but lately, the memories have been resurfacing more frequently and I'm not sure why.

I recently went through a separation from my ex-partner of 27 years. Despite the separation, we still maintain regular communication and she has expressed a desire to remain friends. I've been feeling really down lately. I just can't seem to find any motivation or joy in anything anymore. It's like I'm stuck in this never-ending cycle of sadness and I don't know how to break free from it.

Hello, I am a 15-year-old from Indonesia. I have been experiencing a concerning fascination with self-harm and harming others, as well as a strong attraction to the sight of blood. I've been feeling overwhelmed lately. I'm a 33-year-old mother of a 5-year-old girl. I've been married for 7 years and decided to leave my job to take care of my daughter after she was born. My husband is very supportive and understanding, and I love him dearly.

When I first started dating my boyfriend, we had an immediate connection. We were introduced through a mutual friend and had great chemistry over the phone. I have been in a relationship for almost 5 years, engaged for 2. We want to get married, however, I am facing a dilemma regarding my parents' financial situation. How can I communicate to my parents that their actions are affecting my relationship and my life, and that I need to move out before it ruins everything?

I have been in a relationship with my fiancé for 2.5 years. When we first got together, we shared our past experiences, and he disclosed that he had been married and divorced by the age of 22. I recently ended a long-term relationship with my girlfriend. We started dating in high school and continued into my freshman year of college. We decided to give long-distance dating a try over the summer.

My school has suggested that I seek professional help, but my mom seems to be avoiding the topic of my mental health. Is there anything I can do on my own to address this?

I have been struggling with white coat hypertension, where my blood pressure and heart rate spike when I visit the doctor. It's become a source of anxiety for me, to the point where I avoided going to the doctor for years. It's embarrassing because I don't understand why something as simple as having my blood pressure taken makes me so nervous. I've had this reaction both during medical appointments and in situations like public speaking. It's affecting me as I get older and need to visit the doctor more frequently. Even when I explain the situation to the nurse, my heart rate is still racing and my blood pressure is severely elevated.

From a very young age, I have spent a significant amount of time alone. My parents had to work, so I had a nanny and stayed in school until late in the day. I haven't talked to my parents about this because I don't want to bother them, but I would like to discuss it with someone who can help.

I've been dealing with intense anger and violent thoughts which are distressing for me. I have a history of acting out on these thoughts in harmful ways, including causing harm to animals and people. I've also lost jobs and come close to being arrested due to my temper. I've tried using marijuana to calm myself, but it's not always accessible. I saw a therapist before who said I was fine, but I don't feel fine when these thoughts consume me. I'm concerned that if I don't get help, I might end up in prison.

I have been struggling with a lot of issues lately and I'm feeling overwhelmed. I'm a 16 year old male living in New York. Criticism deeply hurts me and I feel inferior to my peers. I have never been to a social gathering and I constantly feel judged by others. I have never had a girlfriend and find it difficult to trust others. The only escape I have is through my fantasies when I am alone.

I'm wondering if I may be suffering from ADD.

It feels like they don't love or support me, and they don't even seem to know basic things about me like my hobbies and interests.

I developed a strong passion for books, arts, and sciences. It's also worth mentioning that I've never been in a romantic relationship nor have I engaged in any sexual activity.

I've been feeling really empty and bored with life for a while now. I don't have any ambition or motivation to do anything. I see how other people have dreams and aspirations, but I just don't have any desire for anything. Money doesn't bring me any happiness either. On top of that, I only have one friend and I'm not allowed to hang out with them.

I have been experiencing chronic stress and worry for the past three years. Along with that, I have been dealing with constant chest pain and episodes of extreme depression, where I struggle to get out of bed and find myself crying uncontrollably. I have isolated myself from others because I feel embarrassed about who I am and the choices I've made. The fear of being judged by others about my decisions is paralyzing, making it difficult for me to concentrate and function in work environments.

Lately, I've been struggling when I'm alone with my thoughts. It seems like every time I start thinking about my life, I spiral into negative thoughts and start questioning if there's something wrong with me. It's especially difficult because many of my friends and family have their own mental health issues, which adds to the pressure of figuring out if what I'm experiencing is normal or if I should seek help. I had a scary incident where I went to a bridge one night, but realized it didn't have a sheer drop. I'm not sure if I actually wanted to jump or if I was just testing myself. Overall, I feel lost and confused about what's going on in my head and I don't know what to do. It's hard to describe because I often forget my thoughts until the next time I'm alone.

For nearly two years, I’ve been struggling with increasingly severe symptoms of anxiety. One of the main challenges I face is my inability to sleep when I'm away from home, including in my dorm. This has been going on for over a year now, and I've noticed that when I can't sleep, I tend to focus on all the things that feel wrong in the room, such as it being too quiet or too hot. I also constantly go through a mental list of assignments, meetings, and events, and I have to rewrite the list in my planner every day. I usually go through the list in my head, but I've noticed that I sometimes speak out loud to myself when I'm walking to and from class, going through the list and planning the order in which to complete tasks. I do this multiple times until I reach my destination or encounter other people because I'm afraid of being judged for talking to myself. Even when I've completed the tasks for the day, I still find myself thinking about them and panicking about how much more I have to do. As a result, I never feel fully relaxed. I'm always worried that I'll forget something on the list and that something bad will happen if I don't complete a particular task. I also struggle to concentrate because I'm constantly consumed by these thoughts. When I'm having difficulty concentrating and feel extremely anxious, I end up picking at the skin around my nails. On particularly bad days, I pick at them until they bleed. Although I'm afraid of being judged by others for this behavior, it actually helps me calm down and refocus. While school-related worries are typically my main focus, I also find myself worrying about my relationships, especially that my friends don't really like me and that I don't truly have feelings for my boyfriend. Lately, I've started to wonder if I might have OCD rather than just anxiety. I've mentioned some of these concerns to my doctor, but should I discuss my worries about the anxiety resembling aspects of OCD?

Over the past three years, I've been struggling with overwhelming feelings of self-hatred and insecurity. It has led me to engage in self-harm, as a way to punish myself. Although I was able to stop for a period of time, whenever I face emotionally threatening situations, I find it difficult to resist hurting myself again.

As a teenager in the U.S., I've been struggling with a difficult relationship with my dad ever since I found out he cheated on my mom. For the past 7 years, he has been both physically and mentally abusive towards me. Recently, when I was with him and he started picking on me again, I couldn't take it anymore. We got into an argument and he ended up hitting me in the mouth.

I have been struggling with obsessive fears for the past 7 years. Recently, I've developed an obsession about experiencing anxiety during important and happy moments. It's like a vicious cycle - as soon as a special moment is about to happen, the thought of anxiety creeps in and I start panicking. This only makes the anxiety worse, and I can't seem to break free from it.

"I've been feeling really isolated lately. I don't have any close friends and I spend most of my time alone. I eat lunch by myself, go to and from school without talking to anyone, and I don't even speak to my family."

Lately, I've been feeling really overwhelmed with school. I recently moved to a new place and I haven't been able to make any friends, which makes dealing with the stress even harder. I don't feel comfortable talking to my mother about these issues because she tends to scare me. Last quarter, I had a decent GPA of 3.6, but now it's getting worse. On top of that, I'm struggling because I don't like the environment in this new place. Everyone around me is into drugs and alcohol, which goes against my values. I really miss where I used to live, and it's been bringing me down. I've noticed that whenever I read articles about depression, I start crying for no reason. I'm really worried about myself and my grades. Can you please help me?

Three years ago, I had a terrifying experience where I felt like I was having a heart attack or stroke. I went to the hospital and the doctors reassured me that it was just a panic attack caused by stress. However, two days later I had another panic attack that was accompanied by depersonalization and derealization. It was incredibly scary and I felt like I was losing my mind. I was also afraid that I might harm my children during these episodes.

I'm struggling with some thoughts and attractions that are causing me concern. I'm a 25-year-old male and I find myself attracted to 16-year-olds. I used to think this was normal because I believed that many men were attracted to teenage girls. I also rationalized it because the age of consent in my state is 16. However, recently I saw some online discussions where people were calling someone a pedophile for being attracted to 17-year-olds, even though they were only 20.

About a month ago, my 16-year-old son confided in me that he has been experiencing intense feelings of rage over seemingly small incidents, such as someone making a rude comment to him at school. He mentioned that he was wondering if he might be bipolar due to these emotional fluctuations. In response, I reassured him that some level of frustration and anger is normal, but it's important to learn healthy coping mechanisms. I suggested techniques like relaxation exercises and visualization to help him manage his emotions when he feels upset.

When I was young, my parents went through a difficult separation, and as a result, my mother entrusted me to my grandparents. During that time, my grandfather would often yell at me, physically harm me, and repeatedly belittle me by saying hurtful things like how I would amount to nothing and end up like my father who had substance abuse issues. Even now, I still vividly recall his face and the hurtful words he used to say.

Over the past four years, I have had a persistent belief that I may have a personality disorder. It has always felt like there is something fundamentally wrong with me, separate from my experiences with depression or anxiety. It's more about how I perceive and interpret the world around me.

Hello, I'm a 19-year-old girl from the Netherlands. I've recently been diagnosed with borderline personality disorder, anxiety, and depression. My life has been quite challenging, filled with pain and loneliness. Currently, I'm taking a gap year from studies and working as a cleaner. When I'm not working, I spend most of my time at home watching YouTube videos and movies to try and distract myself.

Hi. Lately, I've been having trouble sleeping. My boyfriend and I recently moved to southern California due to my new and highly stressful job. This move marked the first time I've been away from San Francisco, my family, and friends, as I even attended college in SF. I think I may have been more stressed or depressed than I initially realized, as I'm not very in tune with my emotions.

My daughter is ten months old and her legal father (L.F.) is not her biological father (B.F.). L.F. has been actively involved in raising her and she sees him as her father. Recently, L.F. has decided that he no longer wants to be a part of her life. I'm concerned about the potential long-term effects on my daughter due to the sudden loss of this bonded relationship.

I have been experiencing what I believe are anxiety attacks, but they only occur in response to extreme confrontation or when recalling a sad event. During these episodes, I feel overwhelmed and exhibit symptoms such as forgetting to breathe, shaking my body, gripping my scalp while crying, or feeling immobilized and disconnected. The exception is my partner, with whom I have a healthy and happy relationship. I don't feel that my experiences fit neatly into the typical symptoms of depression or anxiety, as I consider myself rational and composed. I am seeking a better understanding of what I'm feeling and where to find help.

Today my boyfriend shared with me that he has been experiencing difficulties in perceiving and connecting with the emotions and lives of others. He mentioned that he sees people as just individuals and not as complex beings. This concerns me because I wonder if he is able to fully understand and express his love and care for me. Since the age of 6, he has been living with his grandparents. He also mentioned having no remorse for burying animals, including previous dogs, and killing numerous rats and bunnies. I am both scared for him and myself and I would like to understand what could be happening. I want to be able to support him and I am desperate to know if there is a possible diagnosis. Please help me.

I have been seeing my therapist for over a year now, but I have always questioned if they are the right fit for me. Despite my doubts, I have seen some improvements and feel like they are helping me. However, I can't help but wonder if my own issues are clouding my judgment.

I have been in a committed relationship with my partner for over 10 years. We are both women and have always had a strong bond.
