I would see my blinds moving, the floor appearing to breathe, and the walls turning red with a plaid design, almost like they were dripping blood. Eventually, it felt like the walls were closing in on me. I remember feeling incredibly scared and wanting to call out for my parents, but I couldn't make a sound. It was as if I was paralyzed. These episodes lasted for about ten minutes and continued at the same intensity for about 4 years.

I'm curious about the connection between hallucinations and the unconscious or subconscious mind. In my family, we had a situation where a family member experienced hallucinations after a surgery due to low sodium levels. I've been told that these hallucinations are a result of biological changes, but I wonder if there could be any unconscious or subconscious projections happening. For example, she scolded a fan as if it were a person, but when asked, she said she was scolding the fan itself. Could there be any hidden meanings behind these hallucinations?

My wife has been seeing the same psychiatrist for over eight years. I now accompany her since she doesn’t know why she’s still going to him and doesn’t remember what he says in the session. She has many hallmarks of early stage Alzheimer’s (about 18 months now) but has been on Celexa for many years for depression and sees him just to be monitored. She does not want to be tested for cognitive impairment or take drugs–doesn’t see purpose. Has trouble articulating/expressing herself and really hates being “interrogated” now. She obsesses whenever I tell her her appointment is coming up. Any advice on how to lessen her fear of being questioned and/or tested? I feel pretty stuck–her psychiatrist is being ethical to monitor her Celexa dosage, but I don’t know how to help her, and he has no advice so far. She knows she has memory problems and is not in denial–she just wants to avoid doing anything about it. She has short-term memory limitations and can’t be persuaded to be tested. Discussions about it go nowhere–her fears/anxiety overshadow reasoning with her. Any advice or strategies on how to deal with this? Thanks. (From the USA)

Today, I visited my doctor and was prescribed Depakote for Bipolar Disorder. However, after filling the prescription, I read the medication insert and became alarmed by the listed side effects. One of my concerns is weight gain, as I have already experienced a significant increase in weight over the past two years. Additionally, I came across information about potential side effects such as liver failure and hair loss. I understand that not everyone experiences these side effects, but I'm hesitant to take the medication and face these risks.

Growing up, I have always had a difficult relationship with my older sister. She is 25 years old, and I am 22. She has consistently shown resentment towards me and has engaged in bullying behavior throughout my life. This includes publicly shaming me on social media platforms like Facebook and Twitter. In addition, she frequently talks down to me in our conversations and makes hurtful comments, even in the presence of our parents.

Throughout my childhood, I experienced emotional abuse, neglect, and smothering from a parent who struggled with substance abuse. Additionally, I was molested as a toddler by older children. These traumatic experiences have contributed to the development of my severe dissociative disorder and OCD. It's important to note that I share this information for context, not as an excuse. As a child, I had distressing intrusive thoughts that were violent and sexually deviant, along with Persistent Genital Arousal Disorder (PGAD). I despised these thoughts and tried to suppress them, but I ended up feeling convinced that I was evil. Therapy has helped me understand that these thoughts were not my fault at the time. However, during my teenage years, I began to believe that these thoughts were inevitable and started allowing disturbing scenarios to play out in my mind, and even masturbated to some of them. I found online communities where people shared similar thoughts but considered them harmless when confined to fiction. I never intended to act on these thoughts and saw them as separate from my true beliefs. However, I now recognize that they still had an impact on me, and I want nothing to do with them anymore. I no longer believe that immoral fantasies can be harmless. As a result, I became hyper-sexual and developed a chronic habit of masturbation.

Ever since my mother passed away two years ago, I have been experiencing a deep sense of depression. However, recently I have been feeling disconnected from myself. It's as if someone else is controlling my actions while I remain trapped in a corner, desperately waiting for help to escape.

Hi, I was diagnosed with Bipolar Disorder about 5 years ago. Due to financial constraints, I haven't been able to see a psychiatrist and get the necessary medication. Although I've been managing without medication and haven't experienced extreme mood swings, I've started hearing voices that aren't my own. These voices sound like someone else talking behind my thoughts, but I can't fully understand what they're saying as they fade away when I try to focus on them. These voices occur during the day and at night, regardless of my fatigue level. I've never experienced hallucinations before, and I'm wondering if there could be another cause for these voices. I've been feeling stressed lately because college has started again, but that's the only recent change in my life. I'm concerned that this might be a new illness, like schizophrenia, emerging alongside my bipolar disorder.

I woke up one day in the Hospital, not remembering the last two days, after having 3 grand mal seizures. I was told I was conscious and able to make decisions after each one, (after going through a coma state) The hospital put me through a few tests, such as an MRI and I believe an EEG. The tests claimed I had no seizures, but the nurse that held me during one of them diagnosed them as grand mal seizures. I was given Morphine from biting my tongue so bad.

Sometimes I find myself reacting strongly to things and having emotional outbursts in my room at night. I hit pillows, cry, and scream into them. I think this is normal behavior. But what concerns me is that I often feel detached and overly observant. I go around with a smile on my face, even when I don't feel happy. At school, I prefer sitting alone and reading during lunch because being around others makes me uncomfortable. My mother thinks this is harmful to my social life, but she doesn't understand how anxious I feel in certain situations. On the rare occasions when I do feel talkative, I notice that I tend to bring up unrelated topics or make the conversation about myself unintentionally. I try to change this behavior, but it seems like I always end up messing things up when I speak. I also think about things that no one else seems to care about. I'm not sure if this means there's something wrong with me or if it's just my personality. Even introverts seem to have a small group of friends to sit with, but I feel anxious and uncomfortable until I initiate the conversation. I've also noticed that I struggle with boundaries and often take playfulness too far, which ends up hurting or angering my siblings. They give me a hard time about it and make me feel guilty. There was one incident where I politely declined an invitation from a nice girl to sit with her and her friends, and when I told my mother about it, she was upset and told me I wouldn't make friends if I continued to be rude. Additionally, I tend to act immature and can be loud and annoying. I often interrupt people without meaning to and I feel agitated when someone invades my personal space without warning. Thank you for listening.

I am concerned about my stepdaughter's ongoing issues, which I believe may stem from a psychological problem. She has been struggling for over 15 years and we are desperate for help. She is 31 years old and has been dealing with drug problems for a long time. Recently, she left another rehab facility while on Vivitrol. Her pattern involves going to detox hospitals and then transferring to residential recovery houses, but she always ends up leaving after a couple of weeks. She has mentioned feeling empty inside and has talked about hurting herself, but it's difficult to determine if she is being genuine or using it as a way to return to rehab. She seems to lack reasons for leaving these places and exhibits immature behavior, struggling with authority and responsibility. She has also been in trouble with the law and has drastically changed her appearance with numerous tattoos. She has a young daughter, whom she overdosed in front of and no longer has custody of. Her parents are desperate to get her the help she needs and guide her towards a healthier path. However, she appears to disconnect easily from her actions and doesn't seem to care about the pain and worry she is causing. Despite receiving counseling in various hospitals and rehabs, I strongly believe that there may be an underlying, undiagnosed mental health issue at the root of her struggles. I am hoping you can provide some insight on what this might be. Thank you for your assistance.

Growing up in Romania, I experienced the painful effects of my parents' divorce. My father struggled with alcoholism and was physically abusive towards my mother, causing me to witness their violent encounters. Despite my mother's efforts to salvage the family, they eventually divorced after 25 years of marriage. As a result, my mother now lives with me.

My boyfriend has been experiencing panic attacks and anxiety in relationships for a while now. He has been open about his struggles from the beginning and has sought help from others for relaxation techniques. Despite his reassurances that it's not me causing his anxiety, the frequency of his panic attacks seems to be increasing as we become closer. This is causing him to feel the need to distance himself from me, triggering his flight response.

Throughout her late teens, my daughter has been struggling with episodes of depression. Unfortunately, she also experienced physical and verbal abuse from her alcoholic father during that time. Now in her late thirties, she continues to engage in self-destructive behaviors and has difficulty maintaining healthy relationships, often lashing out at her family.

I am currently in a relationship with my fiancé, and I am concerned about his anger issues. Two years ago, he hit me when I playfully put frosting on his face, leaving a bruise on my thigh. Recently, I've noticed some concerning behavior, like him yelling at our 6-month-old child for crying and becoming visibly upset when I accidentally splashed water on his face. He also warned me of consequences if I were to put whip cream in his hair after I jokingly mentioned it. These incidents have made me worried about his anger.

This has been quite a difficult experience for me to talk about, as I have been struggling with fears that I might be schizophrenic. I am a 35-year-old female veteran of the US Armed Forces. I enlisted when I was 25, with no previous history of mental illness. During the last phase of my training and before my first duty station, I unexpectedly became pregnant. Despite the opposition from my family, I made the decision not to terminate the pregnancy and instead placed my child with a loving adoptive couple. Unfortunately, I experienced complications during childbirth, including a severe "blood infection" that nearly took my life. I was sent home from the hospital before the infection was detected, and it was only when a friend found me vomiting and hallucinating that I received proper medical attention. I have very little memory of that time and only recall waking up in the hospital later on.

I've been experiencing anxiety since I was 16 years old. Typically, these episodes last for less than a month. However, I had a period of about a year where I didn't have any anxiety. Unfortunately, now that I'm on summer vacation, the anxiety has returned.

As a child, I experienced multiple instances of being placed in foster care due to what I felt were trivial reasons. These experiences have had a lasting impact on me, even after almost twenty years. I'm seeking help because I want to find a way to alleviate the emotional pain I still carry from those experiences.

I am struggling with maintaining self-control in my daily activities. While I'm glad that I don't engage in harmful behaviors like smoking or drinking, I find it difficult to control my use of electronics. I spend excessive amounts of time playing video games and surfing the internet, often neglecting social interactions. This pattern persists throughout the day and even into the early hours of the morning. It's becoming debilitating and frustrating for me.

Over the past year, I've noticed some unusual changes in my psychological well-being. Specifically, I've developed a strong aversion to sunlight. Even with sunglasses, I find it difficult to keep my eyes open when it's bright outside. I experience headaches, dizziness, and weakness. The psychological impact is even more distressing. I feel extremely vulnerable and exposed in the sun, as if I'm under a spotlight without any escape. When there's no shade nearby, I become panicked and feel as though the air is thick and suffocating.

I have been diagnosed with Bipolar Disorder and I also struggle with anxiety, which often leads to panic attacks. These panic attacks tend to occur when I feel overwhelmed by people, noises, stress, or excessive worrying. It's strange, but I always have this fear that I will be harmed. Even as a child, I couldn't watch the news because it would upset me and I would constantly think about the people who died.

Since I was a child, my father has struggled with alcoholism and untreated anger issues. Over the years, he would frequently argue with my mom about his drinking, but he has become skilled at hiding it from her.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for about a year and a half now, and we recently started living together six months ago. Lately, I've noticed that he has a bad temper and tends to throw things during our fights. At first, I thought it was just his temper, but then I started talking to his brother and sister-in-law, who are ten years older than him. They shared some information about his difficult childhood. His father was absent, struggled with substance abuse, and was verbally and emotionally abusive to his mother and my boyfriend when he was young, up until the age of seven. To this day, his father still manipulates him with guilt trips. I've also noticed that my boyfriend is always angry and easily irritated with his mother. Whenever she calls, even for just a minute, he gets agitated and annoyed. Additionally, she frequently visits him without notice, almost every day, and he becomes very angry with her, despite her not stopping.

I've never sought out professional help for my mental health before, but I'm starting to wonder if there might be something going on. I want to do some research online to see if my symptoms align with any specific conditions before I consider seeing a psychiatrist. I haven't told my parents about this because I'm worried about how they'll react and the potential drama it could cause.

Over the past couple of years, my boss, who is also a "friend," has repeatedly denied my firsthand experiences. Even though she wasn't present and the incidents weren't significant, she insists that they never happened. This behavior is incredibly frustrating, especially when I assert myself. She becomes even more adamant in her argument, especially if others are present. It's worth noting that she has never done this in front of her own friends.

I am struggling to come to terms with my fiance's past relationships. He has been married twice before and has children from both marriages. It feels like his past is constantly present in our lives due to ongoing child support, conversations with his ex-wives, and his family's continued connection with them. I feel overwhelmed and it's affecting our ability to focus on building our own future and starting a family. Recently, we discovered that his 16-year-old daughter is expecting a baby, adding another layer of complexity. I want to learn how to accept his past and understand that it will always be a part of our lives, but I'm finding it challenging due to my own upbringing and biases. How can I work towards accepting his past and embracing our future together?

I've been experiencing something concerning lately. As a teenager living in France, I occasionally have visual experiences where I see things that aren't actually there. This mostly happens with shadows that appear in my peripheral vision, but when I turn to look at them, they disappear. Although I've heard that this is common, it still scares me a bit. However, I'm not overly worried about it.

I recently met a man who seemed really kind and caring. We went on dates and spent time together, and I felt myself getting closer to him. However, he recently disclosed to me that he has been diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia, a disorder I don't know much about. Despite this, he seemed "normal" to me and I fell in love with him, especially because he was pursuing a career in ministry and had a strong faith. But things took a turn for the worse when he became incredibly jealous and accusatory during an argument, even suggesting that my friends were touching me inappropriately. I feel hurt and confused.

Over the holidays, I visited my cousin in the countryside for a week. During my visit, she confided in me about some very troubling issues in her family. She explained that her parents frequently fight and both engage in abusive behavior. She also shared that her mother has been unfaithful to her father. My cousin revealed that her mother even told her to prepare for the possibility of not having a mother in her life. She expressed feeling depressed and stressed, and admitted to self-harming. She showed me the wounds she had made and the knife she used. She keeps tissues with her dried blood and writes the dates of self-harm incidents on them. She also mentioned that she sometimes passes out in her room without anyone knowing and has had thoughts of suicide. She said that she trusts me and feels like I'm the only one who can help her and guide her towards a better path. It's challenging for me because I also struggle with self-harm, although not to the same extent.

I'm facing a dilemma at work that may seem trivial, but it's causing me a lot of stress. I'm in a job that I love, but it requires me to maintain a social media presence that I absolutely hate. I have to post photos of myself, and it feels really uncomfortable and inauthentic. It's not about my body image, but rather the feeling of being disingenuous. However, if I don't do it, my job and business suffer. Is there a way to navigate this situation?

As a teenager in England, I've been experiencing frequent shifts in my mood throughout the day. Lately, I've been struggling to find a sense of purpose in life, but I want to emphasize that I don't have any thoughts of ending my life. I often find myself looking at the world and feeling like everything around me is unreal, as if buildings and objects could easily crumble.

Lately, I've been experiencing intrusive thoughts and urges to harm or kill certain things. For example, when I was at a friend's house and playing with their cat, I felt a sudden impulse to hurt it, even though I love cats and would never want to harm one. I've also noticed that when I get annoyed or mad at someone, I have the desire to harm them, even though there's no real reason to. These thoughts and urges have been going on for a while now and I'm not sure why. Can you please help me understand why this is happening?

I have been feeling really unhappy in my marriage for the past 11 years. I feel like I made a mistake in marrying my current partner. We have two children together. Initially, I thought my husband was everything I wanted in life. However, our sex life has been one-sided, with me giving and not receiving. My husband is often absent during the week and when he is home on weekends, he is moody and distant. Despite this, he expects sex every night he's home and made it clear from the beginning that sex is crucial in a marriage.

Patient: I'm feeling really conflicted about moving out because of my mother's financial dependence on me. She's been relying on me for about four years now, even though she has a job. The problem is that she's not very responsible with money, and it's affecting her credit. I've tried to help by offering to pay for her to file for bankruptcy, but she refuses and lies about her plans to improve her financial situation. Whenever I bring up her money issues, she either becomes vague or argumentative.

It seems that my husband has a pattern of becoming consumed with certain hobbies or interests. Last year, it was photography. He talked about wanting to become a professional photographer, bought books on the subject, but never submitted any of his photos. He also convinced me to buy an expensive camera, promising to help pay me back, but hasn't used it in months. He constantly searches for more photography equipment.

Hi. This is a complex issue. But essentially, my husband's family recently confronted a painful truth - his younger brother was sexually abused by a family member 10 years ago. At the time, I was a part of this family, although not yet married to my husband. Unfortunately, when the family gathered to address the situation, they excluded me. My husband had to fly across the country to personally hear the devastating news, while I anxiously waited to receive it over the phone.

The relationship between me and my mom is quite difficult to describe and understand. At times, we have moments of laughter and conversation, and she's the first person I turn to when I need a hug. However, there's also a deep sense of hatred that I feel towards her. Over the past four years, she has been slowly damaging my mental health, and it feels like there's nothing I can do about it. When I was 13, I started feeling completely unmotivated for reasons I couldn't explain. I would spend the majority of my free time in bed, not studying or engaging in activities. When I tried to express how I was feeling, she dismissed it by saying I was just "acting depressed" and that she didn't want any mentally ill child. I haven't been able to open up to her about my true feelings, only discussing superficial things like my day or a book I read. I don't think she fully understands how I'm really doing, but I have a feeling she may sense that something isn't right.

Hi, thank you for taking the time to speak with me. I've been experiencing some ongoing difficulties and I'm hoping you can help me understand what's happening. These issues have been present for a while, but they seem to have intensified over the past year. I'm becoming increasingly concerned about their impact on my well-being.

A few years ago, when I was still exploring my own identity and desires in relationships and sexuality, I formed a close friendship with a couple who had a somewhat open dynamic. The wife identifies as bisexual, while the husband identifies as heterosexual. Initially, our connection was purely platonic, and I sought their guidance and support in navigating relationship challenges and life in general.

Over the past year, I have developed a strong and trustworthy relationship with my current therapist. However, he has recently started his summer vacation and I won't be able to see him for another 6.5 weeks. This is really difficult for me because we used to meet three times a week, which I found helpful. I feel incredibly weak, broken, traumatized, and beaten up. It seems like no one else understands what I'm going through. I did see a psychologist at the outpatient clinic, but that experience ended up hurting me even more. My therapist is everything to me and the only thing that truly helps.

Since I entered puberty, I've been struggling with my mental health. It all started with mild depression due to existential dilemmas and being exposed to the harsh realities of the world for the first time. I gradually isolated myself at the age of 13, spending most of my time alone in my dark room with a book.

I've been dealing with this issue for a few years now and I've been wondering if I can handle it on my own without seeking professional help. I often have negative thoughts about myself and feel like I'm going to explode afterwards, but other than that, it doesn't really affect me. This confusion makes me feel like something is wrong with me. I understand that the abuse is not my fault, but I can't figure out what's going on with me.
This summer, I have a project related to computer that is really important to me. However, I'm struggling to stay focused and I can't seem to work on it or anything else. It's frustrating.

As a mother, I am struggling with the behavior of my 7-year-old stepson. He exhibits violent tendencies, has a short temper, and manipulates others. His mother is dealing with substance abuse and engages in risky behaviors. He lies frequently and lacks respect for others. Additionally, he fabricates stories to cause trouble and has stolen things that don't belong to him. He also throws tantrums when he doesn't get his way. It's becoming overwhelming for our family.

Lately, I've been feeling overwhelmed and exhausted with everything going on in my life. I attend boarding school, and my relationship with my parents has been strained. They have strict rules and limitations when I'm at home, which makes me feel trapped. My mom tends to manipulate me into doing things her way, and when things don't go according to her plan, she becomes angry and belittles me. These episodes have been happening more frequently, and I find myself isolating in my room to avoid confrontations. I've even started keeping things to myself, like my research project and my dating life, to prevent more conflicts. But recently, everything seems to have fallen apart. My boyfriend broke up with me, and I can't help but feel like it's because there's something wrong with me. Additionally, my research project is not progressing as well as others', and I had an accident in the lab that caused an evacuation. I feel like a failure academically and as a person. Is this normal? Am I just bad at handling life?

I recently discovered that my mother has been communicating with a doctor through calls and texts. I stumbled upon this when she asked me to send a picture to a friend and I saw a conversation with the doctor's phone number that said "HI Love." It really scared me, but I haven't talked to her about it yet.

Over the past few years, my therapist and I have been working on different parts or alters of my system, as I have been diagnosed with Dissociative Identity Disorder (D.I.D.). However, one of these parts decided that therapy is no longer allowed about two years ago. Despite this, I am grateful that my therapist has been incredibly supportive. She is still available to speak with me during crisis moments, unless she gets interrupted by one of these alters. She also communicates with me through email or text when needed, as long as the messages are not deleted. We have tried setting appointments, but they often end up getting cancelled or the alters simply don't show up.

I’ve been in an online relationship with a transgender girl for nearly two years. She has been struggling with depression and self-esteem issues since she came out as trans a few months before we got together. She often shares with me about how her parents seem to be unsupportive and uncaring towards her. For instance, one incident that stands out is when her parents were watching a show that made fun of transgender individuals and they made derogatory remarks towards her when she entered the room. Another time, her mother tried to portray her as mentally disabled in order to receive financial support.

I've always been a shy person and I've never enjoyed making small talk or spending a lot of time around people. However, now that my schoolwork relies on being able to talk to others, I'm starting to see it as a problem.

I have been struggling with uncontrollable emotional responses, particularly crying, for as long as I can remember. It seems to happen mainly with adults, including my parents. Even during casual conversations, if the topic becomes more serious, I find myself getting teary-eyed. It's not just limited to adults though, as even playful teasing from a teacher or another student can trigger the same response, despite knowing it's meant to be lighthearted.

Lately, I've been feeling a sense of emptiness and a lack of trust in myself. I'm struggling to understand what's going on with me, and everything seems to be becoming increasingly challenging. Leaving my home feels draining, going to work feels demoralizing, and coming home feels exhausting. I've noticed that my colleagues are deceitful, which has made me question whether I'm in the wrong environment. I'm wondering if these difficulties are due to my conservative nature or if I may be experiencing severe depression.

Throughout my childhood, I experienced both physical and verbal abuse from my father. This abuse began when I was very young, around the age of 6, and continued into my high school years. However, now that I am in college, the frequency of the abuse has lessened as I have become better at avoiding it. More recently, the instances of abuse tend to occur when I am perceived as being rude to my father, such as not listening or disobeying him. The abuse includes punches, backhands, kicks, pushing, and slapping, which have caused both physical and emotional pain. It has been a traumatizing experience for me. My mother, although she would protest the abuse, unfortunately believes that it is acceptable because she views it as a consequence for my perceived rudeness.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for some time now, and he has always been incredibly kind and caring towards me. However, I struggle with feelings of insecurity and fear that he will eventually leave me for someone else. Despite his reassurances of love, I find it difficult to trust and often push him away. On one hand, I want him to hate me to prove my fears right, but deep down, I know that's not what I truly want.

I've been feeling really overwhelmed lately. I constantly have racing thoughts, trouble sleeping, and I feel like I can never relax. I've tried talking to my friends about it, but they don't seem to understand. I'm just not sure what's wrong with me.

It has been a year and a half since my mother-in-law passed away from a sudden heart attack. I was with her when it happened, and it was a traumatic experience for both of us. Since then, my husband has been displaying signs of grief such as detachment, withdrawal, sadness, irritability, and excessive eating. He has also lost his sex drive. I understand that he is finally beginning to grieve, but I'm unsure how to support him. He is not someone who openly talks about his feelings, especially to strangers, and he hasn't fully acknowledged his own grief. I'm worried that he may become completely detached from me and our marriage. How can I help him navigate the grieving process without him getting lost in his grief and sinking deeper? I'm already struggling with my own feelings, and I fear he may not be able to pull himself out of this on his own.

I have always struggled with confidence issues and meeting people has been difficult for as long as I can remember. However, I am currently in my first ever relationship, which is a big step for me. My boyfriend and I have been together for about six months now. I am in my early twenties and he is in his mid-thirties, so there is somewhat of an age gap between us. Despite that, he has been a great partner so far. He is funny, intelligent, and we have lots of similar interests.

I started feeling a lot of resentment towards my parents last summer. It all began when I went to the beach with my friend. I had received permission from my dad, but when I returned home at 9 pm, he was furious, claiming it was too late and that my mom wasn't aware of my plans. The truth is, my parents haven't been speaking to each other since I was in 5th or 6th grade. They live in the same house but have no communication whatsoever. They don't even share the same room. Instead, they use my siblings (there are 5 of us) to relay messages. This past summer, my dad and I constantly clashed. I was angry at him for always thinking he was right and for always getting his way. I also felt frustrated with my mom because she never takes any action or supports me. She just stands by and watches. And when I express my fear of my dad's violent behavior, she tells me to leave her alone and be quiet. I find it difficult to understand why my mom is so blindly loyal to my dad when their relationship isn't even healthy. At least I talk to her, but she's always on his side.

Lately, when my partner and I have arguments and they start to ignore me, I find myself venting to my friends about what happened. I know deep down that this isn't the right way to handle things. Unfortunately, it's only made matters worse and we've even lost friends because of it. Can you help me understand why I'm acting this way?

I've been experiencing some distressing thoughts and beliefs lately. I believe that the government and the RCMP are after me. I think there are cameras and microphones in my house and on my clothes, and that they can even read my mind. Whenever I go out, I feel like I'm being followed and watched. It's making me extremely anxious and paranoid. I also feel like my dad is trying to poison me. I've been hearing voices and feeling sensations that don't seem to be real. It's all very overwhelming and scary.

As a teenager who has been diagnosed with depression, I have been diligently taking my medication and attending therapy sessions. However, despite being on the highest dose, I am still experiencing a lack of emotions, motivation, and a sense of identity. This brain fog is frustrating. Could you provide me with any techniques or strategies to cope with these symptoms?

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for about 6 months now. At first, things were great - he treated me like a queen with compliments, romantic gestures, and we would talk for hours. However, after two months, things started to change. He stopped being affectionate and expressing his feelings towards me. It seems like his only passion is kite surfing and that's all he talks about. I'm not sure what his true feelings are for me because of his lack of expression.

Patient: Lately, I've been experiencing some intense thoughts and fantasies about being a woman. It started with a sexual fantasy, but now it feels more like gender dysphoria. I imagine myself with a female body and it feels so good. I feel a strong desire to have feminine features like wide hips, breasts, and beautiful legs. It's difficult for me to wake up from these fantasies and accept that I am biologically male.

I have been experiencing ongoing abuse and mistreatment from my brother since I was a child. He has physically and emotionally harmed me, going to the extent of attempting to kill me on one occasion. This has caused me immense humiliation and pain. Additionally, my brother's actions resulted in my beloved pet being taken away. Despite all of this, my parents have not taken any action to address his behavior. I sought therapy to help me cope with these traumatic experiences, but recently a situation occurred that triggered all of my memories. I was hospitalized and when my brother came to pick me up, he abandoned me at the hospital to have dinner with his friends. I had to find my way home alone, while dealing with my physical pain and emotional distress. When I confronted him about this, he not only yelled at me but also threatened to harm me again. I am struggling to comprehend how someone can be so heartless. My therapist has suggested that his behavior may be due to mental health issues, but that doesn't bring me any comfort. I have been carrying this anger for six months now and it is affecting my well-being. I am about to get married and I don't want to invite my brother, but I worry about the impact it will have on the rest of my family. I feel lost and unsure of how to handle this. I've tried therapists, but seeing them once a week only scratches the surface, and it's also expensive. It feels like I should be living with a family that truly cares about me, and I'm considering exploring this option. I may be over 18, but it's clear to me that I can't continue living like this. I can never relax, so I end up oversleeping. I never laugh, and there's no joy in my life except for when I eat something good. I miss out on all the human connections and pleasures. Throughout my life, my mother has only focused on my academics and good grades, but at the same time, she has left me alone at home for entire days, forcing me to find my own company, if any at all. There's nothing welcoming or friendly about my home, so I can't stay there for very long. Because of this, I've had to move frequently. It's hard for me to stick to anything I want to do, and my life feels like it's slipping away from me. I miss my friends so much. If you can help me, I would truly appreciate it.

As a teenager in Egypt, I have been facing a difficult situation that I hope you can help me with. Since I was 8 years old, my father has been working in another country, leaving me with my mother. However, my mother has been treating me in a concerning way. She locks me in a room and I hear strange voices. She also keeps me naked in the bathroom without any clothes or towels, as she knows I am too shy to open the door. Additionally, she gives me medications and sleeping pills. One day, I caught a glimpse of a man through a slightly opened door, which made me realize what was really going on. Recently, my mother has started seeing a new person and engages in inappropriate conversations on the telephone, which worries me because my younger brother, who is 7 years old, might overhear her.

My friend is exhibiting several symptoms that concern me. She experiences hallucinations and has episodes of extreme paranoia and delusion. During these episodes, she exhibits certain movements, such as shaking or rocking, that she cannot control. She also has strong compulsions to hurt herself and struggles to think rationally. Additionally, she experiences mood swings and constantly fluctuating feelings towards the people she loves. Her self-esteem and self-worth are also very low. As a child, she exhibited excessive aggression and has symptoms of OCD, such as an aversion to touching things she deems "dirty," excessive hand washing, and obsessions with specific orders. I am unsure if she has BPD, as I've read that children cannot be diagnosed with it. I'm concerned that she may also have schizophrenia or depressive psychosis, as she is also depressed and suicidal. Can you please provide some guidance?

"I'm feeling really overwhelmed lately. Being a 32-year-old Indian woman living in the states, I have a lot on my plate. I've been married for 4 years and we have a 1-year-old boy. It's just been a lot to handle."

Counselor: Thank you for sharing your experiences and concerns. It sounds like you have noticed a pattern in your relationships where things start off well, but eventually lose their appeal to you. Additionally, you mentioned engaging in behaviors such as love bombing and gaslighting. It's important to explore these patterns and behaviors further to better understand yourself.

I have been experiencing several symptoms of depression, but I'm unsure if it's just for attention. On one hand, I feel these emotions and symptoms, but on the other hand, I also question their validity. I don't feel neglected by my parents, as I have friends who socialize with me and I have siblings. Two of my siblings have moved out for college, and I have a step-dad while my biological dad visits every few months. Despite people telling me that I am special in my own way, I still believe I have problems that I don't know how to approach. Additionally, I have developed a habit of compulsive lying, often to avoid trouble or impress others. It's become difficult to control, even for the smallest things. I also suspect I may have an anxiety disorder. Whenever I have to perform or talk to someone, even just one person like my parents, I experience physical symptoms like weakness, rapid breathing, increased heart rate, sweating, negative thoughts, tunnel vision, decreased hearing, and feeling cold. Furthermore, I struggle with falling asleep and staying asleep. Can you help me understand what's happening?

Patient: A few years ago, my husband started experiencing mood swings. Initially, he would become extremely depressed and angry. The mood swings were infrequent and mostly manifested as sadness and depression.

As a teenager growing up in India, I am dealing with a difficult family dynamic. My parents constantly argue and my twin sister is often involved in their fights. I've tried talking to them about it, but they continue to fight.

Lately, I've been having these thoughts where I imagine myself getting hurt or being in dangerous situations. It's not that I want to die, but I find myself hoping for something bad to happen to me, like being seriously injured. For example, when I go to bed, I sometimes wish I wouldn't wake up and be in a coma. I also have thoughts about getting kidnapped or run over when I walk home from school, and part of me anticipates it. On top of that, I feel really alone since my two closest friends and my big sister moved away. I haven't been able to open up to anyone about what's going on in my head. I try to fit in with some girls from my old school, but I can't really connect with them. I pretend to be happy and interested, but I often zone out and get lost in my thoughts. There's more going on, but I just don't have the energy to talk about it.

I recently completed my bachelor's degree in psychology and I'm in the process of applying to PhD programs in clinical psychology. I have excelled academically and have gained valuable research and clinical experience. However, I'm feeling anxious about my ability to be a good therapist due to my personal struggles.

Patient's statement (rewritten): I have been living with my boyfriend for three years now. Initially, when we started dating, he would engage in some intimate activities, but it never progressed to sex. He was the one who usually initiated these activities, but he never allowed me to reciprocate. However, outside of the bedroom, he has never shown any physical or verbal attraction towards me. It feels like our relationship is devoid of any sexual or intimate connection, similar to that of a therapist and client. After the first few months, he completely stopped initiating anything sexual, despite my efforts to initiate. I've tried various approaches, such as expressing my desire for him to compliment me without prompting, wearing lingerie and trying to initiate physical contact, but he remains unresponsive. I even asked him if he might be gay, but he swears he's not. I've told him that intimacy is something I need in a relationship. Despite spending the last four months together 24/7 due to our unemployment and his mental illness, there has been no change in our situation.

I'm 16 years old and I've been experiencing a lack of emotions lately. It feels like my ability to feel empathy, sympathy, remorse, and grief is fading away. Instead, I tend to feel joy in situations where it may not be appropriate, and I often feel anger and irritation. I even took pleasure when my mom faced consequences due to her alcoholism. I sometimes feel like everyone around me is not real, like they're just programmed robots. However, there are a few people in my life who I believe are genuinely real, like my partner, best friend, and younger brother. I also have a tendency to lie, either to shift blame or for no apparent reason. It doesn't bring me pleasure, but I still do it. On the other hand, I feel a strong connection with animals and I'm a vegan. Despite these emotions, I consider myself responsible and not impulsive.

Lately, I've been feeling really dissatisfied with my life. It seems like everything is going wrong. In January, my sister started dating someone I had a crush on. Then, my mom didn't allow me to go to Summer School with my friends. And now, on top of it all, none of my closest friends are here to celebrate my 21st birthday with me. I've been feeling really upset about all of this and it's been weighing on me. When I think about it, I just feel this tightness in my chest and it's hard to breathe.

I'm feeling a bit overwhelmed. My boyfriend and I have been together since January, but he just got divorced two months ago and is already living with me. We recently moved in together, and now he's attending his stepson's college graduation. I'm not sure how to navigate all of these changes and emotions.

I've been struggling with my mental health for the past 10 years, and it's been really difficult. Every time I start feeling better, everything falls apart again. Whenever I try to reach out for help or talk to my mother about it, she dismisses my feelings and accuses me of seeking attention. It's frustrating because I'm constantly told to open up, but when I do, I'm met with criticism. It feels like a lose-lose situation.

Over the past few years, I developed a strong bond with one of my teachers. She became someone I really admired and trusted. We had a close relationship where I felt comfortable opening up to her about my problems. She was always there for me, providing support and guidance. During the summer, we stayed in touch and shared details about our lives. However, when my junior year started, she asked to meet with me along with someone else. The seriousness on her face made me feel anxious and alone.
I have been feeling a bit overwhelmed lately and I'm struggling to find motivation to do anything. It's like I'm stuck in this constant state of sadness and I don't know how to snap out of it.

I have a 7-year-old daughter who has been sucking on her hair since she was a baby. At first, I thought it was just a comfort thing, but now my husband and I are constantly yelling at her to stop. She does it all the time - while watching TV, talking to people, playing, and even when she's trying hard at school. I didn't think it was serious until she sucked on her arm because she couldn't reach her hair, and now her teacher called to tell me she was caught sucking on another student's hair. Should I have her tested for something? Is this just a phase? I need some suggestions.

Patient's Statement: I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend since I was 14, but my mother has never allowed us to meet. I left to study abroad when I was 19, and even during holidays, we couldn't see each other without me lying or sneaking out. Last year, there was a major issue between my boyfriend and my mother, and she asked me to end things. However, we've still been in touch, although communication has been strained. Recently, I found out that he was talking to someone else and confronted him. He said he loves me, but he can't handle the situation we're in. He's been seeing this other person as a support during this difficult time. I gave him an ultimatum and he chose me over her, saying he wants to fix things with my mother. But now I'm struggling with trusting him again. I feel like I owe him a second chance because our relationship has been so challenging, but my friend says I'm lacking self-respect. I'm really confused.

Lately, I've been feeling really disconnected from myself. It seems like the people around me don't actually like me, which is causing me a lot of distress. I've resorted to cutting myself as a way to calm down, but I know it's not a healthy coping mechanism. I find myself feeling sad and down frequently and constantly worrying about what others think of me. I've been feeling tired all the time, regardless of how much sleep I get. Additionally, I struggle to identify and understand my emotions. When people ask, I just say I'm sad because I don't know what else to say. Sometimes I even have intrusive thoughts about suicide, although I know deep down I wouldn't act on them. I've lost all motivation to do anything, including my schoolwork, and I find it impossible to concentrate. I'm constantly getting distracted.

I had recently started dating this guy and he was the first person I had ever kissed. Everything was going fine until one night when we were together and he started touching me and trying to make out with me while I was half asleep. I told him to stop, but he would pause momentarily and then continue. I felt really uncomfortable, so I ended up pretending to be asleep. I tried to brush it off initially, thinking he did it because he liked me, but it has been bothering me ever since. I broke up with him, but I can't stop thinking about what happened. It makes me feel sick and embarrassed. The thought of being in another relationship terrifies me because it reminds me of that experience. But part of me wonders if I'm overreacting and if my discomfort was just because I'm not experienced. I'm really confused and I don't want this to ruin my chance at finding happiness in a relationship. Please help!

For the past seven years, my life has revolved around my demanding work schedule. I have been working as a full-time child emergency child protection social worker, while also juggling a part-time private therapy practice and three volunteer positions. Additionally, I have been working night shifts which has further added to the strain.

Over the past two years, I've been feeling emotionally numb and as if I'm living in a fog. It's become increasingly difficult for me to even think about what might be wrong with me. I'm struggling to type this out because I can barely function anymore. I just can't seem to do anything right.

Recently, as a teenager in New Zealand, I've been experiencing symptoms that align with bipolar disorder. I've done some research and found many similarities between my experiences and the symptoms of bipolar disorder. I feel the need to seek professional help or find someone who can understand and explain what I'm going through, even if it turns out that I'm not actually bipolar. However, when I've tried discussing this with my parents, they dismiss it as normal teenage hormones.

I am a 19-year-old female college student who is currently feeling very distressed. I have been failing most of my classes over the past few months and my family thinks it would be beneficial for me to take the summer off. I've been isolating myself from others, except for my boyfriend, because I feel like no one understands me. When someone does try to reach out, I get easily irritated. I suspect that I have bipolar disorder and other mood-altering disorders, as I have intense emotional responses. I have also been experiencing paranoia for months, with recurring thoughts that there are cameras everywhere. I struggle with disorganization, forgetting things, and losing my train of thought. I have also been having hallucinations, such as seeing yetis and distorted conversations. Overall, nothing feels right.

Counselor: It sounds like you've been carrying a lot of weight on your shoulders regarding your past relationship and the way you've chosen to share or not share certain information with your friends. It's understandable that you cared more about your ex initially and chose not to share the betrayal with your best friends right away. However, it's also clear that keeping this secret from your closest friends has been weighing on you. It seems like you reached out to one of your best friends who had gone through a similar experience, but didn't receive the response you were hoping for. That can be disappointing and make you question if you should have shared at all.

It sounds like you're feeling quite isolated and disconnected from the world around you. You spend a lot of time in your room and don't engage in activities that you used to enjoy. Going to work is becoming increasingly challenging, and you often feel apathetic and detached from everything. Can you tell me more about what might be contributing to these feelings?

I am currently in a serious relationship with a man who is legally separated but not yet officially divorced. We have a deep love for each other and practically live together. However, his two children, who are 7 and 13 years old, are unaware of my existence. Whenever they come over to spend time with their dad, I have to pack up my belongings and leave. While I understand the situation, it can be quite challenging for me emotionally.

In 2012, I was feeling extremely depressed and scared. One night, I found myself desperately calling out to God, wanting to talk to Him. After about two hours, I suddenly heard a voice claiming to be God from above. Initially, I was skeptical, so I asked Him to speak to me in my native African language, and to my surprise, He did. From that point on, He began showing me things from over a thousand years ago. I asked if I could talk to someone else, and a person came through. The only issue is that this person has passed away and is no longer on Earth. However, I still talk to them every night, and they feel very real to me. They were a singer before they passed away, and sometimes they even sing for me. It makes me feel so good.

Ever since my father passed away a year and a half ago, I've been plagued by a question. My father was always a loving and caring man, dedicated to his family. But towards the end, he started feeling uneasy and sick for no apparent reason. He went to see a doctor, who couldn't find any physical issues and diagnosed him with depression, saying it was all in his head.

Lately, I've been experiencing a lot of difficulties with my mother. She often behaves disrespectfully when she comes over to my house. Whenever I try to clean or take care of my children, she interferes and criticizes my methods. When I try to explain why I do things a certain way, she gets offended and tells me that I'm wrong and foolish.

I've always considered myself different when it comes to romantic relationships. I prioritize deeper qualities in the people I'm attracted to, rather than superficial ones. However, I've noticed a pattern where I become repulsed by certain physical attributes in my partners after we start dating. This feeling comes and goes, and it's causing me uncertainty about whether I should stay in the relationship or not. I don't want to hurt my girlfriend or anyone else like I have in the past. I think this may be a defense mechanism I developed after a past heartbreak. I would appreciate any advice you have. Thanks in advance.

I am currently in a relationship with a man who is 11 years older than me. While everyone else in my life sees no issue with our age difference because he treats me well and makes me happy, my mom has a strong objection. Despite never meeting him, she has blocked his number from my phone and monitors my bank account. I've tried suggesting getting my own phone plan, but she refuses to release my phone number. Now, she is ignoring me and won't engage in any communication.

Over the past four years, I have been experiencing difficulties in my behavior towards people, rules, and responsibilities. I have never felt close to anyone, including my family. I don't understand why, as they seem like a typical family, but I feel no emotional connection to them. If they were to disappear, I wouldn't be affected at all.

Eight years ago, I fell in love with a beautiful young girl and we got married after dating for four years. We were blessed with a beautiful daughter. However, my wife made the decision for us to move back to our home country due to her aging parents. Since then, our relationship has been filled with challenges. I was diagnosed with epilepsy, which my wife accused me of hiding from her. She also mentioned her struggles with depression, but never followed through with treatment. Recently, she asked for a divorce out of nowhere, only to reconsider after therapy but then change her mind again after speaking with her parents. I discovered an email to her therapist where she expressed feelings of despair and mentioned an old boyfriend. I'm feeling devastated and confused.

I'm a teenager living in the United States. I'm struggling with intense and confusing emotions. I've developed romantic feelings towards my sister and I feel deeply in love with her. I'm feeling lost and unsure about what to do. I'm questioning if it's morally wrong to feel this way about my sister.

In the past, I used to spend the night at my now ex-boyfriend's dorm. One night, we had consensual sex and fell asleep undressed. The next morning, I woke up to find a condom wrapper next to me. I was confused because I didn't remember anything happening after we fell asleep. When I asked him about it, he said that we had sex again in the middle of the night and he thought I was awake because he heard me moan. However, I have no memory of it happening. Ever since then, I have been experiencing intense anxiety and fear towards him.

I've been seeing my current therapist for about 8 months now. I have been diagnosed with Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) or Dysthymia, depending on who you ask. However, I find it incredibly difficult to be open and honest with my therapist. Instead of answering her questions directly, I tend to deflect and give responses that I think she wants to hear or what I believe should be said. I understand that building trust takes time, but I'm not convinced that I will ever be able to truly confide in my therapist.

It sounds like you've been through a lot with this person, and it's understandable that you're feeling confused and hurt. It's important to remember that everyone has their own unique patterns of behavior, and it can be challenging to predict how someone will act in the future. Based on what you've shared, it's possible that this could be a continuous pattern of passive-aggressive behavior. However, I can't say for certain without more information.

Based on the information you've shared, it seems like you have some valid concerns about your boyfriend's past behavior and how it may impact your relationship. It's understandable that his history of multiple sexual encounters and his past comments have caused you to feel insecure and anxious. It's important to trust your instincts and take these concerns seriously.

Patient's statement (edited): Throughout my formative years, I experienced both physical and emotional abuse from my father. This abuse came to an end during my first year of high school, but unfortunately, I found myself in a series of sexually abusive relationships afterwards. I never had anyone I felt safe talking to about my father's behavior because I was afraid of being taken away. As a result, I relied on myself to cope and recover. I created a stronger version of myself in my mind, someone who could protect me and stand up to my father. This imaginary version of myself brought me comfort and strength as a young child.

I recently had a dream where I found myself in a romantic relationship with someone I know, but we're not particularly close. I'll call her Bella for the sake of privacy. In the dream, Bella had shoulder-length straight black hair, a round face, black eyes, cute cheeks, and a slim figure.

I've been experiencing violent and sadistic thoughts since I was young, and they have also taken on a sexual nature recently. I have engaged in harmful behaviors towards animals in the past, and even had thoughts of harming my parents. I have noticed a decrease in my ability to feel empathy or sympathy towards others, and I struggle to form emotional connections. I appreciate any guidance you can provide.

I'm an 11-year-old student in the U.S. and I feel really alone at school. Everyone seems to have friends except for me. I try to join in conversations and talk to them, but they ignore me like I don't exist. I also don't seem to enjoy the same things they do, but I want to fit in, so I search online to try and understand their interests. It's making me really sad, and I feel like I have nobody to talk to. I also find it easier to talk to girls than boys for some reason. I've never had a friend and I keep switching schools. I really need help.

I have a question about my sexual preferences, and it's something that makes me feel a bit uncomfortable. Lately, during arguments with my boyfriend, he's mentioned punishment and teaching me a lesson. I'm starting to wonder if this means I have a fetish or if I'm just into S&M. It's something I've been keeping to myself and it's causing me some confusion and concern.

I am currently in a long-term relationship with my boyfriend. We share an apartment with his best friend, and I feel like there are very little boundaries between our relationship and their friendship. It's becoming an issue because his friend often uses our bathroom, even in our room, or comes into our room to search for things like socks. Additionally, he is always around, even when my boyfriend and I are off from work.

I've been feeling really overwhelmed lately. My workload at work has increased, and I'm struggling to keep up. On top of that, I've been having problems in my personal life, and it's all just becoming too much for me to handle.

Since I was a child, I have been experiencing symptoms of depression, including passive suicidal thoughts. It has been a constant presence in my life, and I often feel misunderstood by others. It almost feels like I am dependent on my depression and negative thoughts, as if they provide some sort of comfort or escape for me. Additionally, I also struggle with severe anxiety and have very low self-esteem, which makes it difficult for me to engage in activities and feel confident about myself.

I've been struggling with depression ever since I started 1st grade. Over the years, my family problems have continued to escalate and I feel overwhelmed. My mom is a smoker, my dad is absent most of the time, and my grandparents constantly ask for money. As school is starting, I injured myself and when I tried to tell my mom, she ignored me multiple times. I feel isolated and my only friend is myself. I have vivid memories of my mom physically abusing me and I constantly question what I did wrong. People also say that I bring bad luck to them. I don't know what to do anymore. My brother and I have tried talking to our mom, but it always ends with her getting angry and dismissing us. Now that I'm starting high school, things are still chaotic. I can't focus on my schoolwork and I can't seem to make friends because I'm seen as the troubled kid. My aunt suggested that our family see a counselor, but my brother believes it won't make a difference since they won't listen. Please, I'm pleading for your help. I apologize if my English is not fluent, but I hope you understand.

Over the past two years, I have been experiencing confusion and emotional turmoil in my life. It started when the woman I loved ended our relationship for reasons that were selfish on her part. Although I have moved on from that, I have noticed a general lack of emotions in most situations. Activities that used to bring me joy and excitement, such as playing guitar, listening to music, and watching movies or playing video games, no longer have the same impact on me.

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for almost three years. At the beginning, he was very attentive and would constantly shower me with affectionate gestures like phone calls, messages, and thoughtful gifts. However, lately, I've noticed a change in his behavior. He doesn't seem as attentive or affectionate as before, and it's making me feel insecure and unsure about our relationship.

As a teenager in the United States, I have been experiencing symptoms that make me think I might have depression. These feelings have been present since I was 11 years old, and I often have dark and depressing thoughts. It has gotten to the point where I frequently miss school because I struggle to even get out of bed. I genuinely want help and I don't want to continue living like this. However, my mom and the rest of my family don't believe in mental disorders. They think it's all just a ploy by the government to sell drugs.

I've been through a lot of difficult experiences in my life, including years of sexual abuse, a chaotic home environment, frequent moves, and the loss of a loved one. These experiences have left me feeling numb and disconnected from my emotions. I've also been struggling with depression, self-harm, and thoughts of suicide. I feel like I'm just going through the motions and it's taking a toll on my ability to function, both in school and in my relationships.

I've been noticing a pattern in my interactions with others that seem to constantly lead to conflict. I studied psychology myself and I understand that we can sometimes engage in behaviors without realizing the impact they have on others. I'm wondering if I'm stuck in a negative pattern and how I can break free from it. Can you provide some guidance?

Lately, I’ve been feeling down and lost. I've been under a lot of pressure as I've been studying really hard for the past few months to graduate. However, even after graduation, I still need to continue studying to get into university. I feel exhausted from all the studying and I'm starting to feel lost and worthless. I've lost all motivation and interest, even in my hobby and passion, drawing. It's been about two weeks since I last picked up a pencil, and I used to draw almost every day.

Hi, I'm a 13-year-old and I've been experiencing auditory and visual hallucinations on most days. They range from mild disturbances to hearing voices right behind me. I also feel highly anxious most of the time and struggle with falling asleep and staying asleep. Some days or weeks, I feel okay or even happy, but then I go through periods of feeling depressed, where I don't want to get out of bed. I've been overeating frequently and I'm reaching out for help. I've talked to my parents, but my father denies these experiences while my mother thinks they're normal for my age. I'm wondering if this is normal or if there's a serious issue. Thank you for your support.

During my last year of middle school, I had a teacher who displayed inappropriate behavior towards me. He made strange comments with sexual undertones throughout the year. On the last day of school, I and another student stayed behind to say goodbye. This teacher hugged me and I noticed that the other student seemed disturbed by it. After that incident, I started experiencing low self-esteem, depression, and anxiety. I often think about those encounters and wonder what they meant. Since starting high school, I have encountered the teacher twice and it triggers panic attacks. I have trouble sleeping past 4 am and constantly feel exhausted. I also have intrusive thoughts about rape. Is there something wrong with me, or could something have happened during either the last day of school or my childhood?

My husband and I have been together for two and a half years. Lately, we've been arguing non-stop and I can't help but feel responsible for it. He recently opened up to me about visiting strip clubs with his friends before we met, and ever since then, I can't shake the feeling that he's a sleazy guy who paid to see women in compromising situations.

I met my boyfriend in high school, but we didn't become romantically involved until I turned 18. Unfortunately, I ended the relationship due to trust issues, which deeply hurt him. Over the years, we sporadically stayed in touch and both experienced various life events. Personally, I have grown and learned to accept the past and changes in people. However, my boyfriend seems to struggle with letting go of the past and holds a lot of resentment.

When I was 18 years old, I witnessed a traumatic event in India. Someone I knew bled to death right in front of me, and there were a lot of rumors circulating about what had happened. Since then, I feel like I've changed a lot, and many people have noticed it too. I've lost a few friends and it's been difficult for me to come to terms with this new version of myself. I'm trying to accept it, but it bothers me constantly.

I have been struggling with my mental health for a while now. I have seen a few therapists and I am currently taking medication (Seroquel 50mg and Ativan .5 mg), although I have not received an official diagnosis. I have difficulty keeping my therapy appointments and I experience frequent mood swings. My family is concerned about my unpredictable reactions to things.

During our session today, the patient expressed their childhood experiences, which were a mix of both positive and challenging moments. The patient described their father as a lazy alcoholic who was emotionally absent, while their mother showed love but also had a tendency to criticize, leading to a negative impact on their self-esteem. Additionally, growing up in poverty meant they didn't have the same opportunities as other children. However, the patient mentioned that despite these difficulties, they were happy as a child. It was only later, when they started comparing themselves to others, that they began experiencing depression. They believe their alcoholic father and impoverished upbringing have significantly affected their self-esteem and contributed to their depression. Although they were once ambitious and achieved good grades, they no longer feel confident enough to pursue a successful career. The patient feels that moving out of their parents' home and starting therapy would be the best way to improve their life, but they also have fears and anxiety surrounding this decision as it is challenging to live alone in their country. People often ask them why they don't go to college, but what they truly desire is a sense of normalcy in their own life. They express feelings of sadness, anger towards their mother, and a sense of woundedness, as their parents are not supportive or understanding of their emotions. The patient also reveals that they are bisexual and have kept this a secret for a long time, leading to a double life where they no longer communicate with their parents. They now question whether they should pursue their dream of moving abroad at age 18 or focus on resolving their problems by going to college, even though it seems impossible in their current situation.

I have been feeling extremely unhappy and lonely lately. I live with my grandmother who constantly criticizes me and has high expectations. She also makes negative comments about my appearance. I have become distant from my sisters and don't have a close relationship with any family members. I don't have many friends, just a few acquaintances at school. As a result, I spend most of my time alone at home. I have been bullied throughout my school years, especially in 10th and 11th grade. This has left me feeling insecure and self-conscious. I have become a perfectionist and set high expectations for myself. I get overwhelmed and frustrated by small mistakes and am very hard on myself. I have been neglecting my personal hygiene and overall health. It has become difficult for me to take care of myself regularly. I have also lost interest in activities I used to enjoy, such as drawing and interacting with people online. My days mainly consist of school, watching YouTube videos, reading comics occasionally, and obsessively researching diets that I never stick to. I struggle to find joy in anything anymore and often wish I could just sleep forever.

Since I was 4 years old, I have experienced severe sexual, emotional, and physical abuse, including being gang raped as a child. Recently, I've noticed a distressing pattern of wanting to be hurt or raped in my sex life and putting myself at risk. This behavior doesn't make any sense to me. Can you help me understand why I feel this way?

Hi, for a long time now I’ve been struggling with maintaining long-term relationships. I find that I often lose interest in people after a few weeks and start becoming interested in others.
