This pattern also affects my relationships, as I unconsciously act out as a jealous girlfriend or a bossy person, creating scenarios in my head and leading my relationships down those paths. This has resulted in a lack of long-lasting relationships. Honestly, I'm scared that I might lose myself. What should I do?

I have been experiencing a range of distressing symptoms that are causing me a lot of anxiety and paranoia. I have been seeing things like shadows, faces, and even demons, as well as cats that aren't really there. Additionally, I occasionally hear voices, mostly people yelling at me, but the hallucinations happen more frequently. I constantly feel like I'm being watched or followed, and right now, I have a strong belief that there is someone outside my bedroom door. I have this strange feeling that my reflection in the TV is actually a supernatural creature watching me. I also have developed a fear of eating food that wasn't prepared by myself due to worries about it being poisoned or tampered with. Earlier, when my mom tried to comfort me during an anxiety attack, I had an intense feeling that she was going to harm me. In public, I often feel like people are laughing or talking about me, leading to a lack of trust in others. I have covered all the cameras on my devices because I believe the government is watching me. Although I have considered schizophrenia, I am aware that something is not right with me, which seems different from what I've read. Mental health challenges run in my family, with various members experiencing anxiety, depression, anorexia, and bipolar disorder. My mom even thinks I might be clairvoyant. I am feeling nervous about reaching out for help, but I wanted to ask if it would be advisable for me to seek assistance.

Lately, I've been experiencing some troubling symptoms. I find myself spacing out randomly and seeing tall silhouettes and people following me, even though no one is actually there. I also hear a voice in my head that whispers to me throughout the day, but it becomes more intense at night. Sometimes, this voice tells me to do strange things like hide under a desk or confess my love or hatred to a stranger. It's even more distressing when it urges me to harm myself or others. The voice seems to have control over my thoughts and emotions, influencing how I feel about people. I also have this strong belief that people can read my thoughts, at least most of them. It's frustrating because nobody else believes me and I'm desperate for answers. Thank you for listening.

During my time in primary school, I experienced bullying from younger children. They would make fun of my weight, which was incredibly embarrassing for me. I never told anyone about it. When I transitioned to secondary school at the age of 12, the bullying stopped, but I developed an unhealthy relationship with food. I started dieting, and it gradually escalated to the point where I became dangerously thin by the time I turned 13. I believed that even eating something as innocent as a banana would cause me to gain a significant amount of weight.

I've been experiencing some symptoms that make me think I may be experiencing depersonalization (DP). I feel like my world is surreal and I have a sense of detachment from my body. I want people to see me for who I am mentally, rather than just my physical appearance. It's like my body is a puppet and my mind is the one controlling it. Sometimes I feel like my body is not my own and I struggle to recognize myself in the mirror. I have moments where I snap out of this surreal state, either randomly or due to certain triggers. During these moments, everything feels unfamiliar and I become hypersensitive to my surroundings. It's like I don't even know who I am anymore. I hesitate to label it as DP because I've had a tendency to think I have various disorders in the past, but in this case, the symptoms were present before I even learned about DP.

I have been diagnosed with complex post-traumatic stress disorder (CPTSD) and major depressive disorder (MDD). My therapist and I are still exploring what treatment approaches work best for me. Lately, I've been disengaging and even broke my sobriety before a session. Despite this, we did an anger exercise in which I experienced some release, although I also felt it could be dangerous to do alone. I reached out to my therapist for an additional appointment because I have been in crisis. However, she asked if I wanted a referral, which made me feel like she was questioning if she wanted to continue working with me. I expressed my feelings about this in an email, including my anger and frustration with the progress. I feel uncertain now because she mentioned being unsure of what works for me and if she can meet my needs, she may refer me out. Today, she arrived 10 minutes late to our session without an apology. She mentioned she had 10 minutes to finish her lunch, and then proceeded to her office after 15 minutes. During the session, I updated her on my recent experiences and progress. She also mentioned that we would review the emails I sent. She made it clear that she would not give me additional time until we figure out how to work together. The session was cut short, lasting only 35 minutes, and she seemed disinterested in discussing important matters. As I was leaving, she turned her back on me and displayed a look of distaste. I expressed my feelings about her attitude towards me, but she dismissed me and closed the door. I feel like there is unfinished business and that termination may be imminent, even though I haven't found another therapist specializing in trauma treatment like her. I mentioned to her during our walk down the hall that if she doesn't want to treat me anymore, she should just say so. We had a disagreement about a year ago when I asked for a break, which she interpreted as termination. However, she accepted me back three months later and informed me of referrals, both of which have had disciplinary actions against them. She is aware of this. I understand that healing is my goal, and I respect her abilities, but I feel like she is leaning towards terminating our therapeutic relationship. She acknowledged that this isn't just about me, but I feel like she isn't fully invested in my treatment, despite having future appointments scheduled. I asked her to change her attitude towards me and expressed that last week's session felt more about her than me, as she couldn't accept my affirmation of the therapeutic session. I have been struggling with deep depression, and my anger is real. I want to heal, but I don't have faith that she is willing to continue working with me. Now, I am waiting for our next session to see if we can discuss our relationship and come to an agreement on how we can work together. Unfortunately, I lack confidence that she will be reasonable, and today I pushed her buttons. She ended the session after 35 minutes. What are your thoughts? I feel like she has no desire to engage in any meaningful discussion. She was also willing to make a referral last week, which confused me because I only wanted an additional appointment. It feels like games are being played with me. I just feel defeated and vulnerable, as I believe she is actively searching for someone else to treat me. I cannot and will not start over with someone new. I feel there is no resolution, only hostility towards me and vice versa. I have expressed to her that I see and hear her anger towards me, but she remains silent and makes decisions that further damage our relationship. What are your thoughts?

About 8 months ago, my little stepdaughter started calling me mommy on her own. My husband and I decided not to correct her and instead taught her how to say my name. We believe that if she's comfortable with calling me mommy and it makes her happy, then there shouldn't be an issue. It's important to note that she has a biological mom whom she loves, lives with half the time, and is a content, confident, and well-adjusted little girl. She is happy in both of her homes with all the parents and step-parents involved.

I've been diagnosed with OCD, GAD, depression, and an eating disorder. Currently, I'm taking 30mg of Prozac, which has been somewhat helpful. However, I've noticed some changes in my behavior and I'm not sure how to interpret them. I had to stop seeing my previous therapist, but I'm scheduled to start with a new one soon. However, I'm concerned because I'm supposed to discuss gender identity issues with the new therapist, and I don't think it's the right place to talk about these other concerns. Lately, I've been feeling very paranoid, particularly in social situations. I would convince myself that others hate me, delete my social media, and harbor resentment towards them for not responding to a text. Due to some trouble I got into, I've become quite isolated and only have myself to talk to. When I'm driving, I'm constantly looking behind me, wondering if someone is following me or thinking negative thoughts about me. I even find myself speeding just to get away from them. I'm overly suspicious and always feel like something is wrong or someone is after me. I also experience depersonalization and derealization, where I feel detached from reality. During these episodes, I convince myself that the reality I'm trapped in doesn't matter, and I should focus on the reality I create in my own mind. Another thing that's been happening is that I've become more religious lately. I've always been agnostic, but recently I've developed a strong affinity for Jesus and even bought a crucifix to hang on my wall. I'm worried because both my grandpa and uncle were schizophrenic, and I'm 17 years old, which is supposed to be an early warning period. However, I don't want to jump to conclusions. I just feel really strange, and life feels very unfamiliar to me.

Since starting graduate school 2300 miles away from home, I've been feeling a mix of emotions. It's the first time I've lived away from my parents, as I lived with them during my undergrad years. They've been supportive, helping me with the move and providing groceries while I'm in grad school.

Hello, I've been struggling with my mental health lately. I have a diagnosis of depression and anxiety disorder, and I've noticed some symptoms that make me wonder if I might also have bipolar disorder. It's been a challenging journey for me, especially because I experienced sexual assault when I was 11 years old. I used to self-harm and attended therapy sessions, but I stopped because I believed I didn't need them anymore. However, I still feel like someone is watching me, even when I'm alone. I have irrational beliefs about bugs being hidden cameras and people spying on me. I'm also suspicious of others, thinking they might be fake. Additionally, my father has expressed concern about my interest in horror movies, serial killers, and exploring the deep web. I've had disturbing thoughts about harming others, even though there is no specific motive. At night, I become paranoid about the trees and the people in the house across the road. I'm unsure if these experiences are delusions or based in reality, but I really want to find out.

I've been feeling really left out at work lately. Most of the staff on my floor go out for drinks on Friday nights, but not everyone is invited. It's been really difficult for me to hear them talking about their outings the following week. I've been thinking about organizing my own get-together that includes everyone on the floor. I was thinking of scheduling it for a different Friday or even on another night, at a different location, so it doesn't clash with their regular plans. What do you think?

I am a co-facilitator for a men's domestic violence support group at a non-profit organization. One of the group members recently mentioned his fear of losing his probation for a crime he didn't commit and potentially being imprisoned for years. Unfortunately, he did end up being jailed and there is another hearing to determine his fate. He has made significant progress despite a difficult upbringing and has been actively participating in other support groups and working towards rebuilding his relationship with his children. However, he has expressed suicidal thoughts in the past due to his fear of going back to prison and is currently feeling worn out and depressed due to the challenges of dealing with the legal system. We are deeply concerned about his mental health, especially since he hasn't had any visitors. While there is a consent agreement in place for improving mental health resources in LA County, the therapist leading the group is unsure about whether it would be appropriate to visit him in jail due to ethical boundaries and dual relationships. The non-profit organization also doesn't have a policy in place for this situation. I believe that in these circumstances, the potential benefit to the man's mental health and even his life outweighs the risks associated with boundaries. What is your perspective on this?

Hello, I've noticed something about myself that I've been wondering about for a long time. I find myself having strong emotions towards my pet, like my puppy, but I struggle to feel those same emotions towards other humans. I've also noticed that I tend to manipulate people, making them think I care about them so that they'll be there for me when I need them. The strange thing is, I'm not even aware that I'm doing it in the moment, only realizing it afterwards when I reflect on my actions. It's like pretending to care has become second nature to me. And when I do finally realize what I've done, I don't feel guilty or distressed, just a bit uneasy about myself.

I've been thinking a lot about the concept of "grit" and how it relates to self-esteem. I'm wondering if it's possible for someone to possess grit, which is often associated with determination and perseverance, but still struggle with low self-esteem. Is this a rare occurrence? If not, how can these two seemingly contradictory traits coexist?

Our 25-year-old daughter is going through a really difficult time right now and it's causing a lot of distress for us as parents. She has been struggling with substance abuse, relationship issues, and her reactions to stress have been escalating recently. She's been having meltdowns, damaging property, making threats with knives, engaging in excessive drinking, getting into legal trouble like DUIs, and experiencing severe depression. It's concerning because she's refusing to seek treatment at the hospital, even though she has seen a specialist in the past. We're worried that she's becoming a danger to herself and others. She tends to surround herself with enablers when she's stressed or emotional, which leaves her in risky situations. She already has ongoing legal issues related to public drunkenness, DUI, and now assault. As her parents, we need to know what options we have to ensure she gets the medical treatment she needs and to protect her and others, even if she doesn't recognize or accept the dangers.

I've noticed that people who don't know me well often seem impressed by me. They see me as good-looking, intelligent, and charismatic. I excel at engaging in conversations and problem-solving. However, despite these qualities, I still feel a sense of dissatisfaction and wonder why I'm not as successful as I believe I should be.

I've been feeling stuck in a quarter-life crisis for over a year now. It all started when I received a longing look from a stranger. Suddenly, I felt disconnected from my husband and unsure about everything. I've spent the last three months torturing myself, analyzing and questioning my life. I've realized that I'm harboring resentment towards my husband, even though he's a good man. There are two main reasons for this resentment: his drinking problem, which consumed my twenties, and the lack of intimacy in our marriage (less than once a year). These issues didn't bother me before, but now I feel like I've missed out on the best years of my life.

Lately, I've noticed that I have been obsessively seeking out diagnoses or labels to understand what is happening in my mind. It's like I have this compulsion to categorize my thoughts, maybe because I struggle with identifying and labeling my emotions. It's been challenging, but I have managed to come up with a few things.

Patient's Statement: Two years ago, a family member began exhibiting strange behavior. She started talking strangely and asking our family to praise God. We didn't think much of it because she is a devout person. However, that night she started asking if we could all sleep together, and the next night she began shouting loudly in the name of God. We took her to the doctor the next morning and she was prescribed medication. The doctor also suggested that she stay with relatives for a few days. After two weeks, she returned to normal but continued taking her medication. I asked her why she behaved that way, and she explained that she heard a voice commanding and controlling her to praise God. She also mentioned experiencing crawling sensations in her spine, head, and stomach. She has been doing well, but last year she stopped taking her medication for a month and, once again, exhibited strange behavior. We went back to the doctor, got her medication, and she returned to normal. However, she sometimes complains about not being able to stop her thought process. She repeats conversations she had earlier in the day and gets irritated by it. She also mentions feeling something moving like a dot inside her head. Our doctor listens patiently and adjusts her medication based on her symptoms, but the problem keeps recurring. She stopped taking her medication two weeks ago because she felt too sleepy during the day. She seemed fine initially, but this month she has been having trouble sleeping, getting only about five hours of sleep. Yesterday, we saw the doctor and he said she could stop taking the medication because it was making her feel sedated. However, her behavior was strange again this morning. I asked her multiple times and even got angry, but she eventually came to my room and explained that she heard a voice commanding her to praise the Lord again. She tried to resist, but couldn't sleep. I suggested she drink milk with honey and take her medication, and now she is sleeping.

I am currently a 17-year-old junior in high school and I am struggling with severe OCD. It has been taking over my life and causing intense anxiety. I have intrusive thoughts that keep me up all night and sometimes I even think about harming myself. I really need medication to help me cope with this.

I'm feeling really anxious and insecure in my long distance relationship. I've had issues with accusing my boyfriend of cheating, even though I want to trust him. I feel like he needs to prove his loyalty first, which is causing me a lot of anxiety and fear. He seems emotionally distant and logical, which makes me question if he truly loves me. He's mentioned that he's been through something that prevents him from fully loving me, but he won't open up about it. I don't want to lose him, especially since he's coming to see me soon. However, we keep having issues, mostly related to social media, and it's making me feel really down about myself. I've had a hard time trusting him since he cheated in the past, but I also feel like my own insecurities pushed him towards that. I love him so much and want to make things work. Am I the problem? What can I do to fix this?

I've been in a relationship with my girlfriend and my family doesn't approve. They believe that there are better matches for me out there and want me to reconsider our relationship. I feel like they just want me to break up with her and don't understand how I feel. They think I'm just infatuated with the idea of being in a relationship and can't see the bigger picture.

When I was around 9 years old, my parents got a divorce. Unfortunately, my father's behavior towards me became abusive. He would starve me, physically assault me, and even lock me in my room for days. Eventually, I made the decision to cut off contact with him. However, I still carry a deep sense of guilt. I constantly wonder if I should have endured the abuse longer, if I could have been less prideful and tried harder to salvage the relationship.

I have been struggling with various issues that I can't quite pinpoint to a specific disorder, but I exhibit traits and symptoms of several depression-related disorders. Some of my friends have suggested that seeing a therapist could be beneficial for me, and I have reluctantly come to agree. However, my struggles are mostly internal and not easily noticeable to others, including my mom. Confessing my feelings to her feels like a daunting task, as our relationship is more of a parent-child dynamic rather than a friendship. I find it challenging to express my thoughts even when I'm alone, so explaining them to her seems almost impossible. I don't know where to start and I don't have any other trusted adults in my life since my father is not involved.

I am currently in my third trimester of pregnancy and have come to my mother's house for the delivery of my first baby. However, the presence of my eldest sister, who recently left her husband and is awaiting a divorce, has been causing a lot of disturbance. My mother seems to be very bothered by my sister's presence, especially because of her 10-year-old child who lacks good manners. My mother wakes up early in the morning and tries to wake my sister up to help her in the kitchen, which often leads to arguments and yelling. I feel like I'm caught in the middle of these two women who struggle to communicate effectively. However, I believe that the main issue is my mother's anxiety to get things done immediately, which is negatively affecting my niece. It has become an emotionally torturous situation for me, especially considering I am in my third trimester. I understand that my sister came home to find peace from her abusive husband, but it's becoming increasingly difficult to handle.

I have been struggling for a long time, feeling off and trapped in a cycle of bad relationships. I've noticed that I treat others poorly and struggle to find happiness. I love my kids, but sometimes I question my ability to be a good mother. I've tried counseling before, but it hasn't been helpful. I feel like something is wrong with me, but everyone says it's normal. I have difficulty getting along with my mother, rely on relationships for happiness, and have anxiety about many things. I turn to drinking and gambling to cope, and struggle to make friends. I feel incapable and anxious about trying new things. I just want to know if there's hope for me to change and live a happier life.

Hello, I hope you're doing well. I wanted to reach out because I'm feeling a bit overwhelmed lately. I'm an 18-year-old first-year college student from Denmark. I attend a special college for individuals on the autism spectrum. I have been diagnosed with high functioning autism, also known as Asperger's syndrome.

Patient: I’ve been struggling with fear and sleep issues since I was young. I have a strong fear of the dark and I often hear unexplained noises both inside and outside of my house. This fear prevents me from being able to fall asleep easily, and I often stay awake until morning. If I do manage to fall asleep, I am frequently awakened by nightmares. These nightmares typically involve themes of home invasion, violence, supernatural hauntings, abandonment, or feeling trapped.

Over the past year and a half, I have been attending weekly therapy sessions with the same therapist. I have also been participating in group therapy for the past year. Initially, it was challenging for me to identify and express my emotions, but I have developed a sense of trust and comfort with my therapist. I have been dealing with anxiety, depression, childhood trauma related to bullying, divorce, and isolation, as well as a medical condition called scarring alopecia with psychosomatic causes. Although therapy hasn't been focused on specific goals and I'm unsure of when it might end, I have gained insight into my functioning and the root causes of my distress through self-reflection. However, I haven't seen significant improvement in my issues. I want to believe in my therapist and our relationship, hoping that it can help me build better relationships and reduce my depression and anxiety. At the same time, I recognize the importance of evaluating the progress made over the past 18 months.

I am currently living in a challenging and unsafe environment with my alcoholic father, grandmother, and two younger siblings. Despite my grandmother's threats to kick him out if he drinks, she continuously allows him to stay. Unfortunately, our financial situation prevents us from taking immediate action, as my grandmother is currently unemployed due to a recent accident. My father's behavior, such as breaking things and endangering us with his cooking, has become unbearable. Both my grandmother and I want him gone, but we lack the financial means to do so. I work a part-time job earning $60 a week, which is not enough to cover our expenses. I would greatly appreciate any advice on how to cope with this situation or find a way to afford to remove him from our home. We have been dealing with this for years and it has taken a toll on us. Thank you in advance for your assistance.

Over the past three years, I have been experiencing some distressing symptoms. I have been hearing voices that instruct me to do things, and occasionally, I see things that others cannot. At first, I believed these experiences were messages meant for me, and I was terrified and unable to escape them. However, I have made some progress, and now I am feeling a bit better. I believe this may be a form of psychosis. What confuses me even more are these vivid memories I have of events that never actually occurred. In these memories, I am a completely different person, but they feel incredibly real. I'm feeling quite bewildered and disturbed by all of this.

Counselor: I'm really sorry to hear that you're going through such a difficult time. It sounds like you're feeling betrayed and devastated by the recent revelations about your girlfriend's past. It's completely understandable that this has had a profound impact on your emotional well-being.

I've been in a long-term relationship with my wife for 23 years and we have three children. When I reflect on my life, I don't have any regrets. However, when I think about the future, I find myself yearning for more experiences like traveling, having more freedom, meeting new people, and going out at night.

It sounds like you and your mother have been experiencing a lot of conflict lately. It can be frustrating when she yells at you and claims it's because you don't listen, even when you genuinely didn't hear her. It's understandable that you feel annoyed when she starts screaming right away. Coping by quietly saying okay is a way to avoid escalating the fight, but it also makes you feel like you're backing down. Is that correct?

I have been struggling with my mental health for quite some time. While I haven't been officially diagnosed, my mom believes that my symptoms are just a normal part of being a teenage girl and that they will eventually go away. However, I have been through an abusive relationship with my best friend that has had a significant impact on me both mentally and physically. I experienced depression during that time, with symptoms such as loss of appetite, poor academic performance, and excessive sleep. Although I have made progress, I still find it difficult to trust people who are not my family. Now, let's get to the real issue. I noticed that you were unable to provide advice in response to a similar question, and I hope that by providing more information, you will be able to help me.

As a teenager in Italy, I have been struggling with my self-esteem and body image. I have always been introverted and found solace in nature and my love for dogs. However, my classmates started making fun of me due to my weight, which led to me developing anorexia. During that challenging time, my two dogs played a significant role in saving my life. Despite recovering from anorexia, my classmates continue to torment me, calling me ugly and devaluing my worth. This has caused me to turn to self-harm, specifically cutting, although I have never attempted suicide.

From a young age, I have experienced significant anxiety when in large crowds, particularly when surrounded by strangers. This has resulted in me spending most of my free time at home, avoiding situations with many people. Additionally, I struggle with social interactions, finding it difficult to initiate or maintain conversations. I often find myself speaking at inappropriate times or misinterpreting others' emotions, which leads to anger and frustration. It's a conflicting experience because while I desire social engagement when I'm at home, I often long for the comfort of being alone when I'm with friends and family.

I have been in a relationship with a man for 2 years and we moved in together early on. However, I recently discovered that he had been cheating on me with prostitutes for most of our relationship. We went to therapy and decided to work through it, but I have found evidence that he has been texting prostitutes again. He denies any wrongdoing and claims he hasn't cheated in a year, but I am skeptical. I bring it up often because I doubt his honesty.

My girlfriend's childhood was filled with trauma and instability due to her father's abusive and loveless behavior. When she was just 13, her mother had to escape with her and her siblings from their father, who was also a slum lord. It took seven years of fighting in divorce court for her family to finally have a chance at a stable and fresh start. Understandably, she harbors a deep despise for him.

I've always had a strong sense of self-confidence, to the point where some people have mistaken it for arrogance. Additionally, I have been told that I come across as charismatic, making a positive impression on others when we first meet.

I'm a 21-year-old woman who has been in a long-distance relationship for 3 months. Recently, my boyfriend visited me and met my family for the first time. However, there was tension between my family and him due to a rule they set, which prohibits us from being in a room with the door closed. I had to inform my boyfriend about this rule because it would hinder our plans to try anal sex, which I had previously expressed interest in. This upset him because he is 23 and just left the army, feeling burdened by rules and believing that as adults, we should have more freedom.

I've been struggling to come to terms with the fact that my mother is a narcissist. It has been pointed out to me by a counselor in the past, and with each conflict I have with her, I see more and more of those narcissistic traits. Despite this, I still find myself seeking emotional support from her. Throughout my adult life, even through getting married, I held onto the hope that she would change and treat me like a loving mother. Unfortunately, that hasn't happened. Now that I'm pregnant, I feel a mix of sadness and anger because she only offers support if I go to her, and she constantly makes her own problems the center of attention. When I don't want to coddle her and focus solely on her issues, she accuses me of not being there for her. The truth is, I've spent most of my life catering to her emotions and health concerns. Sometimes I suspect that she exaggerates her health issues just to get attention. Last month, she had me convinced she had osteoporosis, but when I questioned her this month, she suddenly said it was just osteoarthritis. Deep down, I know that my mother will never truly approve of me, respect me, or be there for me, but my heart struggles to accept it. I keep trying to forge a close relationship with her, but it only leaves me feeling infuriated, incredibly sad, or completely drained. Additionally, my husband has to deal with our weekly fights. How can I learn to accept that my mother has a mental illness?

Patient: Lately, I've been experiencing some concerning urges to hurt myself. It's been happening since the beginning of the year and it's been getting worse over the past two months. When I'm alone, these thoughts completely consume my mind. My breathing speeds up and I can't stop thinking about it until I act on it. It's strange because it doesn't usually happen when I'm around other people, but when it does, they become a part of it.

About ten months ago, I started dating my now ex-boyfriend. He had recently overcome a period of depression due to a previous toxic relationship. At the beginning of our relationship, he seemed very much in love and would constantly text and want to spend time together. In response, I felt the need to be the perfect girlfriend, always suppressing my anger and providing unwavering support.

I'm finding it difficult to connect with my daughter when she goes through tough times. She always says that I don't understand and insists that she is the only one experiencing these problems. I try to share my own experiences and offer advice, but she rejects everything I have to say. It's frustrating because I went through similar situations and managed to overcome them. She has a strong support group, but she insists on doing everything herself. I was a single parent too, so I do understand her struggle.

I experienced severe depression and anxiety a few years ago and sought therapy for a period of two years. My therapeutic relationship with my therapist was neither too close nor too distant, but we had a good rapport and she provided valuable support. I am now considering pursuing a career in psychotherapy and was wondering if it would be appropriate to reach out to her for guidance on accessing career opportunities and training in our local area.

Lately, I've been noticing that my significant other has been getting increasingly angry over simple things. It's gotten to the point where even minor annoyances escalate into big fights. When I try to address these issues, he becomes verbally abusive, yelling at me, telling me to shut up, and even saying hurtful things like he doesn't care about me.

I've noticed a significant change in my family dynamics ever since my son got married to his Armenian wife. We used to be a close-knit family, with my grandmother, sister, cousins, and aunt, but things have changed. I feel like my son's wife has influenced him to distance himself from us. We don't even know where they live, and he admits that she is mean to me, as if she wants to keep me away. It's hard for me to understand why he allows this behavior from her.

Lately, I've been experiencing some shifts in my emotions. Last week, my friend made a comment about my lack of creativity, and it really affected me. Initially, I felt a wave of sadness, but it quickly turned into anger, making me want to lash out at her. Then, today while shopping with my mom and sister, I suddenly erupted in anger for no apparent reason. I think my sister annoyed me, but it felt like more than that. Whenever I get angry like this, I tend to forget what triggered it. The anger seems to overpower me. I've also been feeling really down before or after these episodes of anger. I know I need help, but I'm scared to talk to anyone because I feel like my problems aren't important and that others have more important things to do. I'm really nervous about how these mood swings will affect me as the school year begins. I just want to be able to relax, but even when I'm alone in my room, I feel this urge to release my anger physically. And to make matters worse, my stepfather's behavior towards me is really hurtful. He talks about me as if I'm not even there and it really brings me down. I don't think he understands how much it hurts me. Please, I need help understanding what's happening to me.

I have been in a relationship with my girlfriend for three years. She has had a difficult upbringing, with her mother struggling with schizoaffective disorder and a cocaine addiction. Unfortunately, her mother took her own life when my girlfriend was just 12 years old. Her father has also been emotionally abusive, causing her to leave home at the age of 18. We have been living together since then. Around two years ago, she had a severe suicide attempt that resulted in a coma and mild brain damage. I'm wondering if anyone else has gone through similar experiences.

I'm a 15-year-old girl from Australia and I'm currently attending school. I've been doing well with my grades, but I'm going through a tough time with my friends. They've all turned against me because I stood up for a boy they all dislike. Now, they're ignoring me and pretending to have a great time in front of me.

Throughout my life, I have always had a strong passion for musical theatre and dreamed of pursuing it as a career. However, I have encountered some challenges in my academic journey. I did not get accepted into any good colleges for musical theatre, and I am currently enrolled in a program that I am not happy with. I have recently been accepted into a prestigious school that is quite far from home, but I am now questioning whether musical theatre is truly my calling. I have been feeling disconnected from my passion and unsure if it is due to the program or a change in my interests. The school I am currently attending is relatively close to home, but I still find it difficult to adjust and leave behind my old life and friends. I miss the simplicity of high school and feel overwhelmed by the uncertainty of my future. I have contemplated the idea of ending my life by the age of 30, which concerns me greatly. On one hand, attending the school that is far away seems like a great opportunity, but on the other hand, I fear that I may be making the wrong decision. I have also applied to a state school that is close to home, where I could commute and be surrounded by familiar faces from high school. However, this option would mean giving up on my dream of pursuing musical theatre. I am feeling immense pressure to make a decision within the next month, and while I am leaning towards the school that is 8 hours away, I am filled with fear and uncertainty. I am scared of wasting my life in an ordinary job, yet I struggle to envision myself in any other career. I long for my old life and the carefree days spent with friends. I apologize for the lengthy message; I just needed more space to express myself.

Over the past decade, I have been undergoing mental health treatment and have recently been informed that my perception of reality may not align with actual reality. This realization has left me feeling unsure about how to cope with this new understanding. It's causing me to question everything, and I am feeling overwhelmed by the task of discerning what is real and what is not. Can you offer any guidance on how to navigate through this?
A little over a month ago, my boyfriend decided he was no longer happy with me and broke off our four-year relationship. He thought I didn’t trust him and believed that I wanted to keep him isolated.

Lately, I've been experiencing some troubling thoughts and behaviors. I find myself having a fascination with violent acts like murder, and it's accompanied by a strong sense of hunger. These thoughts make me feel like there's something wrong with me. Additionally, I've engaged in illegal activities such as cheating on tests, lying, and being unfaithful to my partner. I can't help but wonder if these behaviors are connected to my violent thoughts. I've been reflecting on my past experiences of being bullied in school, and I'm wondering if that has any influence on my current state.

Hi, I am from Denmark and I recently came across your website. I found the information about ADHD very interesting, and I have a question about medication that I would like some advice on. I apologize if my message is a bit long.

For the past few months, I have been experiencing intrusive thoughts about harming myself or my family. These thoughts make me believe that I am a bad person and have led me to contemplate suicide as a way to avoid hurting others. I have received a diagnosis of OCD, specifically harm OCD, but I struggle to accept that I am not truly a terrible person. Although I never actually want to harm anyone, there are moments when it feels like my mind is forcing me to, as if it is inevitable. I feel completely overwhelmed and out of control.

I'm really struggling with the loss of our daughter. She took her own life at the age of 20 in September 2014. She was incredibly intelligent, but she had difficulty with her studies and forming lasting friendships. She was diagnosed with either autism or schizoid personality disorder, but she chose not to pursue treatment. She always had a hard time expressing her emotions, often saying she couldn't feel anything. On September 9, 2014, she took pills and left us. It's been incredibly difficult for our family to cope with this tragedy.

I have been living with my boyfriend for almost a year, along with his parents who are not working. We support them financially, but they take advantage of my boyfriend's generosity. They constantly expect him to provide for them and disregard our boundaries. His dad even uses my car without permission. I feel trapped and want to move out, but we can't afford it. My boyfriend refuses to reduce his support for his parents. Am I wrong for wanting our own life?

My 13-year-old son has been diagnosed with Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) in the past, but lately, he has been exhibiting signs of depression. He only seems happy when he has food or toys, and spends most of his time alone. His grades are fine, but he has no interest in leaving the house or socializing with his friends. Two years ago, he switched to a private school with smaller classes, hoping it would help him participate more, but now he feels detached from all his friends. He gets easily angry, even over minor things, and has trouble sleeping due to worrying thoughts that won't stop. He is also experiencing social difficulties, with girls preferring to hang out with wealthier and more popular boys, and other kids making fun of him for being a "nerd." He used to enjoy many activities that he no longer finds pleasure in, and he no longer plays sports. He feels alone at school and avoids the only people he is friendly with because they become overwhelming when he is not in a good mood. I'm not sure how to help him.

In 1999, when I was 29 years old, I was diagnosed with depression and agoraphobia. Since then, I have struggled with finding the right medication. I have tried around six different SSRIs, but none of them seemed to work. To manage my severe anxiety and panic attacks, I was prescribed Lorazepam, also known as Temesta. Unfortunately, I became addicted to it and I am still struggling with that addiction.

During my middle school years, around the age of 13-14, I received a diagnosis of psychotic depression. It involved experiencing auditory hallucinations and occasional visual hallucinations, engaging in self-injury, and having thoughts of suicide. Each voice had a distinct name and personality, and they interacted with each other and with me. I was prescribed a high dose of risperidone, which helped alleviate my symptoms. I stopped seeing a psychiatrist at that time. However, now that I am 17 years old, I have noticed that I am having inner dialogues between my own consciousness and two distinct voices that I do not consciously create. These voices are male, while I am female. One voice is the same age as me, and the other is in his late teens or early twenties. They each have their own names and personalities, similar to what I experienced in the past. Recently, I have also been struggling with memory issues. I forget things I have done or am currently doing. For example, I have received classwork and exams with my name written in a different handwriting that I don't recall. My friends ask me about conversations we had, and I cannot remember them. Sometimes, I forget what I was doing in the middle of a task and have to ask my friend to remind me. However, the voices sometimes remember these things and confirm them. I'm feeling concerned and confused about what is happening. I'm unsure if I am experiencing another psychotic episode or if this could be signs of Dissociative Identity Disorder (DID). I know I should reach out to my psychiatrist, but I would appreciate your thoughts on this situation.

I met this boy last year in December and we had a brief fling. However, he has become obsessed with me and has been stalking me. He spreads rumors about us being in a relationship and has been contacting me despite me blocking his numbers. I'm scared to report this and I hope to remain anonymous until something serious happens. He has also been saying negative things about me to my close male friends, causing me to lose contact with them. I feel isolated and don't know who to talk to besides this website. I've tried talking to him, but he refuses to listen. I'm also afraid to tell my parents because I don't want them to worry or escalate the situation. Please respond to this. Thank you.

Throughout my life, I've experienced a number of challenging situations that have greatly impacted my mental well-being. From a young age, I faced neglect, abuse, abandonment, and the presence of mental illnesses within my family. Although I always had underlying anxiety, I learned to hide it out of fear of being judged or labeled as "different."

I have been in a relationship with my current boyfriend for about 2 years now. We actually knew each other since our freshman year and always had a little crush on each other. However, during that time, I was also involved in an on-and-off relationship with my ex for about two years. My ex was very controlling and possessive, and we would frequently break up and then reconcile. The longest we managed to stay together was about a month.

Patient: A couple of years ago, I spoke to my doctor about my emotional state, but I downplayed it and didn't want to admit that it was still ongoing. He suggested that I might have been experiencing depression. I thought it would go away, but it has only gotten worse over the past three years. Last year was especially difficult for my family, with multiple hardships like death, divorce, and my sister's diagnosis with psychosis. Even before her hospitalization, my parents' drinking had spiraled out of control and my mom's gambling had worsened. They have been trying to fix things lately, but I'm feeling worse and having more frequent experiences of almost swallowing a bottle of sleeping pills. I've lost my relationship with my parents, and I feel like I'm drifting further away from who I used to be. I'm just going through the motions every day, like a robot. I don't trust or rely on my parents to handle any of this, as they are very unstable. I'm only fourteen and I need help. I can't rely on the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline anymore, and alcohol isn't helping either. How can I get help without destroying my parents' lives?

Since moving to another state to be closer to my son, who is living with his father and stepmother, things have been really difficult. I've been dealing with unemployment, financial struggles, and a lack of support from my family. A friend back home has offered to help me return, but has only been sending money instead of a plane or bus ticket. It's been really emotionally challenging for me, as I haven't caused any issues with my ex and his new wife and just wanted to be here for my son's senior year. I find myself crying every day and feeling deeply hurt and sad.

I recently had a conversation with my boyfriend, and he revealed to me that he experienced childhood abuse from multiple individuals. He shared that one of the abusers was a family friend, another was a classmate, and the third was a family member. He also mentioned that his parents reacted with anger and blame, expressing disappointment in him for not speaking up earlier.

I'm from Finland and I've been in a committed relationship for 10 years. However, I've been having an affair for the past two years, which has involved lying and cheating on both sides. I'm struggling with letting go of either person.

I've been dealing with a lot of stress, depression, and anxiety for as long as I can remember. My parents had a dysfunctional relationship while I was growing up, and it has had a lasting impact on me. Recently, I suffered an injury to my neck, and it feels like it's taken a toll on my overall well-being.

I feel overwhelmed and like I have no control over my life. I'm constantly busy with studying, working, and listening to my mother's problems. I used to find solace in playing the bass, but even that doesn't provide me with the satisfaction I need.

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for 3 years, but I don't feel any desire for physical contact with him. We are both in our 40's, divorced, have children from previous marriages, and we share the same Christian faith. We initially decided not to have sex, but eventually gave in after a month or so. However, we later decided to back off from it.

I have been feeling really down lately and I don't know why. I wake up every day with no motivation, no energy, and a sense of sadness that lingers throughout the day. I used to enjoy the things I loved doing, but now everything feels dull and uninteresting. I find myself isolating from friends and family, and I just can't seem to shake this feeling of emptiness. What's wrong with me?

I have been struggling with a lot of emotional and physical challenges lately. I recently started experiencing erectile dysfunction and noticed a curvature in my penis. After seeing a urologist, I was diagnosed with venous leak. This news completely devastated me and I spiraled into a deep state of despair. I began having panic attacks, feeling worthless, and having suicidal thoughts. It became impossible for me to focus on my studies, so I had to drop out of university. To make matters worse, during this difficult year, I also experienced the loss of my grandfather and my cat went missing. Any mention of sex or sexual content triggers intense negative emotions, and I no longer feel any sexual attraction towards women. It's an incredibly distressing situation for me.

I'm currently 17 years old and facing a decision about whether or not to go to university next year. However, I'm feeling extremely scared and uncertain. I have a history of depression, low self-esteem, and I've noticed symptoms of OCD and anxiety, specifically generalized anxiety disorder (GAD). The thought of going to university is terrifying because I worry that my existing problems will worsen to the point where I won't be able to cope anymore. Right now, the only reason I feel like I'm managing is because I have friends I can talk to when things get tough, but I won't have that support system when I go to university. I'm really unsure of what to do. I keep going back and forth between not wanting to go at all and thinking that maybe it wouldn't be so bad. Although I've applied and even received a couple of offers, the process of applying itself was difficult and required a lot of convincing. I just feel completely stuck and panicked.

I am an 8th grade boy from Canada. I've been struggling with severe ADHD and sluggishness, which makes it extremely difficult for me to motivate myself to work or study. I'm concerned that this is impacting my grades and confidence. I want to be able to stay true to myself and have a successful future. Is there any help available for me?

I'm a 20-year-old female and I've had a history of engaging in promiscuous behavior. It all started when I was 16 and was coerced into having sex with a 20-year-old guy that I wasn't even interested in. This experience led to more casual encounters afterwards. At the time, I acted like I wanted it and took pride in being sexually active, but deep down, it made me feel empty inside.

Over the past month, I've been experiencing some really frightening and unsettling things. I've started hearing voices in my head with different accents, constantly saying different things. There was one incident where I saw a man in the forest and the voices told me to harm him. I also find that time seems to pass by quickly, especially at school, and I struggle to remember what I've done. It's incredibly terrifying and I feel exhausted all the time. I rarely find joy or smile anymore. My grades are suffering, mainly Ds and C minuses. I don't spend any time studying or doing homework, and it's hard for me to focus and understand what I'm supposed to be learning. I just don't seem to care. I'm silent throughout the day and give short responses when confronted.

Throughout my life, I have never experienced the emotions of embarrassment or shame. Whenever I come across these words in books or on TV, I find it difficult to relate to them. In fact, when I was younger, I used to confuse the feeling of anger, which I frequently experience, with embarrassment. Looking back, I now realize that in situations where most people would feel embarrassed, like when I was bullied or ridiculed, I only felt anger.

I wanted to discuss my living situation with you. My boyfriend and I met at university, and since graduating, we have been living with his retired parents. They have been kind enough to let us stay with them while we figure things out. I work part-time and contribute financially, while my boyfriend receives a small allowance from his parents until he finds a job. We are grateful for their support and make sure to always be respectful in their home.

Over the past week, I have been experiencing intrusive sexual thoughts about children. These thoughts are distressing to me because I find them annoying rather than arousing. However, they have been causing me to panic and experience stomach pains. I recently visited a website that claimed having these thoughts automatically makes me a pedophile, but I want to assure you that I have no intention of ever harming a child.

Patient: I've been attending Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) for the past 7 months. Despite being in therapy for a while, I still find it challenging to open up and share my thoughts and feelings honestly. This is causing me to feel stuck and frustrated. How can I begin to share openly and honestly with my therapist?

Hello. I have been struggling with depression for the past 15 years, but recently I've been experiencing new symptoms that I've never had before. Along with the usual feelings of emptiness, numbness, fatigue, and occasional thoughts of suicide, I'm now experiencing something different.

Throughout my life, I have experienced extreme depressive lows and have had persistent suicidal thoughts. At the age of 16, I was diagnosed with both anxiety and depression. On my 18th birthday, I discovered that my boyfriend had cheated on me with my best friend, but I chose to stay in the relationship. However, the relationship became emotionally abusive, resulting in the loss of all my friends. This caused me to sink into a deeper depression than ever before. Eventually, we broke up just before I moved out of state for college. During this time, I was still struggling with suicidal thoughts and turned to alcohol, drugs, and frequent casual sex. As a result, I failed most of my classes. It was during this period that I sought therapy and was diagnosed with ADD.

I have been struggling with my mental health for a while now, and it has been difficult to find support from my parents. Whenever I try to talk to them about it, they dismiss my feelings and tell me to just get over it. It feels like they don't care about me at all. I want to seek treatment for my diagnosed mental illnesses and explore the possibility of having other ones, but I worry that my parents will continue to invalidate my experiences. I recently spoke to my mom about my concerns regarding dependent personality disorder and avoidant personality disorder, but she didn't take them seriously. It really hurt and made me feel disappointed. On top of that, I already struggle with depression and anxiety.

About four years ago, I was discharged from a psychiatric hospital after staying there for a month. When my mom picked me up, I happened to glance at the papers and noticed that, in addition to my previous diagnoses, it also said 'psychosocial'. I asked my mom what that meant, and she told me it meant I have no social skills. Honestly, I could have already guessed that myself!

I am feeling really frustrated and concerned about my mother's current state. She is 57 years old and has been dealing with depression for a while now. It's really taking a toll on her as she's constantly tired and sad. One of the main reasons she's feeling down is because of her knee pain, which is making it difficult for her to walk. She's scared to undergo surgery, even though it could potentially improve her condition. On top of that, she's not getting any help around the house, which is adding to her stress. My grandmother visits her every day, but instead of providing support, she ends up driving my mom crazy. My dad is also not being very helpful and is quite messy. All of these things are causing my mom to reach out to me every day to vent and complain.

Throughout high school, I was in a relationship that lasted for two years. It was my first serious relationship and I developed strong feelings for my partner. We had plans to make our relationship work in college, despite the challenges. However, unexpectedly, he broke up with me before summer began. He never provided an explanation or communicated what went wrong. This sudden and complete removal from my life left me devastated.

"I struggle with a lot of negative thoughts and worries. I constantly feel self-conscious and think that I am fat. I also tend to think of worst-case scenarios, like my husband getting into a car accident when he leaves the house. I worry a lot about my relationship with my children, fearing that they will hate me when they're older. I find myself being negative when people ask for advice and I get angry easily over small things. It's frustrating and I hate how easily I can be set off. I also have trouble falling asleep at night because I'm afraid of someone breaking in and hurting me while I'm sleeping. I tend to ruminate on situations, especially when I think I've looked foolish."

I have been struggling with trust and self-esteem issues ever since my ex-wife cheated on me twice, once while we were dating and again while we were married. Despite getting divorced 4 years ago, these issues continue to affect my current relationship with a wonderful woman. Recently, I expressed my concerns to her about something not feeling right and asked if she was hiding something from me. She suggested taking a break, which she clarified meant we are broken up for now. However, she also mentioned that if I work on my issues during this time, there is a possibility of reuniting in the future.

I have been struggling with depression and thoughts of ending my life. In addition, I recently learned that I have a dissociative disorder called de-realization. I also experience frequent nightmares, about one every 10 days. I was abused and neglected as a child, and it wasn't until three months ago when my depression became severe that I sought therapy. During my therapy sessions, I've noticed something strange - I can't visualize my therapist's face, even though I have no trouble recognizing her. This is odd because I have a good memory and can visualize other people and situations easily. I'd like to know your thoughts on this and if it's a known phenomenon. Thank you for your help.

I've been seeing my therapist for about two years, but I've noticed something that makes me feel uneasy. During our sessions, my therapist often seems restless and fidgety. He spends a significant amount of time either playing with his wedding rings or running his hands through his hair. It's distracting and makes it hard for me to fully focus on our conversations.

Since my parents' divorce when I was just 2 years old, I've been caught in the middle of their ongoing conflict. Now that I've moved away for college, they continue to communicate through me, constantly calling to rant about each other and ask me to relay messages. It's overwhelming and I don't know how to handle it.

I've been having some issues with my current general practitioner (GP) and I'm not sure what to do. Whenever I ask questions or provide information about my injury or illness, I feel like I'm not getting satisfactory responses. Overall, my GP has been decent, but I can't help but wonder if they're just tired of seeing me.

I was in a highly abusive relationship with someone who not only cheated on me but also allowed his girlfriend to harass and torment me. They even engaged in sexual activities in my own bed. After a severe physical attack, I made the decision to involve the police, and he is currently in jail. Recently, a mutual friend approached me, which initially caused me some concern. However, after discussing it with him, he assured me that there was no connection. However, a month later, he brought another woman into my home and engaged in sexual activities with her while another friend of his was present. This woman sounds very similar to the one my ex was involved with. She has caused significant harm and distress in my life by breaking my windshield, tormenting and injuring one of my cats, stealing from my purse, and even taking control of my house and car keys. My ex has consistently denied any involvement and has called me crazy. While packing his belongings, I discovered a pair of small-sized airline slippers under his nightstand, along with baby monitors and power cords. In an attempt to gather evidence, I hid a video camera outside and it recorded her entering our bedroom window with my ex's assistance while I was downstairs preparing dinner. I have had suspicions in the past but was hesitant to investigate further due to the fear of being wrong or appearing crazy. Given the prolonged nature of this situation, I have reached a point where I even contemplate harming her if I were to catch her. I feel completely isolated and without anyone I can trust. I have tried my best to be a good person, so why is she fixated on tormenting me? Is it simply for her own amusement? I have been unable to obtain her name, which makes it difficult to seek legal protection through an anti-harassment order. Even before the involvement of the mutual friend, I had a sense that she had been in my house again but dismissed it as paranoia. However, this recent incident has shaken me and intensified my confusion, leading me to question my own sanity.

Recently, I've been feeling really confused about my own mentality. On one hand, I find solace in being alone and tend to avoid forming and maintaining friendships. I think it's because I value my daily routine and am reluctant to compromise on it. I tend to meet with someone only if I genuinely want to, which doesn't happen often.

Patient: I have been experiencing symptoms of anxiety and depression since I graduated from college in 2000. Currently, I am taking 40mg of Celexa daily. However, I still find myself feeling moody and easily angered, even with the medication. Little things tend to put me in a negative mood, and it affects my entire day. Most days, I feel grumpy and not enjoyable to be around. I was prescribed medical marijuana for my back pain last May, and I only take a 25-50mg pill when I am in pain. What confuses me is that when I take the medical marijuana, I feel like a different person. It's not about getting stoned, but it removes the pain and allows me to be kinder, less stressed, and more emotionally available. I feel like the person I should always be. However, when I'm not using medical marijuana, I go back to feeling anxious, easily angered, and grumpy. Even simple tasks like going to the store become overwhelming. I really want to understand why I can't consistently show my emotions to my family and be the positive person they deserve. I want to find a way to overcome these issues.

I've been experiencing episodes where I become extremely angry and lose control, damaging things that I love. I also have OCD and often feel frustrated with my compulsions. These outbursts are rare, but when they happen, they can last a long time until I break down in tears and self-harm. I've spoken to a psychologist who mentioned I might be on the autism spectrum. Is this normal or do I have a personality disorder?

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for over a year now, and we have built our connection on trust, honesty, empathy, and communication. Around four months into our relationship, he opened up to me about his fetish for tummies and stuffing. After doing some research, I understand that this is a part of him that will always be there, and I have accepted that fact.

Recently, I have noticed a decline in my mental capacity. I am having difficulty recalling names of objects, remembering school work, and often feel like my mind is blank. This also happened three years ago when I experienced numbness in my head, insomnia, and trouble concentrating. I saw a neurologist at that time who did an MRI, but they found nothing wrong. However, they suggested I follow up if the symptoms persisted. Due to financial problems, I never went back. But now, things have gotten worse. I forget simple things, like the name of a velcro strap, and even important events like my uncle's birthday. I've been sleeping a lot, eating very little, and struggling to concentrate. I tend to diagnose myself using Google, and right now, I think I may have depression. I also have anxiety, which stems from a difficult upbringing with a mentally ill mother. I used to avoid people, but now I get stressed around them and even stress myself out because I don't know what's wrong. I sometimes have thoughts that I might be making up my problems or that nothing is really wrong with me, but most of the time I feel horrible with memory problems, lack of purpose, difficulty concentrating, worrying, and even feeling slightly suicidal.

I have been in two different relationships that have left me feeling unsatisfied emotionally and sexually. In my current relationship, I am with someone who is passionate and attractive, but also emotionally unstable. We fight a lot and recently I have started to feel like I am the one causing the fights and questioning my own sanity. One issue that bothers me is my partner's admiration for young women and his profession as a photographer. I feel insecure and jealous, and it's affecting my self-esteem. I also worry about our future and whether our values align. I'm feeling depressed, angry, and unsure about what to do next.

When I was about 4-5 years old, there was an older boy, around 7, who would take me into hidden places like the closet and under the bed. He would touch me inappropriately, take my pants down, and sometimes even put objects in my underwear, telling me to leave them there. I can't remember everything clearly, but I can't help but wonder if it's my fault as much as his. Was I a victim of abuse?

I am a 22-year-old college student who is about to graduate. My dad has been seriously ill for the past 6 years and is now at home, experiencing severe depression due to his inability to support the family. My parents constantly fight, and my mom uses my dad's sickness as a way to guilt trip him, my siblings, and me. She blames him for all her problems and mine as well. They both confide in me about their marriage and sex life. When I come home from college, they become overly clingy and make me feel guilty for leaving, even for just a few hours. I've spent extended periods of time at home during summer vacation, barely leaving the house.

Hi, I'm a 15-year-old student who has been struggling with insomnia for the past couple of months. It's been really difficult for me because I have school and I can't sleep, which is making me feel really sad and emotionally drained. It's also affecting my self-esteem. I've been in therapy for the past 5 years and I've tried exercising and meditating, but nothing seems to be helping, not even the strong pills I've been taking. I'm exhausted and really need to get some rest, but my parents are getting angry with me because of it. What can I do?

Since childhood, I have struggled with feelings of exclusion and loneliness. From kindergarten onwards, I was always left out when other kids formed groups to play. In primary school, my classmates were consistently rude to me for no apparent reason. I only had one or two friends, but they never included me in their circles.

Recently, my nanny informed me that she caught my 6-year-old daughter engaging in sexual behaviors, such as touching her abdomen and attempting to involve her 18-month-old brother. I'm deeply disturbed by this and unsure of how to proceed. I've already removed the iPad from her access and made sure she is never left alone during playdates. Should I have a conversation with my daughter about sex? If so, could you provide me with some resources to guide me in discussing this topic with her?

I'm really concerned about my 22-year-old male cousin. He seems to be extremely dependent on his mother. She doesn't push him to get a job or even pursue his education. She does everything for him, from making his bed to preparing his meals and doing his laundry. I think he's perfectly capable of taking care of these things himself.

Over the past two years, I have been grappling with a chronic health issue that has really taken a toll on me. During this time, I have also started experiencing intense anxiety and panic attacks. Initially, I was driven by a desire to regain my previous life and engage in activities that my chronic illness prevented me from doing. However, as time has gone on, I've noticed a significant lack of motivation and excitement for anything. I now find myself overwhelmed by feelings of regret, believing that I could have avoided my current situation.

Patient: I've been working as a secretary in a private elementary school for the past 8 years. Two years ago, our former principal, who had been with the school since the 60s, retired. She was very well-connected to the community, being a nun and all. However, the new principal is a lay person from a different diocese. While she is professional, the former principal used to play favorites. Ever since this change, two mothers have started verbally abusing the current administrator, myself, and others. They do this in front of the children and other parents, and they spread malicious gossip and rumors. My boss doesn't seem to take it seriously and just brushes it off. I'm really concerned about this situation and I think it needs to be resolved.

Over the past two years, I have noticed that my current boyfriend has been neglecting me and not giving me the attention I need. We do not live together, which adds to the feelings of disconnect. About two months ago, I started texting and chatting with my ex, but it was purely for emotional support and not in a flirtatious manner. During this time, my current boyfriend went out of town and continued to prioritize other things over me, which was hurtful. My ex invited me to a Christmas party, and I agreed to go as friends. However, at the party, I ended up drinking too much and my ex crossed a boundary by fingering me, even though we did not kiss. I realized things were going too far and asked him to get me an Uber ride home.

I am a single mother of three boys and one daughter. My daughter will soon be 16 and I have been dating a man for two years. I have noticed some concerning behavior between my daughter and my boyfriend. They engage in physical closeness, such as him putting his hand on her thigh, holding her down and tickling her, pulling her onto his lap, and teasing her if she doesn't sit next to him. I even witnessed him touching her waist from behind. I'm worried about the appropriateness of these actions. Recently, my daughter had a crush on another boy and my boyfriend seemed distant, which made me wonder if he was jealous. I don't believe he would harm my daughter, but I've tried discussing my concerns with him, and he accused me of calling him a pedophile. Am I being unreasonable? What kind of behavior is acceptable and what is not? I also wonder if my own relationship with my father, which was distant and lacked physical affection, is influencing my feelings. Recently, I experimented with a drug called LSD, which is a psychedelic. During the trip, I had a really intense experience that caused my anxiety to skyrocket. I felt like I "died" and then came back. I'm not usually someone who uses drugs, but my friends convinced me to try it. Since then, I haven't reached out to any of my friends who weren't there that night. I'm afraid of what they might think of me. I don't know if they would accept me or not. I think they would probably be okay with it, but I'm not okay with myself. I know that suicide is not the answer because I can't do that to my family. I'm lucky enough to have the opportunity to come to Australia for further studies, which I see as a chance to escape my past. However, I've noticed that I've started talking to people with a "filter." I don't reveal my true feelings, I just keep things very surface-level. This has made it difficult for my friends to get close to me, and I feel lonely and lost in my life. I don't know how to move forward. I'm not ready to seek help about my past because it would mean talking about it and facing it, which I'm afraid of because of how my family and others might judge me. I'm sorry for the long post, but I hope to hear from someone. I can't thank you enough in advance.

He's now dating an old friend of ours and they seem to be living a carefree and party-filled life. I still love him after being together for 27 years. It scares me because I catch myself daydreaming about these violent acts. I've had a decent life overall, despite my absent mother and distant father. My grandparents have been supportive. I feel like I could actually kill someone without feeling any remorse. I know it's wrong and a terrible crime, but I don't really care. It's confusing because part of me is reaching out for help, but I'm not entirely sure if I truly care. I think my fear of legal consequences outweighs my fear of taking a life. I don't believe I'm crazy because I can rationalize these thoughts, but I wanted to know if you see any issue with this.

I want to open up about something that has been weighing heavily on me. Several years ago, when I was 12, I made up a false story about being sexually abused by a random person. Unfortunately, this lie has had a significant impact on my father's mental health. He has quit jobs and completely shut down. I feel immense guilt for causing all of this. Before I told my parents the lie, I was already struggling with drug abuse, depression, and dropping out of high school. My friends were the first ones to hear the lie, and it started to eat away at me. I'm grateful that I have been able to stop using drugs and am now in college, but my father's deteriorating mental state has negatively affected my academic performance. My self-esteem is at an all-time low, and I have developed unhealthy habits, especially in my romantic relationship. I can't seem to accept their forgiveness. In addition, I have developed an obsession with horoscopes, even though deep down I know they're not accurate. I rely on online magic 8 balls to answer questions about my future, acceptance, and even my partner's love for me. It's particularly challenging when my partner and I are fighting. I have spent a significant amount of money on psychics and online readings, and I have started to believe in superstitions, even though I know they're not real. I have seen a therapist before, but I couldn't bring myself to share the truth or my past experiences at that time. I was still holding onto the lie. During that period, I also engaged in drinking and drug use between the ages of 15-17. My romantic relationship has consumed most of my attention, and I am willing to do anything to make it work. Despite everyone's care and concern, I genuinely believe that I don't deserve it. Honestly, the only thing that has kept me going is the presence of my romantic relationship. Can you please help me?

I'm unsure whether I should give in to his demands to prevent any harm, or if I should insist that he seeks help. This behavior has been going on for years and he never takes responsibility for it.

My husband and I got married four months ago, but he is currently living in another country. We have always lived in different countries, but we have known each other since childhood. He emails me multiple times a day, usually around five times, with lots of loving words. However, there are times when he doesn't email me for hours, especially if he has something important to do. During my childhood, I struggled to live up to my potential and was diagnosed with ADHD without hyperactivity. I ended up dropping out of college and got into trouble with the law due to marijuana use. I've always felt lazy and unmotivated, even when I am capable of doing the work. After my arrest, I started to have thoughts of suicide and would often dip my head in the bathtub while contemplating it. I lived with my mother for a while, but our relationship became strained and she kicked me out. I then went to live with my father, which was a more stable environment for me. My parents had a tumultuous relationship, and I have blocked out many of the details of my childhood due to the constant fighting and screaming matches. Their divorce when I was 16 added to the drama in my life. Living with my father was a positive experience, and I felt happier there. I had a job and a friend, and my sexual activity decreased. I had multiple partners before getting married, which initially boosted my self-esteem but later led to feelings of shame and guilt. Following my father's advice, I joined the military and had a great experience during boot camp and A school. However, once I entered the navy, I struggled to fit in and felt extremely criticized. My social anxiety made it difficult to perform my job, which required public speaking and interacting with people for long periods of time. The constant pressure to perform left me feeling overwhelmed, often crying and dreading each day. I impulsively got married to my husband after boot camp without really knowing him well. I have a tendency to make impulsive choices, and while things have worked out so far, it hasn't always been for the best. Eventually, I left the navy and sought help after having fantasies of driving my car off the road. I was diagnosed with adjustment disorder and borderline traits, although I feel like the adjustment disorder diagnosis was given just to get out of disability. Ultimately, I just want to be successful in life, support my family, and find happiness.
