I know this may sound irrational, but it has led to social isolation and my days are filled with futile attempts to drown out this constant fear using temporary coping mechanisms. I worry that these mechanisms may not be enough in the long run.

I've been feeling like something is wrong with my life for the past year and a half. I've been researching my symptoms online and trying to fit myself into different diagnoses, but none of them seem to fit perfectly. To try and fit into these diagnoses, I've started mimicking their symptoms. For example, I force myself to feel bad and think of myself as worthless. The problem is, I've become so successful in faking these symptoms that I can't tell what's real and what's not anymore. I've also noticed that I often lie, manipulate, and misdirect people. Past friendships have ended tragically because they called me manipulative and unemphatic. I have to agree with them. I feel like a worthless and evil person, and I often experience periods of feeling down in the dumps, although they aren't as extreme or long-lasting as manic episodes. I also think I'm impulsive and tend to see the world in black and white, which makes me wonder if I have borderline personality disorder. But I can't tell if any of these symptoms are real or just in my head. I also don't understand why I long to be mentally ill. Maybe I want to fit in or be loved and understood. I'm unsure. That's why I haven't seen a therapist yet. I'm concerned that I wouldn't accurately describe my symptoms and might even exaggerate or make up fake characteristics. So, my question is whether I'm actually mentally ill or not, and if I am, what kind of mental health problems I might have. Should I seek help from a therapist or not?

I was in a same-sex relationship with my ex-fiancée, and we were supposed to get married six months ago. However, my family had a hard time accepting our relationship. My ex had been dealing with depression, but she never sought treatment until about nine months before the wedding when she started to decline. I encouraged her to see a doctor, and she was prescribed citalopram. Unfortunately, a month before the wedding, she called it off, saying she wasn't in love with me anymore. I moved back in with my parents and explained that we were taking a break while she sought help. After a month, we started talking again, and she apologized, saying she didn't know who she was and that she still loved me. But my family blames her for everything and doesn't support our decision to try again. I feel devastated and don't know what to do.

I'm facing a situation with a 12-year-old boy in my family who seems to have developed a strong attachment towards me. His parents divorced when he was very young, and his father was violent towards him. As a result, he seeks a lot of physical affection and displays behaviors like thumb-sucking. I let him seek comfort in my presence because I understand his history and want to provide him with kindness and tenderness. Recently, we spent two weeks together during a family vacation, and he became even more attached to me. He didn't want to leave and expressed a desire for me to be his father, despite his mother being in a loving relationship with someone else.

I'm currently facing a dilemma in my relationship as my partner and I are getting married in 7 months. Lately, I've been questioning whether we should stay together. I have borderline personality disorder, and I have communicated to him that honesty is crucial for our relationship to work. A few months ago, we almost broke up when I discovered that he had lied to me about contacting his ex. It was painful because he lied to my face. We managed to move past it, but now I've noticed that he lies to me about small things frequently. He thinks I don't know, but I do. I haven't confronted him because I don't want us to argue. However, recently I overheard him talking negatively about me behind my back when he thought I was asleep. I would never speak ill of him like that. He also mentioned that I prevent him from attending certain events, even though he has never mentioned them to me. He even called me angry and crazy when I never objected to him going out. I'm currently 8 months pregnant, and when I expressed my concern about being alone during the weekend our baby is due, he seemed supportive and promised not to be too far away. However, I later found out that he was telling his friends that he would make an excuse and still go out. I've told him before that he can go out as much as he likes before the baby arrives, but I would appreciate his support once it's here. Instead, I feel abandoned and betrayed. I don't want to be with someone who speaks poorly of me to his friends. He should be defending and supporting me. I feel completely isolated and unsure if I can trust him anymore.

I'm a college freshman and my girlfriend is a high school senior at a sister international school. I constantly feel jealous and panicked when I'm around her family and friends because their experiences are so different from mine. Her family is highly involved with her school and her friends always seem cheerful. Recently, she achieved the impressive feat of being on the varsity cross country team, making her a three-season varsity athlete. I'm really proud of her for overcoming her past injuries and working so hard. However, I can't help but feel jealous and insecure. It's also difficult for me when she talks about her academic achievements and her plans for internships. I don't understand why I get upset and feel like my life is inadequate compared to hers.

When I was a little girl, my parents had a unique sleeping arrangement for me and my older brother. Instead of sleeping in our own room, we would sleep on a sofa-bed in their bedroom. Each night, one of my parents would sleep between my brother and me, and they would eventually go back to their own bed. I don't have any memories of witnessing my parents having sex, although I'm unsure where else they would have done it.

I recently discovered that my boyfriend engaged in intimate conversations with women online at the beginning of our relationship. Although he never met up with anyone, I can't help but see him differently and it's been difficult for me to move past it. Then, I found a text from him expressing interest in my cousin, but he claims it was out of jealousy and he was drunk at the time. I feel disgusted and it's affecting my feelings for him. I don't know if I should try to forget and move on, or if I should stay in the relationship. I still love him, but not in the same way.

In the five years of my marriage, my wife has engaged in what I believe are two emotional affairs through text messages with other men. While there hasn't been any physical cheating, the messages are sexually explicit and she has even received explicit pictures and videos. When I've expressed my concerns, she denies any inappropriateness and accuses me of being insecure. She justifies her actions by saying she sees these men as friends since she lacks female friends she can relate to. However, my wife experienced sexual abuse as a teenager. Could this be impacting her ability to recognize boundaries with opposite-sex friends? Or is she just a compulsive cheater that I can't work things out with? I love her deeply and want to understand if her past trauma is influencing her behavior. I'm considering seeking therapy for myself to gain insight into her actions.

Throughout my life, I have struggled with anxiety and depression. I experience physical symptoms like racing heart, dizziness, headaches, and neck pain. Despite having a seemingly perfect life, I often feel lonely and upset. It has always been difficult for me to share my emotions with others, even those I care about, and I tend to remain silent. Sometimes I feel like I have a dark personality, and although I feel emotions deeply, I struggle to cry alone at night. Lately, after a surgical biopsy, my depression has worsened compared to the past 12 years. Additionally, I have been watching a movie every day for the last 10 days, and it triggers intense crying and increases my anxiety and heartache. I don't understand why I feel this way when I have no personal connection to the movie. Lastly, I have a history of self-harm that I have overcome, but I still experience occasional urges. I would appreciate your help.

I recently had an argument with my mom. I said something that she misunderstood and it upset her. I tried to clarify and apologize for not explaining myself well, but she responded harshly by suggesting an alternative way of explaining. I apologized again and promised to be clearer in the future. I didn't feel like I raised my voice or overreacted.

Hello, I recently started dating someone who has bipolar disorder. He has been taking his medication for the past four months and is actively seeing his psychiatrist. However, he is still experiencing severe depression following a manic episode that landed him in the hospital for a month. I care deeply for him, but I'm feeling scared and confused about what to do. Sometimes he seems to accept his condition, but other times he denies being bipolar. I didn't know much about bipolar disorder until I met him, and now I'm trying to educate myself and understand how to support him. It's difficult to see him depressed all the time, and I'm starting to question if this is the life I want for myself. I want to be there for him, but I also worry about my own well-being. Is it true that medication can help but that mood swings will still be a part of our life together? Sometimes I feel guilty for thinking about leaving, but I want to fight for our relationship and support him through this. Thank you for your guidance.

I've been in a relationship for the past year and a half with a man I met through a personal ad. However, my family doesn't approve of him because of his financial situation. I support him financially, but it causes stress and arguments between us. I love him and we've talked about a future together, but I worry about the responsibilities and my family's disapproval. I've invested a lot in this relationship, but I'm unsure if I should continue. Should I prioritize love or consider the financial and family factors?

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for the past 6 years, and he has always exhibited what he calls OCD habits. At first, I was able to adapt to them, but it has become increasingly difficult to live with. Waiting for him to complete his rituals before stepping over cracks or entering doorways has become embarrassing for me. Lately, however, his behaviors have become more severe and complicated. He engages in head rubbing, ear plugging, and shouts out numbers or strange sounds while performing his rituals. If anyone interrupts him, he becomes aggressive. Additionally, he displays physical manifestations of overwhelming thoughts and emotions during these episodes, such as jerking his body, rolling his eyes, and making strange movements. I'm genuinely scared and concerned that there might be something more going on. He refuses to seek therapy, arguing that therapists will dismiss his thoughts as not being grounded in reality. Moreover, when he is upset, he seems to jump from one problem to another as if seeking out reasons to remain upset. I would appreciate your opinion on whether I should encourage him to seek professional help or if this behavior is within the realm of normal for someone with OCD, and if so, how can I cope with it?

I am an eighteen-year-old who recently graduated from high school and will be starting college in the Spring. My struggles with intrusive thoughts and compulsions began back in 6th grade when I would feel a sense of "wrongness" when looking at people. To cope, I started faux-coughing twice while looking at them. In 8th grade, I developed a need to touch things a certain number of times and had morbid thoughts about dying in unusual ways. My friends thought I was crazy, but these thoughts persisted. Eventually, I started experiencing anxiety about locking doors and checking the stove, accompanied by a fear that something bad would happen if I didn't perform these actions. The nature of the bad things I fear has become more generalized over time.

I met my boyfriend on a social media site 6 months ago and we fell quickly and deeply in love. He lives in the U.S. and I in the UK, and I'm planning a trip to meet him in the next month or so. I have never felt more cherished and more connected to anyone, and 90% of the time things are wonderful, but I'm plagued with insecurities.

Over the past year, I've been struggling with motivation, interpersonal relationships, and a deep sense of self-doubt. This pattern has been recurring throughout my life, where I go through phases of high energy and interest in things, but eventually fall back into feeling hopeless and useless. During these times, I find it difficult to connect with others naturally and my sleep patterns are disrupted. I often find myself putting on a facade of happiness.

My husband retired 3 years ago and he is 77. We have been married for 47 years. It has been a tough marriage not due to the usual reasons like cheating or addictions or sex or any of that. We are financially good, are both healthy. Our kids are settled and we are close to them. I have plenty of outside interests, friends I go out with, I volunteer and I write.

I've been struggling to make friends for a long time. Being 53 years old, I feel like people are too busy to let new people into their lives. Additionally, my partner refuses to socialize with me and build a community together, which leads to me being questioned about his absence. With limited options for going out, I don't engage in many activities and worry that this makes me seem boring.

Patient's statement (rewritten): My best friend recently shared some significant life changes with me. She informed me that she is in the process of transitioning to become a man and is going through a divorce. However, her family is not accepting these changes and is ignoring her. She has also self-diagnosed herself with bipolar mania but refuses to take anti-psychotics. She has engaged in self-harm, although most of her cuts do not leave scars. She mentioned attempting suicide but her blood clotted too quickly. I'm deeply concerned for her well-being, especially since I live far away and she is going through multiple challenges.

I have been struggling with severe symptoms during my menstrual cycle that are affecting my relationships. Despite seeing three doctors over the past two years, I still don't have a clear explanation for what I'm experiencing. The symptoms include extreme depression, anger, hopelessness, and physical pain that lasts from ovulation until my period ends, which can be up to two weeks. It's causing a lot of stress and is taking a toll on my mental health. I'm open to trying therapy, medication, or any other possible solutions because I just want to feel like myself again.

I'm facing a difficult situation with my boyfriend and my family. We've been together for almost 5 years, but my family initially disapproved of our relationship because of our different races, educational backgrounds, and cultural differences. Eventually, my mom came around and allowed us to continue dating, although she and my family still have reservations. Now, my boyfriend is hesitant to come to my brother's wedding reception because he feels like he's not fully accepted by my family. I convinced my mom to let him come, but now he's saying he doesn't want to go because he doesn't want to be where he's not wanted. I want him to come with me, but I'm worried about the conditions my mom mentioned, like him needing to stay at a hotel. I don't know how to handle this situation.

I have been in a long-distance relationship with my boyfriend for about a year now. We met online and have been getting to know each other through daily communication and occasional visits. We have even discussed the possibility of getting married. However, during arguments, he tends to criticize me, which is something I cannot tolerate. Despite my love for him and my desire to spend my life with him, I made the difficult decision to end the relationship because I refuse to engage in a verbally abusive dynamic.

Throughout my life, I have always been isolated and struggled to make friends. In school and college, I was bullied and excluded because I wasn't good at sports. However, I excelled academically. Around the age of 16, I noticed that I became more hostile and would lose my temper easily, especially when I felt someone had offended me. This anger and aggression still come out when I am confronted about anything. Recently, I acted aggressively towards a bus driver who asked for my age for a student discount, even though I am 25.

I often feel like I'm not able to fully express myself due to my social anxiety. It's difficult for me to put myself out there and be more outgoing. What's been bothering me lately is the way my mom looks at me. We went shopping together once and when I tried on clothes, she seemed disappointed and disapproving. It's confusing because she brought me shopping in the first place. It's also frustrating that she doesn't like when I spend money, even if it's my own. She has issues with the way I dress, even when it's appropriate for the weather. It feels like she's judging me and making me feel ashamed of my body when I already struggle with body image issues.

Over the past few years, I have been involved in a complicated situation with my fiancé and his ex-wife regarding custody of his children. It has been a very stressful and emotionally draining experience. Recently, my fiancé went to see his children without discussing it with me and lied about it. I feel hurt and betrayed, and I'm not sure what to do.

Patient: About a year and a half ago, I went through a period of depression that lasted for almost six months. I never received an official diagnosis, but I experienced symptoms like dragging myself out of bed every day, feeling disconnected from my friends at school, and having thoughts of suicide. I also had disordered eating habits and started self-harming during that time.

I've been struggling with some issues lately. About three months ago, I was diagnosed with pure-o OCD. I've been managing it without medication, using CBT, diet, and exercise. I have good days, but mostly bad ones. I also think I might be experiencing depersonalization. It happened occasionally before my OCD started, but it's gotten worse since then. It usually happens after a tough episode of OCD when I don't have anything else to worry about. It's hard to describe, but it feels like I'm disconnected from my inner self, like I've lost myself. I feel empty and numb, like a shell. When I interact with people, it feels like I'm just pretending, like I'm not really there. It's causing a lot of anxiety, especially because it triggers my harm OCD. I worry that I'll go insane or hurt someone. Is this depersonalization or something else?

I have been dating my boyfriend for a few months now, and he has an almost 3-year-old son. We're unsure about when I should meet his son. My therapist suggested waiting 6-12 months after the split to give the child time to grieve. It's been 8 months since my boyfriend and his ex split.

Patient: I've been struggling with trust issues and it's causing me to be afraid of people and avoid social situations. My relationship with my mother seems to make things worse. She constantly gives me advice and gets upset if I don't listen to her. It makes me feel useless and second-guess my emotional attachments. I've never been in a relationship because I don't trust men who ask me out. I wonder if I just don't need a partner right now or if it's because I'm trying to be independent. How can I take my mother's comments more lightly while maintaining a good relationship with her?

I've noticed that I have a tendency to repeat stories or anecdotes without realizing it. It used to be worse when I was younger. The problem is that I can't remember who I've already told or how I shared the information.

I am currently in a relationship with a woman who has a history of childhood sexual assault and adult physical assault. I am a very passionate and affectionate person, and she can be too at times. However, recently I've noticed that she has been emotionally distant and has put up a wall between us. Although we talk on the phone every day, she avoids spending time together intimately or one-on-one. She puts on a tough facade and hides her pain, but she breaks down when she's alone. Her past experiences have left her feeling insecure and unwilling to let anyone get close to her heart. While we have an amazing friendship, I feel that her past trauma is impacting our relationship. How can I navigate this situation when she puts up walls and refuses to communicate with me?

I have recently discovered that my mother is having an affair with my sister's sports coach. This has caused a significant drop in my respect for her, as she had always taught us the value of honesty and loyalty. I found explicit messages and nude images on her phone, indicating the extent of their involvement. I feel betrayed and confused. Additionally, I have noticed that she regularly books a hotel room in our city every weekend. I don't understand why she would need a hotel room in the same city she lives in.

I recently moved to a new country because my previous one didn't offer many career opportunities. However, I miss the ease with which I could find someone I was attracted to in my previous country. It gave me a sense of motivation and hope, making me feel alive as I worked on improving myself as a man.

I have been struggling with my mental health lately. I have been diagnosed with Asperger's Syndrome and Major Depression, but I'm starting to doubt if these diagnoses are accurate. I still experience hypnagogic hallucinations, and even though I have tried two different types of antidepressants, my depression has only improved slightly.

I'm a 17-year-old young woman in the U.S. and I'm having a difficult time with my sister. She tells our dad about everything I do, as if we're little kids. If I go outside, talk to boys, use my laptop or phone, she feels the need to report it. I'm really frustrated and I don't understand why she behaves this way.

Over the past few years, I've noticed that I feel different from others. I don't experience emotions as intensely as those around me, and I struggle to understand or empathize with their problems and pain. I find myself having violent thoughts, visualizing harming others, and strangely enjoying it. However, I have enough self-control to recognize that acting on these thoughts would hinder my personal goals. I've done some research on psychopathy and took the psychopathy checklist (PCL-R), scoring 33 out of 40. I'm not a professional, so I'm seeking an expert's opinion on my situation.

I received a distressing call from my 13-year-old granddaughter today. She expressed that she is feeling very unhappy at home and revealed that she has been engaging in self-harm by cutting herself. When I asked if she had spoken to her mother about it, she shared that she did mention it two years ago in 6th grade but her mother never took her seriously or sought professional help. She confided in me that she cut herself again just last week. I am deeply concerned for her well-being and unsure of what steps to take. How can I support her in this situation?

Counselor: Thank you for sharing your experience with me. It sounds like you had a very vivid and intense dream that felt like real life. It can be quite unsettling when dreams feel so realistic. The fact that you were able to recognize it as a dream halfway through is actually a positive sign, as it shows some level of lucidity in your dreaming. However, I can understand why you found it scary and unsettling, especially with the difficulty in breathing and the inability to wake up.

I've noticed a concerning pattern with my fiancé whenever we're around his family. He becomes distant, treats me poorly, and speaks to me disrespectfully, as if I'm unintelligent. He ignores me while sharing stories, but opens up more to his mother. When I confront him about it, he denies any knowledge of his behavior and becomes defensive. As our wedding day approaches, I believe it's important for us to communicate and for him to show me respect regardless of who is present. I'm struggling to address this issue with him, as he's stubborn and tends to shut down. I need guidance on effective communication strategies and helping him understand the need for respect, even in front of others.

I'm feeling really hurt and confused right now. My boyfriend broke up with me last week and it was really unexpected. He called me and was crying, saying he couldn't handle the distance between us when we weren't physically together. He also mentioned that he acted differently around me compared to his friends.
Patient: I've been wondering about something, can erotic transference only happen between a patient and their therapist, or can it occur between any two individuals?

I'm really struggling with some disturbing thoughts and impulses that I've been having. I'm scared to seek help because I'm worried that if I'm honest about what's going on, I'll be locked up. I just want to get better and find some relief through medication. Today, I got into a physical fight with my fiancé, and I lost control. I tried to hug her after we argued, but she told me to stop and let go. I couldn't control my anger and ended up choking her and holding her down. I had thoughts of hurting her even more, and it felt like there were voices telling me to do terrible things. I have a difficult past, but I genuinely want to improve and be happy. Will I be locked up for these thoughts? Can't someone just talk to me and provide medication?

I'm a 15-year-old only child and I've been struggling with my mom's behavior for a while now. When I was 10, I learned that my mom had depression after a stillbirth. Since then, she has gone through periods of extreme sadness, weight gain, and excessive sleep. Even though she got a new job, she continues to struggle with her emotions and neglects household tasks and my needs. My dad says it's because of her brain, but it's hard not to take her outbursts personally. I feel like I'm not good enough for her anymore, and I don't know how to help her.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for almost a year now, and I am currently struggling with his insecurities. He believes that he is short, unattractive, and not considered a man in the outside world. I have known about his insecurities from the beginning of our relationship, so I have made efforts to boost his confidence without him knowing that I am aware of his insecurities. However, my efforts have not yielded any results. Recently, I discovered a forum where he posts about feeling "soul crushing" as a manlet. His insecurities are starting to affect me as well. I feel hurt that he feels this way, and I am saddened because I feel like I am not enough. Worse, I find myself occasionally snooping to ensure that he doesn't harm our relationship. Now, I want to help him overcome these insecurities, but I am aware that it may be difficult. I have tried explaining to him that he is not short at 5ft8 and that I do not see him that way. I have encouraged him to accept himself and make the most of the qualities he has. However, he says he has accepted it, but he will always hate his height. I am seeking an expert opinion on what I should do next. Should I accept his insecurities and distance myself? Should I express my frustration and tell him to focus on other aspects of life? And how can I prevent his insecurities from affecting me?

This 25-year-old woman from India is expressing her feelings of hurt and confusion regarding her long-term friendship with a guy. They had a close bond where they shared everything, including hopes, ambitions, embarrassing moments, secrets, and even sexual experiences. However, he suddenly left without saying goodbye. She was always there for him during his difficult times with past girlfriends and even supported him through a troubled engagement.

Patient: I've been having some issues with my dad when it comes to household chores. We generally get along well, but he doesn't seem to do them properly. For example, he doesn't wash his hands before cooking, and he doesn't thoroughly clean the kitchen. I've tried talking to him about it, but he gets annoyed and makes excuses. It's especially concerning now because my mom, who usually takes care of these things, is away. It's frustrating because I just want to ensure that my sister and I have a clean kitchen and healthy meals.

Lately, I've been experiencing intense feelings of anger and hate towards everything and everyone, including myself. It's gotten to the point where I physically feel pain in my chest and have disturbing thoughts of causing harm to others or even myself. These thoughts are intrusive and I can't seem to control them anymore. It's affecting my ability to connect with others and I find myself withdrawing from socializing.

I'm turning 21 soon and I've never been in a romantic relationship or even kissed a boy. It's been bothering me because part of me thinks I should be in a relationship, but another part of me doesn't want anything at all and just the thought of being in a relationship makes me feel sick. Everyone keeps telling me that I can't say I don't want something if I haven't even tried it. Two days ago, I joined an online dating site and chatted with a few guys. There's one guy who seems interested in me. He's attractive and has a great personality, but the idea of meeting him or being in a relationship with him makes me feel sick, not because of him, but because of myself. I regret joining the dating site and I feel guilty because I think he's looking for something I can't give him. I don't want to hurt his feelings, but the truth is, I don't feel like dating, kissing anyone, or being in a romantic relationship. Sometimes I fantasize about it, but as soon as it could become a reality, I feel uncomfortable. I don't want to be in a relationship just because I'm desperate and afraid I'll never find someone who's interested in me. I'm scared that I'm getting older and might end up single for the rest of my life. I want to have kids, so I don't want to be alone forever. I have this feeling that if I force myself to do something I don't want to do, I might never want to try it again. But maybe I should force myself into a relationship... I really don't know. I apologize if my English isn't correct, and I appreciate your time and response.

As a 16-year-old guy in Morocco, I've been feeling pretty messed up lately. I've tried looking for answers online, but nothing seems to help. It's overwhelming to try and summarize everything, so I'll share some statements about myself instead. I'm here because I want advice on whether I should see a psychologist and what the potential benefits would be. Can you help me understand why it might be worth it?

I have been dealing with a challenging situation involving my aunt. She has been consistently belittling and saying hurtful things to me. This behavior has always existed, but it has escalated since my mother's passing a few years ago. I believe my aunt feels entitled to mistreat me since I lost the one person who always supported me.

Lately, I've been experiencing disturbing thoughts and urges to harm others during the night. These thoughts don't occur during the day, but as soon as it gets dark, they intensify. I want to emphasize that I don't have any desire to harm myself, although I have had suicidal thoughts in the past. I've even started planning and fantasizing about ways to carry out these violent acts. I've been immersing myself in crime novels and books about death as well. It's alarming to me that I'm only 13 years old and dealing with these dark thoughts. I shared this with a friend, and she suggested that I seek help. I'm feeling scared and unsure about what to do, but I would really appreciate your assistance. Thank you.

My adult son was diagnosed with schizophrenia about 15 years ago. Recently, I've noticed a significant decline in his mental health due to his use of meth and synthetic drugs like spice. Surprisingly, I've observed that marijuana seems to have a calming effect on him. Additionally, he has been using nicotine more frequently, claiming that it helps calm his mind. However, both substances require increasing amounts to achieve the desired effect. I've come across conflicting studies regarding the relationship between marijuana and schizophrenia. I'm curious about the potential effects it could have on someone who has been living with this illness for many years. Can you provide any insights?

I've been through a lot of experiences throughout my life that have left me feeling lost and confused. It started when I was just a child, feeling responsible for my grandfather's death. Since then, I've dealt with insomnia, hyperactivity, and even physical violence during my time in boarding school. I've had my heart broken and turned to substances like weed and alcohol to cope. Recently, a friend's psychosis and a comment from another friend made me question my own sexuality. I sought help from addiction experts and a psychiatrist, but their diagnoses and recommendations have left me feeling unsure and scared. I now realize that I am straight, but I'm still concerned about my mental health and whether I may have bipolar disorder or schizophrenia.

Over the past year, I've been struggling with issues related to motivation, relationships with others, family dynamics, and most importantly, my own self-worth. Throughout my life, I've noticed a pattern where I go through phases of high energy and enthusiasm for certain things, but eventually, I always seem to regress into a state of hopelessness. It's like I feel as though I'm just wasting space and not living up to my potential.

Hello, I recently received a diagnosis of Bipolar II from a clinical psychologist. However, I am struggling to accept this diagnosis as I don't believe I have bipolar disorder. I do experience periods of hyperactivity where I take on multiple projects, feel confident, and require very little sleep. But I also have periods where I feel down, have low self-esteem, and struggle with basic tasks. I have never engaged in any destructive behaviors during my hyperactive phases. I work hard and achieve a lot, and when I feel down, I have occasional thoughts of suicide but I know they are illogical. I don't understand why I would need mood stabilizers and antipsychotics as I haven't had any major breaks from reality. I'm torn between accepting the diagnosis and thinking it's not accurate. How do I navigate this uncertainty and should I consider medication? I don't have a support system in place and I'm concerned about compliance with treatment.

I have been experiencing a lot of distressing thoughts lately. Specific lines from songs and insults towards myself keep repeating in my head for extended periods of time, sometimes lasting up to 45 minutes or even an hour. These thoughts occur randomly throughout the day, and it's especially difficult when I wake up with a particular line stuck in my head. I also find myself repeating derogatory insults to myself out loud, as if they are being directed at me by someone else in my head. This happens until I feel like I don't need to say them anymore. I have been diagnosed with anxiety, and both the repetitive thoughts and insults worsen when my anxiety levels are higher than usual. My mind is always racing, and it feels like there's never a quiet moment. I have trouble holding onto a complete thought, which leads to confusion about my own thoughts and feelings. The only time I can sleep is when I exhaust myself completely by staying up very late. This racing thoughts and confusion also affect my ability to focus, making it difficult to read and prepare for the upcoming semester. I'm worried that everything is only getting worse. Can anxiety be the cause of all these symptoms? (age 20, from US)

I've been feeling a lot of conflict lately when it comes to my interactions with people. While I wouldn't say that I hate them or wish them harm, I find it very difficult to tolerate them. I have this general dislike for people and view them as idiots, regardless of their level of education. This is concerning to me, especially because I'm currently unemployed and the thought of working with people is discouraging. I feel overwhelmed at the idea of interacting with others, as making small talk and meeting new people is incredibly challenging for me. I want company at times, but when I have it, I find myself wanting them to go away. Even with the few people I do know personally, I don't particularly like them. This includes my family, whom I love but also feel a strong dislike towards. I have one friend that I do like, but I worry about spending too much time with her and potentially starting to dislike her as well. I also have concerns about becoming too attached and dependent on her, and the fear of our friendship breaking apart and causing me emotional pain. This is all causing me a great deal of worry.

For the past 7 years, I have been experiencing difficulty getting through conversations without crying. It feels embarrassing and uncomfortable for everyone involved. I have noticed that there are three general triggers for my tears, which are actually things that I wouldn't typically find emotional. Firstly, any large group activity, such as baseball games or choir performances, always leads to me crying at some point. Secondly, even the slightest sentimental sharing from others, like my friend talking about her son's kindergarten graduation, causes me to burst into tears uncontrollably. Lastly, whenever the topic of spirituality comes up, I find myself getting emotional and have even stopped attending church because of it.

Lately, I've been experiencing some concerning thoughts and behaviors. I find myself having curiosity about what would happen if I were to stab someone with a sharp object when I have it in my hands. It's not because of anger, but rather a sense of curiosity, particularly about what the blood would look like. This curiosity led me to cut my hand open with a knife last week, just to see the blood. It didn't occur to me that this was unusual until I was cleaning up. Additionally, I've noticed that whenever I touch someone, I start imagining what their insides would look like if they were cut up.

I've always been a very imaginative person, and that trait has carried on into my adulthood. I used to believe that I could think things into existence and even see the future. However, I also had some beliefs that were harmful to me, particularly an obsession with my weight. This fear of becoming fat turned into a distorted perception of my own body and a belief that others were hiding the truth about my appearance. I became obsessed with counting calories and it took me a while to realize how delusional I was. I thought I had overcome this fear, but recently I've noticed those same thoughts resurfacing. I had a panic attack when I saw pictures of myself from a family picnic, even though I logically know I am thin. I'm worried that this fear will become severe again and I'm avoiding triggers. How can I stop this from escalating?

I have been feeling really isolated and left out recently. I used to have a close group of four friends, but it seems like they have formed closer bonds with each other and I'm left feeling like the odd one out. They even have a group chat without me and make plans without including me. At school, they still talk to me but it feels like they are just putting up with me.

Lately, I've been struggling with handling my problems. Normally, I can push through my day without any issues, but now it feels like I need to do something different. Specifically, when I'm in school, I think everything is going well, but then I receive a letter saying that I failed my classes and need to take summer school. It's frustrating because I want to change the way I think, but I end up feeling trapped and just push the problem aside for another day. This has been my coping mechanism for as long as I can remember, but I know it's not a healthy way to deal with things. My teachers have suggested going to extra help, getting a tutor, or staying after school, and while I know these are great ideas, I struggle with accepting help. Whenever someone tries to help and tells me what I need to do, I just feel stressed out for no reason. I understand that I need help, but I don't know how to make myself actually seek it instead of brushing it off and pretending it won't have any negative consequences in the long run.

I'm an 18-year-old young man from the US. About two years ago, I injured my knee and ever since then, I've become hyperaware of any pain in my body. It's gotten to the point where I thought I was having a heart attack and went to the ER four times. I've also worried about having cancer and have undergone numerous tests and doctor visits. I even had a colon test because my mom had colon cancer and I'm constantly worried about my health, as well as my parents' health, especially my dad.

I am a 23-year-old female who has always identified as heterosexual. However, I've been experiencing some confusion and anxiety lately. Although I have never been in a romantic or sexual relationship with a man, I have always felt emotionally and physically attracted to them. The thought of being in a romantic relationship with a woman repulses me and makes me feel sick. However, I have noticed that I feel aroused when I watch two women engaging in sexual activity, which is confusing and scary for me. I have been struggling with intrusive thoughts that I might be gay, even though I know deep down that it's not true. This has affected my sleep and appetite, and I constantly worry about losing my interest in men. I recently read about HOCD and found some similarities in my experiences, which provided temporary relief. However, I keep doubting myself and convincing myself that I'm in denial about being gay. I have spoken to my mother and a few friends about how I'm feeling, which helps temporarily, but then I doubt myself and feel depressed. I feel like I've lost my identity and I want to feel the way I used to, excited about the prospect of meeting a man and falling in love. I can't afford therapy right now, so I was hoping for some techniques to help me calm down and think more rationally.

Throughout my life, I have often felt like an outsider and have struggled with self-acceptance. I used to resent myself for being different, but I have worked on letting go of that self-hatred. When others didn't understand me, I would often blame them for their lack of understanding, especially when they would bully me. As a result, I developed a general dislike for people and now struggle to initiate new relationships. However, I do have healthy relationships with a few close friends.

I'm a 14-year-old living in the United States. I'm feeling overwhelmed because my parents have complete control over my life. They even resort to physical force at times. For instance, recently, my mom got angry at me for spending 15 minutes on the phone in the basement. She called my dad for support, and he ended up hitting me on the side of my head four times, causing my glasses to bend.

I'm feeling overwhelmed with my 25-year-old daughter's constant financial struggles and dependency on us for help. She has a five-year-old son and has been experiencing ongoing drama in her life. We've been assisting her for the past ten years with various issues, such as paying rent and fixing her car. It seems like there's always something happening, like her hours being cut at work, her inability to pay rent, and her poor credit rating due to a misdemeanor on her background check.

When my sister and I were younger, we experienced both physical and emotional abuse from our mother. It was a difficult time for us, but I want to clarify that the abuse is not ongoing. My sister has not had contact with our mother since she was nine years old. However, the experiences have had a lasting impact on me, leading to severe depression and multiple suicide attempts.

My girlfriend and I have been in a rocky two-year relationship. We are engaged now, but we have been facing a lot of challenges. I am in medical school and she is unhappy with the city we live in. We also both struggle with insecurities, anxiety, depression, and trust issues. I've realized that a lot of my issues stem from my own insecurities and low self-esteem. As a result, I tend to rely on my girlfriend to validate my self-worth.

My brother's behavior is really concerning me. He's 21 years old and displays extreme aggression when things don't go his way. He verbally abuses those close to him and blames us for not helping him. He's also lazy and refuses to work, using our parents' divorce as an excuse to be depressed and miss work.

When I was 6 years old, I experienced sexual abuse from my brother. It's been difficult for me because I only have fragments of memories from that time. My brother acted like it never happened and never touched me again. Growing up, I was confused about whether or not I was actually abused. I've struggled with self-control since childhood, such as continuous eating and excessive TV watching for 8 to 10 hours. I neglected my health and kept all of this to myself. Recently, I cut off contact with my brother and my condition has worsened since accepting that I was indeed sexually abused. My daily activities have been severely affected and I feel like I am being controlled by someone else when I'm alone. I tend to procrastinate a lot and deliberately harm myself, even though I don't want to. I tried therapy before, but it didn't work out for me. I feel lost and don't know what to do. Can you help me? (age 23, from India)
I've been dealing with severe social anxiety for the past two years. It was so bad that my stutter, which I've always had, made it even more challenging for me. I'm 22 years old and from the UK.

Patient: Hello, I've been experiencing frequent mood swings for the past 6 years while in a relationship with my partner. I used to attribute it to my personality, but now it's affecting our relationship. Even a simple joke can make me angry and I struggle to snap out of it. I also struggle with unfounded jealousy and obsessive thoughts that I can't seem to control. My partner has stopped sharing things with me out of fear of my reaction. I often feel overwhelmed, crying over small things and feeling sorry for myself. I love my partner deeply but worry that I'm holding them back and making them unhappy. I'm not sure if this is just my personality or if I should seek help. I would appreciate some advice on where to start.

I have been struggling with two goals that I really want to achieve, but I can't seem to get started on them. It's frustrating because I know I have the skills and abilities, but I constantly doubt myself and lack confidence. My sleep schedule is also really off; I stay up late watching TV and then end up sleeping until noon. It's affecting my motivation and productivity. Additionally, I have a lot of things in my house that I want to give away, but I can't seem to take action on it.

Over the past few months, I have been struggling with intense periods of depression and anxiety. However, I have found that through a combination of prayer, meditation, and self-reflection, I have been able to confront these challenges head-on and work towards resolving them. This has allowed me to discover effective solutions to my problems and regain a sense of motivation.

I have been in a relationship with my girlfriend for about six months now. She tells me that I am everything she has been looking for and I believed her, as I have been completely open and honest in our relationship. However, I have noticed that she still communicates with people from her past in ways that make me feel hurt and insecure. They send her messages that are sexually suggestive and it really depresses me. I have expressed my concerns to her, but she says these people have been there for her in the past and she doesn't want to cut them off completely.

I've been in a relationship with this guy for almost 3 years, and I'm feeling really lost right now. Throughout our relationship, I've discovered that he's been engaging in inappropriate conversations with other women. Despite confronting him about it and setting boundaries, I recently found out that he's been messaging random girls on Facebook and expressing interest in them. I'm feeling anxious and physically unwell. I don't want to be a single mom of two with no income, and I still love him. Is it unhealthy for me to hold onto this relationship?

Over the past 5 years, I have been struggling with ADHD, trichotillomania, compulsive lying, compulsive eating, and low self-esteem. It's been really difficult because even though my mom is a psychiatrist, my compulsive lying has caused my family members to turn against me. They all seem to hate me and when I try to reach out for help, they ignore me. It's painful to know that I brought this upon myself.

I recently rented a beautiful flat, but ever since I moved in, I've been plagued with anxiety. I have this constant fear that my sister-in-law, who has a history of copying me without giving credit, will also buy a flat in the same society. I worry that she will overshadow me and take credit for finding this place, even though we rented it first. It's causing me so much stress that I've stopped inviting anyone, especially my in-laws, to my home. I'm even considering moving to a different society before having anyone over. What's wrong with me, and how can I overcome this?

I've been feeling really down lately. I don't have any motivation or energy to do anything. I used to enjoy hobbies and spending time with friends, but now everything feels like a chore. I just can't seem to shake this feeling of emptiness.

I recently started dating a man who has three children. Initially, I thought it was nice that he introduced me to his kids. However, I quickly noticed that the kids didn't seem to want me around. They even took some of my belongings and damaged them within the first three weeks. Feeling unwelcome, I spent a lot of time in my room and stayed close to my boyfriend, which made the kids think that I didn't want them involved in our relationship.

I’m an 18-year-old from the US and I've been experiencing suicidal thoughts on and off for about two years now. A few months into having these thoughts, I started to self-harm. I'm feeling confused about whether or not I should seek help for these thoughts. Sometimes they become really intense. To calm myself down, I reassure myself that it's okay and that I won't act on these thoughts right now. I have a few different plans, though. I'm afraid that if I do seek help, they might dismiss me as an "attention seeker" or say that these feelings aren't real since they're not always present. However, I do feel motivated to stop self-harming and get better. This feeling of hopefulness doesn't last very long, usually just half a day or maybe a day or two if I'm lucky. Sometimes I experience overwhelming sadness and it's hard for me to resist self-harming. Certain people in my life cause me a lot of anxiety, which sometimes leads to self-harm. During these moments, I feel dizzy, weak, and start shaking and sweating. It feels like everything is unreal or like I'm in slow motion. I'm not sure what's wrong with me. Should I be worried? Is seeking help the right thing to do?

I often find myself living in my own world, where I imagine various scenarios and even create my own movies. In these imaginative moments, I envision myself as a singer, altering lyrics and languages to make the songs my own. I've even imagined inventing a machine that can erase people's memories, specifically the songs I've borrowed. However, when I snap back to reality, I still hold onto the belief that this machine exists and can make my fantasies come true. I've even stopped studying because I believe this non-existent machine will change my life. This is just a small part of my story, as there are many other instances where I've suffered due to the perfect version of myself that only exists in my imagination. Sometimes, I even contemplate the idea of wanting to be mentally ill, as it seems like a way to escape from reality. I've even searched for ways to become mentally ill.

Counselor: It sounds like you've been experiencing some difficulties in your long-distance relationship and have noticed a pattern of feeling upset and irritated with your boyfriend. It's important to explore your feelings and reactions in order to gain a better understanding of what might be going on. It's possible that the stress of being in a long-distance relationship is contributing to these emotions. Additionally, you mentioned that you had anxiety last year, and it's possible that this could be influencing your reactions as well.

I recently started a serious relationship with someone I met on OkCupid, but I'm feeling uncomfortable because my boyfriend still has an active profile on the site. He claims he's just looking for new friends, but it makes me feel jealous and I find it inappropriate. I've asked him to delete his profile, but he says he doesn't want to feel controlled by me.

When I was around 7 years old, I began experiencing intense feelings of guilt whenever I did something that I perceived as "bad." As I entered my teenage years around 13 or 14, I started experiencing sexual urges, despite coming from a semi-religious background. In an attempt to stop these urges, I would physically harm myself by punching my arms, legs, and head until I was bruised. This behavior continued until I was 15, when I started experiencing symptoms of depression that eventually escalated to suicidal thoughts by the time I turned 16. At the age of 17, I even went as far as planning a specific date and method for my suicide, although I did not act upon it.

I'm a 14-year-old trying to understand myself better. I struggle with sharing my feelings with my parents and others, often shutting people out. However, I find that I excel in giving advice to my friends and acting as a therapist to them.

I have been dating my boyfriend for almost 4 years, and lately, I've been feeling disconnected from him. We argue frequently about things like his prioritizing time with his friends over me and his failure to keep his promises. It seems like he doesn't care because he instigates fights and blames me for starting them. Whenever we argue, he leaves and then acts as if nothing happened when he returns. I've tried expressing to him that leaving is not a solution and that we need to communicate to resolve our issues, but he keeps repeating the same pattern. In our relationship, we both acknowledge our mistakes and apologize, but he has grown tired of apologizing and refuses to do so anymore. Additionally, earlier in our relationship, he cheated on me and I'm struggling to understand why I'm still with him. Part of me feels like I love him and have invested so much time, but another part of me wonders if I'm just holding onto something that isn't healthy. Recently, we had a fight because he bailed on me after promising to come over. I decided to ignore him, and in response, he got an Instagram account, which makes me feel uneasy due to the attention he receives from other girls. This pushed me to break up with him yesterday, but I'm finding it difficult to cope because I miss him, even though we keep falling into the same patterns of fighting. I'm unsure of what to do. Can you please provide some advice?

I am a 22-year-old man from India. I have been experiencing a recurring issue where I develop feelings of affection for others very quickly. I'm unsure if this is a problem or not, but this time it feels different.

I am a 19-year-old female student from Albania, currently in my second year of studying economics at a private university. I've been struggling with concentration issues, lack of self-confidence, and depression. I feel a sense of hatred towards everything I do. I've invested a significant amount of money and effort to get into this university, yet I haven't passed a single exam. I feel incapable of studying, and I constantly question my intelligence and worthiness.

I've been feeling really lost lately. I've struggled with depression in the past, and about a year ago, I had a really severe episode. I felt completely immobilized, like I didn't want to exist anymore. It was hard to even get out of bed. I'm not sure if I'm still depressed or if this is just a temporary slump.

I've been struggling with a deep sense of inadequacy and feeling like an imposter. Despite accomplishing impressive things like attending a top Ivy League college and being a medical student at one of the best medical schools, I constantly fear that others will discover I'm a fraud. This feeling has plagued me since high school, where I excelled academically but always felt insecure about my intelligence. I attribute my successes to working tirelessly rather than natural talent. It's frustrating to see peers achieve greater success with less effort. I feel like I'm a slow learner and lack the ability to grasp basic concepts quickly, which is concerning given the demands of a career in medicine.

Patient: Hi, I’m new here and I hope you can help me. I've been feeling lost and unsure about my values and interests lately. In the past, I used to have a strong moral code as a Christian, and I had a mix of conservative and liberal beliefs. I enjoyed reading and forming my own opinions on various topics. However, during high school, which was a difficult time for me, I went through significant changes. I became an atheist, then a satanist, and along the way, I lost all interest in studying and making friends. One of my teachers influenced me greatly by promoting the idea that there is no absolute good or bad, and everything is relative. I embraced her teachings at the time, but now I feel disconnected from myself. Nothing seems to matter anymore, and I've lost my passion for making a positive impact and helping others. I no longer feel like a human being with a soul. I regret the influence of that teacher and the phase I went through. I've been trying to find my old self again for years, but nothing seems to work. I would appreciate any insight into what might have caused this change in my character and any guidance on how to rediscover my true self.

I've been through a lot of difficult experiences in the past few years. In October 2013, my beloved Granny passed away after a long battle with cancer. Then, in January 2014, my girlfriend of 6 years developed psychosis and has been in and out of the hospital since then. I've been by her side throughout this challenging time. Additionally, I've had two friends who became violent and angry towards me in April and stopped talking to me. In May, I tragically lost a friend to suicide. I still have some friends, but I feel like they are avoiding me.

My best friend has always struggled with social interactions and frequently experiences episodes of depression. He has sought help from therapists in the past, but he is hesitant to open up about his urges to harm himself or others due to fear of judgment or mistreatment.

I have been doing a lot of research on relationships, but I can't seem to find any advice that fits my specific situation. I am from Brazil and I have been dating my girlfriend for over a year now. The only issue is that there is an age gap between us - she is 31 and I am 24. Despite this, I love her deeply and want to build a future together.

Throughout my entire childhood, I experienced deep trauma. My parents divorced when I was six, and I ended up living with my abusive mother. From a young age, I have struggled with chronic depression and have had spiritual experiences, including seeing demons both when awake and asleep. I even had terrifying imaginary friends who were demons. I have attempted suicide multiple times and often go through episodes of intense sadness, self-harm, and psychotic thinking when I am alone. I also struggle with paranoia, severe depression, anxiety, insomnia, and compulsive self-hate. I'm only 13, and I haven't received much help for my mental health issues. I tend to hide my true emotions, but they can easily overwhelm me. I'm unsure if I have schizophrenia or psychosis. What do you think?

Over the past few years, I've found myself caught in a complicated situation. I had a close friendship with a girl, whom I'll refer to as B, and we were all part of a tight-knit group of friends. However, during that time, I also had an experience with another girl, Q, which awakened my sexuality. Q and I became intimate and she even expressed interest in a relationship. I ended my ties with B to pursue this new connection, but Q eventually changed her mind and I found myself going back to B. I've been stringing B along, making false promises, and when she tries to distance herself from me, I go back to Q.

Two months ago, I started engaging in self-harm by cutting myself. This behavior has been a coping mechanism for me due to long-standing feelings of insecurity and self-hatred. The situation worsened when my sister began body-shaming me by calling me fat, and even my dad made comments about my weight. One night, I found myself alone in the kitchen with my dad's razor blade on the counter, and I impulsively cut my arm. I found some relief in the act and continued doing it. When my mom discovered the scars on my arms, I had to explain everything to her, including how I felt about myself. She informed my dad and sister, but therapy was never suggested, and I still have access to the blade. My sister has not apologized and continues to make hurtful comments, sometimes even encouraging me to self-harm.

Patient: I’ve been diagnosed with PTSD, which I believe stems from the severe bullying I endured for almost 10 years. I started therapy two months ago, and while it has helped with my crying and anger, I feel increasingly tired, frustrated, and miserable. I also feel like I'm failing in life and school. I don't have many friends, and the ones I do have are from high school. I'm terrified of talking to people, although I can do public speaking without any issues. I don't think therapy is helping me, and my psychology teacher's dismissive attitude makes me feel like my problems are insignificant.

Counselor: It sounds like you're experiencing a lot of frustration and resentment towards your husband and your current situation. Moving to a new country and being unable to work can be incredibly challenging, especially when it goes against the promises that were made. It's understandable that you feel a loss of identity and self-esteem as a result. It's important to acknowledge and validate these emotions.

I recently ended my engagement with my fiancé. We had been together for six years, and the last two of those years we were engaged. I made the decision to move out because my fiancé was feeling overwhelmed by the pressure of his job, and he also felt that I was putting pressure on him. Whenever I tried to initiate conversations, he would accuse me of nagging and leave.

I've been struggling a lot lately and it's really affecting me. I was diagnosed with schizophrenia, but I don't feel like that diagnosis accurately represents what I'm going through. It's frustrating because even though I'm in an early psychosis program, I still feel like I'm not improving in certain areas. I'm starting to lose hope that I'll ever be able to live a normal life.

My father has experienced a significant transformation in recent years, embracing a newfound devotion to Christianity. Unfortunately, he has also undergone a radical nephrectomy due to kidney cancer. Throughout the challenging process of battling the cancer and the numerous hospital visits, he displayed remarkable strength and positivity. However, since the surgery, he has been expressing thoughts of suicide, which is completely out of character for him. Additionally, his previous struggles with anger seem to have resurfaced even more intensely.

I'm feeling really down and dissatisfied with myself. I currently work as a teacher at a university and also teach at a high school. I feel like I'm just going through the motions and my thoughts are consuming me. Last year, I taught without a break and it left me feeling exhausted and even had some breakdowns. My psychiatrist has diagnosed me with bipolar disorder type 2, but my psychologist thinks I have generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) instead. I've tried so many different medications and the side effects have been really uncomfortable. I want to stop taking them, especially because I feel like they're affecting my thinking and making me slower. I also don't get to see my psychologist very often, which adds to my feelings of tiredness and lack of purpose. I know I'm being hard on myself and making excuses, but I just feel so worn out. I hate that my primary physician also includes the bipolar diagnosis. I don't want to take lithium and even the ticks I experience are bothersome. It's all becoming overwhelming and I don't know what to do.

I've been friends with a girl online for almost 10 years. She's always struggled with depression and has had a history of dropping out of school. She's currently 24 years old and just landed a great job. However, shortly after starting, she began to rapidly deteriorate. Given that I have Bipolar II, I suspect she may also be experiencing bipolar disorder. She goes through rapid cycles of manic states and depression, and she has confided in me that she constantly thinks about suicide.

I'm a 14-year-old male from Hong Kong, and I've noticed that I have a strong interest in looking at the inside of people's mouths. When I do, I sometimes experience sexual arousal and excitement. I even search for mouth pictures and videos online to fulfill this desire. I have also asked my classmates to open their mouths, which further arouses me. Am I normal or is something wrong with me?

Hi there. I am a genderqueer person in graduate school for mental health to become an LCPC. I am worried that having a gender identity that is incoherent to most others will lessen my ability to build a therapeutic alliance with a wide range of clients. I am worried I will not be effective outside of a very narrow community. I have thought about trying to live as more clearly female or male, but this idea is uncomfortable to me. I feel the answer I keep getting is that I have to be myself to create an authentic relationship, but I think that answer ignores the reality that expressing a genderqueer sense of self often confuses most people and impedes building relationships very often. Yikes. What do you think???

Recently, I've been experiencing a distressing situation with my husband. He initially asked me to take videos of my sister naked after she showered, and I reluctantly gave in to his persistent requests. He assured me that he wouldn't ask again, but unfortunately, he continues to do so. This has created a lot of tension and discomfort for me, to the point where I can't even be around my sister without him asking for more photos. It's causing me to feel a deep sense of hatred towards her and resentment towards him. He tries to justify his behavior by saying it's what turns him on, but it hurts because I believe I should be enough for him. I've always felt like I've been in my sister's shadow - she was always the "good" one, while I was more rebellious and ended up facing hardships in life. Seeing her effortlessly attract friends and now witnessing my husband's attraction to her has intensified my pain. We've only been married for 11 months, and we're expecting our first child soon. Despite the challenges, I don't want to lose hope that he can change, but he refuses to let go of this obsession, which is causing significant damage to our marriage. It's heartbreaking to see him indifferent to my tears. We're both quite young, with him being 24 and me 22, and I'm hopeful that he will outgrow this behavior. However, it has become an unhealthy obsession that is causing me immense pain. I just wish I could make him understand the impact it's having on us. What should I do?

Recently, I've been experiencing episodes that I can only describe as blackouts. They seem to occur when something traumatic is happening or about to happen. During these episodes, I feel like I'm being pushed aside and I lose control over my actions. It's painful, and it feels like someone else is in control, laughing at me when I try to fight it. I don't remember the specifics of what happens during these blackouts, but I do remember the intense pain and how they find it amusing. The last time it happened, I was texting my fiancé and I had an episode. When I came to, my fiancé was telling me to wake up and I discovered a patch carved into my leg along with some eraser burns. Now, I'm constantly thinking about the nickname they gave me, "Patches," and how much they enjoyed the pain. It's become difficult for me to be around people and I'm afraid that one day I might hurt someone. However, I don't want to be institutionalized because on the outside, I appear normal. Do you have any suggestions?

I am a 22-year-old recent graduate and my fiance is 30 years old. We started dating when I was 18 and he was 26. Throughout our relationship, we faced some challenges, including my family's lack of acceptance towards our relationship. Despite that, we decided to continue dating and have been together throughout my years at school. Eventually, we made the decision to move in together when I moved to Dallas for the last two years of nursing school.

When I was in elementary school, I developed strong feelings for my best friend. She was always there for me when I was feeling down, and over time, those feelings turned into a crush. Unfortunately, she had to move away in fourth grade, and I never had a chance to tell her how I felt. Since then, I haven't been able to truly move on. I've never been in a romantic relationship because I feel like it wouldn't be fair to the other person, as I still hold onto hope that my friend might come back into my life. I'm 20 years old now, and I know I should move on, but I don't know how. Every time I think I've moved on, thoughts of her bring me to tears.

Lately, I've been realizing that a lot of my actions are driven by a need for validation from others. I catch myself daydreaming about posting something witty or clever on social media, hoping that certain individuals will see it and think highly of me. I also find myself constantly seeking approval by helping others on a public platform, hoping to receive thanks or recognition. Even in conversations, I feel happiest when people laugh at my jokes or appreciate what I say. It feels like everything I do is driven by this need for validation, and it's become like an addiction. Some of my life choices have been influenced by wanting to be seen in a positive light by others. My happiness seems to depend on the approval of others, and even asking for help now is rooted in wanting you to think highly of me and understand my struggle. Can you provide me with some self-help strategies and book recommendations to break free from this pattern and start discovering and pursuing what truly matters to me? Thank you for your support.

Lately, I've been struggling with a lot of procrastination. I find myself putting off chores around the house and even things I used to enjoy doing with my free time. I've noticed that when I'm not at work, I tend to isolate myself and spend a lot of time talking to myself instead of engaging with others.

I've been married for 7 years and recently my husband's behavior has become increasingly suspicious and controlling. He accuses me of cheating, goes through my personal belongings, and has even shown up unexpectedly at places I am. He has also started throwing things and screaming during arguments. This is causing a lot of stress and strain on our relationship. I want to save my marriage, but I'm not sure how.

Patient: I've been dating my girlfriend for about 2 years now, but she gets really upset when I don't share every detail of my life with her immediately. We have a long-distance relationship, with her living in Chicago and me living in central Illinois. We rely on phone calls and occasional Skype sessions due to our busy schedules. I'm currently back in school, and it takes up a lot of my time with studying and homework. It's becoming overwhelming to balance everything, including my obligations to her.

I'm really concerned about my sister's behavior. She has shown signs of anger issues and has been physically violent towards me, leaving me with scars from scratching and pinching. Today, we had plans to attend our cousin's prom, but she refused to get ready and we ended up going without her. She then texted us asking where we were, even though she knew we had left. When we returned home to pick her up for a family gathering at the pub, she became aggressive and started screaming at us. It was really scary and my mom didn't want to leave her alone, so we stayed home. Her behavior is controlling our lives and I'm starting to develop strong feelings of resentment towards her. I also struggle with anxiety and have had suicidal thoughts in the past. This situation is making things even more difficult for me. I'm genuinely afraid of her and don't know what to do because she refuses to listen. Even my best friend has noticed her violent tendencies, as she often hits me quite hard. I only playfully hit her back, but never as hard, and she knows that. I'm starting to wish she would just go live with my dad and leave us alone. What should I do?

I'm an 18-year-old girl who has been struggling with self-harm recently. In the past, I used to cut, but I sought help and started taking medication (Zoloft). However, now I find myself hitting myself and slamming my head against walls. I've taken quizzes for bipolar disorder, and they indicate a high score. But it's difficult to answer the questions accurately when I'm feeling so many different emotions. My boyfriend is worried about me because I become extremely irritated, which is when I start hurting myself. I'm not sure what to do next.

I had a friend in college who reminded me a lot of my cousin. Due to some family issues, my cousin's family and mine became angry with each other and we had to separate about 2.5 years ago. When I saw this girl who resembled my cousin, I couldn't help but pursue a friendship with her. We became very close, spending a lot of time together and sharing secrets.

I'm a 15-year-old boy from Singapore and I've been feeling overwhelmed by the pressure my dad is putting on me. It seems like he expects me to handle everything on my own, and it's causing me a lot of stress. What's even more frustrating is that he treats my siblings differently. They get more expensive gifts and more attention, while I often feel left out and overlooked, like on my birthday when I only received a speaker from my dad and nothing from my mom, while my brother got a laptop, games, and iTunes gift cards. It's really starting to affect me mentally.

I've been feeling really confused lately and I've been doing some research on borderline personality disorder (BPD). I've noticed that I have some traits that align with the symptoms of BPD. I would really appreciate some guidance and support.

I've noticed some concerning behavior from my mother lately and I'm not sure how to support her. She's 53 years old and going through menopause. Ever since my parents moved to the beach three years ago, she's been acting strangely. She becomes extremely jealous when my dad is happy and thinks that we are all against her. She even throws things when she's upset. I'm worried about her and my dad's well-being.

Lately, my mom has been feeling really down. Acting is something she's always been passionate about, but she's been unable to pursue it due to various constraints. Our city doesn't have much of a theater scene and her demanding job as a wedding photographer leaves her with little time for anything else.

Counselor: Thank you for sharing your concerns with me. It's important to address any discomfort or boundary issues that arise in therapy. Based on what you've described, it's understandable why you may feel uneasy about your therapist's actions. It's essential for therapists to maintain professional boundaries to ensure a safe and therapeutic environment.

I'm 15 years old and most of the time, I'm a happy and bright student. My life is generally nice, with many friends and a fantastic father. However, I have been struggling with my mother. She is lazy and constantly complains, which makes it difficult for her to contribute to the household.

When I was a teenager, I had a close male friend who was also exploring his sexuality. Over time, we became more comfortable with each other and eventually shared a kiss when we were around 13-14 years old.

I have been dating a guy who has been really supportive and helpful in improving my life, especially in terms of school and work. However, I find myself feeling extremely bothered and anxious when I think about him talking to other girls. It's causing me to behave in ways that I would describe as "crazy" and impulsive. I feel like I'm losing control and constantly imagining threats, even if they may not be real. This behavior is affecting not only my relationship but also those around me. This is not how I typically am in relationships, as I am usually calm and don't experience much anxiety. I'm concerned about my behavior and its impact on my mental well-being and relationships.

Growing up in Lebanon, I normalized my father's abusive behavior towards my family. As I got older, I realized the extent of the mental and physical abuse we endured. Recently, my father's behavior has escalated, with him spying on us and engaging in infidelity openly. My mother is trapped in this situation, fearing his threats if she leaves. He blames my mother for ruining his life, despite being the one who constantly threatened and harmed us. I've tried getting him therapy, but he refuses to go and we can't afford a good therapist. I'm feeling overwhelmed and on the verge of a breakdown after enduring 24 years of this madness. I want to help him, but I don't know where to start.

In the early stages of my relationship, my boyfriend became fixated on knowing how many sexual partners I've had. I initially tried to avoid answering, but eventually gave in and lied about the number to appease his jealousy. However, I felt incredibly guilty and decided to come clean a few days later. I couldn't bring myself to reveal the entire truth, so I only admitted to one additional partner. He struggled to cope with this information and made me promise that there were no more. Since then, I haven't felt as guilty about it.
