Three months ago, I started working at a grocery store, and it has been triggering my anxiety. I've always been an anxious person, but being in a social environment has made it worse. I struggle with interacting with people and putting on a happy facade. It got so bad that sometimes I would have to hold back tears due to anxiety. Initially, I resorted to using my sister's prescription anxiety medication, which I know is not the right approach. On top of that, I started taking kava root and 5-HTP. I found that being tired all day was more tolerable than dealing with anxiety. Recently, I started self-medicating with a supplement called Phenibut, along with occasional use of 5-HTP. Phenibut is known to be effective for social anxiety and helping individuals be more at ease in social settings. I take the maximum recommended dosage of approximately 1060mg, and it has been quite helpful once I got used to it. I no longer feel intimidated by my male coworkers, I can confidently answer the phone, and I can interact with customers without fear. While I understand that self-medication is not a substitute for therapy, if it is effective for me, does that mean it is still wrong?

My girlfriend and I have been together for a year now. She has been dealing with chronic depression, mild OCD symptoms, and anxiety. She had a difficult upbringing with no emotional support at home. I've noticed that as our one-year anniversary approached, she became more stressed and her depression worsened. We started arguing a lot, often over small things. She even expressed thoughts of ending our relationship and feeling empty. I want to help her without overwhelming her. How can I support her during this difficult time and cope with her emotional distance?

I have been experiencing intense anxiety and a constant disturbance in my emotions. I often find myself unable to determine what I want to do next, which can trigger panic attacks. My doctor insists that I continue working, despite my emotional struggles. He prescribed me "Arpiprazole 15mg" to help manage my symptoms. However, I feel overwhelmed, anxious all the time, and unable to experience different moods or emotions. My mind feels both busy and empty simultaneously. I don't know how to navigate my life when I feel so disconnected from my own emotions. Can you help me understand what might be going on and whether my doctor's insistence on work is the right approach?

I have been struggling with worsening insomnia and it has led me to take a second medical leave from work. My depression has also worsened due to the lack of sleep and I feel frustrated that therapists and psychiatrists focus solely on treating my depression rather than addressing my sleep issues. I have tried various strategies like sleep schedules, sleep hygiene, and exercise, but nothing seems to help. My parents are suggesting I go to an inpatient psychiatric ward, but I'm not sure if that's the best solution. I've also seen sleep specialists and medication hasn't been effective. I wake up feeling exhausted even after sleeping for just 4 hours. Recently, I took a genetic test to determine which medications would work for me. I'm just looking for advice on what my next steps should be in order to function better.

I have been experiencing a multitude of concerning behaviors from my boyfriend. He often avoids answering direct questions and instead redirects the conversation by promising to take action. He also resorts to giving me the silent treatment frequently. During discussions, he tends to change the subject by criticizing me. Our conversations often become circular and he interrupts me, getting angry even when I remain calm and logical. Reasoning with him seems futile as he brushes off any concerns about his own logic. He gets angry when I don't reciprocate his irrational behavior. In financial matters, he repays me in small increments, unnecessarily prolonging it. When I canceled a date due to fatigue, he implied that he would be tired for an entire week. He criticizes me for not encouraging him to eat better and insists on seeing each other at least three times a week. He tries to control how I communicate and compares me to his previous partners. He engages in word play and manipulates me by claiming that terms like 'accusing', 'texting', 'saying', and 'meaning' have different meanings. Additionally, he changed his Facebook status to single after we became intimate, denied it when confronted, and did it intentionally to upset me. After losing his temper, he demands long periods of avoidance.

In the past, I was involved in a relationship that was on and off for about 5 months. It was not a healthy relationship, as we were not in love and it was primarily based on a sexual connection. I made the decision to have sex with him on the first night, which resulted in a loss of my virginity. I understand that my choices led me to this situation, and I fully accept responsibility for the heartbreak and sadness that I am experiencing as a result.

Patient: I've noticed some tension between my second husband and my 16-year-old son. We've been married for 7 years and have 2 sons together, aged 1 and 6. My husband doesn't say much to my son, but he constantly complains to me about simple things like my son drinking all the soda.

I'm currently in treatment for bulimia and alcoholism, and lately, I've been consumed by thoughts of past events that have been troubling me. When I was 12 years old, a stranger touched my breast outside my shirt and said vulgar things to me. I'm not sure if that qualifies as sexual abuse. Additionally, as a young adult, I've had three encounters that confuse me. Firstly, a stranger in college fondled me while I was asleep on a couch. I woke up to his touch but felt like it may have been my fault because I might have responded before fully waking up. Secondly, I had a blackout at a club and ended up bringing a stranger back to my hotel room. The next day, my friend informed me that the man had sex with me while I was unconscious. Lastly, a female friend of mine, who I didn't know had feelings for me, invited me over. I was actively drinking and using drugs, and she started touching me after braiding my hair. We ended up having sex, but I woke up feeling distraught and unsure if something was wrong or if it was just regret.

I've noticed some recurring problems in my behavior that have been present since I was young. One of them is that I compulsively eat my own skin. I spend a lot of time picking off skin and eating it, to the point where I feel sick. This has been happening since I was 4 years old. Another issue I have is that I struggle with trust. My "best friends" have pointed out that I seem incapable of trusting others. I think it might be because I don't believe they will actually be helpful. I've been like this since I was around 6 years old. When I do open up to someone, I try to downplay what I shared and distance myself from them. Additionally, I constantly feel like everyone hates me. I doubt everything people say, especially my "friends," and I carefully plan my words to avoid offending anyone. This has been going on since I was 6 years old. If I feel like a friend doesn't like me, I stop liking them and start seeing them as a villain. It's a pattern I've developed. Another aspect of my behavior is that I have an arrogant demeanor, but deep down, I have no self-esteem. I hate myself for being so arrogant and fake. I believe I don't deserve anything I have because I'm not genuine. No one, not even my parents, truly knows who I am. This has become more problematic recently. On one hand, I am overly confident about my positive qualities, but I also emphasize my negative traits. I always seek a purpose in my life and fantasize about being important to someone. I have grandiose ideas and hope to become famous so that I can reinvent myself as someone likable and have people who genuinely care about me. I've had these thoughts since I was 6 years old. I have this constant need to be adored. I often think about what it would be like to have a boyfriend who adores me unconditionally. Some people have even suggested that I might need someone like that in my life. Lastly, I believe that people are easily manipulated and that there's a formula to make them like you. However, despite my efforts, I still come across as awkward and struggle to be liked by 90% of my class. I've only recently discovered this. I really need help with all of these issues.

I've been noticing that I've been feeling really self-conscious about my appearance lately. I find myself constantly checking my reflection in the mirror throughout the day. There are times when I feel confident and happy with how I look, but then it quickly shifts and I feel incredibly ugly. This cycle repeats itself and I've even experienced moments of depression and crying because of it.

Throughout my life, I have experienced a sense of being overlooked and criticized by my mother. She immigrated to the United States from Europe after marrying my American father. While they were educated, I feel like they missed out on the 60's revolution and had a more traditional mindset. I've always felt a bit deprived and disconnected from them.

Hi, it's nice to meet you. I've recently come to the realization that I may have a problem. I've noticed that there are two distinct sides to my personality. One is extremely obsessive and overly emotional, which I refer to as "Loony." The other is emotionally detached, analytical, and intellectually focused, and I call that side "Bored."

Throughout the school year, I have been experiencing significant distress and anger due to certain movements that people make around me. Specifically, when individuals in my class tap their feet, click their pens, or tap their hands on their desks, I feel overwhelmed with anger. I find myself using my hands to block these movements from my view or covering my ears to try and cope with the frustration. On one occasion, a girl next to me was swinging her feet and I had to keep my right eye closed to avoid seeing it. Additionally, due to my anxiety disorder, I have had to leave class multiple times to find solace in the bathroom and calm myself down. Math class has been particularly challenging for me as the boy next to me constantly taps his feet and makes beats on his desk with his pens. There is also a girl in front of me who consistently swings her feet and another girl who frequently bounces and shakes her legs. These behaviors have consistently irritated me and caused a great deal of anxiety. There was even a time when I left the class crying, which I believe startled my teacher.

Patient: Hi, I've been feeling really worried about my mental state lately. Over the past few months, I've noticed that I've been feeling more and more disconnected. It's difficult to explain, but my brain feels foggy and fuzzy, and sometimes it feels like it's not fully connected. Specifically, my frontal lobe feels disconnected and hazy, almost like there's a barrier. My vision also feels strange, like I'm looking through thick glass. I've been having severe anxiety attacks where I question my own reality and fear that there's an alternate version of myself who has done terrible things. My sleep has been affected too, with my body feeling on edge and heavy, making it difficult to rest. There are times when I don't even feel present in my own body, like I'll walk into a room and not remember how I got there. I also experience sensations of floating or feeling disconnected from reality. I've been having full body tingles and shaking as well. Everything around me sometimes feels like it's moving too fast, and I feel like I'm not a part of it. Occasionally, voices seem distant and hard to understand. I recently found out that my cousin has schizophrenia, which has made me extremely afraid. I'm 18 years old and currently taking 40mg of Prozac for my depression and anxiety. I'm really scared and haven't felt like myself for a long time.

Lately, I've been feeling a lot of frustration and sadness in my relationship with my husband. Whenever I express my wants or needs to him, it feels like he doesn't respond or acknowledge them. I've tried various approaches like asking, crying, and explaining my feelings, but it seems like nothing works. It's causing me a lot of anguish.

My husband recently hired a female worker and it seems like she has developed feelings for him. She admitted her feelings to him through text messages and is aware that he is married with children. Unfortunately, instead of discouraging her, my husband seems to enjoy the attention and flirts back with her.

I met an American who is living in The Philippines online a few months ago. She was promised a modeling job when she got there. When she got there, things were not as they seemed and she ran away from where she was supposed to work. At the time, I was gambling too much and was tired of losing money to gambling. So, I decided to donate money to her to pay for her power bill. It felt good to donate to someone in need instead of spending the money on gambling. But over time, I realized that she constantly wanted money.

I'm still struggling with feelings of jealousy towards my ex-boyfriend's current girlfriend. It's been almost five years since we broke up, but I can't seem to move on from the fact that I let go of the chance to be with him forever. It's been eating at me and affecting my overall happiness. I need help moving forward.

I recently discovered that my dad has been emotionally abusive towards me and my mom for years. It was only after having several conversations with my school counselor that I began to realize the extent of the abuse. The counselor asked if I had ever feared physical violence at home, which was a moment of realization for me. Through these conversations and my own research on emotional manipulation, I have come to understand that a lot of the behavior at home is not okay. The issue is that before this realization, I was able to control my emotions. However, I am not allowed to express any negative emotions at home. I am expected to be the adult in the household all the time and act as a marriage counselor and therapist to my dad. He often vents about our finances, my mom's emotional stability, their sex life, his health, and even his approaching death. I am expected to offer advice and support on these matters, despite being only 17 years old. It is an overwhelming amount of stress for me. I am never allowed to talk about my own difficulties without being yelled at, yet I am still expected to help my dad with his marital issues. This has resulted in me feeling incredibly depressed, anxious, and even having thoughts of self-harm and suicide. Unfortunately, I am not allowed to go to therapy.

Patient's statement (revised): When I was nine years old, I experienced a traumatic event of sexual abuse that lasted for several months. However, I have only fragmented memories of the abuse, some of which are not even visual. I feel frustrated with myself for not being able to remember more, which leads me to question the validity of my experiences. I also struggle with feeling numb when I directly think about the abuse. Instead of feeling upset, I feel nothing at all. My main issue is that I find myself obsessively seeking out movies and TV shows that depict rape. It's not pleasurable for me, but rather a form of self-harm. Watching these scenes triggers intense emotional flashbacks, where I feel like I am experiencing the abuse all over again, with the same emotions I felt back then. I can't understand why I do this, as it causes me so much pain and takes a long time to recover from. It's as if I need to trigger myself with these scenes to validate my own experiences, since my memories are fragmented and easily doubted. I constantly think about rape, and whenever I hear about a rape scene in a movie, I immediately look it up, even though I know it will be harmful. I don't know why I engage in this behavior. What's wrong with me?

I've been in a relationship with my girlfriend for 4 years. I came across a similar situation on PsychCentral where someone asked about their girlfriend losing feelings. I wanted to ask what I can do as the person who will be waiting in this situation.

Over the past year, I've noticed that I lack sympathy and empathy compared to my peers. I haven't cried during any movies or books, even sad ones like war or Holocaust movies. It's concerning to me that I can easily move past these emotional moments while others around me seem deeply affected, including younger children.

I am currently in a long-term relationship with a man who has full custody of his four children, ages 10, 14, 15, and 19. I also have full custody of my three children, ages 8, 9, and 12. We have been together for almost a year and our relationship is committed and long-term. However, when we talk about the future, it often revolves around a time when our children are grown. He has introduced me to my children, and I have met all of his children except for the 14-year-old. He shared that he is hesitant to introduce me to his 14-year-old because she has had negative experiences with his past partners, even causing them to cry.

I have been experiencing periods of extreme sadness that seemingly come out of nowhere. During these times, I feel impossible to talk to and find myself picking fights with everyone, including friends, family, and even my partner if I'm in a relationship at the time. It makes me feel even more miserable when people start avoiding me. In the past, I have engaged in self-harm, although it has been years since the last time. I don't know how to fix this pattern, and when I finally come out of these spells, I feel disoriented and spend days apologizing to those close to me. I want to put an end to this, but I don't know where to start. I have seen a psychiatrist who diagnosed me with "mild depression," but they didn't recommend medication. These episodes occur two or three times a month and typically last for three or four days. Can you please help me?

I've noticed a pattern in my life where negativity and bitterness have become a part of my personality. I've experienced social rejection, bullying, assault, and alienation consistently, regardless of my attitude. I've tried being empathetic and caring towards others, but I either receive nothing in return or face unwarranted hostility. Even when I connect with people who have similar experiences, they don't want to associate themselves with me.

I've struggled with social anxiety for as long as I can remember. It actually started back in pre-school, but I wasn't officially diagnosed until I was 17. A few years before that, though, I started having these strange experiences where I felt disconnected from reality. It's hard to explain, but it felt like my arms didn't belong to me and I was seeing the world through someone else's eyes. Everything around me would feel unreal. I never mentioned these incidents to my therapist.

I am a 16-year-old from England and I have been experiencing persistent daydreaming and creating imaginary scenarios since I was five years old. I often find myself slipping into a character I have created and engaging in conversations with these imaginary people without even realizing it. It happens every day and sometimes before I go to sleep. I feel like I have no control over it and I can't stop myself from doing it.

"I recently had a concerning incident involving my 7-year-old son and his friend. While they were playing in my son's room, my husband overheard my son asking his friend if he could "lick his butt." Our son then proceeded to offer him money from his pocket in exchange for agreeing to it."

Lately, I've been struggling with symptoms of depression and social anxiety. I've been seeing a therapist and tried to explain everything to him, including my struggles with repetitive tasks due to fear and experiences of derealization. However, all he said was that I'm dealing with a lot of anxiety. I'm feeling frustrated because I need more understanding and support. Can you help me?

I've been deliberating whether I should leave my home country to work abroad or if I should return home. I'm 28 years old and have been working as a freelancer in media, photography, and journalism for the past two years. I have extensive experience in these fields, totaling almost a decade. I've always managed to find work in my hometown and have never ventured abroad. However, I'm starting to feel torn because I realize that my personal growth and financial stability may not be limited to my country.

I'm currently in my last year of high school and I'm feeling really isolated because I don't have any friends. This has been an issue for me since freshman year. I used to have two close childhood friends who I spent a lot of time with, but they found different friend groups when we transitioned to high school, and I've lost touch with them. I've tried to connect with some classmates from middle school, but I don't really consider them friends, more like acquaintances. I've been feeling detached from everyone at school since my sophomore year. During lunchtime, I just sit alone on my phone and don't really talk to anyone unless I have to. I've been researching symptoms of Avoidant Personality Disorder, and they seem to align with my experiences. I feel like I shouldn't talk to people because I'm afraid they won't like me for being boring. I spend most of my time at home doing independent activities like programming. The only friends I have are people I've met in the programming community. I only feel comfortable around people who I feel superior to in some way. I believe my sister is a major factor in my social difficulties. She has always belittled my interests and friends, which has made me feel unaccepted by everyone. I confronted her about this, and she has stopped putting me down for about a year now. However, my social life hasn't improved and it's actually getting worse as I go through senior year. I'm just looking for some advice on what to do before this problem becomes permanent.

Hello, I'm a 14-year-old who has been struggling with hair pulling and messing with my hair for as long as I can remember. I've noticed that my grandma and mom also engage in these behaviors. At first, I thought it was just a bad habit, but then I came across the term "Trichotillomania" online and started wondering if I might have it. However, I'm not sure if my symptoms align with this disorder. I don't pull out my hair for the sensation, but rather I repeatedly pull and tug on the ends of my hair until it tears and some hair comes out. I find satisfaction in pulling off split ends, even though it makes them worse. I haven't noticed any balding, just minor thinning. I enjoy the feeling of my hair being pulled repeatedly, but I'm uncertain if this qualifies as Trichotillomania. I do experience headaches from the tugging on my scalp, and I have terrible split ends. It's something I do constantly, anytime my hands aren't occupied. I find myself doing it when I'm bored or anxious, which is quite often. Recently, I discovered that playing with small magnetic balls during school helps me avoid pulling. I would appreciate your help in determining if this is something I should be concerned about. Thank you.

Lately, I've been feeling really down and I'm not sure if it's because I'm dealing with some depression or something else. There are times when I feel like crying all the time. My boyfriend doesn't really help the situation either. I do love him, but sometimes it feels like he's always emotionally attacking me. I find it hard to open up to him because he takes it very personally and gets defensive. I constantly feel like I'm in the wrong in our relationship.

I am an 18-year-old from Croatia and I have some concerns about my neighbor. He is 65 years old and has exhibited harmful behavior towards my pets in the past. About five years ago, he entered my backyard at night and drugged and choked my smaller husky to death. He has also poisoned my dogs previously, although they were fortunate enough to recover. Additionally, he has taken recordings of dogs, not necessarily mine, and played them loudly to provoke my own dogs to bark. Recently, he has resumed playing these recordings. He has also damaged my property by cutting down my fence and poisoning my trees.

I was married to a man with bipolar disorder for 30 years, and it was a challenging and abusive relationship, both verbally and sometimes physically. As a result of this marriage, my 33-year-old daughter has also been diagnosed with bipolar disorder. I find it difficult to connect with her, and it seems like she harbors resentment towards me. I want to clarify that I was not an abusive mother and did my best to protect her from her father's abuse. However, she seems to be closer to her father's family and holds a lot of anger towards me. I have been trying hard to establish a relationship with my daughter and her children, but she constantly starts fights and makes it difficult for me to see my grandchildren. I would appreciate some guidance on how to handle this situation.

I’ve been dealing with social anxiety disorder for most of my life. I used to cope with it well, but recently it seems to be getting worse. I've been feeling sad and upset all the time, crying over trivial things, and struggling to get out of bed. I've even called out of work or left early just to be alone. I feel numb or sad, and I've been having intrusive thoughts that my boyfriend doesn't like me or is cheating on me, even though there's no evidence to support these fears. Initially, I thought it was just my anxiety acting up, but this feels different. It's more like a sense of despair. This isn't the first time I've experienced this, but in the past, I thought it was due to specific circumstances. Usually, this phase lasts for about a month or two before I start feeling better. However, last summer, I had a period of what might have been hypomania. I engaged in risky behaviors, had multiple sexual partners, drank excessively, and experienced a lack of sleep for a week. During that time, I felt invincible, loved by everyone, and capable of anything. But now, I feel completely worthless, unlovable, and alone. At this moment, I feel terrible about myself and my life, and I'm unable to sleep. I've been contemplating seeing a psychiatrist for my social anxiety again, but I'm unsure if I should address these other issues as well. Am I overthinking this?

I've been experiencing disturbing thoughts about hurting others and have even been researching ways to make poisons. I feel particularly targeted by my friends who make fun of me, and it has led me to consider harming them. I struggle with social interactions and feel like my speech is odd. I don't have any close friends, but I have thoughts of harming my closest one. I hold a negative view of humanity and find it hard to connect with others. I have poor memory and often feel cloudy and irritated. I lack empathy and seem to mirror others' emotions to fit in. I have intrusive thoughts and engage in self-destructive behaviors like biting my nails and pulling out my hair. I'm unsure why I'm sharing all this, but it adds to my paranoia.

During my time in college in Singapore, I started experiencing dissociative disorder and partial seizures, which led to months of hospitalization and deferment from school. Now, I'm just two months away from graduation, but I feel like those were the darkest days of my life. My parents have become controlling since I recovered from my illness, limiting my phone and laptop usage, and even restricting me from seeing my friends.

A few years ago, when I was 16, my brother and I got into a physical altercation during which he choked me. This incident happened in front of his children, whom I had been helping to take care of since they were babies. I felt responsible for the situation and begged for forgiveness. Despite this, my mother decided that I should continue living in the same house as my brother. Recently, a similar incident almost occurred when I expressed my opinion about cleaning meat. My brother deliberately ignored me and when I questioned him, he said it was to prevent himself from getting angry. On that day, he was easily agitated, so I made a comment suggesting he needed a Midol, and he became even more angry. He began mocking me and threatened to harm me again. My mother and sister intervened to stop him. Since then, I have refused to eat anything that my brother prepares or buys. It makes me feel nauseous and repulsed. I know people would appreciate having food, but I can't bring myself to eat it. I feel an intense hatred toward my family, except for my mom, younger sister, and nieces. Even my older sister sides with my brother, and I hate myself for having these thoughts. I wish I could die, and I have resorted to self-harm. My mom urges me to forgive my brother, but he has thrown us out of the house three times. I feel lost and need guidance on what to do.

My brother, who is 33 years old, has been diagnosed with schizophrenia for about ten years now. Despite trying various antipsychotic medications, he has not shown any improvement and experiences delusional thoughts a few times a year. He is currently unemployed and receives disability payments. Our father manages his finances and he lives in a house owned by our dad, without having to pay rent. As a result, my brother receives an allowance from his disability payments instead of receiving the full amount.

Lately, I've been watching a lot of TV series about psychopaths and I've started to notice some tendencies in myself that I can relate to. I've become more anti-social and prefer to be alone. I even have thoughts about killing people and have planned a perfect murder on my laptop, although I haven't actually committed any crimes yet. I did, however, kill a dog that frightened me. My friends call me a vampire because I rarely leave my house and keep my curtains closed all the time. I recently took a psychopathy test and scored in the top region of the middle range. I've also realized that I haven't been very emotional for a while, even before watching those series. I had a fight with my father and wanted to kill him, but I stopped myself because I knew it would make me a prime suspect. After that, I went to my room and started slapping myself until my hands were numb. Am I a psychopath? Could I also be an ADHD patient? I'm feeling really confused and lost.

I'm reaching out for help because I've been struggling with a difficult family situation. Two years ago, I got married, and even before the wedding, my parents have been actively trying to sabotage my relationship. To make matters worse, my sister, whom my wife used to have a close bond with, has also sided with my parents against us.

I've been struggling with a strong aversion towards my father, seeing him as contaminated. It's been like this since my adolescence. I can't eat food he's been near, use utensils he's touched, or even sit on the same couch. I have a general dislike of human smell, breath, saliva, and mouths, but it's especially intense with him. I know it's probably influenced by our rocky relationship and his poor hygiene practices. I feel guilty treating him this way, but I can't help it. How can I start overcoming these irrational precautions without making myself too uncomfortable?

I've been feeling really uncertain about my feelings towards my husband lately. We seem to be constantly fighting, especially about money. I feel like he doesn't listen to me and whenever I try to express myself, it always ends up in an argument. I feel disrespected and unappreciated in our relationship. He tends to shift the blame onto me, even when it comes to our financial struggles, even though he's the one in charge of managing our money. He says our financial situation is my fault because I smoke, but he smokes too. I've been trying to quit, but it's difficult because I'm always so anxious. I wake up every day wondering when the next argument will happen and I'm scared to say anything because I don't want to upset him. He apologizes, but it feels like he gets triggered again so quickly, and I'm never sure why. I try to share my opinion, but it seems like he thinks I'm dumb. I'm only 25 years old, but the stress has caused my hair to turn grey and my face to age. I want to help with our finances, but when I try, he doesn't like my suggestions. I'm not sure if I should move on or not. We used to be best friends, but now I feel like I can't even talk to him. There haven't been any issues of infidelity, but I feel emotionally disconnected. We still have intimacy, but sometimes it feels forced because I'm so emotionally drained. We argue every single day and I really think he sees me as stupid, even though I'm not. I don't know if I should end the relationship or not. It breaks my heart to think about losing him, but I don't know how much more I can handle.

Throughout my childhood, I experienced severe abuse and neglect. For five years, I was confined to a room without any human contact or access to food. Now, ten years later, I am married and my spouse and I have recently purchased a new home. However, I am noticing that some of the trauma from my past is still affecting me in my present circumstances.

About 5 months ago, I met someone special who had also been going through a difficult time. We both initially thought we weren't ready for a deep emotional connection, but life had other plans. We started a relationship that became emotionally enriching but physically unhealthy. I've been trying to support him as he deals with the aftermath of drug-induced psychosis, but he had a recent psychotic episode and doesn't recognize his family. I'm not sure if I should continue trying to help him, especially since I'll be leaving for university soon.

I have noticed that I have a particular fascination with children between the ages of 5 to 15 since I turned 30. However, I want to clarify that this attraction does not involve any sexual desires towards them, except for girls who are at least 19 or 20 years old. I am aware that this is still inappropriate, given my age. Additionally, I occasionally find myself attracted to women older than 35 or 40. When it comes to children under 15, I am simply captivated by their physical features such as their beautiful skin, silky hair, and perfect features. I want to emphasize that I never have any sexual urges towards them. Sometimes, their appearance is so strikingly perfect that I am tempted to look at pictures or movies of them, but not in a public setting as I understand that it would not be considered normal and could be misinterpreted as a sexual attraction. I am wondering if there are any resources or information available to help me understand this better. Is this a unique condition or are there others who experience something similar?

I'm a 23-year-old woman from Switzerland and I've been dating my boyfriend for 2 years and almost 3 months. I have OCD and a fear of germs, which often triggers panic attacks. However, my boyfriend has been incredibly supportive and understanding. He has never gotten angry at me and has even changed his behavior in public to help me avoid panic attacks.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for 14 months now. We have had some ups and downs, mainly due to his insecurities and it being his first relationship. He broke up with me once because we were fighting a lot and he wasn't sure about his feelings. After a few weeks, he came back and said he was sure about me and wanted to spend his life with me. Recently, he lost his job and has become moody and stressed. Whenever we argue, he gets angry and dismissive when I try to talk things out. I want reassurance from him, but he just gets mad. I'm scared that he's only saying he loves me because he's afraid to hurt me again. Should I leave him alone when he's in a bad mood or do I have a right to seek reassurance without him getting angry?

My partner has a history of sexual abuse from his childhood, and so do I. He learned many sexual behaviors from the person who abused him, but she has since passed away. Recently, he introduced light bondage into our relationship and I've been open to trying it. However, last night he mentioned being with someone named "bad *her name*." It felt like he was a completely different person, and it was unsettling. He tends to get fixated on women from his past and it's all he talks about. I'm worried about him.

Patient's statement (rewritten): I'm a 14-year-old student in 9th grade. I've been struggling academically and emotionally. In 8th grade, I stopped attending school due to depression and difficulties with my peers. I ended up facing truancy charges. I was diagnosed with depression and anxiety disorder and my life felt like it was falling apart. I developed unhealthy habits and isolated myself from others. I tried attending an alternative high school in September 2014 but couldn't handle it. Since then, I've been attending an online school, but I'm failing 9th grade and feel completely alone. I'm currently on medication and attending therapy, but I'm still struggling to get my life back on track. I find solace in video games and TV, but I feel terrible about neglecting my responsibilities. I'm constantly overwhelmed by feelings of failure and lack motivation. I'm scared to return to a traditional school because of my past experiences with friends. I spend most of my days in bed, feeling sorry for myself. I'm worried that if I don't address this, I won't be able to graduate high school. I'm even considering asking my parents about going to a hospital, although that idea scares me. I really need some reassurance and guidance.

I'm a 21-year-old and I've been feeling empty and confused lately. I'm questioning my attraction to both men and women and I'm not sure about my sexual orientation. I also experience frequent mood swings, going from happy and friendly to suddenly getting angry and shutting people out when I hear or experience something I don't like. I've even tried to harm myself three times because I feel worthless. I prefer to be alone and avoid being around a lot of people because it makes me feel weak. I spend most of my time in my room thinking negative thoughts about myself and questioning my purpose in life. Additionally, I have a fear of germs and constantly use alcohol to sanitize. I have difficulty focusing, thinking clearly, and I feel empty every day. These feelings have been with me since childhood and have been worsening over time. I also experience sleep paralysis, which feels terrifying and makes me feel like my soul is leaving my body. I've had panic attacks as well, especially when I feel the urge to end my life. Can you please help me understand what is happening to me? Thank you.

I'm from Australia and I'm concerned about my friend's daughter. She's a nice person, but I've noticed that she has some controlling and manipulative behaviors towards her dad. We both have abandonment and rejection issues, which we believe stem from our absent mothers. She's 31 years old, married to her childhood sweetheart, and has two little boys. I've noticed that her behavior has been going on for a long time, and it seems to have gotten worse since she had the children.

I'm feeling really overwhelmed and unsure about my situation. I've been struggling with something and I don't know if there's even a solution, but I figured I might as well ask for help. I've been advised to seek professional guidance, but due to various reasons, including being a medical student, I can't do that in person.

I have been feeling very worried lately about my mental health. I'm a 20-year-old with a history of anxiety and hypochondria. In high school, my health anxiety was at its worst and I started hearing internal auditory hallucinations. I'm concerned that this might be a sign of developing schizophrenia or a similar issue.

Patient's statement (rewritten): I am seeking help because I am experiencing a range of troubling symptoms and I don't fully understand what is happening. Unfortunately, I am unable to afford visits to a psychiatrist at the moment. About a year and a half ago, I began experiencing an identity crisis and feelings of dissatisfaction with myself. I started doing things that went against my personal values and would cry afterwards. I pushed myself into uncomfortable situations and engaged in behaviors I didn't agree with, but couldn't stop. Over time, I began to lose a sense of myself and experienced fluctuations in weight. Currently, I am unable to work due to a constant feeling of discomfort within myself. My mind is always preoccupied with something unknown, making it difficult to engage in conversations, sleep, eat, or enjoy activities. I also experience persistent stomach pain and struggle to concentrate on anything, even watching a movie.

I'm really struggling with my relationship with my mother. She was absent during my childhood and now she's constantly trying to make up for it by smothering us with attention. She calls multiple times a day, visits several times a year, and stays for long periods of time. Our interactions are difficult because she treats us like children and demands respect just for being our mother. I've tried to explain that we're adults now and don't need her constant guidance, but she doesn't listen. It's really frustrating and I don't know what to do.

I've been feeling really down lately. I used to be a generally happy person, but now I feel sad most of the time. I've lost interest in things I used to enjoy and it's making me feel like I'm not really living. I'm scared that I might die soon, even though I don't have any specific health concerns. It's like there's a constant war of thoughts in my head and it's overwhelming. Can you help me understand what's going on?

Over the years, I have been struggling with unidentified issues that have caused me a great deal of distress. Despite my own research, I recognize that it is crucial for me to seek professional help. Since I was around eleven years old, I have been engaging in self-injury. It's difficult to put into words, but it feels like there is always a presence in the back of my mind encouraging me to harm myself as if I deserve it. I have always felt like an outsider in my social environment, unable to truly fit in. It often feels like I have to wear a mask and play a role just to blend in. I must also mention that I have no desire to fit in or form close relationships. Affection and physical interaction make me uncomfortable.

I'm really struggling with how to support my partner who was diagnosed with PTSD last year. She experienced childhood abuse and trauma, and it's been really difficult for her to live her life. She's currently receiving therapy, both cognitive therapy and medication like antipsychotics, antidepressants, and anti-anxiety pills. I just want to know how I can help her cope with this situation.

Patient: Lately, I've been experiencing difficulties with a problem that's been affecting my daily life. Whenever something feels off or not right, I have this intense urge to fix it until it feels right. This can apply to various things like the positioning of objects, the way I type, or even how I say things. It's becoming quite distressing because if I can't fix it, I get frustrated and give up. This is especially challenging in class when I struggle to write a word correctly or keep erasing and rewriting it. It's really impacting my grades and my parents don't know how to help. On top of this problem, I've been feeling depressed for the past 8 months. Over the summer, I spent most of my time indoors on the computer and listening to music, which only seemed to fuel negative thoughts about life. Now that school has started, things have gotten worse with declining grades and losing friends. I'm wondering if there are any strategies I can use to control this problem and if there's a name for it. I feel lost and unsure of what to do. I apologize if my explanation is confusing.

My daughter has recently befriended someone who is displaying concerning behavior related to their mental health. This individual, who has not disclosed their specific mental health issues, has been showing up at my daughter's home on a daily basis, claiming that it is their own family home. Despite my daughter's attempts to explain the situation, this person continues to persist. They have a history of being barred from their parents' home and exhibit delusions of fame. I am extremely worried about my daughter's safety and fear that this person may attempt to break into her home and harm her. I am hesitant to pursue a restraining order out of concern that it may escalate the situation. I am seeking guidance on what steps to take next. It is worth noting that this individual struggles with employment and has difficulty forming friendships due to their belief in their superiority over others.

Over the past year, I have faced significant challenges after openly admitting that I have been following the religion of my society out of convenience rather than true belief. This admission has caused a crisis in my life. I have experienced backlash at my conservative school, with teachers and classmates alienating me and spreading lies about me. My own mother feels ashamed and betrayed by my choices. It has been a difficult and isolating experience.

I am currently a PhD candidate in structural engineering. Recently, I received a marriage proposal from a 35-year-old man who is a PhD in pharmacy and works as a faculty member at a reputable university in Iran. However, I have noticed some concerning behaviors in him that make me think he may be suffering from depression. He tends to work very slowly, has very few friends, and doesn't seem to have any hobbies or interests other than listening to classical music and watching movies. Additionally, he has mentioned that he is easily awakened by even the slightest sounds at night.

Over the past two years, my wife has left my son and me, claiming she didn't know who she was or what she wanted. After a few months, she realized her mistake and said she wanted to come back home. Things seemed okay, and we were sexually active. However, I recently discovered that there is another man involved, making it the third person in her life. She once again claims she doesn't know who she is or what she wants, and it feels like she prioritizes herself over our family. She says we are on different paths, but she also admits to hating what she's doing while continuing to do it.

I have been in a relationship with my girlfriend for 4 years. I recently came across an article titled "My Girlfriend Lost Her Feelings" by Dr. Marie Harwell-Walker on PsychCentral. It resonated with my situation, but I'm looking for advice on what I can do as the person waiting for my girlfriend's feelings to return.

I am a 28-year-old female who is in a relationship with a divorcee who has three children aged 7-10. Over the past 8 weeks, I have been experiencing increasingly problematic anxiety attacks. These attacks are not only affecting my daily life, but they are also causing strain in my relationship. I have a history of abandonment and abuse, having been adopted at age 12. During these panic attacks, my past trauma resurfaces, making me feel unworthy. I can sense that I am pushing my boyfriend away unintentionally, and I fear that he will stop loving me because of the hurtful things I say during these attacks. It is becoming harder and taking longer for me to calm down after the attacks, and I feel embarrassed about my recent hiding episodes in the closet. I had some anxiety in college, but it was never this severe. I feel stuck and unsure of what to do. I don't want to continue burdening my boyfriend, but I also don't want to leave him. Should I consider going to the hospital next time? I know they won't admit me if I go when I'm calm, but I feel like it might be necessary soon. Please give me some guidance as I feel overwhelmed and lost.

A few years ago, I was diagnosed with schizophrenia. I started experiencing hallucinations and terrifying dreams. These symptoms, along with an intense fear of water, made me feel extremely unwell and convinced that I was suffering from a terrible disease. I also felt unsafe and believed that people were plotting against me. I was prescribed medication, which helped with my severe anxiety, but I now feel like a different person. I no longer experience happiness or joy in anything, and I've turned to binge eating to fill the void, resulting in significant weight gain. My cognitive abilities have also been negatively affected, and everything feels unreal. I feel trapped in a state of emptiness. Although my fear of water has improved slightly, I still have nightmares and struggle with restless sleep. My waking hours are as hopeless as my sleeping ones, and I've lost touch with my friends. Despite receiving treatment for schizophrenia, I continue to experience depressive symptoms. Are these symptoms related to my schizophrenia, or is there something else going on? I'm reluctant to seek medical treatment again due to past side effects. Is there any hope of feeling like my old self again? Thank you.

I am a fourteen-year-old who has been struggling with severe depressive symptoms and experiencing suicidal thoughts for several weeks now. Additionally, I have been dealing with social anxiety since fifth grade, which has been causing me a lot of distress. I have noticed that I engage in repetitive physical and mental tasks as a way to ensure safety, but I also have disturbing urges to break things or harm others. I have been overeating excessively and have gained a significant amount of weight in the past year. My academic performance is also suffering, and I am feeling incredibly trapped. Suicide feels like the only option at this point, and I am considering making a plan soon.

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for 7-8 months and overall, he's an amazing man who I'm deeply in love with. He's sweet, caring, hardworking, and adores me. However, there's one significant issue that bothers me - he tends to be jealous and insecure.

I'm really concerned about my mother's behavior and I need to understand what's going on. Our family recently moved from Brazil to the United States, and for the past few years, both my father and I have noticed some troubling signs. My mother can be very stubborn, violent when angry, and easily irritated. Her mood swings are unpredictable. Today, for example, I came home early to study after school, but decided to spend some time with her because I know she feels lonely. We had a great time together, but when I asked her to hurry up because I had to leave, she became upset and started calling me names, saying I don't give her enough attention.

I have been in a relationship with my partner for almost 4 years, and we got married less than a year ago. It has been challenging at times, but it hasn't been all bad. My partner, who is 26 and a year younger than me, has been struggling with addiction for the entire duration of our relationship. Despite this, he is mostly wonderful and able to function well, except when he goes through mood swings that lead to job losses or other issues. Currently, we are trying to discuss moving in together, but he is not ready and keeps making excuses. However, he did agree to go to a 29-day detox program and follow the recommended therapies from the facility. Although he has been clean from illicit substances for over a year now, alcohol has become a significant concern for him. He worries that he may not be strong enough to resist the temptation.

Since my husband passed away from cancer 16 months ago, I have been struggling with the loss. We were only married for 9 months, and the whole experience was incredibly challenging. The disease progressed in a rare and atypical way, which added to the stress and lack of support we had.

Hello, I've been feeling quite overwhelmed lately. Over the past few years, I've developed a strong obsession with video games, the internet, TV shows, and sports. It seems like these things have taken over my life and I've lost touch with my emotions. I was in a relationship for a year, but I ended it three months ago after discovering my partner was cheating on me. Since then, I've been struggling with a lack of desires, needs, and wants. I find it difficult to focus on anything and thinking about my past relationship brings up painful emotions. To avoid those feelings, I try not to think about it. My friends have been supportive, but I feel like I don't understand myself and my emotions anymore. I've even had thoughts of ending my life, although I haven't acted on them because I lack motivation. I've been procrastinating a lot lately and it's been causing tension with my mother. Her reactions to my mistakes make me angry, and I've noticed that I hold grudges against anyone who tries to morally correct me. I know it's important to move on, but I feel stuck and unable to do anything properly. I have big ambitions, but I'm uncertain if I'll be able to achieve them. My emotions swing drastically, and I find myself getting easily annoyed. That's why I decided to seek help, and that's why I'm here today. (Age 15, from India)

I've been feeling really down lately and I'm not sure what's going on. I've been having trouble concentrating and I feel tired all the time. I've also been isolating myself from my friends and family. I think I might be depressed.

I was in a relationship with a woman for 9 months, and we decided to move in together. She had a 17-year-old daughter who slept in a separate room. Initially, we had no issues with being intimate after her daughter fell asleep. However, the daughter discovered us four months after we moved in, and she had a strong panic-like reaction. Since then, the daughter has been sleeping in her own room, and we had to move our intimate moments outside the house or when the daughter was away. Our plan was for the daughter to eventually sleep in her own room, but my partner decided to move back to her ex's place to work on herself mentally. They got married a year later, and she explained that it was for health care reasons and to spare me from hardships related to her health issues. However, there were two mysterious contacts: one claiming to know me and accusing me of things I didn't do, and another who I suspect is my partner's alter ego, still in contact with me today. Her friend insists that she didn't want to marry her ex but had to due to health issues. Recently, her friend set up a meeting for us where we had sex, and we've had two other encounters since. My partner had a complicated operation and can't drive, but her friend keeps saying she can't wait to see me again. I've had some therapy in the past for other issues, but I've never encountered someone like her. Our connection feels intense and intimate, but she avoids talking about certain things that bother her. She mentioned that there's something guys always do that starts innocently but ends up the same. I'm confused if she has Antisocial Personality Disorder (APD) or is a sociopath. Does she truly love me or is it just about the sex? I'm really uncertain about all of this.

I'm a 23-year-old who feels like I'm going through a mid-life crisis. Despite living a healthy lifestyle, I have noticed a decrease in my sexual drive and a lack of inspiration or creativity. I also experience frequent episodes of anger, often over small things. I used to be artistic and passionate, but now I feel like I'm stuck in a cycle of anger and unfulfilled ideas. I wonder if my past drug use is still affecting me. I have moments of happiness, but overall, my days are filled with ups and downs. I have intense meltdowns, especially the day before my period. Sometimes I feel better when I was smoking and drinking coffee because now I'm sober and more aware of the pain in the world, which makes me angry. I just want to hide away from everything.
I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for 3.5 years and we recently moved in together. We are also considering getting engaged. I genuinely love him and see him as my best friend.

I've been experiencing some disturbing thoughts and feelings lately. On one hand, I feel pretty good overall, but on the other hand, I have this strong desire to harm others. It's concerning because I don't think I would feel any emotional distress if I actually went through with it. In fact, the thought excites me. The only reason I hesitate is because I don't want to end up in jail and I dislike being bored. I've never killed anyone, but I have killed animals and enjoyed it. It's hard to explain why I want to kill, but it gives me a sense of purpose and excitement that I don't feel otherwise. How can I stop these thoughts and find something else that gives me a similar feeling? I don't want to lose this sensation. (Age 19, from the US)

I've been in a relationship with a guy who has been very supportive in terms of my education and career. However, I find myself becoming extremely anxious and upset whenever I think about him talking to other girls. I've been behaving erratically and impulsively, and it's starting to affect my relationships with others. I want to address this issue because I'm genuinely concerned about my own well-being and the impact of my behavior on those around me.

Hello. I am a young man from India. I have been married for the past four years. Prior to my marriage, I was involved in a deep relationship with another girl. We wanted to get married, but due to societal caste issues, it was not possible. As a result, I made the decision to marry someone else, as her family was not open to the idea of our relationship.

When I was 17 years old, I struggled with alcoholism and smoking. However, one day I made the decision to stop and never touched them again. Unfortunately, I ended up becoming homeless and in order to protect my child from the state, I asked his father to take care of him. I also found myself becoming abusive towards a partner over trivial matters, leading to our breakup. I started to turn my life around, but I began experiencing fainting spells at work and ended up in the ER multiple times. They suggested that I might be dealing with panic attacks and anxiety. Over time, I couldn't stop thinking about my ex, who I had previously abused. After six months of working on myself, I reached out to my ex and we decided to give our relationship another try. Although it has been a rough journey, the abuse has stopped and things started to improve. We got married and I became pregnant quickly. However, my family believes that my husband will not show up for the court hearing and might leave. He works hard for me and the baby, but I'm scared to leave the house and have isolated myself from others. I constantly feel like I'm being watched and followed. After giving birth, I had a major breakdown when a doctor falsely told a social worker that I live in a shelter, which resulted in them not allowing me to leave with my baby. I pleaded with her to reveal who had accused me, and when she did, I had an overwhelming urge to hurt that person. My partner was shocked by this accusation, but reassured me that everything would be okay. He held my hand and the negative thoughts quieted down. Now, this woman has filed paperwork to have me monitored. Although I reject any harmful thoughts towards my baby, I can't seem to shake these negative feelings. I'm terrified of losing my child.

I have been dating my boyfriend for the past 7 months, and I am head over heels for him. He is about 14 years older than me and a college professor. This is part of our dilemma. He talks for a living. So when we are talking, he constantly interrupts me or asks me tons of questions without giving me the opportunity to answer any of them. It’s so frustrating. We both have strong personalities, so it has led to a couple of arguments. I started to do research into how we could communicate better, in an attempt to resolve the issue. 2 weeks ago, I confronted my boyfriend about the situation and told him that he chronically interrupts me or talks over me and how frustrating I found it. He got very defensive and told me that I was being passive aggressive and that I’m too sensitive. Since then our communication has dwindled. We used to talk on the phone every night and now we only talk on the phone a few times per week. I am freaking out a little here, because now there are awkward silences, or he throws in my face that he is letting me speak and that I should be grateful for the opportunity. I feel like this has put a huge wedge between us and it is deteriorating our relationship. We aren’t able to see a lot of each other as we both work long hours and he travels, so we need open communication in order to survive. How can I make things right while still getting my own needs met? (age 31, from US)

Counselor: I'm really sorry to hear about all the trauma you've experienced, especially the recent incident with your ex-partner. It sounds like the presence of your son during that traumatic event has made it particularly difficult for you to cope. It's understandable that you're feeling overwhelmed and unsure of how to overcome this. The fact that you're currently six months pregnant and experiencing intense flashbacks and disturbing dreams is also concerning. It seems like this recent trauma is having a significant impact on your mental well-being.

I'm seeking your opinion on my partner's behavior. She seems contradictory and critical, but also gets upset if any of her ideas or decisions are questioned. For example, she ridicules the books I read unless they are ones she recommends, and she calls them childish rubbish if they don't interest her. The same goes for TV shows or films. She's an aspirational vegetarian, yet she criticizes me for eating meat and asks how I can consume dead animals. However, the following week, she will eat chicken and say how tasty it is. Another issue is our sex life. She often rejects me and calls me disgusting for wanting sex, but then cries and asks why I don't make love to her anymore. It's become quite confusing and frustrating. I've tried being nice to her, thinking it would bring us closer, but it seems to make things worse. The nicer I am, the more demanding and contradictory she becomes. I think her upbringing and the negative relationships she had with her brothers have had a big impact on her behavior.

I am currently in my second semester of college and have lost all of my motivation to keep up with my course load. I have lost my motivation because I feel that no matter what I do, I am not making any progress towards my goal of having a fulfilling life.

Today my future husband shared some concerning information about his family history. His grandmother struggles with alcoholism, and his mother has developed some troubling beliefs. She claims to be a descendant of the Romanovs, the Russian royal family that was tragically killed in 1918. This belief seemed to escalate in 2002 when she started accusing her husband and expressing paranoia about being targeted by others, including doctors. She also believes that her husband doesn't work and that the government financially supports him. This has caused frequent fights between them.

I have been diagnosed with depression and have seen therapists before. I don’t have a bad life but I am bad at handling stress. I will have panic attacks over minuscule things like homework and am anxiety prone. I will cry for almost no reason and in a second, be fine. I have really excited feelings and very very low feelings but they are not far apart like in bipolar disorder. They are within hours or at most, a day. Nobody deals with me or can figure anything out. I want to function normally but I can’t seem to figure a cause to any of it. I am in a completely stable relationship with a boy that I communicate with, although granted, I am only 16. And honestly, I almost feel like I make some of it all up. Sometimes, I feel like I will do things or say stuff just to make myself believe I have something wrong with me. I struggled with self-harm for a while and I usually wasn’t distressed when I did it. I just did it to do it. I am studying psychology in school (although I am not going to be pursuing a career in it) and I think that maybe since I know a bit about mental issues, I am just creating one for myself. I am not seeing a therapist right now, mostly because I don’t have any events to talk about, no traumatic memories, they all treat me like a waste of space. But I could go see one if maybe somebody told me what to try and get out of it? (age 16, from US)

I've been dealing with a recurring issue with my dad regarding a TV show that he wants me to watch. About 5 years ago, I agreed to watch 10 episodes of his favorite sci-fi show, but I didn't enjoy it. Since then, he has been asking me repeatedly to give it another chance, even though I've expressed my disinterest. He tries to argue with me and make me feel guilty for not liking it. He even goes as far as questioning our relationship, saying things like "there's no way you're my daughter" because of my dislike for sci-fi. I feel like he's not respecting my boundaries and is trying to manipulate me. This has been a pattern throughout my life, as he has always been controlling and guilt-tripping. I recently stood my ground and said no to watching the show again, which is a big step for me as I struggle with assertiveness.

I have been to several psychiatrists who have diagnosed me with schizophrenia, but I have also received diagnoses for generalized anxiety disorder, schizoid personality disorder, major depression, OCD, and a phobia of driving. Recently, OCD was removed from my list of diagnoses. I am questioning whether all of these diagnoses are accurate, especially the diagnosis of schizophrenia. I've heard that individuals with schizoid personality disorder may experience brief psychotic episodes, and I have had psychotic symptoms in the past. Is it possible that my psychotic states are actually symptoms of the other disorders?
I've been feeling really overwhelmed lately. I have a lot going on with work, family, and personal responsibilities. It feels like everything is piling up and I don't know how to manage it all.

I've always been selective about who I let get close to me, but I've never had trouble making friends. I don't have a huge group of friends, but I have several individual friends. I met my group of "best friends" 10 years ago at university, and I've stayed in touch with three of them who I am closest to.

Lately, I've been struggling with forming close relationships and feeling connected to others. Despite being confident and able to talk to anyone, I find myself wanting to be alone. It's like there's an invisible barrier preventing me from letting people in, even when I genuinely like them. What could be going on with me?

Patient: I'm 15 years old and I've been feeling disconnected from others. I don't seem to have any sympathy or empathy towards them. I often have thoughts of doing terrible things to people. I also find myself lying, especially when I want something and don't have time to explain. I manipulate others too. I feel like I need help, but I don't think my mother is aware of what's going on. Additionally, I become mute at school or when I don't want to upset my mother. I'm seeking advice or any help to stop these behaviors. Please, I really need guidance.

I've been struggling with trying to communicate to my boyfriend the importance of providing positive feedback, encouragement, and praise to both his kids and mine. I understand the concept of overpraising or praising things that don't deserve it, but that's not what I'm concerned about.

When I was about sixteen, I started experiencing intense and disturbing thoughts and impulses. These thoughts involve violent acts towards others, such as hunting them down, attacking them, and even engaging in cannibalistic behaviors. These urges are distressing and I'm worried about what it means about me as a person.

I've been struggling to find a therapist I can trust and feel comfortable talking to. Due to my past experiences, it has been challenging to find one that suits my needs. I have been diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and have been receiving death threats due to the increasing polarization in our country. I work in law enforcement, so involving authorities is not an option. My family and the people in my area seem to support these threats, which makes it even harder to cope. I've had negative experiences with previous therapists, from one who ended up committing a crime to another who tried to impose his beliefs on me. I just want to find a therapist who respects my religion, sexuality, career, and relationship status. What are some important questions I should ask potential therapists to avoid wasting my time and money? What answers should I be looking for from them?

Hi, I've been experiencing intense mood swings and identity shifts for a while now. It's really confusing because these shifts happen so quickly. One moment I feel suicidal, the next I feel euphoric, and then I become filled with rage. During my euphoric, energetic moods, I become paranoid if triggered. The other night, I even threw my phone against the wall because I felt compelled to do so by these voices in my head. They contradict each other and it's hard to know who to trust. I also have thoughts of my parents trying to harm me. Sometimes I even have thoughts of harming others, but I feel intense empathy at other times. It's hard to make sense of it all. I've been feeling stable for a little over a week, but I'm afraid it won't last. Can you provide some guidance?

My son recently returned home after spending a year in Colorado, where he began drinking and smoking marijuana. Initially, he seemed fine, but after spending three days with friends, he started hearing voices and became paranoid. We took him to the hospital where he was admitted and prescribed medication. He attended outpatient therapy, but it didn't address his individual needs. A social worker intervened and had him admitted again due to concerns about self-harm. He resisted taking medication, resulting in a ten-day stay. Currently, he is back in outpatient care and prescribed 1mg of medication at night and 10mg of Abilify. However, I reduced the Abilify to 5mg due to increased symptoms. The doctor still wants him on 5mg twice a day, but it made him worse. I'm at a loss and have been trying to find another doctor, but it's proving difficult. Can someone develop schizoaffective disorder seemingly overnight at the age of 30? And what other medications may be effective? Thank you for your guidance as a concerned parent.

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for almost 2 years now, and we recently purchased a house together. He's usually an amazing guy, but when he gets angry or stressed, things take a turn for the worse. He starts yelling and cursing at me, even when it's not my fault. It's really scary for me, especially when it's over something small like the dog barking or a simple question I ask. He expects me to join in his anger and gets upset when I don't. I believe in staying calm and finding the positive in any situation, but it's becoming increasingly difficult.

Hi, I recently took some online tests for anxiety, depression, and bipolar disorder. The results showed that my anxiety levels are extremely high, which I already suspected since I have been struggling with it for a while. The tests also indicated high levels of depression and a possibility of bipolar disorder. I am feeling suicidal and my only confidant is my dad, who has a tendency to make jokes even in serious situations. I am afraid that if I open up to him, he might not take my concerns seriously. About four months ago, I had a breakdown where I couldn't speak and just cried in bed. My dad thought I was just being silly. I don't have any other family to turn to. Can you please suggest some coping strategies for me, as I am unable to access therapy at the moment? I have resorted to self-harming by cutting my thighs, as it is hidden from others. Thank you.

I am concerned about my father possibly having Asperger's syndrome based on his behavior. He has always been distant and cold towards me, even resorting to physical punishment when I was a child. Others have also noticed his indifference. He exhibits symptoms such as social avoidance, sensitivity to sensory stimuli, and repetitive behaviors. He shows little interest in me or my brother, and even seems uncomfortable around children. In social situations, he appears aloof and clumsy, often missing social cues.

Hello, I apologize if this appears jumbled, I feel there’s a lot I need to add! I would like to know whether these symptoms may be pointing towards Bipolar disorder. I was diagnosed with Social Anxiety about 6 years ago. Since then, I’ve gotten married, moved cities and went to university. I’ve also had periods of depression, and auditory hallucinations. During the past three years (noticed it more recently) I’ve been irritable, feeling high and low. Irritable, in the sense that I lash out at my husband for no reason. I just suddenly get angry — when he hasn’t done anything- and start shouting. After, I feel an immense sense of guilt and I will often break down in tears. Other times, I have these sorts of daydreams — but they feel more real than daydreams, if that makes sense. The best way I can describe it is I’ll get an idea in my head and I’ll get lost in it — it can range from anything, a recent example was the idea of being in a famous band. In reality, I couldn’t do such a thing due to being so timid. In this sense I also overestimate my abilities, in believing that I can get anything done just because. When it doesn’t happen the way I imagined, I’ll become depressed and feel generally hopeless, useless. If it is of any use, my grandmother had Bipolar. I apologize if this was muddled, but I’m not sure whether I should refer to a doctor or not, or if what I am experiencing is related to Bipolar at all. Thank you for your time! (age 21, from New Zealand)

When I was in high school, I used to be very outgoing and had a lot of friends. I was talkative and had no problem connecting with others. I felt happy and myself when I was with my friends. It was the best time of my life.

My spouse and I have been living apart since day 1, living in different states. He battles issues of addiction, but seems to be fine with kicking the drug piece. Alcohol is still heavily involved. He moved away in with his sister 1,000 miles away to escape the problems faced here and restart his life. He eventually married me after 3 years of dating. He hasnt started a new career, couldnt get into the military, so I want him home. He is worried that moving back will bring back bad habbits, when I feel it was just escapism and more a bandaid verus getting to the issues as drinking is still an issue. He feels most comfortable with his sister, my job is stationary my career being 10 years strong with the federal government, I dont see the need to move when he only works in a bar (of all places) but doesnt fully support himself. I feel his mind races and he has coping issues and learning how to move stuff in the past. He had issues with his parents, being mixed race. He is up and down, agreed to move back but still having issues with facing the area and the people. His alcohol consumption is terrible, through the roof at least 5 drinks per day and sometimes can finish a gallon in as little as 2 days. I don’t know what to do, how to start dealing with this, I know he has to make the choice, but I don’t know what I can say. I am accused of not understanding, I ask why he flew back to marry me.
