I’m dealing with his addiction, childish fear and not wanting to leave his old go to person and start our lives, I’m ready to throw in the towel but don’t want to leave.

Ever since I started questioning my personal identity, I've been struggling to concentrate and finish my school work. It's affecting both my performance in class and my ability to complete assignments outside of class.

I've been feeling really frustrated and hurt lately because it seems like my parents have a different set of expectations for me compared to my brother. He's being supported in pursuing his chosen career path, but I feel like my interests in fashion are being dismissed. My dad even goes so far as to belittle me and say that my brother is smarter and more capable than I am, even though I'm doing well academically. Fortunately, my mom hasn't been as harsh with me.

Since I was a young child, I have experienced strange episodes at night that interfere with my ability to sleep. During these episodes, I feel intense surges of anger throughout my body, yet I also feel physically numb and heavy. When I was younger, I coped with these episodes by kicking, screaming, and eventually falling asleep unintentionally. Now, I find myself harming myself through punching, scratching, and cursing at myself until I "pass out" again. These episodes don't happen every night, but I want to understand what they are and find a way to resolve them. I have already been diagnosed with depression, but I believe there may be other underlying issues that are more psychotic in nature. I haven't discussed these concerns with anyone, including my therapist, because I fear they won't believe me or that I'll appear foolish for sharing my thoughts and feelings.

I'm reaching out to you because there is escalating tension between my family and my boyfriend, to the point where the police have been involved. My dad and brother have always had issues with my boyfriend, believing he is disrespectful and irresponsible. However, my mom sees a different side of him and appreciates how he makes me happy.

I've been struggling with depression for as long as I can remember. It started off as a feeling of boredom, but in high school, I finally accepted that it was depression. I don't really know why I feel this way, it just seems to be how I am. I've had a few attempts at suicide, but I couldn't go through with it. Lately, I've been having thoughts of hurting others, even though I abhor violence and would never act on it. A few years ago, I had a mental breakdown where I became extremely paranoid and carried a knife for protection. It eventually stopped, but now with these thoughts, I'm scared I might hurt someone if it happens again. I've also noticed that I didn't feel any sadness when several people close to me died. Shouldn't I be at least a little bit sad? I'm not sure if I need help or if something is wrong with me.

During my middle school years, my best friend and I would engage in sexual activities while playing truth or dare. We kept it a secret, only involving one other person in the game. In 8th grade, I stopped participating because I wanted to force myself to be attracted to girls. However, even now in 12th grade, I still don't experience sexual arousal towards girls. It's more concerning to me that I find myself attracted to younger boys. I don't know if my middle school experiences are to blame, but I want to change. I've engaged in sexual activities with a freshman boy this year, even though I don't think he's gay. I have a seemingly normal life, with friends, sports, and past girlfriends, but this issue is troubling me. I've researched pedophilia, and while I don't fit the typical profile, I still have these feelings towards boys. I want this arousal to go away and to be attracted to girls. I would really appreciate any advice you can give. Thank you. (age 17, from US)

Patient: When I was in the seventh grade, I used to make jokes about depression without realizing how serious it could be. My mother left our family when I was young and struggled with drug addiction. My dad has been a single parent for most of my life. In eighth grade, I started to understand the seriousness of depression because I began experiencing it myself. I isolated myself in my room, withdrew from my family and sports, and eventually turned to self-harm as a way to feel something. This eventually led to disordered eating. Recently, my mom came back into my life and I thought she deserved another chance, so I moved in with her about four months ago. However, things have only gotten worse. I want to seek help from a doctor, but I'm unsure how to approach this with my mom.

When my boyfriend and I first started dating, everything was going great. We had a strong connection and he seemed accepting and non-judgmental. However, things changed when he asked about my past. He had been married before, while I had never been married. I opened up about going to clubs occasionally when I was younger, including my sexual history. Since then, he has been pulling away, accusing me of intentionally hiding this information. We've broken up and gotten back together three times, but the issue of trust still lingers. I've been honest each time he asks, but he still doubts me. I've tried everything to reassure him and rebuild trust, but he claims that I haven't done anything to make him believe in me. I'm at a loss and don't know what else to do. How can I prove to him that I was telling the truth and move forward as a couple?

I am concerned about a comment my boyfriend's sister made regarding their past. We were discussing extreme situations and she said something about him possibly harming someone who saw what he did to her when they were younger. He has also made other questionable comments in the past.

I've been dealing with this issue with my husband's uncle for about 5 years now. He has great financial means but spends very little money on entertainment. He often shows up unannounced, especially during supper hour, and doesn't seem to respect our request for him to call before coming over. This intrusion has worsened since his breakup with his girlfriend. We've tried repeatedly asking him to call, but he still shows up and argues with us if we say we're busy. It's causing a lot of strain in our marriage and I can't rely on having a peaceful night.

In the past, I engaged in harmful and violent behavior towards animals. I would harm birds, blow up fish, and abuse pets by beating them and choking them. I'm sharing this because I want to understand why I did these things and how I can change.

I've been feeling really down lately. My best friend and I have been having constant arguments and she recently told me that we can no longer be friends. This situation is really affecting me, and I've reached out to her multiple times but she hasn't responded. I told her how much I'm hurting, but she didn't seem to care.

Over the past three years, I have experienced a series of failures that have left me feeling hopeless and lost. My life feels like it's drifting aimlessly, and I'm struggling to find meaning or purpose. I want to know what practical steps I can take to re-engage with the world, rediscover my dreams and goals, and start working towards achieving them.

I have been in a long-distance relationship for the past 3 years, and it has been incredibly difficult. Unlike my brother and his wife, who were able to date, travel, and live together before marriage, my partner and I have had to navigate this relationship under parental supervision and without the financial means to go on trips together. It's frustrating and I feel like we're missing out on important experiences.

I have been in a relationship with my husband for 7 years, and for the most part, things have been great. We have always worked well together, and it often feels like I married my best friend. However, over the past year of having a long distance relationship, I've noticed that my feelings for him are starting to fade. I'm worried that I might be falling out of love. While I still enjoy our conversations over Skype, I don't really miss him when we're apart. On the other hand, he seems to miss me a lot and can't wait for us to be together again.
Recently, I formed a strong connection with a new friend, and our wives have noticed and teased us about it. Now that I am married with children, I'm starting to question everything.

My husband and I have been together for 7 years, married for 6. We separated for almost a year due to his untreated mental issues and infidelity. He's been diagnosed with bipolar disorder and is now on medication. We recently started living together again, and I was hopeful that things would improve in our relationship. However, he now claims that his medication and our children distract him from wanting sex. We've only been intimate about 8 times in the past 3 months, and it's been quick and lacking in emotional connection. I recently discovered that he's been searching for explicit content involving teenagers on his phone. This discovery has crushed me, as I've tried to be understanding and fulfill his desires. He insists that his lack of sex drive has nothing to do with me and that he's been battling these demons his whole life. But I can't help but feel undesired and worthless when I'm right here, willing to meet his fantasies, and yet he shows no interest in being with me. I'm at a loss and feeling broken-hearted. The infidelity nearly destroyed me. Can you please help me make sense of all this? I don't have much left to give. Please help.

I've been struggling with these symptoms for several years now and I've reached a point where I feel hopeless. I constantly experience a sense of anxiety and detachment from reality, which makes it difficult for me to function. I also have trouble sleeping and when I do manage to fall asleep, I wake up feeling anxious and have strange thoughts and visual disturbances. This has left me feeling depressed and numb, like I'm just going through the motions. Sometimes, the detachment from reality gets so intense that I worry I'm losing my sanity. I'm at a loss for what to do next and I'm not sure if this is still just anxiety or if it's something else entirely.

Patient: I've been experiencing some troubling symptoms and I'm not sure what's going on. It all started when I went on a trip to Europe with my brother and got really sick with the flu. While on the tour bus, I began having a psychosis where I thought I could hear the other passengers talking about me, saying mean things. Even after that incident, there are times when I go out and I feel like people are calling me names or laughing at me. I moved to the city recently, but I'm afraid to go out because I'm worried about having another episode. My boyfriend notices when it happens because I become quiet and disoriented. I only hear these voices when there are people talking, not when I'm alone. I'm not sure if I should seek help from a therapist.

During my childhood, I experienced three traumatic events that have had a lasting impact on me. I lived alone with my mother who suffered from severe depression and had volatile mood swings, which terrified me. I also endured a long period of violent sexual abuse that culminated in my rape when I was 9 years old. On top of that, my father openly rejected me and abandoned me. Now that I'm 23, I feel like my life is beautiful and I've dealt with most of my issues. However, one thing that continues to bother me is that I feel stuck with the emotional maturity of a small child. I cry every day, even over things that most people would consider insignificant. It's embarrassing, especially when it happens in public. I'm not depressed and generally happy, but my emotional responses are childlike and I struggle to control them. Is this something I will have to live with forever? Are there any specific types of therapy that you could recommend? My previous therapist told me that I'm just a highly sensitive person and that I should accept it, but I don't want to be so emotionally overwhelmed all the time. Is this normal? Did my childhood trauma hinder my emotional development? Can it be resolved?

Since I was young, I've had a strong aversion to speaking, to the point where I actively avoid situations where I have to speak. This started with other children, but as I've grown older, I've stopped talking to teachers and even my own family. They think I'm ignoring them, but the truth is, I have thoughts and responses in my head, I just can't bring myself to say them out loud.

As a child, I remember being involved in some sexual games with a friend when we were around 7-9 years old. These games included humping, kissing, and examining each other. I felt guilty and sad about it, especially when my friend would force me to continue playing even when I didn't want to. However, I also recognize that I was a bossy child and may have initiated some of these activities.

Over the past couple of years, my relationship with my step-dad has been quite difficult. Since my mom and step-dad got married, he has been treating my siblings and me poorly. I am the oldest, at 16, and I have a 12-year-old sister and a little brother who is just over a year old. My step-dad often gets in my face, yelling and screaming. This behavior has been witnessed by other family members and friends. It seems that no one in my family likes him, except for my mother, who has a history of being involved with abusive men. She even left my father to reconcile with the man who physically harmed her while she was pregnant with me. My step-dad has approached me multiple times, asking if I want to fight him, and he has gotten uncomfortably close. I'm starting to fear that he might actually hit me one day.

I've been feeling overwhelmed lately due to various sources of stress. Financial difficulties, job responsibilities, and family issues have been weighing heavily on me. As a middle-aged single white female, I have maintained close ties with my dysfunctional family from my hometown.

I am a 17-year-old living in Australia. Throughout my life, I have struggled to find a true passion for anything. While I do have fleeting interests, I quickly lose interest when I try to pursue them. Furthermore, I lack real-world experience as I have never had a job, can't drive, and haven't participated in any extracurricular activities or hobbies. My life has primarily revolved around studying and maintaining good grades in school.

Ever since I was young, I have engaged in self-talk. However, recently it has become more problematic. I find it difficult to communicate with the people around me, whether it's in class, with friends, or even with my family. When I'm alone or disinterested in a conversation, I start talking to myself. I have even created imaginary relationships and friendships in my mind. The concerning part is that I've had thoughts of violent acts towards these imaginary people and those around me. When I try to engage with others, I freeze up or use my own sense of humor that no one seems to understand. I haven't been able to make friends and my family is worried that I may have psychological issues. I want to be able to connect with people and be friendly, but it feels like they don't understand me, so I retreat back to the people in my head. I'm wondering if I might be schizophrenic or if I'm just crazy. I don't know how to deal with this, and I'm afraid it might worsen if it continues. I'm terrified of telling my mother, and when I tried explaining it to my friends, they labeled me as a lunatic. I don't know where else to turn to for help.

"I've been dating my girlfriend for eight months now and things have been going really well. We have so much in common and share similar values, goals, and outlooks on life. It's been hard for me to find someone like her."

Patient's statement (revised): Hi there, I've been caring for my mother who was diagnosed with Bipolar Disorder four years ago. She has been on Risperidone for the past four years and has generally been stable. However, in the past year, she has had two episodes that caused stress for our family. I have a couple of questions. First, does this mean that the medication is no longer effective? Second, I've noticed some unusual symptoms during her episodes, like speaking French and acting unlike herself. Are these characteristic of Bipolar Disorder?

When I was around 4 or 5 years old, my grandmother used to joke around with me and touch me between my legs. She convinced me that it was all in good fun, and I would laugh along. Now that I'm 23, thinking about it is making me feel like a wreck and causing me to see my grandmother differently. I still live with her and my mother. Can you offer any guidance?

I recently went through a breakup with my boyfriend in early November due to false rumors spread by my friends and family. They accused him of trying to isolate me from them and even labeled him as a woman beater. However, I want to clarify that these rumors are completely untrue. Despite my efforts to defend my boyfriend, the relationship couldn't survive the impact of these rumors. As a result, I moved out of his house and back in with my parents. I know I'm a good mother and I don't deserve this treatment. I'm reaching out for help because I need an outside perspective on this situation.

I'm a 15-year-old from the U.S. and I've been feeling frustrated with my parents' strict monitoring of my phone and computer usage. They have imposed restrictions on my computer, including blocking certain websites, shutting it off at bedtime, and not allowing it to turn back on until a specific time.

Hi there. I'm reaching out because I'm struggling with feelings of jealousy in my relationship. I've been dating this girl for 3 months, but we've known each other for almost a year. We used to text constantly and have a really strong connection. However, I find myself getting very jealous whenever she spends time with her male friend who she's been close with for 6 years. I trust her, but I can't help feeling uneasy about their friendship. The jealousy is starting to affect me even when she hangs out with her female friends. I don't want to lose her and I want to work on these feelings. Can you please help me?

Since the summer of 2013, I have been diagnosed with Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD). I initially started taking 50mg of Zoloft, but had to increase the dosage to 75mg and then 100mg. I've been doing alright on the 100mg, although I sometimes forget to take it. I believe it all started after watching the movie "The Conjuring", which made me afraid of possession and hurting someone I love. I still have these fears, although not as intense. Even previews of scary movies trigger my anxiety. Lately, I've been feeling like I'm being watched by a ghost, but I don't hear any voices. I think it may be related to not taking my Zoloft consistently. I saw my doctor last Monday and everything seemed fine, but I'm not sure what to do next. Should I make another appointment? I have had therapy before and it was helpful. Should I consider going back to therapy? I've been reading a lot online and it's making me more anxious. Can you provide a professional opinion? Thank you.

I'm a teenager who has a lot of love for my family, but I find myself getting easily annoyed and angry with people who I perceive as unintelligent, attention-seeking, and annoying. It doesn't matter if I have any personal problems with them or not, they just really irritate me.

Over the past year, I've been experiencing periods of low motivation and difficulty getting organized. These episodes only last for a few days at a time. Yesterday, I fell asleep early and felt exhausted when I woke up. My mom thought I was sick or upset, but I couldn't pinpoint a reason for my sadness. I often pretend to be happy, but deep down, I feel empty.

I have been the target of bullying multiple times throughout my life, including from friends and family. This has caused social anxiety and emotional stress for me. The bullies project their own insecurities onto me, including accusations of homosexuality and pedophilia. I know the truth about who I am, but these accusations carry a heavy social stigma. I've become self-absorbed and disconnected from others. Should I seek professional help to address this cognitive dissonance, or will it improve with time? I want to reconnect with others.

I am very concerned about my older brother. Over the past 6 months, he has been exhibiting some concerning behaviors. He has been forging my name and our parents' names on rental documents, and he doesn't seem to see anything wrong with it. Additionally, he has been displaying paranoid behavior, such as giving away his beloved cats of 5 years because he believes our father wants to send him to jail. He claims to be an alcoholic, although I have never seen him consume more than a few drinks at a time. He mentioned being prescribed medication by his therapist to help with his drinking, but it's confusing to me why he would need this medication if he isn't an alcoholic. He is making poor decisions and is on the verge of being evicted. Our entire family is feeling overwhelmed and unsure of what steps to take. We don't even know who his doctor is or what medications he is taking. I am deeply concerned that he may pose a danger to himself and others. What can I do?

I'm a 19-year-old woman from Quebec and I've been in a relationship with my current boyfriend for almost 3 years. Compared to my past experiences with men, he is truly amazing. He is kind, generous, caring, and so much more. However, there's one issue that concerns me - he seems to lack motivation and can be quite lazy at times.

I have been experiencing anxiety for most of my life, but recently it has become overwhelming. I constantly worry about my heart, fearing that I might have a heart attack and die. I also get intense headaches that make me fear I could have an aneurysm. I always feel on edge, unable to catch my breath. I have experienced a series of traumatic events throughout my childhood and adolescence. Starting from the age of 11, I was sexually assaulted until I finally ran away from home at 17. Unfortunately, the situation didn't improve as I was sent to a place where I faced verbal abuse and was constantly told that I was worthless and would never amount to anything. I was even accused of being a liar. After returning to my mom's house, the sexual abuse continued. I have struggled with suicidal thoughts and have made multiple attempts, but fortunately, I survived. I have also been admitted to an overnight mental hospital. I'm a 14-year-old from the US and I have a history of child abuse, although I don't have personal memories of it and only know about it from my mom. I've noticed that I have different personalities that I switch between. One is a lively, chatty, and warm personality that I've named Viola, and the other is a calm, sad, angry, and quiet personality. My stepdad and I have called it Broken Mirror disorder because it doesn't match MPD or split personality disorder. The switches between personalities happen quickly, sometimes randomly, and I can control them to some extent. Lately, I've also started having internal conversations with my "crazy half." I'm really confused and want to know what's wrong with me.

Over the past few months, starting in November, I have been experiencing intense feelings of depression and confusion. There was an event in November that occurred which caused me to feel worthless and terrible about myself. As a result, I have lost interest in activities and have a lack of motivation in life. This depressive state lasted for about one to two weeks, and then I started experiencing a jumble of thoughts and feeling mentally overwhelmed.

I have been married for a year and a half, and recently discovered that my husband has been cheating on me for the past four years with multiple women. This is my second marriage and I am completely shocked. He doesn't know that I'm aware of his infidelity. I feel like I have lost myself and I no longer want to focus on him, but rather on myself. I have been feeling disconnected during intimacy and find myself making excuses to avoid it.

I have been in a relationship with my girlfriend for 10 months and she recently informed me that she is pregnant. However, I have been experiencing doubts about the paternity of the child. I have discovered some concerning evidence, such as text messages to her ex-boyfriend and suspicious calls from an unknown number. I have confronted her about these incidents, but she insists that I trust her. This situation is causing me a lot of distress and I can't stop thinking about it. I want to know if my suspicions are valid and how I can find a way to move past this.

Patient: Hello, I've been struggling with persistent negative thoughts for about a year now. It's exhausting and I often give in to these thoughts, which only makes me feel worse. It feels like I'm trying to escape danger with multiple broken limbs. I've tried therapy, but it only provides temporary relief. I've also made efforts to cope and change my negative thoughts, but the constant battle continues. I'm starting to think that medication might be necessary, in addition to therapy and learning better coping strategies. It feels like a heavy burden that I can't shake off. I've reflected on why I'm so hard on myself and I've noticed that it's related to how I react to unfavorable outcomes. Over the years, I've become less effective at winning these battles and more pessimistic. It's become a part of my character. I know that this will be a long process, but I feel like I'm running out of energy to keep fighting. Thank you for listening.

I'm really worried about my sister. She's a single mother in her thirties and I'm concerned about her behavior and how it's affecting my niece. She seems very immature, selfish, and burdened by insecurities. She drinks a lot, often consuming at least 2 pints of beer each day. I feel like she puts my niece in risky situations that a good mother wouldn't.

My partner and I have been in a committed relationship for the past 5 years. We were doing well until I became pregnant with our daughter. During my pregnancy, I experienced discomfort during sex, making it difficult for me to reach climax. One night, I woke up to find my partner touching himself and masturbating. I confronted him and asked him not to do it again. Unfortunately, this happened multiple times, and one night I woke up to him engaging in sexual intercourse with me without my consent. I yelled at him and expressed my frustration, but he justified his actions by saying I was in an arousing position. This continued to happen until our daughter was born, regardless of my objections.

Lately, I've been experiencing intense anger that is negatively impacting my relationship. I find myself getting angry over insignificant things like a small mistake in conversation or when something doesn't work as expected. These triggers often lead me to engage in self-harm behaviors such as hitting myself, hitting objects, shouting, and even pulling out my hair. Additionally, my self-confidence is extremely low. I constantly put myself down, lack confidence in my academic abilities, and struggle with body image issues. I'm seeking help to understand what might be going on with me. Can you please assist me? (Age 15, from Wales)

"Hello. I've been struggling with my mental health for a long time. I was diagnosed with bipolar disorder back in 2008. From the age of 13, I've experienced more periods of depression than anything else. Occasionally, I have episodes of hypomania, but they are infrequent, and there are also times when I feel relatively stable."

I first started experiencing these thoughts when I was seventeen, but they stopped for a while and have recently resurfaced. However, now they are more intense and disturbing. I find myself having vivid daydreams and thoughts about ending my own life. In the past, it was about bleeding out with a razor, but now it's about using a gun or crashing my car into a tree. These thoughts are persistent and I also have a history of self-harm. I know I need to talk to someone about this, but I'm afraid of being hospitalized and I can't afford to miss more work. Are these thoughts normal? What should I do?

I've been struggling with chronic depression since childhood, which I believe stems from having an emotionally absent mother. Recently, my new therapist diagnosed me with both PTSD and BPD. The situation between my son and I has deteriorated since Christmas, triggering my abandonment fears. He has chosen to remain silent and refuses to acknowledge or learn about BPD, which only intensifies my feelings of abandonment. I find myself constantly cycling between overwhelming grief, anger, and numbness, which is taking a toll on my emotional well-being. I desperately want to communicate with my son, help him understand BPD, and find a way to resolve our differences, but I cannot force him to engage in conversation. This sense of perpetual abandonment feels unbearable, and I'm unsure of how to survive this. Is there any way to find a resolution without resorting to drastic measures?

Since my husband and I moved to Aberdeen, we had to give away his cat but brought my dog along. Unfortunately, my husband now despises the dog and blames him for the loss of his cat. I'm torn because I can't bear to part with my beloved dog, but I fear it's putting strain on our marriage. Additionally, I've noticed that I'm starting to have less love for my husband due to the way he treats my dog. It's important to note that we also recently had a baby. I'm at a loss for what to do because I don't want to break up our family, but the thought of losing my dog is causing me immense pain.
Patient's Statement:

I have been receiving talk therapy from the same therapist for the past 15 years. Initially, I was using my insurance, but after six months, it ran out and I have been paying by check. My therapist has requested that I come in for sessions that last between 3-8 hours per day, sometimes for up to 3 days in a row. Additionally, she has started traveling to my home for sessions and I cover the expenses of her hotel stay and other related costs.

Patient: I've been feeling overwhelmed and unsure of how to handle my older brother's schizophrenia. It's just me now, as our parents have passed away. Every so often, he decides to stop taking his antipsychotic medication, despite medical advice. This leads to a deterioration in his behavior and eventually involves the police, resulting in him being sectioned and hospitalized. This cycle repeats every couple of years. I worry about his well-being when he's off his medication, but he becomes paranoid, abusive, and cuts me off.

Patient's statement (rewritten): I have been in a relationship with my partner for 6 years. Unfortunately, my partner struggles with emotional abuse and alcoholism. They are currently on probation for their fourth DUI and do not have a car or driver's license. It took them over two years to find a part-time job, and even though they now make around $1,000 per month, they refuse to contribute to rent or bills. Instead, their money is spent on beer, fast food, and paying off court costs. This unhealthy dynamic is taking a toll on our son, who witnesses the constant yelling, cursing, drinking, and threats of violence in our home. Despite being only 4 years old, my son has expressed his dislike for his daddy and wishes for a different father figure who is not lazy, grumpy, and mean.

My friend has been expressing some unusual beliefs lately. She has become obsessed with the idea of "4 dimensions" and believes that her "soul wavelength" is equal to that of a god who resides in the 4D. I find these beliefs to be ridiculous and have tried to calmly explain why they can't be true. However, she becomes extremely angry and starts yelling at me, even bringing up unrelated things like my past sports activities that I quit.

Throughout my adult life, I have found myself involved with men who end up being emotionally unavailable or already married. It has been a pattern that has caused me a lot of pain and confusion. I've been told that low self-esteem might be a factor, but I generally feel good about myself. I have also dated men who initially claimed to be single but later went back to their exes or were married and never followed through on leaving their wives. The one man I dated who was truly single turned out to be controlling and even stalked me. Now that I'm in my 50s and still single, I'm desperate to understand why I keep making these mistakes. Am I too trusting? I don't consider myself needy or dependent; in fact, I value my independence. I just wish I knew why I continue to choose the wrong partners, as the guilt and loneliness are really taking a toll on me.

I've always struggled with feeling restless and having a lot of energy. It seems like everyone around me is constantly telling me to sit still and stop fidgeting. Sometimes I even joke that if I could bottle my "nervous energy," I'd be rich!

Patient: I am a 15-year-old guy who considered himself heterosexual. About 8 months ago, I made a mistake by engaging in a sexual act with an older man on a video chat website. I feel deeply regretful and have not engaged in any similar behavior since then. However, I am struggling to move past what happened and it's affecting my mental well-being. I'm also concerned about the impact this has on my integrity as a person and whether or not I should tell my parents. Can you help me get over this?

I have been in a relationship that has been characterized by control, deception, and emotional hurt. Whenever something goes wrong, my partner apologizes and blames me, making me feel responsible for everything. He is also excessively jealous and I find myself isolating from my family because of him. Despite knowing that this relationship is harmful, I struggle to end it. He manipulates me and although I have been educating myself about this kind of relationship, he manages to reel me back in with sweet gestures, only for things to go bad again. I fear letting him go because everything seems so romantic. I need guidance on how to break free from this cycle for good.

Lately, I've been experiencing some distressing thoughts and urges that I feel the need to share. I've been having thoughts about causing harm to other people, and these thoughts have become more detailed recently. It seems to happen when I'm feeling frustrated or depressed. In the past, I used to have thoughts of self-harm, but now it's shifted towards wanting to hurt others. It's not directed at anyone specific, just random people. I just have this overwhelming desire to cause violence and destruction.

I have been in a relationship with my husband for 9 years and we have 3 young children together. However, I have recently come to realize that our relationship has been marked by verbal and physical abuse. He has consistently used hurtful language towards me and has engaged in physical violence. The abuse began shortly after the birth of our first child when he was intoxicated and pulled me outside by my hair, locking me out. Since then, the abuse has escalated to him hitting, pushing, slapping, breaking my belongings, and even threatening suicide multiple times. Most recently, he choked me, leading me to call the police. He was arrested and convicted of spousal battery.

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for almost five years. We made the decision to move to Colorado from Texas three years ago. At the time, we were young and felt like it was a good opportunity for us.

I have been experiencing a strong sense of discomfort and awkwardness whenever I am around people my own age. This has been a consistent issue for me, as I have never had the opportunity to socialize with peers due to being homeschooled my whole life. I live with my grandparents and spend most of my time playing video games and doing schoolwork. I believe that this lack of socialization has contributed to my feelings of depression. However, I am afraid of how my grandparents and parents will react if I express a desire to make friends. I worry that they will look down on me.

I have been diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder and it has been affecting my daily life. I initially sought therapy a year and a half ago, but only attended the first three sessions because I downplayed my symptoms. Over the past year, my anxiety has gotten worse and it manifests physically with hives and shaking. I've lost interest in socializing and going to school. I reached out to my family doctor who confirmed that I should see a psychiatrist and consider medication. However, my stepmom has ignored my pleas for help and hasn't followed through on finding a psychiatrist. I feel trapped and alone, with a constant sadness inside me. I don't know what to do anymore and I'm scared to ask for help again, fearing another letdown. My academic performance is suffering and I no longer feel motivated. I feel like they don't care about my mental health. I would appreciate any advice or guidance you can offer. Thank you. (Age 16, from the US)

I have had an incredibly fulfilling and adventurous life. I have experienced joy and contentment, appreciating the beauty of nature and the simple pleasures like the wind blowing through my window at night. Throughout my life, I have pursued my passions wholeheartedly, maintaining a daily practice of gratitude. I have been fortunate to have had numerous high points, including three loving relationships, the joy of being a parent to a son, a supportive family, and an abundance of friends. I have also been blessed with a variety of successful careers, ticking off everything on my "bucket list." From serving as a military officer and pilot to pursuing my passion for music and business, and even graduating from law school at the age of 49, I have embraced every opportunity that has come my way. I have had the privilege of living in different countries and exploring various states in the US. Along the way, I even achieved unexpected accomplishments, such as holding multiple world records in skydiving. I have been fortunate to visit iconic cities like Paris, London, Bangkok, and even witness the grandeur of Red Square. I am immensely grateful to have accomplished and experienced everything I could have ever dreamed of.

As a child, I struggled with understanding time and dates in relation to personal events. I would often forget my own age and had difficulty remembering when things happened. This has been my main concern, although I have experienced other symptoms as well. Interestingly, my niece, who has intellectual and developmental disabilities, also displays a similar difficulty, but to a greater extent. Is there a specific diagnosis or syndrome that could explain this phenomenon?

I have been dating my boyfriend for almost a year now and I’m head over heels for him. He on the other hand recently told me that he knows in his head and his heart that he feels love for me, but he isn’t able to tell me that he loves me… He was in a relationship for 7 years where in the end his girlfriend cheated and broke it off and I guess he’s scared of getting hurt again. I thought that by giving him time he would eventually see that I was no threat. I even wrote him a letter where I spilled my feelings and still nothing from him. In my head I already saw myself married with children to him and it’s eating me from the inside knowing that he’s just not that into our relationship. I’ve met his whole family and I’m the second girl he’s introduced to his parents but I don’t know if it means that much. I’m lost and I’m unhappy but I love him and I just don’t see myself leaving him because he’s the best person I know! I feel like I’m drowning in my love for him with no one to save me…

My brother, who is 15 years old and a freshman in high school, has recently undergone a significant change in behavior. As a child, he was always polite and kind, although he occasionally threw tantrums, which we considered normal for a boy his age. However, lately, he has become unbearable to be around. He is rude not only to me, but also to our parents, sister, his girlfriend, and even his friends. When we ask him if anything is wrong, he just responds with "I'm tired." He has been displaying moodiness, rudeness, disengagement, lack of empathy, and a complete lack of motivation. His grades have also started to decline, and he seems indifferent about it. Additionally, he is a member of our school's JV hockey team, which sometimes has early morning practices. He constantly complains about being exhausted. I'm genuinely concerned that there might be an underlying issue such as depression, bipolar disorder, or something else. However, whenever I suggest to my parents that he should talk to someone, my dad dismisses it, attributing his behavior to typical teenage moodiness. I simply want to know how I can help and whether my dad's perspective is accurate or if we should seek professional help. All I want is for my brother to return to his happy and kind self.

I've been experiencing a lot of discomfort and negative emotions when my mom or dad show affection towards me, like hugging and kissing. It makes me feel dirty and powerless, and I think it might be because I associate those actions with something sexual. Just a few hours ago, my mom forced me to hug her and it made me cry. When I was younger, I had extreme anxiety and engaged in self-cutting. I also developed a habit of picking at my scabs compulsively. Sleeping alone has always been a struggle for me. I used to sleep with my mom by my side, and even when I started sleeping alone, I would turn on the lights and often wake up feeling like I was choking. My nightmares were often about being persecuted and wanting to hide. I had a constant urge to hide from others. I feel extremely uncomfortable when my mom stares at me, even though I don't think she did anything wrong. I also have a fear of water on my face, which has made it difficult for me to learn how to swim. I didn't eat much as a child and still have trouble swallowing, frequently almost choking on food and drinks. Looking back, I remember engaging in sexual behavior with my dolls before I even understood what sex was. I also had sexual thoughts about other toys. I have a slight fetish for older men, even though they scare me. I started masturbating around the age of 12 and now do it very frequently, more than most girls. I have vivid memories of being sexually curious in my childhood, but I don't know why or when it started. I don't have any memories of abuse, but I'm wondering if it's possible that I suppressed them. Do you think I might have been sexually abused?

Two years ago, when I was in 9th grade, I suddenly developed social anxiety. It came out of nowhere and I had never experienced anything like it before. During the summer, I had all the symptoms of social phobia and it made me feel depressed and angry. When school started, I found some ways to cope with it and reduce my social phobia. However, I also started experiencing more OCD symptoms, fearing that if I didn't perform my rituals, I would get anxiety. Eventually, my mother helped me get treatment for my OCD and for the past 4 months, I've had very few OCD symptoms. But now, I'm realizing that my life hasn't been the same since my social anxiety started. I don't speak as confidently or think as independently as I used to. I find myself asking obvious questions and mimicking what others say. I miss my old way of speaking and thinking, but I don't know how to bring it back. I don't get scared around people like I used to, but I know my social phobia is still there, holding me back. It's been so long since I've felt like myself, about 2 years, and I'm starting to question who I really am. I worry that I've lost all my opinions and that I'm being fake. I'm concerned that this may be something bigger than just anxiety. I have trouble sleeping and sometimes I feel a heaviness in the center of my head, near the hippocampus, which makes me feel sad. My grades used to be good, but they dropped during my intense OCD phase and now I feel like an idiot and worry about my future. I think about how I've lost my personality and identity every day, and life feels unfamiliar. I don't feel the desire to hang out with friends or make new ones because I hate the way I talk and how inauthentic I've become. I used to enjoy spending time with friends and my parents, but now nothing feels the same and I don't even know who I am anymore. I used to have interests and think about the future, but now I'm constantly dwelling on the past and how much better it was. I feel like I'm mimicking others and that my thoughts are contaminated by theirs. I don't understand how I've become so lazy in school and I worry that my development is being hindered as a result. Could all of this be caused by anxiety, or is there something else going on?

I have struggled with insomnia for as long as I can remember, but it has become much worse in the last decade. Despite trying various techniques like imagining calm places, listening to mindfulness CDs, and taking warm baths, I still struggle to fall asleep without sleep medication. What troubles me is that, during my attempts to sleep, I often find myself imagining horrifying events, particularly my own death or being abandoned by my loved ones. I am aware that these thoughts are preventing me from falling asleep, but I don't understand why they keep creeping back. Could it be that I don't actually want to sleep? Does sleep frighten me? My therapist has suggested that there may have been a past trauma that I am unknowingly protecting myself from by staying awake. I don't have any recollection of abuse, but I'm open to exploring this possibility. Do you have any thoughts or suggestions?

I've been struggling with my mental health lately and I'm really concerned about whether or not I may be experiencing symptoms of bipolar disorder. I go through periods of intense depression that make me contemplate suicide, but then I come out of it. I also have panic attacks where I feel extremely nervous and angry, but I'm not sure if that qualifies as a manic episode. During these episodes, I engage in dangerous behaviors like driving recklessly, self-harming, and making threats towards my boyfriend, who is my main source of support. I also have difficulty remembering these events, which typically last for about 3-4 hours and happen around 4 times a month. I am currently taking Prozac for my depression, but it seems like things have worsened since starting the medication. My parents are not supportive of medication or the idea of me being bipolar, so it's been challenging for me to seek help from a doctor. Is there anything I can do to improve this situation?

I recently got engaged to my fiancé and have been struggling with a situation that is causing a strain on our relationship. My fiancé masturbates 1-3 times per night in bed next to me, which wakes me up and makes it difficult for me to sleep. When I confronted him about it, he became defensive and accused me of being "crazy" and suggested that I may have been sexually abused in the past. He claims to be a good Christian man and denies engaging in such behavior. However, I am concerned about our lack of intimacy and how this issue may affect our future together. I am unsure if we need counseling before getting married. Can you please help me?

I have been experiencing a significant psychological issue lately that is affecting my performance in public speaking and presentations. Despite having good content and knowledge of the subject, I find myself getting stuck and sometimes unable to speak at all. This problem first started when I was in 12th grade, where I would struggle to say certain words after a specific timeframe. For example, when I was buying a ticket and needed to say "Begusarai," I could only manage to say "bbbbbb" instead. This issue has become more severe, especially when I present in class. I start off well but then this feeling of getting stuck creeps into my mind, causing me to struggle with almost every word and sometimes even abandon my presentation halfway through. I have been trying hard to overcome this feeling, but it keeps resurfacing during presentations, and it's causing me a lot of anxiety. I would appreciate any help you can provide.

I've been feeling really lonely lately. I want to meet new people and have a more active social life, but as an introvert, it's challenging for me. I do have a few friends, but we don't meet up very often and I feel like I need more connections to be happier.

I've recently become friends with a classmate who is often considered strange. We get along well, but he has developed romantic feelings for me and has started following me everywhere. Lately, he has been discussing violent and twisted topics, and his behavior has become increasingly erratic. I know he has a family history of mental illness and has experienced childhood trauma. I'm concerned about his influence on my life and relationships with others, as he makes people uncomfortable and gets me into trouble. While I enjoy his company, I worry about what he might do. Should I continue associating with him, considering his mental health struggles, or should I distance myself for my own safety?

My ex and I were in a relationship for three years before officially splitting in October. I feel a lot of guilt and don't want to speak negatively about her because I know I did some hurtful things. Throughout our relationship, I financially supported her as she didn't have a job. As time went on, I started to resent her for this. I began experiencing severe depression leading up to a fight we had. One night, after she spent all our money on alcohol, I reached a breaking point and took back a phone I had given her, which resulted in a physical altercation. I acted out by flicking, squeezing, punching her legs, pushing her, and saying terrible things.

My Dad passed away a little over a year ago after a 13-year battle with cancer. Everyone in my family mourns him, but I never grieved and all I feel is relief. It doesn’t hurt me the way it does my siblings…it really doesn’t hurt me at all.

I've been in a committed relationship with my husband for the past 8 years, and we recently got married 3 months ago. However, I've recently discovered that he has been sending emotional emails to another woman, expressing love and a desire to be with her.

My 16-year-old daughter is doing well academically, with straight A’s and happy teachers. She has a great group of friends and enjoys spending time with them, going to movies and birthday parties. However, she occasionally expresses feeling awkward and anxious around crowds and lacks confidence, despite not appearing that way. She has always been shy but it hasn't affected her participation. She dislikes physical activity and can feel annoyed with her younger brothers. Her father, although not overly forceful, comes off as pushy and she feels anxious around him. My husband and I are in couples counseling to improve our marriage. Should we be concerned as parents? What can we do to help her?

Lately, I've been experiencing troubling thoughts and feelings related to attraction towards underage girls who appear to be around 12 years old but not prepubescent children. This is a new issue for me and I'm concerned about it.

My friend from Columbia recently went through a difficult situation with a guy she was dating. They were together for about 3 months, but unfortunately, she was overseas during that time and never got the chance to meet him in person. However, he took her virginity during this period. Eventually, they broke up, but they continued to have conversations. Then, out of nowhere, the new girlfriend of the guy called my friend to warn her to stay away from him. Later, my friend discovered that he had been with the new girlfriend at the same time he was with her.

I've been struggling with my emotions lately, and it's really impacting my daily life. On one hand, I want to seek help, but on the other hand, I feel like I might be overreacting or making it all up. I'm afraid that if I reach out, I'll be rejected or told that nothing is wrong. This has led to a lot of shame and guilt, as if I'm to blame for my emotional instability. Additionally, I'm terrified of my parents, family, and friends finding out if I seek help because I'm still covered under my mom's insurance. I can't afford to pay for treatment on my own. I feel stuck and don't know what to do.

I'm really concerned about some recent experiences I've been having. I dropped out of high school, feel isolated, and have lost interest in leaving the house. I have started believing that my mom can read my mind and that there are cameras in the bathroom mirror. I also have a strong urge to smoke and abuse over-the-counter drugs, which I've done a few times. I sometimes struggle to communicate and experience flashes of light in my vision. I've been getting easily scared by noises and have difficulty sleeping. I've also been seeing people or shadows out of the corner of my eye. I've noticed that I get extremely angry over small things and argue with myself in my head a lot. It's really affecting my concentration, and I'm finding it hard to cope. Should I be worried about all of this? Should I talk to my mom about it?

Hi, I experienced what I think was an anxiety attack last night. I started feeling disconnected from reality and questioned whether everything was just in my imagination. It made me really scared and I thought I was going crazy. I also had this fear of losing control and hurting myself or others, which is something I absolutely do not want to do. I managed to fall asleep and woke up with some residual anxiety, but not as intense as last night. A few months ago, I had a similar episode after smoking marijuana and it was really debilitating. I was terrified of dying and having the same fear of harming myself or others. I didn't have any episodes for a few months, but then it happened again last night. What should I do now?

I wanted to reach out because I believe I may be experiencing symptoms of depression or something similar. I constantly feel down, have thoughts of self-harm, and find myself crying without reason. I lack energy and no longer find joy in activities I used to enjoy. I've attempted to express my feelings to my parents, but they dismiss it. Opening up to them now feels daunting, as I fear they will either yell at me or belittle me. I believe this all started around the age of 8 or 9, when my parents divorced and my mom remarried. My stepdad's alcoholism led to constant fighting and neglect, leaving me feeling alone and neglected. I recall a particularly traumatic incident where he even physically abused me for crying when I was just 10 years old. I've tried to maintain a happy façade at school, but inside I'm in pain and too embarrassed and scared to reveal the truth to my friends or bring them home. Recently, I thought I had found a true friend who would understand, but she ended up abandoning me. I'm now afraid to make new friends and find myself crying daily. On top of all this emotional turmoil, I've also had to endure three surgeries. Whenever I'm in pain, I just push through it because I've grown accustomed to it. I often find myself questioning my worth and why I exist. I know others may have it worse, and my friends would likely laugh at me if I shared my struggles. I feel completely unsupported and no one believes me. I desperately need help. (Age: 16, from Estonia)

Hi, my name is Alejandro. I'm an 18-year-old guy from a small town in Mexico. I've been struggling with accepting my sexuality for a long time, and it's been causing me a lot of pain. Living in a conservative community makes it even harder, as there's a lot of judgment and negative beliefs about being gay. I feel like I'm constantly battling with myself, and it's making me hate who I am. I don't have anyone to talk to about this, except for a local psychologist who may not have experience working with LGBTQ+ individuals. I feel like a failure and disappointment because I've never been in a relationship or kissed anyone. The only thing that brings me some joy is my academic success and my future plans in medical school. But even with that, I still see myself as a failure. I constantly feel grumpy and unhappy, and I'm beginning to wonder if this is just who I am or if it's because of the struggles I'm facing. I even find myself being sarcastic and hurting my parents, which I later regret. I'm sorry for this gloomy letter, but I can't remember the last time I truly felt happy. I fear that I'll never find happiness.

I'm concerned about my daughter's 3rd grade teacher. She behaves inconsistently and unusually, which makes it difficult to interact with her. Within weeks of meeting her, she asked me to be her friend (though clarifying that we couldn't "hang out" until after my daughter graduates her class), shared overly personal information, and stated that she needs me in her life. She has been married for 30 years and has three grown children. One moment she acts like we're close friends, the next she's strictly professional and aloof. She talks excessively about herself, is always enthusiastic and energetic, expresses self-doubt, wears revealing clothing, and is overly concerned about her appearance. She also flirts with me on and off. Can someone have histrionic personality disorder (HPD) and still maintain a stable marriage and job?

Earlier this year, in mid-February, I made the decision to quit my job and start my own business. I became completely consumed by it and ended up neglecting my college studies, thinking that leaving both school and work would allow me to solely focus on my business. I put all my energy into it for about a month, but then everything fell apart. I'm usually a quiet person, but I forced myself to socialize and promote my business. After about three weeks, I started feeling like nobody was taking me seriously. Then things took a strange turn. It felt like everyone I encountered was intentionally messing with me. I spent days walking around town, trying to make sense of it all. I stopped eating and although I never felt completely out of control, it was clear that I was being manipulated and not just paranoid. At one point, I reached my breaking point, withdrew all my money, and went to the train station with the intention of leaving. When I sat down on the benches, everyone else (around 8-10 people) suddenly got up and moved away, repeatedly saying the word "branding" - earlier that day, I had mentioned to a friend that I was working on branding my business.

I've been having ongoing issues with my mom for the past four years, and things seem to be getting worse no matter what I do. She constantly berates me and makes me feel worthless, yelling at me over every small mistake I make. She tells me I have no future and won't amount to anything on a daily basis. This constant belittlement has led me to feel so low that I've had thoughts of wanting to die and I engage in self-harm as a way to cope. Last year, I even tried to run away from home, but it only made things worse. My mom no longer speaks to me like a person, she only yells. She's told me she hates me and loves my siblings more. I want to get help to feel better and stop her hurtful words, but I don't want her to know that she's the reason I'm seeking help. I'm scared to reach out to school counselors or my friends because I worry they won't believe me and will just dismiss me as a moody teenager. I'm afraid of being judged and treated differently if I ask for help from someone I know. Can you please advise me on what to do?

I'm currently in my third and final year at university. In my first and second years, I was performing at a high level academically. However, this year has been a struggle. I find it incredibly difficult to concentrate and lack motivation. I've been experiencing constant anxiety for several months now, which has led me to start skipping lectures because they feel overwhelming and scary. I've also been having more frequent panic attacks, which is making it hard for me to focus on studying for my upcoming final exams. This is especially frustrating because I used to only get panic attacks occasionally. It's important to note that I have a history of mental health struggles. When I was 14, I attempted suicide and received Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) as treatment. At 17, I experienced sexual assault, which caused a resurgence of depression that I didn't seek help for and it negatively affected my A-level results. I thought I had overcome these challenges, but now it feels like I'm sabotaging my own success when it matters most. I'm not sure what I hope to achieve by sharing all this, but it feels like it might be too late to do anything about my upcoming exams. I might be subconsciously looking for a way out of them.

I'm feeling really overwhelmed and lost right now. I've been struggling with smoking weed and cigarettes since 2009, and I've been actively trying to quit for a year. But no matter what I do, I can't go a day without smoking. It's all I think about and it's taking over my life. I never used to be like this, but now I'm constantly in panic mode at the thought of never smoking again.

I'm a 23-year-old woman from India and I've been in a relationship for the past 2 years. While my family supports my relationship, I'm finding it difficult to cope with my fiance's possessiveness and outdated thinking. I strongly believe in gender equality and that women should have the same rights as men, but he disagrees. I try to keep myself happy, but sometimes it becomes overwhelming and I end up bursting out. I've tried to communicate my feelings to him, but he remains stubborn. I used to be emotionally strong, but now I feel weak and confused. I find solace in spirituality and reading positive content. Although we don't fight often and he seems happy, I'm not truly happy. I'm worried about my future with him and don't want to hurt my parents or him. I'm feeling lost and confused. What should I do? Thank you for your help.

About 5 years ago, I was diagnosed with major depression with psychotic features. Initially, I was under the care of an early intervention team, but I ended up being hospitalized for 3 months. After 3 years with that team, things started to improve, and I was transferred to a more general team. However, I haven't had a good rapport with them, as I never get to see the same doctor twice, making it difficult to talk to them. Despite no longer feeling depressed and no longer taking anti-depressants, I still take an antipsychotic (quetiapine slow release 500mg) daily. I experience negative voices and visual hallucinations (like my dog turning blue) that others can't see. I can rationalize them and know they aren't real, but I wonder if my diagnosis will change. Doctors brush off my questions about the longevity of my psychosis. It's been 18 months since my last depressive episode, but I still experience ongoing and new/different hallucinations. If it's not psychotic depression, what else could my diagnosis be? I'm able to function in my daily life, so does that rule out schizophrenia? Can you offer any suggestions? I struggle to communicate with medical professionals.

I recently discovered something concerning about my spouse's online behavior. After our wedding, I found out that he had been looking at inappropriate pictures of underage girls on Facebook, including a 16-year-old girl who was present at our wedding. I also found evidence of him engaging with a 17-year-old in the past, where he expressed finding relationships with underage girls exciting.

I've been struggling with a question that I can't find the answer to online. When I was just 4 years old, I was abandoned and then adopted by parents who were incredibly abusive. As a result, I've developed complex PTSD and other issues. Although my adoptive father passed away many years ago, I've been estranged from my adoptive mother for over a decade on the advice of mental health professionals.

For nearly two years now, I've been experiencing a lot of overwhelming feelings that I can't always understand or explain. I've noticed that I've stopped caring about many things and people, except for a few friends and activities that help me pass the time. I've been having panic attacks and anxiety attacks, but my parents don't believe it's a serious issue and think I'm just overreacting. This makes it even harder for me to reach out for help or talk about my struggles. I also wanted to mention that there may be a history of mental health issues on my dad's side of the family. In social situations with unfamiliar people, I struggle to speak up and often feel even more anxious when my quietness is pointed out. Can you help me understand what might be going on?

During my first year of university in Croatia, I felt incredibly shy and insecure as I adjusted to living and studying in a big city. It was a challenging time for me, but I was starting to make friends. One person that stood out was a girl I met who became one of my closest friends. She was likable, funny, and charming, and we had a lot in common. I found myself doing things for her without even thinking about it. At some point, I even developed romantic feelings for her, but unfortunately, she did not feel the same way and is in a committed relationship.

For over two years, I engaged in a harmful habit that not only hurt myself but also others. At the time, I was unaware that what I was doing was wrong. Now that I am a little older, I deeply regret my past actions. I fear that when people find out about what I did, they will lose trust in me and see me as a hypocrite. While my family trusts me, the guilt from my past consumes me. I feel lost and don't know what to do. Additionally, I have been struggling with depression. I desperately want to move on and better myself, but the weight of my past makes me feel like any accomplishments I achieve will be tainted. I feel utterly horrible. Can you please advise me on what to do?

I am concerned about my 56-year-old mother-in-law who has a history of anxiety and constantly seeks attention from the family. This behavior has been ongoing since her childhood, and she engages in disruptive actions to gain attention. She exaggerates her health issues, such as temporary blindness or claiming to have stomach cancer, and picks fights with or feels insulted by anyone who receives more attention than her. Ignoring or giving her positive attention doesn't seem to make a difference. Her sons have moved away in the past three years, and her behavior has escalated. Recently, she even claimed to be pregnant despite having a hysterectomy 15 years ago. Her dedication to this claim and her reaction to the lack of attention are concerning.

When I was younger, my sister, who is 4 1/2 years older than me, sexually abused me for about 3 years. Although I have tried to move past it, the memories still come up from time to time. Recently, my sister, who has been clinically diagnosed as narcissistic and tends to lie, has been visiting our house with her 3 kids and boyfriend for extended periods of time. I find it difficult to be around her because of the abuse and her selfish behavior as a parent. Now, they have been invited to spend Christmas at our house and I feel overwhelmed. How can I cope with all of this?

I have been struggling with disordered eating patterns, specifically bingeing and purging. However, I'm unsure if this means I have bulimia. My purging doesn't always follow a binge, and sometimes I actually enjoy the feeling of fullness. Other times, I purge to seek relief. I don't think my focus is solely on my weight. Additionally, I am genuinely overweight, which makes me hesitant to discuss this with my psychiatrist for fear of being dismissed.

During my adolescence, I struggled with isolation and a lack of typical social behaviors. I was focused on studying and had very few friends. This continued into college when I didn't get into the course I wanted. Despite graduating with honors, I never had a normal social life. It wasn't until I was 27 that I began to improve my personal, love, and sex life. However, hearing about my new girlfriend's past relationships has brought back feelings of regret and emptiness from my own past. I've been struggling to accept that I wasted so many years of my life, and sometimes I feel overwhelmed by despair. I've talked to a trusted friend who suggested that I should move on from the past, but I find it difficult to do so. I'm filled with feelings of regret, guilt toward myself, and detachment from my girlfriend. My mind is filled with confusing images that don't make sense. I take responsibility for my isolation during those years, and I know I need to make a change. I don't just need to talk about it, I need a solution. I appreciate your time. (age 32, from Portugal)

Our son had always been warm and close in our family growing up. He is very smart and had a great childhood. He went away to get his PhD and got married. About 3 years ago, there was a significant change in his personality. He has become prideful, lacks empathy, is highly driven in his work, ungrateful, dislikes showing emotions, distant, and has an inward focus. Additionally, he has become distrustful, suspicious, and arrogant, lacking compassion and seeming indifferent to our love for him. He wants to maintain surface-level relationships, tends to play the victim, has selective memory, is disinterested in his family, accuses us of things that apply to him, refuses to reconcile with his siblings, exaggerates things, has become somewhat of a loner, and doesn't seem to care about hurting people. Can you provide a possible diagnosis for this situation? Thank you for your assistance.

Lately, I've been experiencing intrusive thoughts that are quite disturbing. These thoughts can involve my family members or friends, and they often come out of nowhere. For example, I could be thinking about something completely unrelated, and suddenly a strange and unsettling thought will enter my mind. I find it difficult to ignore these thoughts, as they persist despite my efforts.

Patient's statement (rewritten): I'm a 13-year-old who has been experiencing recurring issues for a few years now. I tend to daydream a lot and have a few imaginary friends. I often engage in conversations with them and also imagine scenarios where we have fun or engage in romantic activities. Alongside this, I frequently have thoughts about suicide, murder, and other disturbing things. I have a history of self-harm and have recently started biting my hands, finding some sort of enjoyment in it. I struggle to sleep at night due to fear and a sense of hopelessness.

I've been experiencing occasional episodes of depression and a significant amount of stress. I'm a 15-year-old girl and I believe that the main reason for these feelings is the pressure I feel as the oldest sibling to my two younger siblings. My parents have high expectations for me, especially when it comes to my studies, grades, and exam results. Recently, I received my O'level results and I failed in three out of eight subjects. I put in a lot of effort to concentrate on my studies, but it seems like all my hard work goes to waste. Now, my parents are placing a heavy burden on me, calling me worthless, and this has triggered a period of depression for me. During these periods, I sometimes even entertain thoughts of suicide. I find myself considering running away from everything or resorting to self-harm because it feels overwhelming. I really need your help. Thank you. (age 15, from Pakistan)

Hi, I've been struggling with major depression and anxiety attacks, which have caused me to take a leave from my job for the past 9 months. I've always had a celebrity crush, but lately, my obsession with their love life has become overwhelming. I find myself constantly checking social media for updates on their relationship and it's affecting my daily life. I've tried deleting Twitter, but I keep going back to it. It's like I enjoy hurting myself. Can you offer any insights or advice?

Patient's Statement: Hello. My girlfriend is struggling with her two boys, ages 5 and 4. The 4-year-old is displaying aggressive behavior towards her, his brother, and me. He urinates all over the house, shouts, and frequently disobeys. My girlfriend has tried various disciplinary methods such as spanking, praise, and rewards, but nothing seems to completely resolve his behavior. He keeps falling back into these cycles of misbehavior.

I’ve been married to my husband for a while, and we have only been sexually intimate with each other. However, I've been experiencing some strange behaviors during sex that I don't understand. While I initially enjoy it, I often find myself crying uncontrollably to the point where it becomes difficult to breathe. This scares both me and my husband because he hasn't done anything wrong. Additionally, I have a desire for more painful experiences during sex, such as being choked or bitten. I try not to ask for these things because I know our sex life is already complicated due to the crying spells. Occasionally, I also have moments where I harm myself by scratching until I bruise and bleed, although it doesn't happen often, it does worry me. I want to mention that I was never sexually abused, but I did experience verbal abuse from my father. I'm not sure how that would impact my sex life. Is there something mentally wrong with me? It's worth noting that I lost my virginity at a normal age (16) and my husband is a loving man.
My wife and I have been married for 4 years now. We started to have issues about 2 years ago. I feel like since we have been officially and legally married that she doesn’t care about me.

Patient's statement (rewritten): I have been in a long-distance relationship with my boyfriend, and I am starting to notice some concerning behaviors. Initially, he courted me as a gentleman, but now he seems to enjoy toying with my emotions, humiliating me, and keeping things from me. I have opened up to him and shared everything about my life, but he has been secretive and defensive about certain things, like not wanting to share his Facebook or acting oddly when I mention visiting him.

Recently, I have been going through a lot of difficult situations involving my friend and my coach. My friend was raped and has been engaging in self-harm as a result. I had to intervene and talk her out of considering suicide. On the same night, I learned that my coach has also been a victim of traumatic experiences like gang rape, hazing, and stabbing. I have been supporting my friend through all of this, but it has been taking a toll on me emotionally. I can't stop thinking about what could have happened if I hadn't been there for my friend. She has been sharing every detail with me, and it's overwhelming. I constantly worry about her and it's affecting me physically, making me feel numb and have difficulty breathing. I have discussed all of this with my coach, and she suggested that I stop talking to my friend, as our friendship seems unhealthy. I did try to distance myself, but then another friend opened up to me about their recent suicidal thoughts. It feels like no matter what I do to try and improve my own well-being, I can't escape the constant reports of self-harm and suicidal ideation from those around me. This has made me feel tempted to self-harm again, but I remember the disappointment on my coach's face when she found out about my previous incident. To distract myself, I reached out to my friend, but deep down I know I need to focus on my own healing. I feel like I'm shouldering everyone's problems as if they were my own. I'm seeking advice and guidance on how to navigate these challenges and take steps towards my own well-being. Thank you for any help you can provide. (Age 15, from the US)

I'm a 23 year old male who currently lives with my father in an apartment. Lately, I've been feeling a lack of motivation and have been failing at everything I've attempted in life. I've also noticed that I actively hate myself and may be self-sabotaging. Some days, I even find myself thinking about death, although I'm scared of the idea of suicide and don't want to hurt those who care about me. My life is a mess with no job, dropped out of school, and facing massive debt. I've also realized that I sabotage my friendships and feel disconnected from everything, including myself. I can't sleep at night because these thoughts consume me, and even in my nightmares, I'm haunted by these questions. I've tried talking to my family, but they don't understand, and I feel like they're giving up on me. I want to know why I feel so out of place in this world and why I can't apply the same determination to other areas of my life. I want to seek help, but I don't have the financial means to invest in counseling. I'm feeling lost and don't know what to do. Any advice or support, even if it's tough, would be appreciated.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for over a year now, and I am concerned about his behavior. He admitted to having anger issues from past relationships and portrays himself as a hero in every situation. He frequently gets demanding with my time and lashes out at me for no reason. He also shows no compassion when I am upset and expects me to support him emotionally. He has also made hurtful and ungodly comments towards me. I suspect that he may be bipolar, but he refuses to seek help. I'm feeling overwhelmed and don't know what to do.

I'm a 14-year-old boy who has been through a lot recently. I've had a string of failed relationships that have left me feeling hurt, betrayed, and hopeless. It seems like everyone I've trusted has taken advantage of me. I'm scared that I'll never find someone who will treat me right. I can't help but wonder if there's something wrong with me. It feels pointless to try again if I'm just going to get hurt. Why is this happening to me?

I come from a family with helicopter parents who have always been overly involved in my life. They even moved with me when I went away to college. During my time in college, I entered into a serious relationship with my boyfriend, which has lasted for over three years now. We are at the point of considering engagement, but my mom refuses to see our relationship as serious and constantly speaks negatively about him, despite having no credible evidence to support her claims. I believe this may stem from jealousy and an inability to let go, especially since there is no valid reason for her to dislike him so much. I'm unsure if I should distance myself completely from my parents. I've tried talking to them and asserting my independence by spending more time with my boyfriend and his family, but it only leads to regression, negative emotions, and a lot of hurt.

It has been a challenging three years for me, as I have been in an on-and-off relationship. At first, my partner seemed like a gentleman, but over time, he revealed a darker side and cheated on me multiple times.
