Despite this, I found myself constantly going back to him, perhaps out of a sense of sympathy for his difficult childhood and the loss of his father. His sister also urged me to take care of him.

I have been in a relationship with my fiancé for 3 ½ years. We have a two-year-old son together, and he also has a three-year-old son from a previous relationship. Unfortunately, the mother of my stepson left and hasn't returned since he was just six months old. I have been there to support and care for him ever since she left.

Over the past two years of our marriage, my wife has been diagnosed with multiple severe medical issues. As a result, she has been spiraling deeper into depression, and it's been incredibly challenging for both of us. I've made numerous attempts to encourage her to seek counseling by providing a list of therapists for her to choose from, but she hasn't taken that step. She has even had thoughts of suicide, and although I've been able to support her through those moments, her depression continues to worsen. I feel helpless and unsure of what to do. I've considered getting a court order to force her into treatment, but I worry it may lead to the end of our marriage. I'm willing to do whatever it takes to help her, but I need guidance. Can you please offer some advice? Thank you.

Hi, I've been struggling with some concerns about my mental health. Lately, I've noticed that I tend to have a sense of superiority over others, which can make conversations feel awkward or even laughable. While I haven't been formally diagnosed, I suspect I may have a personality disorder and some mild psychosis.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for about a year and I feel incredibly happy with him. We have a strong connection where we can communicate comfortably and laugh together effortlessly. We have a lot of shared values and I feel completely comfortable being my authentic self around him. I've never experienced this level of connection with anyone before.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for almost a year now. We were actually together many years ago, but we recently reconnected. We have been discussing marriage and our future plans, but we haven't made any formal announcements yet because of his mother's strong dislike towards me. This has caused the rest of his family to distance themselves from me as well. He can't even mention me in a conversation without it turning into an argument. I've chosen to keep my distance and not attend family events, like dinners and birthdays, because that's what his mother prefers. However, I recently felt upset when he decided to spend Christmas Eve and Christmas Day with his family. He believes that by building a stronger bond with them, his mother will eventually become more accepting of me. He knew I was upset, so he offered to cancel his plans and be with me. But I asked him not to, since his initial plan was to spend the holidays with his family. All I want is for him to treat me fairly, like he does with them. I feel like there are no boundaries or limits when it comes to his family. I understand that he sometimes feels torn between me and them, but I don't know how to handle this anymore. I don't hold any grudges against his mother, as I know she has her own struggles, but I'm concerned that this conflict will only escalate once we get married. Am I being selfish? How can I support him without getting hurt?

My sister, a 33-year-old healthy, college-educated professional female, has been experiencing a concerning phenomenon over the past two years. On multiple occasions (around 3-5 times), while she is engaged in an activity in one room, her husband or mother will enter the room and speak to her. However, when they enter, she loses her sense of identity completely and starts believing that she is the other person. She sees things from their perspective, speaks their words, and has no connection to her own identity. These episodes last for about 20-30 seconds. Although she initially didn't think it was a cause for concern, she has expressed worry that it could worsen suddenly and she might not regain her own body and identity. She wanted to share this in case something like that were to happen.

I am struggling to understand and explain what is going on with me. It seems like I come across as someone who thinks deeply, but in reality, I don't. I have a hard time connecting with others emotionally and I find myself being apathetic. Sometimes, I say things without considering the impact it may have on others, though I don't mean to hurt anyone. I often feel mentally blank and when I do have thoughts, I obsess over why I am feeling this way. I've tried diagnosing myself with various conditions like schizophrenia, agoraphobia, depression, depersonalization, and ADHD. I'm confused about why I am experiencing these symptoms. Even during conversations, I feel disconnected. I no longer find joy in things and it feels like I am unable to feel emotions, except for sadness or fear. I frequently zone out and worry that I may be going insane. My life seems to pass me by and I can't seem to find a reason or a way to engage with it. Some important background information about me is that I experienced childhood sexual abuse from multiple individuals, I lacked a father figure, I spent a lot of time alone, and I excel in mathematics.

I'm a sophomore in high school and I've been feeling really down on myself lately. In my fourth period class, there's this kid who constantly makes fun of me and points out my flaws. I tried talking to the teacher about it, but it only made things worse. It's really hard to ignore him when he's constantly saying hurtful things like calling me ugly or pointing out my physical flaws. No one else seems to notice or say anything about it though.

I recently found out that I am pregnant while being in a long distance relationship. My partner finally moved to be with me after 8 months, but I discovered text messages where he tells his mom that he plans to abandon our child and go back home once he pays off his debts. He claims that he's only saying that to calm his family down. Additionally, I found out that he was talking to other girls and even planning to date one of them if things didn't work out between us. He was telling her that he loved her and all of that.

Patient's statement (background): The patient, a 31-year-old individual living in the US, is experiencing significant stress and feelings of isolation due to visa issues. Their visa is tied to their job, making it difficult for them to change employment or leave the country. They have no close friends in their city and often feel alone. In addition to these stressors, they have been navigating relationship difficulties with two different girlfriends.

Over the past month, I've been experiencing auditory hallucinations. It's happened about five times during this time, and the sounds always seem to originate from the right side of my head. It's almost as if someone is whispering in my ear.

I've been feeling a sense of emptiness and lack of enjoyment in life lately, despite having what others might consider a good life. I have financial stability, a loving relationship, but I just don't feel alive and nothing seems fun anymore.

Recently, I've noticed that someone I know has been experiencing frequent memory lapses. Initially, I didn't pay much attention to it, as occasional forgetfulness is common for everyone. However, my friend consistently recalls events and facts incorrectly. It's starting to concern me.

I’m 17 years old and I have been diagnosed with depression and anxiety disorders. It has been really challenging for me to cope with these conditions. On top of that, I currently live with my grandparents who have custody of me. While they do provide for my basic needs, they are verbally abusive and have hoarding tendencies. It's even more difficult because they deny their hoarding behavior and the way they speak to me. Our home is cluttered, with only one usable bedroom. The rest of the house is filled with junk, and even the garage and sheds are packed with belongings. Whenever I try to help clean, they get angry and accuse me of being disrespectful and ungrateful. I feel trapped in my room to escape the mess and the verbal abuse, which makes it incredibly hard to focus on my recovery. I have reached out for help, but unfortunately, the response I received was focused on my anxiety rather than addressing the situation with my grandparents.

I am from the U.S. and I am concerned about my husband's behavior towards our youngest daughter. While he was a good father overall, he was verbally abusive at times and seemed to be particularly hard on our youngest daughter. I do not believe that he molested her, but she has shared some concerning experiences. She mentioned that he would sometimes rub her feet in a way that made her uncomfortable, kissed her neck once, and made her feel uneasy on multiple occasions. She also mentioned having memories of going to bed with her clothes on as a child, which I find puzzling because I always put her to bed and don't recall this happening. Their relationship has always been stormy.

I'm really concerned about my husband's behavior. He has mentioned that he struggles with having emotions and has admitted to torturing and killing cats when he was younger. He has a history of lying and anger issues that affect our relationship. He has never been physically abusive towards me, but he has expressed a desire to know what it feels like to kill someone. He recently purchased a gun and a sharp weapon, which makes me very uneasy. I'm worried about my safety and the well-being of our daughter. Should I leave him? Can he experience love? Should I confront him about his violent thoughts?

Hello, I have a 16-year-old daughter who has exhibited some concerning behaviors in the past. When she was younger, she would steal minor things like candy and school supplies, but that seemed to have stopped. She also used to engage in destructive behavior towards her sisters, such as cutting their clothes or breaking their jewelry when she was angry, but she would show remorse afterwards. Recently, I've noticed that when she gets angry at our parrot, she hits the cage or holds its feathers back, although she never intentionally harms the bird. She also used to handle her pet fish in a way that could have harmed it, but stopped when I explained the consequences. Overall, she is shy, well-behaved, and loved by her teachers. I believe some of her behavior may be influenced by her father's anger issues. I don't think she meets the criteria for a conduct disorder, but I would appreciate your insights and guidance on how to handle this. Thank you.

I've been experiencing some difficulties with maintaining an erection during sexual activity, specifically when I put on a condom. It's been bothering me because it's affecting my ability to fully engage with my partner. Can you help me understand why this might be happening?

I've been struggling with my mental health for a while now. A few months ago, my psychologist diagnosed me with Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD) and I've been seeing them on a weekly basis. Recently, they mentioned that I also exhibit some signs of sociopathic traits. I'm not sure how to navigate this combination of BPD and sociopathic traits. I've heard conflicting information about the difference between having sociopathic traits and being a full-blown sociopath. Is there a spectrum for how mild or severe someone's sociopathy can be? I'm starting to doubt my diagnosis of Antisocial Personality Disorder (ASPD), maybe my psychologist made a mistake. Can you provide some insight?

Lately, I've been feeling a mix of sadness and confusion. I have friends and family, but I don't feel particularly close to my friends. I really want a best friend that I can rely on and share everything with, but I haven't found that person yet. Sometimes, I find myself getting bored or annoyed with my friends over small things, but I don't express my feelings to them. I also have moments where I don't like certain people, but then I suddenly like them again without remembering why they annoyed me. Additionally, I've always been a bit moody and irritable. I struggle with falling asleep at night and tend to worry and overthink a lot. I've been looking into BPD, but I don't have an intense fear of being alone or abandoned. I'm just not sure if my relationships with my friends are considered unstable since we haven't had any fights and we're on good terms. I also have a tendency to shop excessively and buy things I don't really need. Another thing is that I have a habit of picking at my split ends, although it's not from the scalp and I struggle to control it. I don't think I have BPD, but I wanted to make sure that my relationships with my friends aren't causing any concern.

As a teenager, I was diagnosed with bipolar disorder and ADHD. However, I haven't followed up with any treatment because therapy and medication made me feel tired and angry. I had a difficult upbringing with my father being an alcoholic, and by the age of 13, I experienced several traumatic events. As a result, I developed a coping mechanism of "blacking out" and shutting off my emotions. When I become upset or angry to the point of not caring, I genuinely feel that way and can easily disconnect from my feelings towards others. This emotional detachment can last for days, depending on the intensity of my emotions. I acknowledge that this behavior is not ideal and sometimes I can be cold, hateful, and even called evil. I'm unsure if this is related to my bipolar disorder or ADHD, or if it's something else entirely. I just want to name this behavior so that I can seek appropriate help. I'm aware that I need help for my ADHD and bipolar disorder, but I want to address my attitude issues first. I know I need help, but I haven't reached out beyond seeking answers for now.

Patient's statement with background and context: My friend is going through a difficult time right now. Her dad is battling cancer, and it's taking a toll on her and her family. Recently, she shared with me that she believes their neighbors and other people are trying to harm them. She thinks they are breaking into their house, poisoning their food, and following them. At first, I believed her, but now I'm starting to think that she might be experiencing paranoia, especially because things seem to be getting worse. I suspect that her mom might have influenced these thoughts, and now both of them are having trouble sleeping. I'm concerned about how this is affecting her life, especially since she's an intelligent person who is pursuing her education. I'm wondering if the stress of her dad's condition has triggered this paranoia. I'm also worried about what will happen to her mental state after her dad passes away. How can I approach this conversation with her?

I have met someone who I deeply love, but I'm struggling to face my feelings and be honest about them. Several years ago, I crossed paths with a man who has exceeded all my expectations. We have developed a strong friendship and enjoy spending time together. However, I find myself unable to acknowledge these emotions to him, myself, or anyone else. It's complicated by the fact that I was raised Catholic and was in the process of getting a divorce when we met. Additionally, he was already in a relationship. Society's norms tell me to distance myself from him, and I have been doing so. Even a simple friendly interaction like a wave or eye contact fills me with regret.

Lately, I've been having trouble sleeping. It's not just a matter of staying up late on my phone or anything like that. I'll lie in bed for three hours, which is usually how long I give myself to fall asleep, but I still can't seem to doze off. This has been affecting my school performance because I often go to school without getting any sleep at all, at least two out of the five days. I have a diagnosis of Dysthymic Disorder, so it's possible that my insomnia is related to that. However, when I do manage to fall asleep, I can sleep for at least twelve hours straight without any interruptions. My sleep schedule is all over the place - no sleep one day, one hour the next, and then fourteen hours the day after that. If there's a specific name for this issue, it would be really helpful to know so that I can explore treatment options. Do you have any suggestions?

I have always felt different from my peers, even since kindergarten. However, recently, I've started to feel bothered by what people think of me. My parents say that I am unsympathetic, selfish, and disrespectful, but I don't always understand why. I prefer to be alone most of the time and when someone invades my privacy, I react with anger and feel violated. There was one incident about a year ago where I almost harmed my little sister when she touched me in the pool. I only experienced intense anger like that once, but I'm scared it might happen again. I get angry over any kind of physical contact, even hugs. I also have extreme verbal outbursts, either screaming or crying. I don't have close friends and I tend to lie and pretend to be different people to impress others. I even created a detailed story about having diseases and shared it with my best friend, but eventually, I lost that friendship because the lies got out of control. I often feel disconnected from others and struggle with self-image. I have high levels of anxiety and feel empty most of the time. I also have no interest in romantic relationships or sex. I struggle to enjoy things and have a hard time accepting praise or criticism. I feel like a liar, a recluse, and an outcast. I came across an article on schizoid personality disorder and it resonated with me. Do I seem to be suffering from schizoid personality disorder? And how can I help my parents understand my need for space?

I'm 16 years old and I've been through a challenging relationship with a guy who is 15. Initially, I thought he was amazing, but then he confessed that he had feelings for my sister. It turns out my sister had been lying to me and was actually reciprocating his feelings. They even talked about intimate things. I felt betrayed and hurt. He blamed his actions on his depression, and I sympathized with him because he had attempted suicide before. However, he continued to break up with me and flirt with my sister. He even used his gender as an excuse, saying it was because he was a guy and blamed it on testosterone. Eventually, my sister cut off contact with him.

I started dating someone while we were both receiving treatment at a mental health facility. We were both working on our depression, so the relationship wasn't encouraged. Our child youth workers contacted his parents and expressed concerns about our relationship, but they also mentioned that we could possibly get back together once we're stable and no longer in the facility. He spoke to his parents about it, but they still have reservations. Additionally, I'm 15 and he's 17. While it's legally acceptable under Canadian law due to the age of consent having an exception for relationships within a five-year age gap, his parents are struggling to accept the fact that he's dating someone younger. We want to be open and honest with his parents, but we're not sure how to make this work. Can you provide any guidance on how we can navigate this situation?

I have been struggling with panic disorder (with agoraphobia) and severe generalized anxiety disorder since I was 7 years old. I am currently 19 years old and going through a major depressive episode. I have tried various treatments in the past, but I am not currently taking any medication.

"I'm feeling really lost in life right now. I recently turned 23 and just finished my university education. I'm struggling to make decisions and have no confidence in myself. It's difficult for me to express my emotions, even as I write this. I have so many worries and concerns about my future. I'm wondering if my background has any impact on how I'm feeling."

I have always been overwhelmed with the urge to pursue multiple interests and hobbies. Alongside my job, I find myself immersed in various activities that make it difficult to focus on one thing or make decisions. Lately, I have developed a strong fascination with creating electronic music. However, instead of actually making music, I spend most of my time researching and studying techniques. This obsession has led me to consistently miss work deadlines and struggle to stay focused on my job.

Over the past year, I've been experiencing a range of intense emotions and thoughts that have been troubling me. I often feel lonely and believe that no one cares about me, despite having friends. My self-esteem is low, and I have a negative body image. I engage in binge eating and feel disgusted with myself afterwards. I've also engaged in self-harm, primarily to see if anyone would notice. The fact that my parents didn't notice when I wore short-sleeves made me really upset. Thoughts of suicide and violence have crossed my mind, which scares me. However, I recently experienced a period of feeling extremely happy for several months. Now, those negative feelings are resurfacing. This time, I've been hoping for something bad to happen to me, like a car accident, so that I can either die or be taken care of in the hospital for a long time. I've even attempted to break my own bones and cut my wrists. Although I have these thoughts, I don't believe I will actually act on them. Instead, I hope that something random will happen to me. I've also noticed that I'm fascinated by horrific things on the news or TV, which doesn't feel normal. I have a quick temper and get angry easily, even over small things like mispronounced words. Additionally, I've been experimenting with drugs and alcohol, and my use has started to become more frequent when I'm alone. I haven't experienced any traumatic events in my life, and I'm just trying to understand these feelings.

In the past two years, my family has experienced some significant difficulties. I recently discovered that my mother had been having an affair for four years, which made me feel furious and I still harbor resentment towards her. However, I also found out more recently, this morning at 7:30 am to be exact, that my parents have been engaging in threesomes with strangers. It seems that my father may be seeking forgiveness from my mother for her infidelity. I stumbled upon this information when my father asked me to open his phone and unintentionally saw explicit photos of my parents with someone else. Additionally, I suspect that my mother may be involved in another affair with my dad's friend, as my dad seems unconcerned due to my mother's fulfillment of his sexual desires.

I'm really concerned about my 15-year-old sister. She's struggling both at school and at home. She skips school frequently, her grades are low, and she associates with the wrong crowd. She seems overly attached to her friends, constantly texting and hanging out with them, but becomes upset when those relationships end badly. At home, she refuses to do any chores, lacks motivation, and often feels tired and lethargic. She's easily angered, frequently experiences depression and anxiety, and complains of physical symptoms like stomachaches and headaches. She tends to blame others for conflicts, especially when it involves her not wanting to do anything productive. She has low self-esteem, struggles with anger, and has had a bedwetting issue since childhood, although it has improved over time. She tells me she feels incapable of making responsible decisions and always seeks instant gratification. These problems are causing a lot of tension within our family, as she not only refuses to go to school (leading to my mom being called to court for truancy), but she also refuses to do any chores. I believe there might be an underlying disorder or issue that is contributing to her behavior, but I'm not sure how to help her. She's been tested for ADHD and learning disabilities, but the results came back negative. She's intelligent and capable, so it seems like her struggles stem more from motivation and self-control. What can I do to assist her?

I've been struggling with a lot of symptoms lately. My psychologist doesn't think I'm depressed, but I'm having trouble believing that. I have difficulty concentrating and I lack motivation to do anything. I feel incredibly hopeless and everything in life seems pointless. Sometimes, I even have thoughts of death. Additionally, I've been told that I have delusions and paranoia. For years, I believed that there was an audience watching me and I would talk to myself, thinking I was communicating with them. I felt like I had no privacy and that everything I did was being observed. Even though I've been told that this is not true, it's still difficult for me to fully accept. I still find myself talking to them, but now I'm confused about it.

I recently came to terms with my sexual orientation and accepted that I am gay. However, I have always felt different and I am deeply afraid because of the negative things I hear people say about gay individuals. I am unhappy and have a strong belief that I will continue to feel this way in the future, leading to a life of misery and loneliness. I also struggle with self-esteem issues, constantly putting myself down and feeling unlikable. Being gay only adds to the complexity of these feelings. My conservative parents often make derogatory comments about gay people, which makes it difficult for me to imagine their acceptance if I were to come out. I also have intrusive thoughts about my dad possibly being gay and it bothers me a lot. There are so many thoughts and scenarios running through my mind, causing a great deal of stress. I can't afford therapy and even if I could, I would have to discuss the issue with my parents first. I just want to escape somewhere where I can start fresh, as I don't know how much longer I can handle living like this. I apologize for the jumbled letter, I just don't have anyone to talk to about all of this.

I have been feeling incredibly lonely and empty lately, and it's starting to have a major impact on different areas of my life. It's important to note that I have a history of clinical depression and was diagnosed with it in 2009. For a period of four years, I struggled intensely with it and was in and out of inpatient facilities due to suicidal behaviors. However, from fall of 2013 to summer of 2014, I experienced a period of remission and decided to move to a small ski town for a fresh start. Unfortunately, this town lacks sufficient mental health resources. About three months ago, my depression began to resurface and has been progressively worsening. I've been trying my best to seek help during this time, but it's been incredibly difficult as I have to wait three weeks to see any mental health clinician. To make matters worse, the wait time to see a psychiatrist here is 2-4 months, which feels incredibly discouraging. I don't indulge in any mood-altering substances except for smoking cannabis. I avoid alcohol completely. I'm feeling desperate for help as I've been experiencing severe mood swings and intense anxiety, which makes it difficult to function. If this website can offer any assistance, it could make a significant difference for me. Given the current state of my mood, I'm not sure how much longer I can cope before it starts to seriously impact me in ways that I don't need.

Patient: Hi, I'm a 17-year-old female still in high school. I've been struggling with my weight, and it's really affecting my self-esteem. I've tried dieting, but it often leads to binging. I'm currently in a long-distance relationship, and while my partner tells me I'm beautiful, I'm worried about what will happen when he sees my weight in person. I was recently diagnosed with PCOS, which has made it even more challenging to lose weight. I feel lost and don't know what to do. Can you please help me?

I've been struggling with suicidal thoughts, attempted suicide, depression, anxiety, bulimia, and self-harm. I've been attending outpatient therapy twice a week consistently. Recently, I had a major argument with my mom and ended up cutting myself worse than ever before. I know I need to talk to my mom and therapist about this, but I'm really scared and don't know how to approach the conversation. Can you please help me? I'm 14 years old and from the US.

I have been in a relationship with my girlfriend for 4 years. Recently, she told me that her brother and sister-in-law are pressuring her to get married and she wants me to talk to them about marrying her. This has caused me to have trust issues and question the honesty of our relationship. I've also noticed that she is very friendly with guys and has had past instances where guys have expressed interest in her. I'm worried that she may be cheating on me or not being truthful. Additionally, I've been feeling stuck in my career and spending a lot of time at home, which is adding to my confusion and negative thoughts. Can you help me figure out if she's being honest and how to address my trust issues?

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for about 1.5 years. Recently, I discovered that he has been communicating with multiple girls online, exchanging explicit pictures and expressing love for them. He claims that these relationships mean nothing because they live abroad. I also found out that he has been seeing a local girl, but he insists they are just friends and refuses to let me meet her. He started attending a class at the church to address his sexual temptation, but he hasn't ended his online relationships. Is he addicted to this behavior? Can he change? Should I give him another chance?

I am currently in college and have been in a relationship with my partner for almost two years. My partner was born with a rare condition called Spina Bifida, which is a birth defect. Despite his condition, he is able to walk and do most things that a person without his condition can do. However, he still faces daily challenges. Nevertheless, I love and accept him for who he truly is.

Since I was 2 months old, I haven't been able to grow up with my family. On weekdays, I am only with my grandma while my parents and brother are elsewhere. I feel like my mother dislikes me because she scolds me harshly. It's difficult for me to see my brother receive everything he wants, like a new house, a PS4, and even an iPhone.

I'm a 15-year-old girl who recently moved with my family from Connecticut to Utah. Since the move, there have been escalating issues within my family. One particular issue that overwhelms me is my mother's mood swings. Although she claims to have finished menopause, I still find myself making excuses for her behavior. The mood swings have become more frequent and intense since the move. We now have explosive fights, with my mother saying hurtful things and refusing to resolve the issues. I often find solace by taking long walks with my dogs to cool off. However, when I return, my mother ignores me and complains to my father about my supposed disrespect. It's a difficult and frustrating situation.

Hi, I'm a 20-year-old who has been dealing with anxiety and depression since 6th grade. Lately, I've been really worried that I might have schizophrenia. My family doesn't believe I have it, but they think I should talk to someone about my anxiety and depression. My anxiety has gotten so bad that I rarely leave my house. I also have thoughts that I might have a psychosis disorder and that I could turn into a dangerous person, even though I don't want to hurt anyone. I don't hear voices, but I've been having visual hallucinations, like seeing figures in the corner of my eye that disappear when I turn my head. Sometimes I see colors too, but I'm not sure if it's related to my eyesight. Thank you for listening.

My mother and I have always had a volatile relationship. Last night, she drank a bottle of red wine and became angry when I asked her about it. She went to her room, grabbed her bags, and said she wouldn't stay where she's not wanted. Since she lives 7 hours away and was intoxicated, I blocked the door and told her to go to bed. She threatened to harm me and things escalated into a physical altercation.

I'm a 25-year-old guy from Iran with a bachelor's degree in English translation. I've been feeling really empty and depressed lately. I've struggled with depression since I was 17, but it feels worse now. In the past, I thought being alone and unattractive was the worst thing, but now I feel even worse. About 8 or 9 months ago, my ex-girlfriend broke up with me and I found out 2 months later that she's engaged. We were together for a year and had our ups and downs. She wanted to get married, but it all ended. I realized too late that she was the meaning in my life and I would do anything to have her back. I think about her every day and I don't know if I'll ever find love again.

During our session today, Jordan shared that their parents divorced when they were 10 years old. They lived with their mother, who used to treat them and their older brother well. However, a year ago, their mother left them and took their younger brother to Dubai. Whenever Jordan and their older brother try to reach out to their mother, she responds with hurtful and aggressive remarks. Jordan is feeling deeply hurt by their mother's behavior and misses the way things used to be.

I've been doing a lot of research and I don't think I have an eating disorder. I don't own a scale and I'm not focused on changing my appearance or weight. But lately, I've been noticing that food is starting to control my life. I'm becoming increasingly concerned about what I eat.

I'm struggling with some mixed emotions regarding my relationship. I love my fiancé very much, and we have a great bond with his 5-year-old son. However, I feel incredibly sad knowing that he has a child with another woman. We both want to have a baby together in the future, but I'm scared of how this situation might affect me. I fear that my fiancé won't see our future child as special or unique because he has already experienced fatherhood. The thought of him having flashbacks or comparing our child to his first son makes me anxious and depressed. I've tried using a mantra suggested by my therapist to change my negative thoughts, but it hasn't been effective. I also find myself feeling jealous whenever my fiancé talks about his son or his ex.

I have been in a committed relationship with my girlfriend for over 3 years now and we have been living together for almost a year. This is the first long-term relationship for both of us and I truly love her. In the beginning, we were very affectionate with each other, but as our relationship progressed, it started to fade. About 3 months ago, she opened up to me about her past and how she wasn't very faithful in her previous relationships. Even though I understand that she had the right to see other people before we met, I can't shake off the thought of it. Recently, when I was at her place, I accidentally wore a jumper from her wardrobe that she asked me not to wear because it wasn't hers, and it triggered those negative thoughts again.

Lately, I’ve been struggling to fall asleep and it's causing me a lot of distress. I've tried different over the counter sleep aids and even resorted to drinking alcohol to help me sleep, but nothing seems to work. When I do manage to fall asleep, I have these intense and vivid dreams that make me question my reality. It's difficult for me to wake up from these dreams and when I do, I feel confused and disoriented. These dreams also seem to affect my emotions during the day. I'm not sure if this could be related to a sexual assault I experienced almost 2 years ago or if there's something else going on. I'm really struggling with this and it's impacting my daily life. Can you help me understand what might be happening?

I have been experiencing a challenging situation with my dad. He often uses unkind and derogatory language towards me, such as calling me names like retard, bitch, and fat. Despite his attempts to be a good father, his behavior persists, and it has become unbearable for me to be around him. My mom has also tried to intervene, but her efforts have been fruitless. During a conversation where I expressed how I felt, he laughed it off and dismissed our family contract, which was meant to address the name-calling issue. He even went as far as mocking individuals with mental health conditions, suggesting that I act similarly when I get upset about his name-calling. As someone with ADD, this topic is particularly sensitive for me, and his words have started to make me respond with anger towards him and my family. Consequently, I have been feeling increasingly depressed. What steps should I take to address this situation?

Hello, I'm a high school junior and I've been feeling really overwhelmed lately. I've always been a high achiever, but lately, when I'm alone, I feel sad and tired. It's like there's a different side of me that comes out. I'm usually outgoing and positive around my family and friends, but when I'm alone, I start doubting myself and worrying that I'll never meet my own high standards. I've been fixated on the idea that if I make any mistakes, I'll get kicked out of NHS and lose my scholarship. I have a lot on my plate with schoolwork, participating in musicals and plays, being a Student Ambassador, horseback riding, volunteering, and tutoring. I'm afraid I might have a breakdown.

When I was eight years old, I made the decision to leave home and study abroad at a boarding school. It has been 16 years since then, and I have been living away from my family ever since. However, I have come to regret this decision and have started blaming myself for the unhappiness I have been experiencing. It wasn't until recently that I realized how much my personality has changed over the years, and how unhappy I have become. Before going abroad, I used to be happy, but that changed after starting at the boarding school. As I grew older, I started keeping more secrets and hiding my true self. My parents and teachers have always emphasized the importance of being good, and since my first day at boarding school, I have learned to only act good, follow the rules, and never step out of line. It seems like people and teachers prefer students who are well-behaved and cause no trouble.

I'm a 15-year-old who recently mustered up the courage to seek help. I would have preferred this conversation to be private, but I really need some guidance. I'm uncertain about whether I can label my experiences as molestation. My older sister used to touch me inappropriately, and she would also make me do things to her. These incidents stopped when she reached puberty at around 11 or 12 years old, which would have made me around 7 at the time. My first question is: Can I consider myself a victim of molestation? Thinking about these experiences internally devastates me. I feel disgusted, and as someone raised in a Catholic household, I'm constantly afraid that I'm no longer a virgin.

Yesterday evening, during a sexual encounter with my girlfriend, she unexpectedly became physically aggressive towards me. She slapped, punched, dug her nails into my arm, and pressed into my chest forcefully. I was taken aback by her behavior. She abruptly stopped before reaching climax, but I suspect she was close. When I asked her if she enjoyed hitting me, she denied it and said it was impulsive. We didn't discuss the incident in the morning, but she later texted me an apology. I told her that if she wants to explore these types of activities, we need to have a conversation before engaging in them. In the past, she has expressed interest in being slapped, choked, and having her hair pulled, but only when she explicitly requests it. We had a face-to-face conversation about this, and I expressed my desire for her to have a satisfying sexual experience. I'm open to experimenting if it's something she genuinely enjoys. During our conversation, I asked her with an open mind if she found pleasure in it. She explained that she hit me out of impulsive anger towards me, without knowing why she was angry in the first place. She mentioned that if she could have caused me to bleed, she would have. However, she doesn't believe it's something she is into for erotic purposes. I reassured her that if it is a desire of hers, there's no need for embarrassment, and we should have an open discussion about it.

Over the past year, I've noticed some changes in my relationship with my girlfriend. We've been together for three years, and the first year was amazing. However, since we graduated and moved in together, I've been feeling some distance between us. My sex drive has decreased, and I've found myself getting irritated by small things she does. I didn't think much of it initially, but now I'm starting to worry that I may be losing interest in her, even though I still love her.

My mother's hoarding behavior has been a significant challenge in my life. I have witnessed her collecting various items, from cans to old clothes, throughout my entire life. Despite my efforts to confront her and prevent her from negatively impacting our lives, she remains manipulative and insists on having things her way. Our apartment is cluttered with unnecessary items, including empty cans in her closet. She also hoards newspapers, hiding them under her bed or in the basement.

During my time in middle school, I experienced repeated instances of bullying and harassment from my peers. They would slap me on the butt at the lunch table, make sarcastic comments, and even physically harm me, such as poking me with a pencil or kicking me in the back. This behavior left me feeling extremely uncomfortable and emotionally pained. I also faced difficulty when seeking help from teachers, as they dismissed my concerns and labeled me as "crazy". I now find myself still holding a grudge against my middle school and experiencing negative emotions from those memories. I am concerned that these experiences may have resulted in post-traumatic stress disorder.

I have been struggling with a variety of difficulties for a long time. Since middle school, I have experienced challenges with organizing my thoughts, focusing, and maintaining consistent sleep patterns. These struggles have persisted into my adult years, and I have also experienced feelings of darkness, disconnection, and nihilism. I have had thoughts about committing acts of violence, but I want to emphasize that I have no plans to act on these thoughts. I feel isolated, lack meaningful relationships, and find it difficult to experience pleasure or arousal. I engage in activities like masturbation, nicotine consumption, and music recording, but they no longer bring me joy. I have difficulty maintaining employment, make impulsive decisions at times, and generally dislike socializing. I often feel detached from reality and have a strong dislike for life, yet I am also afraid of death and the unknown. I have contemplated seeking help, but financial limitations prevent me from accessing therapy or medication. I am unsure of what I am seeking, but any advice or insight would be appreciated.

Over the past 7 months, I've been experiencing irritability, negativity, and difficulty focusing. Work stress has increased, making me anxious about graduating. I've been having conflicts with my friends, unintentionally hurting them and feeling hurt in return. I'm hesitant about seeing a therapist, but my friend offered to come with me. What do you think?

Hi, I'm an 18-year-old who has been questioning my gender identity. While I was assigned female at birth, I don't really feel connected to any specific gender. I've always been more of a loner and my social interactions have become even more limited lately. In high school, I only had a small group of friends that I would hang out with during school hours. Outside of school, I preferred to be alone in my room. Now that I'm in college, I don't have any friends there and I spend all my time alone at home. I also dislike parties and large crowds and tend to avoid them. I've never really understood how people form friendships and struggle to connect with others on an emotional level. My friends have mentioned that I always appear calm and indifferent, which is somewhat true. I find it difficult to express my emotions and feel uncomfortable around others. Additionally, I have no desire to get married or have children, and the thought of it actually makes me feel worse. I also have no interest in romantic or sexual relationships, which could be because I identify as aromantic asexual. I'm perfectly content living alone for the rest of my life, but others often tell me that it's wrong and I should change. I also have an aversion to physical touch and dislike being hugged, even by people I know, including family. Strangely, when some of my friends moved away, I couldn't feel sad about it. To me, everything felt the same. The same goes for when I meet someone I haven't seen in a while - I don't get excited. Can you help me understand what's going on?

I am currently going through a lot of confusion. I became close friends with a girl (Let’s call her G) with whom I shared a deep emotional and intellectual connection even though there was no physical attraction initially. However, our emotional intimacy led us to start dating. We dated for a few months and I found G to be an amazing, caring, supportive woman. I found in her a lot of characteristics that I find in my mother. We are very different as individuals in terms of our likes and dislikes, but there was a deep bond we both felt.

My partner and I have been in a committed relationship for over 7 years, including a year of marriage. However, we have been experiencing a significant decline in our sexual intimacy for the past 6 years. It has become irregular and infrequent.

I'm a 15-year-old from Australia and I've been feeling really different lately. Normally, I'm outgoing and love being around people, but for the past few weeks, I've been feeling irritable and wanting to isolate myself. I just want to sit in a dark room and stare out the window. I've been reacting differently to things my friends say, even though they wouldn't usually bother me. I've been snapping at them and saying things I don't mean. I'm also feeling sad most of the time and have a really low self-esteem. I feel like nobody wants me around and that I'm worthless.

I have been experiencing disturbing thoughts and urges to do harmful things to others, including my sister and animals. These thoughts seemed to disappear as I got older, but they have recently become worse. I also experienced a traumatic event of sexual abuse when I was 15, which seems to have triggered these thoughts. I have had incidents where I felt compelled to hurt others, like chasing a friend with scissors, and thoughts of causing harm while driving or at work.

Despite having a supportive boyfriend, family, and close friends, I still feel a profound sense of loneliness. I believe that none of them truly know the real me, and I've been considering seeking professional help to address these feelings. Currently, I am taking medication prescribed by my psychiatrist, which helps me maintain a facade of normalcy and happiness. However, deep down, I am still struggling with mental illness and have a darker side that no one is aware of. My emotions tend to be intense and limited, ranging from anxiety and depression to rage, empathy (to a greater degree than most people), and occasional moments of elation. I also find myself frequently fantasizing about suicide, although I have no immediate plans to act on these thoughts. There is something important I feel I need to accomplish before considering that option. Lately, I've been yearning for at least one person in the world to truly understand who I am, and I've been contemplating seeing a therapist. However, the fear of being involuntarily committed to a psychiatric hospital, which has happened to me in the past, is holding me back. I'm concerned that if I disclose these thoughts and feelings to a therapist, they might have me committed. I do not want to be hospitalized, and I have not made any attempts in the past decade because I want to ensure that if I were to take that step, it would be under the right circumstances. Since I don't currently have a specific plan, do you think a therapist would still commit me if I reveal this information? If that's the case, I may choose not to pursue therapy, even though my hidden dark side is taking a toll on me.

I recently took a mental health assessment and my results indicate that I have high scores in dissociation, PTSD, depression, and anxiety. These symptoms seem to align with Dissociative Identity Disorder (DID). I've also been experiencing memory loss, both short-term and long-term, when it comes to events. However, I don't seem to have any trouble retaining information. I've been having visual and auditory hallucinations, both internally and externally. I also experience feelings of depersonalization and derealization, where I feel like the world around me is not real. Additionally, I have frequent out-of-body experiences, trances, and moments where I feel like I'm observing myself from a distance. I've noticed that my personality shifts in different situations, with different states emerging depending on the context. For example, I have a more social personality for communicating and a more confident one for presenting. I've been struggling with identity confusion as well, feeling like a boy on some days and a girl on others. I've been identifying as transgender, but it doesn't quite seem to fit. The voices I hear are always either commenting on or conversing with me, and I'm able to respond to them. I also feel like my thoughts, feelings, and behaviors aren't always my own.

Hello, I'm really struggling and my family isn't providing the support I need. They have conservative beliefs and rely heavily on religion to address mental health issues. However, that approach hasn't been effective for me. I have faith in God, but my panic attacks are becoming unbearable and people see me as strange. During these episodes, I experience trouble breathing, a racing heart, sweating, and disorientation. I find that focusing on facts helps me anchor myself in reality. I have some concerns about my part-time job as a teenager. Will it have long-term consequences? I have aspirations that require a clear mind. Do all teenagers experience negative effects from work, or are there some positive outcomes? Will things improve on their own, or do I need strategies to cope? I prefer factual information, as it tends to be more helpful for me. I work in retail twice a week. I'm feeling desperate and would appreciate any guidance.

Over the past year, I have been experiencing persistent feelings of sadness and depression. This started after I moved to a new state with my boyfriend and began a new job. I am grateful for any help you can provide. Thank you.

I've been feeling really overwhelmed and desperate for help lately. My husband and I have been married for 16 years, but throughout our entire marriage, he has struggled with addiction. It started with gambling, then progressed to weed, alcohol, and cocaine, and now he's addicted to prescription pain pills. On top of that, he's had affairs in the past and is constantly lying. I have been feeling extremely depressed lately. It's not just a fleeting sadness, but a deep sense of despair. I've noticed a significant weight loss of 60 lbs since February, which is concerning. My mother has had a difficult upbringing marked by poverty and abuse. Her father, who was often drunk, would physically harm her brothers out of jealousy towards her mother's attention. Growing up, my mother experienced extreme poverty, having to mend her shoes with cardboard and facing ridicule from her peers for not being able to afford basic necessities like a bra. Over the past year, I have lost over 50 pounds in a healthy manner. However, in the past few months, I've noticed that I've become obsessed with food. I constantly think about what I will eat and plan my calories for the day. I try to make myself eat more because I know I'm not consuming enough, usually less than 700 calories. Eating with others makes me anxious because I fear they will make me eat more, so I often make excuses to avoid social meals. When I do eat, I experience intense guilt and anxiety, with a voice in my head telling me I will become fat if I continue eating. Sometimes, if I eat something I shouldn't, I end up binge eating and feeling the urge to purge, although I haven't acted on it. I have a strict schedule for everything, including eating and exercising, which I believe may be related to my OCD. I work out every day and ride horses as well. The thought of becoming overweight again terrifies me, especially because of the impact it had on my horse. Despite people telling me I'm thin, I only see myself as fat. I've tried to stop these behaviors, but the thoughts of being fat, obese, and ugly persist. It feels like there are two conflicting voices in my head, constantly arguing over what I should do, and I can't determine which one is right. Additionally, I constantly feel cold, dizzy, tired, and fatigued. I've wanted to confide in someone about this, but I fear they may think I'm seeking attention or find me weird. For reference, I am 15 years old, from the United States, and currently weigh 120 lbs at a height of 5'6" or 5'7".

It has been really challenging for me and my family to deal with my mother's unusual behaviors. She often acts feeble, adopts a victim mentality, and always needs to be different. For example, she wears a fur coat in hot weather, brings her own food in old Tupperware containers, and pours water in it claiming she has bad digestion. We feel ashamed and embarrassed by her actions and it has affected our relationship with her. Can you suggest any strategies for us to cope with this situation and live a healthy life? Thank you. (Age 34, from US)

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for over 3 years and we recently moved in together. Overall, we have a great time together and he possesses many positive qualities. However, there have been instances in the past where he displayed angry behavior, particularly when he was drinking. He has verbally mistreated me and even physically shoved me on one occasion. Although it happened a while ago, I feel like we have worked through it.

I have been experiencing some concerning behaviors during my sleep. Sometimes I find that my hand is inside my shorts or underwear without my conscious awareness. I'm unsure why this is happening. Recently, I had a disturbing experience where I felt like someone was watching me while I was sleeping. When I slightly opened my eyes, I saw my dad standing there, watching me. I quickly moved my hand away and pretended to still be asleep. It was even more distressing because I wasn't covered by my blanket at that moment, so I grabbed it and waited for my dad to leave.

About a year and a half ago, I had a really intense panic/anxiety attack while using cannabis. It triggered a fear that I had somehow caused schizophrenia by smoking, and I've been struggling with that fear ever since. It's like a phobia of developing schizophrenia, where I constantly worry about experiencing delusions, hallucinations, paranoia, and being in the prodrome of schizophrenia.

In April, I was hospitalized for suicidal ideation. It was an incredibly stressful experience and I found it to be more stigmatizing than helpful. I still have nightmares where I wake up sweating, thinking I am back in the locked ward. I was diagnosed with borderline personality disorder during my hospitalization, but both my past and current therapist disagree with this diagnosis. However, I'm still struggling with strong suicidal thoughts and I don't want my loved ones to experience the pain that suicide would bring. I've started fixating on ways I could die, like contracting a serious illness. This is making it difficult for me to move forward in life, even though I have dreams and goals. I'm not sure if I have the energy to accomplish them in my current state. I want to know the best way to discuss this with my therapist without risking another hospitalization. I'm also in the process of transitioning to a new therapist because my current one is leaving. I was just about to bring up these issues with my current therapist, but I'm worried it will be seen as a way of avoiding abandonment. Should I wait to discuss this with my new therapist or should I share it with my current therapist since it takes time to build trust with someone new? The pain I'm feeling is serious right now. Thank you for your guidance.

Throughout my life, I have experienced consistent bullying and criticism from my parents. This has led me to internalize my emotions and only express them when I am alone. Additionally, discussing depression is highly stigmatized in my culture, making it difficult for me to seek support. While I have had thoughts of suicide in the past, it has been a while since I last experienced them. Recently, my sister got married and I feel a deep sense of loss as if my best friend has left. I have never been in a romantic relationship and struggle to maintain friendships for more than a few weeks. I constantly feel overlooked and forgotten. How can I find genuine friendships and prevent my depression from worsening?

Patient: I've noticed a pattern in my relationships where I can't seem to make them last. I really want to be in a relationship, but after about two weeks, I start getting bored and find faults in my partners. It's like I want to escape from them, even though they treat me well. I've been feeling really devastated and confused lately. A few weeks ago, my wife suddenly asked me for a divorce, which came as a huge shock to me. I'm a 12-year-old student from Australia. I started year 7 in February, and lately, things have been really tough for me. Although I don't see or hear things, I have a strong feeling associated with these thoughts. It makes me incredibly anxious because it's unpredictable. I don't understand why, but these thoughts also tell me to do specific things, and I end up doing them when I'm upset. I find solace in isolating myself in my room and spending a lot of alone time. I've been experiencing thoughts of giving up and have even considered suicide multiple times. It's gotten to the point where I hope for a car accident so it doesn't appear intentional. I just want to feel whole and have my parents listen to me, but whenever I try to talk to them about it, they dismiss it as if it's not a real problem.

Hello, I'm a 28-year-old female. Over the past year and a half, I've been experiencing a decline in my mental health. My fiancé doesn't seem to understand or listen to me. I had a difficult time in my senior year of high school after losing my best friend. It took me a few years to recover, but when I met my fiancé, things started looking up. I'm constantly stuck at home and it's affecting my role as a mother and wife. I desperately want to change and regain control of my life.

I find myself losing control and reacting impulsively to even the smallest things. It's only later, after the incident, that I feel regret and remorse. I'm scared that one day I might end up hurting them unintentionally. I really need help to gain control over these intense feelings and reactions. I'm here because my boys mean everything to me, and I don't want to feel this way anymore. Please, can you help me?

My 23-year-old daughter is struggling with both paranoid schizophrenia and methamphetamine addiction. She doesn't want to try counseling and wants to work through it on our own. I'm concerned about losing her. Should I give her space or try to bring her back?

I wanted to share some background information about a child I am concerned about. He is currently 4 years old and lives with my fiancé because his mother does not seem to want to take care of him. It's important to note that there hasn't been any legal custody arrangement made. The mother smokes weed and drank alcohol while she was pregnant. My fiancé has always worked two jobs to provide for him and his own child. The mother used to be his babysitter but didn't teach him any rules or structure. As a result, the child is disrespectful, lacks manners, and doesn't seem to have much common sense.

My boyfriend is dealing with a lot of family issues that are affecting our relationship. His parents' marriage has been plagued by infidelity, with his father frequently cheating on his mother. Despite their children being grown and financially independent, his mother continues to stay with his father, even though he barely works and has another woman out of state. It's frustrating to see how much his mother allows him to mistreat her. Additionally, his older brother cheated on his wife while they had a child together, resulting in their divorce. His second oldest brother is in a volatile and unmarried relationship with the mother of his three sons.

At 15 years old, I experienced a traumatic accident where I sustained severe burns on 30% of my body. The incident has had a profound impact on me, as I constantly replay it in my mind. I feel overwhelming guilt for the financial and emotional burden it placed on my mother, who cried every day during my hospitalization. Since then, I have struggled with crying myself to sleep, nightmares, and being teased at school. This isolation has led to deep feelings of loneliness and depression. Recently, my girlfriend broke up with me after I opened up about my thoughts and feelings. Although the news of my mother's pregnancy with my little brother has kept me from acting on suicidal thoughts, I still question the purpose of living amidst all the hate and stress. I long for someone who understands and cares about what I've been through.

When I was about 12, my older brother would want to hang out and watch movies and stuff, while we were watching he would pull his penis out. He wouldn’t really do anything or try to touch me, it was just there and he just took it out. I don’t know why he did it, and he did it several times.

When I was younger, my sister and I were very close. However, there were instances where she would exclude me from activities, like starting a club with her imaginary friend. As we got older, our church had plenty of people her age that she could hang out with, but I felt left out because I had always been with her. I wanted to be friends with them too, but my sister seemed to want them all to herself. Then, a new person my age joined the church and was allowed to hang out with the older friends because she was new. Once again, I was left out. Now, as an adult, I find myself experiencing similar feelings when I feel rejected by others. I tend to exclude myself and then feel jealous and bitter towards them. How can I overcome these childhood experiences so that they don't negatively impact my current relationships? Thank you!

I'm a 21-year-old college student who is currently unemployed. Throughout my childhood and teenage years, I struggled with anger management issues that were never fully diagnosed, although Manic-Depressive/Bipolar Disorder and Asperger's were suspected. I find it difficult to make friends, although I don't have trouble talking to people. Initiating romantic relationships is particularly challenging for me. I go to great lengths to avoid conflict, often inconveniencing myself to prevent inconveniencing others. While I claim not to care about others' opinions of me, deep down, I do. I often feel unaccepted, worthless, and like a burden to those around me, even when I'm alone. I also have a fear of being taken advantage of by others, which makes me skeptical of anyone who shows romantic interest in me, likely due to past experiences.

I'm really struggling with a situation at home. It seems like my mother may be cheating on my dad. A few months ago, my sister overheard her on the phone with another man and the way she was speaking to him raised some major concerns. My sister told me about it and I trusted her. However, when we confronted my mom, she denied everything and called us both liars.

I've been struggling with a problem that feels really strange to me, but I hope you can listen and help me understand what's going on. I've noticed that for as long as I can remember, I've had issues with pathological envy and a lack of a clear sense of self. I find myself constantly shifting and changing my interests and behaviors to match other people's expectations. I feel inferior to others, especially those who are smarter or more powerful, and I often mimic their looks and behavior because I want to be like them, even if they are fictional characters or not good role models. This started when I was very young, and I can't pinpoint any specific reason for feeling this way. Now, I find myself comparing myself to real people around me, and if I don't measure up, I become extremely anxious and feel physically unwell. It's become overwhelming, and I don't know why I feel this way. I worry that there might be something clinically wrong with me, even though I can't find a specific disorder that matches my experiences.

My boyfriend and I are both 16 years old. We have been dating for about a year. I broke up with him once because I had just come out of a 3-year relationship and wasn't ready to date again. But we got back together, and he treats me really well. However, when we fight, he gets very upset, curses, and becomes aggressive because he doesn't want to lose me. I suggested taking a break, and during that time, he was mean to me and even pushed me twice. This behavior is new, and I think he was overwhelmed. My mom, who has experienced abuse in a previous relationship, is concerned that it may escalate. He has been apologizing and trying to make amends, but my mom won't let me talk to him. I love him and want to be with him, even if it means not being alone.

Dear counselor, I recently went through a difficult breakup and have been leaning heavily on my friends for support. However, I've noticed that they have started pulling away and avoiding me. They suggested that I see a psychologist, so I went with them. But honestly, I didn't find it helpful and the psychologist recommended psychotherapy. I don't feel that my situation is bad enough to warrant weekly therapy sessions. However, I have now developed a problem where I constantly text my friend, exaggerating how bad I feel and making up stories to seek attention and care. I also feel extremely anxious if she doesn't reply immediately and end up bombarding her with multiple messages. I'm starting to realize that this behavior is causing more harm than good. Is there a book you can recommend that might help me with this issue? And do you think I really need psychotherapy? (age 24, from the UK)

My partner and I have been in a committed relationship for about a year now, and overall things are going well. However, I've noticed that my partner seems to struggle with trusting me. I want to assure you that I have been faithful and have never given them a reason to doubt my loyalty. It hurts me to see them so skeptical, as I truly love them and would never even consider cheating on them.

Since I was a child, I have experienced extreme mood swings without any apparent reason. Counselors have attributed it to my history of physical and emotional abuse. I am now almost 30 years old, married with two children, and should be happy, but I constantly feel unhappy. My temper and attitude seem to worsen each year, particularly between August and October. During this time, I become overwhelmed with sadness and dissatisfaction with my life. I make impulsive decisions that affect those around me. Recently, I left my home, where my husband of 10.5 years still resides. I only see my children every other day, and I cannot enter my own home due to extreme anxiety and anger. I cannot identify a specific cause for these feelings, and although I want to return home, I cannot bring myself to do so. The worst part is that I don't understand why I feel this way. I am constantly angry but cannot explain why. I believe everyone would be better off without me. I have no medical insurance, no money, and medications have not helped in the past. This leads to overwhelming, unexplained anger. Why am I always angry without a reason? Why can't I enjoy simple moments with my family without irrational thoughts of violence? I am not a violent person, but I become one when I feel attacked. I feel overwhelmed and there is a buildup of energy inside me that needs to be released, leading to blackout episodes. Afterward, I have no memory of what happened. However, there is often a mess left behind. This anger is controlling my life, relationships, and work. I don't want my children to hate me or fear me, like I did with my mother. I don't want to become her. This fear has influenced my decisions since I was 10 years old, and it is becoming increasingly difficult to control. What can I do? Please help!

I have been in a long-term relationship with my fiancé for six years, and we have been engaged for one year. For the past five years, I have been extremely happy, but recently I have developed feelings for a friend and coworker. We have known each other for three years, but our relationship became more intimate when we started working together. We have even started a private business together, which has brought us closer. Although I have always had a crush on him, I never thought he felt the same way. However, he recently confessed his love for me before leaving to continue his education. We gave in to our desires and spent three amazing days together before he left. Now, I can't stop thinking about him and it is affecting my relationship with my fiancé. My fiancé loves me deeply and wants to fight for our relationship, but my feelings have changed. I am torn between the familiarity and security of my relationship and the exciting new connection I have with this other person. I feel guilty and unsure of what to do. It has been a month since he left, and I am feeling depressed and overwhelmed. Please help me.

I have been in a relationship with a lovely man for 2.5 years. We are engaged and have booked our wedding. Last week, we went to a party and he got way too drunk. I had asked him to stop drinking spirits in May as he once became aggressive towards me (threw keys at me, verbally abused me). He has promised to stop drinking altogether, and so have I. I’m now also afraid that his turbulent childhood will impact upon my life. My friends think that I shouldn’t marry him as he became so aggressive when drunk, and in London everyone drinks a LOT all the time. I am trying to make the wisest decision possible. It’s been a terrible week and would be grateful for any input.

Patient's Statement: Two years ago, I was diagnosed with depression and anxiety. I was prescribed 20mg of Seroxat and 1.5mg of Xanax per day. Initially, the medication helped improve my mental state and I experienced significant relief from symptoms. Over time, I gradually reduced my intake of Seroxat and eventually stopped taking it altogether. However, recently I have been experiencing a return of some symptoms, including anxiety and obsessive thoughts. I'm unsure if this is due to SSRI withdrawal or if I'm regressing to my previous state. Although I've made progress in therapy, these lingering issues still bother me. Can you help me understand what might be going on?

My wife and I have been together for about 14 years, but lately we have been experiencing frequent and intense conflicts. It's really taking a toll on me emotionally. I know I don't deserve the contempt she shows me. I really need some guidance and advice on how to navigate this situation. I've set boundaries and hope they will be respected, but I feel like the intimacy and affection we once had is gone.

He experiences auditory hallucinations, paranoia, and delusions, including believing I am a witch who steals his energy. I have urged him to seek help and have involved emergency services multiple times, but he refuses to get treatment. I am worried for his mother's safety as well. What can we do to help him?

I didn't go to the funeral, and when we talked about it, I felt deeply hurt. It took me a long time to rebuild my trust in him.

I have been struggling with intense sadness for as long as I can remember. It feels like a never-ending cycle, and I find it hard to recall moments of happiness. Since my teenage years, I have been plagued by thoughts of suicide. There is a constant sense of emptiness within me, like a black hole that drains my energy and zest for life. Initially, I thought it was just a phase that many teenagers go through, but as I've grown older, these feelings have only intensified.

I've been feeling really overwhelmed lately, and I don't know what to do. It seems like everything is falling apart, and I can't seem to catch a break. I feel like I'm drowning in all of my responsibilities and it's suffocating me.

Ever since I developed restrictive eating habits and struggled with anorexia, I've noticed that I've become more withdrawn and anxious in social situations. I avoid personal conversations, don't respond to text messages, and reject most invitations to hang out. I feel like I might say something stupid or weird and it makes me incredibly stressed and anxious. I also struggle with sensitivity and have difficulty dealing with change. I used to be a social butterfly, so I'm not sure what happened.

As a child, I experienced feelings of exclusion and jealousy when my sister started a club with her imaginary friend and excluded me. This pattern continued as we grew older, with her excluding me from hanging out with people her age at church. I now find myself feeling rejected and excluding myself from relationships when I perceive even a slight rejection. How can I overcome these childhood experiences and prevent them from impacting my current relationships?

She has developed a rude attitude towards me for some reason, and denies me things even though I have always been there for her, helping her with homework and teaching her important skills. Patient: I’m eighteen years old, and I hate myself so much. I feel like I can’t do anything right, that whatever I do, it won’t be good enough. I've been feeling really overwhelmed lately and I don't know who to talk to. I feel like my problems aren't important enough and that I'm just being dramatic. I'm not sure if anyone will understand or if they'll even care.

I have been seeing my therapist, who is male, for several months now and it has been a positive experience. Throughout my life, I have felt neglected, so having someone who listens and understands is really valuable to me. However, I have started developing feelings for my therapist. I looked up transference and realized that this is not uncommon. I want to clarify that these feelings are not due to him leading me on or any jealousy towards other women in his life. Recently, I even had an erotic dream about him, which I believe is a form of erotic transference. I want to mention that I have never experienced physical or sexual abuse, but I do have some issues with sex. I am a nymphomaniac but haven't shared this with my therapist yet. It's because in the past, when I have talked about sex with men, it has often led to heartbreak. I find that I get objectified a lot and my feelings are not considered. I am afraid of intimacy, and my therapist is so wonderful that I fear losing him if I bring this up. I don't idolize him, but I appreciate his down-to-earth nature. I am just unsure about how to discuss this with him. When I talk about sex with men, it is usually to seduce them, and I don't want my therapist to think I am doing the same. Additionally, I struggle with controlling myself around someone I am attracted to. I have complete faith in my therapist and believe he won't overreact or freak out, but I am worried about how I will handle everything. I have been told that I tend to overwhelm men, and I want to avoid that moving forward.

Since elementary school, I have engaged in self-harming behaviors such as pinching and punching myself. In 7th grade, I started cutting, and by 8th grade, thoughts of suicide began to consume me. I attempted suicide with pills in 8th grade, but it didn't have the desired effect. Throughout high school, I have taken various online screenings which have shown moderate levels of dysthymia and cyclothymia. I am now a junior in high school and I want to talk to my parents about it, but I feel like they won't understand. My mother has a negative view of self-harm and mental health issues, believing that those who self-harm are just spoiled brats with too much free time. She even made insensitive comments about a friend's daughter who attempted suicide. How can I open up to someone who has such a dismissive attitude towards my struggles?

My spouse's ex is causing a lot of stress in our life. They threaten to withhold my step-child, cause financial hardship, and are generally hostile towards us. We've been in and out of court, and there has been domestic violence in their household which worries us for our child's safety. Lately, I've noticed physical symptoms like a consistently high pulse rate, feeling immobilized, and a tightness in my chest. I'm scared that the stress will lead to a heart attack. I don't know if this is normal or how to fix it.

Last night, I experienced a really intense emotional reaction when I was lying next to my little brother and started thinking about the fact that one day he will pass away. It made me cry uncontrollably for about an hour and it was difficult to catch my breath. I'm struggling to accept the inevitability of his mortality and it's affecting my ability to be happy. I've been battling depression for three years and this constant fear is making it even harder.

Hello. I come from a family in Azerbaijan with four children - three girls and one boy. My brother, who is the youngest, was born after a seven-year gap. He is currently 17 years old and has recently graduated from high school. He is planning to start university in September.

I have been struggling with cheating for the past few years. It all started when my wife stopped working and we were facing financial difficulties with the arrival of our second child. Despite my attempts to discuss the situation and encourage her to find a job, she refused. This left me feeling overwhelmed, depressed, and burdened with debt. I ended up having a fling with a coworker, mostly for the physical aspect, but it made me feel loved again.

Sometimes I experience extreme fluctuations in my mood. There are times when I feel an overwhelming sense of energy and confidence, believing that I can achieve anything. However, there are also times when I feel incredibly low and consider ending my life to spare others from the burden of my existence.
