During these moments, I hear a voice in my head urging me to harm myself or others. Additionally, I find myself becoming angry and resentful towards those who seem to enjoy life. Is this a normal experience for someone my age?

I've been in a relationship with my partner for a few years now and we've had some trust issues from the start. He had been cheated on in the past and it caused him to have trust issues. In our first year together, he would constantly accuse me of cheating and I would try to assure him that I had never been unfaithful. Eventually, I reached a breaking point and ended the relationship. He pleaded with me to stay and the accusations stopped. However, recently he admitted that he had cheated on his ex as a way of retaliating before ending things with her. He didn't sleep with his ex or the other person, but he still lied to me. I'm feeling depressed because I love him so much but I don't know if I can trust him. Our relationship has improved in other ways, but the lying is causing me a lot of distress. I need advice for my own well-being.

I have been feeling concerned lately that I may be developing symptoms of schizophrenia. About a month ago, I went through a period of heavy substance abuse, and just as I was getting sober, I started noticing changes in my thinking and perception. Even though I am now sober, I feel more spacey and absent-minded, and it seems like my brain is not processing information as well as it used to. While I don't have hallucinations or delusions, I do occasionally experience odd visual and auditory perceptions, like seeing clouds moving quickly or mistaking objects for people. In the past, I had terrifying thoughts that came out of nowhere, but I was able to overcome them. However, that experience planted the fear in my mind that I might have schizophrenia, which has been causing me a lot of anxiety and fear. I often feel tense and anxious for no reason, even when I try to distract myself from the idea of having schizophrenia. Additionally, I have noticed a decrease in my ability to experience pleasure in activities I used to enjoy, as if my reality and emotions have become dulled. I would greatly appreciate any help or feedback you can provide. Thank you.

I've been experiencing episodes where I lose track of time. It started about two years ago, but it was only for a few minutes back then. Lately, it has gotten worse and it can last anywhere from a few minutes to a few hours. I'm a 23-year-old male and I live on my own in Canada.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for over a year now. Initially, things were good and we spent a lot of time together. However, after a few weeks, he became controlling and I started to feel isolated from my friends. I am scared to even touch my phone because I don't want to cause a fight. Communicating with him about my feelings has been difficult, as he often gets angry. We started living together very early on in the relationship and we fight daily over trivial matters. He has a tendency to make a scene during our fights. One time, he even blocked me from leaving the room during an argument and ended up falling down the stairs. I feel like he invades my privacy by constantly checking my messages and watching what I'm doing. He also doesn't contribute to household chores and often makes me late for things. Whenever I express my frustration, he gets mad at me and expects me to apologize and cuddle him. I've mentioned breaking up several times, but he gets upset and accuses me of using it as a threat. I love him, but I'm at a loss for what to do anymore.

I have been struggling since my grandfather's passing last year in Bangalore, India. I witnessed his death as he was brought home from the hospital. He went to sleep and never woke up again. I blame myself for not being able to call an ambulance when I tried, as the call didn't go through. I feel responsible for his death, even though deep down I know it wouldn't have made a difference. Since then, I can't stop thinking about the possibility of my other family members dying in a tragic way. Every day, on my walk home from school, I imagine different scenarios and feel overwhelmed by the thought of losing them.

Patient's statement (rewritten): A few years ago, my father passed away while I was in university. Our family owns an independent grocery store, which my father used to manage. Life was comfortable for me until his passing. I have an older brother and sister, but my sister got married, so it's just me and my brother handling everything now. Lately, it has become increasingly difficult because my mother relies on me emotionally and wants me to be there for her all the time. I'm trying my best to juggle running the store and maintaining a work-life balance, but my mother also expects me to take care of the household and her. I find myself getting easily stressed out. Sometimes, my mother has mood swings and even says she wants to die during outbursts. I know it's not right, but there are moments when I think that if she were no longer here, my life would become easier. I feel incredibly guilty for having such thoughts. Am I being selfish for thinking this way?

Over the past four or more years, my mum has been struggling with heavy drinking. My dad works away and is unable to intervene. When my mum is drunk, she becomes abusive and frightening. She hits me, insults me, and says hurtful things. She even goes out for hours and comes back covered in blood and urine. Sometimes she even threatens to expose herself to me if I don't comply with her demands. This has been going on since her dad passed away, and it's become too much for me to handle. I have a social worker who has been trying to help my mum, but she refuses to accept any assistance. Recently, I was told that I should prepare myself for the possibility of my mum taking her own life. I feel incredibly sad about all of this, and I feel like I have no family to turn to since my mum has pushed them away. I only have one friend I can confide in, but it doesn't seem to make much of a difference. I'm constantly feeling depressed and have even had thoughts of suicide. The stress is making me physically sick, and I often get so angry that I lock myself in my room to avoid hurting my mum. I feel completely out of control, both with myself and with the situation. What should I do?

I've been experiencing anxiety attacks since middle school, and it's been really confusing for me. Sometimes, I can be having a great time, and suddenly, I break down. I've also had some thoughts of suicide, which started in eighth grade but then stopped. Recently, they have been coming and going. I want to talk to my mom about getting help, but she's a psychiatrist, and I feel like she'll think she can handle it all on her own. I actually want to seek help from someone else, but I'm not sure how to communicate that to her. My anxiety is starting to affect my ability to enjoy myself or even sleep. I never know when it will strike or why.

Patient: Yesterday I received a diagnosis of paranoia and my doctor prescribed me Saphris. I can't help but worry that my paranoia will eventually develop into schizophrenia. I'm currently 16 years old and will turn 17 in two weeks. To make matters worse, I have an older sister who has schizophrenia, so I feel like I may be at a higher risk. Before being diagnosed with paranoia, I struggled with anxiety. I constantly felt like people were staring at me, laughing at me, or judging me at school. Whenever someone spoke to me, I always suspected they had ulterior motives. I'm just really anxious about the possibility of developing schizophrenia.

I recently started dating my best guy friend, but now we've decided to go back to being just friends. He told me that in his previous relationship, he only had physical attraction towards his ex-girlfriend and didn't actually love her or miss her when she wasn't around. He feels like he has similar feelings towards me, but with stronger emotions. He had a difficult relationship with his ex and even had thoughts of suicide. I'm wondering if it's possible for someone to not have emotional feelings for someone, like not missing them even when spending a lot of time together and being physically involved. Also, is there anything I can do to help him? He's never experienced love and he's 23, so I believe it's something everyone should experience.

I'm really concerned because I suspect that my daughter may have been sexually abused. I took her to see a doctor, but unfortunately it was too late to gather any physical evidence. The doctor and I had a conversation about it, and they mentioned that based on my 3-year-old daughter's behavior, they didn't believe she had been sexually abused.

As a child, I spent a significant amount of time isolating myself and becoming addicted to my computer. It consumed my life for six years, leading to feelings of virtual life dependency similar to a drug addiction. At 17, I finally saw myself in the mirror and realized I was obese. This triggered a period of anorexia, self-harm, and even a suicide attempt. Despite no longer engaging in those behaviors, I still struggle with constant thoughts of suicide at 20. The past continues to haunt me, as I have never had a job due to intense fear and anxiety. I struggle with basic interactions, such as making phone calls or ordering food, and I have no friends. I feel like a coward and wonder why I can't just function like everyone else. Can you help me understand?

I grew up in a household with a narcissistic mother, and it has had a significant impact on my life. When I was younger, around the ages of 6 to 8, my brother and I engaged in sexual behavior. It started with him coercing me into giving him oral sex, and eventually, I started asking for it in return, which he often obliged. There was also an incident where my brother and his friend involved me in a sexual act without reciprocation. My memory is foggy, but a friend recently mentioned that he witnessed my brother engaging in anal sex with me. I'm feeling confused and unsure if this qualifies as sexual abuse, especially considering the exchange of oral sex between my brother and me. It's been causing me a lot of emotional distress, and I would appreciate your prompt response.

In my relationship with my wife, I've noticed that she has a fear of being controlled. This fear stems from her childhood experiences of mild sexual abuse and lack of emotional support from her parents, especially since her father left when she was young. While we love each other and are committed, I've noticed that she tends to distance herself from me emotionally whenever we start getting closer. She accuses me of being controlling, citing past situations where my intentions were misunderstood. I believe that her fear of losing control and vulnerability is what hinders her from engaging in a deep emotional relationship with me. I want to understand how to approach our relationship in a healthy way without trying to change her, so that she can feel more comfortable and we can both be happier. Despite having four children together, my main concern is our relationship not progressing and remaining in this cycle of getting closer and then distancing. Your guidance would be greatly appreciated.

Lately, I've been struggling with a strong need to know where people live. It's like I can't fully trust someone unless I have that information. Knowing their address somehow puts my mind at ease and allows me to begin building trust with them, if they prove to be trustworthy.

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for almost a year now, and I'm starting to feel frustrated with his lack of intimacy. He attributes it to being raised differently and having a more traditional mindset. While he shows minimal affection, such as a goodbye kiss or occasionally holding hands, we rarely have sex and he avoids discussing it. He is also reluctant to hold or cuddle me, but shows affection towards our cat. When I bring up my concerns, he dismisses them as me being too needy. I feel lonely in my own relationship and don't know what to do. Is it me being too needy or is it him?

Over the past year and a half, I have been struggling with therapy. It starts off well and I find it helpful for a little while, but then we seem to reach a point where it's no longer effective and we have to stop. Unfortunately, the negative feelings eventually resurface, leading me to seek therapy again.

I have been in a tumultuous relationship with my husband for 14 years. We have separated multiple times over the years, but even after officially getting married, he continued to cheat on me with several women. I eventually left him and filed for divorce. However, we ended up getting back together after 5 years apart and it feels like we're in a constant state of turmoil. It's been really tough.

I have been dating my boyfriend for over 3 years now. He is 29 years old and has an 8-year-old daughter. I am 25 years old. When we first met, his daughter was 5 years old and we got along really well. However, about a year and a half into our relationship, I started experiencing intense feelings of jealousy towards her. I have sought help from two different therapists, but nothing seems to have alleviated these negative emotions. In fact, I'm afraid that my dislike for her is turning into hate. I now see her as an annoying little sister whom I can't stand to be around.

I'm 19 years old and I've been experiencing symptoms of anxiety for a while now. I've noticed that some people I know with similar symptoms have found relief through anxiety medication and therapy. The problem is, I don't think therapy is the right fit for me. I don't want to be forced into something that I don't believe will work for me. I have frequent panic attacks that make me feel dizzy, lightheaded, and sick, often accompanied by headaches. I also have random mood swings where I feel overwhelmed and anxious for no reason. I struggle to focus on anything and sometimes zone out. Sleep has become a big issue for me too - even after a busy day, I still struggle to fall asleep. I'm not sure what to do. I know medication isn't the first option, but I don't think counseling is right for me. Will the psychologist give me any other options?

I’m 20 years old and I have been feeling a strong urge to leave everything behind and start fresh. I don't have many responsibilities or obligations, and I feel like I didn't have a good start in life. I want to leave my current life, including my friends, family, and job, and relocate somewhere new. I don't want my family to worry or think that something bad happened to me, but I still feel like this is something I need to do. Is it wrong or abnormal to feel this way?

My three-year-old stepson has been experiencing frequent episodes of crying at random moments. He claims he can't control it and when we try to find out what's bothering him, he says nothing. We've noticed that he cries during meals, playtime, family time, and even when watching cartoons. Initially, we thought it might be attention-seeking behavior, but we haven't been giving him attention when he cries. Instead, we send him to his room and tell him to come out when he calms down. However, this approach hasn't been effective. He will be turning four next month and still struggles with communication. While he has had ear infections and tubes, we don't believe that's the cause of his crying. Can you provide any suggestions on how to handle this situation or what might be going on with him?

Patient: I have been diagnosed with Pure O OCD, and I suspect that I may also have Asperger's Syndrome. I'm really struggling with my OCD because I constantly have intrusive thoughts that bring me down, and I don't know how to calm myself down. The biggest challenge for me is that I have difficulty understanding what is happening in reality. For example, when I enter a room, I can't grasp what's going on unless someone explains it to me in clear and logical terms. In conversations, I find myself just staring at people's facial expressions and hand movements without actually understanding what they're saying. When it's my turn to speak, I struggle to find the right words and often feel like I don't even know what I'm talking about. It seems like other people can effortlessly understand what's happening without needing words. Additionally, I struggle to feel any emotions and have a hard time convincing myself that my intrusive thoughts are not true. I feel like I don't understand reality at all, even though it's all there. I really want to understand what's going on with me so that I can learn more about myself and improve. I don't even know what to call this blank mind or difficulty in understanding and speaking, and without addressing this, I feel helpless in my journey to recover from OCD. Thank you for listening to me.

My son, who is 5 years old, sometimes exhibits a concerning behavior during tantrums. Typically, his tantrums are normal for his age. However, occasionally, when he feels desperate, especially after escalating with one of us, he suddenly shifts from being angry and screaming to speaking in a small, obsequious voice and saying things like "I love you." This sudden transformation is extremely unsettling for my wife and me. We're concerned that there may be an underlying mental issue causing this behavior.

Last year around Christmas, my boyfriend and I went out drinking with friends. We had a blast. Unfortunately, when we got back to our hotel room, we got into a verbal fight and he ended up kicking me in the face. I was shocked and felt sick to my stomach. We had gotten into fights before while drinking but it had never turned physically violent before. He was horrified by his actions and we spent the next week talking about it. We agreed to quit drinking together. We eventually started drinking again recently. He also smokes tons of weed and hash oil and pops Vicodins every two weeks. He has a medical marijuana card for back pain. I prefer to drink wine and compared to last year, I have cut way back. My birthday was last week and I met up with several people for some birthday drinks. Well, he thinks I have a problem now and insists that I stop. I like drinking wine, it tastes good and calms me and I already have it under control. I have never asked him to cut down in his pill-popping or his weed intake. I feel that I deserve to drink a couple glasses of wine with friends on the weekend if I want, since I do not do anything else. I don't take medication, pills, or smoke weed or cigarettes. I said that if he wanted me clean and sober then he had to do so as well. He thinks it is unfair of me to ask him to quit smoking and defends it by saying that it is a legal medicine now. To me, it seems that he has replaced his drinking with Vicodins and hash oil. I just want to be able to enjoy my wine on the weekends and for him to get off my back.

A close friend of mine, who is a 44-year-old mother of two children and a grade school teacher, recently shared a distressing experience with me. On the last day of school before summer break, she called me from her car and seemed very upset. She revealed that she had put the class pet hamster in a baggie and held it closed until it died because no one could take care of it over the summer. This incident continues to deeply upset me whenever I think about it. Am I overreacting? How can I come to terms with this?

It seems like my daughter is feeling distant from our family and doesn't really care about us anymore. She's 21 years old and has an older sister. We moved from Boston to Dallas when she was younger, and while her sister was vocal about the transition, she was more quiet and seemed to adjust because she made friends. However, in middle school, she became withdrawn, especially with her father. We've tried talking to her during meals, but she won't open up. We've made many attempts to find out what's wrong, but we haven't been successful.

I recently ended a relationship with a younger guy from Egypt. Initially, things were great and we had a strong connection. We spent weekends together, shared thoughts and memories, and supported each other. Eventually, we ended up almost living together due to our strong attraction.

I am deeply concerned about my sister's overwhelming situation. She feels trapped in a difficult marriage due to her husband's health issues and financial difficulties. On top of that, she is dealing with her adult daughter's mental health struggles and legal issues regarding custody of her grandson. Additionally, she is the primary caregiver for our mother who was injured in a car accident. She works long hours in a stressful job and cannot afford counseling. I feel helpless and wonder how long she can endure this. Is there any help available for her?

I have been struggling with feeling anxious whenever I receive praise. This stems from my upbringing where my mom would deflect any praise I received and then snap at me later, accusing me of being conceited. Sadly, my mom has passed away since then, but I still find myself overwhelmed with anxiety when I am noticed for something positive. Strangely, after her death, I have been feeling trapped and paralyzed, making it incredibly challenging to put myself out there and pursue my potential. This anxiety has led me to choose work as a pet sitter and house cleaner, where I can fly under the radar and work alone. While there's nothing wrong with my current line of work, I recognize that my decision is driven by this unhealthy anxiety. Do you have any strategies or advice to help me overcome this issue? I appreciate any guidance you can provide.

I'm feeling a bit concerned about a situation at home. I'm a 17-year-old and I have a step-dad who acts in a way that makes me uncomfortable. He has asked me a few times if I could be his "secret girlfriend" and compliments my looks, saying he wants me to be comfortable with him. I'm not sure if this is normal or not.

Over the past few months, my mental health has deteriorated significantly. This has caused me to struggle both at home and at work. I feel like I am failing as a father, as I am unable to be there for my family in the way that I want to be. I fear that I may lose my ability to provide for them altogether.

I have severe asthma that is triggered by dogs. It doesn't matter what breed, any exposure to dogs causes me to have an anaphylactic episode. My children have grown up knowing about my condition, and unfortunately, my daughter witnessed one of these episodes in the past. My ex-husband has a history of downplaying the severity of my asthma and lacks empathy or sympathy towards my condition. He often expresses disbelief and questions the severity of my symptoms, despite my children and I experiencing them firsthand. My oldest son has been diagnosed with Asperger's, which may explain some of my ex-husband's difficulties with empathy.

Two and a half years ago, my father passed away. Since then, I've experienced periods of depression, but I initially attributed it to school pressure. Looking back, I'm not so sure anymore. While I used to have random bouts of crying when I missed him, lately I've been feeling numb when I think about him. Recently, I looked through old pictures of him and didn't feel any sadness or even a sense of okayness. It's almost as if the man in the pictures is a stranger to me. I also struggle to recall memories of him, which is concerning. Although I've been doing alright lately and haven't had any suicidal thoughts in months, I'm starting to wonder if it's because I've blocked everything related to my dad in my mind. I just want to know if this is a normal part of grieving or if there's something more going on. It really disturbs me to not feel anything about him at all. (age 19, from Dubai)

I am a 22-year-old medical student and I have been experiencing recurrent thoughts and conflicts, as well as compulsive checking behaviors. For example, while studying, I feel an impulse to check under my bed for any dropped pages. Even after checking, the impulse persists and I have to look under the bed again. I also find myself obsessing over past interactions, like when someone swore at me online and I keep thinking about why I didn't respond at the time. I constantly re-read messages to see if I actually stood up for myself. Additionally, I have a tendency to stare at words and images, examining every detail multiple times. It's becoming increasingly frustrating, especially with exams coming up. I would appreciate your advice on how to manage these thoughts and compulsions.

I am a 24-year-old man who has been working in the engineering field. I have been having a difficult time adjusting to my job and it's starting to take a toll on my mental and physical health. I often experience severe panic attacks when I think about work or my future. I have sought professional help in the past but eventually stopped going. I am feeling very overwhelmed and unsure about what to do. I want to explore other career options, but I worry that it may be too late and that I won't be able to find contentment in any job. I don't necessarily need to be happy, I just know that working in an office environment isn't right for me. Can you give me some guidance?

Ever since I had my youngest child (5 months), I have developed an intense fear of going into anaphylactic shock. This fear specifically revolves around food, even foods that I have eaten many times before without any issues. I have never experienced an allergic reaction to food in the past, and I cannot identify any triggers for this fear. I am wondering if there are any natural methods to overcome this phobia without relying on medication. I have become very cautious with my food choices, and I mainly stick to drinking water or cola.

Patient: Around April/May, I started experiencing chest pains that lasted for a couple of weeks. When I brought it up to my doctor, he diagnosed it as gastroenteritis and attributed it to a warm weather virus or exercise. He also mentioned that stress could worsen the symptoms. I have generalized anxiety disorder, so stress is a constant presence in my life. Since it was my first time seeing this doctor, I didn't disclose my anxiety because I didn't think it was necessary and I prefer not to share that information with others.

I have been feeling really down lately because of the way my husband treats me. He often makes hurtful jokes that make me feel bad about myself, and when he's angry, he becomes really nasty and rude towards me. It seems like he gets mad about small things that don't go his way. When we argue, he wants to be left alone, but I feel like I need him with me and end up begging for reconciliation or a hug. I even end up apologizing, even when it's not my fault, just to make things better. He says really hurtful things like I'm begging like a fool and he doesn't want to see or listen to me. I cry a lot and it feels like nothing is worth it if we're apart. I want to learn how to let go and not care about his moods or the way he treats me when he's mad. I also find it difficult to talk to him about my feelings because he gets annoyed. I'm really miserable right now and I don't want to live like this anymore. Can you please help me?

Thank you for sharing your experiences and concerns with me. It sounds like you have been through a lot of traumatic incidents in your past, and it's understandable that they have had a significant impact on you. It's important to remember that what happened to you was not your fault and that you did not deserve to be treated that way. It's also common for survivors of trauma to feel a sense of guilt or shame, but it's important to remember that you did nothing wrong.

In the past, I have experienced infidelity in my relationships and have witnessed it within my own family. Currently, I am in a new relationship with someone I am developing strong feelings for, but I am feeling insecure and fearful that he may cheat on me too. It was surprising for me to feel this way because I usually project confidence. When people found out about our relationship, a particular female coworker messaged him, which made me uncomfortable due to her history of causing drama. I'm worried she might try to create issues between us.

Patient: I've been experiencing these persistent voices in my head that have started to become more negative and bothersome. It's like a constant battle between my rational thoughts and this "little voice" that tells me otherwise. I don't know if it's depression, but I feel empty even though I know I have opportunities and a decent life. Sometimes, I even question if the good things are real. I've looked up different diagnoses, but I see similarities in each of them. Can you shed some light on this?

I've been experiencing some challenges in my daily life and I'm wondering if I might have Asperger's syndrome. Here are some of the issues I've noticed: I have difficulty making eye contact, especially with new people. I tend to have limited social interactions and struggle to understand sarcasm. I'm sensitive to loud noises, bright lights, and tags on my clothing. My short-term memory is not great, but my long-term memory is quite good. I find it hard to tell how people are feeling and often feel emotionally detached. I can only express myself well when I have a pen and paper. I have obsessions and enjoy learning and sharing random facts. I engage in certain movements, like tapping my fingers together and rocking, to calm myself down. I easily get overwhelmed by small things. Following indirect instructions is challenging for me. Being in crowds is difficult. While I don't repeat what people say, I do trace their words compulsively. I'm often told that I seem to be in my own world. I'm very honest, even if it can come across as hurtful unintentionally. There are certain words I refuse to say because they feel awful to me. I find it easier to handle hard work than easy tasks. I don't pay much attention to fashion trends. While I don't have a strict schedule, I do have certain patterns in how I do things.

I have been struggling with nail biting since I was around 3 or 4 years old, as reported by my family. I've made attempts to quit on and off since I was 10 years old. I've tried various methods I found online, like fake nails, band aids, rubber bands, bitter nail polish, and using a "buddy" for motivation. I've even tried stopping one finger at a time and regularly manicuring and filing my nails. I've managed to quit cold turkey twice, but it only lasted about 2 weeks. I believe the habit started due to the high levels of stress in my home environment and ongoing personal issues until the end of my sophomore year. I have since eliminated many of my major stressors, although some unavoidable ones remain like school, work, and daily responsibilities. I have successfully completed counseling for depression, anxiety, and PTSD, but I am still taking two medications daily as mood stabilizers. Overall, I have become a more easy-going and calm person, but the nail biting habit remains deeply ingrained. I've come across information online that suggests nail biting may fall within the OCD spectrum. While my previous counselor was aware of the nail biting, it wasn't a major focus. However, I now feel that the habit has become severe enough to seek additional support. I don't want to self-diagnose or exaggerate the issue, but I am aware of the negative impact it has on my hands, teeth, and overall health due to the bacteria I ingest from biting. I frequently experience bleeding, and I feel like I've lost control over the habit. While I'm tired of seeing doctors due to my other mental health issues, I'm open to gaining insight. Is it necessary for me to see a doctor regarding this matter?

I have experienced a series of traumatic events, including the deaths of my parents, grandmother, cousin, and other family members and friends. I have been feeling numb, angry, anxious, and irritable. I have been relying on substances like marijuana and alcohol to cope. My boyfriend has been supportive, but I find myself lashing out at him and feeling resentful towards him. I have also noticed a pattern of negative events happening in my life. I feel overwhelmed and unsure of how to move forward. My boyfriend suggests therapy, but I am hesitant. I don't want my relationship to suffer, but I also don't want to live in a constant state of depression.

As a child, I experienced two significant episodes of anxiety. The first occurred when I was 9 years old, and the second when I was 12. Both times, my anxiety was triggered by my fear of religion, the afterlife, and death. These fears were brought on by a junior camp counselor who shared information that scared me and made me think about death and being separated from my family. I would often cry and feel overwhelmed during these episodes, which lasted for around two weeks to a month each.

I feel like my emotions are constantly suppressed, and it's really starting to affect both me and my relationship with my spouse. Living with my in-laws has made it difficult for me to express myself because they don't always accommodate my needs for privacy and personal space. As a result, my anger has been building up, and my tolerance level has significantly decreased. I've even resorted to sending nasty messages to my husband, blaming his family for their irritating behavior. However, this is causing arguments between us. Additionally, my husband threatens me that if I speak out against his family, I'll have to leave our shared house. It's worth mentioning that we have our own place, but we don't live there because my husband feels a strong obligation to his parents. I'm feeling lost, depressed, and suffocated. Can you please help me?

I am really concerned about my 12-year-old son's behavior. He recently found some inappropriate videos online, and I discovered one of them where a girl was being mistreated. I had a conversation with him about how this is not normal or right. However, I've now discovered that he inserted the handle of a bathroom plunger in his own rectum. He claims it was a one-time occurrence and that it hurt, and he won't do it again. I'm scared and don't know what to do. I don't want this to escalate.

I am really struggling with my wife's diagnosed paranoia and chronic anxiety. Lately, she has become increasingly paranoid about anything I say, and it seems like she doesn't trust me anymore. This has led to explosive bursts of anger, and I feel like I'm constantly walking on eggshells around her. I love her and want to support her, but I don't know how to do it without upsetting her. How can I cope with her condition and show her that I genuinely care and want to help?

I'm really concerned about my wife's recent behavior. She's 33 years old and has a history of being diagnosed with ADD and anxiety. She was previously on Methadone for 6 years and Xanax for 2 years, but she's currently in a program to come off both medications. However, since March, she has been experiencing increasingly paranoid thoughts. She believes that someone she met online is hacking into our computers and email. Despite my efforts to secure our devices, she remains convinced that it's happening. Her paranoia has escalated to the point where she now believes there is a large team of people following her everywhere she goes and constantly monitoring her. She thinks our house is bugged with hidden cameras, our phones are tapped, and our cars have tracking devices. She even believes that certain TV and radio commercials are sending her coded messages. This paranoia extends to everyday situations, such as thinking the cashier at the grocery store is one of these people. She feels constantly watched and followed, even when traveling. She recently flew to her current location and believes there was someone on the plane who is now watching her there. I'm really hoping that her medication withdrawal is causing these symptoms, but even with a decrease in her dosage, she continues to believe these things. It's gotten to the point where she can't even use the bathroom without feeling watched. I'm at a loss for how to support her because she gets extremely angry with me for not believing her. She feels like I'm dismissing her reality, even though many of the things she says aren't logically possible. She keeps this all to herself and nobody else is aware of what she's going through. Our family is deeply concerned, and any advice or guidance would be greatly appreciated.

It sounds like you have been through a lot of difficult experiences with your family and relationships. It's understandable that you would feel a lot of shame and hatred surrounding these situations. It's important to remember that you are not defined by the opinions of others, and that you deserve to be treated with respect and understanding.

I'm really struggling with how to handle my mother's behavior and parenting techniques. It's been difficult because she puts on a facade of being a caring and attentive parent in public, but behind closed doors, it's a different story. There's a lot more information I could share, but I'm limited by the word count. Can you offer any guidance?

I'm a 15-year-old from the United Arab Emirates, and I believe I may be experiencing depression and other mental health issues. While I know online tests are not a professional diagnosis, they have given me an idea that something might be wrong. It all started on Christmas when I suddenly felt sad for no reason and lost interest in activities. Since then, my symptoms have worsened. I've had a mental breakdown, and although I went to one therapy session, I haven't continued. I'm failing in school, distancing myself from my family, and avoiding socializing. It's summer now, and I prefer staying in bed all day rather than going out or spending time with friends and family. I've been experiencing symptoms of depression, bipolar disorder, and anxiety, but I'm not completely certain. I feel sad and want to cry constantly, and I don't know what to do. Can you please help me? Thank you in advance.

Hello, I wanted to talk to you about some concerns I've been having. Lately, I've been experiencing strong urges to harm someone I dislike. These thoughts come to me randomly, but especially when I'm angry. I find myself making detailed plans for how I could poison them or make it look like an accident. Additionally, I've noticed that I have become quite distant from others and my social life has suffered as a result. While I enjoy the solitude, I also feel unhappy about it at times. Recently, I've started talking to myself in a manner that resembles a toddler, and many people have trouble understanding me unless I make an effort. I also have a sort of personal religion where I believe I am a god. When I'm falling asleep, I feel the need to lie down in a specific way within ten seconds or else I believe an evil ghost will see me. However, after that, I feel protected by my own guard ghost and don't have to worry. I have also had some troubling hallucinations in the past, such as seeing beheaded bodies with their heads beside them staring at me in the middle of the night, which would wake me up abruptly. I've also seen a red-tinted apple with a bird's mouth that made a scary noise and chased me. These experiences have made me question if what I'm going through is normal. I would appreciate your help and guidance.

I recently entered into a casual relationship with a male friend due to my desire for affection and physical attention after being single for over two years. Initially, this arrangement was satisfying, but as time went on, I developed deeper feelings for my friend. However, I've noticed a decrease in my sexual desire and difficulty reaching orgasm. My partner also feels unsatisfied if I don't experience pleasure. This situation has happened before in a previous relationship, and it's causing me to feel defective. I would appreciate any suggestions to address this and prevent the relationship from falling apart.

I'm a 28-year-old female from the UK, and I've been diagnosed with Hypothyroidism. I've been feeling really down lately because I'm overweight and I tend to turn to comfort eating when I feel this way. It's become a vicious cycle where I eat because I'm down, which makes me feel even worse, so I eat again. I've had a history of bad relationships, with my last boyfriend pressuring me to be a size zero and not accepting me for who I am. This has caused me to lose self-confidence and I hate the way I look. I try to bring my gym kit to work with the intention of working out, but by the end of the day, I'm just too tired and all I want to do is sleep. I want to regain control of my life and stop using food to fill my sorrow. I feel completely powerless right now. Can you please help me?

I am a 21-year-old with two children and engaged to their father. I have been struggling with intrusive thoughts about a sexual encounter that supposedly happened when I was four years old. I also feel deep shame and disgust for engaging in inappropriate behavior with my cousin when I was 11 years old. I have a history of self-harm starting at the age of 11, which I partly blamed on my parents' constant fighting and my father's abuse. I am currently seeking attention from my fiance, but often feel unsatisfied. I have trust issues and want to find true happiness with my fiance and for the sake of our children. I come from a family with a history of bipolar disorder and depression.

I'm 17 years old and it seems like people view me as a sociopath. I've always been in trouble, getting kicked out of school for drugs and fighting. But I've always managed to talk my way out of serious trouble and avoid legal consequences. I've been told that I have a way with words and can manipulate people easily. I also admit to being a pathological liar and not feeling any guilt or remorse for my actions. I'm a light drug addict and have struggled with anger issues. I change my interests frequently because I get bored easily. Do I sound like a psychopath? Do I need help?

Thank you for providing this platform to seek guidance. I am a 26-year-old individual who grew up in a tumultuous environment. My parents recently divorced, but their relationship was always filled with various forms of abuse. While my father didn't physically harm us, I believe there was emotional and verbal abuse present. I have come to terms with my troubled childhood, but I struggle with forming relationships, both platonic and romantic. I am also unsure about my life direction and worry that these issues are holding me back. I try to avoid thinking about what happened, but it often leads to tears and anger. I feel a deep need for my father to apologize, even though he has never acknowledged his behavior. Can you guide me on steps to address these challenges, while respecting my desire to handle this on my own? Thank you for your assistance.

Hello counselor, I come from a family in India where I am the eldest daughter. My father is a business man and my mother is a housewife. I have two younger sisters, so there are five of us in the house. Unfortunately, disputes between my parents have been happening since my childhood and seem to have escalated over time. Now, all five of us are constantly quarreling over small issues, and it has even resorted to physical violence like slapping each other.

Over the past two years, I have been engaging in a pattern of binging and purging as a result of my extreme depression. Additionally, I have been restricting my food intake, leading to significant weight loss. Despite seeking therapy for my depression, my struggles with food have not been addressed. Currently, I continue to engage in bingeing and purging behaviors, while also severely restricting my food intake and exercising excessively. This has negatively impacted my relationships, as friends have noticed my purging and someone I liked has given me an ultimatum to seek help. I experience high levels of stress in various areas of my life and struggle with low self-esteem and body image issues. Additionally, being blind and albino adds to the complexity of my challenges. While my grades are good and I strive for perfection, I question if I truly need help or if people are simply jealous of me.

My cousin is a 56-year-old woman who has experienced multiple divorces and has had several serious relationships, but none lasting longer than 2 to 3 years. Recently, she became unemployed, which has been a significant source of stress for her as her line of work is not easy to find. I've noticed that she has been feeling very isolated in her home and when she has conversations with friends, she appears to be crying uncontrollably or feeling extremely sad. Lately, she has been having delusions that her close friends have implanted magnets in her body, which she believes are connected to a national database for law offenders. She also believes she has been sexually violated and has filed a police report. When I visited her, she seemed like a completely different person - fragile, timid, and skeptical, firmly convinced of her allegations. However, when I visited her again before leaving the state, she was back to her normal self, but had a new "friend" whom no one else in our family or her circle of friends has ever met. I recall her being somewhat paranoid in the past, worried about food being poisoned by a brother-in-law. I'm concerned and would like to understand what's happening to her. How can I help her?

Over the past three years, I have been struggling with severe depression and anorexia. As a result, I have constantly felt exhausted and irritable. However, in the past six months, I have been experiencing additional symptoms. I feel extreme fatigue to the point where even walking is difficult. I become dizzy whenever I stand up, and I often feel detached from myself. I also have a strange ringing in my ear and a lack of emotions, except for anger. Although I haven't been struggling with eating disorder issues or self-harm lately, my dependence on drugs has significantly increased. I have difficulty maintaining conversations and frequently experience migraines. I have gained more than 10 pounds, but I don't seem to care about it or anything else. It's as if everything feels like a dream. My grades at school have dropped dramatically, which is unusual for me as I usually do well academically. I'm feeling scared and confused about what is happening. Additionally, my insomnia is worsening, and I have started seeing things again, although I'm not frightened by it anymore.

I've been feeling really overwhelmed lately. I have a lot of responsibilities at work and at home, and it's starting to feel like I can't keep up. I'm constantly stressed and anxious, and I'm finding it hard to relax or enjoy anything. I don't know what to do.

I have been living in San Francisco for two years, where I met my ex-partner who is from Turkey over a year ago. Initially, everything seemed fine, despite a few issues that I attributed to cultural differences. However, as time went on, things started to escalate. He became extremely controlling, forbidding me from seeing my friends, checking my phone daily, and expressing intense jealousy. He would dictate how I should dress and look, often resorting to yelling and even physical violence when I stood up for myself. He would also break my belongings and threaten to move out whenever there was a disagreement. Although this relationship ended a few months ago, he continues to exert control over me, sending threatening emails and accusing me of infidelity. I still have feelings for him, but I know we can't be together. I just want to understand what might be going on with him psychologically. Can you offer any insights that could help me understand his behavior? I also want to find ways to help myself heal and move on. Thank you for any guidance you can provide.

Patient: I have a close friend who became my romantic partner about a year ago. Recently, he cheated on me with a colleague, and I feel extremely hurt because we were also best friends. Additionally, he has been engaging in destructive behaviors such as excessive drinking, smoking, poor performance at work, uncontrolled spending, and getting into trouble. He's been displaying mood swings and expressing feelings of guilt, even saying he doesn't deserve to live. I'm torn because I care for him and want to help, but I'm also deeply hurt. I suspect he may have a personality disorder, which sometimes elicits compassion from me, but other times I feel angry and hurt. I would appreciate guidance on how to handle this situation. Should I approach him? Should I be angry or compassionate? Thank you.

Patient's Statement: It seems like there have been ongoing conflicts and issues among your three sons. Your eldest son, along with his wife and daughter, have been living with you for three years after experiencing the tragic loss of their son to SIDS six years ago. It appears that they have been struggling to move forward since then. On the other hand, your middle son has been distant and unwilling to communicate with you, and he has also been keeping your grandson away from you. Additionally, your youngest son, who is now 26 years old, has recently broken his silence and shared something very shocking. He revealed that your eldest son had sexually abused him at the age of four, in front of your middle son, who was five at the time. This has left you feeling extremely overwhelmed and unsure of what steps to take. You are concerned for the safety and well-being of your sons, particularly the eldest, who has expressed thoughts of self-harm in the past.

My partner and I have been together for 5 years and became parents really young. We were 18 at the time. Currently, we have been constantly arguing over the same issues. We have tried communicating and working things out, but for some reason we continuing fighting. We can go as far as two whole weeks without saying one word to each other unless it is about our daughter. Now there is past cheating and hurting we have done to each other; which caused plenty of respect to go down the drain. I have offered a break and some space to maybe ease the tension we have, but he says that a break is not an option, its either we completely split or try working it out. However, working it out only lasts about two days and then we are back at it again. We are not sure what would be the best option for us. We have tried many different things to make our relationship better, but have failed. Would it be best for us to end our relationship before we end up in really bad terms or is there something else we can possibly try that will help our relationship?

Our daughter is 6 years old and recently received a large brown stuffed bear named Chubbie as a Valentine's gift from cupid. She has developed a strong attachment to the bear and truly believes that it is real. She engages in long, detailed conversations with the bear and becomes very emotional if anyone suggests that it is not real or tries to take it away from her. Additionally, she often plays "brother and sister" with her father, pretending to go to school on a bus and play classroom. We had tried to have another child after she was born, but due to a medical condition, we were unable to. It seems like she wants a brother, and I'm wondering if the bear is fulfilling a void for her. Will this create anxiety for her in the future? Could this emotional attachment to a stuffed animal cause her to become emotionally detached? I love her dearly and want her to be happy. We spend quality time together and play lots of games. She is a wonderful child, and I just want to understand if this is a healthy coping mechanism for her. Thank you for your help!

I am really concerned about my mother's well-being. She has been struggling with depression for a while now, and she doesn't have a strong support system. My brother also suffers from depression, and my mother's only sister is going through the same thing. On top of that, my mother has experienced multiple significant losses, including the deaths of both her parents and two divorces. She tries her best to take care of herself financially and mentally, but things seem to be getting worse. One major setback has been her inability to find work after leaving her previous job due to health and mental abuse. It has been two years since she last worked, and her financial situation is deteriorating rapidly. I'm really worried because my husband and I are not in a position to support her financially. I feel lost and don't know how to help her. Any advice would be greatly appreciated.

I have been in a serious relationship with this guy for 2 years now. He is 28 and I am 29. We met while working in South Africa where we both currently reside. As far as our relationship goes, we get along quite well but he has such an unhealthy relationship with his mother. The more I get to know him the more I see it and it scares me.

I met my wife in the Middle East and we moved to the US in 2013. However, my wife constantly accuses me of cheating on her. She believes this because someone had been in our room and engaged in sexual activity while we were at work, just two weeks before we left the Middle East for the US.

Two years ago, my girlfriend and I started a relationship that was different from any we had experienced before. It began as a friendship, and we quickly fell in love. We would constantly communicate through phone calls and text messages, not because we had to, but because we genuinely wanted to. We even started making plans for our future together, believing that our love would last forever. However, when my girlfriend started university a few months into our relationship, she became worried that it might put a strain on our connection. We both made a promise to each other that we would do whatever it takes to stay together and overcome any challenges that come our way.

My mother was involved in a car accident in South Africa a few years ago, resulting in permanent damage to her back and neck. As a result, she experiences chronic pain and has difficulty sleeping. Additionally, she has developed unhealthy habits, relying on technology and consuming only dinner, soda, and hot chocolate. It's concerning to observe her deteriorating health, and her doctors have also expressed their concerns.

I've been feeling overwhelmed and unappreciated lately. My grandmother recently passed away after being in the hospital for five days due to a stroke. During her time in the hospital, my mother and I took turns caring for her. However, my sister went on vacation during this difficult time. Now that my grandmother has passed, I find myself helping my mother with funeral arrangements and taking care of her apartment. The issue is that my mother has expressed her desire to take my sister on various trips and adventures, while seemingly disregarding all the support my husband and I have provided. I feel hurt and overlooked, as though my mother doesn't truly value me. I'm at a point where I want to sell our house and move out of state, as my husband and I have been wanting to do for years. But I'm torn because of my mother's health issues. I just don't know if I can continue being taken for granted and treated as a doormat.

I'm a 16-year-old from the U.S. and I've been struggling with some mental health issues lately. I think I might have a few disorders, but I'm not sure how to bring it up to my mom and actually go see a therapist. Part of me is hesitant and doesn't want to go through with it.

Lately, I've been experiencing a lot of anger, rudeness, and sadness for no apparent reason, and it's starting to affect my relationship with my partner. We've been together for a long time and have a great relationship, but I'm finding it difficult to handle any changes that come our way. I lash out when I feel threatened or insecure, which only distances us further. I've also been unemployed recently, which has given me a lot of free time to overthink and get angry at my partner for no valid reasons. I don't want to ruin our relationship with my insecurities and negative behavior. It upsets me even more that my partner blames himself for my unhappiness. I need help understanding why I focus on the negative aspects and how to change this pattern.

My wife, who is 43 years old, becomes upset whenever we discuss cleanliness. Despite a therapist's opinion that it is not OCD, it seems to be related to her upbringing and values. For instance, she gets upset when our in-laws come home and don't immediately take a shower. She goes to the extent of cleaning the areas they have been in, like the sofa and the floor. Whenever I try to talk to her about it, she becomes very stressed. This distress has been building up for a long time, as my mother, who is a midwife, initially thought it was OCD.

Over the past few months, I have been going through a really difficult time in my life. It all started when I was 14 and began experiencing depression, which has lasted for the past three years. Recently, I had an unsettling experience while I was out with friends - I was drinking and possibly using drugs. During that time, I started having intrusive thoughts about a neighbor coming out to harm me and my friends because we were playing pranks on his house. These thoughts were so disturbing and I couldn't get rid of them. I became worried that there was something seriously wrong with me and that I might become violent.

I am 22 years old and my parents have been very controlling in my life. Despite not being religious, they strongly adhere to traditional Mexican beliefs. They believe that I should get married before moving out of the house, that men have more freedom simply because they are men, and that as children, we have no say in anything.

Thank you for reaching out. I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for a while now and I've noticed that he has been struggling with depression. It seems to stem from a difficult childhood and he tends to stress about everything. I've noticed that he often spaces out and it's difficult to grab his attention. He has shared with me that he feels empty and alone, and that I'm the only person he confides in about his feelings. His parents and friends are unaware of what he's going through. I really want to support him and help him find happiness again. Can you please provide some guidance?

Patient's statement (rewritten): Throughout my life, I have always felt like I didn't quite fit in. As a child, I struggled to connect with others and felt different. I had a happy upbringing in a loving family, but I also had a strong sense of femininity from a young age, which I didn't fully understand at the time. I suppressed these feelings due to societal expectations and felt embarrassed when questioned about my interests and behaviors. When puberty hit, I experienced significant emotional turmoil, becoming withdrawn, depressed, and apathetic towards everything. I started taking anti-depressants at 14, and around the age of 16, I began to realize that I might be transgender. However, this realization hasn't brought me any relief or clarity, and I'm now 19, feeling lost and isolated.

I have been taking care of my grandson since he was 3 months old because my daughter-in-law has been struggling with mental health issues. It has been challenging for me to deal with her behavior and I feel uncertain about what steps to take. Initially, I was taken aback by her parenting and wondered if she was irresponsible, abusive, or had substance abuse problems.

During high school, I had a wonderful relationship with a guy named Dude. We were together for about 2.5 years, from my senior year of high school to the end of my freshman year of college. Dude is my age and he's a military man, but he's also a goofball and we had a great connection. However, he broke up with me when a family member passed away and he needed some space. We didn't talk for a while, but now, after several years, we've reconnected and are great friends again.

Hi, I’m a seventeen year old girl who is concerned about my mental health. I come from a household where my parents drink alcohol. When my dad is drunk, he becomes violent and overly strict, leading to frequent fights. On the other hand, my mom becomes emotionally distant and indifferent, leaving me feeling threatened and unsupported. This pattern of drinking and sobriety has been going on since I was five years old. In the past, my dad used to physically punish me, even for reasons I didn't fully understand. Now, at seventeen, my parents are drinking again and I'm experiencing new symptoms. I have intense headaches from 8am to 10am upon waking up, and I find myself crying easily. I also have pent-up anger with no outlet. Sometimes, I have dark thoughts while driving, but deep down, I don't truly want to die. I just yearn for more independence, but my parents are overly restrictive. I don't do drugs, but I occasionally drink beer. I feel trapped and lonely, as my friends have more freedom than I do. I often feel overwhelmed by sadness. Can you offer any advice on how to cope with these feelings and regain control? Thank you.

I'm a 23-year-old male from Serbia and I'm feeling a lot of depression and sadness inside me. I've never had sex and I've never been in a real relationship. I often feel like the girls who are interested in me aren't good enough for me, but the ones I'm interested in never give me a chance. Sometimes I'm not even sure if I truly like the girl or not.

Based on the information you've shared, it seems like your boyfriend has been experiencing some significant ups and downs in his mood and behavior. It's understandable that you're feeling confused and uncertain about the situation. It's important to recognize that I cannot diagnose your boyfriend or predict his future actions. However, I can offer some general insights and suggestions.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for two and a half years. In December 2013, I gave birth to our child. However, I experienced postpartum depression just a week after giving birth. During that time, I made a mistake. My ex-boyfriend reached out to my mom, expressing that he missed me. I responded to him on Facebook, confessing my love and missing him. Unfortunately, my boyfriend discovered these messages when he went through my Facebook account.

I'm going to be seventeen in a few months, and I've been struggling with mental health issues for several years now. I've dealt with self-harm, suicidal thoughts, anger towards myself and others, and more. My parents are unaware because I didn't want to burden them. I've tried to help myself as a minor, but I still feel like something isn't right. I don't feel normal, and sometimes it feels like I'm just faking being positive. Am I overreacting or should I seek help?

I have struggled with a compulsive picking behavior for as long as I can remember. It started with picking scabs as a child, which resulted in excessive bleeding and scarring. Then I began picking and biting my lips, leading to constant sores and scabs. In middle school, I started picking at my acne, which left unsightly scars. Recently, I have been picking at the inside of my ears and even the soles of my feet. It's become a way for me to cope with anxiety, although I don't do it intentionally to harm myself. I feel disgusted and overwhelmed by these behaviors and I'm seeking help.

I have been carrying the weight of my brother's abuse for the past seven years. It's been difficult because I've kept it a secret to protect my family from having to choose sides. Now, I feel like I'm falling apart and have no one to talk to because everyone acts like it never happened. My brother even hires me to babysit his daughter and acts like everything is normal. It's driving me crazy. I'm scared that if people find out, they'll reject me or treat me differently. Sometimes I question if it actually happened or if I'm just making it up because my family acts so nonchalant about it. I want to move on from this, but I don't know how. Even reaching out for help feels like a struggle. It took me a month to write this because of the panic and self-doubt. I want to live my life without this burden, but I'm lost.

I'm really struggling with my mother's mental health issues. She has been diagnosed with schizophrenia and severe bipolar disorder for several years. Ever since my dad divorced her, she has been spending all the money she received from the divorce settlement. Recently, my mother has been living with my grandparents, but they can no longer handle the stress and financial burden. They have moved into an assisted living center. Now, my mother has returned to my hometown with very little money left. She wants to bring our family back together, but she is difficult to be around and refuses to work or support herself. We are running out of money and she is at risk of becoming homeless. Unfortunately, she is unwilling to commit herself or accept help, as she believes we are trying to control her. Additionally, local laws prevent us from involuntarily committing her. My family and I are going through a very tough time, and it feels like we have exhausted all our options. I'm not sure what to do anymore. Can you help us explore any other options that may be available?

I'm currently in my second year of high school and I feel like my mother treats me as if I'm still in elementary school. We have a lot of misunderstandings and don't see eye to eye. One of the reasons for this is that my mom grew up in Somalia and experienced her teenage years there, whereas I am a teenager growing up in America. This cultural difference makes it difficult for her to understand my perspective and where I'm coming from.

For the past seven years, I have been experiencing severe sleep disturbances. I struggle to sleep for more than three hours every few days, and even when I do sleep, it feels like I'm just lying awake. I've been trying to improve my sleep, but nothing seems to work. Additionally, I have been experiencing violent twitches and spasms. If I go without sleep for too long, I start hearing a muffled voice that tells me terrible things and makes me feel worthless. There have been instances where I went a whole week without sleep, and when I finally passed out, I woke up screaming and feeling like someone was physically harming me. I have also been having visual hallucinations, seeing blood, and bodies in flashes. One time, I opened a door and saw decapitated heads on the floor, screaming in pain. I have fallen to my knees in fear because I see disturbing images whenever I blink. I am unsure how much longer I can endure this. Do you think it would be helpful for me to check into a mental hospital?

I recently met a girl from Australia and we've been getting to know each other for about a month now. We were in bed together, just fooling around, when she suddenly had a freak out. I stopped her and asked her what was wrong, and she revealed that she had been sexually abused by a family member in the past. I reassured her that it's okay and I want to help her. We eventually slept together, but she's now feeling dirty and hating herself. I really want to support her, but I don't know how. Can you please advise me on what I can say or do to help her without seeking outside help?

I have been struggling with a lack of self-motivation, particularly when it comes to tasks like housework. I'm curious if my past experiences could be contributing to this issue. Growing up, I endured abuse from my brother, which included mental, physical, and sexual abuse. My parents discovered this when I was 9, leading to their divorce. I have no memories from that time until I was 16, but I've been told that I experienced beatings and intentional trauma. My mother attempted to put me in counseling, but I refused to participate. Additionally, I went through a period of abuse from my soon-to-be husband, but he received therapy, and we participated in a group therapy course together on managing emotions. We have now been happily married for 11 years. I also struggle with anxiety, fears, and insomnia, and while I had depression in the past, I haven't experienced it in the past two years. Is it possible that my lack of self-motivation is linked to these experiences? And can therapy help improve my self-motivation?

I have been experiencing a strong attraction to death lately. I've been spending a lot of time researching about violent events and individuals like Sid Vicious and the Columbine High School shooting. It's intriguing to me, and I don't feel disgusted by their actions. I also have a history of violent outbursts when my depression was at its worst, but I haven't acted on those impulses in almost a year. However, I still catch myself thinking about violent things and it scares me. It's like a dark pleasure that distracts me from the kind person I know I am. I'm currently in therapy, but it's difficult for me to talk about this with my therapist.

I am from India and I recently sought advice about my relationship with my boyfriend who has OCD. The therapist suggested that I end the relationship because it has become emotionally abusive. However, we have been together for a year and it's not easy for me to just forget about him and start over.

I've been feeling incredibly overwhelmed and stressed lately. My husband and I are going through financial difficulties and we had to move in with my in-laws, who have a very different personality and communication style than I do. I've been setting boundaries with them to protect my mental health, but my husband sometimes struggles to understand and respect those boundaries. On top of that, I'm 13 weeks pregnant and experiencing a lot of physical pain and discomfort. Recently, my husband came to my workplace in a panic about our bills and I got frustrated with him because I was already dealing with so much. I told him to stop and reminded him why I set those boundaries in the first place. This has been happening quite frequently and I'm finding it harder to tolerate. Yesterday, during my break, he refused to listen to my opinion and it escalated into an argument. I became angry and told him I was done speaking to him. Later, I tried to explain to him that I was in a lot of pain and needed his understanding, but he continued to focus on his own emotions. I reached my breaking point and took care of my physical pain by making a splint for my foot. I told him that I couldn't tolerate any more discussions and that my focus was solely on managing my pain.

I'm facing a challenge that has been causing me a lot of distress lately. I'm from Portugal and I spend most of my workdays searching for answers on the internet, but I can't seem to find anything. This is seriously affecting my productivity at work.

Counselor: It sounds like you and your boyfriend have been dealing with trust issues throughout your relationship. Both of you have engaged in behaviors that have broken trust, which has created a cycle of lies and mistrust between you. It's understandable that you're feeling confused and unsure about what to do next.

I'm feeling overwhelmed with the stress of being a first-time parent. My partner and I are both exhausted from the sleep deprivation that comes with taking care of our 10-month-old daughter. I'm struggling to cope with all of these emotions.

Patient: I've been in a relationship for five years with a man who was diagnosed with schizoaffective disorder, depression with psychotic features. Overall, his disorder doesn't significantly affect our relationship. However, he struggles with maintaining cleanliness in his living space and taking proactive steps towards positive growth. Currently, he's making progress by going back to school and actively seeking better job opportunities.

I recently had a conversation with my friend who expressed some concerning thoughts and feelings. He mentioned not wanting me to get him a birthday present because he considered himself a "bad person" and felt guilty about me spending money on him. However, the conversation took a dark turn when he started talking about wanting to harm others as a form of revenge. I tried my best to talk him out of it, but he seemed persistent and even mentioned owning guns. This situation has caused my anxiety to escalate, and I'm really worried about my friend. I care about him deeply and want to help, but he seems resistant to any support I offer. I'm at a loss for what to do.

I've been struggling with depression, anxiety, and mood swings since I was a child. In high school, I resorted to self-harm and in my early 20s, I had major suicidal thoughts and attempted suicide a few times. I've tried using drugs, alcohol, and seeking validation from others, but nothing seems to help. I struggle to form emotional connections with people, and I constantly battle intrusive thoughts and voices in my head. Lately, I've noticed myself spiraling into a downward pattern and feeling disconnected from the world. Unfortunately, I don't have insurance and won't have coverage for another six months. I'm also in the process of finding a new job. I'm in desperate need of help as I carry a lot of pain inside and feel like I'm slowly dying. Any assistance you can provide would be greatly appreciated. Thank you.

I have been in a relationship with my partner for over 6 years, and during that time, I've also been involved in raising his daughter who was 2 years old when we first met. However, I find myself struggling with feelings of resentment towards my 9-year-old stepchild. She often expresses her desire to have her father back with her mother, which makes me feel like an outsider. Additionally, when she comes to our apartment on weekends from her mother's house, I notice a lack of structure in her routine. She doesn't seem to prioritize basic hygiene like bathing or brushing her teeth, and I constantly have to remind her to do these things. I've put effort into decorating her room nicely, but I still feel like I don't fully belong when she is around. I worry about how she will interact with my future children and if her jealousy might cause harm to them. I also fear that as she enters her teenage years, there might be more drama in our home. My ultimate goal is to create a peaceful and stable environment for everyone.

Patient: Over the summer, I worked as a counselor at a stay over camp and had a great experience. I enjoyed taking care of the girls, being myself, and making friends. I loved the responsibility and how the girls looked up to me. However, when I got home, I noticed changes in my behavior. I spend more time alone in my room, feel moody, and cry at night, which is unusual for me. I've been going to this camp since I was seven, but this is the first time I've felt like this after coming home. Could this be a form of depression?

I'm really struggling with something in my relationship and I could use some guidance. My girlfriend and I have been together for almost a year and things were going well until we had a deep conversation about our pasts. I learned that she has had a lot of sexual partners before me, and I can't seem to get it out of my mind. The sheer number of partners is really bothering me and I can't help but imagine her with them. It's causing me a lot of distress and it's even led to me lashing out at her. I love her, but I don't know if I can move past this. I need advice on how to handle this situation.

Lately, I've been experiencing some intense emotions that have been affecting my relationships with my friends and family. I find myself avoiding them and I've been having random crying spells that I can't control. Additionally, I constantly feel like I'm on the verge of having a panic attack. I've had severe ADD for as long as I can remember, but I don't think it's the cause of these symptoms. After reading an article about a girl with anxiety, I could really relate to what she went through. However, unlike her, I have a supportive network of friends and family. Despite this, some of my symptoms also resemble depression. I'm not sure if this is a big problem or if I just need someone to talk to who understands. Should I consider seeking professional help?

Recently, I had a vivid dream that has been bothering me. I am a devout Christian and actively involved in my church community. In this dream, there was a woman whom I find attractive, although we have never been romantically involved. I want to clarify that I have never had any sexual thoughts about her. In the dream, I entered a room where she was lying in bed, completely covered by the blankets. The room had several mirrors on the wall, but they were all covered in wood, resembling the wooden coverings on castle windows. Somehow, I knew they were mirrors despite being covered. I approached the woman, leaned down, and gave her a gentle kiss on the forehead before the dream abruptly ended. I have been trying to find an interpretation for this dream, but I haven't been successful. Can you help me understand its meaning?

Over the past two years, I've been experiencing symptoms of depression. This isn't the first time I've felt this way, but it's never been this severe. About a year ago, things got really bad and I started self-injuring and having suicidal thoughts. It went on for months, and it felt like no one noticed or cared (or maybe I was just good at hiding it...). I hit rock bottom and realized I had two options: tell someone, most likely my mom, or try my best to get better on my own. I chose the latter.

I have been in a long-term relationship with my partner since we were teenagers. We had a baby at a young age and have been living together ever since. My partner has been struggling with depression and recently spent two weeks in a psychiatric hospital. Since returning, she has been making progress and seems happier. However, our relationship has been deteriorating slowly. She has become unreasonable and says she is falling out of love with me. She never takes responsibility for anything and I feel unwanted. I'm unsure if her feelings are genuine or if it's just her depression. Sometimes she passionately hates me, but then loves me when she thinks about me leaving. I feel used after all the hard work I've put into supporting her. Whenever I try to address my concerns, her reaction is over the top. How can I determine if her feelings are due to her depression or if she genuinely doesn't love me anymore? And if it is the depression, how can I help if I feel like I'm the problem?

Throughout my life, I have experienced the challenges of being an only child with extremely overprotective parents. Their strict rules and limitations prevented me from fully engaging in social activities during high school, leading me to feel like an outsider among my peers. However, when I went off to college, my parents allowed me to stay in the dorms and I finally had the opportunity to experience things that were previously off-limits. It was during this time that I met my first serious boyfriend, and we ended up dating for over 5 years.

Hello, I've been struggling with my self-esteem lately and it's affecting my ability to pursue my goals. I find myself constantly comparing myself to a friend of my boyfriend's who seems to have achieved so much in her life.
