I feel jealous and insecure, and it's leading to obsessive thoughts and feelings of inadequacy. My boyfriend doesn't seem to understand how much this is impacting me. I used to be happy and content, but now I'm stuck in this cycle of obsession, comparison, and depression. I want to break free from this and focus on my own abilities and accomplishments. Can you help me?

Hi, thank you for reaching out. I recently disclosed to my mother that I have been engaging in self-harm since the 6th grade. In response, I started seeing a psychiatrist and therapist at Sherbody Psychiatrists in Greenville. They prescribed me mood stabilizers, but didn't explain the specific purpose. After coming across an old journal, I asked my therapist about bipolar disorder. She informed me that my current diagnosis is NOS. I'm not sure what that means, especially since she gave me a workbook for teens after discussing the possibility of bipolar disorder. I won't be seeing her for the next three weeks due to camp, so I really want to understand what NOS stands for. Thank you for your help.

Patient: I’m always worried about having a heart attack. I even had a catheterization 5 years ago. The cardiologist told me there was nothing wrong with my heart and he wished he had my arteries. Since this was one of the best diagnostic heart tests, I thought that my fears would stop. I felt as though I had faced my greatest fear and it would go away. I forgot to add that I’ve been worrying about my heart since I was 20-years-old. The fear has not gone away and I wanted to know if you have any suggestions to help me. 48 years is a long time to be afraid. I do meditation, yoga and I try to walk 2 miles at least five days. I haven’t done this for about two months because I twisted my ankle and am now afraid to start again. My ekg’s are always normal. I see a psychiatric nurse once a month.

Two years ago, I got married. Before getting married, I was clear with my husband that I did not want to live with my in-laws. However, due to financial constraints, we agreed to live in the same apartment but in separate flats and have meals together. However, after getting married, I realized that my in-laws expect me to be with them all the time, only going home to sleep at night. Additionally, my husband spends most of his time at his parents' place, which has caused strain in our relationship. He now expresses regret about marrying me and has stopped being intimate, blaming me for the poor state of our relationship. I believe in an equal partnership, but my husband and his parents have different expectations. I don't have my own home, and my life is controlled by my in-laws, which is not acceptable to me. My husband refuses to move away from his parents. Should I continue this marriage? Please help.

When I was eleven years old, I experienced a traumatic incident of sexual assault by an older boy. Since then, I have noticed changes in my behavior and interests. I have become fascinated by serial killers and have been experiencing heightened irritability and violent urges towards others. While I haven't acted on these urges, I have engaged in verbal and physical abuse towards some individuals whom I believed deserved it. I also struggle with high levels of stress, which has affected my ability to complete tasks like homework. Although my parents think I am doing well because I haven't self-harmed in a while, I feel guilty about asking to see my therapist again. I don't want to admit that I want help because I have these violent thoughts, and I'm worried about how it will affect my mom.

I am concerned about my 5-year-old nephew. I believe he may have Sensory Processing Disorder (SPD) based on his limited food preferences, potty training difficulties, attention issues, and emotional reactions. His grandmother, who is raising him, does not believe this is the case. His teacher thinks he may have ADHD, but I'm not convinced. He also has PICA, which I've read is a form of autism. I want to help him, but his caregiver won't consider it. How can I get someone to listen or take him to the doctor?

I have been struggling with anxiety for several years now, and it's becoming exhausting. I first started experiencing symptoms in high school, but it wasn't until college that I realized it was anxiety. The transition to college was really tough for me, and I felt lonely, upset, and overwhelmed. That's when I decided to reach out to the counseling center on campus. I've been seeing the same counselor since my first semester of college, and I'm about to start my fourth year in August. While counseling has been helpful, I still find myself experiencing anxiety and I think I need to explore other options to manage it.

I've been diagnosed with a severe case of OCD and my husband has schizoaffective disorder leaning towards bipolar. I see a psychiatrist and occasionally go to my counselor, but my husband hasn't sought treatment in a long time. Lately, he's been shutting me out and yesterday he completely ignored me and went to bed. I started feeling detached from reality, lightheaded, and woozy. I want to scream but I'm afraid to wake my husband. What's happening to me? How do I regain control?

I have been experiencing various challenges throughout my life, but recently I have been struggling to overcome new ones. Over the past couple of months, whenever I encounter a tense or stressful situation, I notice physical symptoms such as racing heart, a sensation of heat in my head, restless hands, and a tendency to smile and make excuses to walk away. It has become so overwhelming that even making decisions about which college course to choose or reject triggers panic in me. Everyone around me seems to have a clear vision of their future, while I am completely unsure. This uncertainty is causing me to have episodes of hysteria. In the mornings, I feel reluctant to get out of bed because I am afraid of experiencing stress. This situation is starting to have a negative impact on my life.

Thank you for sharing your concerns about your marriage. It sounds like you and your husband have had a lot of challenges over the years, and you've recently started counseling to address these issues. It's understandable that you're feeling conflicted about what to do next.

Over the past year, I have been in my teacher's class. Recently, he gave me his phone number in case I needed someone to talk to. I reached out to him for advice, but the conversation took a disturbing turn. He began making inappropriate comments about caring for me and asking about my body. I was shocked and deleted the messages. I immediately responded, telling him that his behavior was unacceptable. He then confessed that he needs help and admitted that he is not a role model. I confided in my mom, who contacted the police. Unfortunately, since I deleted the initial texts, they couldn't take any legal action, but the school is investigating the matter. This situation has left me feeling completely unlike myself. I've been crying constantly. He was a respected teacher at my school, and I just want to find happiness and regain my sense of self.

I started dating my boyfriend when I was very young, in my early teens. I am now twenty-one and have come to realize that he is controlling and I have become co-dependent on him. I rely on his car, which is in his name, and I live with him. I know deep down that I need to leave him, but I am terrified to do so. I have no idea how to go about getting a car on my own, and I feel like I have nowhere else to go. I am feeling lost and unsure of what steps to take. I guess what I am hoping for is guidance on how to address my codependency issues, so that I can begin to work towards leaving him. I just want to find happiness.

Patient's statement (rewritten): Recently, I have been dealing with increased anxiety and panic attacks as a result of a history of sexual abuse. These experiences have led me to develop disordered eating patterns, specifically tendencies towards anorexia and bulimia. I have reached a point where my BMI is now considered underweight (17.5), and I suspect that I may also be experiencing symptoms of depression. Although I want to find relief from the depression and panic attacks, I am apprehensive about addressing the eating disorder because it provides me with a sense of control and self-confidence. I'm unsure about what my next steps should be. Is it possible for a therapist to help me with the anxiety and depression without having to address the eating issues? I haven't noticed any negative health effects from my current weight, and I just want to lose about 7 more pounds. Thank you for your assistance.

I met this guy online in January. Things started out great. But slowly, I began to notice things that were not normal with him. Here are a few examples: 1. One day I was out with my co-workers and while were were out he texted me. I texted him back telling him that I would call him back in 20 min. The get-together went over and I called him 15 min after I said I would. Instead of just letting me know that he was disappointed because I called later than I said I would, or say nothing (Most people I know would not make a big deal of that), he answered the phone and said that I sounded bitchy and that he was in a good mood until I called. He made me cry. 2. He has accused me many times of conspiring against him with other people to make his life miserable. One day I sneezed and he accused me of knowing someone who hates him. Accused me of working with that person and I was sent to mess with him. I couldn’t sneeze, cough or scratch my nose without being accused of conspiring against him. I didn’t know any of the people he was accusing me of knowing. 3. He has accused me of cheating on him and lying. He called me a fraud. He invaded my privacy by going through my computer and checking my email. He didn’t find anything but swore that when he did, he would be very vengeful. We broke up because I couldn’t take it anymore. He has said so many hurtful things to me. He accused me of cheating every time he would text me and not hear from me for just 15 min. The problem is, I am pregnant with his child, therefore it can’t be a clean break. Now he is using our unborn child as a mean to keep control over me. I have asked him not to contact me now, seeing I am only 10 weeks pregnant, But he still does. He has sent me over 100 texts and emails in one day claiming that he only wants to be in the baby’s life. He wants to be at every Doctor’s appointment and at the birth. He has even sent an email saying what the baby should be named. I do want him to be in the baby’s life because I definitely understand the benefits of a child bonding with his father. But I fear for my safety. He is very unpredictable and emotionally abused me. Also, I feel that something is wrong with him. I want him to get help. I asked him to go to therapy many times. He claims that he goes, but I don’t think so. I even suggested couple’s counseling but he refused. Right now, I don’t feel comfortable leaving a child with him. Every time something doesn’t go his way and he feels hurt, he makes sure to hurt me. Any suggestion would be greatly appreciated. Thank you.

I've been struggling with my emotions for a long time, ever since my family moved when I was in 5th grade. The death of my dad in 7th grade made things even more difficult. I've experienced feelings of sadness, questioning my existence, and even had thoughts of suicide. In 9th grade, I started having intense mood swings, going from calm to furious in a matter of minutes. I've been crying a lot and recently started cutting myself as a way to cope. While it has provided temporary relief, I know it's not a healthy solution. All I really want is to be left alone, to have some solitude and not be judged by others. I don't understand why it's such a big deal, as I feel like I'm only hurting myself.

I have been experiencing a range of emotional difficulties. I feel emotionally numb, unable to recognize or experience love. My other emotions seem muted, except for annoyance, which I feel strongly. I also struggle with a lack of guilt and empathy, except for occasional feelings of sympathy towards abused children and the homeless. I don't react emotionally when even close relatives pass away. I have a strong need for things to go my way, have difficulty accepting others' viewpoints, and tend to avoid conflicts. I can be selfish but sometimes wonder if my acts of generosity are genuine. Additionally, I have extreme antisocial tendencies and disregard others' feelings. I pretend to be sympathetic when necessary but don't actually feel it. I have an obsessive-compulsive urge to read constantly and find solace in fictional worlds. Overall, I feel apathetic and neutral most of the time. Can you help me understand what may be going on?

Today was a significant day for my family as my daughter graduated from high school. It was a joyful event, but also brought together some complex dynamics. My ex-wife's father and sister traveled from out of state to support our daughter, as did my own mother. During the graduation, we all sat together, but I couldn't help but notice that my fiancé seemed unhappy and uncomfortable. After the event, we went out to eat to celebrate the graduation.

My cousin "Robin" is 58 years old and lives alone. She has been experiencing difficulties in managing her daily affairs and is at risk of losing her job due to her personality disorder. Despite being intelligent, her ability to focus and stay organized has been declining over the past 20 years. She exhibits behaviors that are perplexing to me, such as being scatterbrained, unable to focus, and displaying signs of OCD and histrionic tendencies over trivial matters. This has caused her to isolate herself from friends and family. For instance, she tends to obsessively talk about a topic until it becomes exhausting and then starts over, leaving others feeling overwhelmed. Additionally, she struggles to complete basic tasks in a timely manner due to being easily distracted. I witnessed her taking two hours to prepare breakfast, even discarding scrambled eggs because they didn't meet her standards. It's concerning to see her struggle like this.

I've been struggling with my mental health for a long time, and it started when I was just 11 years old. I experienced deep depression at a young age and felt like no one believed me. I engaged in self-destructive behaviors like cutting, starving myself, and purging. My dad noticed and helped me stop, but now I'm slipping back into that dark place. I'm barely eating, extremely depressed, and experiencing auditory and visual hallucinations. I've had thoughts of self-harm and suicide. I know I need help, but I don't want to involve my family. Can someone please help me?

My husband and I have been struggling with a pattern of yelling in our relationship. I've noticed that my husband has a history of being treated poorly by his family, including verbal, emotional, and to some extent, physical abuse. It seems that he has internalized this mistreatment and believes he deserves it. I've tried positive encouragement, but it often escalates into yelling. Recently, I gave in and yelled at him, and he seemed relieved by it. He even admitted to wanting me to hit him, which I find concerning. I believe his upbringing has contributed to this unhealthy view of himself. What is going on and how do we move forward?

Hi, I'm a teenager and I'm feeling unsure about whether or not I might be socially anxious. I've done a few things that don't seem like something a socially anxious person would do. For example, I tried out for my school's water polo team even though I didn't know much about it and didn't know many people there. I also became a candidate for my school's student advisory council, but they rejected my speech at the last minute and pulled me out. I play soccer every day at lunch with people who are much better than me, and I even danced in front of my English class and took off my t-shirt. I also joined the kickboxing club at school and volunteered at carnival day and for the NOW program. I even tried out for volleyball. However, I've noticed that when I play soccer, I rarely get to play in the forward position, even though my friends who are really good at soccer do. This year, I didn't try out for volleyball because I felt like I wasn't good enough and it's always the same people trying out every year. Lastly, when there's an after-school soccer game on the field, I tend to not go because the guys there are really good. I also don't really want to join a club because I feel like sports isn't my thing. These are a few reasons why I think I might be socially anxious. What do you think? Thank you.

Since moving to the UK, I have been feeling really frustrated and trapped. I am 24 years old and highly educated, but I am unable to work due to visa restrictions while I am studying. I made the decision to move here because my partner claimed that they were depressed and needed my support. However, I have always experienced physical abuse from them when I was growing up.

I've been experiencing a sense of detachment from certain things, while feeling overly immersed in others. Additionally, I've been feeling like people and even television are sending me signals. I'm aware that these thoughts may sound irrational, but they've been a part of my life for as long as I can remember. In a way, it has provided some comfort, making me feel less alone and understood. However, I don't want to continue feeling crazy and I want to find a way to stop these experiences. Lately, I've been feeling ashamed and distressed by some of the thoughts I've been having. It's incredibly distressing to feel like I'm being watched, even in private moments, only to then realize that it's unlikely to be happening. I believe that people on TV are speaking to me and saying certain things, but then I remember that I'm foolish, crazy, and unattractive, which leads to embarrassment for having such thoughts. My mind is constantly active, making it difficult for me to sleep. I find myself engaging in imaginary conversations where I can be myself and others can see that I'm a good person, but even in these fantasies, I find myself feeling embarrassed by my own behavior. I desperately want to overcome this and live a normal life. Any advice or feedback would be greatly appreciated. It feels even more foolish when I see all of these thoughts written down, and it's causing me to worry. Thank you for taking the time to read this.

I am concerned about my stepdaughters who both have bipolar disorder. The younger one, in particular, seems to struggle with extreme mood swings and difficulty controlling her emotions. During the three years that the older daughter lived with us, she exhibited similar behavior, with intense highs and lows. She would isolate herself in her room for long periods and often seemed jealous and made excuses for her actions. It was difficult to predict her moods, as she could go from pleasant to withdrawn within moments.

During my childhood, I experienced a lot of bullying which was difficult for me to cope with. However, my main concern now is the impact of my grandmother moving in with my family when I was a sophomore in high school. It was just my mom, dad, and me, as I don't have any siblings.

I had been seeing my therapist for 2 and a half years. Last week she dropped a bombshell on me and told me she couldn’t be my therapist anymore because she didn’t feel like she could help me with my OCD. She said it would be unethical to continue with me since she has no knowledge on how to treat OCD. Yesterday was our last appointment. She gave me her email a while back and said I could email her whenever I want. She told me not to email her anymore. I also asked if she was going to not see her other OCD patients anymore and she said she would still see them.

I've been struggling with intense urges to harm people, even those close to me. These urges feel overwhelming and I'm scared of acting on them. I've also been fascinated by violent acts, like those during the Holocaust, but I don't agree with their beliefs. I have a friend who I confided in, but I've started to distance myself from her because I don't want her to be affected by my issues. I'm afraid to tell my parents because I don't want to hurt them or be judged. I know I need help before things escalate. Please, I'm begging for your assistance.

I have been experiencing emotional detachment, and I struggle to recognize or feel love. My other emotions are muted, with annoyance being the only one I can feel strongly. I have difficulty experiencing guilt and empathy, except for certain situations involving abused children or the homeless. I feel indifferent towards most people, including family members, and do not react emotionally to their deaths. I am impatient, always needing things to go my way and find it hard to accept others' perspectives. I am aware of my selfishness, but sometimes question if my acts of generosity are genuine or just a facade. Additionally, I am extremely antisocial, disliking being around people and disregarding their feelings. I pretend to be sympathetic when necessary, but deep down, I don't actually feel it. I have an obsessive-compulsive urge to read constantly and find solace in fictional worlds rather than reality. Most of the time, I feel emotionally neutral. What could be the underlying issue?

I've been in a long-distance relationship (LDR) with my boyfriend for the past 6 years. We met just before I transferred away for college and he left a year later. I'm currently in California and he's in New York. While we've managed to make it work, I'm finding the LDR to be incredibly difficult and it's turning into a nightmare for me.

My boyfriend is a caring and encouraging person, but he is struggling with some difficult issues that both scare and confuse me. He has a fear of driving, which has prevented him from learning. He also has fears of being abducted by aliens or shadow people and is afraid of being physically separated from me for too long. I know very little about his past abusive relationship, as he is not comfortable discussing it. Additionally, he has expressed a desire to physically harm criminals in a vigilante-like manner, but acknowledges that it's a difficult impulse to control. I've tried to help him find alternative ways to cope with his emotions and fears, but I feel unequipped to provide the support he needs.

I'm really concerned about my best friend. Her husband has a serious addiction to pills and is also struggling with depression. Last night, things escalated when he became violent and destructive in their home. He even threatened to harm himself if she were to leave him. I've tried suggesting that she seek help from his doctor or a therapist, but she's reluctant due to fear of his reaction. I'm worried about her safety and the safety of their child. What should she do in this situation?

About a month and a half ago, my wife started experiencing paranoia and delusions related to her online presence. She believes someone is hacking into her Facebook account and monitoring her activities. Despite my efforts to reassure her and enhance security measures, her beliefs have escalated to include the belief that people are watching us through our devices, following her around town, and even entering our home and car. This has greatly impacted our marriage and I'm deeply concerned for her well-being. I'm unsure how to approach the topic of seeking professional help, as she does not believe anything is wrong. Any advice would be greatly appreciated. She is 33 years old and we have two children. She is a loving and dedicated mother and, aside from these beliefs, she still seems like the person I've always known. I'm new to this situation and any guidance would be helpful.

Hello, I'm feeling a bit lost and unsure if I'm in the right place. I don't want to come across as seeking pity, but I acknowledge that I may appear pathetic. Normally, I keep things to myself, but I believe that sharing my struggles anonymously will help me gain a better understanding. Lately, I've been experiencing a range of issues that I'm not sure how to label - whether it's depression, anxiety, anger, or resentment. These emotions are holding me back from becoming the mother and future wife I aspire to be. I'm 23 years old and my fiancé and I have been engaged for 5 years, together for 6. I tend to overthink and try to solve things on my own. I often engage in self-reflective conversations to find ways to improve myself and understand why things are the way they are.

My brother recently started working at a new company as an independent contractor. Since then, he has been expressing concerns about his co-workers playing secret mind games with him. He claims to have met them before and describes elaborate encounters that supposedly took place years ago while he was in college. He also believes that one of his co-workers is related to a former boss, despite research proving otherwise. Additionally, he thinks that people are watching him. I suggested he consider talking to a psychiatrist, but he insists that he's fine. I'm extremely worried about him and unsure how to proceed in getting him the help he needs.

Patient: I have been in a relationship for three years with someone who has been diagnosed with Paranoid Schizophrenia since 2008. Initially, I didn't know about his condition and we fell in love. However, over time, his behavior has become increasingly hostile and he has been physically aggressive towards his family. We now have a one-year-old child, but his mother has decided to separate us due to his condition. I don't know if there is a chance for us to be a family again and if he can be a normal father. Can you help me?

I have been struggling with my girlfriend's behavior lately. We are expecting a baby, and when I come home from my language course, she just sits there silently while I eat. She claims that this is considered spending time together, but I disagree. I believe that in a successful relationship, couples should actively spend quality time together. When I try to express my feelings, she dismisses them and accuses me of being jealous of her first child or being depressed. She even uses it as an excuse to distance herself from me. She believes that the 20 minutes I spend eating alone is sufficient, but I don't think it's enough. Am I wrong in thinking that a successful relationship should involve more meaningful time spent together, rather than just being in the same room without any communication?

My wife and I have a loving relationship, but we face a recurring problem that seems to be related to PMS or PMDD syndrome. When she gets irritated by something trivial, she fixates on it and starts blaming and nagging me. She even brings up my past and expresses disappointment in marrying me. This behavior makes our lives miserable, and we've considered separating. It's not just typical PMS behavior, as it's much more severe. During these episodes, she yells, says hurtful things, and everything gets blown out of proportion. Even if I stay quiet, things still escalate with her threatening to leave and throwing things. However, once the episode is over, she goes back to being loving, compassionate, and happy. She acknowledges her behavior but feels like she can't control it.

I've been experiencing some unusual things lately and I'm not sure what to make of it. I have these voices in my head, almost like different personalities, with names, traits, and even different handwritings. They sometimes take over my body when I get stressed or anxious, and I feel like someone else is controlling my actions. However, I don't completely dissociate and I can still see and hear what's happening. Sometimes, I do dissociate and when I come back, my memory of what happened is like a slow-developing polaroid picture. I've been seeing a therapist, but she didn't seem to take it seriously and my parents ended my sessions abruptly. I'm wondering if you have any thoughts on this?

I am a 20-year-old woman who has been in a relationship with my 27-year-old boyfriend for 2 years. We have made the decision to move in together in a month, but we have decided to wait until I finish my BSN program and he finishes his masters program before getting engaged. My mom strongly disapproves of our age difference, but it doesn't bother me. I've had negative experiences with people my own age and slightly older, so I feel grateful to have found someone who treats me well and loves me for who I am. However, my mom continues to criticize my boyfriend and make hurtful comments about him. I just want her to be happy for me and accept my relationship. Why is that not enough for her?

It seems like I have a strained relationship with my mother. She has often made me feel like a burden and constantly criticizes me, even in front of others. I've tried to brush it off and not let it affect me, but it still bothers me. My mother has had a difficult past, involving drug use and an absent father. I'm wondering if I should cut ties with her. What do you think?

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for almost a year now. He recently disclosed to me that he has OCD. However, his OCD has started to significantly impact my life. He constantly interferes and tries to control me. I feel trapped because his family is also involved and they would scold me if I were to leave him. Whenever I don't listen to him or do what he wants, he cries, hits himself, and uses foul language.

Ever since middle school, I've been experiencing a persistent feeling that everything around me is not real, as if I'm living in a fake or game-like reality. As I've grown older, this feeling has intensified, to the point where I question the reality of the things and people around me, even my own existence. Lately, I've been having troubling thoughts and dreams about harming others, which makes me worry about losing control over myself. I feel a sense of indifference towards everything because nothing seems real. Can you help me understand what might be going on?

Counselor: Thank you for sharing your experience and dreams with me. It sounds like your therapeutic relationship with Bill was very important to you and had a profound impact on your life. It's understandable that you would have recurring dreams about him, especially given the strong connection you felt. Dreams can often reflect our subconscious thoughts and emotions.

Over the past year, I've been experiencing some intense emotions and have noticed a shift in my relationships with friends. It feels like these connections are now forced and even painful to be around people. I've also been having episodes of depersonalization. A few years ago, my ex-boyfriend passed away, which plunged me into a deep depression. I'm not sure if I ever fully recovered or if I've just grown accustomed to it. I constantly feel annoyed, tired, and prefer to be alone most of the time. However, when I shared what I've been going through with my best friend, she seemed unaware and said I seemed normal, just a bit distant. But the differences I perceive are undeniable. I also experience short bursts of rage for no apparent reason. My relationships are what truly worry me. I find myself drawn to guys who are emotionally unavailable and have sociopathic tendencies. I hate it, but I'm not interested in anyone else. This lack of genuine feelings is my biggest concern. It feels like I convince myself that I'm "in love" with these guys just to prove that I can have them. When we break up, I don't miss them, but I can't bear the thought of someone else taking my place. I become obsessed and lose control, bombarding them with texts and calls. Sometimes, I even show up at their house unannounced, only to question my own actions the next day. I feel emotionally disconnected from everyone, and I believe that others can sense that something is off about me. I constantly crave conflict with them and desperately try to hold on to them out of fear of being abandoned, even though it's almost like I'm asking for it. I always end up being the one left behind, but it's almost as if I unconsciously sabotage the relationship. I've seen a therapist, but I couldn't bring myself to share all of this. Please help me understand what could be going on and what steps I should take.

I have been married to my husband for almost two years and we rarely have sex, maybe only twice a year. This has been an ongoing issue for us, even though we are deeply in love and have good communication. In past relationships, both of us had low sex drives which caused problems. We don't pressure each other and are understanding about not wanting sex. My husband is on Prozac, which affects his libido, and my desire is influenced by my menstrual cycle. However, I still have difficulty initiating sex and become tense when he initiates. I don't understand why this is happening, as I find him attractive and we are affectionate with each other. What could be the underlying issue?

Counselor: Thank you for sharing your experiences and concerns. It's important to remember that childhood sexual curiosity is a normal part of development. It sounds like you were exploring your own curiosity without any understanding of the concept of sex itself. It's reassuring to hear that these experiences seem to be distant memories and that you haven't noticed any negative effects on yourself or others.

I'm really struggling with my younger sister and I don't know what to do anymore. We have a significant age gap, with me being twenty and her being thirteen. Our living situation is also complicated since I still live at home while attending school. To add to the complexity, my sister has always had weight issues, while I am quite petite. This has caused tension between us. Additionally, our parents went through a divorce about eighteen months ago, which has been incredibly challenging for both of us. My sister had a particularly difficult time as the courts decided she would live with our dad part time, while my mom obtained full custody of her.

Hello, I am a 28-year-old woman from India. I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for the past 4 years, and we have recently set our wedding date. My boyfriend is a wonderful person who loves me deeply, and I care for him a lot as well. However, I have noticed that while I am emotionally connected to him, I am not as physically attracted to him. I enjoy kissing him, but I don't feel the same level of enjoyment in other physical aspects of our relationship.

I'm really concerned about my brother's behavior. He's 20 years old and I suspect he may have a psychological disorder. He seems to have an extreme obsession with religion and claims to see Jesus. He's also very hateful towards other religions and lacks empathy, especially towards our grandmother who is taking care of him. He verbally abuses our younger sister on a daily basis, even though she's not promiscuous at all. He constantly thinks someone has poisoned his food and goes to the emergency room frequently. He's also obsessed with joining the military, even though he's unable to. He's self-absorbed, lacks empathy, and is very conceited.

I'm a 13-year-old from Singapore and my parents have been having issues since December 2013. They haven't been talking to each other much, except for discussing my tuition fees. It all started when my dad gave $1000 to his brother without telling my mom, which broke their agreement to inform each other about expenses over $200. My mom was upset and felt that she couldn't trust my dad anymore. Now, my dad refuses to pay for my mom's expenses and tells my brother that she takes money from him. My mom, on the other hand, wonders why my dad can spend so much on something that doesn't benefit our family, but not contribute to our household expenses. This situation has made both of them very upset, and I'm worried that they might get divorced. I love my family and don't want to see anyone unhappy or be separated from anyone. Can you help me?

Patient: I've been experiencing these strange mood swings that don't align with my menstrual cycle. There are times when I feel really happy and productive, like last week when I stayed up all night, created art, wrote lyrics, and socialized. But now, just a few days later, I feel tired, isolated, and worthless. I don't know if this is just normal stress from school or if it's something more serious. I've also been crying a lot and feeling irritable. This has been happening for most of the year and I'm trying to understand it better.

Since October 2013, I've been experiencing some unsettling symptoms. It all started with my first panic attack, which was accompanied by numbness, tingling, and a strange sensation in my head. Objects around me seemed to change in size, and I felt a constant cloudiness in my mind. Despite seeking help from various doctors and even a psychologist, I haven't found any answers or relief. I'm concerned about what this feeling is, why I'm suddenly having panic attacks when I've been calm, and how I can get rid of it. It's affecting my school work and my relationships with friends and family. Any help would be greatly appreciated.

A year ago, my son's father was involuntarily admitted to the psychiatric ward at a hospital. He initially took his medication for a week but then refused to continue and claimed he didn't need to be there. He was diagnosed with unspecified psychosis and prescribed olanzapine. His mother has a history of schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. Prior to his hospitalization, he displayed paranoid behavior and had unusual thoughts. While in jail, he believed that there were harmful substances in the food he ate, that people were tampering with the water pipes, and that there were individuals out to harm him. He even accused my dad of trying to poison him. He shared these beliefs with his family, accusing them of plotting against him. He often feels as though he is being watched by others, even at stoplights. He has difficulty maintaining employment or contributing financially. I believe he is mentally unstable. He frequently has angry outbursts, yelling and screaming at his grandparents, mother, grandmother, sisters, and myself. His behavior was particularly intense and frightening during my pregnancy. He was extremely possessive and did not want me to have contact with my own family or anyone else, including his own family members. He would always come and get me whenever I tried to leave during the past three years. Recently, I moved to a different county, three hours away, to live with my family. However, he showed up uninvited and unexpected. He would park outside my house for extended periods of time before driving away. Sometimes, I mustered up the courage to go outside and tell him that I wasn't going with him, which would result in him screaming and driving off. A few days later, he would repeat the same routine. He even did this at my grandfather's house when I wasn't there. When a family member confronted him about being there and informed him that I wasn't present, he made up a bizarre excuse, claiming that I owed him money. He does this at all hours, whether it's 11 PM, 4 AM, or even during the day. He sends me texts using foul language, telling me to pack my things because he's coming, only to follow up with messages saying he loves and misses me. It's a rollercoaster of emotions. He has been diagnosed with bipolar disorder. I currently have a restraining order against him, and both his family and I have informed him about it, but he is in denial. I feel constantly uneasy due to his harassment and stalking. I feel like I have exhausted all options to get him the help he needs. How can he be encouraged to take his medication? I have involved the police, but he doesn't have episodes in front of them. On top of that, he knows how to appear calm and charming to get out of difficult situations. The doctor has informed me that I cannot force him to take his medication. His family and I are desperate for help. He is 23 years old, and we have a one-year-old son. Any advice?

I have been married to my husband for 4 years and we have a blended family with a 19-year-old daughter from my previous relationship and a 19-year-old son from my husband's previous relationship. When my stepson moved in with us full-time after graduating high school, issues started to arise. He has been lying, stealing pills from me, and violating my daughter's privacy by entering her room without permission. I suggested that he move back in with his mother to seek help, but my husband initially resisted. Eventually, my husband agreed and my stepson moved out for a month. However, my husband resented me during that time. When I allowed my stepson to stay the night once to rebuild trust, my husband took it as an opportunity for him to move back in permanently. Now, I feel unsafe in my own home and my husband has even put a lock on my daughter's door. I don't want my stepson to live with us anymore, but I'm afraid my husband will resent me if I bring it up. Any advice would be appreciated.

Hello, I'm really struggling with severe anxiety and I don't know what to do anymore. It all started when my family moved to a new province when I was 10 years old. I had a hard time adjusting and making friends because of the language barrier. I became isolated and bullied, and even when we moved back to my hometown, I still struggle to interact with people. I feel like there's something controlling me and preventing me from speaking. It's affecting my self-esteem and I'm afraid it will impact my future. What should I do?

Four years ago, in 6th grade, I transferred to a new school with a great magnet program. Before that, I had always made the A-B honor roll. However, since transferring, my grades have dropped to C's. Ever since, my mom's behavior towards me has changed. She yells at me more and blames me for things. It feels like she treats me badly no matter what I do, and I'm worried about the consequences if she finds out I'm sharing this.

Over the past two years, I have noticed a significant decline in my mental state. I struggle to complete simple tasks at home, like doing dishes and laundry. I lack motivation and find it difficult to get out of bed, even on days off. While I manage to go to work on time, I am finding it harder to complete my tasks there and my memory has gotten worse. Despite feeling guilty for not completing things, I don't think I am depressed because I am happy around others. However, I do experience anxiety in unfamiliar situations, which leads me to avoid tasks and interactions that make me uncomfortable. I'm seeking advice on how to overcome these worries, find motivation, and improve my memory.

Hello. A few years ago, I experienced a traumatic event that has had a significant impact on my emotional well-being. Since then, I have been feeling depressed, struggling with sleep, experiencing unexplained weight loss, and losing interest in social situations. I initially sought medical help, but the medication did not seem to have any effect. I've been considering that my struggles may be related to mental health issues, as I have also been experiencing hallucinations and gaps in my memory. I have had recurring thoughts of suicide for a long time, but I don't feel comfortable opening up to my parents about it. I am intimidated by the idea of seeking help from a therapist, as I fear judgment or dismissal of my experiences as just "having the blues." However, I have been suffering for over two years and it's impacting my quality of life. I want to find ways to cope and regain my previous well-being. How should I approach this?

I'm a 20-year-old student who has been in a relationship with my boyfriend for about 4 months. Before we started dating, I shared some personal information about him with my parents, including the fact that he has bipolar disorder. Their response was to tell me to stay away from him, saying that I didn't need that kind of "crazy" in my life. To avoid conflict, I told them that I didn't like him anyway, even though I actually do.

Over the past 5-7 months, I've been experiencing periods where it's difficult for me to get out of bed. I feel a strong aversion to being alone, but being around my family or anyone else feels overwhelming at times. I've noticed that certain triggers, like music, can suddenly make me feel very sad and I start to cry. It's during these moments that I feel like I'm in a deep, dark hole and that no one can help me. Sleeping has been a challenge for me lately, and there are times when I can't even bring myself to open my eyes. I try to stay occupied, but even simple tasks that I used to enjoy feel like a struggle. My last semester in school was particularly difficult, as I had trouble studying and keeping up with my classes. However, there are some days when I feel completely fine. I can wake up, take care of myself, and have a positive attitude. I've read that exercise can help improve mood, so I started exercising regularly, but even getting to the gym can be emotionally draining. I'm not sure if this is just a phase I'm going through or if there's something more going on. Do you think I should seek help?

I’ve been married for 17 years and my husband is the type that likes to criticize a lot, every little thing I do. Lately this happens a lot at work as well, so I’m really down on self-esteem. I am a good person, I do a lot of things at home as my husband has a very demanding job, but all I ever hear is the things I forget to do or I don’t do it the way I’m supposed to do. Same at work, there are always more ways to do a job and my boss never likes my way. I am overly sensitive and defensive, I know that, but it’s hard for me to be any other way with so much negativity around me. I cry a lot lately, which annoys my husband who thinks I should just take his opinion and improve. I can’t find the energy to improve as I’m being put down so much, and I feel like I’m losing my mind and can’t trust my judgment at all. I’ve been reading lately about how I should not let people bring me down and find happiness inside myself, but I just can’t, and my depression deepens day by day. Do you have any advice on how to deal with this? How can I trust myself and find some way to be confident again? Thank you!

I have been feeling really overwhelmed lately. I still live with my parents, and they have very strict rules that make me feel trapped. On top of that, I am unhappy with my job and I have stopped going to school. I am constantly feeling angry, sad, and hopeless. I have had rough experiences in my relationships, and I often isolate myself because I don't feel understood. I have even had thoughts of self-harm, although I have only acted on it once. I feel lonely and ignored by my family, who sometimes make me feel unwelcome and unsafe at home. I recognize that I have made mistakes in the past and have apologized, but my parents continue to bring up the past and put me down. I am really in need of professional help as soon as possible.

Counselor: Thank you for sharing your situation. It sounds like you have a lot going on right now, both in terms of your relationship and your family dynamics. It's understandable that you feel strongly about your partner and believe that this is love based on your experiences together. It's also important to acknowledge that age and career differences can sometimes create challenges in relationships.

I have been dating my boyfriend for about a year now. Before me, he had a long-term girlfriend who he remained friends with even after they broke up. I suspected that he wasn't completely over her when we started dating, and although he denied it, their interactions whenever we run into her confirm my suspicions. I've caught her texting him twice, and when I confronted him, he showed me the texts and claimed they hadn't been in contact for a while. Despite him giving me no reason not to trust him, I find myself questioning everything he says and having terrible thoughts that he's lying to me. I love him, but this mistrust is taking a toll on me. I have a feeling that he might use his coworker's birthday as an excuse to spend time with his ex-girlfriend. How do I address this mistrust with him, or should I? And how can I stop these negative thoughts when he hasn't done anything wrong?

Over the past few months, I've been experiencing intense sadness and emotional instability without any apparent cause. I find myself crying over the smallest things, even crying before bed without understanding why. To cope with my racing mind and stress, I've resorted to staying up watching movies. However, this has affected my sleep and mornings, as I struggle to wake up and face the day with a negative and sad mindset. I've significantly cut back on my alcohol consumption, going from heavy drinking every weekend to not drinking for almost a month now. Additionally, I've noticed that my short-term memory has been affected. I used to be sociable and enjoyed attending events, but now I avoid crowded places like the mall on weekends. I'm uncertain if there's something wrong with me or if it's just stress from everything going on in my life.

When I was around 14 years old, I was diagnosed with Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD). It was explained to me that if I didn't manage it with medication, it could lead to severe depression. Throughout the rest of my life, I've experienced feelings of insecurity, edginess, and sometimes even thoughts of suicide. I often have uncontrollable thoughts and feelings that make me want to run or scream. Lately, I've been feeling really down, but I was excited when I got hired for a well-paying job. However, after just two days of working, I had a terrible panic attack out of nowhere. I was completely fine, but then my mind seemed to go haywire and I almost blacked out. My friend had to calm me down, and I tried to continue working for the rest of the day, but I felt confused and couldn't keep track of what I had done or what was real. I ended up going home early, and ever since then, I haven't been able to function. Everything scares me, I'm extremely paranoid, and I keep waking up at night with panic attacks. I'm really in need of help.

Patient: Hi, I've been experiencing some difficulties lately with what I believe is an imaginary friend. He's not very friendly and constantly repeats the hurtful things that people say to me at school. It really affects my self-esteem and sometimes he even prevents me from eating because he wants me to be skinny. He says he loves me and wants the best for me, but he constantly pressures me to be perfect, which is really bothersome. I don't want him to go away, but I want him to stop telling me I need to be someone I'm not. My friends think I might have Dissociative Identity Disorder (DID), but I'm not sure because I can communicate with him. I'm considering telling my parents and maybe seeing a psychiatrist, but it's hard for me to accept that something might be wrong with me. Can you help me understand what's happening?

I have been experiencing overwhelming anxiety when it comes to social situations. I have recently moved to Scotland and have not registered with a doctor yet because I am afraid of having to interact with the receptionist and sit in a waiting room with strangers. This fear has made it difficult for me to leave my house, find employment, and make friends. Even talking to family members has become a challenge. I find it nearly impossible to communicate with individuals, let alone groups. It's getting worse to the point where I isolate myself in my room and even have panic attacks when the phone rings or someone knocks on the door. I want to seek help before this escalates to the point where I never leave my house. However, I am terrified to ask for help. Even as I type this, I am experiencing physical symptoms like shallow breathing, sweaty palms, and palpitations. Please assist me.

I have been diagnosed with ADHD and anxiety disorder. Lately, I've been experiencing a persistent voice in my head that gives me troubling thoughts and commands. It tells me things like "if you don't do this, you'll die" or urges me to harm myself. I also spend a significant amount of time talking to myself and this internal voice. I mentioned it to my psychology teacher and she mentioned the possibility of schizophrenia, but I'm hesitant to seek further clarification due to the fear of being judged. Additionally, I believe I may have Asperger's syndrome because of my lack of social skills and obsessions. Can you provide any advice or guidance?

Since graduating from university three years ago, I've been struggling to find stability in my life. I've been constantly moving around both geographically and professionally because I prioritized maintaining a relationship with my now ex-boyfriend. We were together for 3.5 years, but we broke up three weeks ago. While I'm saddened by the loss, I'm also hopeful for the future and the new opportunities it may bring.

Over the past couple of years, I have been experiencing some concerning behaviors that I would like to discuss. I have noticed that I often get caught up in delusional theories that I can't fully explain. These thoughts involve believing in government coverups and conspiracies. It has become so extreme that I actually start believing that the government is using the TV and radio to brainwash me and that my water supply is being poisoned. As a result, I now only drink bottled water or water that I have personally purified. These thoughts occur frequently and sometimes my mind races with hyperactive rapid rampages where I have endless wild ideas.

Recently, I've been experiencing intrusive thoughts of violence and killing people. I want to clarify that I have no desire to act on these thoughts because I am aware of the consequences it would have on my future, family, and friends. However, these thoughts are becoming more vivid and real to me, and I find myself engaging in activities like watching violent shows, playing violent games, and reading about crime scenes to try and satisfy these urges. I must admit that in the past, I have engaged in harmful behavior towards small reptiles and occasionally squirrels, but I have never harmed cats or dogs as I have an affinity for them. I feel like I need help, but I'm unsure of where to turn. I'm afraid that psychiatrists won't see me due to the fear that I may pose a threat to them or others. Additionally, I'm concerned that my insurance won't cover me if I disclose these thoughts or engage in self-harm. I feel stuck and don't know what to do.

I have been struggling with my mental health and it's starting to feel unbearable. I'm 16 years old and I've been experiencing intense sadness, dark thoughts, and self-harm urges. My parents don't take my feelings seriously, so I've kept it all to myself. I've even started having thoughts of ending my own life. It's getting harder for me to go to school and I often leave early because I feel overwhelmed. I don't want to hurt my parents, but I'm starting to believe that I shouldn't be alive anymore.

I have been dealing with a history of abuse from various people in my life, including my mother, brother, ex-husband, employers, and even friends. It has been a long and difficult journey, but I thought I was making progress until recently. I made a deposit for my aunt and somehow lost the $60.00 cash she needed for groceries. I am currently unemployed and don't have any money to repay her. This incident has made me feel defeated, broken, and hopeless. On top of that, I have been trying to build my own business, but lack of funds has been a major setback. I also lost my two jobs due to circumstances beyond my control - one organization lost its state contract and the other job ended when I became seriously ill from exposure to mold. It has been over 2 1/2 months now and I haven't been able to find another job. I had to file for bankruptcy in 2013 after my divorce, which caused my credit union to revoke my membership. This means I can no longer make my car payments online and face fines or possible repossession if I'm late. I have been in counseling for the past 12 years, but I can't find any free services in Los Angeles and I don't have the means to pay for it. I feel trapped and like nothing is working out for me. It's as if all my efforts are going against me. I really need help.

I have been married for 9 years and we have a daughter who is currently attending school. Overall, I love my wife and our child, as well as my in-laws. However, I have noticed that I tend to feel possessive at times. Specifically, I have noticed a change in my wife's behavior when her parents are around. There seems to be a lack of intimacy between us during those times. I recall feeling much happier and more connected to my wife when we were alone overseas. Additionally, when we go out with my in-laws, I feel disinterested in following them and it seems like they feel the same about me. This leaves my wife in the middle, splitting her time between them and me. I find myself not happy with this situation and feel like my wife should prioritize me over her parents and brother. Although we have our own house and my in-laws have their own, I am contemplating a bigger decision of moving away from them. However, I don't want to do this because I do acknowledge their importance to our family. I am seeking advice on how to handle this possessiveness and address the situation with my wife.

Hi, I'm a 16-year-old girl and I've been struggling with a lot of self-esteem issues. I think it stems from being bullied a lot in middle school. I also have social anxiety and don't have many friends. I have one friend who doesn't really understand me and often complains about me, but she doesn't want to end our friendship because I'm her only friend too. Sometimes she likes me because I make her laugh. When I'm at school, my mood improves when I see my classmates and my friend. But when I'm home, I feel really down and alone. I don't have a good relationship with my stepfather, who financially supports me and my mother (who currently works in another town). He's very distant and grumpy, and I'm happier when he's not around because I can do things I enjoy on my own. As a child, I didn't have the best upbringing. I was abused and molested by the woman who took care of me when my mother was overseas, as well as her older children. Fortunately, I've repressed many of those memories since they were too painful for me to bear. Nowadays, I constantly feel low and unworthy because I'm not perfect, pretty, smart, popular, or wealthy like others. I might come across as attention-seeking, but I just want people to notice and think well of me. I wish I received more attention from the opposite sex like other girls because that would make me feel prettier. However, I've been told by many guys that I look like a 12-year-old, and I've had instances where I embarrassed myself in the past, which led to being bullied. My biggest issue is that all these thoughts consume me when I'm alone at home, and it makes me afraid to go out on my own because I fear feeling bad, people staring at me, gossip, or feeling isolated. I've even had thoughts of suicide during my low moments, but my mother doesn't want to hear about it and gets angry with me when I bring it up.

I'm a 17-year-old from Romania and I've been struggling with a troubling desire. Since I was 14, I've had this fantasy about engaging in sexual activity with a young male between the ages of 10 and 14. It's been weighing on me, even though I enjoy the company of girls my own age and have had a girlfriend. I want to completely eliminate this fantasy from my thoughts. The problem is, I can't seek therapy because I'm afraid my parents will find out and I'll be judged by my family and those close to me. I don't want to harm any young relatives, but this desire is overwhelming me mentally.

Since my late 20's, I've noticed that making personal decisions has been incredibly challenging for me. It's strange because I have no problem making business decisions during my career. I think this issue might be a combination of a phobia and OCD. Whenever I do make a decision, whether it's impulsive, based on extensive research, or following advice from others, I experience intense panic and even physical sickness for days. I've seen numerous psychiatrists and therapists, but many of them don't seem to fully understand that this is more than just indecisiveness. I've tried various tranquilizers and antidepressants, but nothing has really helped. Do you know of any therapists or psychiatrists who have successfully treated this specific phobia? If not, what type of therapy should I seek?

Two years ago, I entered into a relationship with my ex-partner. Unfortunately, three months into the relationship, I became pregnant. Throughout our time together, my ex put me through a lot of pain and turmoil. He would talk to his ex-girlfriends behind my back, engage in substance abuse, disappear for extended periods, and refuse to answer my calls. He never held a job, and he used my personal struggles against me, throwing them in my face. Eventually, he left me for our roommate, though he claims they didn't have a sexual relationship. I am feeling incredibly lost and confused because I gave my all to this relationship. I was loyal, forgiving, and loving. He would apologize profusely, express his love for me, but claim that he couldn't control his actions and felt like something else was controlling him. He struggled with depression, anxiety, and substance abuse, having been prescribed Seroquel and another medication whose name I don't know. After enduring enough emotional and mental abuse, we broke up. However, I am overwhelmed with guilt and confusion because I still love him, despite the immense pain he has caused me. I believe he is severely mentally ill. I cannot continue to be with him due to his intense anger and the other issues I mentioned earlier. He is now telling me that he will harm himself if I leave him and expressing how sorry he is for everything, but I have heard these promises countless times before. It seems like he doesn't understand that he needs to change. Based on my research, he exhibits traits consistent with borderline personality disorder. Can someone please provide me with guidance? Do I give up on this relationship after enduring betrayal and abuse for so long? I feel utterly lost. I am currently raising our son alone in a different state, and I desperately need insight on what to do.

Over the past nine years, since I was 9 years old, I have been struggling to find happiness. It started with experimenting with substances like weed and alcohol, but when I sought help from therapists, they didn't fully understand my situation and suggested that I see a psychiatrist. We tried different antidepressants and high doses of Klonopin to manage my extreme anxiety, which causes me to struggle with public speaking, attending school due to fear of crowds, and excessive sweating. Unfortunately, neither the antidepressants nor the Klonopin provided relief. I eventually started abusing Klonopin, and after a suicide attempt, I was admitted to a psychiatric ward. After my release, I fell into a pattern of using hard drugs, stealing, and robbing. I feel a strong dislike towards my family and "friends." I try to stay occupied with various activities, but drugs are the only thing that temporarily distracts me from my deep unhappiness. My self-esteem is extremely low, and I long to experience what it's like to be genuinely happy and feel a sense of belonging. I feel like I have nothing to live for except for my drug use, and I fear that something terrible will happen if I can't find contentment in life and become drug-free.

My husband has been diagnosed with PTSD (not military-related) and bipolar disorder about five years ago. I've noticed that his behavior has changed a lot over the years, and it's become increasingly difficult for me to recognize him. He isolates himself from others and spends most of his time in the basement working on his projects. Our conversations have become one-sided, with him going on long rambles. He also has trouble maintaining a stable job and has accumulated a lot of debt. I take care of our daughter while working full-time, and he only watches her for a short amount of time. He sees a psychiatrist and takes medication, but he often stops seeing his counselor. He doesn't believe that his illness affects me or our relationship. I'm feeling overwhelmed and have thought about leaving him, but I worry about the impact it will have on our daughter.

I've been feeling empty most of the time and experiencing a lot of anger and anxiety. I've noticed that I often work out and eat healthy just to impress others and make them jealous. I also find myself envying others and feeling upset when I'm not complimented on my looks. I have these dark fantasies about harming those close to me and even the bullies at school. I frequently lie and insult others to boost my own self-esteem. My family members have called me antisocial, sociopathic, and arrogant. I have a high opinion of myself, but I struggle to handle criticism and it often leads to anger and hostility. Sometimes I find humor in things that others would find serious, like death, and I tend to talk about things that others may find strange. I believe all of this stems from the loss of my mother when I was eleven and the lack of involvement and anger from my father. Additionally, the frequent bullying at school has made me paranoid.
Before we dive into my concerns, I want to express my gratitude for the therapists on this site. Their kindness and good work in helping people is truly appreciated.

Patient: I've recently moved back in with my mother and sister after my father passed away two years ago. Now, my long distance girlfriend and I are at a crossroads where one of us needs to move to be together. I've been trying to convince her to move here to Canada, but she lives in the southern states. The problem is, I don't know how to approach my family about the idea of moving in with my girlfriend. Adding to that, my girlfriend has struggled with depression and has even mentioned suicidal thoughts in the past. My family is aware of this and I think they have some concerns about her. I would appreciate any advice you can offer.

I come from a cultural background where first cousins are allowed to marry, and I have been struggling with my feelings towards my cousin. When I was younger, we engaged in consensual sexual activities, but I always felt guilty afterwards because of her age. Now that she is 15 and I am older, I still feel a strong bond with her and want to marry her. I worry that I may be a pedophile or abnormal. Can you help me understand what is happening?

A few years ago, I experienced a very intense out-of-the-blue panic attack while out for a walk with my wife. I was convinced I was having a heart problem and dying. We went to the ER where they ran some tests that ruled out a heart issue. When discharged, I was given no explanation or even theories as to what happened to me, but was told to see my primary care physician. I did, and he didn’t have a clue either. My first correct diagnosis came from a Facebook friend who read my post telling my story, which I confirmed using WebMD. Since then one therapist told me I have GAD, and another panic disorder (I think they’re both right). I use Ativan as needed. I once tried Zoloft but it gave me a paradoxical reaction and I haven’t taken one since. While there are times when I can point to a specific trigger that sets me off, there are many other occasions when I experience “free-floating anxiety” which I can’t explain. I have read that CBT can be helpful in treating GAD, but I don’t see how identifying faulty patterns of thinking can help when there doesn’t seem to be any rhyme or reason for the anxiety in the first place. I recently saw a therapist for CBT who believes there is always a trigger for anxiety, even though it may not seem like it. Is free-floating anxiety real, what causes it, and can CBT help? Thank you very much.

I have been struggling with two separate issues. First, I experienced sexual abuse from my biological father. Despite not spending much time with him throughout my childhood, there were two instances of abuse, one when I was a child and the other when I was 14. I still have traumatic flashbacks from these experiences. Additionally, I am forced to hear about him through family, as I have not disclosed what happened to anyone. People around me can sense the tension, but until I tell them, they may not fully grasp the severity of what I went through.

I'm really concerned about my sister. We're both teenagers and we both have been diagnosed with major depressive disorder. My sister also struggles with terrible anxiety. Lately, I've noticed that she has been withdrawing from family and friends and having gruesome thoughts. She has also been paranoid about demons and ghosts spying on her. Yesterday, something really scary happened. We were home alone together and she suddenly came downstairs with her hands over her face, shrieking and crying. She kept saying that her eyes were black and that she needed help. I tried to reassure her, but she insisted that only she could see it because I didn't have the abilities. She was very scared and even hit me when I denied that her eyes were black. She ended up scratching her face so hard that she still has scratches. It took her about 20 minutes to calm down. I tried to distract her with videos until our mom came home.

Three years ago, I experienced a significant loss when my mother passed away. Shortly after, I began to experience symptoms of anxiety, feeling detached and unreal. I lost my appetite and stopped engaging in activities I once enjoyed. I was able to overcome it, but recently I've been feeling the same way again due to financial and relationship stress. Unfortunately, my wife and I don't have work or health insurance, so I can't seek professional help. I just want to feel like myself again, but I constantly worry about my health and have lost enjoyment in life. I don't have suicidal thoughts, but I want to find a way to regain my sense of self.

Lately, I've been experiencing a significant change in my emotions. A while ago, I was under a lot of stress and I reached a breaking point. Since then, I haven't been able to feel emotions the way I used to. It's like my conscience has disappeared and my emotions are gone. What's strange is that I've developed a newfound enjoyment for violence. I know it's common for young men to have an interest in violence, but the urge to harm living things, like wanting to kill a goose and actually acting on it, is alarming to me. I'm not sure what caused this change, but part of me kind of likes it because my life has become easier. However, should I be worried about these thoughts and actions?

I have been diagnosed with bipolar disorder, and as part of my treatment, I am required to receive therapy in addition to medication from a psychiatrist at my community mental health center. I find this approach to be extremely beneficial and it has greatly improved my well-being.

I have been taking 5mg of Escitalopram (Lexapro) for the past 10 years. However, I am experiencing a very painful physical condition that I believe is due to suppressed emotions. My muscles are constantly tense and I have been diagnosed with muscle atrophy. I have been in dynamic psychotherapy for 2 years, but it hasn't been effective. The only thing that seems to help is meditation. However, I have noticed that the medication gives me a sudden burst of energy and overactive emotions about 5-6 hours after taking it. This makes it difficult for me to find relief because it feels like the medication is controlling my emotions. Increasing the dosage makes me feel completely numb. On the other hand, if I don't take the medication, I experience extreme fatigue, rapid heartbeat, hot flushes, and numbness in my chest. This happens even with just 5mg of the medication. I'm not sure what to do. Thank you for your help.

I've been experiencing a lot of mental and emotional struggles lately. I constantly feel like my mind is foggy and it's difficult for me to think clearly. I'm often irritable and find myself feeling either sad or angry most of the time. While I do have some good days, they don't seem to last very long. It's really hard for me because I can see how my mood swings and inability to express myself are affecting my fiancé and our children. I have a hard time opening up and talking about how I feel, which only creates more issues in our relationship. I also struggle with anxiety, especially when I'm away from my loved ones. However, I've noticed that isolating myself sometimes makes me feel better. Occasionally, I experience moments of euphoria, almost like I'm in a movie. In the past, I had hallucinations, both visual and auditory, but now I mainly experience delusions where I believe that people are out to harm me or constantly watching me. I even have thoughts that animals are somehow robotic or acting as spies. I want to clarify that I've never acted on these beliefs, but it's distressing to have them. It's been especially difficult when I've snapped at my kids for no reason, and I feel guilty for treating them that way. I'm just really confused and don't understand why I'm going through all of this. I was previously diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia, but I'm considering getting a second opinion.

I've been struggling with severe anxiety for a while now. I find it difficult to interact with others and often prefer to stay by myself. I don't have any close friends and have experienced a series of traumatic events starting from when I was 20. I lost both my parents, went through a miscarriage, and had two physically and mentally abusive relationships. I was diagnosed with depression six years ago but never received therapy. I've had six suicide attempts in the past, but none in the last three years. However, thoughts of suicide still linger in my mind. I also engage in self-harm, specifically cutting.

I've been struggling with a lack of motivation and I also experienced a sexual assault over the summer. I've started seeing a school psychologist, but I'm concerned about the mandatory reporting laws. If I disclose the assault, they will have to report it to the police and my parents. I don't want my parents to find out because I'm afraid I'll be blamed. I don't know who else to talk to about this, and it's been weighing me down for six months. I really want to start healing and moving forward, but I can't do that if I can't talk about what happened. Is there any other way I can get help as a minor without involving my parents?

Thank you for reaching out and providing this platform for support. I'm feeling lost and trapped in my current situation. I'm turning 27 soon and I don't have a job or attend school. I have very limited social interactions because I have the responsibility of taking care of my younger sibling while my mom works. When I do go out, I have to pretend to be happy, but deep down I'd rather be alone in the darkness. I've been contemplating suicide because I feel like I'm just wasting space. My emotions have become uncontrollable, shifting rapidly from anger to sadness. I don't know what's wrong with me and the fear of judgment has prevented me from seeking help. This is causing problems in my relationship with my mom, and it deeply upsets my little sister when I'm upset. I know I need help, but I don't have the means to access it due to lack of income and health insurance. I feel stuck and unsure of what to do.

My first year of college was really tough for me. I had a lot of challenges, including struggling academically and feeling unprepared from high school. On top of that, I experienced the death of a close relative, illness, abuse, being kicked out of my home, losing many friendships, and dealing with exam anxiety and panic attacks. I tried to get myself back on track in my second year by taking on a heavier course load, but it all became too much. I didn't have any breaks for three months straight, except for when I was too sick to study.

Since getting married in India, I have taken on the responsibility of managing my joint family household. Although my mother-in-law has passed away, I still live with my father-in-law, brother-in-law, his wife, and my husband. I have always taken these responsibilities to heart and never felt forced to do anything. As a working woman, it can be challenging for me to balance my job, festivals, relatives, and household duties. Despite the difficulties, I have always gone out of my way to manage everything happily.

I am a 17-year-old who has been struggling with self-harm for about 3 or 4 years. During my earlier years, I experienced bullying which made me highly sensitive to criticism. The self-harm began as a way to cope with bad days or feelings of sadness. Recently, however, these feelings of sadness have been intensifying, and I suspect that I may be depressed. I have episodes of deep sadness that can last up to 3 or 4 days, during which I don't feel like leaving my house or bed. Although I do have good days, the predominant emotions I experience are disappointment, sadness, and boredom with my life. I've read accounts of people with depression who hate everything all the time and constantly have thoughts of wanting to die. Since I'm not like that, I worry that I'm just overreacting and that these are normal mood swings. While cutting initially helped with the sadness, I now find myself doing it for the adrenaline rush as well, even in situations where I am only slightly unfulfilled or worried. I want to assure you that my cuts are not too deep and I don't have any permanent scarring, so I don't think it's too concerning. My sister once noticed my cuts and jokingly asked if I was cutting myself. I fear that if I were to confide in my family, they wouldn't believe me and just dismiss it as typical teenage moodiness, despite my father having a history of depression. Do you think I need help, or is this something I will eventually outgrow?

I have been struggling with a drug addiction to methamphetamine. I have tried going to residential centers, but I always end up running away because the anxiety and depression become overwhelming. I feel like the only way for me to quit is if I die or end up locked up in jail or a mental hospital. I used meth during college to help me study and focus, but now I realize that the degree I earned is not worth the addiction. I feel hopeless and it's causing me a lot of anxiety and depression. Is there any hope for me?

I have been married for 4 months and currently live with my in-laws in India. My sister-in-law is also living with us temporarily due to some marital issues she is facing. I appreciate that my husband is a supportive brother and tries to help her by talking to her about her problems. However, I feel uncomfortable when they speak behind closed doors or turn off the lights at night to have private conversations.

Over the last year, I've experienced a lot of distress in my relationship with my mom.
