Whenever I confide in her about personal problems like my suicidal thoughts, she ends up telling everyone, which makes me feel like a bad person. I've stopped opening up to her about these things and it's been difficult. The only person I feel I can trust is my sister, but sometimes I worry that she doesn't care as much. Lately, my mom has been focusing on the negative things I do and sharing them with others, which is really affecting how I see myself. I've tried talking to her about it, but she doesn't take it seriously. I'm afraid that if things continue this way, it might push me to do something I'll regret. I just want to understand why my mom is behaving like this and how I can rebuild trust with her. I don't want to keep feeling like I'm a bad person.

I have been in a relationship with a man I believe to be experiencing symptoms of schizophrenia for the past two years. He exhibits paranoia, aggression, and has auditory hallucinations where he hears negative voices. These symptoms are causing a lot of distress, especially when he becomes verbally abusive towards me for things I haven't said. He has also exhibited delusions, such as believing he is being followed, recording his colleagues at work due to a perceived racial abuse, and thinking his neighbors are part of a cult. He even accused me of being a witch and claimed to be God. I want to help him, but I'm not sure how.

My wife has a history of depression and is currently experiencing a recurrence of symptoms. She had a difficult time a few years ago, losing her grandmother and her job within a short period of time, which caused a lot of anxiety, depression, and emotional issues. We sought help for her and she has been on Wellbutrin for about 2 years, which seemed to stabilize her. However, she recently went off her medication for a few months due to difficulties in getting a new prescription after our move to a new city. She has now resumed taking the medication, but her old symptoms have resurfaced. She believes that certain people are constantly talking about her and plotting against her, which leads to tension and anger within our family. She also seems agitated, upset, and has trouble focusing.

Hello, I’m a 15-year-old girl from India. Lately, I've been experiencing a mix of emotions that have been overwhelming me. I don't quite understand what I'm feeling, but it's been making me feel incredibly sad and worthless. It seems like everything I try to do ends up going wrong, and it's causing me to doubt my abilities. I also feel like my friends don't care about me, and this constant loneliness is making me want to cry. I've tried making friends, but they always end up betraying my trust. It's a sudden change, and it's affecting my ability to focus on anything, including my studies. I'm not sure why I'm feeling like this, and I'm desperate to find a way to overcome these emotions. Can you help me?

I have been dealing with a lifelong struggle of feeling rejected and unloved by my mother. From as far back as I can remember, she showed me no affection and often resorted to physical punishment. She never expressed love or support, and it's been hard for me to understand why. Despite my efforts to win her love by being a well-behaved and successful child, she never treated me the same way she treats my sister. This inequality has caused me a great deal of pain, and it continues to affect me even now. Recently, my family went on a vacation to Rome, but I and my children were left out. It hurts deeply, and I can't comprehend why they would exclude us. This is just one example of the many instances where my mother has hurt me. I've sought therapy for many years, and my therapist suggested confronting my parents. I did so when I was 39, but my mother denied everything and even tried to physically harm me. My father acknowledged their mistreatment but couldn't get my mother to admit it. Now, she tries to hide her animosity towards me but it's still evident. She lies about the things they do for my sister and her family, like the trip to Rome. They claimed they were just visiting to help her, but it turned out to be a lavish vacation. Meanwhile, I live nearby and receive no support. I am a single grandparent raising my grandchildren due to my daughter's health issues, and it's disheartening that they don't offer any assistance. They have also excluded me and my children from their will, while treating my sister as the favorite. Despite all the therapy I've had, I still can't let go of the past because these hurtful actions continue and my mother refuses to acknowledge them or apologize. How can I move forward?

Patient: I'm from Australia and I'm seeking advice on how to support my partner who is struggling with depression. He has had a history of depression, but recently it has been affecting him for the past three months. He tends to overthink situations, which leads to increased stress and difficulty in focusing on his studies. He puts a lot of pressure on himself to succeed and is never satisfied with his work. He often feels guilty or lazy when he's not studying and finds it hard to have fun or feel happy. Lately, he has mentioned that being with me brings him some relief from his worries and makes him happy. However, he's also aware that relying solely on me for happiness is not healthy. He only revealed this to me recently.

Over the winter, I experienced a challenging phase where I struggled with both PTSD and borderline personality disorder. During this time, I had delusions that lasted for about four months. These delusions involved feeling as though there was someone else's presence in my mind. It became so intense that this presence, while in my head, wanted to harm me or even wanted me to harm myself.

I am a child abuse survivor and, unfortunately, I also abused a girl when she was in her early teens. After going through therapy, I reached out to her, admitted my wrongdoing, and took responsibility for my actions. She forgave me and now she wants me to support her by being a listening ear for the abuse and other struggles she has faced. I want to make up for my past mistakes, but I'm not sure if it's the right thing for her to trust me, considering I was once her abuser.

Throughout my life, I have struggled to maintain meaningful friendships. I often feel like I don't connect with people who share my interests, and the friendships I do form tend to fade over time. I feel extremely lonely and lack a sense of direction or meaningful interests. Despite being an attractive young woman, I can't seem to find a fulfilling romantic relationship. This pattern has been present since childhood. Could psychotherapy help me live a more fulfilling and normal life?

I am a 16-year-old boy and I have been struggling with disturbing thoughts about engaging in sexual acts with children between the ages of 10 and 13. I have engaged in inappropriate behavior with younger children in the past, but I am also experiencing these thoughts currently.

I recently discovered that my father has been living with paranoid schizophrenia for the past ten years. However, I only found out about it recently as it was kept hidden from me. Thankfully, his condition doesn't seem to be severe as he doesn't experience suicidal thoughts or hallucinations, from what I've observed. He has been prescribed Abilify to manage his symptoms. However, last summer, his psychiatrist decided to decrease his dosage, possibly due to a change in doctors at the hospital. Since then, his symptoms have resurfaced, and he has been showing increased anxiety, even going as far as labeling certain types of food as poison.

I'm 8 months pregnant and just found out that my boyfriend has been cheating on me for the past 4 months. I decided to forgive him and give our relationship another chance, but now he doubts my commitment. He believes that I only want him back to prevent the other woman, who is also in a relationship, from being with him. I asked him if he would take me back if our roles were reversed, and he said no. This situation has caused me to fall into a state of depression and I've been losing weight, which is concerning for my unborn baby.

Seven years ago, I fell deeply in love with the father of my children. He had been in a long-term relationship for over 18 years, but he cheated on his girlfriend with me. We ended up having two little girls together. He made promises that I was the one he wanted to marry and that he couldn't imagine me being with anyone else. Unfortunately, I believed him and put my own life on hold for him for the past seven years. I even supported him during my second pregnancy, despite him showing little concern for my well-being.

Today I had my first appointment with a psychiatrist. I shared my fears and insecurities with her, including my fear of schizophrenia. She reassured me multiple times that I don't have it. She prescribed Wellbutrin and Klonopin and asked me to try them for a month. I'm unsure if I can trust her opinion since she didn't run any tests for schizophrenia. What are your thoughts? Have any of you taken these medications before? Do they help with panic and fear? I'm also scared of taking medications because I've heard stories of negative experiences and how they can make things worse.

I had been in a relationship with this guy for 4 years and everything seemed fine until recently. He started expressing unhappiness with his life, but assured me it had nothing to do with our relationship. However, he decided to break up with me right before our 4 year anniversary. He claims he still wants me in his life, but ever since the breakup, I've been experiencing trouble sleeping and loss of appetite. The pain from the breakup is affecting me physically. I've been struggling with depression throughout the relationship, and now it feels even worse. I'm not sure what to do anymore and I'm unsure if he genuinely wants me or if I'm just a backup plan in case he changes his mind.

I'm concerned about my daughter's emotional outbursts. Sometimes when we tell her no or raise our voices, she starts crying uncontrollably. It's not like a tantrum, she just sobs and needs to be held. She can't explain why she's crying, she just says "I don't know." She seems fine afterwards, but I worry that her emotions are overwhelming her. Any advice?

I am concerned about my 9-year-old nephew who is being homeschooled. I have noticed that he is often spoken to negatively, and our frequent Facetime conversations have confirmed this. Although it has been said that he has outgrown his "monster phase," his younger brother has now taken on that role, and the older one still receives hurtful comments. On the other hand, I hear the younger one being told "I love you" multiple times a day, but the older one never receives spontaneous expressions of love. His mother seems to constantly criticize him. Additionally, despite having a strong vocabulary and good self-expression skills, he is only starting to sound out words and do simple math problems. He also displays signs of anxiety, and his mother believes it is due to gluten intolerance and OCD rituals.

I've been experiencing some social difficulties lately. I often feel awkward and struggle to respond to others in real-time. It's like my mind is slow and I have trouble paying attention and understanding what people are saying. I find myself zoning out and daydreaming frequently, and I have a habit of asking "what?" to buy myself some extra time to process information.

I have been in a relationship for around 18 months. The girl I am with is wonderful for me. However, lately I have been experiencing conflicting feelings. The longer we spend time together, the more I feel the need for her to leave. I even feel disgusted when we kiss or engage in intimate activities. I don't think it's fair to her, and I want these feelings to go away. We have tried various strategies like getting in better shape and being spontaneous, but nothing has worked. I care about her a lot and I don't want to change her just to make these feelings go away. Should I end the relationship permanently?

I am a 17-year-old boy from Cyprus, currently studying for my university exams. Lately, my mom, who is 51 years old, has been displaying signs of psychological disorders. She used to be a calm and loving person, but now she acts strangely. She can become extremely harsh and insulting towards people, especially plumbers and sellers, when something goes wrong. She also becomes easily angered by even the smallest things. Recently, she had an extreme outburst when my grandma asked her to stay and help. She threw chairs in the air and called me a useless boy when I simply asked if I could go out. Later, she acted as if nothing had happened, but this pattern is becoming more frequent.

About 12 years ago, I sought help from a psychologist for struggles with homicidal thoughts, depression, and insomnia. I was prescribed Celexa, Trazodone, and Resiperdol. Unfortunately, I had to stop seeing the doctor due to the loss of my insurance coverage. Lately, I've been actively searching for him because I believe I still need help and would prefer not to start over with a new therapist. I've had no luck finding him online and I'm feeling desperate to find support. I know I can control these thoughts, but I need guidance and answers before I can't justify the control anymore.

Hi, I'm a 15-year-old student who has been feeling increasingly depressed and unhappy since the beginning of this school year. I find it extremely difficult to talk about my issues with anyone, which has prevented me from seeking a diagnosis for my depression. I've always struggled to open up about my feelings, feeling like a burden and undeserving of sympathy. My self-esteem and self-respect are low, and I often feel ugly, dumb, and worthless. I've also experienced sexual harassment from my friend's dad, which has caused trust issues with men. I've come close to self-harming and my grades are suffering, leading to conflicts with my parents. I feel lost and unsure of what to do, even though my boyfriend suggests seeing a therapist. However, the idea of discussing everything with my parents is overwhelming. I want to stop feeling sad, improve my grades, and prevent further conflict. Can you please advise me on what to do?

I've been noticing that I have trouble remembering a large portion of my childhood and even my time in high school. It's been bothering me because I've heard that this can be common for trauma survivors, but I don't understand why it's happening to me. I think it might be related to an incident when I was 13, where I was almost raped. I repressed that memory and only remembered it in 2013. Since then, I've been afraid of being in a relationship and now I'm planning to live with two male roommates, which I find confusing. I'm wondering if this assault could be the reason for my lack of memories and if there's any way to retrieve them. I've thought about visiting my high school to trigger some memories, but I'm scared because I was severely bullied there. I hope this all makes sense.

I've been struggling with my mental health for a while now. As a 22-year-old male, I've been reflecting on my past and have come to the realization that I may have been sexually molested by my father when I was younger. This realization has brought up a lot of difficult emotions for me, as I've had a challenging childhood marked by low self-esteem, bullying, and a constant sense of shame and guilt. I always felt uncomfortable around my father, fearing his touch and feeling repulsed by him, despite him appearing "nice" and gentle. I also had a strange preoccupation with my own sexual organs and had a fascination with rape. Coming to terms with my homosexuality has also been a struggle. Recently, I was diagnosed with OCD and started taking medication. My main concern now is that I fear my nephew may be at risk of sexual abuse if I allow my father to have close contact with him. I've shared my concerns with my mother and sister. However, what troubles me the most is that I've been experiencing intrusive sexual thoughts and fantasies involving newborn babies and young children, including my nephew. These thoughts are distressing and cause me a great deal of guilt. I want to know if it's common for someone who has experienced molestation to have these thoughts, if they are related to my OCD, and if I should feel guilty about them. I am planning to start therapy, but it may take some time, so I would appreciate any brief answers you can provide in the meantime.

I recently started spending time with someone and I'm feeling unsure about their behavior. They never seem to show any anger, even in situations where it would be expected. Additionally, they make comments about women that are both conversational and demeaning. For example, they referred to a former teacher as a "feminazi" because she made a comment about a gym bag being a "guy thing". This is not the first time I've heard them use this term.

Hello, I'm a 21-year-old who has been regularly smoking marijuana for about a year. It started off infrequently but became more frequent as time went on. Since last winter, I've been facing psychological challenges, feeling insecure and having paranoid thoughts about being excluded by society. I tried to quit after New Year's but have recently started smoking again. I do find some benefits in smoking, like increased creativity and a more relaxed state of mind, but it also brings social insecurities. My best friends are unaware of my habit because I fear their judgment. Lately, I've felt somewhat distant from them and unsure about myself. I wonder if they know about my smoking and exclude me without my knowledge. Additionally, I've been experiencing memory issues. Despite all this, I struggle to quit as I often dismiss these concerns as irrational thoughts. I'm reaching out for help because I feel like I'm losing myself. Any assistance would be greatly appreciated.

I had been seeing my therapist for three years and he had helped me through some really difficult times. However, recently I got very angry with him and ended up firing him. Our sessions had turned into a cycle of trying to prove who was right and feeling wronged. He kept telling me that I was avoiding my anger, but I felt like he was bullying me and trying to make me feel angry at him. I felt hurt and misunderstood. In the past, I had fired him before but always ended up going back because there was something scary I didn't want to talk about. Now, I feel like the relationship is too damaged to continue. Since I fired him, I've actually been feeling more empowered. I've enrolled in school, started taking meditation classes, and have been able to take care of some important tasks that I had been putting off.

Lately, I've been experiencing extreme mood swings that range from intense anger and irritability to feeling completely apathetic and lacking motivation. I also have moments where I feel disconnected from reality, as if I'm observing myself from a distance. I often have a constant sense of emptiness and find myself wanting to consume alcohol excessively, despite not enjoying the feeling of being drunk. I also experience frequent daydreaming episodes and have a high sex drive. I'm currently taking antidepressants for irritability, but I'm unsure if there might be something else going on. I feel like my mind is distorted and I don't know what to do. It's gotten to the point where I don't even care if I died tomorrow, and I'm worried that this isn't normal.

During a day at the spa with my sisters, I had a massage that my sister had booked for me as a gift. However, I felt uncomfortable because the massage therapist was a man, and I usually prefer women. He began talking to me non-stop and making comments about me being special and beautiful. I felt uncomfortable with his touch and the way he was stretching my body instead of giving me the massage I asked for. Although he didn't touch my breasts or buttocks directly, I felt uneasy about his proximity. I froze and didn't know how to react because I came to relax, not for a therapy session. It brought up emotions and memories that I couldn't express myself. I've been feeling depressed and low on energy lately.

I'm a 21-year-old female and I've been dealing with anxiety for as long as I can remember. As a child, I would check everyone's pulse while they were sleeping. I had my anxiety under control until I had a scare about having an STD. Since then, I've been experiencing panic attacks twice a day. I also had a sinus infection and when I googled my symptoms, I became convinced that I was having a stroke. I had weeks of fearing that I would die from a stroke. Now, I'm experiencing sharp pains in my head, shoulder, chest, hands, legs, and feet. I also feel chest tightness and have become obsessed with my heart. I've had an EKG, ECG, CT scan, and X-ray, and they all came back normal. I left the hospital thinking they were lying to me and that I'm dying. I've also had a CT scan and had the same thoughts. I feel like I'm dying every day. I've experienced weird symptoms like tingling, pins and needles, migraines, muscle twitches, and vibrations, even in my head. I also feel chest pressure. I'm having a hard time believing that anxiety can cause all of this. Am I going crazy?

I am a 23-year-old university student who is currently struggling with depression, social anxiety, low self-esteem, and low confidence. I have also been using marijuana as a way to cope. In the past, I have been preoccupied with what others think of me and have sought validation from them by complaining about my life, even though there is nothing actually wrong. However, since leaving home to attend school, my depression has worsened and I have even had thoughts of suicide. I feel like I'm seeking sympathy from others to help me deal with my own issues. I'm looking for advice and help on how to overcome these challenges and navigate life without feeling overwhelmed.

My niece, who is 12 years old, has been living with me and my mom in the Philippines since her parents moved to another city. They left her with us because her mom is currently pregnant with their second child. My niece has always seemed like a typical child - active and curious. However, I have recently noticed that she is struggling with reading and writing. For example, she often confuses the letters 'b' and 'd', and she also writes numbers 4 and 7 in reverse, as well as the letter 'p'.

I recently went through a breakup after dating my boyfriend for 4 months. The reason he gave was that he couldn't accept something about me. Before we started dating, I had opened up to him about being a survivor of childhood sexual abuse. At that time, he seemed fine with it. However, as our relationship progressed, he changed his mind. I am 23 years old and he is 38.

When my niece was an infant and toddler, I noticed that her behavior was different from other children. Some people have even suggested that she might be autistic. It's hard to explain, but she tends to get upset over things that most children wouldn't. For example, she doesn't like it when things are moved or when there are loud noises like the vacuum. She also becomes very upset if someone tries to move a puzzle she's working on or if something isn't exactly the way she wants it to be. Additionally, she gets extremely anxious when someone comes over to the house, even if it's someone she knows.

Throughout my life, I have experienced various forms of abuse and trauma. My family emotionally and psychologically abused me, and at times, it turned physical. Additionally, I was relentlessly bullied from grade school all the way through high school. I have also endured the horrific experiences of being raped three times. It doesn't end there - I was stalked and bullied by one of my rapists, who coerced others into joining in. Lastly, I faced mobbing at a job I remained at for seven years.

I'm a 15-year-old from Canada and I've been struggling to deal with my issues in a healthy way. I'm currently in school, but I've been too afraid to go for the past week. My mom is out of the country and will be back soon, so I'm home alone. My dad lives nearby, but we're not very close. I've been experiencing low moods that are really impacting me, but I also have moments of extreme happiness. I'm not sure if it's a big deal or if it will go away on its own. I'm hesitant to talk to my mom because she didn't take my previous low mood seriously and seemed judgmental. I used to self-injure and when she found out, she said only "crazy" people do that. I don't do it anymore, but her reaction made me doubt myself. I thought about telling my dad, but I'm not sure how he'll react given his beliefs. I also considered talking to my school guidance counselors, but I'm afraid they won't take me seriously or that they'll tell my parents. I don't know who to turn to for help.

I've been struggling with my 8-year-old stepson's behavior for almost a year now. He consistently misbehaves and engages in destructive actions such as stealing items like food, money, and random objects. He has also damaged his room, writing on the walls and creating holes. He displays violent behavior when he doesn't want to do something, resorting to kicking, slapping, and biting. Additionally, he has shown concerning behavior like eating non-food items and talking to himself in strange voices. He also engages in unsanitary behaviors like playing with his feces and urinating on the walls. He struggles with communication, often speaking like a 3-year-old or struggling to express himself, frequently repeating himself and starting from the beginning. He tends to be manipulative and lacks empathy towards others, but becomes overly emotional when it relates to himself. He exhibits bossy and mean behavior towards those who are mentally challenged, younger, or smaller, including pets. However, his behavior at school seems to be different, as his teachers have never reported any issues.

I've been experiencing recurring nightmares for about a month now. In these dreams, I find myself alone with someone in a dark place, and I am repeatedly stabbing them uncontrollably. I wake up around that point. Additionally, I have disturbing thoughts where I have a strong desire to harm people, regardless of who they are. I am drawn to the sensation and smell of blood, and I even recall killing small animals, although I can't fully remember doing it. Am I crazy or is this a regular problem? I've had these experiences since I was young, starting with harming a dying bird, which oddly felt good. I find it difficult to talk about this in person, so I appreciate being able to share it in writing. I've also been struggling with thoughts of suicide, although I haven't been able to go through with it.

I'm feeling frustrated with my boyfriend's decreased interest in pleasuring me sexually. He used to bring me to orgasm frequently, but now he rarely puts in the effort. I'm not sure if this is related to his recent diagnosis of depression, his lack of confidence due to my difficulty reaching orgasm, or if it's just a natural progression in our relationship. I want to know how to address this issue without upsetting him or making him feel inadequate because of his illness.

I've been feeling increasingly agitated and it seems like my life is falling apart. I used to be motivated and excited about life, but now I struggle to sleep, getting only about 28 hours of sleep a week. I've lost all motivation and find it difficult to focus on my college work. I've been relying on smoking weed to relax and quiet my racing thoughts. I have no friends and find it hard to be myself around others, except when I'm alone. I think I may have a memory of being abused, but I'm not sure if it's real or just a bad dream that has stuck with me. I haven't had a meaningful relationship with anyone in years, and I don't trust anyone. I just want to feel normal again, but I don't want anyone to know that I'm struggling. Things have never been this bad before, and I'm going down a dark path. I can't stop these thoughts from constantly running through my head. Do you have any idea what could be wrong with me?

Over the past two years, I have been struggling with depression. Lately, I have been experiencing nightmares and daydreams that bring back memories of a past traumatic event that I witnessed. These episodes leave me feeling terrified and I often wake up crying and sweaty. Additionally, I have been having physical symptoms like aching in my chest, and I find myself crying for no apparent reason. I know it's not a heart problem because I have seen a doctor, but my mom dismisses it as just a "phase." I have also been feeling constantly angry and irritable, even in situations where I should be happy. Sometimes, I have thoughts that maybe I should just let something bad happen to me, although I wouldn't actively harm myself. I have been asking my mom to help me find a therapist, but she hasn't taken any action yet, despite my reminders. I'm not sure how to get her to actually get me the help I need.

I have been experiencing ongoing harassment and discrimination at work due to assumptions about my sexual orientation. It's causing me a lot of distress and I feel stuck because nothing I do seems to make it better. It's even affecting my ability to keep a job. I feel frustrated and hopeless, especially because no one is willing to stand up for me or provide any evidence to support my case. It's disheartening to see how people can be so two-faced and cruel. It's gotten so bad that I've even started having violent thoughts, which worries me. What should I do?

I have been in a complicated situation with my best friend. We developed strong feelings for each other while I was already in a long-term relationship. Despite the distance, we kept in constant contact after my friend moved away three years ago. I made the decision to end my previous relationship and planned to move in with my friend, but I got cold feet and went back to my ex. Now, I deeply regret my actions and want to regain my friend's trust. However, he doesn't want me to contact him until he is ready. I'm torn between reaching out and respecting his wishes. Is there anything I can do to show him that I am sincere and trustworthy?

My son is 19 years old and lately, he has been withdrawing from our family. He never had a close relationship with his father, but we used to be very close. Over the past few years, I've noticed a change in him. It started around the time of his school pictures, but whenever I mentioned it, he denied needing any help. As time went on, things got worse. He became manipulative towards me, always twisting things to make me see it his way and shifting blame onto others. Recently, he went through a breakup and it seemed to trigger a downward spiral. He started drinking, but since many young men in our town do, he tries to pass it off as normal. However, I've noticed him drinking alone in his room and going to his friend's house frequently. It's starting to make me worry that he has a problem with alcohol. I've tried talking to him about getting help, but he refuses and even blames me for ruining his life, though I'm not sure what I did. He rarely speaks to me and when he's home, he isolates himself in his room. He's very vocal about hating our home, his life, and the town we live in. I'm convinced that he's depressed, but I can't seem to get through to him. How can I help him realize this? Should I just wait until he hurts himself? Since he's 19, I can't force him to do anything. The other night, I told him that if he doesn't change his behavior, he needs to find a new place to live. I was met with anger and he called me a horrible mother for even suggesting it.

Hi, I'm a senior in high school and I'm struggling with a few things. Firstly, I find it difficult to be social because I have a fear of rejection. I think this stems from being adopted and I often think about my birth mom. I also feel disconnected from my adopted parents and find it hard to open up to them. Additionally, I experience extreme mood swings, going from happy to depressed within a short period of time. When I'm sad, it can last for days and sometimes I feel numb afterwards. I've had thoughts of not wanting to live anymore, although I've never attempted suicide. I haven't shared any of this with my adopted parents and I'm feeling lost about what to do.

Over the past three years, I have engaged in sexual relationships with five different guys. I'm only 16 years old, and I'm feeling a lot of self-hatred because of it. I constantly find myself regretting these encounters, as the guys always end up leaving afterwards. I don't understand why I keep doing this to myself. I think I crave sex because it helps me feel connected to someone, and I'm tired of being alone. I've tried to stop this behavior, but it's difficult because I've never had a real relationship before. I know deep down that giving in to sexual encounters won't lead to a meaningful relationship, but a part of me still believes it will. I'm disappointed in myself because I used to have a purity ring. I desperately want to change, but I don't know how. I give in too easily and have unrealistic expectations. I feel like there's something wrong with me because I not only desire sex, but also enjoy being treated roughly, even though I know it's not okay. I recognize that there's an issue with my thought patterns, and I'm seeking help to fix it. Can someone please assist me?

I have been diagnosed with Bipolar II with Psychotic Features and I have been experiencing auditory and visual hallucinations recently. Today, it escalated to a point where I had a vivid and uncontrollable mental "movie" of someone holding my arm and about to harm me with a knife. Although I knew deep down that it wasn't real, I still felt scared. Shortly after, I saw an image of the grim reaper behind me, threatening to harm me. It felt distressingly real, even though I knew it wasn't. I've had similar experiences before. Can this be considered psychosis or is it something else entirely?

I recently started dating a guy that I've known for almost a year. He has had feelings for me for a while, and I finally decided to give the relationship a try. I genuinely think he's an amazing person, and I'm happy to be with him. However, I've been experiencing a lot of anxiety when it comes to physical intimacy beyond cuddling, hugging, and holding hands.
Patient's Statement:

I have been struggling with depression for the past 5 years. I have tried various medications, including anti-depressants, anti-anxiety medications, and ones for psychosis, but none of them have provided any relief. I have also tried engaging in hobbies, exercising, and adopting a healthier diet, but nothing seems to help. Over time, my depression has worsened in severity. Additionally, I have been experiencing a sense of unreality in myself and my environment, although I'm unsure if it's related to my depression. I have been feeling this way since I was 14, and now that I'm approaching 20, I find myself frequently thinking about suicide. I have been admitted to a crisis stabilization unit five times already. I have tried various avenues in life, but they all seem futile, and I can't help but feel that life is meaningless. I had two MRI scans a few years ago, and they showed no abnormalities, so this is not due to any neurological issues. I have tried different medications, counseling, and even holistic approaches, but I am running out of options. I feel increasingly miserable and don't see any clear cause for my feelings. I don't expect this website to magically resolve everything, but I thought it was worth a try.

I've never been in a relationship and I'm struggling to understand why. I've been a party girl since I was 14 and I have a lot of friends who like me. I've talked to many guys, but never had a serious relationship. Lately, I've only been interested in casual sex and don't seem to care about guys' feelings. But sometimes I do want a relationship, and when I start developing feelings, I push them away and cut off contact. It's frustrating and makes me cry. My friends and family don't understand, and I'm scared of commitment. This fear extends to other areas of my life too, like jobs and school. I've also struggled with depression and ended up in a psych ward after attempting suicide. I joined a therapy group and it helped a lot. I've been feeling better and no longer have suicidal thoughts. I was also diagnosed with ADHD, but I know that doesn't explain my fear of relationships. I'm just very confused.

I have been struggling with self-harm and depression, and I'm considering seeking therapy. However, I don't want my parents to find out about my struggles. I've seen a therapist in the past for social anxiety, and I was thinking of asking my parents to take me to another therapist for that reason, but it's really the depression that I want to address. Can I go to therapy without my parents knowing about my depression and self-harm, even though I'm not currently self-harming? Would the therapist be obligated to inform my parents about my depression? I want to make sure I understand what the therapist would have to disclose to my parents before I proceed. It's important to me that my parents don't find out because it could cause them stress and pain, and I've worked hard to keep it a secret for this long. I'm 17 years old. Thank you for your guidance.

Hi, I’m 14 years old and in the 8th grade. I came here because my anger has been really overwhelming me and causing problems. Like usually when I’m angry I think about hurting these people in horrible ways or hurting myself sometimes even and this scares me a lot. I’ve even thought about killing someone and planned it out in my head and this is terrifying to me? I mean its something I’d never actually do like I couldn’t probably bring myself to do it because I am not a violent person whatsoever, but i definitely think it. I think maybe it’s because I’m young or if there’s another possible problem I really want to know. I’ve told my mom sometimes I think violent things when I’m really angry, but I never elaborated off that. I’m scared she’ll send me to some mental institution or something. I just want to stop thinking like this. I’m scared that one day I just might act on it.

Counselor's response: Thank you for sharing your concerns and providing some background information about your experiences. It sounds like you have been through a lot with your recent diagnosis of schizophrenia and your struggles with substance abuse. It's great to hear that you are attending AA meetings regularly and have made progress in your sobriety.

I've been in a relationship with my girlfriend for ten months now. We moved quickly because we've known each other for years and she moved in with me after a couple of months. She treats me really well and I can't imagine anyone else treating me better. But lately, I've been having second thoughts and it's hard for me because she's such an amazing person.

My daughter, Sally, is 14 years old and she has been experiencing some unusual symptoms for about a year now. She has been seeing shapes floating in the air, hearing music, radio static, footsteps, and people whispering. She also mentions having "thoughts" in her head that talk about things she's doing, things our family is doing, sometimes upsetting or random things. These experiences are causing her a lot of anxiety, agitation, and stress. In addition, she experiences periods of depression. Sally has difficulty communicating with others and struggles to see things from perspectives other than her own. She has always had some level of paranoia, but I didn't realize how much it was affecting her until recently. She has been prescribed Prozac, a low dose of Risperidone, and Clonidine, but we haven't seen much improvement. I'm wondering if there are any diagnostic possibilities or ideas that could help us understand what she's going through.

I have been seeing my therapist for a while now, and I have developed some feelings towards him. He's younger than me, still in school to finish his masters. He's attractive, smart, and charming, and I find myself thinking about him outside of our sessions. He has complimented me and made me feel good about myself, but he has also made comments that seem more personal, like looking forward to our sessions and calling them "little sessions." Sometimes he seems distant and brings paperwork to our sessions. I know about transference, so I haven't expressed my feelings to him. I'm just wondering if this is appropriate or if I should be concerned. We have some similarities, and he has mentioned that too. I would appreciate any advice or input you can provide. Thank you.

Hi! I am currently a junior in a Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) program. Nursing school can be quite demanding, and I'm experiencing a lot of anxiety lately. Despite my efforts to stay organized and manage my time well, I always feel like I'm not doing enough. I spend a significant amount of time studying and often find myself re-reading the same material multiple times out of fear of missing something important. It feels like a waste of time, but I can't shake the feeling that I'll fail if I don't do it. School has become my top priority, and I even sacrifice sleep to complete my to-do lists. I rely on adrenaline and Adderall to keep me going. While I scored well on my first exam, I felt disappointed. And when I received two B grades on subsequent exams, I was disgusted with myself. I know I should be more accepting of these grades, but I keep telling myself that I can and should do better. At night, I struggle to fall asleep as I constantly think about my to-do lists and what I need to study. I feel guilty when I try to have fun because I believe I should be studying instead. I'm constantly afraid of failing and never feeling good enough. My friends admire my organization skills and dedication, but I wish I could be more relaxed like them and still perform well academically. Unfortunately, the only way I can truly relax when I'm with them is by drinking, which I know is not a healthy coping mechanism. I always feel ashamed the next day. Additionally, I find that my leg is constantly shaking, and it becomes embarrassing when others notice and comment on it. I've been considering talking to my primary care physician about anxiety medication on an as-needed basis, but I'm hesitant due to the addictive nature of medications like Xanax. I just want to be able to sleep without stress or guilt, and maybe have some help before exams to alleviate my constant need to re-read and second-guess myself. I often feel like I take longer to complete tasks compared to others because of my perfectionism, but I wonder if maybe I need to lower my standards a bit. Maybe I don't need to color-coordinate my notes all the time, but in my mind, not doing so feels like it would guarantee failure. It even gives me a rapid heartbeat (tachycardia) when I don't complete an assignment to my high standards, even if it's objectively "good enough" to pass. I also have this issue with odd numbers, where everything has to be in even numbers or I fear something bad will happen. It's been a lifelong quirk that my family jokes about, but it's become increasingly anxiety-provoking this semester because it always seems to tie back to potential failure. I'm just tired of feeling constantly on edge and like a failure, and I feel like I've lost control over everything in my life.

Over the past year, I've experienced a series of difficult events that have left me feeling lost and depressed. I lost a family member, had to move from one parent's home to live with the other and their stepfamily, and have been struggling to find a job despite having good qualifications. I feel hopeless and useless, and all I want to do is escape from my problems. I've been isolating myself, spending most of my time alone in my room and questioning my worth. I recently took a "Sanity Score" and the result was shocking to me.

I have been through a long and difficult journey of coming to terms with the emotional and psychological abuse I experienced growing up, which was sometimes accompanied by physical abuse. It has been particularly challenging for me since becoming a parent myself. Additionally, when I was 17, my older sisters had involvement with a rape, and I was subjected to further degradation and humiliation by my perpetrators. I feel a deep sense of ugliness and worthlessness as a result.

Patient: I have been experiencing intrusive thoughts that are violent and sexual in nature. I'm really scared and don't know why I'm having these thoughts. I have heard that it could be related to OCD and anxiety, which I know I have. When these thoughts come up, I feel out of control and it's really distressing. I'm afraid to tell a therapist because I don't want to be locked up, and I'm also worried about acting on these thoughts. They are taking over my life and I'm not eating or sleeping properly. Please give me some advice.

I've always known that I am an introvert, but recently I had an experience at school that made me feel even more self-conscious about it. During a personality test in class, I was labeled as an introvert, and a girl behind me made a comment about it. Now, I feel like being an introvert is even harder in high school. My friends don't understand why I need alone time, and I'm dreading an upcoming presentation because I get so nervous speaking in front of the class. It feels like nobody gets why I prefer writing or reading over public speaking.

I used to struggle with depression, especially during the time I was being bullied. I'm currently in 10th grade and have been homeschooled for a year now. I've noticed that my depression has improved, although I still experience occasional episodes that last a few hours to a few days. Strangely, I find myself missing the intensity of my depression at times. I don't know why, but I wish I could feel that way again. While I'm not very happy now, I do feel more happiness than sadness, which for some reason, I don't like. Can you help me understand why I feel this way?

Patient's statement (revised): Lately, my 3-year-old son has been showing interest in his genitalia. At first, we ignored it, thinking it was just a phase. However, he has started trying to touch between my legs and saying inappropriate things like "I'm touching your penis." We've been correcting him and telling him that it's not appropriate behavior. While this behavior has slowed down, he continues to say it to my mother-in-law when he visits her. I'm not sure how to handle this situation. Should we continue to ignore it and treat it as a phase?

Patient's statement (rewritten): I have been struggling with my mental health, including epilepsy, severe anxiety, depression, and bulimia. My mother, who went through a severe depression in her early 40s, has been unsupportive and insensitive towards me. She is reluctant to provide the same level of support that I provided to her during her depression. She seems dismissive of my feelings and tells me that I should be over my struggles by now. It is also difficult for me to discuss my past experiences of abuse with her as she refuses to engage in those conversations. Despite her help with my son and financial support, her attitude towards me is hurtful and I feel that she prioritizes my father over my well-being.

Since I was 16 years old, I have been experiencing ongoing music in my head that I sometimes believe others can hear. Lately, I have also been having brief episodes where I see things that appear to be crawling like bugs. Additionally, I go through periods of feeling very depressed and crying, followed by moments where I feel better. I tend to be more of an introvert and sometimes find it difficult to respond or give a blank stare when someone tries to talk to me. Could these be signs of schizophrenia?

I'm a 14-year-old who has been struggling with an eating disorder since November of 2012. It started with occasional purging after meals, but then I started restricting my food intake to only 600-800 calories a day while still making myself vomit. I also have been experiencing feelings of overwhelm, suicidal thoughts, and self-harm. About six months ago, I stopped all these behaviors because I didn't want my boyfriend to be upset. However, recently I've been obsessing over calories again and not eating enough. I eat around 1000 calories a day, but it makes me feel panicked and faint. I have a lot of self-hatred and feel fat. Unfortunately, I can't seek professional help without my family finding out, and they are unsupportive. Is it possible to recover without professional help? If so, how can I do it?

Since I was young, I have always had intense anxiety and fears about being murdered. It consumes my thoughts, especially with all the news about horrific murders in society. The fear is so overwhelming that I constantly worry about my family and myself being brutally killed, particularly with knives or axes. Even the sight of a knife in my father's hand triggers a panic reaction. I feel completely out of control and vulnerable, as if anyone could easily harm me. At night, I lie in bed imagining someone coming up the stairs to kill me. I have to check my room multiple times before I can even try to sleep. I can't be alone in the house, even during the day, because I believe being murdered is inevitable. Even something as simple as taking a shower is filled with thoughts of being harmed. It has escalated to the point where I stay awake at night, crying, and feel the need to wake up my father for reassurance.

When I was 13 years old, I started stealing money from my parents' bank account. It started with 50 pounds, but it got worse over time. In January of this year, I stole a total of 400 pounds. My family doesn't have a lot of money, so I feel incredibly guilty and ashamed of myself. My dad even threatened to put me into care and called me names like liar, cheat, and fraud. It hurt so much to hear that from him. That's why I'm here, I need help and someone to talk to because I no longer feel welcome in my own home. I know it took me a while to seek help, but I'm begging for someone to assist me and provide guidance. I really need help!

Over the past few years, I have been diagnosed with Borderline Personality Disorder, but after multiple hospital admissions, my diagnosis was changed to Type 2 Bipolar Disorder. About a year ago, I gave birth to my son and initially managed my mild depression fairly well. However, the challenges of adjusting to a new routine and taking care of a young child led me to stop taking my medication, despite my doctor's concerns. Recently, I've been feeling quite low, although I'm not sure if it's depression. I have no motivation to do anything, I feel distant from my son, my appetite has decreased, and I have a sense of hopelessness.

Patient's statement (edited): I am seeking guidance on how to approach my husband, who has recently been diagnosed with PTSD following years of alcohol and drug abuse. He is normally a loving man, but he undergoes sudden changes and distances himself from me and his loved ones. In the past, I would remove myself from the situation due to the accompanying abuse, thinking it was solely an alcohol problem. However, after his last episode, where he was nearly fatal, we had a heartfelt conversation where he explained his episodes and we made a pact for me to continue showing affection and support despite his rejections. I was able to get him to see a doctor, leading to his PTSD diagnosis. But now, I feel like I've lost him again. It's as if he's a different person during these episodes and he can't remember being in that state. He only remembers the aftermath. His trust in me has diminished because of my reactions to his behavior. He has found someone who enables his codependency and doesn't trigger his trauma, but it has led to increased alcohol consumption. Last week, he experienced psychosis and reached out to me in a frantic state, shouting for help. I fear that my attempts to contact him are making things worse. This is a life-threatening situation, and I feel lost without any guidance on what to do and what not to do.

Lately, I've been noticing that I don't really experience strong emotions. For example, when my great aunt passed away last week, I didn't feel sad at all. And even though I just got an offer for my first job, I don't feel excited. I mean, I'm generally happy, but it's like a vague feeling. During the day, everything seems fine, but at night, I have this indescribable feeling that's kind of sad. I really want to figure out why I feel like this. Any insights or advice you have would be greatly appreciated.

I am a 22-year-old from Canada who is struggling with anxiety and depression. Recently, I've become concerned that I may also have OCD and bipolar disorder. I feel very isolated as I am a virgin, have no friends, and often have thoughts of wanting to die. I can't understand why I am so unlikeable. I always try my best at work and worry about making mistakes. Despite receiving praise from my managers and coworkers, I still feel incredibly low and have no one to talk to.

During my childhood, I faced numerous challenges, such as persistent bullying at school and difficulties managing my anger. These experiences left me feeling isolated and alone. However, there is something else that has been troubling me for a long time. I have been hearing a woman's voice inside my head. It starts off quietly, almost like a whisper, but then gradually grows louder. This voice gives me random commands that make no sense, like telling me to go downstairs. Additionally, I have this strange obsession with believing that I am thousands of years old and some sort of demigod. I understand that some people may dismiss these experiences as an over-active imagination, but the latter part of this continued until I was about 15 years old.

I have been struggling with controlling my anger, even over small issues. I tend to rush through tasks and have a difficult time being patient. If I don't get exactly what I want, I become angry, and sometimes I even behave poorly towards my husband. I have a habit of tearing up my clothes, books, or throwing my mobile when I'm angry. However, after a few minutes, I feel really down and low about everything. I work as a researcher, and I find it hard to tolerate this emotional state for a long period of time. Initially, I enjoyed my job, but now I feel frustrated. Can you please give me some suggestions on how to overcome this?

As a child, I experienced a series of distressing and frightening experiences that have left me with unanswered questions. One particular experience involved a hand-like figure attached to a toy with wheels. Whenever someone stared at a spot for too long, I believed it would trigger the hand to appear and harm me. I also heard the sound of a train passing by, despite not living near any train tracks. I would feel a tickling sensation on my feet and see a bulge at the bottom of my bed, which would then try to strangle me when I uncovered my feet. These experiences, along with hearing voices and having hallucinations, made it difficult for me to sleep at night. I have many other unresolved issues from my childhood, but I would appreciate any insights you can provide on what may have caused these specific experiences.

I have been dealing with severe depression for most of my life, and it has taken a toll on my well-being. Alongside that, I struggle with binge eating and as a result, I am now super morbidly obese. For the past 8 years, I have been on disability, but during that time, I took the opportunity to enroll in the pass plan which allowed me to receive training as a jeweler. I got a job at Tiffany and despite the initial mistreatment and bullying, I worked hard and eventually became a trainer myself. However, the bullying has taken a toll on my mental health and I've had to involve HR twice. I feel torn because I don't want to leave the supportive colleagues I have, but the mistreatment is becoming unbearable. On top of all this, my fiancée is in a different country due to work and we have been apart for three years. We plan to get married in July, but I need their support now. I feel empty and unloved, and I constantly fluctuate between functioning well and feeling completely broken. I'm tired of fighting for everything in my life and all I really want is to be loved and accepted. How do I hold on? What can I do when therapy and medication don't seem to help? Why can't I be normal and just be treated like everyone else?

I have noticed a pattern of behavior where I tend to betray others' trust to protect myself or shift the blame onto someone else. This recently happened at work when I was planning to take a group of students to a hockey game. A coworker I like expressed concern about me handling all the kids, and ended up reporting the situation to the office. When one of the teachers who was supposed to take their own students confronted me, instead of being honest and saying I didn't know how the information got out, I implicated my coworker. I feel like I betrayed their trust and I'm really angry at myself for doing that.

I have been diagnosed with Autism and I am currently in a relationship with a man. We also have two children together. Lately, I've been having distressing dreams about sexual abuse involving my partner and one of our children. I know deep down that these dreams are not real, but the feelings they evoke are incredibly intense and realistic. This isn't the first time I've had these thoughts - I experienced similar concerns when our first child was born, who is now 3 years old, and our second child is 5 months old. I want to emphasize that I truly believe my partner would never harm our children or me, as he is a dedicated provider and my best friend. However, these dreams are causing significant distress and confusion, making it difficult for me to distinguish between reality and imagination. I unintentionally accused him today due to these intrusive thoughts, and I am unsure how to undo the damage. Is there any way to make these thoughts go away? Also, I was sexually abused as a child - could this be related to my current experiences?
Lately, I've been having frequent disagreements with my mother. It's becoming increasingly difficult for me to find someone to lean on for support. Our most recent argument happened last night.

I'm a 61-year-old woman and my boyfriend, who is also 61, keeps in touch with his ex-girlfriends on Facebook. They don't know about me, and they make comments about how handsome he still is, and even private message him. It upsets me that they don't know about me, even though he tells me he loves me. He claims it's not a big deal and that I should trust him. How can I get past this and what more can I do?

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for almost 7 years. When things are going well, everything feels perfect. However, I have an issue with his lying and his reaction when I catch him in the act. I've caught him in various situations such as seeing another girl daily for a year, skyping girls from our church, and even holding hands with a girl who messaged him on chat roulette while we were on a break. I've expressed my disapproval of him interacting with random girls, but he continues to lie and be around girls who are potentially problematic. I've made mistakes too, but I've always been honest and open with him. It's concerning to me that he lies about everything and doesn't seem to show remorse when caught. I love him deeply, but I'm unsure how to approach him about this. I need guidance on how to communicate with him effectively.

Throughout my life, I have experienced emotional, physical, and sexual abuse from my mother. This abuse has caused a strain in our relationship, leading to her not speaking to me for the past two years. From the moment I was born, it seemed that my mother harbored a deep dislike towards me, and this sentiment was evident to the entire family. She even went as far as spreading false stories about me, which ultimately resulted in me losing my entire family. I strongly believe that she may have Narcissistic Personality Disorder (NPD), as she consistently made me the scapegoat for her own issues. Additionally, it is important to note that my sister had her three children taken away by the state due to her neglect and abuse, which I believe is part of the generational cycle of harm that our mother inflicted upon us, as she should have been our protector.

I have been feeling really overwhelmed and frustrated lately. My husband and I both work for my parents in our family business. While my parents have always been somewhat difficult to deal with, we used to be able to work things out. But recently, my husband has been getting criticized constantly for every little thing he does. It's not just at work, but also at home. They criticize our choice of house, his parenting skills, his education level, and more. It's getting to the point where every other day at work, he is told everything he's doing wrong and never receives any positive feedback. It's also frustrating for me because my parents never comment on any mistakes I make, but they bring up all of his mistakes to me and my sister.

A few months ago, I had an incident where I ended up in the hospital due to excessive drinking. I made the decision to quit drinking after that, but since then, some of my old friends have distanced themselves from me. They even sent me a note saying they don't want to hang out anymore. It's been really tough for me since then. I was already feeling embarrassed about what happened, but their rejection just made me feel even worse. I've never really dealt with depression before, but I've been feeling a lot of shame and self-hatred since then, and I can't seem to recover from it.

I'm 17 years old and I've been in a relationship with my girlfriend for a year now. We recently found out that she is pregnant, and I'm happy about it. However, our families have different reactions to the news. While her parents are understanding and supportive, my parents seem to be handling it differently. They are not being as supportive and seem more concerned about their own image by wanting to keep it a secret and imposing strict rules. This has been an ongoing issue with them even before the pregnancy. It's just hard because our society is changing, but my parents have traditional values.

I am a 20-year-old individual from the United States who recently got married to a U.S. citizen. However, I am not a citizen myself and have been experiencing symptoms of depression. These symptoms include feelings of emptiness, loneliness, despair, as well as sleeping and eating problems. These depressive symptoms have been ongoing but have been worsening lately. I am currently under a lot of pressure to obtain a U.S. driver's license and my green card in order to be able to work. Despite wanting to progress in life and accomplish these goals, I am struggling to find the motivation to even get out of bed in the morning.

Patient: In 2008, I was diagnosed with bipolar disorder with psychosis after experiencing auditory hallucinations for almost a year. After about 1 1/2 to 2 years of taking medication, the voices stopped. However, after having a baby and about a year and a half later, the voices returned. They are even more malevolent and cruel than before. Medication doesn't seem to be effective, although it slightly helps me cope. I have been diagnosed with several conditions including severe separation anxiety, PTSD, dissociation, and possibly more. Can dissociation and anxiety really cause these very real voices? They constantly torment me, accuse me of terrible things, humiliate me, threaten to harm me, and repeatedly ask the same questions for the past two years. They even claim that I'm psychic. Why won't this end? I'm in therapy and regularly see a psychiatrist, but it's unbearable. I can hardly function anymore. Sometimes I find myself responding to the voices out loud in public and then I realize I may seem crazy, which triggers panic attacks. Please help me.

I've been struggling with compulsive lying for as long as I can remember. It started off as harmless, but recently, my lies have crossed boundaries and caused a lot of pain in my life. I recently got engaged, and I had to come clean about everything to my partner. I feel so weak and heartbroken for hurting him. I don't understand why I do this, as nothing terrible has happened to me in the past. I feel broken and lost, especially with the added stress of university. I need help to understand and overcome this behavior.

Before my husband and I got married, he had a close female friend. They have a history of supporting each other through various challenges, such as dealing with family deaths, financial struggles, work issues, and even marital problems in her own marriage. They were also co-workers at the time.

Over the past two years, I have been struggling with ending my relationship with my boyfriend of 6 years. There is a significant age gap between us, as I am 28 and he is 52. I want to leave him because not only of the age difference, but also because of his jealousy, constant suspicion, flirting with other women, and lack of common interests. I did leave our shared home after living together for four years, but the separation has not made the breakup any easier. I realize I am emotionally attached to him, and it complicates matters further because we work at the same company and he is close friends with my mother, which defines my social life.

My name is Amy and I’m a 14 year old girl. I’ve been struggling with some difficult challenges lately and I was hoping to get some guidance from you. Last year, when I was 13, I experienced bullying which led to a diagnosis of depression, anxiety, and psychosis. I was prescribed risperdal and it has helped me significantly, but now I find myself conflicted about taking it. Part of me feels like I still need it, while another part thinks I don't. I've been feeling overwhelmed and sometimes even have thoughts of suicide as a way to escape. I've been neglecting my medication as a form of punishment and have been caught up in thoughts of an alternative reality where I feel accepted. It's been tough at school too, as people view me differently because of what happened. I feel like my life is completely messed up. Can you offer any advice?

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for 8 months now, and we are currently living together in a small studio apartment. Both of us have struggled with trust issues - he has been hurt in the past, and I have developed trust issues because he has lied to me and hidden things from me. A few months into our relationship, I discovered that he had been frequently talking to other girls on social media and having them text him. He would delete the messages, and whenever I confronted him about it, he would become defensive. About a month ago, I looked through his phone again and found out that he had still been talking to other girls, even after he had assured me he wasn't. When I confronted him, he admitted that he lied because he knew I would be upset. I'm really struggling to understand why he would do this if he truly loves me. I am able to control myself, so why can't he? He says he wants to regain my trust, but whenever I ask him questions, he becomes defensive and it feels like he's still hiding things. I don't know if I should stay or leave. It seems like he's not putting in enough effort to rebuild my trust, and it's making me question if he still feels the same way about me. I'm feeling unsure and confused. Can you provide some insight?

Patient: I'm a 35-year-old woman, married to a 41-year-old man. When we go out and see other women on the streets, I feel a lot of jealousy. I trust my husband and know he's faithful, but I still get really annoyed and end up taking my anger out on him. Sometimes I accuse him of looking at other women, even when I know he didn't. This often leads to fights between us.

I am a 22-year-old woman who recently graduated from college and I am currently living with my parents. I have been struggling to find employment and it has been causing me a lot of stress. Today, my mom's friend called with a potential job opportunity for me. After making a small comment about someone who bothers me, my mom became extremely upset and has been yelling at me all day. This is not the first time something like this has happened and it's really taking a toll on my mental health. I have been feeling very overwhelmed and have even had thoughts of suicide. The only thing keeping me going is my friends, who are aware of what I'm going through. I have never been diagnosed, but I think I may be experiencing some stress disorders. I'm running out of ways to handle my mom's constant yelling and any help or advice would be greatly appreciated.

My brother committed suicide in 2012, and lately, I've been feeling like I can relate to how he must have felt. I'm frustrated with my work and my home life, even though I love my family. It feels like nothing brings me happiness anymore.

I've been seeing my psychotherapist for almost 10 years and overall, she has been caring and insightful. However, I've noticed that when I discuss issues involving other people, she tends to give them the benefit of the doubt. For example, when I confronted a coworker about standing me up, my therapist suggested that she might have been telling the truth. This pattern has frustrated me to the point where I've considered quitting therapy. My therapist initially responded by suggesting that I focus on finding evidence before making assumptions, but she has since acknowledged my concerns and promised to be more mindful. I feel angry and resentful towards her, and I'm not sure if I should find a new therapist or if we can work through this together. I have anxiety about discussing issues with others, as I fear my therapist will automatically side with them. Can we move past this or is it time for a change?

Throughout my life, I have dealt with both seizure disorders and depression. Despite these challenges, I have managed to maintain my daily routine and not allow them to hinder me. My mother, who has also struggled with her mental health, has been taking medication such as Xanax or Zoloft for many years. She is encouraging me to consider medication as well.

I'm feeling really conflicted about my fiancé's relationship with his estranged father. They recently reconnected after over 20 years apart, and it's been difficult for me to trust his father's intentions. His father has a history of abandoning his children, drug use, and relying on others for support. I worry that he may be seeking a relationship with my fiancé for monetary reasons.

I've been struggling with a lot of issues lately. I am currently seeing a therapist, but I find myself lying to them frequently. Firstly, I have trouble sleeping through the night and spend a lot of time on the internet during the day and night. My sleep schedule is very irregular, often sleeping until midday. Secondly, I have a strong sexual appetite that I can't seem to satisfy. I engage in explicit conversations with multiple women online and enjoy treating them poorly. It gives me a sense of detachment and amusement. Thirdly, I am currently unemployed and living with my father. My parents have been divorced for years, and I believe this has contributed to my fear of marriage. Additionally, I have an extreme fear of commitment and avoid any emotional aspects in my sexual relationships. I also have a tendency to belittle others and feel superior to them, despite hating myself and frequently contemplating suicide. I come from a wealthy background, but the expectations placed on me are overwhelming. I have very few friends and prefer to spend time alone rather than going out with my family. I often feel bored and experience intense anger, frustration, and guilt. I have engaged in morally questionable actions and have a tendency to fight and hurt others, only to feel guilt afterward. I smoke, but I do not heavily drink or use drugs. I was also bullied in school. I feel incredibly lonely and the motorcycle I used to ride provided a temporary sense of excitement until I crashed it and couldn't afford to fix it. I feel like I have no one to turn to and am constantly emotionally and physically isolated. I have mixed feelings about my parents, as my mother has always been distant and I feel more connected to my father.

Over the past two years, I have been in a relationship with an amazing guy and we are living together. However, I have been struggling with trust issues, even though he has never given me a reason to doubt him. I have a history of trust and anxiety issues that have worsened since being with him. I constantly analyze his actions and words, always finding a way to make it about him leaving me. We have talked about it and he understands, but he can't solve these issues for me since they are mine. I also find myself worrying excessively about our relationship and everyday things, blowing them out of proportion. Is there anything I can do to gain control over my anxiety and stop worrying so much?

I have been experiencing the presence of an additional voice in my mind since I was 14 years old. This coincided with a traumatic event where my friends treated me very poorly. The voice is internal and I recognize it as my own, but the thoughts it produces are not mine.

I was in a long-distance relationship and when I went to visit my partner, he accused me of cheating on him. I have never been unfaithful and I would never do that to him or anyone else. He was going through a difficult time in his life and didn't feel worthy of me. Now, he doesn't trust me and we've broken up. We both still love each other, but he can't move past this trust issue. It's been five years since this happened and his ex-wife cheating on him has made it even harder. We were so happy together, and I don't know what to do. How can I regain his trust or convince him that I never cheated?

Sometimes throughout the day, I experience sudden flashes or images of myself in situations where I could be seriously injured or even die. These flashes seem to come out of nowhere and there's no consistency in when they happen. It's like I'm seeing them while I'm still awake and they are intrusive thoughts that I don't intentionally think about.

I apologize in advance for the lengthy explanation. In February of last year, I went to my general practitioner to request a referral to a psychiatrist because I suspected that I might have Bipolar disorder. After an evaluation, the GP diagnosed me with Cyclothymia instead. I was then referred to a psychologist and underwent 8 weeks of cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), but unfortunately, it didn't seem to have any positive effect on me.

During my childhood in the United States, I experienced physical abuse. One memory that stands out is of a larger individual jumping up and down on my back until I started bleeding from my mouth. Lately, I've noticed that I undergo sudden changes in my behavior and speech patterns. These changes often result in me becoming angry, uncaring, and alienating my friends. It's distressing for me and I'm not sure why it's happening.

I have been feeling a strong sense of isolation and withdrawal from my family and friends. Whenever they try to reach out to me, I find myself becoming angry and responding in a dismissive manner. This has caused me to distance myself from them, and I prefer being alone. However, despite feeling lonely and desiring human interaction, I struggle to answer calls, open the door, or make plans to meet with friends.

Growing up in Indonesia, I have always felt like the black sheep of my family. As the second child, I constantly face criticism from my parents and cruel comments from my older sister. I have tried talking to my mom about it, but nothing has changed and the comments have only become more hurtful. I have been avoiding my sister and staying silent when she makes these remarks, but it is taking a toll on me. I find myself crying in the bathroom and feeling ashamed of myself. I wonder if maybe she is right, and I am truly "stupid and useless." What do you think I should do?

After high school, I became heavily involved in smoking marijuana and watching conspiracy theories. I isolated myself from others and started to believe that there was a conspiracy against me, with people thinking things about me that I wasn't aware of. This led to confrontations that damaged my relationships. Eventually, I gave up trying to uncover the truth.

Over the past year, I have developed a close friendship with a woman at my company. She was going through a difficult time due to her abusive second marriage. My own marriage has been stable for 21 years, and I have never been unfaithful to my wife.

I'm a 21-year-old guy who has been in a relationship with my girlfriend for a couple of years. Recently, she stayed over at my house for a few days, and afterwards, my mom started asking about our relationship. It turns out that my mom doesn't like my girlfriend, even though she has met her before and stayed over at our house. My mom couldn't give me a specific reason, but mentioned that sometimes people are just not likable. I think part of the issue is that my parents, who are first-generation immigrants, have a slight language barrier with my girlfriend. She feels that they are shy and constantly judging her. I love my girlfriend for who she is, but my mom seems to have a different idea of what kind of person would be suitable for me. We argued about it, and my mom even said she doesn't see us being together in the long term. I'm feeling confused and don't know what to do. Can you help me make sense of all this?

About 1.5 years ago, I met a girl at church and we started a relationship. Overall, things have been good, but there is a recurring issue. Whenever she doesn't have her kids for the weekend and I suggest having a night to myself, she becomes angry and demanding. She even takes back her house key and declares that we're breaking up, only to call me a few hours later in tears, questioning why I am with her. It's all very dramatic.

About a year ago, I met someone who I believe is the love of my life. Before him, I had been in a few relationships that didn't work out. These past relationships failed because the men I was with were immature and not ready for a committed relationship like I was. I was sexually active with them, and we were exclusive. When I met my current boyfriend, I had honestly lost hope in finding someone suitable. Despite being only 23, I consider myself mature for my age and have always been interested in a long-term relationship.

When I was around 6 years old, I started developing beliefs that there were people outside my window watching me and cameras hidden in my walls and teddies. This made me feel constantly watched and monitored. As I got older and started using computers more, I became convinced that my computer was being tapped.
