I was always cautious about my words and actions, believing that I was being observed and assessed. I believed that I had latent powers that would one day become significant.

I have a friend who has been through a series of relationships in a relatively short span of time. She dated one person for four years in high school, then shortly after breaking up with him, she entered into another relationship that lasted one year. After that breakup, she and I became involved romantically and had intimate moments together. However, she recently decided that she needs time to be single and focus on herself.

Patient: Hi, I'm a 17-year-old girl who is feeling overwhelmed. It's my last year in high school and I'm preparing for the university exam. I have a lot of exams and it's been really stressful. But there's something else bothering me. I consider myself a good person. I care about others' feelings and I find joy in making people happy. I'm quite sensitive and easily affected by what others think. However, I feel like nobody wants me and nobody would care if something happened to me. People are there for me when they need something, but when I need support, I feel alone. It's heartbreaking and it's making me really sad. I need help. Can you please help me?

My daughter, who is 12 years old, is showing some signs that indicate she may have sensory integration differences. For example, she cannot tolerate seeing metal while eating, she is excessively sensitive to cold temperatures, and she hyper-reacts to certain textures of food. Although she seems to have difficulty relating to authority figures, she is doing well socially with her friends and at school.

Patient's statement (revised): My boyfriend of 3 years recently ended our relationship over Skype, while he was texting someone else. He mentioned that he felt the relationship was toxic and expressed concerns about my behavior being manipulative, controlling, and abusive. He didn't provide specific examples and cited my struggles with finding a job and the stress I've been under as contributing factors. I'm confused because he never mentioned these issues before, and I've always encouraged open communication. I'm devastated and wondering what I'm missing and what steps I can take.

My 5-year-old son has been struggling with chronic constipation since he was 2 years old. Despite my efforts to encourage him to use the toilet, he refuses to poop anywhere except in a diaper. I've tried various strategies like begging, bribing, and even punishing him, but nothing seems to work. He's able to pee in the toilet, but he's never pooped in it. This is causing a lot of stress as he's supposed to start kindergarten soon and I don't know how he'll manage if he insists on wearing a diaper all day. I've tried buying him his own toilet, a seat for the regular toilet, and even had influential people talk to him about using the toilet, but he still feels the need for diapers. I'm at a loss and I've exhausted all my ideas. What should I do?

I've been feeling really isolated lately. I don't understand why I haven't been able to make any friends for years. Last week, when I bought a new phone, the cashier was surprised that I had only used 40 phone minutes in a whole month. I guess not having friends has its upside in saving phone minutes. Although I do have positive interactions with my coworkers and I'm involved in various groups like a church group, a choir, a singles group, and the PTA. I'm even the leader of one of the groups.

When I was eight years old, I had a traumatic experience with my cousin Amber who sexually abused me. She also forced me to play a dangerous game with cars on the highway. Now, at 22 years old, I'm struggling with nightmares, depression, anxiety, and self-harm urges. I've been clean for two weeks and I'm considering therapy and medication. Can you help me figure out what to do next?

Over the past two years, I've been experiencing feelings of isolation, lack of motivation, and a sense of worthlessness. I've even started having thoughts about suicide and ways to make others feel guilty for my unhappiness. I tend to avoid social interactions but then regret not having more friends. School causes me so much stress that it often leads to mental breakdowns. I used to think these were just normal teenage emotions, but now I'm not so sure. I've also developed binge-purge cycles that I feel like I have no control over. Lately, I've been second-guessing everything people say, including my closest friends. I've been having trouble falling asleep at night, which is a recent change. And more recently, I've noticed that I can't sit still and feel fidgety. Despite having a caring family and close friends, I always feel so alone. I'm not sure if all of this is normal, because it definitely doesn't feel normal. Thank you for listening.

Over the past year, I've experienced a series of challenging events that have impacted my motivation and academic focus. I had a difficult time during the previous school year due to sickness, social drama, and the loss of loved ones, including pets. However, I entered this year feeling happier and more positive. Recently, I made new friends and became more socially engaged, but I've noticed a decline in my academic motivation.

I'm a 14-year-old girl who has been struggling with social anxiety and self-esteem issues. I tend to isolate myself and have difficulty speaking to others, which causes me a lot of distress. I've also experienced bullying because of my unique clothing style and have lost my close friend as a result. I have feelings for him, but I'm too afraid to express them. Additionally, I've been engaging in self-harm by scraping myself with a razor. I feel like I have no self-confidence and I'm constantly teased for not conforming to societal expectations of femininity. People only interact with me for academic help or to make fun of me. I recently experienced a traumatic incident where someone exposed my scars and made hurtful comments. I'm not sure what's wrong with me, but I know something's not right. Can you please help me?

My daughter is 25 years old and about two years ago, I met a man whom I felt an instant strong connection and chemistry with. Due to our demanding work schedules, we didn't have much time to spend together, so I asked him to move in with me. However, things became complicated when my daughter's boyfriend had a confrontation with my partner. Since then, there has been tension and animosity between my daughter and my partner, which puts me in an uncomfortable position. In March of 2013, my partner moved out, but he came back because we still loved each other. However, in October, they had a huge fight and my partner moved out again, saying he wouldn't come back. But he still doesn't want to let me go and insists on being friends, saying he loves me. I'm confused and unsure about what to do. I love him deeply and would be with him in a heartbeat if he wants to be with me again, but he keeps telling me we're just friends. I don't know if he's waiting for my daughter to move out or get married before considering getting back together. I'm feeling lost and unsure of what his true intentions are.

I have been in a complicated situation with two men. There is an old friend who loves me deeply and I have strong feelings for him too. However, due to circumstances, we couldn't be together. In the meantime, I met someone else and fell in love quickly, but our relationship has been turbulent. I recently ended things with the second person, but now I'm feeling conflicted and missing him. I also feel guilty for loving both of these men. I don't know what to do.

Over the past few weeks, I've been experiencing a range of emotions that have been overwhelming for me. I've been feeling a deep sense of emptiness and hopelessness, and it's been difficult for me to sleep at night. I've also noticed a loss of interest in things that used to bring me joy. On top of that, I've been experiencing periods of intense happiness and energy that seem to come out of nowhere. I'm not sure if these extreme mood swings are normal or if there's something more going on.

Since I hit puberty, I have been dealing with stretch marks all over my body. I used to be overweight and didn't have a healthy diet, which I think contributed to the development of these stretch marks. It's frustrating because they're literally everywhere - on my arms, breasts, hips, thighs, knees, and even behind my calves. Some people may downplay it, but these stretch marks have caused me a lot of emotional distress. However, I have learned to love my body the way it is now and appreciate the hard work I've put into taking care of myself.

When I was 15 years old (I’m 22 now), my dad left to work overseas, leaving me alone with my Mom. My Mom has always exhibited hyperactive and impulsive behavior, and she also struggles with alcoholism. She has been this way even before my dad left. It has been challenging to cope, especially during the first time he left.

I am here today to talk about my mom, who has been deeply impacted by my sister's mental illness for over 30 years. I'll refer to my sister as R for anonymity. My mom has faced numerous challenges in trying to support R and it has taken a toll on her own well-being.

I've been in a relationship for the past two months. Overall, my partner is kind, caring, and charming. However, I've noticed that he gets angry very easily over small things. He often tells me to be more sensible and to say and do things according to his expectations. I'm not used to overthinking things, so it's difficult for me to predict what might make him angry. When he does get angry, it makes me cry because I never want to hurt him. For example, when he asked about my past experiences, I hesitated to be completely open, which hurt him and made him feel like I wanted to lie. I never intended to lie, but it took him some time to understand and support me.

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for almost 2 years now, and we have a good sex life. However, there are times when I don't feel like having sex. It could be due to physical discomfort from my menstrual cycle or when my boyfriend has been insensitive during dinner, which makes me hesitant to be intimate with him.

Hi, I'm a 30-year-old male. I am happily married and love my wife very much. However, I got emotionally and physically involved with a coworker last year. Initially, it was just for fun and we both made it clear that there were no romantic feelings involved. We would meet once or twice a month, but I never initiated those meetings. Recently, we had a fight and haven't spoken for over a week. While I want to move on from this situation, the thought of her being with someone else gives me a lot of anxiety. I feel guilty and recognize that I made a mistake. Can you please help me?

My sister, age 57, is experiencing significant challenges in her life. She is a BSRN but currently unemployed due to difficulties with working relationships. Additionally, she has gone through multiple marriages and was recently fired from her last job. Lately, she has been expressing extreme beliefs about the government being the enemy. She believes that they plan to confiscate people's property and force them to rent it back. She also thinks that the government is placing reflectors on mailboxes to identify who will be sent to concentration camps. She is convinced that a "coup" will happen between Dec 21st and Jan 6th. Our family has experienced similar doomsday predictions in the past, with nothing happening. She is in poor physical health and significantly overweight, but she refuses to seek disability assistance out of fear that the government will take away everyone's pensions. I want to help her understand that these beliefs are not grounded in reality. Is there a specific disorder associated with these symptoms?

Lately, I've been feeling a lack of interest in things and a decreased capacity to love others, including my family and my fiancé. It feels like my life is stagnant and that my future in-laws will always harbor animosity towards me. I'm finding it hard to see a purpose in continuing on because I feel empty and resentful towards myself and those around me. Even the idea of getting married doesn't bring me joy anymore. I'm reaching out because I'm lost and don't know what to do anymore.

I have been struggling with my husband's low testosterone levels and its impact on our sex life. He is also overweight but is working on addressing this issue. I find it difficult to cope with the lack of sexual intimacy we have been experiencing. We only engage in sexual activity once or twice a month, which leaves me feeling unsatisfied. I have resorted to using masturbation and sex toys, but what I truly desire is to have a fulfilling sexual relationship with my husband. This issue has been growing and causing a lot of distress for me. We are hesitant to try testosterone therapy drugs due to their potential impact on sperm count, as we hope to have children in the future. Additionally, we are dealing with infertility issues related to Azoospermia, which may also be contributing to his low sex drive. I feel a range of emotions, including feeling rejected, alone, sad, depressed, and frustrated. I am desperate for help and considering seeking counseling. However, I was hoping to find some tips to cope with this situation in the meantime. Thank you.

Hello, I'm a 21-year-old who has been diagnosed with ADHD, minor Tourette's, anxiety, and depression. I've been out of high school for a few years and have struggled to maintain steady employment. I completed a year-long apprenticeship in carpentry, but after working for six months, I found myself despising my job and decided to quit. Lately, I've been concerned that there may be something more going on with me than just the conditions I've been diagnosed with. I currently take Pristiq for my depression and anxiety, which has been helpful in improving my mood and socializing. However, I've noticed that my mind is always racing and I tend to obsess over small things in my day-to-day life. For example, if I have a conversation that I think didn't go well, I can become fixated on it for days or even months. I also have a lot of anxiety when it comes to approaching and talking to girls, to the point where it almost feels like a phobia. The idea of approaching someone I'm interested in makes my heart pound extremely fast. As a result, I've avoided these situations for most of my life due to a fear of rejection and worrying about what others would think of me. I struggle with low self-confidence and often feel useless or stupid. On the physical side, I exercise regularly and am in good shape. I'm very sensitive to what people say about me, and I've done some research on different disorders, though I'm not trying to self-diagnose. I'm just looking for some reassurance and would appreciate a professional opinion. Thank you for your time.

I have been diagnosed with Asperger's syndrome and have been struggling to find a romantic relationship for the past seven years. Despite my efforts, I have been rejected by almost every girl I've asked out. However, a couple of years ago, I met someone at college whom I connected with deeply. Although we remain good friends, I can't help but feel hurt by the rejection, even after all this time. I did attempt to pursue another relationship, but it ended abruptly due to the other person's dramatic behavior. This experience has left me feeling increasingly hopeless and doubtful about finding someone compatible with me.

Patient statement: I have noticed that I have become increasingly introverted over the years. As a child, I was outgoing and had no trouble expressing myself and making friends. However, now at 23, I struggle with expressing extreme emotions, which has affected my ability to form meaningful relationships in both personal and professional areas of my life. While I have various friend groups, I feel like I don't truly fit in with any of them and I have never had a best friend who reciprocated that feeling. Although I am well-liked, I feel like no one truly loves me or hates me. My romantic relationships have been short-lived and lacking emotional depth.

Over the past year, I have been taking Quetiapine to help manage my mental health. I initially started this medication due to difficulties I was experiencing at home with my former partner and at university, which eventually led to a complete mental breakdown. I have since ended my relationship and dropped out of university, so those specific stressors are no longer present in my life. However, I have noticed a pattern of relapse whenever I start to make progress in my recovery. I have been diagnosed with Anxiety, Depression with suicidal tendencies, Psychosis, and Borderline Personality Disorder.
I've been struggling with two different issues for as long as I can remember. I'm 18 now, but these problems have been with me since birth. I apologize if my English isn't perfect.

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for four years and we're still quite young. Yesterday was my birthday, but we were supposed to celebrate it the day before. My boyfriend had told me a month ago that he got me the most thoughtful gift ever. However, when the day came, he said that going out to dinner was my birthday gift. I expressed my disappointment and he called me ungrateful. It turns out he had lied about getting paid his final paycheck.

Over the past two years, I have been experiencing disturbing and violent thoughts. These thoughts involve me or my loved ones dying in horrific ways, and I even had a thought about self-harm by opening my own stomach with a box cutter. I also have thoughts about stabbings, shootings, falling to my death, and being attacked by fictional or demonic creatures. My family is more concerned about my sudden outbursts of anger over small things. Additionally, I constantly feel paranoid, as if someone is always watching me or that something dangerous is lurking in the woods. These thoughts are getting worse, and I'm afraid that I might harm someone close to me. If you need more information, please let me know. I'm not sure what else to share.

In my youth, I was a very quiet and introverted boy. I enjoyed spending time alone, reading books, and generally keeping to myself. However, around the age of fifteen or sixteen, I noticed a significant shift in my demeanor.

I've been struggling with intense emotional outbursts and self-destructive behaviors since I was young. It's gotten worse as I've grown older, and now I find myself engaging in harmful actions like attempting suicide, skipping school, and even getting into physical fights with my family. I know I need to see a psychiatrist, but I'm hesitant to bring it up with my mom because she hasn't taken action in the past. It's a difficult situation, and I don't want it to become awkward or cause her stress. I was supposed to see a psychiatrist last year, but it never happened. I'm really worried about my well-being and want to seek help before something truly awful occurs.

I am 18 years old and I always want to be alone. My mother gets angry at the fact that I hardly leave my room. I have a few friends but I try to avoid hanging out with them. I make up excuses at times. When I’m alone I feel okay and for some reason when I’m around other people I get sadder. Around friends, I get anxiety even though I have known them a long time. Once I started shaking with anxiety, I felt like I wasn’t in my own body and I got frightened at the feeling I was experiencing. I didn’t know how to stop myself and got really scared until I focused and talked myself into calming down. I sleep a lot, to the point my mom was worried and said she was taking me to the doctors to make sure I’m not sick or anything causing me to sleep so much. Weeks can go by and I won’t leave my room and she doesn’t like that. I just don’t feel comfortable around people. At home, I like being alone in my room in my own world more than being with my family. I do not know why I feel this way and I don’t know how to explain it to my family. Should I go to a doctor for depression and anxiety? Or should I not take it too seriously? I feel lost.

I'm a 26-year-old woman who has been married for the past 7 years to someone who has been dishonest and unfaithful. During a period of separation, I reconnected with my high school sweetheart, who I had dated before and had a child with. My mother strongly dislikes him due to his troubled past. However, he claims to have changed and is willing to prove it to others. I feel like I'm sneaking around with him, just so my mother won't be upset and stop visiting my children. I love him and my children adore him, especially my son since he's his father. I don't know how to tell my mom that I've been spending time with him and that it's time for her to let me make my own mistakes. My mom is like my best friend. Can you please help me?

Patient: I've been in a relationship for 3.5 years, and we've discussed marriage. However, whenever I bring up the topic of when we'll get married, he distances himself and seeks out sexual encounters with women who have low self-esteem. I have an autoimmune disease that prevents me from working, so I'm financially dependent on him. If we were to break up, I would be left without a home, car, or money. This has led me to become a people-pleaser, doing whatever he asks of me. I give my all to make this relationship work, but I'm exhausted from being hurt. I don't think it's fair that I should suffer heartbreak just because he's not ready to commit. I recently discovered messages on a dating site where he was trying to hook up with other women. I feel torn between confronting him and dealing with the consequences or pretending everything is fine. He is an amazing boyfriend to my face, but it hurts knowing he seeks out demeaning sexual experiences with strangers. I haven't experienced that behavior from him during our intimate moments. Thank you for listening.

Patient's statement (revised): I recently got married and we have a four-month-old baby. My husband has a tendency to say hurtful things to my parents, but he has apologized for it. He believes that respect should be earned and is quite vocal about it. We were house hunting over the weekend, and my mother came to babysit. Since we live in a somewhat unsafe neighborhood, she locked the door, and we didn't have a key. When we returned, it took her a couple of minutes to open the door, and my husband became furious, calling her disrespectful names. I got mad at him, but I'm not sure if I'm in the wrong since it's our apartment. He did apologize to my mom through a voicemail, but the damage is done. My parents are urging me to leave him, while my husband is concerned about our family and wants to make things work. I'm torn and don't know what to do. My parents have stopped talking to me because I still allow him to live with us, even though I've been covering all the expenses lately. Please help.

I come from a family with one brother who is currently studying for his degree. While I have many cousin sisters, I have always wished for a sister of my own. About a year ago, I met a woman who is not related to me in any way. From the moment I saw her, I felt a strong connection and familiarity, almost like a lightning bolt in my mind. Over time, I found myself becoming attracted to her and caring for her deeply. It's strange to me because I feel these emotions towards her as if she were my own sister. I'm amazed by my own behavior and feelings.

About a year ago, I entered into a meaningful relationship with someone from another city. We started off as close friends and eventually began dating. Both of us had emotional struggles, but we were able to open up to each other and share our true feelings. After four months of being together every day, she told me she was going back to her old city in two months and ended our relationship, citing her fear of falling even more in love with me. This left me devastated, especially since we were in our senior year of high school. I coped by seeking comfort with other people, but internally, I was still hurting. Recently, I discovered that she might be returning to live here, and this has made me feel confused.

When I was around 7 or 8 years old, my older brother, who was about a year and a half older than me, told me about something he heard from a friend regarding how gay people have sex. I didn't really understand what he was talking about at the time, so I jokingly asked if he wanted to try it. Looking back, I realize that he seemed hesitant when he agreed. I want to understand the impact this experience may have had on me.

I have been experiencing persistent worries about my health. I constantly focus on my heartbeat and am always aware of it. The same goes for my breathing. I find myself worrying about various health conditions like heart attacks, cancer, brain tumors, and pulmonary embolisms. Sometimes, I wonder if these worries are just stemming from anxiety. Both my father and grandmother have struggled with anxiety, and I have had panic attacks in the past, although it has been a while since my last one. However, recently I have been dealing with significant stressors in my life, such as moving to a new city for school, being away from familiar faces, the pressures of school, financial concerns, and the job loss of my father. All of this adds to my already existing stress about my health. I feel foolish when I try to discuss this with others, as if they will think I am crazy. I try to rationalize my worries by reminding myself of my age (22) and the unlikelihood of having serious conditions at this stage of life, but the worrying persists. I am reaching out for help, please assist me.

I've been struggling with a need to be perfect for as long as I can remember. It really started to consume me when I was around 12 years old. If I made even the smallest mistake, it would ruin my entire day and I would feel like I had to start being perfect the next day. I've even tried searching online for time machines to start my life over. I constantly think about my flaws and negative comments from years ago. Can you suggest any mental exercises that might help?

Over the past year, I've noticed that I have developed a habit of clenching and popping my jaw. Recently, I discovered that this behavior is quite noticeable to others. My cousin showed me a picture where I can clearly be seen doing it in the background. This has made me feel extremely embarrassed, especially at work. Additionally, I have developed a deep wrinkle under my chin as a result of this habit. I am currently taking 200 mg of Zoloft in the morning, 15 mg of Adderall twice daily, and 1 mg of Klonapin at night. I've been under the care of a psychiatrist for the past 8 years for depression, anxiety, PTSD, and ADD. I have also been admitted to an inpatient facility twice, with the most recent admission being in 2011. I've started isolating myself because I'm so ashamed of my jaw and eye movements. Seeing that picture really highlighted how strange I look. I appreciate any help you can offer.

Three years ago, before my wedding, my ex re-appeared in my life. Despite being happily married to a loving and loyal husband who provides for me, I've been secretly communicating with my ex. The main issue is that my current relationship lacks chemistry and sexual passion, which was incredibly strong with my ex. He has expressed that he only wants a physical relationship without any commitment. I've met him twice to talk, but have refrained from any physical contact to maintain my integrity and honor my marriage. I'm torn because I believe I'm in love with my ex and would consider leaving my husband if he wanted a serious relationship. However, I'm unsure if he can be trusted. What should I do?

I'm really worried about my daughter's relationship with her 18-year-old boyfriend. On one hand, he seems supportive and wonderful when he's around us. But he constantly lies about things that don't even make sense. He's lied about where he's applied and been accepted to college, and he's even claimed to have been in the hospital multiple times in the past few months. It's getting to the point where I think he might be a compulsive liar. Is this a sign of a personality disorder? Why would he lie about things that are so unnecessary?

I've noticed a pattern in my social interactions. When I'm in a situation that feels a bit threatening, I'm initially able to engage and enjoy myself for the first two minutes. However, after that, I start feeling a surge of adrenaline and my body becomes tense. This makes it difficult for me to make direct eye contact, laugh, or feel comfortable for the next 2-3 hours. Once that time passes, everything goes back to normal and I can communicate like any other person would.

I'm 21 years old and have been in a relationship with my girlfriend for a couple of years. Recently, my girlfriend stayed over at my house for a few days. After she left, my mom started asking about our relationship and I sensed something was wrong. It turns out that my mom doesn't like my girlfriend, but couldn't pinpoint any specific reasons. My parents are first-generation immigrants and there is a slight language and cultural barrier between them and my girlfriend. She feels that my parents are shy and constantly judging her. I love my girlfriend for who she is and it bothers me that my mom doesn't see that. This has caused tension between my mom and me, and I'm not sure how to handle the situation. Can you help me with some guidance?

I've been having some difficulties with my boyfriend's mom. She has made me feel unwelcome in the family, and I often feel like she doesn't like me. She also tries to impose her religious beliefs on both of us, and she constantly gives me disapproving looks and scrutinizes my clothing choices. During Christmas, I wore a new outfit for dinner, and she initially complimented it but then held onto me when I tried to walk away. She also followed me to my room and invaded my privacy by looking through my belongings. Later, she overheard a conversation between me and my boyfriend and misinterpreted it, which led to my mom telling me to stop joking around with him. It was really hurtful, and I ended up crying. On the day after Christmas, we went shopping and his mom unexpectedly joined us for the entire day, being overly nice and intruding on our personal space. I'm at my wit's end with her behavior. My boyfriend refuses to go to therapy with his mom because he doesn't like it. I really need some guidance here.

Over the summer, I experienced a devastating loss when my best friend of 30 years passed away unexpectedly. It was a traumatic experience for me, my boyfriend, and our close-knit group of friends. She went to the emergency room feeling unwell on a Monday and tragically passed away due to liver failure on Wednesday.

Counselor: Thank you for sharing your feelings and experiences with me. It sounds like you have been carrying a heavy burden for a long time. It's important to recognize that our past experiences can deeply impact how we view ourselves and our place in the world. It's understandable that you might feel lost and disconnected right now.

Over the past two months, I've been in a whirlwind romance with my girlfriend. We met in October on a blind date and instantly felt a strong connection. Despite our initial intention to take things slow, we ended up being intimate sooner than expected. We've spent a lot of time together, and our feelings for each other have only deepened. She has expressed that I am the most caring and kind man she's ever met.

I'm a 13-year-old who has been diagnosed with depression since the age of seven. Currently, I am taking antidepressants and sleeping tablets, but I feel like they are not helping me and may even be making things worse. Despite improvements in my life overall, my moods, feelings, and behaviors have worsened. I constantly feel angry, have negative body image thoughts, and engage in self-harming behaviors. My sisters are unsupportive and I feel overwhelmed. What can I do to cope with these thoughts, stop being sick, and prevent self-harm?

My boyfriend and I have been together for 5 months. We met on a dating website 8 months ago. He originally hails from Tunisia but has been living in Canada for the past four years as a student. Recently, we found out that his residency application was denied, and he may have to leave the country. He's fighting the decision in court, and we're hoping for a positive outcome. I shared my concerns about this situation with a close friend, and she asked me if I'm certain that my boyfriend truly loves me or if he's just using me for a marriage of convenience to secure his residency. This question made me angry, but it also made me doubt the authenticity of our relationship considering all the stories we hear. I don't want to make a mistake.

Over the past two years, I have been struggling with anxiety and depression. These issues stemmed from a stressful and unhealthy relationship as well as my living environment. I have been on and off medication to address these concerns. In addition, I have engaged in risky behaviors such as sneaking out, having sex, and smoking marijuana. I have also been disobedient. This past year, I went through a difficult relationship that triggered feelings of insecurity, doubt, and depression. Recently, I experienced a traumatic incident at work as a lifeguard, which resulted in me being sent home due to shock. On top of that, the person I was in a relationship with for a year has hurt me and is now with someone else. I feel lost and don't know what kind of help I need. I have had two anxiety attacks in the last two weeks, and I find myself becoming angry and annoyed over trivial things. I always feel the need to be in control and be perfect. I'm tired of crying over insignificant matters and feeling unsure of what to do. As we speak, I'm feeling emotional and unstable. Please help me gain control over these issues. I am willing to do whatever it takes.

I'm really struggling in my current relationship and my anger is causing me to push my spouse away. I find myself screaming at my spouse and sometimes resorting to punching objects and slamming things. I feel constantly irritated by small issues and it's affecting my ability to concentrate and feel better. I've received different diagnoses and opinions, some blaming me and others suggesting I need help. Unfortunately, I can't afford medication or healthcare, and there's no assistance available in my area. I know you can't diagnose without more information, but I really need help. My mind is always racing, replaying things over and over again. It's exhausting and I feel like I can't escape these negative feelings. Am I just twisted and enjoying feeling this way? Please help me find some simple solutions to these issues.

It seems like you've been experiencing a lot of distressing thoughts and feelings. It must be really overwhelming for you. It's important to remember that you're not alone in this and we're here to help. Have you ever discussed these experiences with your therapist before?

Hello, I am reaching out because I suspect that I may have a mental or learning disability. I have always struggled with self-motivation and procrastination, and my difficulties have persisted since high school. In my early childhood, I was diagnosed with ADD. I'm unsure of how to research or find out more about my suspicions.

I'm a 17-year-old with a fairly typical life. However, I frequently struggle with issues such as low self-esteem, feelings of loneliness, and sadness. My parents are often busy with work, particularly my mother who works long hours and sleeps when she's home. While I have a good relationship with her, I find it difficult to open up to her when she's tired or sleeping, which leaves me feeling lonely and on the verge of tears. I'm wondering why this is happening.

Hi, my name is Max. I've been diagnosed with both ADD and depression, but I'm starting to question if those diagnoses are correct. Lately, I've been struggling a lot with my memory and attention. For example, I opened up this webpage at 11:28 AM and now it's already 2:16 PM. I've started using a pad of paper to write down my thoughts as a way to remember things better.

Over the past few days, I've been experiencing a lot of anxiety and distress regarding a recent incident. I got really drunk and ended up telling my boyfriend that I was raped. He said he would talk to me about it, but he hasn't followed through. I've been feeling this overwhelming need to keep texting him to explain things and make sure he understands, but it's causing me a lot of anxiety. I don't know why I feel this way and it's really affecting me. Can you please help me?

I've recently noticed that my boyfriend has been telling me a lot of lies. Initially, I thought it was just him being insecure and exaggerating the truth occasionally. However, after 10 months together, I'm starting to believe that he might be a compulsive or pathological liar. He fabricates stories about his possessions, life achievements, and who knows what else. For instance, he claimed to own a valuable classic car that he fixed up himself and even raced. He even said that while driving the car, he stumbled upon a movie set and ended up having drinks with two actors from the film. These stories sound too good to be true.

I've been going through a tough time since my recent breakup. When my girlfriend and I ended things, she mentioned that she was concerned about a possible disorder I might have. I've noticed that I have intense bursts of anger where I end up doing things I regret. For example, I punched a hole in the wall once after burning my hand in the kitchen. It felt like I was watching myself from the outside, aware that it was irrational but unable to control it. Recently, I had a blackout episode where I became so furious that I kicked a hole in the wall, broke my phone, and found myself crying afterwards. Strangely, I didn't feel remorse for damaging the wall, but I felt an overwhelming sense of sadness.

Today I tried to express to my parents that I'm feeling stressed by showing them multiple websites on teenage stress. However, they responded by mocking me and dismissing my feelings. I believe my stress is partially due to school, as I'm taking challenging courses and striving for straight A's. Additionally, I have been feeling depressed over the past few years and I often wish life would just stop because I feel overwhelmed and unprepared for the future. When I try to talk to my friends about how I'm feeling, they either don't understand or brush it off. I feel like no one truly gets it and I'm afraid to reach out for help. Is there anything I can do to cope with these feelings without directly telling my parents about my depression?

Hello, I hope you can help me. I have been diagnosed with ADHD, bipolar disorder, and anxiety disorder, but I am currently refusing to take my medication. I am 20 years old and these issues are really affecting my life in a negative way.

I have been struggling with depression since my teenage years. I have never sought help or been tested for mood disorders because I chose to hide my struggles. However, as I am getting older, I am experiencing more frequent episodes. Once these episodes begin, I feel unable to stop them. My moods fluctuate drastically - when I am happy, I am extremely happy, but when I am down, I hit rock bottom. After the birth of my first child, I was diagnosed with postpartum depression, but it was not recognized that I have been dealing with depression for a long time. I find myself easily irritated and lacking self-control over my mood swings. These episodes often escalate to the point where I yell or impulsively exit the car during arguments with my husband at red lights. I have been in denial about needing help, but the severity of these episodes is increasing. Should I schedule an appointment with my primary care doctor? What should I say when I call?

Lately, I've been having trouble sleeping because I've been stressing out over which mental technique to use. I have OCD, so these thoughts keep popping up in my head, making it difficult to concentrate on sleep. I've tried different techniques like closing my eyes and trying to stay awake, imagining a black screen, and counting sheep. Should I use a variety of techniques and switch between them every five or ten minutes, or should I just try to relax and fall asleep?

As a child, my father used to make me watch horror movies at the theaters, which triggered my paranoia. I still vividly remember the terrifying scenes, and how I would cry and try to block my view of the screen. It seems like those images are permanently etched in my mind. Over the years, my paranoia gradually worsened and now, at 18 years old, it has become extremely difficult to cope with on a daily basis. I constantly remind myself that it's all in my head, that there's no real danger from the movies. However, I experience anxiety attacks when it's dark, I constantly check my surroundings, and I need to have lights on in every room. Even when I shower, I start to panic, fearing that there might be someone supernatural on the other side. I rely on sleeping pills to calm my mind, and I'm even scared to have my feet exposed in bed, fearing that a "monster" might grab them. I sleep with pillows around me to feel safe. When I'm home alone, I sometimes go hungry because I'm too scared to go downstairs. The worst part is that these thoughts and fears consume me to the point where I experience physical symptoms like stomach pain, backaches, racing heart, and a surge of adrenaline. I can't go on like this. Is this a mental health problem? Can it be treated or will I have to live with it forever? My mother thinks it's just a phase and that I'll grow out of it, but it's only getting worse. I worry about my future and whether I'll ever be able to live alone.

I was in an abusive relationship with my ex-husband for several years before finally leaving him. Now I am in a new relationship, but I am struggling with intense anger and panic attacks, particularly when my current partner goes to work. Even small arguments trigger extreme anger in me, and I have even resorted to self-harm and physical aggression towards him. I immediately regret my actions and feel immense guilt afterwards. These episodes also lead to panic attacks where I have difficulty breathing. This behavior is not reflective of who I am, and it deeply upsets me. I have been married for over 20 years and have two teenage children. My marriage has ended and I am currently separated. Despite the separation, my ex and I have managed to maintain a good friendship and support each other. Two years ago, I met a man who was also separated and had two children of his own. We connected instantly and developed a deep love for each other. Early on in our relationship, I expressed my desire to have another serious relationship and eventually live together. He mentioned that he also shared the same aspirations for the future.

I have been talking to a woman from England for the past 5 months and we've developed a strong connection. We both feel that if we lived in the same country, we would be in a serious and intimate relationship. However, we're unsure about the challenges of a long-distance relationship. As a college student, I don't have enough funds to visit her for an extended trip overseas. We have regular Skype and Snapchat conversations, so it's not a catfish situation. I know who she is and this is a serious relationship. It's just really upsetting that we can't be together. I think about her every night and it's difficult to cope with not being able to be with her. I know I'll be the happiest man alive once I can visit her. I'm seeking advice on how to deal with this distressing situation. Any help would be appreciated.

My boyfriend has accused me of having a sexual relationship with my father, which is completely untrue. He believes he has evidence and thinks I manipulate people with reverse psychology. It's deeply disturbing and infuriating that he sees this as true.

I'm a 17-year-old who has been in a relationship with my boyfriend for about 9 months. He has been struggling with severe depression for many years, which makes it challenging for us to have open discussions about our relationship. His depression consumes him and often leaves me feeling overwhelmed and unable to address our issues. He has a history of self-harm, suicide attempts, and displays of anger. I want to support him, but I also feel trapped and mentally abused. He refuses to seek professional help and threatens self-harm when I mention leaving the relationship. I'm torn between my own well-being and staying to prevent him from getting hurt. I need guidance.

I have been experiencing the presence of a voice inside my head that seems to alternate between being my friend and my enemy. It usually happens when I am alone, either walking or sitting at home. I don't recognize the voice and I believe it's coming from within me. However, it's starting to negatively impact me. For instance, when it's late at night and I have the urge to eat something, I try to resist but the voice convinces me otherwise, coming up with persuasive reasons. This frustrates me to the point where I yell at the voice to stop, and sometimes I even resort to hitting myself out of anger. Eventually, I give in to what the voice suggests (eating). I don't think it's schizophrenia because the voice doesn't feel external, and I don't experience hallucinations. However, it's becoming overwhelming and distressing.

I've been struggling with a lot of anger and aggression lately, and it's really taking a toll on my relationship with my wife. About a year ago, I experienced a violent assault that has changed me in ways I never expected. I used to be peaceful and sarcastic at times, but now I find myself lashing out and being condescending towards my wife. I love her and I know she has been there for me, but I've pushed her too far. I've also noticed that I've become more sexually aggressive and selfish, not prioritizing her needs. I feel horrible about my actions and I don't understand why I've become this way. During my childhood, I engaged in kissing games with my younger brother. It is a memory that fills me with shame and makes me feel nauseated and anxious even now. This experience has had a significant impact on my life, causing me to feel extreme shame towards my own sexuality.

I've been struggling with my parents' drinking habits, particularly my mom's behavior when she's intoxicated. She becomes mean and unpredictable, saying hurtful things to me. There was even a time when she expressed a wish to never see me again after waking up from surgery. It's been happening for at least the past five months and it's taking a toll on me. On top of that, my mom smokes in the house and even in my car, which I can't stand because it makes me feel sick. It feels like she doesn't care about me anymore. I keep telling myself that this is a lesson on how not to act, and that I won't repeat the same mistakes with my own children. I just wish my mom would realize how much she's hurting me by being emotionally absent for the past five years. I constantly feel like I'm not good enough, and I believe that if I were, she wouldn't want to escape her life. It's a difficult situation, and I could really use some help.

I've been feeling really uncertain about my upcoming wedding. My boyfriend and I recently got engaged, but I'm starting to doubt if he truly wants to marry me. He has been procrastinating on booking the wedding venue, which makes me question his intentions. I think he might have proposed just to please me. What should I do?

Over the past year, I have been in a complicated relationship with my best friend. We started off as friends with benefits, but eventually admitted our feelings and entered into a more serious relationship. However, I recently found out that he was involved with other girls, including one who I knew. Despite this, we decided to work things out when he returned from his army obligations. We have been making efforts to rebuild trust, but now my friends have come forward with accusations of him cheating again. I confronted him and asked to see his texts, but he refused. I ended the relationship, but he's been reaching out and saying he wants to make it work. I'm confused and torn because I still love him, but I don't know if I can trust him or if he has deeper issues. Additionally, the long-distance aspect and his trust issues are causing concern, as well as his future in the army.

Lately, I've been feeling really down. I'm having trouble sleeping and my schoolwork is suffering. I feel like I'm being left out by my friends and I used to be so happy and outgoing. I've been experiencing random headaches and I'm under so much stress, even though I'm only 11 years old. I'm scared to talk to my parents about it, so I thought I'd reach out for help online. I have no patience at school and everything and everyone is getting on my nerves. I've been crying myself to sleep sometimes. I'm not sure if I'm depressed or just going through a phase. Thank you for listening.

My friend has been going through a difficult time for the past three years since his breakup. He used to be an active and funny person, but now he has become isolated and seems to be just hoping for a better life without taking any action. He doesn't work and has lost most of his friends. What worries me the most is his unpredictable mood swings, going from happy to angry to melancholic in a matter of seconds. I've tried suggesting therapy and introducing him to new people, but nothing seems to help. Lately, he's been displaying signs of self-pity, envy, and even narcissism. I'm not sure how to support him anymore.

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for a year and a half. Our relationship has been healthy and we treat each other well. Recently, I discovered that he was talking to another girl from Xbox Live. He claims it was a coincidence and they just met, but she told me they've been talking for six months and even communicated through phone calls and texts. I chose to believe my boyfriend and now I constantly feel the need to monitor his activities to make sure he's not talking to other girls. I've become possessive, checking his Xbox Live chats, blocking girls on his account, and contacting everyone on his friends list. This behavior is new to me and it's affecting my trust. I love him deeply and don't want to lose this relationship. Is there a way to rebuild trust?

I teach a class of 8-10 children who are mostly 5 years old. This is part of a kindergarten enrichment program offered by a private childcare learning center. One particular child in my class consistently displays defiant behavior, which sometimes escalates into disruptive outbursts. I find it difficult to control these behaviors. It seems that the root cause of this behavior is the child's desire for constant attention, which I am unable to provide. This child has two dads who do not see her behavior as unusual and do not seek any help for her. I believe that if they were to take her to a professional, she may be diagnosed with a disorder. However, since they have not done so, I am not receiving any outside assistance from my employer.

I've been feeling really overwhelmed lately. I constantly find myself searching the internet, trying to figure out what's wrong with me. I'm 19 years old and I feel like I avoid everything in my life. I don't feel connected to anyone except my best friends. I had one girlfriend before, but I didn't really put much effort into the relationship. Lately, I can't seem to think straight anymore. My family has always seen me as someone with a bright future because of my good grades, but I've been skipping school and avoiding socializing as much as possible. I've always gotten by with the bare minimum, but now I'm worried that I'm destined for failure.

Over the past few years, I have been experiencing symptoms that I believe may be related to PTSD from being bullied and manipulated in middle school. Additionally, I have been struggling with what I believe is dissociative amnesia, causing frequent mental blocks that affect my daily life. I have been relying on caffeine to help me stay focused and think clearly, but it seems to trigger episodes of anxiety and irritability. I have been considering using marijuana for stress relief and psilocybin for deep repressed trauma, although I am aware that both substances are illegal. I know I should see a psychiatrist, but I would appreciate your professional opinion on what I should do to treat these issues before seeking further help.

I am really concerned about my brother who has been diagnosed with schizoaffective disorder and PTSD. He is 28 years old and currently lives with our mother. Unfortunately, he is not compliant with his treatment, refusing to take medication or attend appointments. Our parents are divorced, and our mother is the only one listed as his medical proxy. However, she seems reluctant to communicate with his caseworker and healthcare providers, despite being the only person he trusts. She also seems unable to set boundaries with him, such as denying him money or access to her car, even though he has no history of violence. This situation is causing a lot of stress and my mother is on the verge of a nervous breakdown. I am currently receiving treatment for generalized anxiety disorder, but I am constantly worried that something terrible will happen if no action is taken. My mother complains to my sister and me every day about my brother's behavior, such as disappearing for hours and not practicing basic hygiene, which are common issues for people with his disorders. However, she refuses to take our advice or seek professional help, and we are extremely frustrated. Any advice you can provide would be greatly appreciated.

Last week, my girlfriend's ex-husband sadly passed away due to a drug overdose. They were married for 20 years and have two daughters, a 30-year-old stepdaughter and a 19-year-old biological daughter. It seems that he had a difficult time coping with the divorce and was struggling with depression. The divorce was finalized two years ago, but even before that, he had distanced himself from his younger daughter, rarely contacting her and keeping his whereabouts a secret from her.

I've been feeling really overwhelmed and distressed lately. I've been experiencing these disturbing thoughts about my mother for over a year now. My daughter, who is 17 years old, has been in a relationship with a boy for the past 11 months. He has been well-liked by the entire family as he is polite, respectful, and displays love and tenderness towards her. However, recently, he shared with her that he has had thoughts about wanting to kill someone, not anyone in particular, but to experience the power of determining another person's fate.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for a year and three months. We currently live together and overall, we have been happy. However, there are some issues that bother me. In the past, my boyfriend used to call me names and be mean to me for no reason. It would really hurt me. He also looks at other girls in front of me and uses the excuse that he can't help it because he's a guy. I don't mind if he looks at other girls, but doing it in front of me feels disrespectful. I love him and spoil him with gifts, but he doesn't reciprocate. He is paying the rent, so I understand why he doesn't have much money left for other things, but when he does have money, he spends it on himself. It makes me feel like he is selfish. Whenever I call him out on it, he gets angry and says that I am the one causing him to be selfish by buying him things. I hate it when he gets angry, it really hurts me emotionally. Recently, we had a fight and he threatened to take my keys. He has also stopped me from leaving in the past by unplugging my car battery or deflating my tires. It's becoming too much. I keep giving him chances because I want to believe he can change. He doesn't have many friends and he has mentioned that therapists have told him he wouldn't do well in relationships. I'm feeling lost. We have invested so much in each other and even my family got him a car. But every time we fight, he wants everything back and I end up telling him to keep it all and I'll leave. It's just that he doesn't treat me well. Why can't he change?

I have been experiencing extreme anxiety related to my health. I constantly worry about any minor symptom and catastrophize it into something serious. For example, a headache makes me think I have a brain tumor, chest pain makes me fear a heart attack, and stomach pain makes me worry about appendicitis. At night, I struggle to sleep because I'm hyperaware of my heartbeat and have difficulty breathing. I believe this is anxiety because it only happens when I'm thinking about it at night. I also feel intense fear when visiting doctors and hospitals, as I'm scared of what they might find through tests. Additionally, I have severe performance anxiety, especially when I have to perform as part of my music studies. I can't perform as well as I do during practice because I'm overcome with fear. I also tend to worry about everyday situations like public speaking. Do these experiences indicate anxiety? If so, what can I do about it? I want to talk to someone about it, but I feel embarrassed and childish.

I am a third year history of art student, currently 20 years old. I began experiencing symptoms of depression and anxiety towards the end of high school. Lately, I have been struggling with mental confusion, memory problems, and even getting headaches whenever I try to engage in conversation with others.

I'm really concerned about my 13-year-old who is experiencing bizarre illusions. They're going through puberty and I don't notice any other symptoms of mental illness. Could it be something other than schizophrenia? The more I research, the more worried I become.

I am feeling overwhelmed and stressed. As a mother of two children, I made the decision to live with my parents for additional support. My husband is also living with us. I recently left my job to prioritize the well-being of my kids.

I'm feeling really empty inside. I have trouble sleeping, eating, and I lack energy. My mind is constantly consumed by thoughts of emotional pain. I don't want to die, but I don't want to be a part of this world either. Everything I see just brings me sadness and pain. I'm a 23-year-old male who feels lost and doesn't know where to turn. I come from a broken family, with separated parents who have never been present. I have three brothers who I don't communicate with at all. I work at a Subway restaurant where I feel overworked and stressed. I've been single for almost two years because I don't feel worthy of anyone mentally or physically. I find people to be boring and unintelligent. My friends are okay, but I mainly see them as a distraction from my own thoughts. I just want to be happy and have goals and dreams, but all I ever experience is stress, anger, and negativity. I feel so lonely and I have nothing to look forward to. I apologize if my post is a little vague, but I don't know how else to explain my feelings.

I've been feeling really overwhelmed lately with social situations and having friends. The thought of texting or hanging out with them just gives me so much anxiety. I constantly worry that they will be mean to me or hurt me in some way. I always feel like they're mad at me and don't really like me. I find it much easier to just be alone with my boyfriend, as he is the only person I truly trust and feel comfortable around. The problem is that when I'm alone, I start to believe that everyone is looking at me and judging me, like I'm not normal or worth anything.

Over the course of my relationship with my boyfriend, there have been several instances where he has lied to me and engaged in risky behaviors, such as drinking excessively and driving while intoxicated. These incidents have occurred during difficult times in my life, such as when my grandmother was ill and eventually passed away. I also discovered that he had sent emails to personal ads on Craigslist with pictures of himself attached, although he claims that his account was hacked. Despite forgiving him and attempting to rebuild trust, he continues to engage in these behaviors and even caused damage to our home during a recent incident.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for over four years. He's never been married and is ten years older than me. On one hand, he has many positive qualities - he's loving, generous, thoughtful, responsible, and has a great sense of humor. However, on the other hand, there are some concerning behaviors. He can be controlling, condescending, and often speculates negatively about me. Despite claiming to trust me, there is always some sort of conflict between us. I often feel confused and fearful, although he has never been physically abusive. He has made some progress through personal work, but can still be hyper-sensitive and hyper-critical.

I've been feeling really overwhelmed and hopeless lately. My name is Soren. I've been experiencing symptoms that make me think I might be depressed, like persistent thoughts of suicide and past suicide attempts. Unfortunately, I haven't been able to seek professional help because of financial constraints. School has been a source of distress for me as well, with the other kids being unkind and making hurtful comments about my weight. This has led to issues with sleep and eating, as I've been unable to sleep and have started throwing up after meals. I feel so alone and in need of someone to talk to, but I don't have any friends and my relationship with my parents is strained. Whenever I try to open up to my mom, she ignores me or pushes me away, and I'm too scared to approach my dad because he's often angry and drinks excessively. I'm feeling incredibly sad and lost. Please, I really need help.

I have been in a long-term relationship with my partner for over 6 years. Lately, I've noticed that during times of high stress, she seems to disconnect and adopt a different personality. She refers to it as "going to her box." This other personality takes over for a while.

I have been in a relationship with my girlfriend for almost 2 years. We recently took a big step in our relationship when she moved into the house that I bought in February. Our relationship started in a unique way, as we met after she had a one night stand with one of my friends. Despite that unconventional beginning, we ended up connecting on a deeper level the next night. There is a strong attraction between us, both mentally and physically, which has kept us together all this time.

Thank you for reaching out. I've been struggling with how deeply little problems affect me and it's been impacting my ability to function. I have everyday issues like finances, work, and parenting, but they feel absolutely devastating to me. I'm aware that they shouldn't have such a strong hold on me and that they will pass, but I just can't seem to handle them. For instance, I recently had a conflict with my new boss who has been unprofessional and degrading. It completely destroyed me emotionally. I feel an overwhelming sense of sadness, hopelessness, and anger that is making it difficult to function. It's frustrating because I know this reaction might be irrational, but I can't seem to control it. Yesterday, I had the urge to harm myself by cutting or intentionally breaking a bone, which I know is not a healthy response. It's disheartening because I'm 44 years old, educated, have a career, a husband, and a son, yet I'm thinking like a teenager. I've been on medication for a while now, currently taking Zoloft and Xanax, but I never feel any better. I'm losing hope. Is overreacting to everything a symptom of depression? Is there anything I can do to stop this cycle? Thank you for listening and offering your guidance.

Recently, I made a troubling discovery about my boyfriend of 1 and a half years. I found out that he had been engaging in conversations with another girl online. I was able to see their conversations, and it was evident that he had informed her about our relationship, but downplayed its significance. They flirted and delved into sexual topics, and he even suggested that our relationship was more like being roommates.

I have been in a relationship with my partner for four years now, and we got engaged about a year ago. Lately, I've been having some confusing thoughts and emotions. Sometimes I feel really happy and content with my partner, but other times I question if I made the right decision to get engaged. I find myself comparing my partner's appearance to others and feeling upset that I don't have someone who looks "better." It's been bothering me a lot.

When my husband and I were caring for our grandson, we made sure to follow all of the rules and routines that my son and his wife had set for us. However, whenever the baby would fuss at night, they would become suspicious and question what we had done during the day. It was hurtful, but I didn't want to walk out on them for the sake of the child. Instead, we would explain ourselves and apologize, and my daughter-in-law seemed to accept our apology politely. I thought she was gradually accepting us as part of the extended family.

I've been feeling really overwhelmed and confused since my dad passed away two months ago. He had been diagnosed with COPD five years ago, and even though we weren't very close, I still made an effort to spend time with him every weekend until work got in the way last year. Now that he's gone, I haven't had much time to grieve because I was only given two days off work before going back to my normal 10-hour shifts. Everyone keeps telling me to cheer up, but I don't feel fine at all. All I want to do is cry, but I feel guilty because I didn't visit him as much as I should have. I've struggled with self-harm in the past, and I can feel myself slipping back into that state, but I don't want to go down that path again. I just don't understand how I'm supposed to carry on as if nothing has happened.

Recently, I confessed to my ex about a lie that I had been carrying for months. This lie involved pretending to be sick, and my ex had been supporting me during this time. However, now that the truth is out, he has completely cut off all contact with me. His family has even mentioned the possibility of filing restraining orders if I try to reach out to him. I feel lost and in need of help for myself. However, I can't help but think that therapy won't be effective without his support. How can I make him understand that I have problems and need help and support?

I'm currently in a relationship with my boyfriend who has anger outbursts. We've been together for 5 months and I'm finding it difficult to know how to handle these situations. Throughout our time together, I've learned about his troubled past, including a violent upbringing, a criminal history, and issues within his family since childhood. In his previous relationship, there were domestic violence orders between him and his ex-partner, with whom he shares a 6-year-old daughter. He claims to have sought counseling and anger management to address his anger issues and believes he now knows how to handle them better.

Patient: I want to talk about my childhood and some of the experiences I had growing up. When I was 7 years old, my cousin, who was 13 at the time, sexually abused me. I didn't fully understand what was happening, and he made me promise not to tell anyone. It's something that I don't have clear memories of, but it has affected me in different ways. At that time, my sister was also struggling with mental health issues, and my mom was going through a difficult time as well. We were homeless and dealing with financial problems. Eventually, we were able to move out after living with our cousins for almost 8 years.

Hello, I am a 25-year-old medical student. Since the age of 13, I have been experiencing episodes of depression, which are often triggered by exams. I have noticed that the stress and pressure associated with my childhood dream of becoming a doctor may be contributing to these feelings. Currently, I have been taking Escitalopram 10mg once daily for the past 8 years, which initially helped but is no longer effective. I also have intrusive obsessive images from the past that persist despite the medication. I have lost hope in medication altogether and I'm wondering why I still feel so afraid of exams, even though I have taken countless exams before.

Since I was a young child, I have always experienced excessive worry. Now that I am 15 years old, I have noticed that my anxiety has been getting worse. Anxiety and panic disorders do run in my family, but I am not sure if I have one. I have been researching anxiety disorders and many of the symptoms seem to apply to me. These symptoms include physical weakness, poor memory, fear or confusion, difficulty relaxing, constant worrying, shortness of breath, palpitations, upset stomach, and poor concentration. I can remember experiencing panic as early as five years old. One memory that stands out is when my mom was leaving for work and I watched her drive away, feeling worried that she might not come back or get hurt in an accident. I'm not sure if this level of worry is normal for a young child. Do you think I might have an anxiety disorder? (I should also mention that my father is an alcoholic and my childhood was filled with my parents yelling at each other and a few major incidents. My personality is quite different from my siblings, and it's unclear where it comes from.)

Patient's statement (rewritten): Over the past 2 years, my boyfriend has been admitted to a mental health institution twice. He has been struggling to find employment and was fired from his previous job due to difficulties with concentration and completing tasks. I suspect that during this time he stopped taking his medication. After his first hospitalization, he had a tough time adjusting to the medication and refused to take it for a few months. The second hospitalization occurred because he lied about taking his medication and his behavior became problematic again. Following that, he started taking his medication under the supervision of his mother, but he eventually lied about taking it again. His behavior has become concerning, with signs of laughing to himself, poor eating habits, leaving food unfinished, and difficulty sleeping. I recently discovered that he has been engaging with other women online, which deeply hurt me. Out of the blue, he decided to travel to New York in search of a job, leaving with a one-way ticket and not taking his medication while there. We have been together for almost four years and have never had relationship problems before. I love him and want to support him, but the cheating issue is causing significant strain on our relationship. His mother and I have discussed the possibility of him returning to the hospital for treatment, in the hopes that he can accept his condition and receive the help he needs. I feel lost and unsure of what else I can do. This situation is taking a toll on my well-being, as I constantly worry about him and have tried my best to assist him, but it feels like my efforts are futile.

Patient's statement (rewritten): Throughout my life, I have experienced periods of depression. It became noticeable to my parents when I started isolating myself from my friends and spending a lot of time sleeping. However, there are also times when I enjoy going out and having fun with my few friends. The problem is that when we go out, we tend to drink excessively and I always end up blacking out. This leads to intense feelings of depression and worthlessness when I wake up. Three months ago, I had a negative incident at work and had to take a semester off from school. I've been feeling extremely low, even contemplating suicide, but after my mom threatened to take me to a hospital, I reached out to a hotline for support.

I have been struggling with my mental health for the past three years, but I'm hesitant to seek therapy because I don't want my family to find out. I live with my mom, brothers, and sister, and while my mom knows about my struggles, she doesn't fully understand or support seeking professional help. She believes that depression is a choice and has even made fun of people we know who have sought treatment. It's been really difficult for me because I don't think anyone would choose to feel this way. Additionally, my mom wants to know where I am all the time due to my disability. I've been considering online therapy, but I don't have the financial means at the moment. I live in Illinois. Can you help me explore my options?

I have been experiencing intense fear and anxiety when it comes to situations and people that I can't control. These feelings are accompanied by vivid nightmares about my family and I being taken and tortured without dying. I wake up in a state of hyperventilation and sometimes even vomit. Sending my son to school is a source of great fear for me. Additionally, I have a persistent feeling of detachment from reality. I often entertain thoughts that maybe I am in a coma somewhere and this life is all in my mind. I don't experience any emotions except for panic and fear. I desperately want to feel happy, but I just don't. It's like I'm observing myself from a distance. There are times when I feel like I have no control over my actions, even when I know they're not appropriate. My husband is growing frustrated with me. I want to emphasize that I have never harmed myself or others physically, and I have no intentions of doing so. I am not suicidal.

I've been experiencing severe symptoms during my menstrual cycle for the past two years. It starts with heavy cramps and terrible headaches that make it difficult for me to sleep at night. Even stronger pain medication doesn't seem to help. My period lasts for two weeks, accompanied by migraines and sleepless nights. After it ends, it takes about a week before it starts again. Doctors haven't been able to find a specific cause for my symptoms and have suggested that the pain might be psychological. I feel alone and isolated, as my friends don't believe me and I'm struggling at school. Additionally, I've been having nightmares about experiencing real pain and thoughts of self-harm. I don't know what to do and I need help.

I have been in a relationship with my fiance for over 5 years. He has a history of going off his medication, specifically Abilify, and experiencing psychotic symptoms. Recently, he tapered down from 20 mg to 5 mg of Abilify under his doctor's guidance, but this led to anger, aggression, and other symptoms. He has been back on 20 mg for 3 weeks now, but there hasn't been any improvement. I'm wondering how long it will take for him to get back to his normal self and if 20 mg is enough for him to stabilize. Additionally, his doctor diagnosed him with bipolar disorder, but given his psychotic and aggressive behavior, I'm wondering if it could be schizophrenia instead. Can bipolar disorder cause hallucinations and involuntary movements like nodding and hand movements? I'm doing my best to support him, but it's taking a toll on me emotionally. Is it normal for the medication to take this long to take effect? Thank you for providing this helpful resource.

Over the past year, I have been in a loving relationship with a man. Our relationship is amazing, except for our sexual experiences. He has been unable to orgasm, and he believes it's due to anxiety. We have had two successful experiences in the past, through mutual masturbation and oral sex. However, since then, he has been avoiding any form of intimacy or sexual activity.

I have been married for almost 3 years now. It was a love marriage, but we had to wait 2 years for my husband's parents to approve before getting married. My husband does love me, but it feels like his main concern is making his parents happy. He often prioritizes their happiness over mine, and it's causing strain in our relationship.

I'm a 15-year-old who is currently going through a difficult situation with my mom. We constantly argue and I struggle to control my anger. During our fights, we both say hurtful things to each other. My mom has said some really awful things in the past, like wishing she didn't have me as her daughter. I've also said mean things to her. My friend has been experiencing paranoid beliefs for the past five years. Is that a good idea?

Lately, I've been noticing that I lack compassion for others, and it's been causing me a lot of confusion and concern. I have been diagnosed with Borderline Personality Disorder, depression, and general anxiety, and throughout my life, I've always felt somewhat apathetic. Recently, though, people in my life have been pointing out that my reactions to other people's distressing situations are not "normal." For example, when my grandmother's sister passed away and she became extremely depressed, I didn't feel any sympathy or sadness for her. In fact, I felt contempt and even anger, like she should just move on. It's not that I don't have emotions of my own - in fact, my emotions are intense and unstable. But when it comes to empathizing with others, there's just nothing there emotionally. This lack of empathy also extends to times when I say things that are hurtful or impolite. I don't mean to be mean, but I just can't understand on an emotional level how my words or actions will affect the other person. Half the time, I don't even know what I'm feeling myself. I only realized this about myself when others started pointing it out. So now, I pretend like I'm feeling something. If I hear about something on the news, I'll say, "Oh, that's terrible. I feel so awful for them." I'm pretty good at acting, so I'm the only one who knows I'm pretending. I'm starting to wonder if I might be narcissistic. I've always been self-absorbed, vain, and entitled, so maybe this lack of empathy is connected to that? I've even thought about the possibility of having Narcissistic Personality Disorder, as I've read about it and it seems to match me. My parents have also suspected that I might have Asperger's, but I've never been tested. I'm just feeling so confused right now. Any advice or explanation would be greatly appreciated.

Counselor: Thank you for sharing your concerns and experiences with me. It sounds like you've been through a lot and it's important to address these issues in a safe and supportive environment.
