While medication can help stabilize moods, it's important to remember that it doesn't define who you are as a person. Your true self is still present, and the medication is simply helping manage symptoms.

Recently, I've been feeling a bit overwhelmed with my close friend of 21 years. Our relationship has had its ups and downs, but in the last two years, we've become really close. We talk on the phone 4-5 times a day and try to meet up at least once a month. Overall, things have been going well.

I have been experiencing disturbing dreams every night where I lose people close to me, or even everyone, including myself. When I wake up, I feel confused and sometimes question if it was real. Hi, thank you for being here. I've been in a long-distance relationship with my boyfriend for over a year now, and we're facing some significant challenges related to his anxiety and OCD. The distance seems to exacerbate the issues.

I've had negative experiences with counselors who only offer talk therapy. How can I find a counselor who can teach strategies and help with boundaries?

Recently, I had a conversation with my boyfriend where he expressed excitement about seeing his friend that day. In that moment, I felt compelled to tell him that he doesn't have to pretend to feel things around me. I reassured him that he doesn't have to pretend to care about people just to please me, as I won't judge him. Can you provide some clarity on this?

I suggested buying a new home, but he doesn't think that's the issue. The tension is increasing, and I'm not sure what the best course of action is.

He has carried this burden for years and has always expressed a desire to seek revenge on her for falsely accusing him. The only thing that has prevented him from taking action is his responsibility to financially support his family.

I have faced a series of challenges throughout my life, starting with my mother's unknown illness that has caused me to constantly fear losing her. In first grade, I experienced bullying, which led me to cope by eating and subsequently gaining weight. This only made me a bigger target for bullies due to my shyness and sensitivity. However, when I entered junior high and moved to a new location, the bullying stopped and I began to lose weight. Unfortunately, the cumulative effects of eight years of bullying had taken a toll on my mental health. Despite maintaining a facade of happiness, the situation took a turn for the worse when my brother had a surgery that went wrong. This caused me to completely break down, resulting in excessive eating, sleeping, and a constant state of anxiety, distress, and depression. My attendance at school significantly declined, and I even started experiencing panic attacks while there. Although I had previously excelled academically, my grades suffered during this period. It was difficult for my teacher to believe that I was struggling since I had always presented myself as having everything together. He attributed my behavior to my age, dismissing the severity of my mental health struggles.

For instance, he repeatedly checks if everything is secure, like the car and the house lock. Sometimes, he clenches his fist or does strange arm movements, seemingly venting anger. While he is generally down to earth and enjoys talking to strangers, his anger seems to be building up inside him. He trusts me enough to share this because it has been worsening over the years, especially during times of financial stress and frequent school changes. He feels disturbed and fears losing control mentally, although he assures me he would never harm an innocent person. Despite his intelligence, optimism, tenacity, and hard work, he feels like a chaotic mess. Do you have any insights into what he might be struggling with?

"Hello, I have been experiencing the presence of multiple voices in my head. These voices often provide suggestions and commentary on my daily activities. I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for the past 10 years since we were 19 and 22 years old respectively. Currently, we are 29 and 32 years old, with me being the older one. I've been struggling with a question that has been bothering me for quite some time now. Throughout most of my life, I felt like I was functioning normally, but over the past few years, I've been dealing with a lot of problems that seem to be evolving.

Throughout my life, I've experienced a lot of unhappiness. Although I have some good memories, a lot of what stands out to me are moments of crying or fighting with my mother since I was very young. I first attempted suicide at the age of 4 by trying to jump off my roof, and I continued to struggle with suicidal thoughts until a few years ago. My younger sister brought some temporary relief, but when I reached middle school, I faced bullying and began to question if there was something inherently wrong with me. Then, my parents' divorce added to the challenges. To cope with the emptiness I felt, I turned to partying, friends, and boyfriends. However, whenever I lose any of them, it only amplifies my sadness, hopelessness, and emptiness.

Hi, I've been struggling with my emotions towards my friend, Ben. We've known each other since September 2012, and I developed strong feelings for him in October of that year. I confessed my feelings to him in March 2013, but he didn't give me a clear answer. Since then, I've tried to distance myself from him, but it only made things worse. I feel nervous and afraid around him, and I have trouble holding conversations. I care about him deeply, but I want these feelings to go away. What should I do?

I have been struggling with my mental health for the past 30 years. I have tried various therapists and medications, but it feels disheartening to see that none of my dreams have come true. The future appears bleak and I'm feeling quite hopeless.

Patient's Statement: I'm really concerned about my son's behavior. He's turning 4 in just 2 days, and while he can be sweet and loving, he also displays violent and aggressive tendencies. It feels like there's no middle ground for him, it's either extreme sweetness or extreme aggression. Recently, his aggression has been escalating. For instance, his 7-year-old sister, who has ADHD, reminded him not to touch the computer while she was using it for her spelling practice, and he tried to punch her in the face. It was clear that he was filled with anger, and if she hadn't moved, she could have ended up with a black eye.

I've been in a relationship with my girlfriend for about 8 months now. She's an incredible person and meets all the qualities I look for in a life partner. However, I recently discovered some information about her past that is really affecting me. While I understand that she is still the same person I fell in love with, I'm struggling to let go of her previous sexual experiences. These thoughts and images keep haunting me.

I am currently in a relationship with my boyfriend of nearly 4 years. We have a blended family with his 2-year-old son and I am currently pregnant. My boyfriend has a lot of trust issues due to being cheated on in the past, and he often accuses me of being unfaithful. He has strict rules about me interacting with other men, even in a professional context. I find myself avoiding any contact with men at work and rushing home to avoid accusations. It's exhausting and I feel emotionally drained. However, I'm afraid to leave him because I fear change and being alone. I worry that I might miss him if I leave. I don't know what to do.

I have been living with a man for the past three years, and I am seeking guidance on how to address his inappropriate behavior. On multiple occasions, he has touched females in our family or close friends without their consent. For example, he touched my sister's arm multiple times and even held onto her arms without saying anything. Another incident involved him putting his arm around my niece in a way that made her uncomfortable. How can I approach him and communicate that this behavior is inappropriate and makes others uncomfortable?

I'm a 15-year-old student in my second year of high school. I have been diagnosed with ADD and depression. Lately, I've been experiencing disturbing thoughts of harming other people. These thoughts seem to come out of nowhere and they are really frightening. I don't have any specific reasons for these thoughts and I haven't been bullied. Although I don't have any friends, I prefer it that way. The idea of causing harm to someone, slowly and intimately, sends shivers down my spine. It's not something I find pleasurable, but it feels like a compulsion, like a drug addiction. If I don't act on these thoughts, I become hot flashes, twitchy, nervous, and anxious. I feel like I have to do it. It could be anyone, I wouldn't care. I know I need help for this, and I'm desperate to get it, but I'm afraid. First, I'm worried that my family won't believe me. I'm afraid they might think I'm lying for attention or that it's somehow related to my other mental health conditions. I'm also scared that they will see me as abnormal or treat me differently. I really need guidance on how to approach this situation and seek the help I need.

I've been dealing with a lot of stress and sadness lately. Both my parents are facing serious health issues. My mother has Huntington's disease, and it has been difficult to see her condition worsen over the years. Recently, I learned that Huntington's is hereditary, and I'm worried that I may have it too. On top of that, my father was diagnosed with Lou Gehrig's disease about a year ago, and his health is declining rapidly. I haven't talked to him about his situation, and it's been weighing on me. I've been feeling very depressed and anxious, and I have this constant stomach pain. I haven't reached out to my sisters because I feel it will only make me more depressed. Any advice?

My 7-year-old son has been engaging in inappropriate behavior with his friends and younger brother for several years. This includes touching each other's private parts, pulling down their pants, and laughing about it. I have spoken to him about this repeatedly and he knows it's wrong, but he continues to do it. I'm concerned and need advice on how to address this issue.

My 11-year-old daughter has been expressing fear and worry about having an illness or disease. She seems to be fixated on this idea and has been talking about it every day. She also mentioned being afraid of dying, which I understand is a common fear, but it seems like she is becoming obsessed with it. She complains of various aches and pains daily. I want to know if this is a normal phase that kids go through during puberty or if I should seek therapy for her. I took her to the doctor for a lump she felt under her jaw, and the doctor mentioned something about it being psychosomatic. I'm not really sure what that means despite looking it up. Can you please help me understand? It's been going on for about two months, and there hasn't been any major traumatic event in our family. Her biological father has never been in her life. My fiancé, who has been in her life for 10 years, is strict but loving. However, sometimes he goes on long rants when he's upset with her. I'm not sure if this is somehow impacting her mental well-being. I'm really worried and don't know what to do.

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for a while now, but his mental health struggles have really taken a toll on us. While he hasn't received an official diagnosis, there is a history of bipolar disorder in his family, and he exhibits symptoms that seem to align with multiple disorders. One physician unofficially mentioned bipolar with schizoaffective disorder.

Over two years ago, I experienced a significant loss when my father passed away from pancreatic cancer. In order to support my mother, I made the decision to leave my life and friends on the east coast and help take care of him. Before his passing, my parents adopted my young niece and nephew. Following his death, I made the choice to stay with my mother to assist her in raising the kids. Eventually, my mother decided that she wanted to move away from the place where my father passed, and we relocated to the west coast. During this time, I maintained a close friendship with a woman and we eventually decided to pursue a romantic relationship. However, I have concerns about the age difference between us, as she is 23 and I am 35. She moved out west with me approximately six months after I made the move.

Counselor's response: Hello, thank you for sharing your concerns about your relationship with your parents and your current boyfriend. It sounds like you have had some challenging experiences in the past with previous relationships, and it's understandable that you may feel hesitant about how your parents are reacting to your current relationship. It's important to remember that you are an adult now and have the right to make your own decisions about your relationships. However, it's also important to consider your parents' perspective and understand that they may have concerns for your well-being based on their past experiences and desire to protect you.

Counselor's Response: Hello, Michaela. Thank you for reaching out and sharing your experiences with me. I want you to know that I'm here to support you. It sounds like you have been through a lot, and I'm sorry to hear about the loss of your mother and friend. The abuse and trauma you have experienced are not your fault, and it's important to remember that. It takes a lot of strength to keep going, and I admire your resilience.

Lately, I've been feeling really frustrated with myself. It feels like no matter what I do, things just don't go right and it's really starting to bother me. I've noticed that whenever I try to change a habit, I end up giving up on myself so easily.
I've been going to a psychiatrist at the local hospital, but I'm hesitant to share my true thoughts and actions with them because I'm afraid they'll think I'm crazy and want to institutionalize me.

Patient: Over the past year, my family has been coping with the aftermath of my sister's suicide attempt. Initially, my parents expressed concern for my well-being by constantly asking if I was okay. However, lately, they have been withdrawing from me and even blaming me for most of the negative incidents that occur at home. It's been really difficult to handle.

I am a 24-year-old homemaker and mother. I have been dealing with anxiety for most of my life, but it has intensified since becoming a mother. I quit my job to take care of my children, including my stepdaughters. I feel overwhelmed and frustrated with my responsibilities, as well as with my husband's lack of understanding. I also feel anger towards my stepdaughters and my own toddler, even though I don't want to hurt them. I have a history of occasional depression and I'm wondering if this could be postpartum depression or if it's related to my father's manic depressive episodes. I don't have insurance or the means to seek expensive help. Is there a support hotline or resource you can recommend?

Hi, I'm a 23-year-old graduate from a prestigious university with a strong academic record. Despite my achievements, I've been struggling with how my parents treat me compared to my younger brother. They seem to favor him and treat him like royalty while disregarding my feelings and needs. It's been a pattern throughout my life and has deeply affected my self-worth and mental well-being. Even recently, when there was a shooting at my school, their lack of concern for my safety was shocking. I feel unloved and it has caused anxiety and a loss of motivation. I'm not sure how to lift myself up from this situation.

Recently, I've been feeling really overwhelmed and stressed out. It feels like no matter what I do, I can't catch a break. I'm constantly juggling work, family responsibilities, and personal commitments. It's starting to take a toll on my mental and physical health.

Lately, I've been experiencing a mix of anger and sadness. I've noticed that I feel fine when I'm alone, but when I interact with others and they do something I don't like, it puts me in a bad mood. I've also been consistently rude to my mom, and I don't understand why. I want to feel happy again, but I'm not sure what's causing these emotions. Sometimes, I even question my will to live, although it's not happening as frequently anymore.

I met this guy at a casino in November 2012. Initially, I turned him down, but over time, I developed feelings for him. However, I was hesitant to pursue a romantic relationship because I didn't want to jeopardize our friendship. Eventually, we ended up dating for two months. However, he recently encountered some difficulties with his housing situation and expressed that he wanted to just be friends. I became concerned and started to reach out to him frequently, even going behind his back to involve my mom. I've been trying to make things work, but he keeps telling me that he has other problems and to stop texting him.

My friend has been diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia for the past 10 years. He is currently on medication to manage his symptoms, but it has been a challenging journey for him. He lives with his sister and her family, but he doesn't have many social connections and often feels isolated. Additionally, his mother has passed away, and his father doesn't spend much time with him due to his illness.

I have been in a relationship with my girlfriend for almost three years and we have been living together for two of those years. However, I have discovered that the girl my girlfriend used to see before we got together keeps finding ways to come back into our lives. I found out a year ago that they were secretly communicating, and it seemed like more than just a friendly conversation. I confronted my girlfriend and she confessed, but now I've recently discovered that they have been talking since before we even got together. I haven't brought this up with my girlfriend because she gets defensive whenever I try to discuss it. I'm worried about confronting her and being accused of snooping. How can I resolve this and find forgiveness, while also addressing my concerns with her?

I have been struggling with disturbing thoughts and fantasies about committing acts of violence towards others, including my family members and strangers. These thoughts have progressed to the point where I feel strong urges to act on them, but I have been able to resist so far. It's concerning to me that these thoughts both intrigue and excite me, even though I know they should sicken me. Recently, I have even included myself as a victim in these fantasies.

Throughout my childhood, my dad was absent from my life, both physically and emotionally. He would leave early in the morning for work and come back late at night, only to argue with my mom and then go to sleep. When I was 9, I discovered that my mom was suffering from depression due to my dad's behavior, which made her really ill. I never felt like my dad cared about me or my brother, and I resented him so much during my awkward puberty phase. I can't help but think about what a terrible father he was to us.

I am a 22-year-old individual who has never been in a romantic relationship. I have noticed a pattern where whenever things start to get more intimate, I feel scared and run away. I have attempted to overcome this fear multiple times, but I always end up finding flaws in the people I am with or making excuses to end the relationship.

From a young age, I have experienced bullying which has caused me to develop a fear of going out alone or to public places. I constantly feel like people are watching me or out to harm me. Additionally, I have been having relationship issues with my girlfriend. I unintentionally start arguments and then experience panic attacks afterwards. When we are apart, I become paranoid, making accusations and doubting our relationship, leading to even bigger arguments. I find myself crying often and I struggle with low self-esteem, often calling myself fat and ugly. I also get anxious when people compliment my appearance. I'm starting to wonder if my past relationships have contributed to these issues.

I've noticed that my husband displays extreme anger and reacts explosively whenever things don't go his way or when someone disagrees with him, especially me. He engages in fits of rage, screaming, cursing, breaking and throwing things. For instance, he once called me derogatory names and damaged my car's dashboard during a disagreement over a game our kids were playing. Another time, he became violent when I suggested he handle a disagreement with his father differently.

I have been struggling with a sexual arousal towards women's panties for most of my life. It's something I've kept hidden and nobody knows about it. I find myself becoming extremely turned on by the thought, sight, and touch of panties, to the point where I sometimes wear my wife's satin panties and masturbate when I'm home alone. I've even bought a few pairs for myself that I keep hidden. This fetish seems to be growing stronger over the years, and I'm worried about it taking over my life or being discovered. I can't even go near the lingerie section of a department store without feeling overwhelmed. I can't talk to my wife about it because I fear she would have me committed. Can you help me?

It seems like my boyfriend's mom has a really hard time when we don't eat dinner at their house. She gets upset and it feels like she overreacts. One time, when we were leaving to go to my place, she seemed really shocked and upset when my boyfriend said we were going to my house instead. She reacted as if it was the worst thing in the world.

I'm really sorry to hear that you've been through such a difficult and challenging upbringing. It sounds like the pressure and demands from your dad have had a significant impact on your mental health and well-being. It's understandable that this has caused you to experience depression, OCD, eating disorders, and suicidal thoughts. It's important to recognize that these feelings are valid, and I'm glad you reached out for support.

Patient: I've been dealing with self-esteem issues for a long time. In high school, I was known as the "weird girl" and I've had trouble sleeping for the past 4 years. I've also had some weight fluctuations due to an emotionally exhausting long distance relationship. I've only been with 3 guys and they were all unstable and controlling. I have some paranoid thoughts about people, and sometimes I think my best friends don't like me. I feel guilty about past decisions, and I experience intense mood swings - sometimes feeling hyper and happy, and other times feeling irritable and upset. I've even had episodes of anger where I've broken things. I also struggle with self-criticism and perfectionism.

I'm a 16-year-old who has been struggling with depression for the past three years. I've turned to self-harm as a way to cope, and it's affecting my sleep. I constantly argue with my family and have difficulty forming and maintaining friendships due to being bullied for the past five years. I feel isolated and find it hard to open up to others because I don't want attention. I feel like a careless and selfish person, but I know it's not true. I want to talk to someone about how I feel, but I also fear being judged. My emotions are overwhelming, and I often explode at my family. I feel misunderstood and have thoughts of dying, believing that no one cares about me. I'm scared that things will get worse.

I started working a night shift job in November and it really took a toll on me. I was already taking an antipsychotic and an antidepressant, but my difficulties with the night shift led my doctor to prescribe another antidepressant. I started feeling better for a while, but then I ended up losing my job. Surprisingly, losing the job was actually a relief, but now I feel like my life is falling apart.

I'm 12 years old and I'm having a hard time at home with my mom. She frequently picks fights with me and yells at me every day. On top of that, she makes me do all the chores in the house. I believe her behavior might be influenced by her own past experiences, as her mom passed away when she was just 11 and she had to live with her mean-spirited grandpa. I've tried addressing the issues and talking things out with my mom, but she becomes extremely defensive and dismissive. She often threatens me with punishments like cutting off my hair or taking away my clothes. Whenever I cry, she tells me to stop or threatens to smack me. It feels like no matter what I say, she accuses me of talking back. I really don't know what to do anymore.

Over a year ago, I made the difficult decision to leave my verbally abusive husband after giving him multiple chances to change. Although he made some small improvements, our relationship ultimately reached a breaking point. Recently, I started dating someone new, and that's when my ex checked himself into a psychiatric hospital and began taking medication. He's now claiming to have had a genuine change of heart and is taking responsibility for his past behavior. I want to believe he has truly changed, but I'm struggling with trust and fear of falling back into the same patterns. Can people really change for good? Can I change and be myself without fear? Are there any programs or resources that could help us succeed? I'm torn between my new partner, who treats me well, and the hope of rebuilding a happy family with my ex, even though my friends and family dislike him.

My boyfriend has been experiencing paranoia and hearing voices after confronting our roommate about gossiping. He used to smoke pot every day but has stopped for the past two days. I'm worried about him and want to know if the pot could be causing his symptoms. I also need advice on what we can do to help him while he refuses to see a therapist.

I am a 32-year-old single female. Recently, I reconnected with a man I knew in high school. I used to have a crush on him, and we have been meeting casually. However, I became concerned when he mentioned that he doesn't remember the past with any emotions. This struck me as odd. I have my guard up because in the past, I have been attracted to men who have mental health problems. My last serious relationship ended when I discovered that my boyfriend was stealing from my parents to buy prescription drugs online. He came from a traumatic and broken family background.

Lately, whenever I try to open up about my feelings or talk about this particular issue, I start to feel uneasy. I think part of it is because people often respond with cliché phrases like "love yourself" or "the perfect guy will come along" or "it's just not your time yet." It makes me feel like my emotions are being dismissed and invalidated.

My wife and I have been struggling in our marriage for some time now. We have been seeing a therapist, and I personally feel like it's been beneficial. However, my wife is unsure about its effectiveness. We both make an effort to work on our relationship, but it feels like our attempts fall short of meeting each other's needs. Our "love languages" are so different that it feels counter-intuitive to give each other what we need. Despite all this, we are staying together for the sake of our 5-year-old son. Both of us come from divorced families and have seen the negative impact it can have on children. Our son is very sensitive, and we believe that a divorce would be traumatic for him. As a result, we feel compelled to stay in this loveless marriage. We try our best not to fight or display any negativity in front of our son, but he is starting to notice the subtle signs that we are not acting like a loving couple. We want to know what strategies I can pursue on my own as the one partner who still believes in the potential of therapy.

I'm a 15-year-old girl and my teachers have been concerned about me being antisocial since the passing of my good friend and her family. My guidance counselor called me into her office and said that I needed to work on some things with her. She wanted me to meet with her three times a week and come into her office twice a day to say hi. She would also talk about her kids and ask me to hang out with her on weekends or go out to lunch. I find it strange and I'm not sure if this is okay or odd.

I have been struggling with skin picking since 6th grade when I first started getting pimples. It started off as a monthly occurrence, but it has gotten progressively worse. Now, I pick at my skin every single day, and it's not just on my face anymore. I have scars and wounds all over my body. It's affecting my self-esteem and how I interact with others. I've tried different methods to stop, but nothing seems to work. I even avoid taking care of my hygiene because it triggers my skin picking. I'm only 15 and I'm worried about how out of control this has become.

Patient: I'm feeling really stuck right now. My parents won't allow me to see my boyfriend of 8 months because they don't understand what I see in him. He's had a difficult life, but they seem to judge him based on that. We've broken up a couple of times in the past, but we're back together now and he's really committed to making it work. My parents keep saying he's a player and using me, but he's never cheated on me and we haven't been intimate. I understand that my parents want to protect me, but I feel like they're going about it the wrong way. My boyfriend and I have decided to stay together even if we can't see each other, but I know it's not a sustainable solution. I don't want to damage my relationship with my parents, but I also want to be able to see my boyfriend. I just want them to understand and support my love for him. Can you please help me?

Since my teenage years, I have been feeling dissatisfied with my life. I constantly compare myself to others and feel like I missed out on certain experiences, especially during my teenage years. I spent a lot of time being afraid of growing older and now I find myself longing for high school. I wish I could go back and be someone special, like a football player or an academic. I tend to downplay my talents, such as my proficiency in ASL, because it doesn't seem to be highly regarded. I also feel sad about being an adult because I worry that I won't excel at anything or feel recognized. I'm not sure why I feel so unworthy, and I know these thoughts are unusual. Can you help me understand them?

"I don’t know what to do. When I was a child, I experienced sexual abuse from my step-brother. It started when I was very young, around 6 years old, but my memories are vague, so it's possible it happened even earlier. I understand that young children may struggle to process and remember such traumatic events, which is why abusers often target them."

When I was younger, my brother took advantage of me. I can't remember if he actually 'did' anything, I blanked everything out. Today, I love my brother. Is that normal? I feel that because I was so young and didn't fully understand what was happening, he may have influenced my decisions to engage in inappropriate activities that I now regret. No one knows about what happened, not even my brother. For some reason, these memories resurfaced in January and I can't understand why, after all these years when I thought I had moved on. Should I just leave it in the past and try to forget about it, considering how long ago it happened and the lack of clarity in my memory? I just want to get over this without causing my family any pain.

I'm 26 years old and I've been in an ongoing feud with my parents for over a year because of my boyfriend. We've known each other since childhood and reconnected two years ago. However, my parents dislike him due to his lack of a college degree, cultural differences, and appearance. They judge him based on pictures and refuse to get to know him. My mom calls me offensive names and sends my boyfriend offensive texts. I want to be with him, but our fights are getting worse and my family is ashamed. I need guidance because I feel overwhelmed.

This year has been challenging for me as I navigate being a junior at a prestigious university. Not only am I juggling a heavy school workload, but I am also a varsity swimmer and a member of a sorority. Unfortunately, the stress and pressure have led me to gain about 20 pounds over the past two years. While some of it can be attributed to muscle gain from weight training, a significant portion is due to poor diet habits, particularly stress eating. When I returned home for the summer, my mother constantly criticized my appearance, which only exacerbated my existing body issues. Despite my accomplishments as a member of the national team and my overall success in swimming, she seems to focus solely on my weight and even suggests that I quit the swim team to become thinner. How can I help her understand that her criticisms are not only hurtful, but also detrimental to my self-confidence and appreciation for what my body can do?

About 6 months ago, I discovered that my husband had been experiencing suicidal ideation for a year. At the time, I didn't realize how serious his condition was because he managed to function relatively well despite his depression. Depression and suicide run in his family. Around the same time, I noticed that my 16-year-old daughter was frequently upset and stressed. One of her acquaintances died by suicide a year ago, and two of her friends have been struggling with depression and seeking treatment. Worried about her well-being, I arranged for her to start therapy. While her father and friends have shown improvement with medication and therapy, my daughter and I feel that her therapy sessions haven't had much impact. She is still very reserved and shy with her therapist. Tonight, she had a breakdown and was crying again. She often wishes she could live in the fantasies she imagines and feels disappointed that she can't. Sometimes, it feels like those fantasies are more real to her than actual life. She finds real life boring and feels anxious in large groups of people. Being around her family irritates her, and she feels the urge to be mean to her siblings, which makes her feel guilty. She is often disrespectful to my husband and me and feels guilty about it too. A couple of weeks ago, she got angry with us over chores and stormed out of the house, disappearing for a few hours. It scared me, but we didn't want to reinforce attention-seeking behavior, so we treated it as if she had retreated to her room. She used to enjoy writing, but now she's discouraged because she can't seem to capture her imagination on paper as well as she wants. She acknowledges that she's being too perfectionistic but can't move past it. I think she also struggles with low self-esteem because, despite being bright, imaginative, and enjoyable to be around, she compares herself to others, particularly her siblings who excel in areas like academics, music, and athletics. As a teenager, she has become more reserved and insecure, especially outside of our family. She believes something is wrong with her. Her sleep is unaffected, and there have been no changes in her weight or diet. She maintains straight A's in school. She doesn't want to continue with her current therapist or start with someone new. I'm not sure if she's just going through normal teenage struggles or if she requires more intervention. Additionally, my failure to recognize my husband's needs makes me doubt my own judgment. Ultimately, I want my entire family to be happy again. What can I do to help her?

I've been engaging in self-harm by cutting myself for a while now. Typically, the cuts are small and the bleeding stops after a couple of minutes. However, today I went deeper and the bleeding was more severe, lasting for about 4-5 minutes. I'm unsure about when it's necessary to seek medical attention for my scars. Additionally, I'm worried because my father is a doctor and I fear he will find out if I go to the emergency room. I live in a small town, so word tends to spread. I'm also unsure if I can properly care for my scars. Can you please help me?

It seems like I've always had a difficult relationship with my mom and grandma. I don't really understand why, but we just don't seem to get along. They constantly make me feel like a disappointment and it hurts a lot. It also makes me angry about our relationship. When I turned 15, I started acting out like a typical teenager. I would party and be out of the house all the time. Then, at 18, I got into a relationship with someone I truly love. We had dated before but it didn't work out. By the way, I dropped out of school at 16 because I was feeling lost and didn't know what to do. Even now, I still feel like I don't have anyone. But let's talk about my boyfriend. We've had our ups and downs for a while. We both have good intentions, but we struggle in terms of work and school. Overall, our relationship has been difficult. I have to admit that we used to be abusive towards each other. And that brings me to my family. I feel like I've never made the right choices in life. I can't tell if it's just bad luck or if it's me. I don't really know what I want or who I am. I don't know how to rebuild myself and make my family happy. Recently, my boyfriend and I had a huge fight and I ended up breaking my hand. My grandma found out and she was furious. Before, my family didn't really like him but they tolerated him. But now, they absolutely hate him. I feel like I'm stuck between my boyfriend, my family, and myself. I love all of them, but the depression and stress they put me through is tearing me apart. I know it might seem like a simple problem, but for me, it's taking over my life. I lost my job, I'm trying to go back to school, but I just can't seem to find a way to get back on track. I'm very confused.

Throughout my life, I have struggled with low self-esteem. Initially, I dismissed it as being humble, but as time went on, compliments started to feel foreign and even insulting. This feeling of being a waste of space and time has led me to handle my own injuries and illnesses so as not to burden my mother and brother. In fact, I even question if I'm wasting your time by sharing this with you. Additionally, I have been diagnosed with depression, anxiety disorder, and borderline personality disorder, but sometimes I wonder if my doctor just rushed through the diagnosis to get me out of his office.

Lately, I've been experiencing a lot of anxiety about things that are beyond my control. I attempted to confide in my parents, but unfortunately, it didn't go well. It has only worsened my self-esteem and heightened my concern about how others perceive me. On top of that, I don't have many friends, which infuriates my parents, especially my dad. He constantly nags me to make friends and stay in touch with them. I assure him that I'll put in more effort, but the truth is, I feel like I've already given it my all.

I met my boyfriend during my junior year of college in Florida. We started out as friends, but he was also my marijuana dealer. At the time, I was working as an exotic dancer in local strip clubs with my group of girlfriends. Although I had plenty of dating experience, I had never been in a serious relationship before. Over time, we both developed strong feelings for each other. However, I have been unfaithful to him multiple times, which has caused a lot of strain in our relationship. He has become jealous, possessive, and even violent at times. Despite all the difficulties, we feel a deep connection and find it hard to stay away from each other. I have tried to end the relationship to spare us both pain, but I always end up going back to him. I'm confused if this is love. Can you provide some advice?

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for about 3 years. He smokes a lot of weed, which I have always disliked. When we argue, he becomes verbally abusive, throws things, and tells me to leave the house. He also steals from me and currently owes me Ł70. He refuses to use protection during sex and calls me selfish for not wanting to go on the pill. I worry every month that I might be pregnant. I keep telling myself I will end the relationship, but I always give him another chance. Why do I keep doing this? Please help.

For the past couple of years, I have been experiencing some disturbing thoughts and perceptions that make me feel like I am different from others. I have encountered individuals who think they might be evil, but none of them seem to truly understand the depths of true, destructive evil.

After my mom's passing in April from brain cancer, I found myself in complete denial throughout the year leading up to her death. Despite knowing that her end was near for about three weeks, the day she passed came as a huge shock to me. Following her death, I initially went into a state of shock, but in the days that followed, I gradually started to feel okay and acted normal around others, even returning to college.

When my boyfriend and I first met, he was already a father to a one-year-old son and his ex-girlfriend was pregnant with their second child. We have been together for almost a year now and things between us have become serious quickly. We are now living together.

I've been dating someone secretly behind my parents' backs, and now everything feels like it's falling apart. My parents found out, and we had a big confrontation. They initially wanted to take away my phone and ground me, but then they changed their minds and said I could continue dating him. However, when I asked my boyfriend to meet my parents, he seemed hesitant. Things are tense at home, and I feel suffocated by my parents' strict religious beliefs. I don't know what to do anymore.

Counselor: Thank you for sharing your story and being honest about how much you're still struggling with the end of your relationship. It sounds like you went through a lot of challenges and faced significant emotional pain during and after the breakup. It's understandable that you're finding it difficult to let go, especially considering the strong emotional connection you had with this person.

I've been struggling with various mental health issues for quite some time now. I've had an eating disorder for the past 30 years, and I also engage in mild self-harm, experience depression, and have issues with dissociation. Recently, I've come to recognize that trauma is a significant part of my past, and I suspect that I may be dealing with post-traumatic stress as well.

Since a young age, I have been plagued by intrusive sexual images that feel like flashbacks. They involve the same person and feel disturbingly real. After these episodes, I withdraw and avoid touch, with a deep fear of being raped. Interactions with men are awkward, and stories or images of rape trigger intense distress and suicidal thoughts. I also have an unfounded fear of molesting children. I've researched repressed memories and wonder if my symptoms suggest childhood abuse. I have struggled with eating disorders, self-harm, anxiety/panic attacks, low self-esteem, and fear of abandonment. No diagnosis has provided answers. Could these symptoms indicate abuse and flashbacks?

Throughout my life, I have struggled with feeling like an imposter. This feeling of being inadequate and not fitting in has been present even within my own family. I constantly feel like an outsider, never measuring up in terms of intelligence, strength, or confidence. I have experienced numerous failures, so much so that I've lost count. My personal relationships have always been chaotic and unstable. Whenever I develop a connection with a woman and feel a mutual attraction, I immediately push her away, questioning why she would want to be with me. I have always believed that I would be a terrible husband, not because of cruelty, but because I struggle with closeness and intimacy. It has caused so much distress to my wife and nearly destroyed our marriage. I don't want to be alone, but I fear that it is my inevitable fate and what is best for those I care about. I feel lost and unsure of what to do.

I am a recently divorced woman who entered into a casual relationship with a man eight years older than me. However, he pushed for a serious commitment and professed his love for me after a few months. We have now been together for seven months, and I also told him that I love him. Recently, I had a gut feeling that something was off when I saw him with another woman at a cookout. When I confronted him, he admitted to having a sexual encounter with her while he was drunk. He apologized and wants to make things work, but I'm unsure about what to do. He doesn't want to go back to a casual relationship, but the other woman frequently stays at their house, and he drinks often. I also have joint custody of my children, and my boyfriend has expressed discomfort about never having been to my house. I'm torn about whether to stay or leave.

Thank you for reaching out. I'm currently in a relationship and we just celebrated our 6-month anniversary. However, I find myself feeling suspicious and worried about my girlfriend potentially cheating on me, especially since she has a history of meeting people online. She has opened up about her previous online relationship, where she engaged in video calls and intimate conversations. Despite her reassurances that she has changed, I still struggle with trust due to her frequent video chatting with her online friends, including her ex. Our relationship has also become more focused on online interactions rather than going on dates. I feel helpless and unsure about how to address my suspicions. Can you provide guidance on how to trust her and overcome my jealousy?

My partner and I have been in a committed relationship for the past three years. We live together and have built a life together. However, two months ago, I discovered that my partner had been texting another woman while we were out for dinner with his mother. It turns out that the woman's husband found out about the messages and confronted my partner late at night. The next morning, my partner confessed to me, revealing that he had exchanged explicit pictures with her and had been expressing romantic feelings towards her. He also mentioned that she has claimed to be in an abusive relationship and has even threatened to harm herself. She has two children.

I first met my boyfriend in 2007 when we were in the same class, but we didn't really know each other well. In 2011, he reached out to me on Facebook and we started dating. He became my go-to person whenever I had a problem. He was like a safe haven for me when I felt tired of dealing with other people. He meant everything to me. However, I have a naturally angry disposition, but I have a good heart and tend to express all my feelings. During that time, my boyfriend was very caring, but I didn't appreciate it. I was sociable with everyone and took pride in my appearance.

I have been dealing with depression for a significant portion of my life. Despite being on and off medications, the symptoms keep resurfacing. I discussed this with my family doctor, who attempted different medications, but the relief was only temporary. Eventually, my doctor prescribed the maximum dosage of Wellbutrin (450mg) and 0.5mg of Klonopin. However, she also mentioned the possibility of needing a mood stabilizer, so I reached out to a psychiatry practice for further clarification.

I'm a 13-year-old who is feeling overwhelmed by my mom's excessive drinking and my father's concerns about our family's well-being. My mom drinks alcohol constantly and neglects her health by not eating properly. My dad is worried about all of us, but I'm particularly concerned about my siblings. My mom's drinking has caused tension between my parents, and my dad often relies on me to take care of everyone. I've been shouldering this responsibility since I was 8 years old and it's starting to weigh on me. I've even had thoughts of running away or worse, but I don't want my siblings to go through what I've been experiencing. I want to intervene and help my mom stop drinking so that we can have a better life. What do you think I should do?

Hello, I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for two and a half years. Lately, we've been experiencing some challenges that have made me question his commitment to saving our relationship. I've created a list of the specific problems we're facing to make it easier to discuss and address them.

Lately, I've been feeling more sad than happy. I often feel like I'm not good enough for anyone, and when I try to express these feelings to my family or friends, they dismiss me and tell me to just get over it. It's frustrating because they don't understand that I'm not trying to play the victim, I'm genuinely struggling. Sometimes, I retreat to my room and regret even attempting to open up to them. It's difficult to communicate with my family, and talking to others is challenging too because they either don't understand and get angry, or I end up overreacting and breaking down in tears, finding it hard to breathe. I often cry myself to sleep and lately, I've been having trouble sleeping. I wake up multiple times throughout the night to use the bathroom, and my family members who have shared a room with me have noticed that I toss and turn in bed and grind my teeth frequently.

I'm a 19-year-old named Anne. I have a therapist, psychologist, and support from my family, but I'm struggling with some things that I don't feel comfortable sharing with them. I find myself talking to myself as if I'm a different person, using a guy's name and identifying as gay. Lately, I've been having disturbing thoughts about harming others, using knives or chainsaws. I also have fantasies about younger boys, even though I know it's illegal. I've started hearing and seeing things. I'm on Xanax and Abilify, but I haven't been taking my Abilify as prescribed. I've even started writing a song about a disturbing scenario. I feel like I'm spiraling and I don't know what to do.

Recently, I met someone at work who was charismatic and charming, and we became friends. However, I started to notice some concerning behavior from this person. After reading an article about psychopaths and doing some research, I realized that many of the traits described in the article matched this person. I have since cut them out of my life, but I'm wondering if I should still be concerned about my safety. There were instances where I felt afraid of them and sensed their frustration and anger, particularly when I refused to engage in a sexual relationship. Can you help me determine if I have taken enough precautions to ensure my safety?

My marriage only lasted for 9 months, even though our relationship had been going on for 8 years. It was not a healthy relationship, as my partner was unfaithful and would dismiss my concerns whenever I tried to address the issue. He even admitted to cheating on me when he proposed, which was after we had already been together for 6-7 years. Despite all of this, I found it difficult to end the relationship. I don't understand why.

I have been experiencing extreme anger attacks, particularly towards my boyfriend. I find that I get easily annoyed by even the slightest things, such as looks, facial expressions, and certain behaviors. I have a perfectionist nature and expect people to be considerate and conscious. Although I don't lose control completely, I do feel extremely irritated by unfair and unjust behaviors, especially from my boyfriend. I feel like I don't have to keep my guard up with him, as we are very close and I consider him my soul mate. However, his behavior triggers such extreme anger in me that it scares me. For example, when he recently went abroad and didn't inform me as promised, I felt panicked and sent a message to his sister to check on him. It turned out he was just sleeping and hadn't contacted me due to coverage issues. I was extremely angry at his lack of care for my feelings. In fact, I even had thoughts of wanting to harm him. This scares me and makes me feel bad about myself. I'm afraid that he won't change his behavior. What should I do?

Throughout my life, I've noticed that my relationship with my mother has always been somewhat perplexing. Unlike other mothers and daughters, we never had the same level of comfort and affection. She rarely expresses her emotions and has never said "I love you" to me, except when my father forces her to say it to him. I've observed how other mothers and daughters interact, joking around and hugging, and it highlights the stark difference in our relationship. I rarely receive emotional support or wise guidance from her. It's been challenging for me to understand why she is this way.

Lately, I've noticed that I become short-tempered, testy, and even angry when my girlfriend questions me. I recognize that I'm not always right, but I seem to have this need to defend myself. I want to change this behavior because I don't want it to negatively impact my relationship. I've realized that this pattern occurs most frequently with my girlfriend, although it has happened with others too. I am typically an organized, tidy person and have a tendency to be a perfectionist. Can you help me understand why I react this way?

I have been feeling overwhelmed and concerned about my family situation lately. My parents are both in their mid-eighties and my brother, who is 51 years old, has schizoaffective disorder and is living with them. The stress on my parents is becoming incredibly difficult for them to handle. I've suggested the idea of a group home for my brother, but my mother refuses. She strongly believes that as family, it is our responsibility to take care of him.

Over the past three years, since I was 16, I've been experiencing symptoms that make me believe I may have a psychological disorder. I haven't sought help from a specialist because I don't think I can explain it to my parents. However, now I'm considering seeing one just to confirm my suspicions. I wanted to get your opinion on this matter.

When I first met my boyfriend three years ago, he was outgoing and relaxed, just like me. However, after we moved in together, I noticed that he became more reserved and quiet when we were at home. It was as if he was constantly distracted and I had to wave my hand in front of him to bring him back to reality. I later learned that he had made some major changes in his work life, including leaving a stable job to start his own business, which unfortunately failed and took a toll on his self-esteem. Since then, he has become distant, stopped showing affection, and has even pushed me away. I understood that he was upset about his career, so I let it go for a while. However, he recently found a great new job and things haven't improved.

I'm really struggling right now and I'm not sure what's going on with me. I feel like it's more than just depression. I'm having a hard time coping with everyday life. I'm a single mom living with my parents because my boyfriend ended our relationship when I was five months pregnant. My son is now 18 months old.

Lately, I've been noticing that I feel a surge of anger whenever my best friend interacts with this other girl at school. It's been happening consistently for about 8 weeks now, and it doesn't seem to be getting any better.

Hello, my name is Jessica. I'm a 24-year-old transgender woman from San Diego. I've come here today because I've been feeling incredibly lonely and I need to talk about the thoughts that have been building up inside me. Growing up, I never had a stable family. My parents fought for custody over me for years, and my biological mother was physically abusive. I also faced challenges because of my gender identity, which only added to the tension at home. Things got worse as I got older - my mother stabbed me when I was 17 and my father would physically assault me for expressing my true self. Eventually, I left home and joined the military, hoping to find a sense of belonging and maybe even "cure" my femininity. But all it did was make me feel even more disconnected from myself. After I was discharged, I tried to suppress my identity as a trans woman, but that only made me feel like I was denying my true self. It was a mistake to prioritize others' expectations over my own well-being.

I have been in a relationship with my partner for four years, and we have been engaged for two. I genuinely love him and believe that he loves me too. However, I have noticed a pattern where he constantly questions me and doubts my trustworthiness. Although he claims to trust me, he often makes subtle comments about my activities and the people I spend time with. It's important to note that I have recently moved 300 miles away from my hometown to live with him, and as a result, I only have two close friends. Despite having a busy job in a bustling office, he often becomes paranoid and insecure.

Patient: I've been diagnosed with bipolar disorder and I'm currently married but separated. My ultimate goal is to reunite with my family. Right now, my 5-year-old stepson, my wife, and I are all receiving therapy, but we each see separate therapists.

I have a 15-year-old brother who often asks me to sleep in his room because he claims to be scared of the dark. Recently, I've noticed some uncomfortable incidents where he tried to touch me inappropriately while we were both in bed. I've always had a feeling that he might be gay, which doesn't bother me, but I'm confused and concerned about his behavior. What does this mean?

My husband and I recently got married after living together for two years in his home country. I am originally from Latin America, while he is from Europe. Six months ago, he started a new job where the majority of his colleagues are women. Over the past two months, he has developed close relationships with three of his female coworkers and they often go out for drinks after work. I'm finding it difficult to accept this situation.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for five years, since I was 21 years old. We have a good relationship and love each other, but I am worried about our future. Two years ago, I asked him about our future and he said he wasn't thinking about marriage yet. We agreed to talk about it later, but he never brought it up again. I recently expressed my concerns about our age and the difficulty of ending our friendship, but he only acknowledged my concerns without saying anything further. I feel angry and concerned, and someone even told me that he may not see a future with me. I love him, but I can't be undecided anymore. I need help in deciding what to do while maintaining my self-esteem. Thank you.

The other morning, I woke up and took a shower, the next thing I remember is that I was driving on a busy highway approximately 60 miles from home, I immediately turned around and headed back. I have no recollection of why I left my house, I didn't have my cell phone, purse, anything. The key I had to my vehicle was a spare key, not the usual one that I use on a keychain. I stopped at my daughter's house (halfway between where I was when I "came to" and my house) panicked, scared, this has never happened.

Lately, I've been experiencing difficulties with my speech. I often mix up words and end up saying gibberish. This has been noticed by others. In addition, when I write, I tend to miss out on letters and punctuation, even when writing my own name. I also have a constant inner voice that talks to me. Most of the time, we get along, but sometimes it can be really harsh, like the other day during an argument with my boyfriend. It caused me to have a panic attack, although I can't recall the specifics very well now.

I'm an 18-year-old who is currently in a relationship with this guy. At first, things seemed great and I enjoyed spending time with him. However, lately, I've been feeling unsure about whether or not I should end the relationship. It's not turning out to be what I had imagined it to be.

I've been through a lot in my life, starting from a young age. I've experienced physical and emotional abuse, my parents went through a difficult divorce, and I've been betrayed by people I trusted. I've also endured bullying at school and work, and I've struggled with self-harm and attempted suicide. These experiences have really impacted me, and I've been trying to cope on my own, but it's been challenging. I've tried to self-diagnose using the internet, and my symptoms seem to align with conditions like Asperger's or different types of schizophrenia. These symptoms have been present since I was about ten years old, and they make it difficult for me to function in everyday life. No matter how hard I try, I can't seem to change myself.

Patient's statement (rewritten): I made a mistake by sneaking my boyfriend over while my mom was at work and we ended up having sex. I confided in my best friend about it, but her mom found out when she went through her phone. Recently, my mom had a conversation with my friend's mom and it seemed like she suspected something, but I denied it out of fear. I know I need to tell my mom before my friend's mom does, but I'm scared of her reaction and I don't know how to approach the conversation. I've been feeling really anxious about this and it's consuming my thoughts. I need help addressing this as soon as possible.

Recently, my mother had a concerning conversation with my 17-year-old brother. He has been expressing thoughts of jumping off a building, which understandably worried my mother. She tried to talk to him and it seemed to make him feel a little better. However, I'm also concerned because he has recently shared disturbing thoughts about harming our mother, including graphic daydreams of violent acts. This is alarming and I strongly believe that he needs professional help. We are now afraid to have him babysit my 8-year-old sister after he grabbed her and yelled at her.

I've been feeling really down lately and I can't seem to shake this feeling of unhappiness. I'm a 38-year-old man and it's almost like I enjoy being sad. I have some challenges in my life that contribute to my unhappiness, but I can't help but wonder if there's something deeper going on.

I'm considering returning to the UK to get treatment. Growing up, I had a difficult childhood marked by abusive behavior from my alcoholic father, who also physically harmed my mother and brother. Both of my parents struggled with suicidal thoughts, and as a teenager, I engaged in destructive behaviors such as binge drinking, drug use, self-harm, and disordered eating.

I'm really worried about my younger brother who is 17 years old. It seems like he has two different sides to him. In public, he appears to be well-spoken and calm, but at home, he becomes irritable and hostile for no reason. His eating and sleep patterns are also disturbed. Sometimes he feels really down and lacks motivation, especially when it comes to his writing. Other times, he's in a really energetic and talkative mood, but it's accompanied by inappropriate behavior and poor concentration.

Counselor: Thank you for sharing your thoughts and feelings with me. It sounds like you have always been more comfortable keeping your social interactions limited to your classmates and maintaining a certain level of privacy. You mentioned that you do not feel the need for physical touch beyond what is necessary with your family members. It's important to remember that everyone has different preferences and comfort levels when it comes to physical contact.

Patient: So, I'm currently in my fourth year of studying psychology and I'm set to graduate with my bachelor's degree in the spring. My ultimate goal is to go to grad school and become a clinical psychologist. However, I could really use some guidance with my current situation.

Over the years, I've noticed significant changes in my parents' behavior. When I was born, my mom started displaying unusual behavior, such as moodiness, depression, and an intense focus on religion. She seemed to interpret every life event through a religious lens. Growing up, she didn't prioritize hygiene for either of us, and our living conditions were quite messy. Recently, she lost her job and believes it was part of a conspiracy against her. She has also developed a fascination with conspiracy theories, ranging from government-controlled tornadoes to harmful substances in vaccines. I'm concerned that her condition may worsen over time.

Hi, I'm a 13-year-old female from Switzerland, and I've been experiencing some changes in my mood that concern me. I often find myself snapping at my parents without being able to control it, and I go from feeling happy and pleased to suddenly feeling sad. This has been going on for a while now, and I'm not sure if it's related to being a young female or if there's something more going on. Sometimes, I feel so angry and sad that I have the urge to throw things. I'm usually a happy person, but when something brings me down, I feel like I lose control. I was hoping you could give me some advice on how to manage these emotions or help me understand what might be causing this. I would really appreciate it. Thank you.

I'm feeling overwhelmed and heartbroken about my current situation. I've been in a 15-year relationship and we have 9 cats together. My partner is unhappy about the number of cats and says we can't find a place to rent with so many. I've tried finding them new homes, but no one seems interested. I even reached out to no-kill shelters, but they couldn't take them. I've even thought about the possibility of euthanizing some of them, but it breaks my heart. On top of all this, my partner keeps adding more problems to our relationship. I wish he would understand my love for the cats and help me care for them. I feel like he doesn't love me the same way I love him. After all these years, I can't believe he's considering leaving me. I'm feeling depressed and like I'm losing my sanity.

Lately, I've been experiencing frequent mood swings where I go from feeling okay to feeling extremely upset and angry. I never seem to find happiness, no matter what I'm doing. When I'm alone, I crave company, but when I'm with people, I long for solitude. I try to handle conflicts with my parents maturely, but I often find myself acting like a child, screaming, crying, and getting angry. I even resort to destructive behavior like punching holes in walls, despite being a small girl. As I prepare to go off to college, I still feel like a failure in my parents' eyes. It seems like everything I do is wrong, even though I try to meet their expectations. I have moments when I feel content with my life, but then the next week, I'm overwhelmed with hatred towards everyone and everything, and I find myself constantly on the verge of tears. I'm struggling to understand and express my emotions because they are all over the place. I can't figure out why I can't find contentment in anything. For example, even when I want to be alone, I'm still unhappy. And when I finally get to be around my friends, I end up disliking them and wanting to be alone. It's not because of college or education, as I am excited to pursue a career and gain knowledge in college. I just want to know why I'm always feeling angry, sad, or just not happy. This emotional roller coaster is exhausting, and I'm desperate for answers.

Over the past year, I have experienced significant losses and have been struggling with various relationships. My 18-year-old brother, who I was very close to, passed away. During this time of grief, my childhood cats have been my main source of comfort. However, I have had strained relationships with my mother, father, stepmother, and stepsister. I have also had difficulty maintaining long-lasting friendships. I am currently on medication for depression and ADHD and working a job that I find demeaning. Due to financial constraints, I had to move in with my dad. I have been considering a teaching job abroad, but I am concerned about leaving my aging cats behind and potentially losing them before their time. This dilemma is causing me distress and I am unsure of what to do.

Growing up, my family dynamic was quite complex. On one hand, my parents showed care and affection towards me. However, there were moments of neglect and frequent conflicts, particularly with my mother displaying aggressive behavior. She would yell, kick, and throw objects, although no severe physical harm was inflicted. My father would attempt to calm her down or withdraw, never resorting to violence.

I've been dating a man for 8 months. He's 45, never been married, and doesn't have any children. I'm about to finalize my divorce in a month, and I have two young boys with my ex. My marriage has been over for years, and I've dated other people before getting into my current relationship.

I'm 15 years old and my life has been really difficult so far. My parents are separated and my dad hasn't been in my life since he got married to my cousin last summer. I've tried reaching out to him, but he hasn't responded. I blame myself for him choosing someone else's kids over his own. My mom has struggled to take care of my brother and me, and we've had to move a lot because she couldn't pay the rent. Meeting Julian, a guy I fell in love with, seemed to bring some happiness into my life, but it turns out he's been cheating on me. I'm torn between wanting to leave him and staying with him. He mentally abuses me, and it's taking a toll on my well-being. My mom called me a "failure" today, which hurt me deeply. My brother, who used to give me hope, has been distancing himself from home since he graduated. I've been engaging in self-harm, but I've managed to stop. However, I'm feeling hopeless and don't want to live anymore.

I've been experiencing ongoing feelings of sadness, restlessness, mood swings, stress, difficulty concentrating, and violent tendencies for about 7 years now. I'm not sure if this is normal or if there's something wrong with me. I haven't discussed it with my parents because I'm afraid they'll dismiss it. Can you provide a professional perspective on this?

Since remarrying five years ago, I have relocated to my husband's native country, where English is not the primary language. My two sons are now adults and have established their own lives in my native country, which I visit every two months.

I am a 28-year-old woman who works as a produce clerk at a grocery store. Lately, I've been struggling with social anxiety at work. I feel uncomfortable speaking to my co-workers about anything other than immediate work-related tasks. It's gotten to the point where I work myself to exhaustion just to avoid conversation. My co-workers think I'm overly obsessed with my job and make jokes about me behind my back. It's impacting my life and I'm considering quitting, but I worry the same problem will arise in a new job.

I recently discovered that my partner has been engaging in a close and intimate conversation with another woman he met through a game. They have been messaging each other for hours, late into the night, and even discussing the possibility of meeting in person. I feel devastated and betrayed by this emotional affair. I confronted him about it, but he insists that they are just friends and that I am overreacting. I have told him to stop talking to her. Am I right in doing so?

I recently started a relationship with someone I met on Facebook. We hit it off right away and felt a strong connection when we finally met in person. We've been dating for a few weeks now and things have been going really well.

I have been married for 23 years. My husband used to be more affectionate but it has waned over the years. It is however, not completely gone. He will hold me at night as he falls asleep, kiss me upon arriving home and we are still regularly physically intimate. Although I’ve had to guide him throughout the years, he is supportive and kind despite being a bit distant and unexcitable. I know that most women would be fairly happy with this situation but for some reason, I have moments where I feel he could be more affectionate and romantically focused. He is an excellent provider and we have a beautiful home, nice kids and a blessed life. What on earth is my problem then?

I have a close friend who lives in New Zealand while I live in California. Since we first met, there has always been a mutual attraction between us. Whenever I traveled to New Zealand for work, we would spend a lot of time together and sometimes become intimate, but we always maintained that we were just friends. We both knew deep down that there was something more, but we never acknowledged it because of the distance and our young age.

I've been feeling really frustrated with my doctor lately. I've been experiencing a lot of symptoms that are affecting my daily life. I feel depressed most of the time and my mood is consistently low. Sometimes, I have bursts of energy that make me feel like I have too much adrenaline in my body. It's strange, because when I look in the mirror, I often dislike what I see, but other times, I feel surprisingly confident. I've been experiencing extreme fluctuations in my energy levels, either feeling very fatigued or overly energetic. I also struggle with rapid speech and frequently lose my train of thought in the middle of a sentence or discussion. Additionally, I've been dealing with constant itchiness all over my body.

I'm 12 years old, almost 13, and I've been experiencing some troubling situations with my dad. It seems like he wants me to have the same difficult upbringing he had. I can recall several instances where he became really angry with me, but the earliest memory I have is when I was 7 years old. He was picking me up from girl scouts and I mentioned that I wanted my mom to pick me up instead. This made him extremely mad, and he started throwing things at me - anything he could get his hands on, whether it was heavy or light. When we got home, I ran inside and was crying as I tried to take off my coat and shoes. That's when he came in and kicked me down, right in front of my mom. This incident seemed to be the starting point. Just two days ago, I was sitting in the back seat of the car when he exploded in anger. He yelled at me, saying he wished he never had me, among other hurtful things.

I am a 17-year-old Muslim girl who is currently facing significant challenges within my family. My parents strongly disapprove of my relationship with a non-Muslim guy who happens to be Catholic. However, we deeply love each other and have plans for the future, including him asking my dad for my hand in marriage. My parents have confiscated my phone and restricted my access to social media, and my dad has even discovered information about my boyfriend. Despite all of this, I am determined to stay with him because I believe in our love. I am only able to contact him through the landline, but even that has caused major conflicts with my parents. It hurts me deeply because I don't have the courage to break up with someone who loves me so much. He is understanding, supportive, and treats me well, and I cannot imagine my life without him.

Growing up in a divorced home was challenging for me. My parents often spoke negatively about each other, even discussing inappropriate topics like infidelity. As an only child, I had to shuttle between their houses multiple times a year. Although my parents never physically abused me, my mother would sometimes discipline me with a hit to the head if I was disrespectful. They both had a tendency to be harsh and bordering on verbally abusive, although it never reached a level that would require intervention from Child Protective Services.

I am eighteen years old and have been struggling with depression for the past five years. Recently, I developed a fear of going to school during my sophomore year of high school. Despite having friends and manageable classes, I would wake up in the mornings crying and experiencing panic attacks. I would often black out and wake up later in the day. This caused my depression to worsen and I ended up isolating myself from my friends for a few months. I'm not sure what could have caused these fears or what I was experiencing.

I've been in an on and off relationship with my boyfriend for over two years. We constantly fight, sometimes going without talking for months. We rarely go on dates and most of our fights happen through text messages. He doesn't take me seriously, verbally attacks me, and belittles me. He speaks poorly about my family and friends, and I feel insecure and abused by him. I'm unhappy more often than I'm happy with him, but I keep going back because I feel alone. He got me pregnant and when I had to make the difficult decision to end the pregnancy due to health reasons, he criticized how I handled it. He speaks horribly about women and it's confusing why he stays in a relationship if he hates them so much. I need help.

I've noticed that I prefer to be alone and I'm struggling with feeling like I should be a "normal girl" who enjoys being around others. When I'm alone, I feel a sense of relief and don't want to make an effort to go out. Even just writing about being around people makes me anxious. I feel calmer and better when I'm at home alone or when my parents aren't around. I know that as a high school student, I should want to go out with friends, but I often make excuses to be alone. My family knows that I don't like being around people, but they don't fully understand how much it affects me. Just the thought of being around others makes me feel trapped and anxious, like someone is choking me. While I may come across as friendly and outgoing, I struggle to truly trust others and always fear getting hurt. I also experienced inappropriate touching by a family member when I was younger, but when I told my mother, she brushed it off. I'm not sure if she doesn't believe me or if there's something she doesn't want to talk about. I genuinely enjoy being alone and not having to worry about anyone or anything. Whenever I have to be around people, my heart races and I feel jumpy. Can you help me understand how to feel more "normal"?

Patient: I'm really worried about my mom. She has schizophrenia and she refuses to take her medication. She often hears voices and has conversations with them. Lately, she's been getting into car accidents frequently and has pushed away many of her friends. Years ago, after she was first hospitalized and released, I was asked to attend outpatient therapy sessions with her. During those sessions, she would talk about the things her voices told her to do, and it was really scary because they often involved harming her grandchildren who were very young at the time. Now, her condition seems to have worsened even more, and she has great-grandchildren who are very small. She currently lives with my brother because she can no longer live on her own. We're all really concerned about her behavior and the anger she sometimes displays. Can her illness potentially harm others? My mom used to be such a gentle person, but now it's hard to see any trace of that person in her.
