I have been married to my husband for 12 years and we have four children. Our oldest child is nine years old and our youngest is just nine months old. Lately, my husband and I have been experiencing ongoing difficulties in our relationship.

I'm a 16-year-old teenager living with my mom and sister. Unfortunately, my dad passed away four years ago, and he was an alcoholic. Lately, I've been feeling increasingly worried about everything. I have a passion for drawing and want to pursue a career in tattooing, but my mother disapproves. She puts a lot of pressure on me to focus on school, and she can be very strict and overbearing. Sometimes I feel like she doesn't trust me and constantly reminds me of the sacrifices she's made for me. It's making it hard for me to be myself.

I've been struggling with depression for quite some time now, but I haven't sought therapy yet. My past experiences with psychologists have been negative, particularly when I was 16 and dealing with what I think was anorexia. It wasn't severe, but I did restrict my calorie intake to be thin. When my parents found out, they immediately sent me to a psychologist and wanted me to go to a clinic. The idea of leaving home for a year was overwhelming, and I even contemplated suicide. As a result, I'm extremely apprehensive about seeing another psychologist.

I've been living a seemingly normal life, going to school and everything. But there's something that's been troubling me for a while now. I have this imaginary world where I am someone else named Ashley. In that world, Ashley is a successful superstar with the perfect life. I'm turning 17 soon, and in Ashley's world, she'll be turning 19. It's gotten to the point where certain events in my life have corresponding events in Ashley's life. I also struggle with maintaining relationships, as it feels like I'm betraying both the person I'm with and Ashley. I even have conversations in my head with people who aren't actually there. I feel trapped and it's causing me to feel depressed. Can you please help me?

When I was a child, my father was emotionally abusive towards me. He would constantly insult me and make me feel inadequate, especially when we were doing homework together. I remember crying almost every day because I couldn't meet his expectations. He would mock me when I made mistakes and would often scream at me. It felt like he didn't value my opinions or autonomy, as he would tell me that I was only there to obey. I'm not sure what my mother's role was during this time, as I have very few memories of her being present. She has mentioned that she was afraid of my father, but I cannot recall her specific actions or words from that period.

When I was in fifth grade, there was this boy whom I usually picked fights with. I never understood why, but he always seemed to annoy me for no reason. I would intentionally start arguments with him. After fifth grade, my family and I moved away from that town, and I haven't seen him since. However, when I was in eighth grade, I started having dreams about him and realized that I am in love with him. I assumed it was just a crush because he was the complete opposite of me. Unfortunately, these feelings haven't faded over time. I find myself obsessing over him, constantly checking his social media accounts and fantasizing about him. I've never been in a relationship because I can't seem to let go of these feelings. I've never been attracted to any other men besides him. I've tried everything to get rid of these feelings, but nothing has worked. Lately, I've started to hate his female friends for being close to him, and I can't sleep because I'm constantly thinking about him. I even have thoughts of harming his friends because I want him all to myself. I know he probably doesn't even remember me, but I still include him in my plans and fantasies. I've even had thoughts of harming him so that no one else can have him. I don't want to be a stalker. What should I do?

I've had a really difficult upbringing, with both of my parents being drug addicts before I was born. They managed to quit drugs when they found out my mom was pregnant, but my dad continued to struggle with alcoholism and became physically violent towards my mom and later my grandparents. I've also faced bullying throughout middle school and high school. At home, my dad constantly belittles me and makes me feel worthless. I've even had thoughts of suicide, but I'm hopeful that things will get better once I can leave this toxic environment. However, I've also had thoughts of harming my dad. I'm starting to question if these thoughts mean I'm insane. I can't seek help from a psychologist in person since my dad disapproves of it.

Lately, I've been struggling with negative self-talk. There's a constant voice in my mind that puts me down whenever I make a mistake, like forgetting a word in my speech. It tells me that I'm stupid, ugly, and worthless. It even goes as far as saying that no guy will ever love or want me. It's really affecting my self-esteem and overall well-being.

I have been married to my wife for 24 years. She is 51 years old and has a diagnosis of Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD). Over the past 4-5 years, her behavior has followed a consistent pattern. In the mornings, she seems loving towards me, but by early afternoon, she becomes agitated, accuses me of not loving her, and engages in verbally abusive rages. This has become a nightly occurrence. I am considering separating from her, along with our two teenage sons, but I want to communicate my concerns to her through a letter. It is not possible for me to have a calm conversation with her as she tends to yell and scream. I am thinking of giving her an ultimatum to either take medication to control her emotions or consider leaving the relationship. However, I am unsure of how to best word this letter. I am feeling desperate and in need of guidance.

I've been feeling really lost and unmotivated lately. It all started in my last year of high school when I didn't put in enough effort because I wasn't sure what I wanted to do after graduation. Now I'm in college, but I failed all my classes because I didn't try. I'm currently on probation and I just don't have a clear goal or purpose for what I'm studying. It's like I'm lacking motivation.

I recently started seeing someone and I've noticed some patterns of behavior that concern me. I've done some research and I think he might have a personality disorder like Pathological Lying or Pseudologia Fantastica. I'm also wondering if Facitious Disorder could be a possibility. He's 27 years old.

Hi, I hope you're doing well. I've been diagnosed with bipolar disorder and have generally managed it quite effectively. However, during my recent session with my psychologist, they suggested that I reach out and talk to others about my experiences with depression. It's something that's often emphasized in the media and mental health services. While I understand the benefits of opening up, I can't help but feel apprehensive. When I'm in a depressive episode, I become a different person and over the years, I've lost valuable friendships because people couldn't handle my depression. It's disheartening because everyone claims to be there for you, but I've reached out to three people in a tentative manner - just asking to meet up or have a casual conversation - and I haven't received any response. Two of them are too busy and one didn't even bother to reply. It's making it difficult for me to trust others and wonder who I can really talk to.

I have been experiencing distressing symptoms lately. I frequently hear voices in my head that give me orders and comment on my actions. I feel uncomfortable sharing this with my family, particularly my mom, as I worry she might not understand. I have been described as emotionally distant and secretive, even to my closest friends. I tend to keep my distress internalized and rarely share it with others. I also have a constant fear of getting hurt, hurting others, or being victimized. This fear often prevents me from fully engaging in activities and I struggle with maintaining focus. I also have violent thoughts and can sometimes exhibit violent behavior. I feel anxious about disclosing this to my parents and have been hiding it from them. Additionally, I frequently experience muscle tension and what feels like involuntary spasms. I am hesitant to open up about myself because I fear that someone may use what I share against me. I feel scared even writing this.

I've been questioning whether or not I should seek therapy. It seems like my main issue is that I have a tendency to seek attention and compulsively lie. This has been a pattern since my childhood, where I would exaggerate my abilities in sports or school. However, now it feels like lying has become a habit, even when I don't want to. I find myself fabricating emotions, thoughts, and even simple details like what I had for breakfast. It's become clear to me that I've also developed attention-seeking behaviors.

I'm really struggling with my mom. She refuses to acknowledge any issues and I feel lost on how to help her. Throughout my childhood, she was excessively protective, even asking me what Santa Claus brought me when I was 25. It was suffocating. She had these explosive tantrums in stores and her current husband says she still has them at 60 years old. She would make comments about my future, focusing on materialistic things like shopping and finding a man who could support that lifestyle. It was hard for me because I was more concerned about our basic needs. She spent so much money and time at malls, constantly moving us around. I was only able to have some stability because my father, who was emotionally absent, financially supported me.

Lately, I've been feeling really confused and I'm not sure what's going on with my brain. It's been difficult for me to talk to anyone about it. Just last week, I went to my friend's house and I found myself unable to engage in conversation or keep it going. My friend suggested that I need to open up more and push myself out of my comfort zone.

I am 24 years old and have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for over a year. He is 9 years older than me and has two children, a 9-year-old daughter and a 10-year-old son. Recently, his ex-partner left town, leaving us with the responsibility of raising his two kids permanently. This is all new to me, as I went from being a mom with three years of experience to suddenly having a 3, 9, and 10-year-old. His daughter has started talking to me disrespectfully and when I try to discipline her by sending her to her room, she reacts by kicking, screaming, and moaning for hours. She even tells her dad that she hates him for being with me, despite most days being completely fine and even loving me. His 10-year-old son, on the other hand, seems to have jealous issues towards my 3-year-old son. He acts mean towards him, taking away toys, food, books, and anything that will make him cry. He has admitted that his problem with my son is that he still has his mom in his life.

I'm a student in a mid-high school. My grades are average, not great but not terrible either. However, I've been dealing with bullying and harassment since I was a 7-year-old girl. It's confusing because I don't understand why this happens to me. On top of that, the people I thought were my friends often use me.

Lately, I've been experiencing changes in my sleep patterns. I find that I rarely have dreams, and when I do, they're difficult to remember. I often see darkness when I close my eyes at night, and it feels like only a few seconds have passed, but when I check the clock, I've actually slept for hours. This didn't used to be a problem when I was younger, and it seems like the older I get, the fewer dreams I have. I also used to have daydreams frequently, but those are fading away too. It takes me a long time to fall asleep, and I sometimes spend hours lying in bed trying to sleep. I've asked my mother for advice, but she simply tells me to turn on my side and go to sleep. I'm unsure of what all of this means. My friends think I'm fine and just need more sleep. On weekdays, I typically sleep for about 4-8 hours. I could really use some guidance on how to manage this.

Hello, I'm a 15-year-old who has been homeschooled all my life. I've never had any friends and I feel like an outcast. It's really difficult for me to see other girls my age having fun with their friends and going to parties or the beach. I don't have any friends at all. I'm really passionate about psychology, serial killer stories, horror movies, dramatic photography, and gore. I find myself crying myself to sleep and crying a lot throughout the day. Recently, I've had a breakdown and I feel like I need alcohol just to feel okay.

My 17-year-old son has been experiencing visual and auditory hallucinations for the past two years. These hallucinations started off as minor, like seeing things out of the corner of his eye, but they have become more vivid and disturbing over time. He denies experiencing any other symptoms related to depression, bipolar disorder, anxiety, or schizophrenia. He is not on any medication and has been screened for drug use, which came back negative. He recently confided in me about the hallucinations, stating that he has been keeping them to himself but they have started to wear on him. He also mentioned having trouble sleeping for the past couple of months. I'm concerned as his mother and I can't understand how this has been going on for so long without any other signs or symptoms. We have an appointment with a psychologist next week. Can vivid hallucinations and multiple voices in his head occur without any other symptoms?

During my high school years, I experienced a persistent feeling of sadness that affected me on a daily basis. To address this, my doctor prescribed medication and I started seeing a therapist once a month. However, I didn't notice any improvement with the medication and eventually stopped taking it. While therapy continued, I felt like I was being rushed and that I was wasting my therapist's time, as if there were others who needed it more than I did. Opening up became increasingly difficult for me, which eventually led to frustration and my decision to stop going to therapy.

I've been struggling with a secret friendship that is causing a lot of distress for me. I feel like I can't talk to anyone close to me about it because I'm worried they will judge me. I'm in a healthy and happy relationship with a great guy who I deeply love. He accepts me for who I am and I've never felt more secure in my life. But this secret friendship is constantly interfering with my happiness.

I'm a 20-year-old woman who is currently 7 months pregnant. I started dating a guy when I was 19, whom I met during a party phase. We fell in love and when I got pregnant, he promised to leave his unhealthy habits behind to support our new family. Unfortunately, after about 6 months, he has started drinking and using cocaine again. I used to engage in the same lifestyle before I became pregnant, but now I'm determined to make positive changes for the sake of my baby.

I've been through a lot of trauma in my life, including experiencing sexual assault and abuse, growing up with an alcoholic and absent mother, and losing my father to a sudden medical emergency. I struggle with feelings of rejection, paranoia, anger, and depression. I have difficulty forming and maintaining friendships, and often feel insecure and upset when someone doesn't respond to me as I expect. Can you help me understand what might be going on?

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for over four years now, but it hasn't been easy. Initially, the first three months were great, but things took a turn for the worse. He occasionally becomes physically abusive, hitting me about once every two months. However, what hurts me even more is the constant verbal abuse he subjects me to. He calls me names like stupid, bitch, idiot, and fat on a daily basis. He insists that I'm too sensitive and that I somehow provoke him to treat me this way. It feels like everything I say or do angers him, and whenever I try to address the issue, he deflects and accuses me of changing the subject.

I am a 16-year-old only child living with divorced parents who constantly argue and blame me for their conflicts. Lately, my father has been absent, and my mother and I constantly fight. About two months ago, I got sick with the flu, but my mother didn't believe me and forcefully tried to get me out of bed. She ended up slapping me and I got injured by shattered glass. My parents then had a family conference where they berated and belittled me. I also have major anxiety and fear for my safety at home, as my mother exhibits concerning behavior. I feel scared and don't know what to do anymore.

Patient: It seems like I come across as a typical man to many people. I've always excelled in sports and school, giving off the impression that I'm fun and easygoing. However, deep down, my emotions feel sensitive and misunderstood. I've always had a tendency to feel angry and somewhat manic. To maintain my public image, I've become skilled at suppressing these volatile emotions.

I am here because I’m losing hope and I’m running out of options. I’m here because I have many reasons to believe my mother is a paranoid schizophrenic. She is a single 56-year-old woman with 4 children. Three boys and me, the youngest and only daughter. I have a very bad relationship with my mother because she lacks trust with me and she always thinks I’m out to get her. For example, I don’t live with her and I barely go visit her, but for some reason, she constantly accuses me of stealing her things from her home. I don’t have a key to her home so there’s no way I can get in her home if she’s not there, and when I am over there visiting she follows me around the house. One time she left a very belligerent vulgar message on my answering machine accusing me of stealing her credit card and paying my cellphone bill. She then called me apologizing saying it was a misunderstanding. I was completely in awe. Then another time she cursed me out saying once again I stole her credit card and went to Wal Mart and tried to buy some contacts. Mind you, I don’t wear contacts or glasses. I don’t have access to her card info or any of her personal information. I’m not the only person she accuses of stealing from her, she will say things like “someone’s been coming in my house and stealing my DVDs.” One time she even said “someone” has been driving her car. My brother and I told her that's ridiculous, and no one is gonna steal her car and then return it. There is another time she called me and she was very upset. She told me she went to her friend of 20+ years house and saw a picture hanging on her wall that belonged to my mom. My mom said her friend was recently at her house and she believes she stole the picture from her house. She called her friend accusing her and telling her she’s no longer welcomed in her home anymore and that their friendship is over. I told my mom she sounds crazy and there is no way her friend could’ve taken the picture without her noticing, seeing how the picture is about 32 inches long and wide. I told her to check her hallway closet and she found it. I told her she needs to call her friend and apologize and she needs to seek help. Whenever my brothers or I tell her she needs help she yells at us and won’t speak to us. Another thing I notice about my mom is the way she speaks. She sometimes reminds me of a child, especially the way she puts her sentences together, they sometimes don’t make sense. She misreads words all the time and also speaks words wrong a lot. If this is any helpful information she worked at a mental institution for over 15 years. She often brought her problems at work home with her and would take her anger out on me and my brother. She spends a lot of time by herself and pushes away a lot of her friends. She has been single for about 10 years. Another thing my brothers and I notice about her is that she often fabricates stories or she seriously over exaggerates them. She believes her lies, I think. One thing I don’t understand is how she treats my brothers like royalty but treats me as an untrustworthy criminal that’s out to get her. The way she is to me makes me not like my mother or want anything to do with her. I’m seriously concerned with her and I need answers.

Counselor: Thank you for sharing your experiences and concerns with me. It sounds like you've been experiencing some distressing thoughts and memories that have been causing you a lot of confusion and fear. It's important to remember that I am not a licensed mental health professional, but I can offer some insights and support.

I've been experiencing auditory hallucinations for the past three years. It started with a gentle and calm female voice calling my name repeatedly. Over time, I started hearing a more aggressive male voice as well. These voices ask me questions like "Are you okay?" or "Why did you do that?" The voices sound like they're coming from behind me, very close, almost as if they're right behind my shoulder. Sometimes I hear both voices whispering simultaneously, but I can't understand what they're saying. Whenever I try to focus on them, they suddenly stop. It's worth mentioning that I went through sexual child abuse during my childhood, which I haven't disclosed to anyone. I'm currently still living with my step-dad. I used to self-harm and experienced intense paranoia, but it has improved somewhat. I'm wondering if the voices could be related to my past trauma. I'm hesitant to seek professional help because I don't want my mom to worry or for me to be diagnosed with a mental disorder, as I believe my mental health is generally okay. Is there any way I can make the voices stop without seeing a doctor?

I've been living with a roommate for the past 7 months and I've noticed some concerning behavior from him lately. He's always been a very private person, but it seems like he may be dealing with social anxiety. Additionally, I've noticed that he vomits frequently, usually starting in the evening and continuing throughout the night. I'm worried that he may be struggling with either bulimia or alcoholism. He often binges on food and hides the junk food wrappers in his room, but I've also found bottles and noticed other signs that he may be drinking excessively. This behavior is causing a disturbance at home and it's giving me a lot of anxiety, so I'm really concerned about his well-being.

My current boyfriend and I have been dating for about 3 1/2 years and living together for about 3 years. We are in a band together and rely on this for most of our income. Since I’ve known him, he has dealt with minor depression. I believe it is due to having a hard childhood, constantly being passed around in foster families that treated him badly. He has always been able to deal with it rationally though, until the past 6 months.

I've been in a long distance relationship with my fiance for a year now. We were previously dating and engaged for four years before I ended the relationship and moved across the country. However, we got back together a year ago, but the issues from our past are resurfacing. We argue, sometimes quite intensely, especially when it comes to how I spend my free time. This was a problem in the past as well. Over the past year, I've become somewhat of a hermit, but at my fiance's urging, I've been trying to make friends and engage in activities. Recently, I mentioned to a female co-worker that I love cooking and she mentioned that she occasionally hosts dinner parties. I expressed my interest in attending one of her dinner parties.

Lately, I've been noticing some concerning behavior from my wife that makes me believe she may be experiencing symptoms of bipolar disorder. Whenever I ask her about herself, her parents, or her upbringing, she becomes extremely angry and has fits of rage. Additionally, she constantly belittles me and speaks negatively about my family in front of our children.

Good afternoon, I am a 21-year-old college student from a strict Hispanic family. I am the youngest of three siblings. My mother had two children before she met my dad, and then I came along. My older sister still lives with us, while my brother recently got married. I just started my first year in college and I'm doing well academically. However, I feel like my family still exerts a lot of control over me. Whenever I go out, they expect me to call them and provide details about my whereabouts, the people I'm with, and when I'll be back.

My boyfriend and I have a history of heavy drinking, partying, and infidelity. We've been together for 14 months without any breakups, but there have been some fights. I've caught him lying twice, once while he was drunk texting another girl and another time when I saw a picture of him at a bar after he said he was going to bed. He's been teasing me with the idea of an engagement for the past 6 months, which is becoming frustrating because I feel like his commitment would help with my own issues. We spend a lot of time together, but still live apart and have two dogs together. He wants to move out in the Spring of 2014, but I can't get past the past. Whenever he mentions going camping alone or spending time with another girl, I cry and feel like he's doing it to hurt me. I want to trust him, but it's difficult because of everything I've gone through with him. It's taking a toll on my mental and physical health and all I want is to be happy and believe that he truly wants to be with me forever, but his comments and actions make it hard for me to believe him.

Patient: I’m 16 and I’m feeling really lost. Lately, I've been experiencing a lot of difficulties, and I suspect it might be depression. I haven't been diagnosed by a doctor, but I've done some research online and my mom, who has depression, thinks it could be the case. I used to handle stress well, but now it's becoming overwhelming. I feel like hiding from the world and cry frequently. I experience intense sadness and irritability for extended periods, even over small things. I used to pretend I was okay, but now I struggle to keep up the facade. I feel weak and pathetic because I can't find a reason to be depressed, but it's taking a toll on me. I'm struggling academically and socially. I've self-harmed a few times and thoughts of death are constantly present. I need help, but I don't know where to start.

Hi, I’m sixteen years old and a male. I’ve been diagnosed with major depressive disorder and generalized anxiety disorder since the age of 13. I have been engaging in self-destructive behaviors such as drug and alcohol use, self-harm, and thoughts of suicide. I have low self-esteem, poor self-care habits, and a lack of motivation to do anything. I have also experienced sleep issues, which led me to switch to online high school. My mother and older brother are concerned about me, but my relationship with my mother has been strained due to her inconsistent parenting and harsh punishments. While I don't have immediate plans for suicide, I find myself drawn to the thought. Can you help me?

I was diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia and depression, and I am currently taking medications. However, I am seeking help to address my unusual behaviors and emotional hypersensitivity. I find comfort in being requested to attend counseling or therapy sessions, as well as medical check-ups. I also have a habit of cracking my knuckles and joints for no apparent reason, whether in public or private. I easily experience anxiety or excitement, and sometimes indulge in self-pity, finding solace in it. Additionally, I tend to cry when I am alone after receiving criticism. Does this loneliness indicate a need for more emotional attachment, possibly through seeking marriage? I would appreciate your input and advice. Thank you.

I know some people may not understand, but my girlfriend and I are in a serious relationship and we have a lot of fun together. We're both in high school, but we're planning to move in together after we graduate next year. The problem is that her parents are being difficult. They reacted negatively when they found out we had sex, even though we were being safe and have been together for a while. They're even threatening to make her transfer schools, which has her really scared. Her parents don't treat her well, and although my own parents aren't the greatest, I'm really worried about her. Her brother, who has already graduated, supports us as a couple, but he doesn't know about the situation with their mom. It made me so angry when her mom told her that she hates her. I know some people might dismiss our problem as just a high school relationship, but it's more than that to me. I feel a deep connection with her, and she's the only one who brings true happiness to my life. We're feeling scared and confused. I know you can't solve our problem, but I just need support and reassurance that things will get better. Thank you.

I've been feeling a sense of emptiness and disinterest lately. I used to be motivated and engaged in school, but now I find myself not caring. I've also noticed that I don't seem to feel much empathy towards others, even though I know it's hurting them. I recently experienced the loss of my grandfather, but I didn't feel much of an emotional response. I even adopted a pet hoping it would help me connect, but it feels like a chore rather than something I cherish. I don't know what's wrong with me, but I don't want to continue feeling this way.

Hello, my name is Luke. I'm currently in a challenging situation with my mother who has been diagnosed with schizophrenia. Her symptoms have been worsening, with increased antisocial behavior, throwing away items, and a loss of appetite. It's causing me a lot of stress and I feel overwhelmed. Recently, I woke up to find that she had thrown away the coffee table and removed all my belongings from the living room. I've tried to provide her with a new bed, but she refuses to sleep in it and instead sleeps on the couch for long hours without any movement. She isolates herself and refuses help from anyone. I'm only 20 years old and I find myself responsible for taking care of my mother and the household. It's impacting my personal life, as I can't have a girlfriend and my friends are met with anger from my mother. I'm not sure what to do at this point - should I move out and let her be by herself, or consider putting her back in a mental hospital?

Patient's statement (rewritten): I've always felt like I don't quite fit in with others. Apart from my immediate family, I've never really had any close friends. My love for math led me to participate in the Math Olympiad, where I met a girl who could easily socialize with everyone. Two years ago, my father was approached by the girl's father who asked if I had Asperger's syndrome, as he saw similarities between us. This prompted my father to research the condition and share the information with the rest of my family. They have since made jokes about me having Asperger's, which bothers me. I'm unsure whether they genuinely believe I have it or if they're just teasing me. I haven't discussed this with them because I'm not sure if I want to pursue a diagnosis. On one hand, it might help me feel less alone, but on the other hand, I don't want to be labeled and I don't think I would accept therapy. I'm currently seeing a psychologist for my depression and anxiety, and she also treats autism. I've been considering mentioning my concerns to her, but I don't want it to come across like I'm seeking a diagnosis. Will getting diagnosed actually help me feel better? Should I talk to my family about my concerns first?

Lately, I've been experiencing episodes of intense sadness where I become overwhelmed by self-hatred, worries, fears, and negative thoughts. I recently stumbled upon articles about the "Fear of Emotional Intimacy" and decided to take the FIS test, which yielded a score of 150. It resonated with my past and current actions and thoughts. I'm wondering how I can overcome this fear and if therapy might be necessary.

Hello! During my early twenties, I experienced three very challenging relationships that ended in rejection. The last one was particularly difficult, leading to my hospitalization due to extreme stress and loss of appetite. However, I managed to recover and move forward. Now that I am in my thirties, I have noticed a lack of compassion within myself. Friends have commented that I seem to have no heart, as I struggle to feel any emotions when someone passes away. Even when my own father was critically ill and hospitalized, I found myself feeling nothing deep down. While I don't personally feel bothered by this, the people around me are affected and believe I should seek help. Is this a serious concern?

I've been experiencing a lot of mood swings lately, and I'm not sure if it's Borderline Personality Disorder or Bipolar Disorder. Sometimes I feel extremely depressed and anxious, with thoughts of self-harm and suicide. Other times, I feel mildly happy and enthusiastic. However, these shifts in mood don't last very long. I can go from feeling happy one day to feeling sad the next. It's not stable at all. I've heard that Bipolar Disorder usually involves longer episodes, lasting from 6 months to a year, which makes me unsure. Can you help me understand what might be going on?

My 6-year-old daughter has been displaying extremely challenging behavior lately. She seems to have a negative answer for every question and throws huge tantrums at school, sometimes becoming violent when she feels slighted or reprimanded. This has resulted in her being expelled from two extracurricular activities and she's becoming isolated from her peers. I want to clarify that she has never experienced any abuse or neglect, and I have tried to be consistent in my parenting. However, it feels like she doesn't care about the consequences. I am deeply concerned for her well-being. Can you help me understand what might be going on and how I can support her?

In 2007, I was diagnosed with Bipolar II. Since then, I have faced significant challenges with my family and friends accepting my diagnosis. Many of my friends have distanced themselves from me, claiming that I am faking it for attention. Even my own mother has expressed doubts and told a family member that I could change if I wanted to. I often find myself trying to conform to societal norms and be "normal," but I struggle with excessive anxiety and talkativeness at times.

I recently attended a conference and had an unsettling encounter with a former colleague who treated me cruelly in the past. This experience has triggered memories of being a victim of mobbing at a previous job. I have been feeling extremely anxious whenever I have to attend workshops or conferences because I fear that this woman may have sabotaged my current job by talking to my colleagues. The gossiping behavior of my former boss has also damaged my reputation in my field, and now I live in constant fear that someone will recognize me and ask about my past employment. This fear has become crippling, leading to symptoms of anxiety and difficulty sleeping. I believe I may be suffering from PTSD. Can you help me find ways to manage my anxiety and overcome these fears? What steps can I take to regain confidence in myself and my abilities?

I recently had to stop seeing my therapist due to financial reasons, and since then I've been experiencing some distressing encounters with her when she isn't actually present. On two occasions, I saw her in my surroundings - once in my bathroom and another time while I was studying. I could interact with her, even feel her touch, but deep down I know she isn't really there. It's causing me a lot of emotional pain and I wish I could afford to continue therapy. I'm worried that these experiences mean I'm going crazy or becoming psychotic. What should I do? Am I crazy?

I've been feeling really overwhelmed lately. I've always struggled with social anxiety, but it seems to be getting worse. On top of that, I've been experiencing strange sensations in my brain, and it's making me scared to go outside or even attend school. Sometimes I feel like I'm being watched or that someone can read my mind, and it really freaks me out. I've also been having trouble with my thoughts and speech, like they just disappear or come out jumbled. I've been daydreaming a lot and having strange dreams, and I see figures in the dark that scare me. I also have trouble concentrating and remembering things, and I've lost motivation to do the things I used to enjoy.

Over the past winter, I experienced a period of apathy where I lost interest in things that used to be important to me. I isolated myself from friends and spent my days distracting myself with mindless activities. However, at the beginning of this year, I started to feel better. My writer's block lifted and I began to feel more connected to others. Then, in mid-February, I had a sudden breakdown of tears for no apparent reason. Since then, I've had more episodes of crying and some days I feel terrible. Additionally, I've been having trouble sleeping.

I am engaged to the man of my dreams, but we are having difficulties with his mother. She has a drug problem and frequently steals from us. Additionally, she treats my fiance's brother better, which causes tension between us. Despite my efforts to reason with her, we constantly find ourselves fighting. I am exhausted and feel like I am running out of options. How can I break this cycle and improve our relationship?

I have been dating my boyfriend for two and a half years. When we first started dating, he seemed like the perfect guy despite the fact that he is a year and a half younger than me. However, as time has passed, I've noticed certain immaturity in certain areas of our relationship that is causing issues. I'm unsure if I'm being impatient or if this is a sign that our relationship may not work out.

Over the past few months, I've been spending time with this girl. Initially, she told me that the man I saw her with was her dance partner who is much older. However, on our second outing as friends, she revealed that he is actually her boyfriend and he doesn't know about our frequent meetings. Last week, we went dancing and her boyfriend was there, but they didn't acknowledge each other. Afterwards, she pointed out who he was and mentioned that he was present. The next day, she invited me to a party to meet her friends and during the event, she was flirting with me, constantly touching me. I overheard her asking her friend's opinion about me and they expressed liking me more than her boyfriend. She even questioned what she sees in her boyfriend. One of her friends even mentioned that she seems happier when she's with me. She later messaged me to express her happiness about her friends liking me and invited me to another party.

Patient: I was in a relationship with a woman who was 20 years older than me, and it had its own set of challenges. She had a difficult upbringing in Sydney during the 70's and 80's, where she was involved with drugs and dangerous individuals. Although we loved each other and had a genuine connection, her occasional stories about her past involvement with drugs triggers a strong negative reaction in me. I find myself getting furious, even though I know she has moved on from that part of her life. I don't understand why I feel this way and why it's so difficult to control my anger.

I was diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia at the age of 15. However, I feel that the doctors at the mental hospital did not thoroughly investigate my symptoms before diagnosing me. They based it on my second admission, where I was experiencing hallucinations and hearing voices. Now, at 19 years old, my symptoms have worsened. In addition to paranoia and hallucinations, I am also having difficulty understanding things. I often misinterpret information and struggle with learning. I've also been experiencing memory problems, where I have visions of my past and question their reality. I recently learned that I've had memory issues since childhood, but they have become more severe. I also display unusual behaviors like repetitive movements and making strange sounds for no reason. I have delusions that feel very real to me, such as being watched through cameras and bugs, or believing that TV shows and music are about me. I even have delusions about being the devil's son and having telepathic powers. It's difficult for me to differentiate between reality and my delusions. I struggle to show emotions, and I've always been antisocial. After being expelled from school, I isolated myself further due to the voices urging me to harm others. Now, I find it hard to trust even my own family because of what the voices tell me. I have become skilled at hiding my disorder, but it doesn't stay dormant for long. I've tried various medications, but they only sedate me without providing relief. I'm seeking your honest opinion on what is happening to me and how it may progress. I would also appreciate any guidance on what actions I can take. Thank you.

Throughout my teenage years, I struggled with body image issues and developed unhealthy coping mechanisms. It started when I noticed stretch marks on my body at 13, which didn't bother me much back then. However, as I turned 17, I became more self-conscious and developed bulimia and anorexia. I started self-harming at 18 as a way to deal with my self-hatred. As a result, I quit studying and isolated myself from social activities. Whenever I do go out, I feel like a complete outcast, comparing myself to other girls and feeling inferior and worthless. I have convinced myself that no man will ever love me and that I don't deserve happiness.

My 8-year-old daughter, who was adopted at the age of 2, has been through four different therapists, including neurotherapy. Despite this, we haven't found anyone who has been able to accurately diagnose her or provide effective help for her specific problems. It's important to note that during the first two years of her life, she experienced severe neglect and abuse.

I have been in a committed relationship for 1.5 years with a man who loves me. We decided to move in together, and shortly after, his 18-year-old daughter also moved in with us. His other two daughters, aged 22 and 16, live with their mother in another state. Unfortunately, I have been experiencing some challenges with his daughters. They have been disrespectful, rude, and seem to ignore my presence. The 16-year-old daughter visits frequently and stays for extended periods of time. Eventually, my boyfriend and his 18-year-old daughter decided to move into their own apartment.

I have found myself in a complicated situation where I am involved with a married man. We have been friends and coworkers for two years, and recently our relationship has become more serious. He is unhappy in his marriage and wants to move out to see if our connection is genuine. While I don't want to hurt anyone, I have strong feelings for him that I've never experienced before.

Hi, I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for a few months now, and I've noticed that he has been dealing with depression. Initially, I thought it was due to the challenges he has faced, such as a near-death experience, his ill father, and his struggling mother. However, as he has opened up to me more, I've realized that his negative thoughts run deeper than just his circumstances. I find it difficult to help him, and sometimes I wonder if he's hiding his true feelings behind a facade of happiness when we're together.

Hello, my name is Jane and I’m from Germany. I have a history of depression and have been in therapy in the past due to suicidal thoughts. However, lately, I've been experiencing disturbing thoughts of wanting to harm others. These thoughts involve acts of violence such as school shootings or physically hurting individuals. I want to emphasize that I have never acted on these thoughts, but they are causing me distress. I have a support system now and I value my friends, but I still struggle with the negative images from my childhood and feeling unloved by my parents. I don't want to continue having these thoughts, but I feel like I have to pretend that everything is okay. I often feel abandoned and unloved, and I'm sorry for being such a mess. I wish I could be "normal," but I feel like I am not.

I am a sixteen year old female and throughout my life, I have moved cities very often and been to 6 different schools in 11 years of education due to my father’s career choice. Because I have moved around so much, it is very hard for me to make close friends now and to generally trust people. I don’t like making close friends because all I’ve ever known was that people always leave and they don’t keep their promises. I have no true friends that I’ve known for a while. I also have a hard time expressing my emotions such as sadness or pain to others. I’d rather keep everything to myself. How can I change this? I would really like to allow myself to become close friends with the friends I currently have.

My boyfriend and I recently relocated from Arizona to different cities due to financial reasons. His focus is on making money while mine is on school. I am currently unemployed and attending school full-time, while he is working to support both of us. He feels like I am taking him for granted because my priority is school and not finding a job. He wants me to quit school and move to Chicago with him, but I don't want to give up on my education. I try to show him that I appreciate his efforts, but he believes the only way for me to prove it is by getting a job and quitting school. I feel conflicted because I value my education and believe it's important at our young age. He, on the other hand, doesn't think it's possible to work and go to school simultaneously. Can you please help me navigate this situation?

I recently experienced a silent miscarriage and learned at my 12-week scan that I was no longer pregnant. Shortly after receiving this devastating news, my sister, who is now pregnant, seemed to be insensitive towards my feelings. I feel like I've been pushed aside by my family, especially my mom, who only talks about my sister's baby. It hurts me to think that my baby didn't mean anything to them. I'm still grieving and find myself crying a lot. I've tried talking to my mom, but she just tells me to be nice to my sister. I feel trapped because my sister has now moved onto my mom's property, making it difficult for me to have a private conversation with my mom. I can't confide in my partner because he becomes angry and starts to dislike my mom. I love my mom deeply and it hurts me to see this division. I'm feeling very isolated and it's hard to shake off this numbness. I just need someone to listen and help me through this difficult time. Thank you for your time and support.

Hi, I’m 19 years old and I've had a difficult past involving foster care and a mother who struggled with substance abuse. Additionally, I experienced the loss of my brother and sister when they moved to a different state. Currently, I live in Florida with my 8-month-old baby and my baby's father. For the past two years, I've been feeling irritable, experiencing a low sex drive, frequent bouts of crying, and excessive worry over minor issues. I find myself getting very frustrated with my baby's crying, to the point where I feel the urge to harm myself or others, and I also have trust issues with my boyfriend. We recently moved from Arkansas to Florida, and I'm feeling homesick and hopeless. It's been over 6 months since I last had sex with my boyfriend. Can you please help me?

I have noticed that my moods change quite rapidly, going from feeling depressed to what I consider to be a "normal" mood. I have a family history of bipolar disorder and wonder if I might have ultradian/rapid cycle bipolar. However, I don't experience manic episodes, just shifts between depressed and normal. During my depressed moments, I feel exhausted, defeated, and pessimistic about the future. These phases can last for a few hours or days before my mood returns to normal. While I haven't considered suicide, I am cautious about putting myself in risky situations. Is this rapid switching between depression and normal mood indicative of a specific mental illness?

As a soldier currently deployed, I am feeling overwhelmed by the financial strain my wife is putting on our family. We have two children, one of whom is about to go through a major surgery for his feet. I don't know what to do and it's affecting my relationship and overall sense of purpose in life.

Three months ago, I traveled back to my home country and reconnected with someone from my past. My best friend's older sister and I started dating and eventually fell in love. However, I'm struggling with her past and it's affecting me emotionally.

I come from a large family with eight siblings. Unfortunately, our father passed away six years ago, leaving my mother as the sole caretaker. She has always struggled financially, relying on benefits like Social Security, disability, Medicaid, food stamps, and Section 8 Housing. My older sister and I have been doing our best to support her emotionally, financially, and with advice. However, we are now working full-time and attending college, so it's becoming increasingly challenging to help her manage everything. My siblings are also facing their own difficulties, with one brother missing school due to bullying and another sister dropping out and working part-time. I'm worried about the upcoming inspection for my mother's home, as she may lose it if she doesn't pass. I feel like I've exhausted all my options and don't want my family to be separated. Can you please offer guidance and assistance?

Lately, I've been experiencing some distressing symptoms. I see and hear things that others can't, like demonic faces that resemble zombie-like aliens with large goat-like horns. I also see quick-moving black shadows that resemble birds, and sometimes I see things, like spiders, that others don't see. I also hear voices that urge me to hurt myself and they sound evil, not human. Additionally, I have periods of extremely high moods where I engage in impulsive spending and have racing thoughts. My friends and family have noticed that I don't make sense and talk very fast. I've shared all of this with my doctor and a counsellor, but they haven't taken me seriously. I feel like they think I'm a freak or making everything up. What should I do? It's getting worse every week.

I am feeling very confused and conflicted right now. I have this constant sense that something is missing from my life, even though I know I shouldn't ask for more. I was adopted at a young age by a single middle-aged woman who is often not home due to work, and we don't have a good relationship. I found out about my adoption when I was younger. My grandmother always speaks negatively about my biological father, saying that he ruined my real mother's life. At first, I thought she was exaggerating, but when I met him, he didn't fit my idea of what a father should be. He has a new wife and my other siblings are with him. It made me resent him even more, especially because my mother passed away during childbirth and here he is starting a new family. I find it difficult to trust and talk to men or adults in general because I feel like they are all selfish, just like my father. However, when I started high school, I realized not all men are the same. I've been trying to open up to them, but I still struggle at times. I do have friends, but sometimes I feel like they don't truly understand me, possibly because they come from complete and happy families. I've never really cried in front of them, and I find myself crying alone often. I'm not sure why I do this—maybe it's because of loneliness or envy? Despite my life being better than it was with my father, I still find myself yearning to be reborn into a normal and happy family.

I recently took some online personality disorder tests and received scores of 38 for borderline, 23 for narcissism, and 15 for psychopathy. I'm struggling to gather the courage to seek professional help. I'm also feeling embarrassed because I've heard that BPD is mainly a disorder that affects women. Can you provide any advice or guidance?

I am a divorced parent who started dating a man whose son is dating my daughter. We have been dating secretly since October, but we have both agreed not to introduce anyone to our kids unless it is serious. Now, we are faced with a decision. Should we continue dating and risk the impact on our children, or should we end the relationship for their sake? We both have a strong connection and enjoy each other's company, but we don't want to keep sneaking around or lying to our kids. They have already sensed something is going on and we have denied it. Can you offer any guidance?

I used to be extremely active and dedicated to my athletic pursuits, particularly basketball. I would run for miles every night and put in hours of training to chase my dream of becoming an NBA player. However, things took a turn for the worse during the summer before my senior year in high school. I was pushing myself to the limit, training for at least 5 hours a day. On top of that, I would stay up all night talking to my girlfriend, leaving me with no time to rest.

I've been feeling really down lately. It seems like people don't want to be around me and I'm having a hard time making friends. My group of friends acts distant and excludes me from their plans. I've tried reaching out to other people, but I always feel like they're treating me strangely. I can't help but think that there's something wrong with me that makes me undesirable.

I've been experiencing intense bullying at school and it's really affecting me emotionally. People throw apples at my head, call me derogatory names like "whale," "useless," "SPED," "ranga," and "faggot." Even worse, my parents have told me they wish I was never born and they also call me useless. It makes me feel incredibly worthless because our parents should love and care for us. When I try to talk to my mother about the bullying, she tells me to just learn to deal with it because she doesn't care. My dad feels the same way. There's a teacher at school who has asked if I'm okay and what's wrong, but I'm too scared to open up. I really need help telling my teacher everything, but I'm even more scared about the situation at home. I can't handle it much longer. It's only been three days into the school holidays and I'm already feeling overwhelmed. Thank you for listening.

I've been in a long-distance relationship with my boyfriend for almost a year. We've known each other for 10 years, but he lives in Cleveland while I live in Columbus. The main issue is that he's a workaholic and his job in the medical field requires a lot of travel. As a result, I rarely get to see him and it feels like all he does is work. Our communication is also lacking, as evidenced by him not informing me about a recent trip to Vegas for a medical convention. He apologized and I told him he needs to prove that he wants to be with me and prioritize our relationship. He's been fighting for us despite my doubts, and he wants me to move in with him. However, I'm not sure if it will work since he's hardly ever home. My friends think he's unreliable, but I genuinely care for him and see a future together. Can you please provide some guidance?

I am a 20-year-old in a relationship with a girl my age for about 8 months now. She is kind, funny, and beautiful, but I have this nagging feeling that something isn't right. In my previous relationship, I was betrayed and it really affected my self-esteem. This current relationship is great, we rarely argue and have no major issues. However, I find myself wanting to flirt with other girls and I'm worried that I might cheat. I feel guilty because my girlfriend is amazing and I don't want to hurt her. Should I talk to her about this or wait and see what happens?

I have been in a relationship with my girlfriend for the past two years. Recently, she moved in with me and my widowed mother. However, I am facing a challenge as she doesn't want to spend time with my family or attend family events. She comes from a family that doesn't get along well, whereas my family is warm and loving. She feels uncomfortable around them and believes they are judgmental. Despite my reassurances, she insists that as we are not married or engaged, she doesn't need to be close to them. This situation is causing me concern and making me question if she is the right person for me. I understand that she isn't close to her own family, but I feel she is overreacting. I have already had to leave her alone at my house for three family events, which is starting to take a toll on me. I'm wondering if I should consider moving on. I am 30 years old, have a stable job, and am responsible. My girlfriend, on the other hand, is currently unemployed but working towards a certificate in medical billing. I do a lot of nice things for her, including paying for her school course. I don't want to avoid my family just because she doesn't see the need to be around them. This is the first girlfriend I've dated who behaves this way, and it's starting to affect me. I would appreciate any advice. Today, my sister and her family are coming over for dinner, but my girlfriend doesn't want to be here, and I'm tired of hiding my family for her.

Growing up, I was always aware of the unique challenges my younger sibling with autism faced. My parents, in their concern for her future, emphasized the importance of my success so that I could care for her when they were no longer able to. While I initially accepted this responsibility, I've recently found myself questioning the meaning of life and my own purpose as I entered grade 7.

Lately, I've been feeling a disconnect from my own humanity. Some of my trusted friends have suggested that I seek help, but I'm afraid that if I do, I'll end up being confined somewhere, which I believe would only exacerbate the situation. Over the past few years, I've been experiencing episodes where I feel like I'm transforming into a werewolf. I know it sounds strange, and I can't really explain why it's happening. During these episodes, I've come close to attacking my friends without any recollection of it afterwards. My friends are the only ones keeping me somewhat grounded, so I can't afford to lose them. If I were to bring this up with my psychologist, would there be a risk of being locked up?

During my childhood, when I was in 2nd grade, I experienced a traumatic incident. The grandfather of a neighbor, who was a few years older than me, molested me. I don't have clear memories of all the specifics, but I do remember sitting on his leg without wearing any bottoms. I recall feeling worried and expressing my concern about the situation being wrong. His response was that I shouldn't worry because his granddaughter did this with him regularly. At the time, I felt conflicted, and I held negative thoughts about her, blaming her for what happened.

My boyfriend and I have been together for a year and a half. We have a loving and communicative relationship, and we resolve our issues by talking things through. However, there was an incident where he lied about going swimming with a girl named Danielle, who I had some concerns about. He admitted to not telling me about her because he didn't want me to think anything happened between them. We had a conversation about honesty and he apologized, promising to be more open with me in the future. I forgave him and we moved forward.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for over 2 years now. The issue I'm facing is his treatment towards me. Yesterday morning, he seemed distant and uninterested when he joined me and his daughter on the couch. He was rolling his eyes and making me feel like a bother. This happens occasionally, where he tells me my stories are stupid and that I talk too much. He tries to control how I communicate with him. I usually end up leaving and staying at a hotel or visiting my family to get some space. He then becomes apologetic, listens to me, and acts perfect for a while. However, it always goes back to the same pattern of him dictating how I should talk to him. I leave again, and he apologizes once more, but I know it's just a matter of time before it happens again.

Over the past decade, I have been grappling with depersonalization, anxiety, and occasional episodes of intrusive thoughts. Recently, after having my wisdom teeth removed, I experienced a severe panic attack and began researching schizophrenia. This led to intrusive thoughts of harming my fiancé, along with slight auditory hallucinations, vivid dreams, and a sense of paranoia. I have sought help from an OCD specialist who diagnosed me with OCD, anxiety, and depression. However, I feel like my symptoms are worsening, and I fear losing touch with reality. I am experiencing emotional numbness, night sweats, loss of appetite for over three weeks, and occasional episodes of fearing I have angered God. I also feel detached from myself, as if someone else has taken over my body and mind. Time also seems to be distorted for me. I have periods of feeling completely normal, followed by episodes of feeling "crazy" for around eight months every few years. I am unsure of what to do and wonder if checking myself into the hospital would be a good idea to address these concerns.

I've developed a friendship with a man who has disclosed to me that he has a personality disorder, although I am unsure of the specific diagnosis. He has expressed that he is incapable of experiencing love, but he does display empathy and charisma. He enjoys being around people and constantly surrounds himself with them. When he is with someone, he is fully engaged and attentive, but once they leave, it's as if they cease to exist to him. He has mentioned suffering from severe migraines and manages them through dietary adjustments and taking Effexor. He also receives therapy from a mental health professional.

I'm 19 years old and have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for 2 1/2 years. I found out that in his previous relationships, he cheated and the relationships ended after just a few weeks. This made me fearful when I entered the relationship with him, as I was worried that he would cheat on me too.

In October of 2009, I was injured in a back country horseback riding incident and fractured my pelvis on both sides. Since then, I have been living in pain until recently when I found out that I have Sacroiliac Joint Dysfunction and Piriformis Syndrome. I am currently taking Gabapentin and steroids, which have been helping. I will also be starting physical therapy next week. However, I've been dealing with this for over 3 years and have been feeling depressed and sad during this time. It has been difficult for me to adjust to my limitations, and I also feel guilty about not being able to work and contribute financially to the household bills. I live with my son, his wife, and their four children, and although they pay their share, I still feel like I'm not doing enough. How can I overcome my sadness and adjust to this situation?

Patient: I've been struggling with falling in love with people who aren't available to me, and it's really affecting my mental health. I have low self-esteem due to my weight, which makes it even harder for me to accept the possibility that someone might reciprocate my feelings. I also have severe depression, which only intensifies my self-doubt. Right now, I'm in love with two people. One of them has been my best friend for over three years, and I sometimes wonder if he feels the same way, although my self-image makes it seem impossible. The other person is also a close friend who is currently questioning his sexuality. He showed interest in me before, but I recently found out it was primarily to explore his own identity. Being in love with two people who I believe I can't have is really taking a toll on my mental health, and I just want these feelings to go away. How can I make that happen? And is there a way to find out if my best friend shares my feelings without jeopardizing our friendship?

For as long as I can remember, I've had this nagging feeling that my mother is emotionally abusive. After a recent fight with her, I found myself turning to Google to look up general characteristics of emotionally abusive or narcissistic mothers. To my surprise, I came across several traits that reminded me of my relationship with my 6-year-old little sister.

I'm a 48-year-old man who divorced my ex-wife, who is 44, five years ago due to my infidelity. Since then, I have been faithful and committed to her. We have two children, aged 13 and 11, and we share parenting responsibilities. We still attend church together every Sunday and sit in the same pew. She frequently asks for my help with various things like her van, loans, and watching the kids. I still love her and want to be married to her. We built and moved into our log home in 2001.

My boyfriend and I have been dating for 4 months and then he left due to his military duties. He is deployed for 6 months. At the beginning we were fine and dandy but we began to go downhill and I am afraid that I am pushing him away. I find myself nagging and nitpicking over every little thing, and he feels helpless because there isn’t anything he can do about it. I have this mentality of "I want what I want, when I want it" and it's causing me anxiety because he is not here with me.

I have been hospitalized three times for attempted suicide. I was diagnosed with bipolar 2 disorder and I am currently on medication for schizophrenia. Four years ago, I experienced what I believe was a breakdown. I started having paranoid thoughts that the school system, my friends, and my family were trying to take my children away from me. I would see things like book titles or hear songs on the radio that confirmed these beliefs. I stopped taking care of myself because I thought I was being monitored through video cameras and police were following me. I also started suspecting that my fiancée and sister were having an affair and that everyone I knew was trying to kill me. This led to extreme weight loss and eventually three suicide attempts. I was diagnosed with bipolar 2 disorder during my hospitalizations, but no one asked about the visual and auditory hallucinations. I have been on multiple medications, including Depakote and Geodon, but they made me feel like a zombie. I struggle with insomnia and rapid thoughts that lead to anger and breakdowns. Currently, I am taking Latuda, which helps with the delusional thinking but not the paranoia. I want to understand if my symptoms align more with bipolar disorder or paranoid schizophrenia and how to educate myself and manage my symptoms better.

I have been feeling overwhelmed and stuck in my current situation. Last September, I lost my job and have been unable to find new employment since then. Initially, I enjoyed the time off, but a few months later, I found out I was pregnant. Due to previous miscarriages, my pregnancy is considered high-risk, so I made the decision to prioritize my health and the health of my baby by not actively seeking work. As a result, my boyfriend and I lost our house because it required extensive repairs. We are now staying with his uncle in a small one-bedroom house. Additionally, I don't have a functioning car because it won't pass inspection and we don't have the funds to get it fixed.

I have been in a relationship with a woman for about 2.5 months. Recently, she asked for "Time Alone" and "Space" to sort out some things in her life. This is the second time she has asked for this, even though she promised it wouldn't happen again. I love her and she loves me too. She is a busy person, juggling college, full-time work, and taking care of her daughter most of the time. I'm trying to respect her request for space, but it's difficult not to reach out. We haven't had any contact for 3 days now. I'm worried that she might be in touch with a co-worker she had an affair with, especially after seeing roses delivered to her workplace. I feel confused and unsure about what to do next, as I have put a lot of effort and care into this relationship.

My boyfriend and I have a turbulent relationship. He has been diagnosed with PTSD, which he attributes to his time in Iraq. However, I believe that his past experiences also play a significant role. He sometimes calls me names that I brush off, but when he calls me dumb or stupid, it really hurts. He often reacts impulsively, placing blame on me for various issues in our relationship. He struggles to have serious conversations with me, but occasionally apologizes afterwards. He intermittently expresses love and appreciation for me. He used to take Valium for anxiety but has now switched to methadone, which seems to be helping him. He rarely acknowledges my accomplishments and can be quite selfish. He frequently promises to do things for me, only to be derailed by minor setbacks. We actually broke up for a month last January, but he kept reaching out to me. I am empathetic towards his past, but I don't treat him like a charity case. I am fully committed to him and support his decisions, even when I disagree. However, his lack of affection and infrequent expressions of love are concerning. Our sexual relationship is also strained, as he struggles with premature ejaculation or a reluctance to be touched. I never pressure him to talk about his experiences in Iraq, and I'm willing to do anything for him. Despite feeling physically safe, I don't feel emotionally secure. There have been instances where he threatened to kick me and my daughter out, although it hasn't happened yet. He is unwilling to seek help from the VA due to the associated costs. I'm torn between staying because I love him deeply or leaving for the sake of my own well-being. I don't think he would initiate a breakup, so it may be up to me to make that decision. However, I suspect he would reach out to me shortly after. Is there anything I can do to improve the situation and reduce the tension between us?

My sister has been experiencing increasing paranoia and delusions. She started using drugs and alcohol a few years ago but seemed to improve when she got a full-time job. However, over the past year, her stress levels have skyrocketed due to work and family issues. Now, she is hearing voices, seeing things that aren't there, and interpreting innocent messages as threats. She believes her husband is out to harm her, accuses her 14-year-old daughter of conspiring against her, and even suspects our mother of being involved in a plot against her. She's been prescribed Suboxone for her drug use. I'm concerned for her well-being, but I'm not sure how to approach her about seeking professional help, especially since she doesn't trust her husband. Is there anything I can do to help her?

Hi, I'm from Serbia. I apologize in advance for any errors in my English. Here's my story: When I was 17, I met a guy on Facebook who was 30 and had a girlfriend at the time. I thought it was harmless chatting, but two years later, I ended up studying in the same city where he lives. By then, he was engaged to his girlfriend. I decided to meet him, but to my disappointment, I didn't like him at all. However, he started messaging me and I found myself getting involved with him. Initially, I told him I wasn't interested in having sex, and he said we couldn't be together without it. But later, he changed his mind and said he was willing to wait. In February of last year, he informed me that his fiancée was pregnant, and we couldn't see each other anymore. I was really saddened by this and confided in my mom, sister, and some friends about the relationship. For about six months, I couldn't stop thinking about him, but eventually, I moved on. In September, he contacted me again, and we started chatting. I felt guilty about his wife's pregnancy, but I also believed that he genuinely liked me since we hadn't had sex and he chose to contact me instead of someone else. However, after the New Year, he stopped calling me. A few days ago, I sent him a message, and he told me that he can't be with me unless we have sex. I recently found out that his girlfriend is wealthy, so I suspect that might be the reason why he's with her. I don't think he truly loves her because he was always chatting with me until she became his fiancée. I'm so confused and torn about what to do. I promised my family and friends that I wouldn't make the same mistake again, so I can't talk to them about this. Can you please help me figure out what to do?

I recently discovered that my almost 17-year-old daughter engaged in inappropriate physical contact with my husband, her stepfather. This incident happened twice, and it has become clear that the boundaries between them have been blurred for some time. My daughter has displayed possessive behavior towards my husband, acting like a jealous girlfriend. I have tried talking to both of them about this issue, but it hasn't resolved the situation. I feel conflicted because I have other children, including one with my husband, and I have no financial independence or family support to rely on. I blame my daughter for being provocative, although she doesn't display such behavior elsewhere. However, I hold my husband even more accountable for his actions. He didn't inform me about the incidents and lied about them when confronted. He had the opportunity to be a responsible adult and prevent this from happening, but he didn't. I'm uncertain about what steps to take. We have been together for 13 years. Please, I need help and guidance.

I'm really struggling with my mother's behavior lately. She's 63 years old, but she acts as if she's much older, like 83. Ever since my father passed away in 2000, she hasn't been taking care of herself and it's causing a lot of problems for me. After my father's death, she went through a period where she stayed in bed for six months and I had to handle everything. Eventually, she found a job and worked for many years, but that was pretty much all she did. She would come home from work and go straight to bed, leaving me to handle everything else in addition to my own job. Recently, she decided to retire early at the age of 60, and now I feel even more overwhelmed.

Over the past few months, I have developed a deep connection with someone I met online. We have been talking and texting every day, and our bond has grown stronger. Recently, we have started to develop romantic feelings for each other and have become even closer. He plans on visiting me in a few months.

Lately, I've been feeling really isolated and find it difficult to communicate with others. It's not that I don't want to, it's just that I can't seem to find the right words to start a conversation. Even when I do manage to start one, negative thoughts flood my mind and I lose my train of thought. It's frustrating and makes me feel awkward. I spend a lot of time analyzing myself and trying to figure out what's wrong with me. I know that this self-evaluation is part of the problem, but I can't seem to stop these negative thoughts from happening. I used to be so outgoing and could talk to anyone, but now even hanging out with my close friends feels uncomfortable. I don't know what's happening to me and it's really affecting my happiness. I'm also having trouble concentrating, like right now, my mind keeps drifting off as I'm trying to express myself.

My boyfriend and I have been in a relationship for 3 years. We met when he was starting his career as a tattoo artist, which involves working on both male and female clients in intimate areas. Initially, our relationship had its challenges, but we managed to improve over time. However, I've recently noticed that my boyfriend is engaging in inappropriate behavior with these clients. He not only flirts with them but also texts them, makes sexual remarks, and even invites them to our home. I feel neglected and hurt, as he says and does things with them that he doesn't with me.

I'm feeling overwhelmed and stressed with my current situation. I am 24 years old, married, and a mother of two children. My husband and I have been married for three years, but we met three and a half years ago. We decided to get married shortly after I became pregnant a few months into our relationship. At that time, I was still a student and didn't have a job.

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for a year and four months. Recently, he expressed that he needed some time apart due to stress. We ended up breaking up about a week ago, but got back together after just one day.

My relationship with my 17-year-old brother has been strained ever since my parents adopted him from Russia when he was 13. We constantly argue and can't seem to get along. Last year, when I was 14, we were sharing a room because our grandmother was visiting. We ended up playing a game of "never have I ever" with my mom's vodka, which was probably not the best decision.

I am feeling overwhelmed and concerned about my 15-year-old daughter's well-being. I have been taking her to various professionals for the past 10 years in an attempt to understand and address her struggles. She has received multiple diagnoses such as ADD, ODD, potential BPD, and depression, but there seems to be no consensus. She faces difficulties in social interactions and academics, often missing social cues and talking excessively. While she longs for friendships, she mainly connects with people online. Her academic performance is suffering, as she frequently forgets or loses assignments. I am currently facing financial constraints and unsure of where to seek treatment to support her. What can I do to help her?

I've recently discovered that I have social anxiety and I'm struggling with a sense of identity. I've had a sheltered upbringing, being homeschooled and having my parents follow me to college after their divorce. I often felt responsible for supporting my mom during this time.

My girlfriend has a strong obsession with the band Hanson, which she refers to as her passion. She has been a dedicated fan since she was just six years old and believes that her love for the band is a fundamental part of her identity. She feels that they have always been there for her and that they define who she is. On the other hand, I have my own obsession with Lord of the Rings, but I recognize that my liking for it does not define me as a person. I enjoy Lord of the Rings because it aligns with my interests and values.

Lately, I've been experiencing an increased preoccupation with thoughts of suicide. It's more intense than anything I've felt before. Currently, I'm seeing a therapist once a month for head trauma, depression, and the loss of my sense of smell due to a head injury. Unfortunately, I don't feel comfortable discussing my suicidal thoughts with him because he reacts angrily.
