He believes I may be bipolar and borderline, which I had to research because I wasn't familiar with those terms. The idea of going back to the hospital is frightening, but the urge to harm myself is getting stronger, and I'm feeling anxious and disconnected from life. I'm wondering if I should switch doctors or if things will ever improve.

I am a 30-year-old mother of two. My depression started after the birth of my first child. I have struggled to form a connection with my daughter, and this feeling has persisted over time. However, my mental health took a turn for the worse when I found out during my second pregnancy that my child could have Down Syndrome and a severe heart deformity. Despite the diagnosis, I chose not to terminate the pregnancy. After my baby was born, it was discovered that he had Double Inlet Left Ventricle (DILV), which required immediate surgery. He was transported to another city for his first surgery when he was just four days old.

About two years ago, when I was 21, I experienced a traumatic event - I was raped. Since then, I've developed an obsession with rape. I find myself reading books, watching movies, and searching the web for content related to rape. It disturbs me and triggers feelings of reliving the experience, making me feel queasy, sad, and disturbed. Strangely though, I can't stop myself from consuming this content. On the other hand, I find it incredibly difficult to discuss my own experience and can't go into the full details with anyone. It feels like I'm reliving it. I also have nightmares about being raped and struggle with fear of the dark. I've been seeing a therapist, but it doesn't seem to be helping. I can't get rape off my mind and it's become an overwhelming and creepy obsession. I'm not sure what's wrong with me or what I should do.

I'm 48 years old, divorced, and have two grown sons and a granddaughter. On the surface, it may seem like I have a wonderful life, but it's far from that. I've been dealing with chronic medical pain for over 8 years now, and it's only gotten worse over time. I have three different chronic pain conditions, each one causing extreme discomfort. My daily life is limited to my bedroom, and unfortunately, there is no cure for what I'm going through.

Over the past two years, I have been experiencing some concerning thoughts. I have started to believe that others can hear the thoughts in my head. Recently, I have also been hearing voices of God, Jesus, demons, and the devil, and I engage in conversations with them. These experiences have led me to feel a sense of superiority and a belief that certain people don't deserve to exist on the same planet as me. Additionally, I have had violent fantasies and an attraction towards notorious killers like Jeffrey Dahmer, which is distressing to me. I am starting to feel scared of myself. Do I need help?

I served in the military for 7 years with two deployments to Afghanistan and two deployments to Egypt. When my first deployment ended in 2008 (a 13-month tour), my best friend committed suicide, and it affected me deeply for a few months. After that, I was sent to Egypt for two years. When I returned to America from January 2011 to July 2011, I noticed that I started drinking heavily, although it didn't cause any problems. From October 2011 to October 2012, I did one last tour in Afghanistan. Since I've moved back home, I've been feeling out of control at times. I've already had a Drunk in Public charge (which was dismissed) and just received a DUI. I feel careless, depressed, and experience crazy mood swings. I don't know why I feel this way, and it's driving me crazy. I've also lost contact with my best friends and even my father in the past few months because I feel like I can't trust anyone. How can I stop overthinking? Life overseas felt so much easier and happier, but back home it's incredibly stressful. I don't know what to do anymore.

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for 5 years now, and his 11-year-old daughter's behavior has been causing some challenges. She has been increasingly disrespectful towards adults, including me. I've noticed that she gives me dirty looks when her father shows me affection. Furthermore, she has called me hurtful names, and her father hasn't addressed this issue. Additionally, I'm concerned about her behavior, as she engages in sexually inappropriate actions for her age, such as texting and talking to boys at all hours and sharing her phone number with them. Her father doesn't seem to see anything wrong with this.

I am a 37-year-old Palestinian woman who recently went through a breakup with my 27-year-old ex-boyfriend. We dated for a little over a year, but he ended things, citing that we are on different paths in life. I believe that my desire to have children may have put pressure on him, even though I expressed that I chose him over starting a family. To make things more complicated, we both work at the same company. He says he wants to be friends, but he avoids me and then randomly messages me about TV shows at work. It's incredibly painful trying to move on from someone I still love and want to be with. I've made the mistake of begging and texting him too much, but I've finally backed off. However, he keeps giving me mixed messages. He'll say we should just be friends, but then he'll say he needs space to see if there's a future for us. I'm confused about his intentions. When he suggests being friends, is it because of my past behavior? And when he asks for space, does he see a potential future for us or not?

I am a young boy who is struggling with some intense thoughts and emotions. I enjoy listening to heavy metal music, particularly artists like Ozzy Osborne and Marilyn Manson. I have a younger brother as well. One of my main concerns is my height, as I am significantly shorter than others my age (144cm). This has led to some distressing thoughts, such as fantasizing about becoming a powerful figure like a king or emperor and cutting off the legs of those who are taller than me. These thoughts are persistent, even appearing in my dreams where I see blood and people without legs. I also feel like my friends secretly laugh at my height and that everyone hates me. My friends have even called me crazy at times. Additionally, I had a concerning incident where I almost harmed my friend while listening to music and losing control of myself. My mother has expressed concern, calling me crazy after I smeared my face in my own blood. I'm wondering if I'm truly crazy or if these experiences are just a result of puberty.

Lately, I've been struggling with excessive overthinking. It seems like my mind is constantly filled with negative thoughts, and I have this internal battle going on between my rational self and the voice in my head. For instance, in social situations, I often convince myself that nobody likes me or wants to hear what I have to say. Although I've made progress in overcoming these thoughts, I still find it challenging to stop myself from overanalyzing everything. It's like I can't help but believe these negative thoughts, even though I know they're not true and that I have plenty of friends.

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for the past two years. We started dating when we were both 20 years old and decided to move in together right away. We lived in our hometown initially, but then we made the decision to move across Canada so he could pursue work opportunities.

I started seeing a therapist and our relationship became inappropriate. We had an emotional and sexual affair for almost a year. When her spouse discovered the affair, she ended our relationship abruptly. I was devastated and ended up attempting suicide.

My childhood was really difficult. My parents got divorced when I was young, and I never really understood why. I suspect my mother had issues with drugs, but I'm not sure. Since then, I've had three different stepmothers, and I haven't had a good relationship with any of them. Throughout all of this, I've mostly been living with my dad.
I've been feeling really down lately and I don't know why. I have a good job, a loving family, and no major problems in my life. But I just can't seem to shake this feeling of sadness and emptiness.

I've been friends with this person for a while now, and I've noticed some concerning patterns in their behavior. They went through a really tough divorce, and their ex-husband had periods of aggression. My friend is usually vague in their communication and has a habit of not repaying debts, always claiming that they owe me. After their divorce, I sympathized with their financial struggles, but recently I've noticed that they take advantage of my generosity. They'll suggest going out to eat and then let me foot the bill, or conveniently have issues with payment at parking lots. I also have doubts about the truthfulness of their stories regarding their ex-husband and their divorce. I'm starting to lose trust in them, especially since they've asked me to collaborate on a creative project. Is there a psychological disorder that could explain their behavior?

I am feeling conflicted about my marriage. I got married at a young age and have been with my wife for about six years. However, I have always felt like we are more like friends than romantic partners. I have recently met someone who I feel a deep connection with, and it has made me question my current relationship. My soul mate lives in Germany, and I am considering moving to be with her. I know it would be a difficult decision, but I can't ignore my feelings. What should I do?

I have been dealing with thoughts of murder for a long time, starting when I was a young child. My father was abusive towards me and my mother, and I have vivid memories of the violence I witnessed. I didn't fully understand the seriousness of these thoughts back then, but they were a way for me to cope with the constant fear I lived in.

I have been diagnosed with major depression with psychosis, but I've been pretending to have these symptoms because I'm scared to admit the truth. The truth is, I don't have any feelings towards people and I have violent thoughts about harming them. I went through severe abuse at a young age and kept it a secret for a long time. Lately, those memories have resurfaced, and it's becoming harder for me to hide my true self. I'm afraid to tell my therapist because I don't want to be hospitalized and lose my cat, who is like my baby. What should I do?

Patient's statement (rewritten): I've been married to my wife for almost 3 years, and she has been struggling with attachment disorder. Along with that, she has been dealing with adrenal fatigue and a gluten intolerance, which we only recently discovered. It has been challenging for me to balance taking care of her physical needs while also addressing the stress in our relationship.

Over the summer, I started smoking weed regularly for about three months. It started as a way to enjoy the nice weather in LA, but then things took a turn. I had a bad experience after trying a bong for the first time, and then another one a month later. Since then, I've been feeling off, experiencing depersonalization, and having panic attacks and anxiety. I'm not sure if it's related to the weed or if it's something else. On top of that, I'm going through a quarter-life crisis and the weather in London is making me feel even more down. I just want to feel like myself again and stop overthinking everything.

18 months ago, my partner and I experienced the premature birth of our baby girl, who weighed only two pounds. While our baby is now healthy, the trauma of that experience has had a profound impact on me and our relationship. Although we had some issues before, I believe this event has brought our problems to a breaking point. I feel like I didn't receive the necessary support from my partner. I've tried to communicate with him now that our baby is doing better, but he insists on moving forward and leaving it in the past. However, I am struggling to move past the feelings of disloyalty and abandonment.

Lately, I've been experiencing a combination of negative and positive symptoms that are concerning to me. While I don't feel depressed myself, others have been commenting that I appear to be. I've also been dealing with long-standing paranoia and heightened senses. There have been instances where I've heard people say things or call me, even though they claim they didn't. I've also had some mild perceptual illusions, like mistaking a shadow for a bug or seeing smoke in a room when nothing was burning. Additionally, I've noticed that I've become more violent, reclusive, and hostile, despite generally having a fine and even happy mood. I often find solace in daydreaming. My views on humanity and religion have become passionate and others might consider them outlandish and cynical. However, I don't talk about things like aliens or other overt delusions. I feel like I'm on the verge of developing delusions. I recognize that my opinions differ from others and can be argued against logically, but I still strongly believe in them. Recently, I've also been struggling with poor attention span and short-term memory issues, with the memory problems appearing first.

When I was 13, I experienced ongoing sexual harassment in my classroom for an entire year. This person not only made inappropriate comments that I could try to ignore, but also engaged in physical acts such as groping my chest, butt, and attempting to touch me in inappropriate places. It was incredibly difficult for me to cope with this situation, as he persisted in his actions despite my protests.

I've been feeling overwhelmed lately. It seems like every area of my life is falling apart. I used to excel academically, but now I'm just average. My writing skills have declined, and I struggle to articulate my thoughts. Speaking has become difficult for me, and I often feel like my words come out sounding foolish. I've lost interest in connecting with others and fear being alone. I feel like a failure and worry that I'll never achieve the success I've always wanted. My mind is constantly filled with negative thoughts, and I can't seem to stop them. The thought of starting university next year is terrifying. I feel stuck and unable to be my true self around others. I've lost interest in things I used to enjoy, like reading and laughter. I don't know who I am anymore and struggle with self-hatred. I'm dealing with intense fears and anxieties, and I feel depressed. My mind feels chaotic. I want to handle this on my own and not involve my parents or a psychologist. Can you please help me?

I've been married for 32 years and have two grown children, but I'm experiencing a lot of fear and anxiety around sex. I finally opened up to my husband about it four years ago, and I've been seeing a psychotherapist who believes I may have repressed memories of childhood sexual abuse. I've been struggling with several symptoms, including dissociation and moments of not recognizing myself in the mirror. I've also had a history of self-harm, suicide attempts, anorexia, and panic attacks during certain sexual situations. Our sex life has suffered greatly, and it's putting a strain on our marriage, even though my husband is understanding.

I am reaching out for help because I want to understand what is happening to me and if I can ever have a normal life. Around 20 years ago, when I was 18, I visited my childhood home and something triggered a strong emotional reaction. That night, I had a vivid dream about a disturbing incident that occurred when I was around 11 or 12 years old. I remember being in my room, partially undressed, and my brother engaging in inappropriate sexual behavior with me. I'm unsure if it went further or how long it lasted. These memories resurfaced recently, causing me a lot of confusion and self-doubt. I've kept this to myself, and it has deeply affected me. I'm now 38, never had a boyfriend, and feel ashamed of my body, leading me to self-destructive behaviors with food. I feel incredibly messed up and just want it all to go away. What is wrong with me?

Throughout my life, I have faced significant challenges due to growing up in a home affected by addiction and neglect. These experiences have resulted in ongoing social anxiety and a sense of disconnection in my relationships, including with my long-term boyfriend.

Patient: I'm really struggling with my relationship with my boyfriend. It feels like he's not putting any effort into it anymore. I've asked him to surprise me sometimes with something like flowers, but he hasn't followed through. On Valentine's Day, I got a card that I knew he bought, we went out for a meal that I knew about, and then we just went back to his house where his parents were and he went to bed early. Am I being selfish for wanting more? I just want to feel loved and wooed every once in a while. We've been together for two and a half years.

I live in the UK and have been struggling with persistent feelings of sadness and low self-esteem. I experienced sexual abuse as a child, and though I went to play therapy at that time, I haven't sought counseling as an adult. The impact of the abuse on my family has been difficult, with my mother experiencing a nervous breakdown and my older brothers turning to substance abuse. I blame myself for not keeping it a secret. I have gaps in my memory from that time, and sometimes I question the reality of my dreams. I feel isolated and have distanced myself from friends, making excuses to avoid socializing. Thoughts of child abuse cases on the news trigger intense emotions and irritability, and I often dwell on what happened to me. My sleep has been affected, with only 4-5 hours of unsettled sleep each night. While I have resisted the urge to self-harm, the thought of being judged for my childhood experiences at work has made me question my own safety around children. I still care for children deeply, but my job satisfaction has diminished, and I recently experienced an anxiety attack when faced with a new task. There is more I want to discuss, but I feel unsure about how to approach a doctor without feeling silly or like I'm wasting their time.

I've been struggling with my mental health for a while now. A few years ago, when I was 17, my doctor prescribed me antidepressants because I had been feeling depressed for about 2-3 years. Unfortunately, things took a turn for the worse when I attempted suicide shortly after my 18th birthday. I can't really explain why I felt that way, but it just seemed like I deserved to die. It's worth mentioning that two years prior to my depression, my grandfather passed away and we were very close. I'm not sure if that has anything to do with how I'm feeling. Throughout high school, I was teased a lot due to my extreme shyness. It wasn't exactly bullying, but it definitely made it hard for me to make friends. My family also doesn't make things any easier for me. They constantly make fun of me, even though they know it hurts. They used to joke about my depression before they realized how serious it was. My mother tends to yell and put me down without realizing the impact it has on me. When I was younger, my father verbally abused me and even physically harmed me by hitting and burning me. I'm sorry for taking up your time, but I would really appreciate your opinion. I'm always scared, hurt, and upset. I find myself crying for no reason, and I have very low self-worth, self-esteem, and confidence. I don't understand what's wrong with me. Additionally, a few years ago, I received treatment for an eating disorder because I was restricting my food intake. Looking back, I don't think I actually had an eating disorder; I just didn't have any appetite. Oh, and I also struggle with insomnia at times.

Lately, I've been struggling with an infatuation and obsession with a female musician. It started when I became a fan of an Australian band and the lead singer, who is female, became my favorite. As a lesbian, I find myself having erotic and romantic fantasies about her. I have over 260 pictures of her on my iPhone and I even give her expensive gifts whenever I have a chance to meet her. I constantly think about her, day and night. All I want to do is stare at her pictures and think about her. I want to stop this infatuation, but I don't want to completely cut her or her band out of my life. She's a sweet person, and I've even written her letters and occasionally talk to her on Twitter. However, these fantasies are driving me crazy and I know they're not healthy. I'm not suicidal, but I'm feeling extremely depressed. What should I do?

Over the past eight months, my mother's behavior has become increasingly concerning. She has been engaging in promiscuous behavior and neglecting her responsibilities at home. My father is currently serving in Afghanistan, and my mother wants to divorce him. She has been pressuring me to keep her actions and plans a secret. This situation is deeply saddening for me, as my father has been a loving figure in my life. If my parents divorce, I may lose contact with him since he hasn't legally adopted me. Additionally, my mother's friend, Bob, moved in with us after being released from jail, causing chaos in our home. Bob's children are disruptive and disrespectful, making it difficult for me to focus on my schoolwork. My mother has also been prioritizing Bob and her children over me, which has been hurtful. I feel like my life has been turned upside down, and I'm not sure what to do anymore. Please help me.

I've been experiencing some troubling symptoms and I'm starting to wonder if I may have multiple personality disorder. A psychiatrist recently mentioned this possibility to me, and it seems to align with my past experiences. However, my mom doesn't understand and thinks I'm just being crazy. When I was younger, I went through a traumatic experience of sexual abuse by someone who was not a blood relative. This was followed by my parents' difficult divorce, and I've always felt responsible for protecting my handicapped older brother. While things are going well for me now, I still feel depressed and have a lot of gaps in my memory. I struggle with concentration and have heard voices in my head, although it hasn't happened recently. I also experience intense anger over trivial things. Additionally, since childhood, I've had vivid and distressing thoughts about harm befalling my loved ones. I often think about self-harm, even though I can't pinpoint a specific reason for it. I would greatly appreciate your insights and opinions on everything I've shared.

Patient: Yesterday, I had a difficult conversation with my three-year-old daughter. She recently watched a movie where both parents die, leaving the main character orphaned. I explained to her that when people get really old, they eventually pass away. Now, she's been crying and expressing her fear of getting old because she doesn't want to die. This morning, she was crying again before school. How can I help her cope with her fear?

My partner and I have been together for 6 years now, and we have had a good relationship. We have a house together and plans for the future. A year ago, my partner agreed to let a friend of his move in with us temporarily because he was injured and unable to work. Initially, it was supposed to be for a few months. However, during his stay, he relied on welfare and was not very tidy. We agreed that once he found a job, he would contribute a modest amount towards rent. Unfortunately, he lost his job and continued to live with us without paying his share of the bills. He would spend his money on alcohol and video games instead of being responsible. I've discussed my frustration with my partner multiple times, but his friend always makes excuses and avoids taking responsibility. Recently, he even accused me of trying to starve him out.

I've been in a relationship for a few months now and everything is going great, except for one thing that bothers me - my girlfriend's sexual past.
