I know I'm not taking care of myself, but when I look in the mirror, all I see is someone disgusting and it makes me want to cry.

Lately, I've been feeling overwhelmed with the pressure of completing college applications, struggling in two of my classes, and having a demanding swimming schedule. I had hoped that once I finished my applications and improved my grades, I would start feeling better. However, I've been feeling worse instead. I find myself constantly angry around my friends and when I'm alone, I feel depressed. I've even considered quitting everything because I think it will make these feelings go away. I've tried reaching out to my parents and friends, but no one seems to understand what I'm going through. I constantly feel depressed and angry, and I don't know why. Some days, I'll be in a good mood for no reason, but it quickly disappears the next day. I feel like everyone is pushing me away and I'm feeling lost and unsure of what to do.

Patient: My sister and I have been living with a roommate in a town that's a couple of hours away from our mother. Every few months, our mother expects to come stay with us for about a week. It's becoming a challenge for all of us. We have difficulty getting along with her as she talks non-stop and has multiple devices running simultaneously. My sister and I prefer a quiet environment due to our chaotic childhood. Our parents separated when we were young, and our mother struggled with depression and managing finances. We often faced yelling and criticism from her. She expects us to spend holidays at her house and is upset when we try to establish boundaries. Each time I spend time with her, it leaves me physically and emotionally drained. I'm not sure how to communicate to her that we need some space and that her presence is causing us stress. What should I do?

I have been in a long-term relationship with my husband since we were young adults. We both had challenging childhoods and found solace in each other's company. Despite some difficulties, including my husband's infidelity and abusive behavior, I chose to stay with him and build a family. Now, in our early 40s, we have three children together.

From a young age, I have struggled with depression, which led to a pill overdose at 14 and a mental health hospitalization at 21. Since losing my virginity at 23, I have engaged in numerous sexual relationships, often involving prostitution. I have been living with my current boyfriend for a year, but I question the authenticity of our relationship due to our initial arrangement. I have insecurities regarding his faithfulness and seek constant validation. Despite these challenges, I have managed to pursue my graduate degree in social work.

Over the past year, I've been experiencing a significant increase in symptoms associated with schizophrenia. I'm currently a third-year university student, 20 years old, and these symptoms are starting to worry me.

Patient: My boyfriend and I have been together for about a year, and he's currently dealing with some personal issues. I'm wondering what I can do, or what we can do together, to support him through this.

I've been studying Psychology and have been in therapy for several years to address my PTSD and recently diagnosed ADD. I've been observing someone in my life and I suspect they may have Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD), but I know I'm not qualified to diagnose them.

Three months ago, I experienced the unexpected loss of my father. I was with him when it happened, and the responsibility of being there has been weighing heavily on me. To make matters more complicated, it happened overseas and I have only recently returned home. It has been a challenging and emotional journey for me.

Thank you for your assistance. About a month ago, I reached out to Dr. Kristina Randle for guidance regarding my struggle with misperceiving reality without medication. After reading her response, I made the decision to reconnect with my former psychiatrist, whom I had previously trusted, and have since started treatment with her.

I am currently in a very challenging stage of my life. At the age of 50, I find myself taking care of a relative who has incurable cancer, while also dealing with a parent who has dementia in a nursing home. On top of that, I had my own battle with cancer two years ago, but thankfully I am in the process of recovering. To add to the stress, my marriage has been struggling for years. Recently, I made the decision to quit smoking, which has proven to be extremely difficult. It feels like a constant battle that requires so much effort every single day.

My partner and I have been in a committed relationship for 2 1/2 years. I have a 3-year-old son from a previous relationship and I am currently pregnant with my second child. Recently, I discovered a message that my partner sent to one of the bridesmaids he was partnered with at a wedding he attended. I immediately confronted him about it and asked if he had feelings for her.

I am very concerned about my friend. She is in her early 40s and has a family history of Schizophrenia. Lately, I've noticed some changes in her behavior that are worrisome. She struggles with memory, has difficulty staying focused, and believes that people are watching, listening, and investigating her. She's even thinking about moving closer to me, leaving her family behind. How can I support her from a distance? What should I consider before allowing her to move in with my family?

I've been feeling really overwhelmed and confused about my wife's behavior lately. It's been causing a lot of stress in our relationship and I don't know how to cope with it. I'm hoping to find some insight or strategies to better understand and handle the situation.

I've been seeing a therapist at my University for my anxiety, and there's something from my past that I've never told anyone. When I was 15, my boyfriend pressured me into performing oral sex on him, even though I didn't want to. I felt scared and trapped, and I'm starting to think it's affecting my current relationship. I want to tell my therapist, but I'm terrified of how she'll react. I trust her and she's always been understanding, but I can't shake these fears of judgment. It's causing me a lot of stress and I really need to talk about it. Can you tell me if therapists get angry when clients keep secrets? And would you consider what happened to me as rape?
Patient's statement with background and context:

Over the past year, I have noticed that many people around me are struggling with depression. I, myself, have experienced ups and downs due to the bipolar disorder that runs in my family. Last year, one of my closest childhood friends attempted suicide, and it greatly affected our relationship. Despite receiving counseling, I have recently been experiencing a return of negative thoughts. Another friend of mine, who has battled depression for a long time, has included my other friend in a "suicide pact" along with one of her long-time friends. I have always accepted this, but lately, she seems more desperate and even talks about not living past New Years. I am deeply concerned as I feel like I might lose two of the most important people in my life on the same day, and it terrifies me. Additionally, she has expressed a long-standing desire to die, and her strained relationship with her mother leaves her feeling hopeless.

As a junior in high school, I have struggled with making friends both in and outside of school. I endured bullying from 5th grade until my sophomore year, which led me to beg my mom for homeschooling. I have always been shy, but my shyness intensified during the summer of 2009. When I transferred to a new school in 8th grade, I was extremely nervous due to the past bullying. I became disconnected from others, sitting alone at lunch and ignoring attempts at conversation. In high school, I became invisible, skipping lunch and avoiding social interactions. I have developed a fear of going into stores alone, experiencing panic attacks in malls and around groups of teenagers. My mom doesn't understand and thinks it's just a phase. I'm worried about my future, as I rely on my family for everything, lack goals, and fear interacting with peers. I feel like I won't be able to get a job and spend the majority of my time at home.

I'm feeling extremely frustrated and excluded because my husband's family is treating his newly-found daughter as if she's the most important person in the world. My husband and his daughter had no contact for the past 17 years due to a difficult relationship with her mother. However, his sister recently located her and brought her back into the family, which has caused tension between my husband and me. In the past six months, my husband has been giving his daughter a lot of money, even though she dropped out of high school and doesn't have a license. He's even planning to buy her a car. This has caused conflicts between us because I thought we shared the same values on raising children and setting boundaries. Now, it seems like his daughter's every wish is being fulfilled, and my own children from a previous marriage are being left out. I've tried to discuss this with my husband, but it always ends in an argument. I'm seriously considering ending the marriage because I didn't sign up for this. Am I overreacting? How do I explain to my children why they are being excluded while his daughter is getting all the attention?

During my childhood, I experienced some distressing incidents that have had a lasting impact on me. My grandfather would take pictures of me while I was naked or in my underwear, which made me uncomfortable. Additionally, I endured verbal abuse from my father. While I don't recall any other forms of abuse, these experiences have stayed with me, especially the ones involving my grandfather. I don't hold my father entirely responsible for his actions, as I believe he may have been influenced by his own difficult upbringing. I first became aware of the impact of these experiences when I was around 14 or 15 years old. At 16, I reached a point where I seriously considered ending my life, but fortunately, I never followed through with those thoughts. Now, at 23 years old, I have never committed any crimes, touched a boy inappropriately, or even had thoughts of doing so. It's important for me to emphasize that I have no desire to act on any harmful impulses. In fact, I am a caring, honest, and compassionate person who goes out of their way to help others. However, I do recognize that my past experiences have affected me and that I need professional help in order to live a happier life.

I have been unemployed for the past 4 months. My previous company shut down, which has happened to me before. I was working as a Recruiter with a US Recruitment Firm, but they closed their branch here in Mumbai due to management issues. I'm feeling lost and unsure about my career. I have thought about pursuing other options, but I feel hindered by the lack of funds to invest in a course. I no longer feel excited about recruitment or any job that is target-oriented.

My sister has been struggling with her mental health for a long time. Since childhood, she has displayed intense emotions and difficulty managing her reactions. This has caused strain within our family, as her tantrums were often intense and exhausting for everyone involved. Throughout her academic journey, she struggled with procrastination and would experience overwhelming panic and distress when faced with deadlines. After college, she faced challenges in finding employment due to her fear and anxiety. She eventually secured a job as a cashier, but continued to struggle with her emotional well-being. Recently, her job contract ended and she also experienced a breakup, which has left her feeling depressed and unmotivated.

During my early childhood, from the ages of 2 to around 5, I experienced repeated abuse and trauma. Since then, I have faced several other traumatic experiences, both physical and mental. Throughout my school years, I always felt like I didn't fit in with others. I perceived them as mindless robots, easily manipulated and lacking a true purpose. This feeling has persisted into adulthood.

Patient: Over the past couple of years, I have been struggling with moderate to severe depression. I tried taking Zoloft for several months, but it ended up causing more problems for me, including a suicidal episode. Thankfully, a friend was there to support me during that difficult time. In late 2011, I went through a period where I felt more relaxed and recovered, but unfortunately, I relapsed in September of this year. Recently, my family has been criticizing me and calling me useless, and my few friends have stopped speaking to me. Lately, I've been experiencing increasingly strong suicidal thoughts, and I feel completely lost and alone. I don't know where to turn anymore. What should I do next?

Patient's Statement: Hi, I'm really concerned about my best friend. Last night, he had a sudden change in behavior and started talking about having an "epiphany" and being spoken to by God. We're not religious, so it was shocking for me. He was acting strangely and mentioned God's love repeatedly. He showed me a video about the book of revelations and started rambling about conspiracies like the illuminati. He even called me "Satan" and seemed terrified. Eventually, he locked himself in the bathroom and submerged a Bible in the bath, claiming it was a baptism. After that, he became emotional and started referring to me as the arch-angel Gabriel, believing I was a messenger of God. He also talked about being poisoned by the illuminati and Obama being the anti-christ. I was scared, so I took him to the ER, thinking it could be drug-related. However, tests showed no drugs in his system. He was admitted to a psychiatric ward, but they don't have a clear diagnosis yet. I suspect he may have schizophrenia due to his symptoms, but I'm terrified and don't know what to do.

Hi, I've been feeling really down for a long time and I think I might have clinical depression. It started during my teenage years and has gotten worse recently. I've been struggling with focus, memory issues, irritability, and a lack of joy or excitement. I've also been experiencing moments of intense happiness followed by sudden sadness. Lately, I've been having suicidal thoughts and feeling extremely fatigued. I scored high on a depression survey and have researched the symptoms. I'm wondering how to seek help, but I'm hesitant about therapy. If I were to see a psychiatrist for a diagnosis, what treatment options might be available?
I've been living with my stepfather and my mother for over four years now. I'm feeling lost when it comes to my education and career path. Currently, I'm working part-time at a pet store.

Counselor: It sounds like you've been experiencing a lot of difficulties with your overprotective parents, especially your father. It must have been challenging for you to constantly hide things and feel like you couldn't be honest with them. It's understandable that you're feeling regret and frustration about the past and the current situation. Moving away for a few years was a way for you to gain some independence, but now that you're back home, it seems like things haven't changed much. It's unfortunate that your father continues to bring up your past mistakes and make hurtful comments.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for over a year now. Before him, I had only dated once and it took me a long time to heal from that heartbreak. When we started dating, it was overwhelming for me because we got close very quickly. I struggle with depression and anxiety, and I found it difficult to communicate my struggles within our relationship. I also felt confused about his past relationships and how quickly he seemed to move on from them. I questioned if I was just the next person in line for him. I ended up breaking up with him briefly, but got back together because I still have feelings for him and couldn't stand to see him in pain. However, I have some concerns about his behavior and trust in our relationship. I'm not sure what to do.

I've been struggling with depression lately. I recently got dropped from college and it's been hard for me to accept that. I'm worried about what will happen if I try to get back in and they don't accept me again. The thought of going back home and feeling like a failure is overwhelming. I also feel like I lack the necessary skills and competence to succeed in life. It's frustrating because I know what I need to do, but I can't seem to motivate myself. I make simple mistakes and it makes me feel even more inadequate. I've been having trouble with spelling and everyday conversations irritate me. I've lost interest in going to class or doing anything else for that matter. Sometimes I even think about dying, even though I know it's not the right solution. I just feel like no matter what I do, I will always fail. On top of all this, I'm dealing with constant money problems and struggling to find a job. People don't seem to believe that I'm capable of even basic tasks. My appetite has decreased and I've been losing weight. I started exercising, but now I worry that it might be too much for me. To cope with my tension, I've started smoking, even though I don't normally drink.

My 19-year-old son has been struggling since graduating high school. He has had several jobs but keeps quitting and blaming the employers. It's been six months since he last worked, and he hasn't taken any steps towards further education. He talks about wanting to go to cooking school, but it hasn't progressed beyond just talk. His girlfriend's mother seems to have a strong influence on him, and she acts very immature. I have tried reaching out to her for help with my son, but it hasn't been effective. He has distanced himself from the family and rarely spends time at home. It seems like he has lost his motivation for his own future and is more focused on his girlfriend's plans. Despite my efforts to communicate with him, he avoids me and doesn't seem to listen or take anything seriously.

Ever since the summer of 2011, when I started smoking marijuana frequently, I've noticed a significant change in myself. I feel empty and disconnected, like I don't know who I am anymore. I initially thought it was just the onset of winter making me feel gloomy, but it persisted. On January 2, 2012, after smoking up, I experienced a terrifying night where my thoughts became repetitive and I convinced myself that I was going insane. It felt like a part of my brain shut down. Since then, I've been feeling detached from my body, like everything is dream-like. This has led to the development of anxiety, which is now impacting my school performance and social interactions. I constantly feel like everyone dislikes me and I'm starting to question the purpose of continuing to feel this way.

I'm a 19-year-old who is struggling with social situations and feeling comfortable around others. I tend to avoid situations where I can't easily leave if I start feeling overwhelmed. I also have some rituals like carrying my backpack everywhere and wearing the same beanie, which make me feel more secure. I'm having difficulty reaching out for help and understanding what might be wrong with me. I've been feeling disconnected from others and find it hard to express my care for them. I also have intrusive thoughts, hear occasional voices, and feel like I'm being watched or recorded. I've experienced abuse in the past and have been through a traumatic event. I'm currently taking Adderall, but I'm not sure if it's helping. I apologize for the length of my message and appreciate any advice you can offer.

I'm really struggling right now with my family situation. Yesterday, my parents had a major fight that was really intense. There was a lot of yelling, name-calling, and even physical aggression. I got caught up in the moment and said something hurtful to my dad that I didn't mean. My younger brother was really upset and even expressed feeling ashamed of our Indian heritage. It was heartbreaking to see my little sister crying and feeling helpless. I just don't know what to do.

I have had a difficult upbringing with a mother who has been physically and emotionally abusive. She has caused numerous issues in my life, even having me arrested and placed in mental institutions. My father is also struggling with drug addiction. These experiences have left me feeling unmotivated and lost. I need assistance in finding a way to regain my motivation and get my life back on track.

Since I was young, I have been involved in dance classes and I really enjoy it. However, because I prefer dancing over football, my classmates have labeled me as gay. The bullying has intensified in 6th grade and it has taken a toll on my mental health. I started cutting myself as a way to cope with the emotional pain. Now, it has become a habit and I find myself doing it even when there's no particular reason. I want to stop, but it's difficult because it provides temporary relief. The bullying at school only adds to the stress and triggers more cutting. I have been diagnosed with Anxiety Disorder, but I suspect I also have depression. My mom knows about my past self-harm, but she doesn't know that I haven't stopped. I'm scared of what might happen if she finds out. I feel lost and don't know what to do anymore. Please help.

I was incredibly unhappy living with my mom and stepdad, so after quite a struggle, I made the decision to move away from the area I've always called home. Currently, I am living with my grandparents. However, my grandmother seems to think that I still need to be raised, even though I consider myself an adult. She is extremely controlling and doesn't even allow me to stay with friends on a Saturday. Additionally, I feel like I have no privacy as she goes through my belongings when I'm not around.

During my prepubescent years, I used to experience mild auditory hallucinations. When I would lay my head down on a pillow at night, I would hear what sounded like distant conversations between two people. However, the voices were never clear and would abruptly stop when I tried to listen. This happened frequently for a couple of years, but now it is rare. However, I still occasionally experience mild auditory hallucinations. The strange thing is that I perceive them as external sounds rather than hearing them in my head. For example, I sometimes hear someone calling my name even when no one is there, doors opening or closing when I'm alone in the house, or the distinct sound of a noisy fan that hasn't been used in a long time.

I have been experiencing symptoms of depression for the past 6 years, which I have been managing fairly well. However, recently I have been dealing with sleep paralysis and hallucinations that are greatly impacting my ability to sleep. These hallucinations started off small, like seeing spiders or towels hanging from the ceiling, but they have become more intense. Just the other day, while I was paralyzed in bed, I saw a figure dressed in all white resembling a KKK outfit, but without eye-holes. It was staring at me from the entrance of my room and I felt a strong sense of fear. I tried to free myself from the paralysis to confront the figure, but it disappeared when I jerked myself out of bed. I can't stop thinking about this experience and it has made me paranoid. I've started sleeping with the lights on and trying to stay awake all night.

My 5-year-old daughter has always been extremely shy, and this has continued into her Pre-K and Kindergarten years. She takes a long time to warm up to new situations and doesn't initiate interactions with other kids on her own. I initially thought it was just a phase and gave her time to adjust to school, but her shyness has persisted this school year. Initially, she even stopped speaking in school, but with the help of her teacher, we implemented some strategies like bringing in her pet gerbil to share, which helped her start talking again. However, her progress seems to have regressed a bit lately.

I have struggled with feelings of unhappiness for as long as I can remember. However, over the past three years, these feelings have intensified significantly. It's gotten to the point where I think about death and suicide almost every morning, even though I can't pinpoint a specific reason for it.

I've been struggling with feelings of unhappiness, self-loathing, and loneliness for several years now. These feelings first started in high school and I began to experience paranoia and a belief that others were laughing at me behind my back. I also started self-mutilating, which has continued into adulthood with occasional periods of being "clean." Can you help me understand why I feel this way and how to cope with it?

I've been feeling overwhelmed lately with my mother's constant desire to send me back to New York to live with my father or aunt. She believes that my presence is causing her a lot of stress and is taking a toll on her health. This constant threat of being uprooted and losing the life I've built in San Diego is my biggest fear.

I’m a single mother and my son is 13 years old. His father and I broke up when my son was 4 years old. Since then my ex has come in and out of my son's life. He does not help me support him and he has a lot of issues. He makes my son broken promises and continues to disappoint him. I have always allowed him to be in contact with my son because I did not want to be the reason he did not talk to him. He goes months without calling him and then pops back into the picture. It hurts me to see what my son goes through. Sometimes I take it out on my son and I know that I shouldn't. A part of me wishes my son would stick up for himself and not allow this to happen, but he does not. How should I go about handling this situation? My ex tells my son lots of excuses which pisses me off, and then I'm the one taking it out on my son with being angry or upset. Please help.

I have always had a difficult relationship with my mother. My parents were not together, as my father was married to another woman and was not around much. My childhood with my mother was unstable, as she fabricated a story about having cancer when we were toddlers, which she maintained for many years until it was revealed as a lie. She sent us to live with her ex-husband while pretending to care for us to everyone else, including my father. She would tell lies and manipulate us, and would become furious when confronted about her behavior by my foster father, even threatening to abandon us or deny him access to us. She would also sabotage our attachment with him. She would frequently mention his inappropriate fixation on me, but never took any action and instead used it as leverage. When I turned 11, my father decided to live with us, and my mother removed us from our foster father, pretending that it never happened and expecting us to uphold this pretense. If I ever questioned this, I would be punished. During my teens, I developed anorexia nervosa as well as behavioral problems associated with ADHD. My mother seized the opportunity to make me the scapegoat of the family, castigating me for discussing our childhood in therapy and forbidding me from talking about it. However, she would speak to others at length about my problems, often exaggerating and telling lies, which left me feeling isolated within my own family. I left home at 19 when I could afford to, but was forced to return temporarily when I lost my job. If it were not for my father's recent passing and my belief that my studies will lead to my independence, I would not have stayed. To others, my mother appears sweet and vulnerable, and they do not see her other side. I feel like I am her emotional punching bag, and it breaks my heart to hear what she says about me to others. She continues to undermine my confidence, relationships, and achievements, and criticizes me constantly. I will be qualifying as a nurse in January and am currently looking at houses. I am wondering if and how I can rebuild a relationship with my mother, or if it would be best for me to create some distance between us once and for all.

I am a 22-year-old married individual with an 18-year-old wife and a 7-month-old child. Currently, I am studying and working, while my wife is solely focused on her studies. However, things have become quite challenging as she constantly expresses her hatred towards our child. This situation is tearing me apart as I deeply love both my wife and child. Financially, we are struggling, and although I give my entire salary to support our family, we still cannot afford many things my wife desires. Moreover, whenever I try to address these issues with her, she threatens to leave me and our baby. I believe her emotional state plays a role in this. How can I help her see life in a more positive light?

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for four years, and we were living together. Recently, I discovered that he had been cheating on me through a sex chat. He initially denied it, but eventually admitted to sleeping with multiple girls. It's been difficult for me to come to terms with this betrayal, especially since there were times when he would drop me off after spending the night together and then go and be with another girl. He seems remorseful and has even involved his family, who believe he deserves a second chance. I have had issues with relationships in the past, as I got married young and had it annulled. My boyfriend knew about my past, but I now realize he has been a player all along. He begs for forgiveness and wants things to go back to normal, but I struggle to trust him. I fear that he may attempt suicide again, as he already tried once. It hurts me to see him like this, but I know that suicide is not the answer. I feel depressed and sometimes have thoughts of suicide myself, but I understand that it's not the solution. He is not letting me go, and I'm finding it hard to stay away from him despite the confusion and pain. I have become dependent on him, and I don't know how to be alone. I need guidance on how to move forward.

Patient's statement (rewritten): I've been dating my boyfriend for 6 months now, and during the first month of our relationship, we discussed the topic of marriage. I've been married before at the age of 19, but it ended after only 3 months. At that time, I thought I had moved on and didn't care about it anymore. However, now that the topic of marriage has come up with my current boyfriend, I've been experiencing symptoms of generalized anxiety disorder and it has been difficult to cope with. Despite my anxiety, my boyfriend has been incredibly supportive and understanding. Lately, though, I've been having doubts about whether he is the right person for me or if I am truly ready for marriage. It has caused me a lot of panic and confusion.

I am a 14-year-old who is struggling with severe depression. I recognize that I need help, but I'm afraid to talk to my parents or the school counselor because I'm worried they will involve my parents. Additionally, I have significant family issues that I don't know how to handle. To cope with the stress, I started cutting myself on Monday, which has only made things worse. I am in constant physical pain, experiencing backaches, shoulder and arm pain, migraines, and a constant feeling of nausea. This physical pain is impacting my ability to function, and it's causing my grades to drop. I used to find solace in my animation class and drawing, but my depression has become so overwhelming that I can't even bring myself to pick up a pencil anymore. I feel like crying all the time, and I recently had a breakdown at school. I'm reaching out because I desperately need help, and I don't know what to do.

I have been experiencing some strange physical symptoms for the past six months, and after visiting multiple doctors, I was recently informed that I am likely to go through early menopause within the next two years. As a 26-year-old who just finished my master's degree and started a job I love, this news has been incredibly shocking and devastating. I am single and haven't really thought about having children yet, so I feel completely unprepared to make decisions regarding my fertility. My doctors have mentioned the option of freezing my eggs, but I'm overwhelmed by the information and opinions from fertility clinics and my friends and family.

During my early teenage years, I was diagnosed with Adolescent Scoliosis, a condition that affects the spine. It was really difficult for me because I was already a shy person, and wearing a back brace made me feel like an outcast. When I turned 14, I learned that the brace wasn't effective and that I needed surgery to prevent further complications. On top of that, my parents' relationship fell apart when my mom discovered my dad's infidelity over the summer. I was completely blindsided by this and spent the entire summer taking care of my mom and worrying about her.

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for four years, but we had to keep it a secret for the first few years because my parents are strict. They have issues with him not being full Greek, as he is half Australian and half Greek Cypriot. On top of that, my parents only allow me to go out with him once during the week and on Saturdays, with strict curfews of 10:30-11:00pm on weekdays and 12:00-12:30am on weekends. They have met him before, but he's not allowed to come over to my house or even knock on the door when he picks me up. It's frustrating because I'm an adult and I feel like I'm being treated like a child. Additionally, my parents' opinion of him seems to change constantly. One day they like him, and the next day they don't. He's a decent guy who doesn't get into trouble and is respectful when he's around my parents. We're both struggling with this situation and we're not sure what to do. Can you please help us?

I am in my mid-20s and recently got married. My husband is supportive of my decision to stop taking ADD medications that I used to be prescribed in high doses. However, I still struggle with days or weeks where I can't focus and feel out of control. I also have resentment towards my parents for starting me on medication at a young age. I'm seeking advice on how to forgive them and understand why I'm suddenly considering going back on medication after two years of being off it.

I am a 17-year-old in a relationship with my boyfriend. We will both be turning 18 soon. Recently, he bit me and left a bruise on my arm, but he claims it was accidental and just playful. Today, he pulled my hair and took my car keys, refusing to give them back. I screamed at him, and my phone called my mom, who overheard the argument. He even threw my scarf out the window and rubbed it against the car. He insists it was all in good fun and an attempt to calm me down. My parents are concerned about potential abuse. What should I do? Is this considered abuse?

Hi, I’m only 15 years old, and I just want to give up. Every day I force myself to mask my emotions and act fun. All I want to do is just disappear. Criticism kills me inside yet I act like I dont give a crap. Recently, I was suspended for losing my cool and punching a guy in the face because of a bunch of issues that caused him to talk behind my back and smack talk me. I had enough. I continually lose friends, people talk behind my back, my grades are suffering, my family is driving me nuts and making my life hell, my dad is in prison, I was beat for 8 years and witnessed unspeakable things. I’ve done 5 years of therapy but nothing changed. I take anti depressants and they dont cut it. My ex girlfriend whom I dated for 3 years cheated on me and ripped my heart out, and I cant keep going on this way.. I need advice. I have been considering suicide, just so the pain inside ends.

Patient: Ever since I had my first baby two years ago, I completely lost the desire to have sex. It hasn't returned and just thinking about it turns me off. This is causing strain in my relationship and I want to fix it. I am now pregnant with my second child, but I only had sex a few times to keep my partner happy. However, sex is actually very painful for me, no matter what position we try. I haven't had a sex drive for over two years now and something doesn't feel right. My boyfriend's mom thinks it could be trauma related since I became a teen mom at 16. Could that be possible? I really need professional help because I don't know what else to do.

Earlier this year, I started experiencing tactile hallucinations when I would go to bed. It felt like rats were crawling on my bed, which was really distressing since I have a slight phobia of rats and mice. I mentioned this to my mental health doctor and they decided to increase my seroquel dosage from 200mg to 1000mg.

Patient: I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for three years. Initially, I was aware that he occasionally smoked weed with friends, but I didn't think it would become a problem. However, when we started college, I expressed my discomfort with his smoking and asked him to stop. He promised he would, but I later discovered he had been lying and continued to smoke. He apologized and promised to change, but I caught him again, and this time he told me to deal with it. Recently, he decided to quit smoking because we're in a serious relationship, and he has been clean according to drug tests. However, I just found out that he did acid with a friend, even though I made it clear that I wasn't okay with him doing any other drugs. I don't understand why he keeps doing these things and lying to me. He apologizes, but I'm finding it hard to trust him. I don't want to break up because we've been together for so long and I love him. What should I do? I'm filled with resentment because I feel betrayed.

I've been experiencing a lot of distress lately. My thoughts feel out of control and I've been having urges to hurt people, even though I'm typically a compassionate person. I've also been feeling anxious and paranoid, constantly worried about being kidnapped or watched by others. Lately, I've even started to suspect that my own family is plotting against me. I've been having strange beliefs, like thinking that other people can read my thoughts or that I'm a werewolf. I also have periods of feeling extremely low and then suddenly becoming energized. I struggle with controlling my sexual desires and it's causing me distress. I've even had thoughts of suicide, but I stay for my mom. I'm scared and I feel like I need serious help.

Patient: I haven’t seen my ex in 7 years, but I still have feelings for him, even though I'm in a relationship with someone else. We were on and off for about 4 years before he moved away. I never really got over him and I used to check up on him and talk to him occasionally, until my current boyfriend asked me to stop. I stopped for a year, but then I found my ex on Facebook and we started talking again as friends without my boyfriend's knowledge. When my boyfriend found out, we almost broke up over it, so I promised I wouldn't do it again. My current boyfriend is a good provider for our family, including my daughter, but he can be controlling. I know he loves me and would support me, but I can't get my ex out of my mind. What's wrong with me? Can you help me?

Over the past two years, I've noticed a steady decline in my social abilities. I have become extremely reserved and only speak when spoken to. This has started to affect my school life as well, as I am too afraid and unable to ask for help or express myself. While I was diagnosed with social anxiety four years ago, the symptoms I am experiencing now feel different. I am constantly afraid in most situations and I even shake uncontrollably. It has become difficult for me to have conversations with my close friends as my sentences are choppy and unclear, leading to them having to ask me multiple times to clarify. Additionally, I was diagnosed with depression and ADHD four years ago. The depression has been particularly severe for the past two years, unlike anything I have experienced before. I started self-harming when I was 10 years old and had managed to stop for three years, but recently I found myself in my bathroom, holding a razor. However, when I went to use it, it was gone and I was in the kitchen. This incident has left me confused and concerned. I also discovered pieces of paper on which I had drawn disturbing images using my own blood, but I have very limited memory of the events. I am avoiding calling or talking to my friends, even though I know I would enjoy their company, because I find myself staring at the phone without being able to bring myself to dial. I have also been experiencing minor hallucinations for some time, with my vision constantly obscured by a layer of static-like disturbances, both during the day and at night. I have been told that this is incurable and it is distressing to see horrifying things within these disturbances. I am reaching out to you because I feel lost and I need some guidance to understand what is happening to me. Thank you for your time.

I'm currently 23 weeks pregnant and my boyfriend and I recently moved to a new place together. However, my mom has been saying negative things about him and it has caused a lot of stress and sadness for me. My boyfriend wants to be involved in our baby's life and I want to be with him too, but my mom strongly disagrees. I feel like it's the right decision for our baby to have both parents around, but I'm struggling to make my mom understand without hurting her.

I'm 17 years old and I've been struggling with depression since I was 15. Recently, I was diagnosed with Crohn's disease and I also suffer from chronic migraines on a daily basis. These health issues, along with my father being sent to prison, have had a significant impact on my mental well-being. I had even reached a point where I stopped eating and began self-harming. However, after a suicide attempt, I realized the importance of seeking professional help and my mother supported me in getting therapy when I was 15. I attended therapy on and off for a few months, but eventually stopped thinking I no longer needed help because things seemed better.

Hi there, I wanted to share some of my experiences growing up. When I was three years old, my parents separated, and I was primarily raised by my hardworking mom who had to balance work and taking care of my grandparents. I've struggled with being underweight since I was around four years old, possibly due to rapid growth. Additionally, I've had severe acne, which has greatly impacted my self-confidence and led me to isolate myself at home, avoiding social activities.

First of all, I want to apologize if my English is bad. I have been experiencing a significant fear of developing schizophrenia and psychosis after reading medical articles about the symptoms. I have noticed that I occasionally hear "voices" in my mind, especially when I am lying in bed and waiting to fall asleep. These "voices" are more like inner speech and do not feel like someone talking to me. I also have closed-eye visualizations of vivid images, sometimes even when I am awake, particularly when I am tired. These visualizations and thoughts are often random and unrelated to what I am thinking about at the time. They come unexpectedly and I don't feel like I have control over what is being "said." However, I understand that these thoughts are produced by processes in my brain. I do not believe that someone is controlling my mind or reading my thoughts. I don't talk to these voices because I don't see them as entities to communicate with. Another concern I have is that I often have random and nonsensical inner speech, but I stop it as soon as I become aware of it. I also experience occasional paranoia and excessive anxiety about potential negative events happening to me, even though I am aware that the chances are low. I recognize that I have irrational thoughts. Several years ago, I was diagnosed with OCD after experiencing fear related to my sexual orientation. Another therapist has suggested that I also have borderline personality disorder. Sometimes, I doubt my diagnoses and seek reassurance. I also wonder if I have explained my problems adequately to my therapist or if they are withholding an accurate diagnosis due to my potential fear of developing psychosis. The anxiety and distress become more intense when I think about "developing schizophrenia." I can have long periods of feeling okay, but when one of these "voices" appears, I become extremely upset and anxious for days.

I am a 21-year-old male and my girlfriend is 20. We have been dating on and off for quite some time, this being our tenth attempt at a relationship. When we first started dating, she was 16 and I was her first boyfriend. However, I ended things after eight months. During our time apart, she dated two other people and had sexual experiences with them. On my end, I have had sexual encounters with around 20 individuals. Despite my own experiences, I find myself feeling bothered by her past. While she claims that my past doesn't bother her, she frequently asks me about my exes and my own history. I choose not to ask about her past because I don't want to know. However, the topic keeps resurfacing and it's creating a divide between us. I love her deeply, but this issue is causing me distress and I want to find a way to move past it so we can focus on our relationship.

I've been in a relationship with a girl that I really like, and it seems like she feels the same way about me. We engage in physical affection like holding hands and kissing, and we spend a lot of time together. However, she hasn't explicitly expressed her feelings to me, but she's mentioned that she's hesitant to commit because I don't meet certain criteria her family has for a potential partner, such as being from the same caste and having a high income. She also faces mistreatment and constant criticism from her family. She's afraid of the potential conflicts and challenges that may arise if we decide to get married. I care about her deeply and I don't want to give up on our relationship because of her family's disapproval. Can you please provide some guidance?

It seems like there has been a significant change in your husband's ability to have an erection, and it's understandable that you're concerned. It's positive that he has sought medical advice and ruled out any physical causes. It's possible that the issue he's experiencing is related to stress or anxiety, especially considering his demanding job and your history with early ejaculation concerns. It might be helpful for both of you to explore this further with a mental health professional who specializes in sexual health. They can provide guidance and support in addressing these concerns within your marriage.

I've been feeling off lately, and I can't pinpoint whether it's external factors or something internal. It seems like something is definitely wrong within me. I find myself slipping back into a place of sadness, although it's hard to even call it that anymore. I've been numb for so long, devoid of any happiness or sadness. It's like being nothing is even worse than being sad. It's a silent pain. On top of all this, I've started college (the British kind) a month ago, and things have only gotten worse. Just to provide some context, I'm 16 years old.

My son, who is 20 years old and lives with his father, recently gave me an ultimatum. He told me that if I don't end my relationship with my boyfriend by November, he will see it as me choosing my boyfriend over him, and he will cut off all contact with me. I have been legally separated from my son's father for 5 years, and I've been dating my boyfriend for 2 years. I also have two other children, aged 18 and 17, who live with me. I love my son and value our relationship, and if I had to choose between him and my boyfriend, I would choose my son. Is this the same as picking my son over my boyfriend? What can I do to reassure my son that he is loved and important?

My boyfriend and I have had an on-again, off-again relationship for about 2 and a half years. Recently, we started dating again and it's been about 3 months. Yesterday, we were at my house and things escalated to the point where we ended up having sex in my room. Unfortunately, my mom unexpectedly came home early and caught us. She asked my boyfriend to leave and later told my dad about it. They have taken away my car and grounded me until the end of winter. They both expressed their disgust and said they feel disrespected. I feel like they are ashamed of me and no longer want me as their daughter. How can I make them understand that I am truly sorry for my actions?

I'm really struggling with how to help my daughter. She's been showing symptoms of schizophrenia and has turned to drugs to self-medicate. My family has a history of schizophrenia, with my grandaddy and aunt both being diagnosed. I've tried getting her into rehab, but she always leaves after a few days. I don't have health insurance and neither does she, so it's difficult to afford the kind of help she needs. I recently heard some news about where she might be, but even if I find her, I don't know how to help her anymore. I'm starting to lose hope and fear the worst.

My dad has been physically abusive towards my mom and me. He has thrown objects at her, spat on her, and even dumped hot coffee and food on her. I want my mom to leave him, but she is hesitant because she is on the verge of getting a promotion at work that would allow her to provide for my brothers and me. I've thought about calling the police, but I'm scared of being separated from my mom. I want to stay with her, but I also want to escape from my dad. When I've asked my mom if she would leave him, she always gives uncertain answers. If she doesn't take action, I'm considering doing it myself, but I want to ensure that my brothers and I can stay with her. Will we be taken away if she can't financially support us? And would our access to healthcare be affected in this situation?

I am deeply concerned about my husband's behavior towards me, which I believe stems from his low self-esteem. He frequently insults, name-calls, and accuses me, which I recognize as verbal abuse. This pattern of behavior started in childhood, where his sister was the target. Although he had a period of kindness and happiness before we married, he quickly reverted to his old ways. He often feels remorseful after these abusive episodes and tries to make amends, although apologizing is difficult for him. When I confront him about his meanness, he claims it is fun. I see this as a classic case of a playground bully who gains satisfaction from putting others down. My main concern is how to support him in overcoming this issue, as it is taking a toll on our marriage and I worry about our 1-year-old son understanding his father's hurtful words about me.

Hi, I wanted to talk about my recent discovery. I've already been diagnosed with mild Social Anxiety by a psychiatrist, and I've always considered myself introverted. However, I stumbled upon something called schizotypal personality disorder and noticed some similarities to my own personality. I looked it up online and found a few aspects that resonated with me. Can we discuss this further?

Throughout my teen years, I've noticed that I've had a different approach to socializing compared to my peers. While they were busy making new friends, going to parties, and exploring romantic relationships, I found myself disinterested in these activities. It took a lot of courage, but I recently opened up to my parents about the reason behind my introverted tendencies - I have a strong aversion to the idea of sex.

Growing up in a middle-class household with two parents and my two younger sisters, who have autism and bipolar disorder, I found myself feeling emotionally and psychologically neglected. Despite having a great education and a roof over my head, my parents were always preoccupied with work and taking care of my sisters. This led to me developing abandonment and attachment issues, as well as a persistent longing for attention.

I come from a divorced family, and my dad has a history of alcoholism. A few years ago, he was arrested and I was his one phone call from the station. I was home alone at my grandma's house, so my mom had to come and pick me up. There have been several instances when my dad would pass out from drinking and I would have to call my mom for help, even when I was just 6 or 7 years old. Two years ago, he entered rehab and I didn't see him for almost a year. We started rebuilding our relationship when he was clean for a year, but a few weeks ago he relapsed and went back to rehab. It's been a month since I've seen him, and recently I've been feeling really upset, especially since it was his birthday last week.
I recently ended a relationship with my partner of four months because I discovered that he had been living with schizophrenia for the past four years and had never disclosed this to me.

When we first met, my husband used to send me sweet texts just to let me know he missed me. We have been together for almost 8 years and have a 6-year-old child. Our relationship was going really well until recently. He used to be very thoughtful, even kissing me in the middle of a sentence. However, things have changed. Now, he takes hours to respond to my texts and doesn't even say thank you when I make dinner. It's really bothering me.

I am a 23-year-old male who has been struggling with a phobia problem for quite some time now. I feel embarrassed about sharing it with anyone because I don't want to be judged or seen as weird. A few years ago, I watched a movie called Saw that had a lot of torture and gory scenes, which I found very disturbing. Since then, I've developed a phobia of saws, knives, and anything sharp or associated with torture. It's affecting my daily life and making it difficult for me to enjoy things. Recently, I came across a video where a man had to cut off his own arm to save his life, and it made my phobia even worse. I'm constantly thinking about these situations and it's interfering with my ability to focus and engage in activities. I've also noticed a fear of enclosed spaces, possibly triggered by scenes in horror movies. I want to overcome these fears, but I don't know how.

My husband and I have been together for 2 years and married for 1 year. Lately, I've been feeling a growing resentment towards him because of his behavior. He prioritizes his son from a previous relationship over me, no matter what. His son doesn't listen to me, and when I try to discipline him, my husband gets upset. Additionally, my husband contradicts me when I give instructions to his son, which undermines my authority. When I try to talk to my husband about these issues, he gets angry and refuses to listen or make any changes.

I was prescribed antipsychotic medication a few months ago, but I had a negative reaction to it. I experienced fainting and difficulty breathing, which made me concerned for my well-being. I attempted to discuss my concerns with my doctor, but I felt like he wasn't listening to me and didn't want to change my medication. As a result, I decided to stop taking the pills altogether.

I am a young male in my twenties and I'm struggling with feelings of depression. Despite what seems like an ideal situation - living with good friends, working at a respected dealership, and being single - I feel stuck. My job is emotionally draining, with co-workers who constantly put me down. I find myself sleeping more and struggling to get out of bed in the morning. I also feel guilty for no reason and often turn to alcohol to cope. I lost my closest confidant two years ago and now I feel alone. I'm constantly questioning my purpose and find it hard to smile. I'm reaching out for help because I want to find new ways to experience happiness. How can I go about doing that?

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for almost two years now. I'm 19 and he is 21. To put it bluntly, he's not the nicest guy. He calls me names and sometimes he'll act controlling towards me. When I tell him I want to end our relationship, he'll act like he doesn't care which freaks me out enough that I never ACTUALLY end things. We've "broken up" before and I always contact him practically begging for him back because I literally go insane without him. It's like I can't breathe sometimes when I'm not with him and it is a dreadfully terrifying feeling. I have become completely dependent upon him for my happiness. The thing is, I know he treats me horribly. He loves to call me stupid and he gets angry at me now for practically no reason at all. The last reason he called me horrible, horrible names was because I didn't respond to him quickly enough through text messages. Sometimes he'll act like I'm not allowed to have my own opinion. He'll threaten to break up with me if I don't agree with him on something so I always end up agreeing even though I think otherwise. Lately, he has called me a bad name pretty much every day. He really never treats me well. I sympathize with him when he's sad, I apologize when I do or say something wrong or rude, I try to talk rationally instead of calling him names. He never sympathizes with me, instead he'd choose to laugh at me. If someone does something to upset me, most of the time he'll take their side. He very, very rarely apologizes. He's probably apologized a total of 10 times in the entire two years that we've been together. He's told me before that his ex is better than me and that he doesn't actually love me. That he has just told me he does so I'll be happy. With each new, horrible thing he says to me, I think to myself "this is the last straw, I will not put up with this anymore." But then the next day I start to miss him and I contact him. It's honestly like I cannot control myself. I know that this is bad and I know that I SHOULDN'T be with somebody like that but I feel that I've become so dependent on him that it's nearly impossible for me to be without him. When we're broken up, I am so depressed. Every ounce of joy is literally taken out of my life and I've thought of suicide because of it. I just don't know how to live, or function, without him. I don't have a job either. I have nothing to do during the day but talk to him and I'm in my house most of the time because I have anxiety around people and most of the time I'm afraid to leave my house. Why am I like this and what do I do?

I have always struggled with trust issues, which have impacted my relationships. I find myself being emotionally unfaithful, constantly questioning everything, and even invading my partner's privacy without any valid reason. Although I had made a decision to never lie again after being caught with a profile on a dating site, I still struggle with insecurities and fear that my partner may want to be with someone else.

Counselor: Thank you for sharing your experience and concerns with me. It takes a lot of courage to open up about something like this. It sounds like you went through a traumatic incident in first grade, and it's understandable that it has had an impact on your relationships and communication with others, especially boys. Traumatic experiences can affect us in different ways, even if we don't realize it at the time. It's important to acknowledge the significance of what happened to you and the potential impact it may have had on your ability to trust and feel comfortable around others.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend since the beginning of this year. Over the past few weeks/months, we have been arguing at least once or twice a week. The problem is that all of the arguments have been initiated by him. The first argument started when someone outside of our relationship made false accusations about me. He called me up and tried to manipulate me with his questions, putting words in my mouth. I got really angry and yelled at him, but we made up that same night. The following week, after returning from a holiday, he accused me of not being grateful for the gifts he bought me and not prioritizing him. I couldn't believe he said all of that just because I didn't call him for three days after my trip. I told him I couldn't tolerate this behavior anymore. He apologized and said he only acts this way because he loves me so much. I was still upset, but I agreed to be "happy and not awkward" with him the next day. But then, a few days later, while talking to a friend on the phone, he asked me to pretend I was married and to show myself on camera. I refused, and he got angry, accusing me of not loving him as much as my ex and not caring about him. I hung up on him, but he kept calling and apologizing, saying he doesn't understand why he acts this way. I'm frustrated and confused. I really need advice and some personal experiences to help me decide what to do. I have strong feelings for him, but I also don't want to tolerate this behavior.

I am a single mother and full-time college student, currently supporting my daughter, myself, and my mother on a single part-time salary. Due to my busy schedule, I rarely have time to spend with my daughter. I leave for school before she wakes up and often return home when she has already gone to bed. My mother lives with us and provides childcare, but lately, it feels like she is raising my daughter while I am away. I feel guilty that my daughter doesn't get to spend much time with me. I am considering letting her live with her father until I graduate from college, but I'm worried if this would make me a bad mother or if people would disrespect me for making this decision. Most importantly, I'm concerned about how this would affect my 5-year-old daughter. This situation is heartbreaking and stressful for me.

Patient: I am currently in the IB program and come from a supportive, loving, middle-class family. On the surface, everything seems fine, but internally I struggle with violent desires and conflicting thoughts. It's almost as if there are two sides to my mind constantly arguing. I don't believe I'm mentally ill, but I feel like something is not right. After watching a documentary on Jeffrey Dahmer, I became inspired and now idolize him. I'm desperate to understand what's happening and find some resolution in my mind. Can you please help me?

Lately, I've been feeling really lost and disconnected. I don't know what my purpose is anymore and it's causing me a lot of distress. I've tried thinking about the people who care about me, but it just doesn't seem to help. Any suggestions?

I've been feeling really down lately and struggling with social interactions. It's difficult for me to come up with things to say, and it often leads to awkward silence when I'm with my friends. I feel depressed every day and I find myself crying every night for no apparent reason. Sometimes, I even have thoughts of suicide. I am seeking help, but I still feel like I'm not able to enjoy social situations like my friends do. I feel boring and hate being in social places. Can you please help me understand why I feel this way?

I've been dealing with some relationship issues lately. My boyfriend has been keeping in touch with a girl who used to date his best friend. They started sending flirty text messages, but my boyfriend assured me it was nothing. Then, I found out that this girl drove him two hours away and they spent a week together at her place. He also lied about a cross-country trip he took with her. I'm upset and don't know what to do.

Hi. I've been seeking treatment for my mental health for a few years now, and it has been a bit confusing because I've received different diagnoses from different psychiatrists. One said it could be bipolar but not completely sure, so they diagnosed me with depression. Another said I have a depressive personality, while another diagnosed me with just depression. I've also been told I have resistant-treatment depression and bipolar depression by two different psychiatrists. The fifth and sixth diagnoses are unknown to me. It's been overwhelming and I'm not sure what to make of it all.

I have been through multiple deployments and even received the Purple Heart for my combat injuries. Recently, I was diagnosed with PTSD, but I am hesitant to take any medication. The doctors in the Army seem to only offer pills, and since I am not feeling suicidal, they don't think there is much they can do for me. Over the past couple of years, I have become increasingly socially isolated. I spend most of my time at work or in my barracks room, watching TV. I don't see the purpose of going out or engaging in activities because I struggle to find motivation. Due to my age and being single, I feel limited in my social circle. Most of the people in the barracks are much younger and only seem interested in going out and partying. I don't drink heavily and find getting drunk pointless, so I tend to avoid bars. This further limits my social interactions and leaves me feeling alone without a group of friends.

My name is Ashley, I am 20 years old. Still very young and have a lot to learn, that is what brought me here. My boyfriend, Michael, is 27 years old, lives with his grandfather and just recently finished Cosmetology school. I have known him for almost a year, but we have only been dating for 7 months. In those 7 months we have spent almost all of our time together and have only had a few big fights. My parents found out about 2 months ago that Michael was on Methadone. He used to do Heroine and Opiate Pills. When I met him about a year ago he was at 40 mg of Methadone a day and now he is down to about 25 mg a day. In the time that I have known him he has never done Heroin that I am aware of and I trust that he hasn’t. However, he has taking a few Opiate Pills, which my parents are not aware of.

When I was 8 years old, I struggled with shyness and had difficulty speaking up. I felt out of place in school, where many of the other kids were more outgoing. During breaks, they would be loud and I would often find myself sitting alone. My teacher made a few comments about my shyness, which seemed to single me out from the rest. This led to everyone else calling me shy and making fun of me, especially when the teacher asked who was being loud and they would falsely point at me and laugh.

I sought therapy because I have been struggling with emotional numbness for a significant portion of my life. Another therapist referred me to a trauma specialist, suggesting that this feeling may be a result of the physical, verbal, and sexual abuse I experienced during my childhood.

I'm really struggling with my feelings towards my boyfriend's daughter. We've been together for two years, and his daughter is now two years old. When we first got together, she was just four weeks old, but I had been seeing my boyfriend even before she was born. There was a period of time where I wasn't aware of her existence, and my boyfriend didn't have much involvement in her life during her first year. However, I encouraged him to spend more time with her, and he has been doing so. Initially, I didn't mind her being around, but now I'm finding it difficult.

My daughter has been exhibiting some concerning behaviors that align with the symptoms of antisocial personality disorder. She took a psychology class last year and recently shared with me that she identifies with many of the characteristics on the list. These include showing little concern for others' feelings, consistently acting irresponsibly and disregarding social norms, struggling to maintain meaningful relationships, having a low tolerance for frustration and a tendency towards aggression, lacking remorse or the ability to learn from past experiences, and frequently blaming others for their conflicts.

Throughout my life, I have consistently felt overwhelmed by feelings of sadness and loneliness. Despite the passage of time, these emotions have persisted and I have held onto hope that things would improve, yet they never seem to. I find myself burdened by numerous problems and feel ill-equipped to handle them all.

I am currently a first-year college student who is studying for a scholarship. Ever since I started experiencing difficulties with studying, my problems seem to have escalated. Whenever I try to open a book, I find myself crying, experiencing headaches, feeling fearful and extremely sad. My vision becomes blurry, and I struggle to concentrate due to anxiety and feelings of hatred towards studying. As a result, my academic performance has plummeted, and I'm feeling even worse about myself.

I have been struggling for years with forming deep emotional connections with others. It takes a lot of time and effort for me to develop meaningful relationships, and even then, I still struggle to be vulnerable around people, especially my parents. I find myself creating a facade to hide my true feelings. Additionally, whenever a relationship starts to become emotionally intimate, I tend to sabotage it. These patterns have caused me a lot of distress, leading to self-harm and deep depression. I feel like I've lost control and don't know how to break free from this cycle. I've isolated myself to the point where I have no one to turn to.

I've been in a relationship with my current boyfriend for almost 4 years. We initially started off as a purely sexual relationship, but then built a foundation over time. While I care about him deeply and we've even said "I love you" to each other, we struggle to have meaningful conversations. Our discussions revolve around superficial topics like food and sports, and I find that he complains when I try to share more personal stories. Additionally, we are in a long-distance relationship, which adds another layer of difficulty. He doesn't share many of my interests and sometimes I feel like he doesn't take me seriously. However, he is incredibly attractive, comes from a wealthy background, and genuinely cares about me. His family is also important to me. Recently, I've met someone else who I enjoy spending time with. We are honest about our feelings for each other but have decided not to act on them to avoid hurting my boyfriend. Despite this, I'm starting to feel conflicted and unsure about what path to take. I'm confused and never expected to be in this situation. Even if I make a decision, I'm unsure how to communicate it to the other person while still maintaining a positive relationship. I'm relying on my faith, but I also need reassurance.

Over the past year, I have been dealing with a lot of problems that have really taken a toll on me. I constantly feel like I am a burden to everyone and that I am annoying. It doesn't help that I have epilepsy and I can never be alone because of it. My parents have been witnessing my seizures for about five months now and it has caused them a lot of stress, to the point where they can't stand to be around me. I feel so alone and hated. Even though I moved out with my girlfriend and her parents adore me, I still find myself feeling sad all the time. I can't seem to find happiness, and this feeling of being a burden is overwhelming.
