Over the past two years, my husband and I have experienced a series of difficult events, including bankruptcy, a short sale, and the challenges of raising an autistic son who has become physically violent. Additionally, we have lost a significant portion of our retirement savings in the stock market. Recently, I have noticed that my husband has become increasingly distant. He spends a lot of time at the gym, coming home late at night, and he no longer calls me during the day. We have also lost intimacy in our relationship. I recently discovered that he has put a passcode on his phone and seems to be deleting his call log. I am worried that he may be having an affair, although I don't have any concrete proof. I feel overwhelmed and anxious about this situation.

Lately, I've noticed a change in my husband's behavior. He has been going out to bars and clubs with his friends or co-workers at least once a week. On top of that, he also plays sports three times a week, which keeps him out in the evenings. Typically, he would come home around 11pm after sports and 1am after going out, but recently he has been coming home as late as 2am after bars/clubs and even 4am on some occasions.

Throughout my life, I have experienced feelings of unhappiness, which began around the age of 12. I believe these emotions may be connected to my experiences with childhood bullying and ongoing weight issues. However, I'm uncertain about the root cause of my distress. Since the age of 13, I have been dealing with suicidal thoughts, self-harm, and frequent mood swings, with the unhappy moods being more prevalent. I have been in a relationship for the past 3 years and 7 months, and though it initially brought me happiness, I have been increasingly unhappy over the past year and a half. While my boyfriend means well and loves me, I constantly feel anxious and worry about him leaving me. It's difficult to fully explain everything I'm going through, but the bottom line is that I consistently feel unhappy and depressed, with suicidal thoughts and self-harm serving as an outlet for my anger. I have made efforts to stop self-harming for the sake of my boyfriend, but I have had some setbacks, and I know he dislikes it. I constantly experience anxiety about my family, friends, and especially my boyfriend. Overall, I feel like I am falling apart and in need of help. I'm unsure if I should seek professional help, as I previously spoke to a doctor when I was 15, but she wanted to involve my parents, and I didn't want to burden them further, especially considering my mother's disability and life expectancy. I love my parents deeply. Although my current relationship is difficult, I find it challenging to let go, even though I am not treated in the way I desire. I apologize if I am coming across as a whiny teenager, as I understand that there are people facing much more severe problems than mine. I may be wasting your time, but if you could spare a couple of minutes, I would truly appreciate your guidance.

I met my boyfriend about a year ago. He is 45 years old, much older than me. We started a relationship, but he was still married at the time. I became his mistress, which I now regret. Recently, he finally separated from his wife as he kept promising. However, he has children who are roughly the same age as me. One of his sons is very rude and troubled. I'm concerned about the dynamics of this situation and whether my boyfriend will want to have children with me in the future.

About 5 months ago, during my first year of college, I experimented with smoking marijuana. Unfortunately, I had a negative experience and ever since then, I haven't felt like myself. I constantly worry that something is wrong with me, especially when I feel anxious. I find myself monitoring my thoughts and emotions, and any negative thought makes me believe that something is seriously wrong. It's affecting my happiness and I'm not sure how to handle it. Any advice on what I should do?

My husband and I have a strong relationship overall, but we do have some recurring conflicts that I would like to address. I know that relationships require ongoing effort, and I want to find better ways to work through our conflicts and improve our communication.

I have a master's degree in education and I have been working as a teacher, which has provided me with a decent income. About nine years ago, I met my husband, who is 17 years older than me and did not finish high school. Despite our educational differences, we have a strong and loving relationship. Our marriage is excellent and we have never had any issues related to education or money. However, my parents have shown a lot of animosity towards my husband, even though they pretend to be nice in front of him. My mother has been especially vocal lately, constantly criticizing me and suggesting that I should divorce my husband. This is really hurting me and causing a lot of sadness. My husband, on the other hand, believes that my parents actually like him. I don't know what to do and I am seeking guidance.

About a month and a half ago, my friend introduced me to a new drug called spice, which I had never tried before. We smoked it outside, treating it like marijuana because it's often referred to as "synthetic marijuana." However, I ended up overdosing. Shortly after smoking, my legs started to go numb and I started panicking. The numbness spread and I eventually passed out. I thought I was going to die. When I woke up, I felt dizzy and lightheaded. Although those symptoms have gone away, I can't stop thinking that something is wrong. My vision feels off and sometimes my eyes seem to zone out. I also have occasional panic attacks, especially when I'm bored, alone, or getting ready for bed. Am I okay? Is this related to stress? Am I just tricking myself into thinking something is wrong? I've looked up some symptoms and it makes me worry that I had a stroke, seizure, or brain trauma. I'm scared that I'll never be normal again and that I'll disconnect from society or go insane. Can you please help me?

I've been feeling incredibly lonely lately. I don't have any close friends and even when I do make friends, I tend to push them away over small mistakes and constantly find faults with them. This pattern has also affected my past two relationships. The first one was a three-year relationship, during which my dad lost his job and we faced financial struggles. He ended up breaking up with me when I needed him the most. After that, I met someone else whom I deeply loved, but I couldn't let go of the past and it led to our breakup as well. My parents divorced when I was 16, and my mom has been struggling ever since. She drinks a lot and is constantly lonely. I carry so much guilt over the mistakes I've made and I feel like I can't forgive myself. All my family members live in different countries, except for my mom and I. I've moved around a lot since I was 9, and I've never been able to maintain long-lasting friendships. Now, I find myself feeling completely alone, and I struggle with opening up to my family about what I'm going through.

Lately, I've been experiencing sudden shifts in my emotions. One moment I feel fine, maybe even happy, but then something someone says can trigger intense anger or uncontrollable tears. My parents have been urging me to be happier, but I genuinely try. However, when these outbursts happen, I feel like I have no control over them. I've noticed that when I try to stop crying, my mind starts wandering and I end up crying even more. My parents want to help, but there are some things I feel I can't talk to them about, which might be contributing to these crying spells. I often tell them I don't know what's wrong or that I'm okay, but deep down, I know there's more to it. I feel like there's a connection between what my parents say and the thoughts that surface when they speak, but I can't quite pinpoint it. What is happening to me?

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend since my freshman year of high school, and we are approaching our three-year anniversary. We spend most of our free time together, and he has become my closest friend. However, I feel like I don't have a female best friend to confide in. Although I have friendly relationships with some girls at school, I haven't really connected with them outside of school. I have always been shy and hesitant to open up to others. My two best friends moved away at the beginning of high school, and since then, I haven't really formed close friendships with anyone else. I want to make new friends, but I struggle with opening up until I've known someone for a while. Do you have any advice?

Hello, I'm a 15-year-old female who is struggling with some concerning issues related to food and my overall well-being. I have developed an obsession with food that is taking over my life. I constantly think about what I will eat the next day and find it difficult to consume more than 400 calories. I also have a fear of social situations and often cancel plans with friends. Additionally, I have urges to throw up, though I haven't acted on them. I also engage in self-harm through cutting. I feel the need to share these struggles because they are affecting my daily routines and relationships with others.

I'm reaching out for help because my marriage has become incredibly difficult. My husband and I got married two months ago, but it feels like we're living in a nightmare. He seems like two different people - one moment he's loving and kind, and the next he becomes verbally abusive and says hurtful things. I know I'm not perfect, but I don't deserve to be treated this way. Here are some specific examples of his behavior:

I have a sister who is much older than me, but we have always been close despite living far apart. We have an emotional bond as sisters. I have been diagnosed with schizoaffective disorder, and I have tried to discuss it with her. However, she doesn't believe that I have it. We haven't lived together since she went to college before I was diagnosed at 17. Even though we are physically distant, we still maintain regular contact, speaking at least once a week. Since my diagnosis, I have become more withdrawn and tend to keep my struggles to myself. My sister thinks I only have depression or anxiety and has even questioned the authenticity of my diagnosed delusions, suggesting that I make them up for attention.

I have been married to my husband for 9 years. Lately, I have been feeling uncertain about our relationship. He often criticizes and belittles me, making me feel inadequate and worthless. He controls all our finances and gives me an allowance. He is also extremely jealous and accuses me of having affairs. He even threatens violence towards my colleagues. I used to take antidepressants, but he mocked me for it, so I stopped. I'm not sure if this qualifies as abuse, but I feel trapped and unhappy.

Hello, I'm a 14-year-old with Asperger's disorder. Growing up, I experienced a traumatic event where my biological father abandoned me. This has left a lasting impact on me, and I find myself feeling overwhelmed with thoughts of revenge and violence. I have been involved in violent incidents at school and have injured others without remorse. I recognize that these thoughts and behaviors are concerning, and I want to seek help before things escalate. I'm afraid that if I don't get help, I may end up pursuing my revenge. I really need assistance before things get worse.

I have been in a relationship with a man who is significantly older than me for the past two years. Overall, my family and friends support our relationship and he is generally a nice person. However, I find myself feeling overlooked at times. Despite having a full-time job, I find myself constantly doing things for him - making meals, doing his laundry, buying him gifts, and taking care of household tasks. I also make an effort to express my love and support for him verbally and physically.

Thank you for taking the time to listen to my concerns. My relationship with my mother has become increasingly difficult lately. She has been verbally aggressive towards me, and I have found myself responding in the same way. I understand that she has had a challenging life, having lost my father and being in a wheelchair. However, our fights have become more frequent and intense, to the point where we can't have a simple conversation without arguing. I admit that sometimes I provoke the fights, but there are times when she is excessively aggressive. She says hurtful things to me, and when she is ill, she blames me for it. She complains constantly, curses a lot, and has a negative outlook on everything, often blaming me for various things. On my part, I can be rude and yell at her, even when she is being nice. I'm not sure why I behave this way; at times, I think it's because I'm upset with her for losing her positive attitude. I know she is an amazing woman, but I don't recognize either of us anymore. I'm at a loss for what to do. Whenever we fight, I apologize right away, but she is never satisfied with my apologies or when I try to change my behavior, so I end up falling back into the same patterns. She has never apologized to me and always makes me feel like I'm at fault for everything. It's becoming unbearable and difficult for me. I can't imagine my life without her, as she is the person I love the most, and I don't understand why things have gotten so bad. I think I may be holding onto some of the hurtful things she has said when she's upset, or maybe I'm angry because I know she is capable of being better than this. I also don't know how to help her overcome her depression, as she refuses help from anyone. I'm begging you for advice or assistance because I can't handle another day of hearing negative words, complaints, fights, and insults.

Over the past six years, I have been struggling with various mental health challenges. It all started when I was 12, after a traumatic event in my family. Since then, I have been experiencing symptoms similar to Bipolar Disorder, engaging in self-harm, and even having suicidal thoughts. Recently, in January of this year, I developed an eating disorder. It has been a long and exhausting journey.

Three years ago, my sister tragically passed away from a pulmonary embolism, just four months after giving birth to her second child. Then, eight months later, my husband's mother, who already had MS, was diagnosed with a rare malignant brain tumor. And to add to the hardship, just two months after that, my husband experienced a severe breakdown and had thoughts of suicide.

I've been really concerned about my partner's body image issues. Ever since we met, he's been obsessing over his appearance, especially his lower abdomen. He thinks he has excess fat there, even though his stomach is concave. I once told him he was too thin, so he tried to gain weight...

I've been experiencing some concerning behavior from a close platonic male friend of mine. He has been following me to meetings even though he claims he didn't know the location and just happened to show up after googling it. I've also noticed him driving past my house multiple times, which is strange because we live 7 miles apart in different towns. It's starting to feel suffocating because he always wants to be around me. He even gets jealous of my other male friends and invites himself to social gatherings that I've been invited to.

My mother has been diagnosed with schizophrenia since she was in her 20s, before she got married. She is now 47 years old. Over the years, she has become increasingly isolated from our relatives and we have very few family friends. I'm starting to worry that she is turning against us as well, as she tends to create scenarios in her mind and believes they are true. Is it possible for someone with schizophrenia to turn against their own family?

I am a 37-year-old married woman. I have been married for less than a year to a man who is widowed and has two children. Prior to this marriage, I had been married twice before, one ending in widowhood and the other in divorce. Shortly after getting married, I discovered that my husband has significant financial problems, including debt and ongoing legal battles. He had not been forthcoming about these issues prior to our marriage, which has left me feeling deceived and unsure about the future. Initially, he exhibited aggressive and coercive behavior, pressuring me to help him financially. I reached my breaking point and made it clear that I cannot meet all his demands and would leave if this behavior continued. He has stopped behaving that way, but I have lost trust in him and feel uncertain about the intentions of our relationship. I think about running away every day and worry about the potential consequences if he goes bankrupt or loses the legal battles. While I make a decent living, I cannot financially support three people. This ongoing stress and uncertainty have left me feeling depressed. I would appreciate your insights on coping strategies and guidance on making a decision. I am also starting to question my judgment in relationships and wonder why I agreed to marry this man in the first place.

I have been struggling with my relationship and sought help from a psychologist. She believes that my past trauma from childhood is influencing the type of relationships I seek out. She mentioned that my relationship with my father may have shaped my preferences. My boyfriend also went to a session and the psychologist mentioned that he may also have his own traumas.

My close friend recently confided in me that she has been struggling with social phobia/anxiety for over four years. This revelation was quite surprising to me, as she has always been reserved in general. She works in the medical profession and has advanced degrees, and she is generally a pleasant but highly driven person. Lately, she has been experiencing physical illness before meetings, even if she knows the attendees, and she has taken about 30 days of sick time since January. This is highly unusual for her. She travels extensively for work, and last Saturday, she seemed to reach a breaking point. Concerned for her well-being, I drove over an hour to meet her, as we now live a couple of hours apart. She was extremely distraught, and I spent hours comforting her until she was able to release her emotions. We ended up staying at a hotel for the night. The next day, she seemed more like herself, and we went our separate ways. I was willing to accompany her back to her city if needed.

I've been feeling incredibly unhappy in my marriage ever since my husband and I tied the knot. It feels like I'm married to a man-child who always expects things to go his way, without considering my needs or giving anything in return. He grew up as an only child in a permissive environment, which I think may have contributed to his behavior. While I could provide more details about his controlling, manipulative, and verbally abusive actions, I just wanted to give you some background on my current issue.

I come from a very driven family and have always felt the need to be perfect, accomplished, and intelligent. However, this need for perfection has started to severely hinder my life. I find myself constantly checking and rechecking my family's words and actions, unable to trust them fully. It has caused strife between my mother and me, and has affected my relationships with friends. Sometimes, I feel so insecure and afraid that I push everyone away. This fear of not being good enough extends to my significant other, where I struggle to trust him and accept compliments. I want to be able to trust and not constantly doubt others.

I've been in a new relationship for the past two months and things have been going really well. We have great chemistry and share similar interests. Despite living 45 minutes apart, he still makes an effort to see me at least once a week.

Recently, I've been experiencing distressing thoughts that someone else is influencing me to self-injure. These thoughts have been increasing in intensity, particularly at night. This presence in my head has come and gone over the past two years, usually appearing when I face difficulties at school, like bullying or fears of it happening again. However, this time, even during my summer break, the presence persists. I can even physically feel pressure in my head when it happens.

Hello, I'm a 14-year-old who has been in high school for about a year now. Lately, I've been feeling incredibly lonely. I used to hang out with my friends, but now I find myself staying home every single day, even during summer. It's been really tough for me, and sometimes I cry myself to sleep because I feel so unwanted. My parents are divorced, and I live with my dad who has a lot of animosity towards my mom. I haven't seen her in four years, which I think might be contributing to my emotional state. I find it difficult to talk about my feelings with others because I feel like I'm unwanted and that they won't care. I tend to keep a lot to myself, and it's really taking a toll on me. I also believe that my dad might have bipolar disorder and anger issues, which could be why I easily get mad. Additionally, I have a lot of body image issues and feel insecure about my weight. I have so many emotions inside of me, and I'm constantly feeling sad. There are moments when I'm happy, but it doesn't last long before I'm back to feeling sad. I've also been sleeping a lot during the day.

Patient's statement (revised): Ever since I was a child, I noticed that I had the ability to manipulate others, which caused a lot of suffering for my mother and family. I struggle to connect with others on an emotional level and often find myself saying hurtful things to loved ones without understanding why it upsets them. This behavior has spilled over into my work life, where people rely on me for support. While it has helped me cope with traumatic situations, I've come to realize that my way of dealing with things is not normal.

Growing up, my grandmother had schizophrenia, and sometimes I worry that I might have a mild form of it too. When I was 13 years old, I experimented with an OUIJA board and became convinced that I could communicate with spirits just by imagining it. I started believing that a spirit was communicating with me through sign language and writing. It scared me so much that I had nightmares and felt physically ill. I would pray for the spirit to leave my body. Eventually, it went away and I forgot about it. As I got older, I realized that it couldn't have been true.

I'm a 13-year-old who has been feeling confused, worried, and sad most of the time. I find myself crying myself to sleep at night and listening to sad songs, which only worsens my feelings. This all started when I had a falling out with my old best friend. She seems to be fine with it and has moved on, but I'm struggling because I miss her. At school, I often find myself walking alone or hiding in the bathroom, crying over the loss of our happy friendship. Recently, she reached out and said she misses me and wants to hang out around school again. However, she often leaves me out and it hurts me deeply. I don't know if I should give up and find another friend or keep trying. Regardless, it's breaking my heart. How can I stop these feelings and protect myself from getting hurt?

I've been feeling really overwhelmed lately. I've been making a lot of mistakes and it's causing me a lot of guilt. I feel like I can't make any right decisions and everything I do just makes things worse. It's really taking a toll on me.

I've been struggling a lot lately. I'm a 15-year-old dealing with ADHD and depression. About 4 months ago, my mom and I discovered that my father has been cheating on her for the past 9 years. It has been really hard for me to cope with this situation. I've turned to binge eating and have gained over 20 pounds. My grades have also suffered, and I have started cutting myself. When I look in the mirror, I feel disgusted with my appearance and how overweight I have become. On top of all this, my only close friend has replaced me with someone else, which has made me feel worthless.

I've been diagnosed with bipolar disorder and I'm currently on medication. Most of the time, I feel accelerated and full of energy. However, I still experience deep and sudden bouts of depression. Yesterday, for example, I started the day feeling fine, but when I got home to have lunch, I suddenly felt a sense of emptiness. I spent the entire afternoon in bed, unable to eat or speak. I felt drained and even cried without any specific reason.

I have been feeling very overwhelmed lately. I have been having thoughts about harming others and planning out violent acts. I also struggle with faking emotions and maintaining relationships. Sometimes I have difficulty distinguishing between dreams and reality, and I used to believe I was being controlled by dark forces. I also suspect I may have narcissistic tendencies. I often feel misunderstood and unable to share my thoughts with others. I also experience random bouts of intense fear. I want to seek help from a therapist or psychiatrist, but I'm afraid to tell my parents. How should I approach this?

I'm 25 years old and I recently completed basic training in March. Fortunately, I was able to do my training close to where my boyfriend/fiancé lives, so we were able to see each other on the weekends. Before I left for basic training, spending time with my boyfriend was the most important thing to me. We worked together, but in different departments, and he would stay with me almost every night. We had good communication for a young relationship. I asked him to marry me before I left, not in a formal way, but it felt like the right question to ask. While I was in basic training, he wrote me almost every day and made my experience much better.

I recently ended my friendship of 12 years with my best friend. I have been feeling disconnected and no longer see the value in having friends. It seems like I have lost interest in being around anyone, including my best friend. I didn't even feel a sense of loss when she left my life.

I am feeling quite anxious and overwhelmed as I am about to graduate from high school and still haven't figured out what I want to do with my life. I have been searching for potential career paths, but nothing has really caught my interest. Additionally, I have this fear of failure, which makes me hesitant to pursue any particular field. Can you provide some guidance and suggest some possible areas of study for me? Allow me to share a bit about myself.

I recently found out that my fiancé, whom I have known since the 9th grade, was previously married and has a newborn baby girl with his ex-wife. Although I've been told that their relationship is strictly about their daughter, I've noticed that he's been texting her frequently at odd hours of the night, like 2am. It bothers me that he hides me from her and their mutual friends, and he also mentioned that she wants him back. I'm not sure how to feel about this or how to handle the situation, especially since we want to have children together in the future. Should I confront him about the need for his ex-wife to know about our engagement? And how should I deal with the late-night texting? I also read one of their texts, and it seemed like casual conversation unrelated to their child. Is this something I should be worried about? Please help!

Lately, I've been feeling lost and unmotivated. I'm really unhappy with my current job, and I can't seem to find any other job that interests me. On top of that, I've had two failed long-term relationships which has really affected my self-confidence. I used to be independent and adventurous, but now I'm terrified of being alone and I find myself doing anything to avoid being alone for too long. I feel like I'm smothering the people in my life and pushing them away. I want to find a new job, but I lack the confidence to follow through or finish anything I start. I'm worried that I have a dependency issue that's preventing me from living a normal life and I don't know what to do.

Patient's statement (rewritten): I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for 3 years, but he suddenly stopped communicating with me. We come from different countries and have different religions, and his family is unaware of our relationship. Recently, he had a heart attack and was admitted to the hospital where I work. However, I was unable to visit him due to his family's presence. Since then, he has not contacted me, deleted me from his BlackBerry Messenger, and has not responded to my messages. I'm unsure if this means he has ended our relationship without any closure.

My son just recently turned 7; He was diagnosed with ADHD just before turning 6 years old. Most of the issues he has had I’ve been able to deal with calmly, promptly, and confidently knowing they were a “phase” or part of the ADHD that would pass or we could remedy. One of these was his stealing, I handled it calmly and it went away. However this new one has me scared, upset, confused, and very afraid that no matter what I do he may turn out to be a bad person.

I've been having constant conflicts with my mother, and it's becoming unbearable for both of us. Whenever I try to express my feelings to her, she either ignores me or criticizes me, making me feel invalidated and disappointed. It feels like she always has to have the final say, and if I disagree, she becomes aggressive and even physically abusive. I've attempted to have calm conversations with her, but they always escalate into fights. She refuses to acknowledge her mistakes, even when they are obvious.

Patient's statement (rewritten): Over the past year, my OCD has become worse. It started when my best friend began having health problems, and I started struggling with rituals. I already had issues with checking things, but now my anxiety is overwhelming. I have this intense fear of harming others with my thoughts or not performing rituals. I know it sounds crazy, and I feel like I've lost control. I can't talk to anyone about it because it's causing problems in my relationships. I want to find a way to end this and be normal again. I also struggle with intrusive thoughts. I'm young and I'm scared that this will define my life. Please help me.

Over the past two years, I've developed strong feelings for one of my brother's friends. Many people, including his own mother, have suggested that we would make a good couple. I've gone to great lengths to impress him and make him notice me, even making life decisions based on what I thought he would think of me. Unfortunately, he has consistently ignored me and treated me as if I don't exist. However, there are also moments when he acts like there is potential for a relationship and it leaves me feeling confused. I also have borderline personality disorder (BPD), which I believe is intensifying my heartache. I've even resorted to self-harm, with scars on my legs as a result. Despite the pain he causes me, I still find myself wanting to be around him. It's a constant rollercoaster of emotions where I alternate between hating him and desperately longing for his love. I put so much effort into this one-sided relationship and it's taking a toll on my well-being. I constantly question my self-worth and feel inadequate. I don't know what to do anymore, as this situation is consuming me.

After my boyfriend broke up with me, I received advice from friends to go out and have fun with my female friends to distract myself from the breakup. They suggested going to a bar, which was a new experience for me. I invited a friend who had just turned 21. While at the bar, we mostly sat on a couch and danced while sitting down. I received attention from several guys, and one of them asked if I would dance with his friend, but I declined. Later that night, that same guy ended up dancing with all of us when we decided to go to the dance floor. To make a long story short, he made inappropriate physical contact by putting his butt on my private area. When my ex asked me if I went to the bar, I forgot to mention this incident due to my heightened emotional state. Now, everyone is advising me not to mention it, but I feel guilty and like I'm lying. I'm afraid my ex will be extremely mad if he ever finds out, as he has jealousy and trust issues. Should I feel guilty? What should I do?

It sounds like your friend is experiencing a very difficult and abusive situation at home. It's important to remember that violence is never okay, and it's not normal for someone to hit their partner. It's concerning to hear that her father has been hitting her for years and that she's been keeping this secret. It's understandable that she feels scared and confused about why this is happening. It's also concerning that her parents sent her to a psych ward when she tried to speak up about the abuse. Is she receiving any support or counseling for what she's going through?

Patient: For over a year now, I've been in a long distance relationship with a man who is controlling and emotionally abusive. It's only recently that I've started to realize this. From the beginning, I've felt increasingly stressed and afraid of doing something wrong, which has caused a significant decrease in my self-confidence. He constantly criticizes me, and I have to be extremely careful with my words, or else he will stop talking to me or become angry. I often don't even know what sets him off, and he refuses to speak to me about it. Recently, I've been making a lot of effort to visit him, which costs me both money and time. However, when he had the opportunity to be near me for work, he didn't want to come to my place or let me visit him. We exchanged text messages about it, but he never gave me a clear reason for his behavior. At one point, he even asked for permission to go out and not see me, which hurt me deeply. He broke up with me over a text message, but then took it back the next day, and we're still together. The problem is, I can't seem to forget what happened. We normally have to travel far to see each other, and I'm the one putting in the most effort. I don't think he doesn't care about me, as he talks about wanting to stay together and even moving to my country for me. But I can't make sense of his actions. I want to understand, but I'm afraid that discussing it with him will lead to a conflict or him shutting down again. How can I get over this? Should I talk to him? And if so, how can I bring it up without triggering his anger or silence? I really need closure and to understand why he did what he did, especially if he loves me.

I've been struggling with expressing myself effectively and it's affecting my relationships. I also suspect I may have Schizo-Effective disorder, as my mother has bipolar disorder. I get easily frustrated when others don't take responsibility or maintain structure. Trust is important to me, and it hurts when people don't take me seriously. I feel alone and need guidance on how to navigate these challenges, especially in my relationship where my girlfriend seems distant.

I’m 34 and have been struggling with a lot of issues lately. The main concern right now is that I have been feeling suicidal, but I can't act on those thoughts because I have a child to take care of. I recently found a counselor and I am also considering seeing a psychiatrist for additional support. However, I'm worried about how open I can be with them because I don't want to be hospitalized in a psychiatric ward.

I'm really concerned about my mother-in-law's behavior when she drinks alcohol. It's like she completely changes and becomes a different person.
