It's causing a lot of tension in our family, with my mom constantly trying to keep the peace and blaming herself, and my dad getting upset because my mom and brother are hostile toward him due to unresolved issues.

Lately, I've been struggling with my behavior and it's causing problems in different areas of my life. It's impacting my performance at school, work, home, and even socially. I feel overwhelmed and recognize the need for help. I apologize for the lengthy and disorganized post. Allow me to briefly outline my issues.

Sometimes, I question whether my parents truly love me. I know they are good people, and they say they love me, but in certain moments, it feels like they don't. I wonder if this is just a normal part of being a teenager, or if it's a sign of a deeper psychological issue. Even when there is evidence that my family does love me, it's hard to shake the feeling that they don't.

Hi, I'm 14 years old and I've been feeling really depressed lately. I have thoughts of suicide almost every night, even during the day. I've been struggling with self-harm for the past two years. I believe I have severe depression, borderline personality disorder, and anxiety. I also think I might be bipolar, but my mom doesn't believe me when I try to talk to her about it. My parents can be really harsh with me, and it's making me feel like I have no reason to live. I just wish someone would take me seriously and listen to what I'm going through. I've noticed that I have anger issues too, sometimes I punch walls or take out my anger on people and my cat, which makes me feel guilty afterwards. I don't want to hurt my friends or my pet, but I do yell and say mean things. I just hate myself and I feel like such a failure. I'm scared, depressed, and I don't know if I can go on. I do have a therapist, but I feel like she doesn't really listen to me. I don't know, maybe it's pointless. I'm considering ending my life within the next three months. I have plans, but I'm also worried about vomiting up the pills if I choose that method. I hope someone here will listen to me and take me seriously. I'm not kidding, I mean it.

I just found out my mom has been cheating on my father. I am not totally surprised because she has been acting sneaky the past year or so, but I am devastated. I love my dad, he is so good to my mother and he doesn’t deserve to be treated this way. I think she’s going through her midlife crisis. I hate the person she’s becoming, I don’t even know her anymore. I have no respect for cheaters and I want my mom to be someone I respect and look up to.

I'm an 18-year-old who has been questioning my sexual orientation lately. I find myself physically attracted to other males, but the idea of having sex with another male doesn't appeal to me. Emotionally, I also feel uncomfortable with the idea of loving another male. I have male friends, but I don't feel attracted to any of them, which makes me wonder if I'm not gay. On the other hand, I do find women somewhat attractive, kissing a girl arouses me to some extent, and the thought of being in an emotional relationship with a woman is appealing to me.

I have been feeling really anxious and scared lately. About 2.5 months ago, one of my relatives was diagnosed with schizophrenia during a psychotic episode. As a member of the family, I heard about all the symptoms she experienced, especially the ones that involved hearing voices and feeling like someone was watching her. These symptoms have been really frightening for me and I can't stop thinking about them.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for almost 2 years now. We also have a 4-month-old child together, and I have another child from a previous relationship. I have caught my boyfriend lying to me about talking to other women in the past, and even though he claims he has been truthful, I still struggle to fully trust him. I also feel like there have been instances where other women have made advances towards him, and he should have immediately shut them down and defended our relationship. For example, when a girl suggested hanging out when I go to sleep and he declined because of work.

I recently took some tests and it seems that I might fall into the category of intermediate schizoid. I still live at home with my parents, and whenever I try to bring this up with them, they avoid the topic. They just don't understand why I can't simply ignore it or control my emotions. I think they are afraid of something being wrong with their daughter, so they are resistant to the idea of counseling or therapy. Honestly, I'm a bit scared myself. I fear that seeking help could have a negative impact on my life. On the outside, I appear to be a successful student with a 4.0 GPA and I'm an accomplished musician. People generally don't think there is anything wrong with me, except for the fact that I don't enjoy socializing.

I've been experiencing a lot of emotional pain lately. Sometimes I feel empty and numb, and at other times, I feel overwhelmed with panic and frustration. I also have physical symptoms like shooting pains in my heart and a racing heartbeat. The issue I'm facing is that I'm hesitant to share my feelings with others because I'm worried it might upset or worry them. It's especially difficult for me to open up to my parents because I love them so much, and I don't want to burden them with my struggles, especially considering their own battles with alcohol and depression. I am currently seeing a therapist, but I find it hard to talk about these intense feelings of sadness, self-hatred, and guilt. I've tried reaching out to friends, but they don't seem to fully understand the extent of what I'm going through. In fact, I had a breakdown in front of a few friends, and it made them uncomfortable and unsure of how to help. Their advice of having a more positive attitude and assuming that everyone feels down sometimes wasn't very useful. I feel incredibly isolated and burdened by guilt. I don't want to cause my loved ones any pain, but I'm at a loss for what to do. Suicide often feels like my only option. Please, I really need help.

Hi, I'm a 25-year-old woman who has been struggling with sexual intimacy. I have only been sexually active with my ex-fiance, whom I was with for 5 years. Every time we got close to having sex, I would tense up and make it impossible. This also happens when I visit the gynecologist and I can't even use tampons. I want to overcome this issue because I want to be able to have a healthy sex life, get married, and have kids. I believe my ex-fiance left me because of this. Can you please help me?

I have some concerns about my brother's recent behavior. He has a history of taking Concerta for ADHD but has been on and off it for the past few years. He recently restarted Concerta at a higher dose and experienced mood swings. One day, he took the medication before bed and then took it again later when he felt it wasn't working. This led to him behaving strangely, hallucinating, and even becoming aggressive towards our father. He was taken to the psychiatric ward and we noticed other odd behaviors, such as confusion, forgetfulness, and talking about unreal things. He has also shown aggression in the past. Additionally, he has recently changed his social behavior and become more interested in religion. I'm wondering if there could be another diagnosis besides ADHD, like multiple personality disorder or bipolar disorder. Please help me understand what could be going on.

Over the past few years, I have noticed that my social awkwardness has intensified into a severe phobia. Additionally, I have gained almost 60 pounds in the last two years due to stress-induced overeating. My parents constantly belittle me and express doubts about my future prospects. As the oldest of my three siblings, I have always felt like a failure in their eyes. With graduation just a month away, the pressure is mounting as my parents want me out of the house as soon as possible. I feel lost and overwhelmed, and thoughts of suicide have started creeping in. Some of my relatives suggested joining the military, but my weight gain has made that impossible, and I question my ability to handle the stress. I don't know what to do anymore, and I don't want to be around my parents. Can you please guide me?

I'm really concerned about my fiancee's behavior. We seem to have fights every other day, and he goes from being happy to hating the world for no reason. Whenever I try to discuss our issues, he quickly comes up with excuses like physical pain or vomiting. I've never witnessed him vomiting and I'm always around. He also puts words in my mouth and tries to push me away. Sometimes I find him curled up in a corner, even at night. I think he's doing it for attention. He tells me to leave him, but I'm not unhappy. He refuses to seek help, and I'm at a loss. I don't want to leave him. Today he told me to leave because he thinks I'll be happier. He wouldn't talk to me, returned my things, and sent me an irrational message. He now claims he was in a lot of pain and disoriented, but this happens frequently. I don't know what to do anymore. (His sister has bipolar disorder).

This week, on Thursday, my boyfriend and I had a conversation where he mentioned needing a break but still wanting to be my boyfriend. Later on, he confessed to liking another girl and wanting a break, which left me feeling confused, angry, and hurt. In my upset state, I retaliated by saying I liked someone else, someone my boyfriend doesn't like, and I noticed that it upset him. However, I later explained to my friends that I was just angry and didn't mean what I said.

I've been feeling really neglected in my relationship lately. My fiancée and I have been together for 5 years and have an 18-month-old daughter. I'm an at-home mom, and my partner is always busy with work or projects. I've tried talking to him about how lonely and sad I've been feeling, but he always brushes it off and says he has too much to do.

I'm feeling really overwhelmed and confused right now. My husband and I have been having a lot of relationship issues, and it's gotten to the point where we're discussing the possibility of separating or getting a divorce. About seven months after we got married, I discovered that he was having an affair with his ex. When I confronted him, he blamed me and treated me very harshly. We decided to stay together, but he never really addressed his infidelity, which has caused me a lot of pain and confusion for the past eight years. A month ago, I reached a breaking point and I just needed him to be honest with me. He admitted to some things, including having an affair with the same woman a year before we got married when we were already having problems. I had suspected this for nine years, but he always denied it and made me feel terrible for even thinking it. The constant lying and betrayal, coupled with our strained sex life, has left me feeling lost and scared.

It seems like my dad is overly concerned about me having a boyfriend. Every time we see each other, he immediately asks if any guys are chasing me. I'm currently a sophomore in college and haven't been in a relationship since my junior year of high school. While I'm content with being single, it would be nice to have a boyfriend. However, my dad's constant questioning makes me feel like he believes there's something wrong with my personality and that I have to rely on my looks to attract a partner.

I've been experiencing a resurgence of hallucinations lately, and it's really taking a toll on me. Whenever I feel stressed, my symptoms seem to worsen. I've been seeing two little girls playing outside my door, but I can't shake the feeling that there's something sinister about them. Every little sound out of place fills me with fear and makes me jumpy. My thoughts feel scattered and chaotic, like a blender on high speed. It's as if I constantly have this impending sense of doom looming over me.

I am a 47-year-old woman who is currently in a primary relationship with a 66-year-old man. We have been together for three years and he is a very kind and loving person. However, I can't help but feel some concern or hesitation. Is there something I should be worried about?

I have been in an on-and-off relationship with my boyfriend for almost 3 years. Most of the time, we have a loving and positive relationship. However, there are periods of extreme difficulty triggered by his stress level surrounding change or physical discomfort. His behavior becomes explosive, he becomes excessively critical, and he often blames me for everything. It's especially challenging because when I try to address it, he either denies it or dismisses it. It's really starting to take a toll on me.

My husband and I started our relationship in February 2010 and got married in April 2011. However, our marriage has been challenging because he lives in Portsmouth for work while I am still in another city. I am planning to move to Portsmouth in September when I turn 18, as he is 19. Recently, he has been distant and stopped communicating with me for several days, only to call without explaining what's wrong.

Counselor's response: It sounds like you've been through a lot in your relationship. It's important to recognize that trust and communication are key components in any healthy relationship. It seems like there have been some challenges in building trust between you and your boyfriend due to the past incidents of keeping in touch with your ex-boyfriends without informing him. It's understandable that he may have felt hurt and betrayed by this discovery. However, it's also important for him to be able to trust and believe you when you say that nothing inappropriate was happening.

Today, I had a realization that I have developed a significant fear of men. This fear seems to arise specifically when I consider the possibility of being involved in a romantic relationship with a man. This fear has been present since I was a child, as my family enforced strict rules against interacting with men. Even now, I feel hesitant to inform my father if there will be boys present at school events or social gatherings. Unlike me, my younger sister doesn't seem to have any difficulties conversing with boys, possibly due to her physical appearance. While I can engage with men in a professional setting, I struggle to have casual conversations that extend beyond academic topics. Making eye contact is particularly challenging for me, and it significantly affects my ability to interact with men in a normal and comfortable manner.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for 8 months. He has a history of a difficult childhood and teenage years, including abuse, substance use, and mental health challenges. He was diagnosed with manic depression and schizophrenia at a young age but no longer takes medication. Recently, he went through a tough breakup after a 7-year relationship. We started as friends when we worked together, and I was in a relationship with someone who was dishonest and involved in illegal activities. Despite my boyfriend's troubled past, he has made positive changes in his life. He currently lives with his mother and supports her financially. Our relationship progressed quickly, but he has expressed that it scared him. He also has a high sex drive, which I wonder if it's related to his schizophrenia. He displays signs of paranoia and insecurity. Recently, he confessed to cheating on me with an old childhood friend who just ended a long-term relationship. He claims to feel guilty but is unsure why he did it or why he has been questioning our relationship. He says he loves me and wants to be with me, but I'm confused about his behavior. I have been loyal and supportive, and he was a great partner until recently. Given his past and responsibilities, I'm unsure if I should give him another chance.

I'm a 14-year-old boy and recently my dad decided to move in with his girlfriend and her kids. I don't get along with them and I feel unwanted when I'm around them. My dad wants me to live with my grandparents now and it feels like he's choosing them over me. He doesn't seem interested in anything I do, like my recent improvement in school. He only talks about moving in and how happy he'll be without me. What should I do?

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for almost three years now. Overall, we have a great connection and are very supportive of each other. However, recently our relationship has hit a rough patch. My boyfriend has been using marijuana on a daily basis, which doesn't personally bother me, but I have concerns about his occasional cocaine use. He has reassured me that he and his friends are responsible with it, but I'm starting to worry about the potential dangers and how it could affect our relationship.

Hello, I'm seeking some guidance. I am a 48-year-old married man with children. Throughout my life, I've experienced some level of anxiety, but recently it has intensified due to several stressors. I have a particular fear of hazardous materials, especially asbestos and the diseases it can cause. This fear has become more prominent in my mind, especially when I worry about my family being exposed as well. Although I've had this fear to a lesser extent in the past, it seems to have reached its peak now.

For as long as I can remember, I have been dealing with severe anxiety. It manifests as social anxiety, but my main source of worry is my health. It feels like I can't do anything without fearing that something terrible will happen to me. Just the other day, my family and I went to Disneyland, and I had multiple panic attacks, fearing that I would suddenly drop dead or have a brain aneurysm because of a minor headache I had that day. It's a constant cycle of health-related worries that drains me. All I want to do is sleep or numb myself with TV so I can escape these thoughts.

Over the past month, I have been staying at my mom's house while searching for a new place to live. During this time, I've had two incidents where I noticed someone attempting to look into my bathroom window as I was getting out of the shower. I couldn't see them clearly, but I recently found out that it was my step-brother. He had moved away for work and has been dealing with a lot of anxiety. He reached out to me on Facebook, apologizing for his actions and expressing feelings of shame, guilt, and worry that I might hate him. I reassured him that I don't hate him, but I found his behavior strange because we are like siblings. I also let him know that he can talk to me if he needs to. I'm unsure if I handled this situation appropriately, and I'm curious about his behavior. I don't want to involve our parents since we're both in our 20s, and I don't want to create awkwardness in the future. I know he's not a threat to me; he's just a shy person who struggles to communicate with girls.

I have been experiencing symptoms that align with schizophrenia. It began in high school, where I constantly felt paranoid and believed that people were talking about me behind my back. As a result, I became very isolated and noticed that others tended to avoid me. I also developed severe stage fright, which is strange because I used to be outgoing and enjoyed public speaking as a child. In college, my anxiety around presentations became so severe that I would skip classes that required them. It's not just normal nervousness, I become terrified and even experience physical symptoms like diarrhea. Once the day of the presentation passes, I feel a huge sense of relief.

Ever since my brother was diagnosed with Bipolar Disorder, Asperger's Syndrome, Attention Deficit Disorder (ADD), and Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD) when I was 12, our relationship has been challenging. He tends to be verbally abusive and occasionally violent towards me and our younger brother, although he has never seriously harmed us. Despite being on medication for years, I still feel scared around him. Additionally, it's frustrating to witness the special treatment he receives and constantly be expected to act maturely, which then triggers feelings of guilt. I have attempted to discuss my emotions with my parents, but my mom dismisses my concerns with a "You have to understand" response that makes me feel unheard, while my dad uses the conversation as an opportunity to lecture me about my own mistakes, shifting the blame onto me.

About 4 years ago, I was diagnosed with dysthymia, major depression, and post-traumatic stress disorder. Shortly after my diagnosis, my mother left. She was abusive, and she influenced my father to be abusive as well. I now spend most of my free time with my grandmother, who lives 25 miles away. As a blind individual, I rely on taxis or someone driving me to her house. However, when I talk to my grandmother about my mental health issues, she often dismisses them and doesn't seem to understand. She tends to be judgmental and opinionated, which triggers me. For instance, she believes that I can simply "get over" dysthymia because she overcame her own major depressive episode. Despite my attempts to explain what my doctors have told me, she disregards their expertise and views my mental health diagnoses as just a passing trend in medicine. Although she is the only family member who genuinely cares about my well-being, I struggle to communicate my feelings to her. I wonder if she talks negatively about me to her friend who also has dysthymia and major depressive disorder, as she often complains about her friend's negativity when she's not around. When I ask her directly, she denies it, but I'm skeptical. Is there a way I can help her understand that my illnesses are real and won't just disappear or be overcome through sheer willpower?

I recently had an evaluation with a psychologist who diagnosed me with paranoid personality disorder and schizotypal personality disorder. Throughout my life, I have consistently faced challenges in fitting into society and have experienced depression from a young age. Additionally, I have struggled with body dysmorphia, eating disorders, and social anxiety disorder, among other issues.

I've been experiencing a lot of anxiety and depression lately, to the point where it's affecting my ability to function. I've been able to hold onto my job, but that's about all I can manage. I'm also trying to repair my relationship with my best friend, who means a lot to me like a sister. Unfortunately, I tend to isolate myself for long periods of time, unintentionally, when I'm feeling overwhelmed. Today, I had a particularly intense episode of anxiety at work, to the point where I thought I might have a panic attack.

I've been experiencing some symptoms that are really scaring me. I'm worried that I might have schizophrenia. About two months ago, at the start of the semester, I smoked really strong marijuana (hydro). Before that, I had only smoked milder forms and not very often.

Lately, I've been feeling really hurt and betrayed by my best friend. She has been living with me because her home situation is not ideal. However, she has been lying to me and treating me poorly, all because she is in a new relationship. Just recently, I discovered some terrible things she said about me to her boyfriend, including personal secrets I entrusted her with. These hurtful words, combined with being constantly called ugly by others, have made me question my self-worth. I struggle with social anxiety and constantly worry that people are talking about me behind my back. I spend a lot of time online because my role-play friends are the only ones I feel close to. My best friend and I have been close for many years, but this recent behavior has made me feel like I've lost everything. I've even had thoughts of suicide, although I could never go through with it because I love my family too much. I don't engage in typical teenage activities and I'm homeschooled, which makes my social anxiety worse. I just want to feel pretty and accepted, but I feel like I don't belong anywhere.

For the past four years, I've been struggling with a growing fascination with videos about humiliation and slavery that I stumbled upon online. At first, I didn't like them, but over time, this interest has grown within me.

As a senior in high school, graduation is approaching and I'm feeling a sense of unease in my household. Despite being the oldest, I don't feel like I'm treated equally. My younger cousin recently got his license, a car, and a job, while I have none of those things. Whenever I try to discuss this with my family, they brush it off and say "maybe later." It feels like favoritism. I find it hard to communicate in this environment because no one seems to listen or care about what I have to say. I rely on religion for some solace, but I need someone to talk to. My other cousin, who I'm closer to, is going through similar problems with his girlfriend. I've tried confiding in others, but they either don't understand or can't provide the support I need. My stepmom is a major source of frustration as she treats everyone else with smiles and laughter, but becomes negative and dismissive towards me. It's both irritating and saddening. Today, I wanted to confront her about it, but my aunt advised me to respect it and hold back to avoid making things worse. I don't feel comfortable talking to my stepmom because I don't think she will listen. What should I do? I need help!

Throughout my entire life, I have had the ability to perceive and communicate with spirits. I also have a deep understanding of Pagan beliefs and have had encounters with what I believe to be a divine entity. Some individuals have been able to validate the information I have shared with them. However, I am a young adult and have been experiencing these phenomena for as long as I can remember. Should I be concerned about this? I am not fearful of anything beyond the spiritual realm, and I consider myself to be intellectually gifted and socially adept.

In 2010, I started seeing a therapist for my anxiety and depression. I went for about six months and she diagnosed me with OCD, Depression, Generalized Anxiety Disorder, Avoidant Personality Disorder, and Dependent Personality Disorder. I felt like I was functioning better after seeing her. However, when I became pregnant, I stopped going to therapy. During my pregnancy, my husband was deployed and didn't return home until our daughter was four months old. Our marriage was perfect before the deployment, but now I feel like I've become more depressed, anxious, and angry. I don't even want to get out of bed in the morning to take care of our daughter. It's affecting our marriage, my weight, and our child. I feel like I can't talk to anyone about it without getting dismissed. My husband thinks I have resentment. I get so angry that I yell, throw things, and even hit my husband. Other times, I get so depressed that I neglect my responsibilities. I desperately need help, but I'm anxious about going back to therapy with a seven-month-old child. I just want to regain control of my relationships, life, and sanity.

My wife and I have been married for five years and have a one-year-old son. About two and a half years ago, she started experiencing symptoms of depression, which led her to seek therapy. She has been attending counseling sessions and taking medication for PTSD, stemming from an abusive relationship with her mother. However, I've noticed some concerning behaviors recently. For instance, she has been secretive about her therapy sessions and has forwarded antagonistic emails, supposedly from family members, to her therapist through our joint email account. She has also asked me to forge her mother's signature on a letter without letting me see its contents before taking it to her therapist.

I have been experiencing some distressing symptoms that I can't fully understand. There are times when I feel frustrated because my thoughts seem out of control. I often get stressed when I have disturbing thoughts, like saying hurtful things about people in my mind, even though I don't mean them. It's as if my brain is daring me to think these awful things, and it makes me feel really sad. I try to distract myself by singing a song or thinking about something else, but it doesn't always help. Additionally, I've noticed some mild tics throughout my life, but they seem to be getting worse lately and I'm not sure why. I couldn't find any answers during my own research.

I recently came across the term "trichotillomania" while reading one of my client's profiles, so I decided to look it up. Now, I'm bothered by it because it reminds me of my own experiences. When I was younger, my parents would constantly scold me for pulling my hair. Even now, at 30 years old, I catch myself doing it unconsciously. Overall, I consider myself a happy and laid back person. I've been married for 5 and a half years and have a 3-year-old son. Although I don't have any noticeable bald patches, I can tell that one area of my scalp is thinner compared to the side where I don't pull my hair. I do remember having less hair in that same area when I was younger.

Hi, I'm a freshman in high school and I've been struggling lately. I find it really difficult to motivate myself to go to school. I don't have any issues with bullying and I have a good group of friends, but I feel overwhelmed and stressed out. Because of my lack of attendance, I'm falling behind in my classes. When I come home, I'm mentally exhausted and I can't bring myself to do my homework. It's hard for me to concentrate at school and I feel anxious and upset when I think about going.

Patient: Lately, I've been thinking a lot about whether or not I have an anxiety disorder. After my friend opened up about her own struggles, I started taking online quizzes and reading about anxiety. It seems like it could explain everything I've been feeling. I mentioned it to a few friends, but I find it really difficult to talk about. I can't even imagine how hard it would be to tell my parents. I'm already a quiet person and tend to keep things to myself. I know things could improve if I talked to them, but I just can't bring myself to do it. I've thought about seeing a counselor at school, but I usually try to handle things on my own. I really want to know if I have an anxiety disorder, but the only way to find out is by telling my parents so they can take me to a doctor. I can't go by myself. Do you have any suggestions on how to make it easier to talk to my parents about this? I know they would understand, but it's just really difficult for me to open up to them. Thanks for your help.

I am a 26-year-old individual who has accomplished a lot academically, obtaining a law degree as well as bachelor's degrees in mathematics and psychology. Currently, I am pursuing medical school prerequisites. However, despite my achievements, I am struggling with a lack of clarity regarding my future path. I tend to enter new endeavors, such as law school, only to feel immediate regret and the need to search for something else. This uncertainty is causing me stress, especially considering my responsibilities as a 26-year-old parent with mounting debt. I would love to choose a career or pursue graduate school with confidence, but I am feeling lost and unsure. I recognize that I need guidance and support in figuring out my next steps.

My adult son has a history of severe ADHD and rapid cycling bipolar disorder. Over the past year, he started using methamphetamine and has been experiencing constant delusions. He often texts me, and his latest delusion is that I am a member of a secret organization withholding a large trust fund from him. He has become threatening in his messages, demanding the money/password or else. I've told him he's delusional and that I won't respond as long as he continues to be aggressive. However, I'm unsure of how to respond to his delusions in general, even when they shift. Yesterday, he claimed to be working for central intelligence. I suspect his grandiose delusions are related to his manic episodes from childhood. He stopped taking medication at 18 and his meth use has worsened over the past three years. He is resistant to help and functional enough to avoid involuntary commitment. Any advice on how to communicate with him would be greatly appreciated.

Hi, I have been in a relationship with my fiance for five years, and recently another person has entered her life. She spent the whole night with him in a vehicle and then at his house without informing me. She initially saw him as a friend, but now she says there are deeper feelings involved. She claims to love him as much as she loves me. We currently live together with my mom and all of her animals, which I helped her acquire. She seems torn between deciding who she wants to be with. I'm concerned that she might only be staying with me because she has nowhere else to go with her animals. How can I be sure of her true intentions?

Counselor: Thank you for sharing your experiences with me. It sounds like you've had some difficult and confusing situations in your past, particularly with animals. It's important to recognize that hurting animals is not a healthy or normal behavior. It's understandable that you're questioning if there may be something deeper going on.

It seems like I've gone through a lot of difficulties recently. I come from a middle-class background and had a promising start at my dream school, but financial issues forced me to leave. Since then, I've been struggling to make ends meet, feeling isolated from my friends, and even resorted to desperate measures like stealing food and engaging in transactional relationships. I've become really good at separating these different aspects of my life.

During high school, when I was 15, I faced a lot of teasing and mockery from my peers because I was not knowledgeable about sex. In my school club, we have mentors who are not affiliated with the school system. I formed a close bond with one of the outside mentors, who is 30 years old, and we became friends on Facebook. He knew about the teasing and offered to teach me about sex. I thought it was a special opportunity and allowed him to "teach" me over Skype. It wasn't until my best friend intervened and made sure he couldn't contact me again that I realized I was being manipulated. I can't help feeling stupid for what happened and I can't talk to my parents or seek counseling because of my age and insurance. Is there anything I can do to find peace and move on from this?

Patient: I've been struggling with depression since I was 9 years old, but I didn't fully understand it until recently. It's been getting worse and it's impacting my ability to live a normal life. I isolate myself in my room and avoid going out, which is starting to bother my family. They want to help me by getting me a job at a pub, but it's way out of my comfort zone and it's adding to the pressure I already feel. They think I can just help myself, but I know I can't do it alone. I haven't seen a doctor yet, but I took an online test that indicated I have major depression. I tried telling my mom, but she seems to ignore it and thinks it will just go away on its own. I feel frustrated and useless. How can I make my family understand what I'm going through?

I recently discovered that my mother-in-law has strong negative feelings towards me, which came as a surprise because she always seemed kind and friendly. I have tried to connect with her, but she shows no interest in being involved in our lives. I found an email where she criticized me, which was heartbreaking. I wrote her a letter explaining my confusion and willingness to talk, but she has not responded or shown any sign of wanting to reconcile. This situation has strained her relationship with my husband, and I feel sad for him. Is there anything we can do to improve the situation and help her see that I am not a bad person?

Patient: I'm 17 years old and I've been feeling really down lately. I think I might be depressed, but I'm really shy and scared to talk to anyone about it. It's been months since I mustered up the courage to reach out and I'm shaking right now because I'm so ashamed.

I am a 19-year-old university student who comes from a supportive family and lives in a comfortable home. However, despite these positive aspects of my life, I feel a deep sense of unhappiness. I have a low opinion of myself, believing that I am ugly and worthless. In high school, I was bullied because of my appearance, and when I tried to seek help, I was dismissed. A few years ago, I even contemplated ending my life, but I managed to talk myself out of it. Though I no longer cry for hours every night, I find myself feeling numb and uninterested in life. I just want to reclaim the joy I used to feel and stop caring about others' opinions. I'm lost and don't know what to do anymore.

I've been in a relationship with someone for over two months now and we've been through a lot together. The problem is that my family has certain expectations for who I should date, and my boyfriend doesn't fit those expectations. They also have concerns about his substance use and mental health, particularly after a recent incident where he attempted suicide. I love him and want to support him, but my family is pressuring me to leave him. What should I do?

I am a 23-year-old female who has been struggling with a pattern of risky sexual behavior since the age of fifteen. I have engaged in multiple sexual encounters in one night, often without protection, and have experienced feelings of guilt afterwards. At the age of 18, I was involved in a legal incident related to underage sexual activity. Even while in a relationship and now marriage, I have compulsively cheated on my partner. Recently, I have been fixated on searching personal ads online for sexual encounters, despite knowing I wouldn't actually engage in them. This addiction to browsing personal ads is causing distress in my relationship, as my husband initially expressed openness but later expressed discomfort with the idea. Additionally, I have become dependent on having sex with my husband every day before bed, to the point where I cannot sleep without it and become angry and upset if it doesn't happen. This has caused strain in our relationship and affected my husband's self-esteem. I feel guilty about my demands and the impact it has on our ability to have a healthy and enjoyable sex life. I am seeking help and support to address these issues.

I've noticed a recurring pattern in my relationships where I become deeply attached to someone very quickly, even after just a few conversations. It's like I fall in love with them emotionally and sexually. This has happened multiple times and it's really troubling because I feel heartbroken when I can't pursue a romantic relationship with them. I recently ended a two-year relationship and this attachment issue has resurfaced. It's confusing because my life is fairly normal and I don't feel outcast or ignored. I'm struggling to understand why this happens. Can you help?

Over the past year, I've noticed a significant change in my behavior towards spending time with others. Despite not having any diagnosed disorders like depression or anxiety, I find myself becoming more rigid and avoiding social interactions. This is negatively impacting my relationships, even though I still desire affection, friendship, and intimacy, but only in limited amounts. For example, I struggle to spend extended time with my girlfriend and end up counting the minutes until she leaves. I feel guilty for being this way and wonder if I should even be in a relationship. Any insight would be appreciated.

I've noticed that I have issues with anger management. Whenever I get angry, I completely explode and everything I've been holding in suddenly comes out. For example, when I have fights with my boyfriend or feel jealous, I have thoughts of physically harming both him and myself, although I've never acted on them. I also become more vicious and take out my anger on everyone when I'm repenting for something and can't express it. In general, if I can't handle my emotions, I get very angry. When I'm angry, my hands start shaking nervously and the veins on top of them pop. My anxiety becomes unbearable, I have shortness of breath, I begin to cry, and I feel nauseous. As a result, I lose control and start throwing things, breaking them. I've been wondering if this may be connected to my childhood, as my father had similar anger issues and I could never express my feelings until I would have outbursts.

I’m a 60-year-old widowed female who has no children and very little family left. Over the past 15 years, I had a small but tight-knit group of friends. Unfortunately, one by one, they have all moved away. It has become increasingly difficult for me to trust and allow people to get close to me now.

I'm a 17-year-old who lost my father when I was around 15 or 14. He had been battling cancer for several years, so his death wasn't entirely unexpected. However, I didn't have a close relationship with him, and I don't have many memories of our time together. When he passed away, I was shocked, but I didn't feel particularly sad.

I've been struggling with depression and self-harm for several years now. Lately, my anxiety has become overwhelming and it's affecting my ability to go to school. My parents don't seem to understand the severity of my situation and just tell me to be strong. I see a psychologist and psychiatrist, and I'm currently on antidepressants. However, I'm still feeling overwhelmed and I'm not sure how to ask for additional help. Should I consider going to a mental hospital?

I am a 52-year-old man from Romania who recently experienced a painful breakup. After six years together, my girlfriend left me for someone else. I am finding it extremely difficult to accept this truth and continue to love her. I am feeling physically and emotionally unwell, experiencing frequent crying spells, anxiety in my limbs, and a deep sadness in my face. It seems like she will never come back to me, especially now that she is with a new man who has more financial stability and helped her open a fashion magazine. I feel like my whole life was centered around her and now that she's gone, I feel lost and lonely in a new town where I've lived for only a short time. I've been taking three amitriptyline tablets a day to try and manage my sadness and anxiety, but I still feel overwhelmed. I can't control my thoughts, which are consumed by this situation, and I feel myself sinking deeper into despair. I made a regrettable decision to be in this unhappy relationship and now I need help finding a way out of this situation. I would greatly appreciate some kind words and guidance on how to move forward.

About a year ago, I experienced a devastating loss when my father died by suicide. Our relationship had its ups and downs, particularly during my high school years, and we were not on speaking terms for two months prior to his death. The circumstances surrounding his death were extremely painful, as his family blamed me and I was not allowed to attend his funeral. I still don't know where he's buried. Over the past year, I have noticed a significant decline in my mental health. Everyday stresses became overwhelming to the point where I had to quit my job. This has now led to a deep depression, which is also impacting my three-year relationship. Unfortunately, I no longer have insurance and financial constraints are making it difficult for me to seek help. I have looked into free mental health care options, but haven't had any luck. I'm feeling lost and in need of guidance and possible solutions to address these challenges.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend, Bob, since July 2011. However, I am constantly worried that he is cheating on me, especially since he has a history of cheating in past relationships. I even had a couple of threesomes with him and another friend in the hopes that it would prevent him from cheating on me. Despite his actions, I still love him deeply. I'm not sure if I should give up on the relationship or keep working on it. What should I do?

I've been struggling with sleep issues since I was in year 5, and it's really starting to affect me. I feel like I'm going crazy and I haven't told anyone about it. The lack of sleep is causing me to feel more stressed and tired all the time. I also never have dreams and I can't figure out why this is happening for such a long time.

I've been in a relationship with my fiancée for three years, and it started off really well. However, recently I discovered that he has been having relationships with prostitutes and even slept with one of my friends and another woman. I feel deeply hurt and betrayed, and it's affecting every aspect of my life. I've been feeling very depressed and have even had thoughts of ending my life. I'm struggling at work, finding it hard to concentrate, and I feel isolated from my friends and family. I feel trapped in this relationship, even though he has shown some aggression towards me. I don't know what to do.

Lately, I've been experiencing some disturbing thoughts about hurting others. It's not specific to anyone in particular, but the idea of causing harm is consuming my mind. I've even started planning what my first act might be, and it feels like I'm losing control. I've always presented myself as a good person, but deep down, I don't feel empathy or connection with anyone. The only time I feel anything is when I think about someone dying. I've had an experience in the past where I didn't intervene to prevent someone from taking their own life, and now I find myself drawn to that feeling again. I'm unsure if I actually want to stop myself, but just in case I do, is there a way to address these thoughts? Or have I reached a point of no return?

I am reaching out because I am currently unable to see a therapist, but I am going through a difficult time in my life. For the past week and a half, I have been feeling extremely depressed. While I have experienced bouts of depression before, this time it feels more severe and I am starting to question my mental well-being, especially as I prepare to leave home in a few months. Normally, I am a motivated and talkative person who enjoys being active and silly. However, lately, I have been experiencing frequent mood swings, feeling angry or tearful. I used to attribute these mood swings to my menstrual cycle, but lately, they have been persistent regardless of the time of the month. I have been trying various activities to cheer myself up, but nothing seems to shake off this depression. I feel like I am in a constant battle with myself, and it's only getting worse. All I want to do is sleep and listen to music, and I find it difficult to open up to my mom about it. The only person I have talked to is my friend. I usually put on a brave face because I don't like people knowing that I'm not feeling well, but my mom can tell that something is off. I have been neglecting my usual responsibilities, and it frustrates me to see myself slacking. Part of me thinks that it's all in my head, but another part of me believes that something is genuinely wrong. While I wouldn't say that I have had thoughts of death, I do find ways to rationalize why I shouldn't act on those thoughts. However, I worry about how much worse things could get before I reach a breaking point. It's worth noting that my underactive thyroid and history of frequent illnesses may not be helping the situation, although I am currently in good physical health and taking all the necessary supplements. Additionally, my home life is stressful, as my dad is sociopathic and has not shown any willingness to change despite seeing multiple therapists. Ultimately, I just want to move forward in life. I apologize if my thoughts are scattered, but any insight would be greatly appreciated.

I have been struggling with extreme jealousy and insecurity in my relationship. I don't allow my fiancé to talk to other women, and I am not allowed to talk to other men either. I constantly worry that he is attracted to other women and that he finds them more attractive than me. Even if he simply looks at other women while we're out, it triggers my jealousy. I have even gone as far as restricting what movies he can watch if they have women in them, unless I am present. I get jealous even if he mentions my best friend's name. I know that men are naturally attracted to other women, but it drives me to the point of feeling suicidal if he finds someone else attractive. I feel like he would be better off with someone else because of my behavior. We have been together since we were 12, and he is all I have ever known. I am 16 now and I recognize that I need counseling, but I am a minor and I don't have parents to help me access it. I am not afraid of him cheating or leaving me because I know he loves me, but it hurts me deeply to know that he has seen other women naked and may find them attractive. I understand that this issue is rooted in my self-esteem and I really want to learn how to love myself. I don't want this to continue damaging our relationship, and it breaks my heart to even talk about it. All I want is for him to love me and find me beautiful. I wish he had never seen any other attractive woman.

Patient: "I was diagnosed with schizoaffective disorder when I was 15 years old. Now I am 21, but I had already been experiencing psychotic features before that age. I'm trying to make sense of my past and how it relates to my diagnosis."

I'm really concerned about my brother's mental state. Mental illness runs in our family, specifically on our father's side, and I'm worried that he may be showing signs of schizophrenia. Earlier tonight, he was extremely aggressive, angry, and violent. He told me that God came to him and said he was the chosen one, and that the world will persecute him. He believes he needs to give up his soul on August 3rd and take his place on the throne of Eden. He also made threats towards our mother and claimed that Obama is contacting him for a place in heaven. He mentioned having conversations with God, Einstein, and Mary Magdalene. He even believes he brought our dead dog's soul back into our new puppy. He became upset when I suggested he might be experiencing symptoms of mental illness and said that people would persecute him for it. I'm really at a loss for what to do. About three weeks ago, he mentioned similar experiences to our older brother and started crying.

I'm only 13 years old and I'm feeling really confused about what's going on with me. I think I might be experiencing some symptoms of bipolar disorder, but I'm not sure. I come from a single-parent household as my dad passed away when I was just 6 months old. Lately, I've been feeling constantly depressed and sad without any apparent reason. I also find myself arguing with my mom and my two brothers every day, and during these arguments, I act in ways that I can't even understand. Additionally, I've been engaging in self-harm by scratching myself with my nails.

About three weeks ago, I experienced a devastating loss when my beloved dog was hit by a car. I have been struggling with depression for some time now, and my dog was my source of comfort and purpose in life. We were inseparable, and her presence lifted my spirits whenever I felt sad or upset. Now that she's gone, everything reminds me of her because she was such a significant part of my life. I miss her every second, and the intensity of my grief seems to be increasing with each passing day. The worst part is the recurring nightmares I have every night, where I see my dog dead over and over again. Sometimes, I even dream that she's crying out for me, but I can never reach her. I feel absolutely terrible, and I don't know how to cope. I feel completely lost.

Lately, I've been experiencing recurrent thoughts that keep intruding my mind. It's like they just won't go away. Specifically, I've been preoccupied with thoughts about Heaven and the meaning of life. I'm not sure why these thoughts are persisting, but they feel different from my usual thinking patterns. It's like they're distorted in some way.

I'm feeling really overwhelmed and lost right now. I'm an 18-year-old senior in high school and I have a lot of things going on in my life. One of my biggest concerns is figuring out my plans for college and how to get a scholarship in the art world. My lack of self-confidence is holding me back from pursuing my goals. I've tried to be more outgoing, but I always come across as socially awkward. I'm afraid of what people might think of me and I struggle to understand what others are saying. I don't have any close friends, just acquaintances at school, and no one ever reaches out to me. My mood can change drastically throughout the day - sometimes I feel really depressed and other times I find myself laughing for no reason during class.

I've been divorced from my ex-husband for over five years. He has a history of domestic violence and has been diagnosed with bipolar disorder, PTSD, and OCD. Despite his claims of no longer being mentally ill, he only takes his medication before his monthly psychiatrist appointment. He's isolating himself, holding grandiose beliefs, and pressuring me to take him back despite my sons' objections. I fear he may become abusive again if I let him back into my life. I'm torn between loyalty to my family and my lingering feelings for him.

I am deeply concerned about my husband's mental well-being. We have been married for 3 years and have 3 children, including 8-month-old twins. Recently, after a fight that led me to leave temporarily, he has become a different person. He has mentioned hearing voices and seeing ghosts in the past, and now he is exhibiting strange behavior like drawing unusual shapes and fixating on a diamond with 69 diamonds in it. He also seems distant and uninterested in our marriage. I want to support him, but I don't know what to do.

Hi, I have a question about personality disorders. Are they really necessary to be treated? I mean, society just considers them as being different, right? I personally feel like I'm functioning perfectly fine at the moment. So, why should I conform to what others say is wrong with me? I don't think it's dangerous, is it?

I'm in a difficult situation regarding prom. I want to take a girl to prom, but I'm afraid of how my mom will react. I live with my mom, who has been exhibiting some concerning behavior for the past 8 years since my parents divorced. She talks to the radio and has become very religious. It's been challenging growing up with her constantly stressed and hovering over me. I've been secretly ensuring she takes her medication. Recently, my mom has been calling my friends and asking questions about my whereabouts. I want to tell the girl I like about my mom's condition and warn her about potential phone calls, but I'm worried about how she'll react. Can you please help me?

I am a mother with two boys from a previous relationship, and my husband and I have a child together. I am feeling overwhelmed because my husband constantly finds fault with my older boys. He nitpicks every little thing they do, expects them to always do what he wants, and feels they don't contribute enough to the household. He also punishes them for their grades and makes hurtful comments. I love my boys and my husband, but this constant tension is wearing me down. I feel stressed, exhausted, and like I'm losing my sanity. I just want my children to enjoy their lives without constantly worrying about pleasing my husband.

I was discharged from the US Navy in 2001 due to "convenience to the government" and was subsequently diagnosed with Borderline Personality Disorder with Schizoid Features. I fell into a pattern of substance abuse, particularly with meth, and even began selling drugs to sustain my habit. In 2001, I was caught with two ounces of cocaine and faced legal consequences, including intensive probation and a felony conviction. Despite attempts at sobriety, I relapsed after completing a drug treatment program and found myself in legal trouble once again in 2011. I am currently on Drug Court Probation, attending regular drug tests and recovery-related groups through my mental health care provider. However, I am feeling discouraged as I believe quality drug treatment is largely inaccessible for someone without significant financial means.

Over the years, I've received various mental disorder diagnoses starting from when I was 17 and up until I turned 22. One of the diagnoses I received at around 21 was Schizoaffective disorder. Despite being in complete "remission" for several years and not taking any medications, I still carry this label. Unfortunately, I no longer have access to a psychiatrist and it could take several months to see one.

I recently started an online relationship with a man in his 40s that I met in a chat. We quickly formed a strong connection and began talking every day, despite living in different countries. We made plans to meet in person once my semester of school was over. However, I started to notice some concerning behavior from him. He would often ask me if I was talking to or seeing other men, both online and in person. He also displayed controlling and jealous tendencies whenever I spent time with my friends. I couldn't help but feel that there was something wrong with his behavior, although he would attribute it to the distance between us.

Patient: When I was very young, my family and I experienced a burglary while we were all at home. Since then, I have been struggling with sleep and feeling anxious when I am alone or sleeping in a separate room. I even feel scared to seek comfort from my parents' room and often rely on having the television on to fall asleep.

I have been struggling with depression for a long time, but I have never sought professional help for it. Lately, it has become unbearable. My husband and I briefly discussed the possibility of me seeing a therapist, but the thought of it terrifies me. Now he keeps pushing me to go, assuming that I am seriously considering it. I really dislike talking about my feelings, and just thinking about going to a therapy appointment gives me a lot of anxiety, which is unusual for me.

During my second visit to my doctor, I felt uncomfortable because her behavior was different from my first visit. I was discussing my husband and she asked intrusive questions about my sister-in-law's relationship with him. I didn't react at the time and continued talking about my husband. She also doubted my parents without reason and asked me nonsensical and inappropriate questions. I feel guilty and sorry towards my relatives. I believe she emotionally abused me. Her questions about my respected family members were shameful, even though I didn't say anything at the time. I tried to explain my mother's depression, but I felt sad and angry when I got home. My anxiety disorder has worsened because of her, and I've been experiencing migraines. I'm not sure if I can continue therapy with her. I like my psychologist, but I don't like the way she asked about my family members. She asked about unreal things that are false by nature. I'm losing my peace of mind. Please help, what should I do?

Patient: Lately, I've been feeling a lot of hate towards my life. It seems like the only time I can find any happiness is when I drink beer. I used to be in the military, but the stress became overwhelming for me. I've had thoughts of ending my life, but I'm hesitant because of my beliefs about the afterlife. Since coming home, I've isolated myself and turned to alcohol as a way to cope. I feel ashamed of myself and the financial burden I've placed on my mother. Sometimes, I even contemplate suicide. I've tried being in relationships, but I always end up feeling unhappy and recognizing that the problem lies within me. I hate my job at Walmart and I can't afford to go back to school. I've been desperately searching for happiness, but I keep turning to alcohol. Sometimes, I feel like I have no purpose here on Earth.

I've been in a relationship with my partner for 2 and a half years. We have two children together and I also have children from previous relationships. When we first met, he was kind, fun, and had a positive attitude. However, after about a year, he started calling me names, putting me down, and became difficult to talk to. He would express disgust at the sight of me and even talk about wanting to harm me. He has physically abused me, leaving bruises all over my body. Sometimes he shows remorse for his actions, but lately, he tends to make excuses instead. It's hard for him to understand how his words and actions affect me, and when I cry, he mocks me. He apologizes occasionally, saying he hates the way he is and that he loves me, but then he goes back to his abusive behavior. I feel lost, trapped, and afraid. I want him to get help, but I'm not sure if he will ever change. I'm tired of living in fear and being isolated in my own home. I love him, but I don't know how to leave because I'm afraid I'll just end up going back to him. This is only a fraction of what I've been through.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for almost 5 years. We have a child together, and I also have two children from a previous relationship. Recently, my partner revealed that his ex-girlfriend, who left the country while pregnant, reached out to him. She informed him that their son is now almost 6 years old and that she has been keeping him updated with photos. I am currently pregnant with my boyfriend's third child, and I feel very threatened by his ex's presence. It feels like she has disrupted our family. I asked my partner to move out so that I can process all of this. How should I navigate this situation? I feel torn apart.

I'm feeling really torn about a guy I've been involved with who lives in another state. It's been complicated because I recently moved to Indiana for my junior year of high school, leaving behind my friends and my previous boyfriend, whom I still have feelings for. He wants me to move back after graduation, but he's currently dating someone else and isn't willing to make the move sooner. During a recent visit, he cheated on his girlfriend, which makes me question whether I can trust him. I'm not sure if I should continue talking to him and pursue a relationship or if I should focus on starting a new life here.

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for almost three years now. We're both fairly young, with me being 18 and him being almost 20. Recently, we made the decision for me to move in with him and his family because our work schedules were making it difficult for us to spend time together.

I developed a strong emotional connection with a man I met at my gym. We quickly became attached to each other, driven by intense emotions. However, I noticed that he wasn't making any progress in our relationship despite our growing attachment. It was a shock for me to discover that he might be married, as he displayed intense emotions towards me. I struggled with his inconsistent behavior, sometimes getting angry if I tried to distance myself and other times getting angry if I got too close. It became a toxic dance that affected my self-esteem. I decided to end contact with him, which made him angry. I have been avoiding him and trying to recover emotionally. If I ever see him at the gym again, what should I do? Ignore him and leave? I suspect he may have Borderline Personality Disorder based on his behaviors, and I believe he is married. Will seeing me cause him distress? I don't want to run into him and I have suffered emotionally. Thank you for any advice.

Patient: I've been in a relationship with my girlfriend for several months now. We didn't know each other for very long before we started dating, but things progressed quickly and now we're together. She's an amazing woman and has everything I look for in a partner, except for her sexual history. We're both 27 and have had previous relationships.

I've been struggling a lot lately and I'm not sure how to explain it properly. I've been feeling really low and it all stems from my difficult childhood. I had a lot of setbacks in school and it made me lose all my self-esteem. When my dad passed away when I was just 7, I received some money and I ended up giving it all away. Now, I really want to get a job but it's been difficult because I dropped out of school. I didn't drop out because I was unintelligent, but rather because I felt so unmotivated and didn't see the value in education.

Hi, it's been over a year since I reached out to you about my feelings of loneliness and isolation. I mentioned that I don't have a driver's license due to my vision impairment, which has made me feel stuck. I also shared that I used to ride a bike for independence, but couldn't do so since I had a septic knee and no friends to turn to. Additionally, I mentioned that I had brain surgery years ago for an AVM bleed, which resulted in visual impairment and learning disabilities. Since our last conversation, I followed your advice and enrolled in a Guide Dog School. I've been here for four weeks now, undergoing training with a wonderful dog named Jimbo. We have developed a strong bond and he has brought so much love and companionship into my life.

I have been feeling increasingly worried about my mental health lately. I recently turned twenty-one, and I've heard that this is an age when some people start experiencing symptoms of psychosis. I'm really concerned that I might be losing touch with reality. Can you help me understand what's going on?
Counselor's response:

I've managed to stay free of self-injury for over 1000 days now, but it's still a struggle at times. I've been trying to find someone to talk to, but it's not easy for me. My best friend is older and busy with her own life, so she's not always available. I do have a counselor at school, but she's currently not an option and doesn't seem to take my self-injury seriously. It's frustrating because she ignores it and moves on.

I've been feeling really isolated since starting college. I don't have many friends and I mostly just talk to my roommate, but we're not very close. In the past, I've had a few suicide attempts, although I'm not sure if they were serious. I've been diagnosed with OCD, bipolar disorder, and ADHD at different times, but I think there's something else going on that hasn't been addressed.

During the session, the patient, a 13-year-old, expressed concerns about their internal thought processes. They described experiencing two tracks of thought throughout their life - their own thoughts and a narrator that would provide commentary similar to reading a novel. However, since going through puberty, they have noticed that the narrator's voice has become more frequent, and there is now an additional track of thought that takes the form of an interviewer. The patient also mentioned that the main track of thought, represented by a rectangular shape composed of two columns of blocks, has been rearranging itself, causing confusion and a sense of internal conflict.

This marriage has had its share of challenges. Over the past eighteen years, my husband and I have experienced both typical and atypical dynamics. In the beginning, there was a lot of violence, and many people urged me to leave. I turned to drugs and alcohol as a way to cope with the situation. My husband made me believe that I was the one causing the problems, which left me feeling trapped. Despite this, I couldn't bring myself to leave and stay away. Fast forward fifteen years, the violence has subsided, and I have managed to maintain fifteen years of sobriety, accomplishing a lot in the process. However, my husband hasn't shown any signs of change.

Throughout my life, I have been fortunate to have an amazing father who has set a high standard for what I believe a healthy relationship should be like. Unfortunately, this has made it difficult for me to find satisfaction in my romantic relationships. I have found myself constantly focusing on the flaws of my partners and it has caused me and them a great deal of unhappiness. I struggle with letting go of this high standard I have set for my future life partner.

My husband was molested as a child. This traumatic experience has had a significant impact on our sex life over the 20 years we have been together. He has communicated to me that his lack of interest in sex is directly related to what happened to him. Initially, I made every effort to try and address this issue and find a solution.

Patient: I just finished my first semester at a major university in New York City. I failed miserably and I know it was my fault. It was a mix of laziness, ADD and depression. I have been dealing with depression since I was 13 (18 now). I have never felt pretty, smart, or worth anything. Everything has worsened after I got dismissed from college. I’m confused about what to do next. It is too late to register at a community college for Spring Semester and I am at a standstill. I cry every night and I HATE myself so much. I don't know if I am ever going to be something in life. I also have to write an appeal to my academic dismissal. I want to explain that I can do better if allowed to stay. Should I do it? What are the chances that the university would let me stay? I really need help. I have hit rock bottom.

About 8 months ago, my husband experienced a sudden onset of symptoms including hearing voices, headaches, insomnia, heightened religiosity, paranoia, weight loss, and incoherent speech. I suspect he had a psychotic episode and may be suffering from psychosis, depression, or even bipolar disorder. A month later, he left and now lives on his own. He seems functional but still believes that my family poisoned him, despite that not being true. He hasn't sought medical attention or medication. Can he recover without treatment or is there a risk of it happening again?

As a child, my brother and I were very close, but as we grew up we started to drift apart. However, we always maintained a good relationship. Unfortunately, my brother had a difficult life, especially when it came to his mental health. A few years ago, I received a letter from him that was quite alarming. In the letter, he mentioned having a rifle and talked about hunting people. I was frightened by both the content and the handwriting, and I wasn't sure if he was joking or not. Since my mother was in contact with him, I decided to forward the letter to her and seek her advice. She called him to discuss it, but I'm not sure how that conversation went. However, a couple of months later, my brother tragically took his own life in a motel room using the same rifle he had mentioned in the letter. I've been carrying an immense amount of guilt ever since. I understand that he ultimately made the decision, but I can't help but feel like I played a significant role in his actions. It's been years, but I still struggle with how to handle this situation, and his memory haunts me every day.

I've been successful in various areas of my life like school, work, and finances, but I struggle with insecurity and maintaining healthy relationships. Looking back, I realized that I experienced physical and emotional abuse as well as neglect from my parents until I moved out at 21. It wasn't until later, at the age of 24, that I also discovered my sexual orientation. I feel like my success makes it difficult for others to understand my insecurities.
