Her inability to handle her life has been exacerbated by her unemployment over the past couple of years. It's heartbreaking to witness her spiral downward and to have her believe that we, her children, are somehow part of the problem. She's convinced that there are hidden truths related to her divorce from my dad 23 years ago, and she claims to see ghosts of us. She constantly makes self-deprecating comments and seems completely detached from reality. While I'm not afraid for my own safety, I am deeply concerned about her future and what will happen to her if she continues on this path.

Hi, I'm a 14-year-old girl and I've always had a rich imagination. It started when I was really young, creating stories in my head to help me fall asleep. Over time, these stories became more complex and detailed, with each character having their own backstory. Recently, I've been fixating on one particular character and putting them through traumatic events. I also became really obsessed with a TV show and it consumed a lot of my thoughts and behaviors. I find it hard to connect with others because nobody shares my interests or wishes the world was like mine. I've been struggling with my mental health and have had thoughts of suicide. I hope you can help me.

I have been feeling overwhelmed and unappreciated by my family for the past few years. I am 22 years old and I take on a lot of responsibilities in the household, such as maintaining the house and vehicles. I am also attending school with the goal of eventually taking over the financial responsibilities of the house. Despite all my efforts, I constantly feel like what I do is never good enough. I am the one who does most of the driving, as my stepfather doesn't have a license. My mother seems to have developed a negative attitude towards me and constantly puts me down, making me feel like a bad person. I don't have any children or student loan debt, which is not typical for someone my age. However, I find it difficult to enjoy the things I have because I have to maintain them all on my own. My stepfather's lack of involvement in household maintenance and cars seems to make my mother angry, and she directs her anger towards me. It feels like she has turned against me, which is causing a lot of tension between us. Is there something else I should be doing? I already contribute financially and take care of various household tasks, such as cutting the grass. I have put a lot of effort and talent into transforming the entire house, but it never seems to be enough.

I am a 39-year-old individual who is about to turn 40. Lately, I have been feeling like I may have Asperger's syndrome. I live alone, have very limited social connections, and struggle with holding conversations. Despite being intelligent, I feel completely isolated from people. Changes make me anxious and paranoid, and I often struggle to understand the intentions behind people's words. When I'm in a car with someone, I rarely speak and instead focus on observing my surroundings. I become obsessed with making friends but quickly lose them. I want to get tested for Asperger's, but I'm worried that a diagnosis might affect my ability to work. I've had difficulties in jobs due to social interactions, not because of my job performance. Even with my family, I can spend hours in silence. Being around a lot of people makes me uncomfortable, and I never know what to say. I'm at my wit's end with all of this uncertainty. Can you help me determine if I have Asperger's or not?

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for over a year now, and I've noticed that he seems to have anger issues. This concern was reinforced when he mentioned that his ex-girlfriend thought the same and recommended therapy, which he did attend. However, his therapist assured him that his anger levels are normal. I have a different perspective though. He gets extremely angry over minor things like a paper falling or traffic congestion, and even forgetfulness. Once, he slammed on the brakes so hard that I almost hit the windshield because he thought he left a tool outside. Another time, he punched the steering wheel due to having hiccups. While he's never directed his anger towards me, it still worries me. I would appreciate your professional opinion on this matter. Thank you.

I'm a 17-year-old guy from the UK. A few months ago, I invited my girlfriend from the US to stay with my family for three weeks. We had some arguments during her visit, but nothing too serious. When it was time for her to leave, I was unsure about our relationship and whether we should break up. In my confusion, I started talking to her cousin, and things turned sexual. My girlfriend found out, broke up with me, and now she tells me she's pregnant. After some time, I convinced her to give me another chance because I realized how much I loved her and wanted to be with her. I feel guilty and ashamed about what happened with her cousin, but I am committed to making things right. However, I am concerned about finances. I just finished an apprenticeship, and there are no job opportunities at the moment. I need to financially support my girlfriend and the baby, which will cost around £3500 or $6000 per year. Additionally, if we want to live together as a family, the easiest visa to obtain would be a marriage visa, but weddings are expensive. I haven't told our parents about the pregnancy yet, and my girlfriend's mom already dislikes me because of what happened. I feel overwhelmed and just need a way to relax and forget about everything for a moment. I know I can handle being a father, but financially, I'm not prepared. I often feel lost and unsure of what to do.

During my driving lessons, I had a really tough experience with my instructor. From the very beginning, I could sense that she wasn't welcoming and her attitude made me feel ashamed of myself. She made comments about my speed and seemed irritated throughout the lesson. When she asked me to turn left at a stoplight, I got confused by the lanes of traffic and she responded in a condescending and frustrated manner. She yelled at me and I remained quiet, hoping she wouldn't yell again. Near the end of the lesson, when I asked a question about reversing, she responded harshly. Despite her saying I did well and improved, I still feel sad and nervous about driving with her. I wish she could assert herself in a gentler way.

I have been feeling really anxious and overwhelmed lately. It's been affecting my daily life, making it hard for me to concentrate and sleep. I've tried talking to my friends about it, but I feel like they don't really understand what I'm going through.

I had been seeing a counselor for social anxiety at a local practice. One of the reasons I struggle with social anxiety is because I feel like I don't fit in. I find it difficult to relate to girls my age because they often engage in behaviors like drinking and smoking, and their style of dressing doesn't align with my personal values.

I've been in a new relationship for almost 5 months now. My previous relationship was abusive and I developed panic attacks towards the end, particularly during high confrontations. I think it's because I was hit a few times in that past relationship. But now, I feel like I'm carrying some unwanted baggage into my current relationship. Whenever we argue, I become overly sensitive to what's being said. I end up feeling manic and fearing that the relationship is going to end. I start sobbing uncontrollably, like a child. In the past, I used to argue and talk back, but now I just cry and try to explain my feelings to my partner. It feels like I've traded one negative trait for another. I used to be able to brush off harsh comments, but now they trigger these crying episodes. I can't explain why I've changed like this. I also don't know if I'm handling confrontation in my relationship appropriately because even little things are setting off these crying episodes lately. For example, when my partner told me over the phone that I was stressing them out and hung up, I cried instead of getting angry like I used to. I'm not sure if my depression and anxiety are contributing to this oversensitivity. It feels like my anxiety has increased over the past year and now my coping mechanism is to cry like a 5-year-old child. I'm currently being treated for depression and anxiety, and I see a counselor once a month. I just thought getting a third, anonymous opinion could be helpful in this case. Any techniques to better cope with my mood swings would be appreciated. I have been prescribed Klonopin for panic attacks, but I would prefer to handle it without medication.

Patient: Throughout my teenage years, I always felt like something was off. During the day, I would put on a smile, but at night, I would cry myself to sleep. When I was 14, I started journaling as a way to cope. I still write in my journals, especially when things get really tough. Recently, I looked back at my past entries and realized that I've been dealing with depression since I was around 15. It's hard for me to accept that I've known about it for all these years and only now am I starting to acknowledge it. Lately, I've been feeling really low, and I find myself getting angry easily or bursting into tears for no reason. My relationships, including the one with my sister, are suffering. She even asked me, "What is wrong with you?" I haven't told anyone about my problem, not even my family, because I'm afraid they'll treat me differently. I'm at a loss for what to do. Should I tell someone, or should I keep it to myself? Can you please help me?

I have been experiencing existential issues and struggling with suicidal ideation. Despite having good affect regulation and impulse control, I feel that my life is pointless and I have almost no ability to form meaningful connections with others. I have been in therapy for two years, but my therapist seems to be on the side of life and is unable to explore my thoughts about death with me. I am wondering if there are any professionals who can provide an impartial perspective on this matter, like a spiritual advisor. Additionally, I am curious if there are therapists who can sign a pre-release to ensure they won't face legal consequences if I choose to die.

I am in a difficult situation with my fiancé. We have been together for almost three years and have a child together. Recently, I participated in a case study for female condoms. As part of the study, I had to get a pap smear and STD test. Shockingly, I received a call from the doctor informing me that I have an STD. I have always trusted my fiancé and this news has left me devastated. When I confronted him, he initially lied but eventually admitted to a one-time encounter with another woman. He apologized and expressed remorse, but I am struggling to forgive him. I feel hurt and confused by his actions. What should I do?

I recently went through a breakup with my boyfriend of 7 years, and since then, my relationship with my mom has become strained. I've started to realize that my mom has always treated me differently from my brother and it feels like she doesn't love me in the way I need. It's been really difficult for me, especially because my mom hasn't been supportive during this tough time. Instead, she makes everything about herself and her own struggles. It's gotten to the point where I can't be at home with her and my dad, so I'm currently living with family friends. I've tried talking to my mom about it, but she rejects me every time. I've even made the decision to go away for 5 months to give myself some space. I can't help but feel like I've done something to cause all of this, and it's really affecting my self-esteem. Should I consider seeing a professional to help me navigate this situation? I'm not sure who would be the right person to talk to. My dad and I have a better relationship now, but he also recognizes that something is wrong and feels powerless to fix it. What should I do?

I have been with my husband since we were teenagers, and now we have two young children. In the past, we both experimented with drugs, but I have moved on while my husband developed an addiction to pain pills and Xanax about four years ago. Despite my husband's occasional periods of sobriety, he recently relapsed and has been coming home high for the past three days. He's a great father and provider, but I'm at a loss for what to do. I've tried being supportive, but it doesn't seem to make a difference. I'm considering divorce, but I don't want to give up on him. What should I do?

I've been struggling with feelings of emptiness and isolation for quite some time now. It feels like true happiness has eluded me for years, and I fear that this is how it will always be. I haven't been able to enjoy my teenage years like others seem to.

It's been really tough at home lately. My dad has a job that requires him to live out of state, so it's just me, my mom, and my three younger siblings in the house. My mom has changed so much over time and it feels like she doesn't care about us anymore. It's like we're not even related to her anymore. She wasn't always like this.

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for over 3 years, but I'm starting to realize that it's not a healthy one. We've been on and off multiple times, and he has addiction problems that lead to hurtful behavior when he drinks. He's cheated on me numerous times, but always apologizes afterwards and promises it won't happen again. He's also become very controlling, constantly questioning my whereabouts and causing me to lose touch with my friends and family.

A month ago, I discovered that my husband kissed another woman while he was stationed in Iraq. I found out through a letter he received from a fellow soldier who claimed that my husband and this woman kissed during a drunken night out before they left for Iraq. My husband admits to reciprocating the kiss, but claims it meant nothing and he was scared to tell me. He says it was just a mistake fueled by alcohol and that he loves me deeply. I am confused and upset by the situation, especially since this woman is unattractive and a lesbian. I found out about this six months later from another soldier, and I have even reached out to the woman and other soldiers who were present that night to get more information. I want to understand what happened and figure out how to move forward.

Two years ago, I was discharged from the military with a diagnosis of Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) and Personality Disorder. Since then, I have noticed a decline in my mental health. The medication I was prescribed had negative side effects, including night terrors and sexual problems. Due to financial constraints, I had to stop taking the medication, and initially, things seemed to improve. However, recently my panic and anxiety have worsened, I experience paranoia at times, and my emotions fluctuate rapidly. I have also started having hallucinations and hearing things. Sometimes, I even feel like I have delusions of grandeur. Is it possible to have psychosis, bipolar disorder, depression, paranoia, and megalomania all at once? Could these symptoms be related to my GAD and Personality Disorder, or is it likely something else entirely? Also, how can we differentiate between delusions of grandeur and self-esteem? Don't we all want to feel a sense of purpose and importance in our lives? Can these symptoms impair one's ability to work, even with medication?

I've been feeling really overwhelmed lately. I find it difficult to express my thoughts and emotions, and I've become more withdrawn. I've tried different medications for my attention issues, but they haven't helped. I'm starting to believe that my life has no purpose, no matter what I achieve. I also act out violently and blame others for the consequences. Even my parents don't seem to understand me. I always feel like people are talking about me in a negative way, and it's affecting my self-esteem. I feel stressed and isolated, and I'm losing motivation. I'm worried that it's not schizophrenia, but I don't know what else it could be.

I have been feeling overwhelmed and frustrated with my husband's behavior since he lost his second job last October. Before he lost his job, he never helped with household chores or taking care of our two younger children, aged 10 and 7. Now that he has been out of work for a long time, I had hoped he would step up and contribute more, especially with our fourth child on the way. However, he continues to spend extravagantly and has been on multiple vacations, bought expensive cars, and goes out to bars frequently. He is not taking care of our children properly, neglecting their homework and not feeding them dinner. The house is also in disarray. I'm working overtime to make ends meet and it's becoming too much for me.

My wife has been displaying impatience and frustration in various situations, including interactions with me, our 2 1/2 year old, traffic, and computer issues. She is currently pregnant and experiencing difficulties. When I come home, she often seems frustrated with the events of the day and with our child. I believe that a significant portion of her frustration is self-imposed.

Over the past two months, my marriage has taken a sudden turn. My husband and I have been together for 13 years and have five children. Lately, we've been facing financial difficulties, he recently met his estranged father, and his best friend is terminally ill. In the midst of all this, he began chatting with his ex from 16 years ago and kept it a secret. Out of nowhere, he asked for a divorce. However, he now claims to have realized his love for me and wants to put this behind us. We have all decided to seek individual counseling. My question is, how can I learn to trust him again without constantly doubting him? I don't want to be paranoid, but I also don't want to be taken advantage of. I want to find a middle ground where I can maintain my self-respect and teach my children healthy relationship dynamics. How can I achieve that?

I've been feeling confused and overwhelmed about my feelings towards girls. I've never been in love with a girl before, but recently, someone called me a lesbian and it's been bothering me ever since. I don't want to be with a girl, but I noticed that I didn't mind seeing a lesbian character in an anime I watched today. It's confusing because I used to feel jealous of pretty girls, but now I find some girls attractive. I also have low self-esteem.

I have been struggling with depression for many years, and it has greatly impacted my life. It has caused me to leave jobs because I couldn't function properly. It has also had a negative effect on my personal relationships with my family, friends, and partners. I've tried counseling and taking medication, but the medication makes me sick and doesn't alleviate my suicidal thoughts. These thoughts consume my mind daily and even appear in my dreams at night. Recently, I got engaged, but the stress surrounding the marriage is overwhelming me. I feel like running away because I can't handle it. I constantly fight with my partner over everything, and I don't understand why they stay with me. I'm in a difficult financial situation because I left my last job due to these problems. I need help but don't have any income. What can I do?

"I've been feeling really overwhelmed in my marriage lately. My husband and I have been together for 16 years, and we're facing some challenges. He works from home, and I'm a stay-at-home wife and mother, so we're constantly together. It's starting to feel suffocating."

I am a 19 year old female who has been sexually active for almost two years now, but I have never been able to orgasm. I have researched all over the internet and bought books and toys but none have proved useful. From what I have learned, most problems having to do with the inability to orgasm have to do either with a lack of confidence, knowledge of your body and what you like, or even an unconcerned partner, however I do not have any of these. Even when I am alone and masturbating I can feel like I am getting close but then it starts to either hurt or completely disappear into no feeling at all. When I am with my boyfriend (poor guy) all he ever does is attempt to help me in whatever way he possibly can, but still nothing. I am worried that maybe there is something wrong with me. Is it possible to be physically unable to orgasm? If not then what do I do?! This has been going on even before I became sexually active and I have become hopeless and concerned. How can I fix this? My boyfriend always tells me I am perfectly fine and not broken (as I argue) but I am not so sure…

Patient: I've been experiencing some distressing symptoms lately. I've been hearing voices that are telling me disturbing things, like that I am part of a murder club and that I am responsible for causing a hurricane. They also suggest that I should cleanse the poison from my body by taking all of my medications at once.

Hi. I've been dealing with anxiety and depression for the past couple of years, and it's really impacting my daily life. I've been taking Ritalin since I was a child because I had a lot of energy and it helped me calm down. I'm starting to wonder if the Ritalin could be a factor in my anxiety and depression. Can Ritalin cause these mental health issues? If so, are there any ways to reverse the effects of the medication?

It sounds like you and your wife have been through a lot together, especially with the recent addition of your second child and your pursuit of a Master's degree. It's understandable that managing all these responsibilities can bring about stress. It seems that you were supportive of your wife by taking time off from school to allow her to have some time with the baby after birth. However, you noticed a change in her behavior once you returned to school, with her going out with friends and leaving you to take care of the kids. This has left you feeling neglected and frustrated.
Patient's Statement:

During my relationship with my ex, we both opened up about our past traumas - he had experienced childhood sexual abuse, and I had been sexually assaulted recently. Despite only being together for a few months, I took our relationship seriously and fell in love with him. I wanted to support him, so I lent him around £1000 to help alleviate his financial stress. However, after we broke up, he refused to repay the money and there is no legal recourse since we never signed a contract.

I often find myself feeling this way. My therapist and doctor have asked me if I want to feel better, and I struggle with the idea of feeling good because it's unfamiliar to me. They believe my depression began in my childhood, and it's difficult for me to stop thinking about that. I've become comfortable in my depressed state because I've been feeling this way for so long before seeking help. The idea of being happy and feeling better makes me feel like a different person. It's almost as if depression has become my comfort zone, and I'm afraid to let it go. I also feel conflicted because I believe that if I do start feeling better, I won't have to visit the doctor and therapist as often because it seems like the only place where people care about me. This feeling is not limited to my psychiatrist's office; it happens at other doctors' offices too, although it does get easier over time. But it's always there, and I'm tired of feeling this way. I have people in my life who probably care about me, but I struggle to see it or understand what it means. I want to understand why I feel this way and how I can change my thinking. One thing that really worries me is that my therapist and doctor might think I have romantic feelings towards them, but that's not the case. I just feel like they care about me more than anyone else has. I'm afraid they might suggest I see another doctor and therapist, but I won't do that. If it comes to that, I'll see my primary care physician and gradually taper off my medication and see how life goes. I'm already anxious about discussing this with my therapist, especially since it's the same office where these feelings arise. At least I don't have an appointment with the doctor for a few more weeks. I'm not sure whether I should bring this up with my therapist since I haven't been able to change my thinking on my own, or if I should just keep it to myself because I don't even know how to start talking about it. I already have an appointment scheduled, but I'm considering canceling it and trying to deal with this on my own, although I know it might only prolong my suffering. Should I talk to my therapist about this or try to handle it on my own, like I've been doing all along?

My family has been experiencing ongoing issues for years, and they seem to be escalating. My mother has a tendency to lose her temper and directs her anger towards me and my siblings. She often blames her outbursts on her past and uses any excuse to yell at us. There have been instances where she has even started fights over events that happened over fifteen years ago with my dad. During these fights, she becomes physically aggressive, throwing objects like plates, peanut butter jars, and lamps at us. She also threatens to harm herself and sometimes leaves with dangerous items like rope or a knife. It's difficult for me and my sister to intervene because if we try to talk to her, she explodes with anger, often targeting one of us.

I met my fiancé in May 2009. At the time, he had recently separated from his wife and was staying with friends while she had custody of their four children. However, she suddenly took off with the kids and cut off his access to them. Initially, I was apprehensive about dating someone with four young children, but then their mother unexpectedly gave up custody and my fiancé moved in with me. Now, over a year later, I find myself struggling to be around the children. They are with us all the time, and I feel overwhelmed and trapped. My fiancé is in the military and could be deployed, leaving me alone with the kids. I'm starting to question if getting married is the right decision. I love my fiancé, but his kids' behavior is difficult to handle. We went to couples therapy, but it didn't help much. The sound of their voices irritates me, and I wonder if it's because I feel they've disrupted my life. I used to have a great relationship, social life, and financial freedom. I'm now working as a waitress to accommodate the kids' schedules, and money is tight. Their mother doesn't even pay child support. I love my fiancé, but I'm unhappy with my current situation. Should I stay or should I go?

Lately, I've been feeling really down and unmotivated. I think I might be dealing with depression, but I'm hesitant to talk about it. I know therapy can be helpful, but I'm scared of opening up to a therapist. I also prefer to keep my therapy private and don't have anyone I feel comfortable bringing into sessions. Is there anything I can do to feel more at ease with therapists?

I'm a 19-year-old who has recently experienced the loss of both my parents. My father passed away four years ago, and just a month ago, my mother passed away right before the birth of my son. It's becoming increasingly difficult for me to navigate these losses and I'm finding it hard to fully connect with my son and fiance because of my fear of losing them too.

I have been struggling with my mental health for a long time, and I'm not sure where to start in seeking help. Since I was a child, I've always felt that my mother favored my other sisters, which has caused me to develop feelings of insecurity and low self-confidence. The constant teasing about my weight, both from my mother and others, has had a significant impact on my life. Additionally, my parents had a troubled relationship, and their constant fighting added to my emotional distress. Moving to the United States at 14 only worsened my situation, as I continued to struggle with my self-esteem and gained even more weight. Throughout high school, I battled with depression and had difficulty making friends, which continues to this day. I briefly saw a therapist who prescribed antidepressants, but I didn't take them. My relationship with my family is strained, and I often feel intense anger towards my mother, leading to outbursts of yelling and throwing things. I have had thoughts of suicide, although I've never acted on them. I blame my mother for my current mental state. Interestingly, when I visit my home country during the summer, I feel happier, but upon returning to the United States, I sink back into depression. To make matters worse, my father passed away last year, and I regret not having the opportunity to apologize to him after our fight. I use food as a coping mechanism, and I feel tremendously alone without friends or supportive family members to turn to. Please help me.

I've been struggling with concentration and focus while doing my book work as an intern at a Seattle Mission place. It's become really frustrating because no matter how hard I try, I can't seem to retain any of the information I read. I've always been good at physical tasks, but this mental challenge is really getting to me. I should mention that I have a history of drug addiction and I want to avoid medication. Is there anything I can do to regain control over my ability to concentrate?

I am a 32-year-old single lesbian female. I am reaching out to you because I am struggling with a situation involving my ex-girlfriend, and I could use some guidance or a fresh perspective. I find it difficult to open up to people, even those close to me. I would appreciate any advice you can offer.

I have been through a series of challenging experiences in my life, including an abusive marriage, a difficult childhood, and dealing with a physical condition. After leaving my husband, I sought counseling and made progress in healing and building a supportive network of friends. However, I still struggle with feelings of loneliness and a lack of meaningful relationships. I have recently relocated to Germany and feel overwhelmed by the loneliness. I am worried that this loneliness may be evolving into something more serious. I am unable to afford counseling at the moment and would appreciate any advice you can provide.

I have been living with my mom since my parents got divorced and my dad joined the military. My mom remarried three months ago, around the same time I was diagnosed with severe depression. Unfortunately, I have also been experiencing sexual abuse from my stepfather for the past four years. To cope with the pain, I started cutting myself and have required stitches fifteen times. He has threatened to harm me further if I tell anyone about the abuse, and I believe he is capable of doing so. I feel responsible for what happened, especially the sexual assault, as I may have provoked it by not speaking to him and having an attitude. I am in desperate need of advice and assistance. Thank you for taking the time to read this and respond. I feel like a loser at the age of thirteen.

I've been dating my girlfriend for two months now. We met through a mutual friend during a really stressful time in her life when she was in the middle of moving. She's also the oldest of five siblings who rely on her for help. Recently, she had a falling out with her sister who just had a baby. Up until now, everything has been great between us. We go on dates and talk about future plans. But suddenly, she's not answering my calls or texts. I thought she didn't want to talk to me anymore, so I stopped reaching out. Then she showed up at my house and said I was acting "funny." I explained that I called and texted but didn't get a response. She told me she has a lot of stress in her life and sometimes avoids calls and texts. She felt like I was putting her on the backburner. We talked, and she left. Later, I apologized for my behavior, and she said it's cool and she needs her own space. I'm confused now. Is she still interested in me? Is she cheating? How did we go from planning future things to her needing space?

Over the past four years, I have been in a relationship with my partner. As time has passed, he has gotten to know me quite well. However, he often makes jokes about me being "Bipolar" or having "mood problems". While he may mean it as a joke, it has had an impact on me because I have personally felt that way myself.

Hi. I've been going through a difficult time in my relationship with my soon-to-be ex-partner. They have been seeing the same psychiatrist for 25 years and have been prescribed Xanax for ongoing anxiety, although they only take it occasionally during stressful periods. They also drink alcohol moderately. They tend to blame me for most things and have had difficulty maintaining employment. I've been attending Al-Anon meetings due to my experiences growing up with an alcoholic mother. I can't help but notice similarities in my partner's blaming behavior. Do you think they might have an addiction or dependency issue? And is it concerning that they haven't shown significant improvement after 25 years of therapy? Besides taking care of myself, do you have any other suggestions on how to handle this situation?

Lately, I've been feeling like an outcast in my family. I'm the oldest among my siblings, but it seems like my parents have favorites and I'm left feeling neglected. I come from a decent family, and I've always tried to be a good person. I haven't done anything terribly wrong, just normal mistakes that everyone makes in life.

Hello, I'm a 17-year-old who has been struggling with stress, depression, and recently experienced the loss of my beloved dog. I didn't realize how much my dog helped me cope with stress until he passed away this year. On top of that, I had a negative experience at school where I was belittled by a teacher. That night, I engaged in self-harm using a safety pin. My mom doesn't understand what I'm going through, and I carry the burden of feeling rejected by my biological father and stepfather. This is my final year of high school, and I'm worried about finding money for college. I struggle with sleep and my eating habits have been affected. I constantly feel responsible for everything, including my grandpa's death and my dog's death. My mom is sick and my stepfather blames me for it, which adds to my stress and physical symptoms. I've had thoughts of suicide, but have never acted on them because I can't do what my friend did. I feel alone and unimportant to my parents, especially when my stepfather made a hurtful comment in front of me. I don't want to feel like this anymore. I need help.

Counselor's response: It sounds like you've been going through a lot of changes and challenges recently. Moving away for college can be both exciting and overwhelming, and it seems like your experience at Bible College took a negative turn in your second year. It's understandable that you felt trapped and like you had lost control over your own life.

Over the past three years, I have been in a relationship with a divorced woman who is 43 years old. She has two sons, aged 12 and 9, and has sole custody of them due to the hostile nature of her divorce. Her ex-partner has not been fulfilling his custodial duties.

I'm a 17-year-old who is struggling with intense emotions surrounding a girl that I care deeply about. We've never been in a committed relationship, but we both acknowledge our strong feelings for each other. Unfortunately, she has experienced traumatic events in her past, including being sexually assaulted while someone was under the influence. She later dated someone who hurt her emotionally, and then had sexual encounters with others, including my former best friend. I feel like I've hit rock bottom and there's no way out. I'm overwhelmed with sadness and find myself crying randomly. It's hard to understand why I feel this way since I haven't experienced any major traumas in my life, which adds to my guilt. I know there are others who are facing much worse situations, so I feel undeserving of my own pain and struggle.

Six years ago, when I was 24, I decided to come out to my parents about my sexuality. Unfortunately, their reaction was much more hurtful than I had anticipated. Since then, we have avoided any discussion about it, and I have been hesitant to bring it up again due to the pain it caused me. Over the past five years, I have been in a loving and committed relationship with a wonderful man. We have a happy and healthy relationship, and we both have fulfilling careers and active roles in our communities. We have been living together for several years, and we are located thousands of miles away from my parents. However, my parents recently informed me that they will be visiting in a few months. I know that during their visit, they will discover my relationship and living situation. The fear of facing their potential rejection once again is overwhelming. I need to tell them, but I don't know how to approach the conversation or how to handle any potential rejection from them.

I know I am very young, but I feel so hopeless, out of control, and desperate that this was my last resort. I have come to realize that I have depression. One of my family members suffers with Bipolar disorder and depression and is currently on medications to keep them under control. I hate myself. Although people would specify me as “popular” in school, I feel like a loser. All my popular friends could EASILY live without me so what is my point in this world? I used to have one very good best friend, but she ditched me for someone else. We stay on speaking terms, but hang out rarely. Since summer has started, I’ve completely isolated myself and spent all my time alone in my room on the computer. I’ve began to obsessively exercise and become obsessed with counting calories. I’m at a normal weight now (5’5 and 114 pounds) but I look so fat that I’m surprised I’m even a normal weight. I still eat, but I only eat half of what I used to and only healthy foods. I exercise SO much. But there is one thing that keeps me going. My hope that someday this will get better. You see, I went to a performing arts high school camp where I was completely accepted for who I was. I made friends instantly, but the camp was over in 2 weeks and we all had to depart. The only thing to keep me going is the hope that in 2 years when I audition for that performing arts school is that I will make it in. I’ve made friends with all the teachers and am currently taking the ADVANCED ballet and modern classes (I’m going into seventh grade and am taking a class with college students). I really want to be a dancer. I just love how I feel when I’m there. I feel like I belong, like I’m part of a family. Everyone is accepted and loved. I just LOVE that feeling! The school is full of talented people, and I’m afraid that if I’m not skinny enough I cannot make it in. I also just want to stand out. My school now is HUGE like GINORMOUS! No one really stands out unless they are massively popular. In this school, everyone stands out in their own way. I just want this so bad, and it’s the drive to keep me going. But I feel like if I’m fat I can’t do it. I feel like I NEED to continue this diet and exercise regimen for an entire 2 YEARS before I make it in (NO DESSERTS, NO WHITE BREAD, ONLY SMALL PORTIONS OF RICE AND PASTA, ABSOLUTELY NO CANDY, AND NO EATING OUT). But I know that’s impossible to keep it going that long, but I just need to do it. I feel like I can’t, but I really want to. How can I cope with being extremely pressured to be skinny, with my depression and isolation, and with my friend problems? Please please please please help me. I’m desperate.

I'm a 14-year-old and I'm feeling really overwhelmed at home. Whenever I'm not happy or don't smile, my parents yell at me. I try to express my feelings by screaming back at them, but it only gets me into more trouble. They don't understand what I'm going through and when I try to explain, they just start yelling even more. When I go to my room to calm down, they barge in and continue yelling. I don't know how to make them understand that their yelling is adding to my stress, especially when I'm already struggling with school and other challenges in my life.

Over the past 3 years, I've been in a relationship with a man who has been diagnosed with borderline personality disorder. Lately, I've noticed changes in my own behavior and emotions that I've never experienced before. It's been really unsettling, especially since we're in the process of separating. Could I actually develop borderline personality disorder myself? I feel like I'm losing control of my mind.

Counselor: It sounds like you're in a difficult situation, and it's important to explore your feelings and concerns. It appears that there are trust issues and a lack of independence in your relationship. Cheating is a complex issue, and it's important to reflect on your actions and the impact they have had on your relationship. It might be helpful to consider why you felt the need to seek emotional or physical connections outside of your relationship.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for 6 years. We have two young daughters together, but we took a one-year break during that time. We argue constantly and it's really starting to take a toll on my mental health. I've tried explaining to him how he makes me feel and suggesting ways he could improve, but it seems like whenever I express my concerns, he just sees it as me complaining. I constantly find myself repeating the same issues, like feeling alone and not receiving help with the kids. Additionally, he has no rules for his 17-year-old, who also doesn't listen to me. Whenever we do manage to have a conversation and agree on something, he ends up going against it and doing whatever he wants.

I've been with my husband for 5 years now. We just got married a little over a year ago and we have a 14 month old son together. I'm also pregnant with our second child. Two days before we got married, he told me he cheated on me with 2 women. We've been able to move past that. He recently returned from bootcamp, and I found some suspicious texts in his phone from a girl he went to high school with. He had her name saved as a man's name and initially lied about who she was. I also discovered emails between him and another girl, where he gave her his number to keep in contact. He admitted to seeing this girl while we were dating. I don't know if I can trust him anymore. Is there any way to work this out?

It seems like your mother has been experiencing severe paranoia for the past 10 years, which started after your parents separated. She has been accusing your father of causing damage to different parts of the house. These perceived damages include natural black knots in the wood grain of paneling, wear on furniture that has been there for years (although she believes it's new), and creaky floorboards that she believes your father intentionally damaged. It's concerning that she has hysterical fits where she cries and calls your dad 'crazy.'

I have been experiencing some significant changes in my mood recently. I used to be much more balanced and content, but now I find myself getting easily upset and even crying for no apparent reason. There have been several challenging events in my life, and I've come to realize that I'm not living life to the fullest anymore. It used to be my motto, but now I feel like I'm the complete opposite. I really want to put myself back together and regain my happiness. I've forgotten how to truly enjoy life, and my schedule is incredibly dull compared to others my age. I would really appreciate your help in finding my way back to happiness.

Lately, I've been experiencing a constant nagging feeling when I get home. It's a sense of worthlessness, as if I'm broken or beyond repair. I don't have any suicidal thoughts, but I do fear that I won't have enough time to fix my problems before something bad happens. At work, I excel and receive praise, but my relationship with my mother, who currently lives with me, has always been difficult. She often says hurtful things, like calling me a 500lb loser, even though I am overweight but not that much. Her aggressive behavior and constant fights when I come home ruin my entire day. In my mind, I know who I want to be and what I want to do, but I feel paralyzed. I want to lose weight, but I struggle with willpower and self-control. My relationships always end in angry and hateful words. I want to turn my life around and establish some structure. What steps should I take?

Over the past couple of years, I have been experiencing episodes of overwhelming dread and hopelessness that occur randomly. During these times, I find myself contemplating whether or not it would be better if I were dead. These feelings can last for a month or longer. Additionally, I also have episodes of intense anger towards others for no apparent reason. When this happens, I feel helpless because I don't understand what triggers it. These episodes can last for a few hours to a few weeks. It's a really unpleasant experience and I don't know what to do.

"I'm a 25-year-old who was discharged from the navy a year ago. Since then, I've been feeling extremely depressed and lost. I don't have a sense of purpose in life and it's putting a strain on my relationship with my fiancée. I feel incapable of learning new skills and my mind feels slow. I'm having difficulty concentrating and articulating myself. I feel like I'm mentally impaired. I thought about seeing a neuropsychologist, but for now, I want to focus on treating my depression. I've been taking Wellbutrin, but it doesn't seem to be helping. I'm heartbroken because I really want to get better for my fiancée and myself, but I don't know what steps to take. Can you give me some guidance?"

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for over two years now, but for the past year, I haven't felt any desire to be intimate with him. We hardly even hug or kiss anymore. Despite still caring for him and finding him attractive, I can't bring myself to make an effort to please him. We also have different views on many subjects and don't really have fun together. Lately, I've been wondering if I would be happier being single and have been fantasizing about passionate encounters with other men, although not anyone specific.

Hi there, I have been dating my boyfriend for about 8 months and we have a sexually active relationship. Early on, he started expressing his preference for wearing track/athletic pants during our intimate moments. He finds pleasure in the sensation they provide against his skin. He also frequently requests that I wear them, specifically without underwear, and enjoys the physical connection we experience while wearing them together. Additionally, he seems to have a foot fetish as he often inquires about my socks and suggests which ones I should wear.

I have been in a relationship with a man for the past 5 years. We have a lot in common and enjoy being active together. However, there are some challenges that arise when it comes to our families. My family is very close-knit, with 9 siblings and my mother in a nearby nursing facility. I am also close to my 2 grown children. On the other hand, my partner doesn't have a close relationship with his 3 children, as they don't get along. Whenever we have family gatherings or if any of my loved ones are going through a tough time, my boyfriend seems to get stressed, angry, and ultimately leaves. This has happened 4 times already. He claims to love me but finds it difficult to cope with my family. I've tried involving his family in our outings, but it hasn't worked out well. He proposed to me last Christmas, but has now left again. Any insights?

Hello, I recently stumbled upon your website while searching for information on how to talk to my doctor about my concerns with ADHD. I'm 20 years old and I took the initiative to make an appointment on my own. I'm having issues with my mom who dismisses my struggles as being dramatic. I constantly have negative thoughts about my body image and when I become overwhelmed, I engage in patterns of binging and purging. I also have a short temper and find it difficult to handle being yelled at. In high school, I used to restrict my food intake and was always thin. Looking back, I wish I had spoken up about my struggles. Now, I find myself overeating when I'm stressed, which is quite often. I have trouble focusing at work, even though I have a great internship where everyone is nice and supportive. I struggle to complete computer work and often lose track of time. On my days off, I tend to stay in bed for the majority of the day, and the morning quickly turns into the afternoon without me realizing it. I am a motivated person and always have a to-do list, but it takes me a long time to get out of the house. Schoolwork is particularly challenging, even when I turn off my phone and eliminate distractions. I'm about to enter my junior year of college and the past year has been very difficult for me. My mom believes that I am simply distracted and having too much fun. I feel like I have to put in more effort than everyone else, which adds to my stress. I'm not partying or watching TV, I just struggle to focus and retain information. It's incredibly frustrating. My boyfriend has ADHD and he suggested that I research ADHD as well. I'm not saying that I have ADHD, but I do identify with some of the symptoms. I'm seeking guidance and support. I visited a regular doctor because I'm not too old for a pediatrician and I'm not physically ill. During the appointment, I ended up crying for no reason, so I left with an anxiety/panic coping packet instead of any answers. I have a short temper and find myself getting upset over little things during important conversations. Upon reflection, I realize that my thinking was off. I don't know what to do. There are many factors contributing to my difficulties, but I have an appointment with a psychiatrist coming up and I'm afraid of not knowing what to say. When I tried talking to my parents about how I feel, they dismissed me. And when I mentioned my struggles to the doctor I saw once, I was given an anxiety packet. I've read through the coping strategies, but holding my breath for 5 seconds doesn't take away my anger. I've always been prone to screaming, raising my voice, and getting into fights. When I try to hold it in, I end up crying for no reason. I'm not sure where I'm going wrong or where to turn for help.

I've been in a long-distance relationship with my girlfriend, and we recently got engaged. However, since getting engaged, she has stopped having sex with me and says she wants to wait until marriage. This is confusing to me because she has had casual sex with other guys in the past without any issues. She also doesn't kiss me as much anymore and has even called me by her exes' name a couple of times. She's asked me to stop calling her during the day and wants us to talk less. It feels like she doesn't love me anymore. I would appreciate any advice you have.

Patient: I'm really struggling with my father's alcoholism. He denies being an alcoholic because he doesn't drink every day, but he would if he could afford it. When he goes out, he drinks a lot and becomes abusive and violent. He verbally abuses my mother every day and destroys things in the house. He also used to physically harm me when I was younger, leaving me with bruises, a black eye, and even locking me in the shed as punishment. I'm no longer living at home, but I'm still dealing with the impact of his behavior. My father is also extremely jealous of my close relationship with my mother and acts out whenever we spend time together. I was recently in a car accident, and while my mother rushed to the hospital, my father didn't even bother to check if I was okay. This situation is really upsetting me, and I'm worried about my mother's health as well. I don't want to be here anymore, but I don't want to leave my mother alone to deal with this. She means everything to me, and I don't know what to do anymore. We both need help.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for almost 2 1/2 years. I'm 17 years old and he is 20. Things were great in the beginning, but since I moved to a different city about an hour away, he has become distant. He doesn't call me as often and we only see each other on weekends. I've expressed my concerns to him, but he doesn't seem to care. It feels like he only wants a girlfriend on the weekends and is single during the week. This really bothers me because I depend on him since I don't have a good relationship with my parents and don't have any friends. I feel abandoned and don't know what to do.

Patient: Lately, I've been feeling like I'm losing my emotions. Activities that used to bring me joy, like listening to music and playing jazz, no longer have the same effect on me. It's distressing because I want to pursue a career in music. I initially thought it could be exhaustion or stress from school, but even during the holidays, I'm feeling worse. I wonder if loneliness could be a factor, as it affected me earlier this year. I've been wanting a girlfriend, but I keep coming up with reasons or excuses that prevent me from pursuing a relationship. Can you help me?

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for 6 1/2 years. We have a strong bond and I am very much in love with him. However, there is a significant challenge in our relationship due to my family's disapproval of my boyfriend's skin color. When we first started dating, my dad reacted violently and kicked me out of the house. Although my dad's attitude softened after a car accident, he still pretends that I don't have a boyfriend. I am now 22 years old and feeling stressed about the prospect of leaving home and facing my family's rejection. I would appreciate guidance on how to navigate this situation and when would be the right time to discuss my relationship with my family.

I am really concerned about my brother, Chris. He is 51 years old and his behavior last weekend was extremely troubling. My father, who is 83, ended up calling the local Mental Health Association for assistance. The association sent someone who called the police. The police ended up handcuffing Chris and taking him to the emergency room, but he was eventually released because of the Mental Health Act. Chris has been experiencing auditory hallucinations and feels like he has no control over them. This is causing a lot of distress for my father, who is very worried. I want to convince Chris to seek help, but he is also refusing to see his doctor for his psoriasis. If I can get him to go to the doctor for his skin condition, do you think I could talk to the doctor privately and discuss Chris's mental health concerns? Chris is also obese and refuses to work or leave the house. He talks about having a "telephone system in my head" and even mentions thoughts of harming others. He has episodes of extreme rage. I'm really scared and don't know what to do. Can you please help me?

I've been feeling really overwhelmed lately and I've been carrying a heavy burden for a long time. I'm a 27-year-old married woman, and I got married in 2008. It was a love marriage and we've been together for almost 7 years now. However, shortly after we got married, I started noticing signs that my partner was cheating on me. Three months into our marriage, I found concrete evidence to support my suspicions. My husband was studying abroad and during that time, I discovered through his email account that he had been engaging in inappropriate conversations with another woman. I decided to confide in my in-laws about it, but I kept it from my own parents to avoid causing any unnecessary problems. I hoped that my in-laws would address the situation and help my husband change his ways. Unfortunately, my father-in-law dismissed it by saying that men can make mistakes and that as a wife, I should forgive him. My mother-in-law, however, made my husband promise her that he would not contact that woman again, and I thought that would be the end of it. However, as a newly married woman, living without my husband and not receiving much support from my father-in-law, the whole incident has deeply affected me and has become a recurring nightmare in my life.

I am feeling overwhelmed and concerned about my brother's well-being. My mother adopted him when he was 13, and he is now 21. He has had a difficult life, being in foster care since the age of 2, and has been labeled as mentally ill. He exhibits behaviors such as hitting his head on the wall, getting upset and not communicating, and having physical tics. He has been in special education classes and has attended multiple schools. Currently, he is in his third year of college but is struggling with regular classes. After our mother passed away, I took him in because my father couldn't handle it anymore. He has a dishwashing job but needs constant reminders and lacks reasoning. He is unable to take care of his financial responsibilities, and I feel overwhelmed as a single mother of three girls. I need guidance on how to get him the help he needs.

From a young age, I have struggled with intense anxiety surrounding change and social interactions. These anxieties have manifested in various ways, including experiencing extreme mood swings that range from feeling like a superstar to feeling overwhelmingly sad and hopeless. Throughout my life, I have been prescribed different medications for depression and anxiety, but I still feel like I don't fit in and have few friends. I used to pretend to be sick to avoid going to school or participating in class presentations. In high school, I would hide in the restroom to avoid being in front of the class. Even in my adult life, I have found myself hiding in restrooms at work to avoid public speaking situations or walking away from jobs out of fear.

Throughout my time in high school and beyond, I have noticed a pattern in my relationships. I have consistently found myself unable to be alone and have continuously entered into monogamous relationships, one after the other. Some of these relationships have lasted for years, while others have only lasted a few months.

I have been struggling with depression for most of my life. In high school, I was diagnosed with dysthymic disorder depression, and since then, I have also experienced eating disorders, anxiety, and panic disorders. These conditions have also led to various medical problems, such as gastrointestinal issues and migraines. I have sought help from different psychologists and psychiatrists, and I have tried numerous medications including Celexa, Wellbutrin, Abilify, Remeron, Lexapro, Zoloft, Xanax, and Pristiq. Unfortunately, none of them have seemed to work and the side effects have been difficult to handle. Could I have treatment-resistant depression? Are there any other treatment options besides medication and therapy?

I work in a busy and emotionally challenging job, providing care for elderly individuals. Since childhood, I have frequently had dreams and a fascination with boarding schools. However, since 2002, after watching the film 'The Magdalene Sisters', I have been plagued by recurring dreams both day and night, in which I am a victim of institutional abuse. It's quite bizarre, considering I had a happy and normal upbringing in a loving family. Lately, these dreams have become distressing, and I seem to find reminders of them everywhere I look. Could it be that I was emotionally scarred by the movie? Or is it possible that I have been in an institution in a past life, or will be in one in the future? I worry that I may be irrational, but I feel the need to share and seek advice. Is this a problem? I hope I have explained myself clearly, and I would appreciate any guidance you can provide.

I've always had this deep-seated belief that my mother hates or resents me. It feels like it's been there my whole life, and I can't help but carry it with me. There are numerous events and situations that have contributed to this belief, but I'll try to give you a summary.

A few weeks ago, I was the best man for a wedding and shared a hotel room with the groom. After a night of drinking, he opened up to me and confessed that he had feelings for me, beyond just a sexual attraction. I initially dismissed it as him being drunk, but the next morning, things escalated and we ended up fooling around. He got married a week later, and I was there to support him, but it's been difficult for me. We haven't talked about what happened, and I don't want to make it into something bigger than it is. However, I'm worried that he may have a breakdown because he tends to keep things bottled up. I also feel like I'm on an emotional roller coaster, going from sad to happy to angry. It's especially tough because we work together and pretend like nothing happened, but it's eating me up inside and I'm feeling confused.

Lately, I've been feeling really concerned about my abilities as a learner and my social anxiety, especially in new social situations. I recently started a new job and unfortunately didn't pass my 3-month probation period. The feedback I received was that I took too long to grasp the job responsibilities, made frequent errors, and worked too slowly. This wasn't a surprise to me, as I was already informed about these issues 4 weeks into the job. Despite working extra hours and putting in a lot of effort, I still couldn't keep up with my colleagues. I've had similar feedback from previous employers as well. It's making me wonder if I have a learning issue or a low IQ, and how I can improve myself. I'm currently in another job and would really like to succeed. So far, the feedback has been mostly positive, but I'm still struggling with working longer hours, checking my work thoroughly, and achieving sales targets. I'm aware that my employers expect my performance to improve over time. Time management is a major challenge for me, and I've been researching different techniques to improve. Any advice you have would be greatly appreciated.

I've been married for 3 years and I have this constant need to be the only beautiful and attractive person for my partner. Even though my husband assures me that he feels the same way towards me, I can't stop questioning him about it. This leads me to constantly ask him questions and compare his answers, which I know is not healthy. I want to change my behavior and be sure of our relationship without always asking and thinking negatively. Can you please provide some guidance and advice on how to do that?

I'm a 14-year-old from England. Lately, things have been changing for me. My family isn't well-off, but I have the basic things that a teenager needs like a laptop and a phone. I've always known that I can't have everything I want, but recently I thought I would be happy with a cheaper brand of smartphone instead of an iPhone. However, my mom didn't follow through and now I'm feeling really upset. She also said I couldn't get a dress for an upcoming party. I've been lashing out at my mom and saying hurtful things, but she thinks it's more than just hormones. I've been crying a lot at school and everything feels different. I feel like no one understands me. Is this some kind of mid-life crisis?

Throughout my entire life, I have struggled with certain aspects of myself. I've done some self-reflection, but it seems like I haven't reached the level of understanding that many others have. I consider myself a generally happy person with a great life and many positive things going for me. The main challenge I face is dealing with my father, who has been struggling with alcoholism.

I've been doing some research online and I stumbled upon a disorder called Dissociative Disorder. I'm 13 years old and I have dyslexia, so please excuse any misspellings. I'm not sure if it's just me being forgetful or if it could be this disorder. According to the article, I tend to get lost in thought about my problems, which can cause gaps in my memory. I often find myself constantly thinking about my problems, which can trigger physical sensations like a racing heart and a twisting feeling in my stomach. Sometimes, I get angry when I think about it. I also tend to dwell on certain problems, which leads me to overthink and get lost in my thoughts.

I was involved in a car accident when I was 17. My best friend and I were hit by a woman who didn't stop at a stop sign. Luckily, we only suffered minor injuries, but unfortunately, the other woman did not survive. I feel a tremendous amount of guilt, and now I'm too scared to drive. My parents don't understand why I can't drive, and it's causing frustration because I need to be able to drive for school and work. Is it normal to feel this way? How can I overcome this fear and move forward with my life?

I've been married to my husband for 4 years now, and I'm really struggling with his constant groping behavior. It happens all the time, even when our 10-month-old son is present, while I'm changing diapers, and even when I'm sick. I've communicated my discomfort to him multiple times, but it only stops temporarily before starting again.

Patient: I have struggled for many years with a lack of emotion. It's something I've noticed since childhood, even in pictures where I never seem to smile. I've been trying my best to fit in and express the right emotions by observing others in similar situations. However, I also suffer from social anxiety, and isolating myself only makes things worse. Despite these challenges, I am a union representative at work and a successful student in college. Although deep down, I would prefer to be a missionary, I have a tendency to do what is expected of me.

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for 2 and a half years. However, for the past year, I've been feeling a lack of desire to be intimate with him. It has gotten to the point where I can't even make an effort to please him, and we're not intimate in any way. Although I still love him, find him attractive, and care for him, I know that something isn't right. We have different views on many topics, and we don't seem to have fun together. Lately, I've been contemplating whether I would be better off being single and have found myself fantasizing about other men and passionate encounters, although not anyone specific.

Hi, my name is Abby. I've been struggling with these feelings since I was 10 years old, and it seems like things are only getting worse. Every night before bed, I find myself crying and hating myself. I know there are people who have less than me and are stronger, which makes me feel weak and worthless. I just want to be skinny, beautiful, and find love. I occasionally cut myself, and I try not to eat, but if I do, I make myself throw it up. These problems with eating and cutting started when I was 14, and I don't have anyone to talk to about it without getting yelled at. They say it's wrong, and I know it is, but I can't seem to care. I just don't know what to do anymore.

I dated my ex-boyfriend for a little over 2 years, but we broke up about 6 months ago due to various problems in our relationship, including his emotional cheating and dishonesty. I struggled with jealousy during our time together, which was a result of his actions. Recently, we have started seeing each other casually again, and things have been going well. We have both grown and changed during our time apart, and I feel like there may be potential for a future together. However, I still find myself feeling jealous at times and struggling to trust him completely. I want to start fresh and have a healthy relationship, but it's difficult to forget what happened in the past. I worry that my jealousy will ruin this new chance at happiness. How can I learn to trust him again and let go of my jealousy? Or should I be concerned that he will revert to his previous behavior?

I'm really concerned about my 16-year-old cousin. She's been engaging in risky behaviors like drinking, doing drugs, and having unprotected sex. She even goes to school and takes tests while under the influence. Despite recently starting to go to church and promising to change, she hasn't followed through. She has a loving family, but they often fight, and she doesn't seem to connect with them. Her older brother went through similar issues and tragically passed away a few years ago. I'm worried about her well-being. Is there anything I can do or say to help her understand the consequences of her actions?

I've been dating my boyfriend for a couple of weeks now, but we haven't been able to see each other since school ended. His parents are divorced, so he's in another part of the state for the summer. We talk on the phone every night, but it's usually late because both of us are busy. Our conversations can go on for hours, sometimes until 3 in the morning. Lately, my parents have been getting mad and taking my phone away, not allowing us to talk at night. I want to tell them about the date we're planning, but I know they won't let me go. My boyfriend is amazing and makes me so happy. It's frustrating that my parents already dislike him, especially because his parents are fun and supportive. Their disapproval really bothers me, and I'm embarrassed by the situation. I just wish my parents could see how much happier I am now and how much I love him. Can you help me?

I've been in a relationship with my fiancé for six years, and we've been engaged for six months. We met when we were teenagers and went through some rough patches, breaking up twice during the first three years. However, we managed to work through our issues and have been living together for the past three years. Recently, I discovered that he cheated on me over a year ago, but I also confessed that I had cheated on him around seven months ago. We went to couple's therapy and tried to move forward, but now I'm having doubts after a recent argument. I'm confused and afraid of making the wrong decision. Additionally, I'm annoyed by my fiancé's mother and the tension between him and my sisters. I want to get married and have a family, but I'm unsure if we're truly meant to be together.

Five years ago, I made the decision to take custody of my 5-year-old grandson and 3-year-old granddaughter. At the time, I was in a difficult marriage, and this decision ultimately ended it. Initially, I thought it would be temporary, as my son, their father, was in prison but planned to take care of them when he was released. Their mother had lost custody due to her drug use and involvement in illegal activities. However, I soon realized that my son would struggle financially and with staying out of trouble. Their mother claims to be sober now but is unable to care for her four children. Since the kids have come to live with me, both have been diagnosed with ADHD. I feel responsible for their security, but I'm miserable. My friends are enjoying their lives after raising their own kids, while my family offers no emotional support. They exclude us from meals and events, and my brother dismisses my concerns. I believe I deserve a clean and odor-free home, but I keep finding dirty clothes stuffed in drawers and closets. Taking privileges away hasn't improved the situation. It feels like the kids have more support than I do, and I'm exhausted from feeling miserable, unhappy, and lonely. I've been prescribed Wellbutrin (300 mg) to help manage my constant crying, and I've tried therapy before, but they all tell me to take better care of myself and find a support system. It's not that simple when you're dealing with financial and logistical challenges like finding babysitters. I've searched for grandparent support groups without success, and I don't know how much longer I can hide my distress.

My daughter is 3 years old and her father and I have been separated for almost 2 years. During that time, I went through a lot of challenges including postpartum struggles, hormone imbalances, stress, the loss of a family member, and health issues related to cancer that required treatment. Emotionally, it was overwhelming. Meanwhile, her father started dating a coworker shortly after we split. I got engaged at one point, but that relationship didn't work out either. My ex-fiancé became very clingy and needy, playing mind games to test how much I cared. It became too much for me to handle, so I put up emotional walls. I tried to explain to him that if I didn't care, I wouldn't have gotten pregnant or engaged in the first place. Although that relationship ended, I feel relieved and no longer controlled. Our personalities were just too different, and I was seeking someone to fill the void of hurt.

I'm really concerned about my best friend. She's been struggling with suicidal thoughts and her parents don't seem to be taking it seriously. I've told a teacher and a counselor at school, but they just suggest seeing a psychiatrist. It's really distressing because she has visible self-harm marks on her body. Her mother has a history of being in and out of prison, and my friend has experienced a lot of losses and difficult situations in her life. She lost her grandmother, had to move, lost friends, and even had to witness the death of her pet. She's also dealing with her mother's mental health issues, including bipolar disorder and borderline personality disorder. In school, she's been bullied and labeled because of her appearance and the people she hangs out with. She started cutting herself last summer, and although she currently only has scars, she's thinking about doing it again. I want to know how I can help her and what I can say to encourage her to stop cutting.

I have been struggling with a problem that has taken control over my life. I constantly worry about it, day and night. I've come across an article on the internet about "memory hoarding" and it resonated with me, but I haven't found anyone else who experiences this. It's different from what I understand as OCD. This issue also seems to be causing other problems in my life. I have this overwhelming need to remember every detail of my daily life - what I did, where I went, and who I was with. It has become the center of my existence. A few months ago, I fell behind in recording this information, and it has thrown me into a downward spiral. I feel an intense pressure to catch up, but it feels impossible. The anxiety keeps building up because I haven't been able to carry out my usual compulsions to relieve it. It's impacting my daily life significantly. For example, I have piles of things scattered around my house, and they have to stay exactly where they are. When someone, like my mom, tries to tidy up or move things, it drives me to the point of insanity. I need to know where everything is at all times. I can't even wear certain clothes because they have to stay in their designated place. I often avoid situations because of this, like requesting a new exam timetable instead of moving the existing one from my room. This is just a brief description of my main problem, and I believe it's causing other issues as well. I feel like there's something else going on that is preventing me from finding relief through recording the information I need. It's as if I can't even start after neglecting it for so long, almost half a year now. I have trouble focusing and concentrating unless it's something I enjoy or find interesting. I'm constantly distracted and find it hard to listen when others talk to me. I also lack empathy for others. My mind is always racing, and it drives me crazy. I desperately want to get organized because it helps me manage the memory hoarding, but I just can't seem to do it. I don't know where to start. Thirdly, my personality and relationships with others have been affected. I can't stand being alone anymore, which is a recent change because I used to enjoy my own company. When I am alone, I spiral down into feelings of emptiness and hopelessness. I constantly crave fun and feel like everyone else is out there having a great time without me. I struggle with being unorganized, leaving things until the last minute, and missing important deadlines. I hope this gives you a sense of my problem, and I'm really hoping for some guidance. Thank you.

Hi, my name is Malana and I'm 15 years old. I have been struggling with Trichotillomania for some time now, and it has been difficult for me. I frequently pull hair from various parts of my body, including my scalp, eyebrows, eyelashes, and even my pubic area. As a result, I have lost most of my eyelashes, a significant portion of my eyebrows, and have developed two bald spots on my head. I have been actively searching for an inpatient rehab or treatment center specifically for Trichotillomania or impulse control disorders, but unfortunately, I haven't had much luck finding one. I'm worried that if I don't receive help soon, my condition will worsen and I will lose all the hair on my head. I have tried medication and have seen a psychiatrist, but so far, it has only helped with my depression and not my hair pulling. I'm feeling lost and not sure what to do. If you could assist me in finding a rehab or treatment center that specializes in this condition, I would greatly appreciate it. I'm open to any form of help that can make a difference. Thank you.

I've been experiencing what I believe to be anxiety and it's been overwhelming my thoughts. Every day, I'm consumed by feelings of insecurity, stress, and obsessive thoughts. It's difficult because these emotions seem to come out of nowhere. I'm only 16 years old and on the surface, my life may seem good with friends and romantic prospects, but internally, something feels off. It's like I haven't figured out who I really am. I'm currently taking Zoloft for anxiety, but I feel like there's more going on than just anxiety. My thoughts often feel foggy and I easily lose focus. This issue is holding me back from enjoying life and my grades are dropping. I find myself constantly looking in the mirror, as if I'm searching for my identity. I'm overly conscious of my appearance and whenever I learn about a new disease or disorder, I start obsessing over it and thinking I have it. At one point, I even convinced myself that I was mentally retarded. I just wish I could feel normal on the inside like everyone else. I have an appointment with a therapist in a month, but I was hoping to gain some insights or advice beforehand. Any help or information would be greatly appreciated.

I am 47 and she is 49 [now] I met Sherri at a place we both worked at, we always got along great. She was married, and we were just friends. Then she ended up getting separated, and then finally divorced. Once she was at the end of her separation, we started casually dating. Once the divorce was final, we dated exclusively. Now, four years later [this happened 3 weeks ago], she came by my place, we ate dinner, she seemed distant. I had to throw out the garbage, and she was leaving through my back door. I asked her what was going on, but she never gave me a valid response. She left, and when I came back inside, I found the jewelry I have given her over the years in a box on my counter.
