I’ve called to try and understand what’s going on and why. I ask what did I do? She replies that I didn’t do anything, she just doesn’t love me anymore or is not in love with me anymore. I say there must be a reason, but she tells me there doesn’t always need to be a reason. I have called and emailed, only to be ignored. I mentioned maybe it would be a good idea to sit with a pastor and discuss this. At first, she said yes, but the day of the meeting, she called me and said to just cancel the meeting because it wouldn’t change anything anyways. I've been trying to get her to sit with me and talk, help me understand what she’s going through, but she doesn't want to. Last night, she finally stopped by to hear what I wanted to say. I spoke, but she barely has. I said maybe we need a restart. In the past, I’ve given her chances, so I said now I’m asking for just one chance to keep it together and not just throw it away like this.

When I was 7 years old, my mom passed away from lung cancer. She was only 43. Now I'm 13, and my dad has a girlfriend who moved in with us. Since then, my dad has been distant and barely talks to me. I feel incredibly lonely, and I think that's where all my problems started. I constantly feel sad and hopeless. My weight hasn't changed, which is good. However, my sleep patterns are all over the place during the school year. Some nights I don't go to bed until 3:00 am and wake up at 6:00 am, while other nights it's the opposite. I have thoughts about death, but I'm too scared to consider it. My best friend is the one who keeps me going. Sometimes I feel happy and have high self-esteem, but other times I feel tired and have low energy. My speech is okay, but there are times when I can't talk properly. I had a breakdown in January. My stress levels are through the roof, and I do experience some anxiety, although it's not that severe. I always blame myself for things and believe that people talk about me and aren't really my friends. I've tried cutting and starving myself, but I couldn't go through with it. I have back pain and headaches for no apparent reason. My aunt has bipolar disorder, which makes me wonder if I could develop it too. I often feel fatigued and irritable. Sometimes I get angry, and I don't even know what I'm angry about. I am currently attending therapy and not taking any medication. I would appreciate your help. Thank you.

I've been feeling really helpless and misunderstood lately. Whenever I try to reach out to someone, I end up feeling let down and like nobody cares. As a result, I've started isolating myself in my bedroom, finding more enjoyment in reading and watching movies than in socializing. But even then, I feel guilty about it. I'm 19 years old and I've only had limited romantic experiences, which makes me feel self-conscious. I know it's my own fault, but it's hard to change and I'm not sure if I even want a relationship. My relationship with my parents is also strained, especially with my dad who often yells at me. My mom constantly nags me about various things, which adds to the pressure. I have intense emotional reactions, both positive and negative, and it seems to annoy my family and friends. I often wish I were different and that life was easier. What do you think I should do?

Patient: I was addicted to gambling for about 12 years. I’ve been in recovery for almost a year now. My problem is that during my addiction, I ended up pushing almost everyone out of my life without really knowing that I was doing it. I was in a fog. I didn’t feel. I couldn’t feel. But now I do, and I’ve realized that I kept people at bay and wouldn’t let them in. I need to know how to open myself up and be more friendly. I’ve met a terrific guy but have pretty much ruined any chance with him because he’s lost interest. I just find it so hard to open up, share my feelings, talk about myself. I want to be able to fix things with him. I want him to feel like I care and to feel a connection with me. How do I fix myself?

My boyfriend and I have been living together for almost 3 years and we have a child together. I have been struggling with trust issues and jealousy. It would be really helpful if he could be more open and honest about his past actions that have made it difficult for me to forgive and forget. It's possible that these unresolved issues are contributing to my difficulty in trusting him.

I'm 36 years old and I've been married for 5 years. However, my relationship with my children's father has been on and off for the past 18 years. We have four children, aged 16, 14, 10, and 5. Looking back, I realize that our relationship has never been healthy. There has been infidelity, emotional abuse, and sporadic instances of physical abuse. I must admit that I have also become physically abusive. He has a way of distorting reality, making me question myself or laughing off my pain. As long as he's happy, our family somehow manages to function.

I have been in a long-term relationship with my boyfriend for over ten years, and we have a one-year-old son together. When we got together, I already had a young daughter from a previous relationship, and although my boyfriend accepted her, they never really formed a close bond. Lately, I've been feeling really uncomfortable and worried that my boyfriend might be attracted to my fifteen-year-old daughter. I can't explain why I'm feeling this way now, but certain things he's said and done over the years have been playing on my mind, especially now that my daughter is growing into a young woman.

I recently went through a break-up with my boyfriend of 4 years and I'm feeling torn about whether I should try to reconcile or move on. Around 2 years into our relationship, he expressed a need for some time alone. We took a break for about a month, but stayed in touch through phone calls. We briefly saw each other during that time to check in. During the break, I met someone else and had sex with him. The problem is, when my boyfriend unexpectedly showed up at my house, he saw the other man there. I lied and said we didn't have sex, but the other man told the truth. We decided to continue our relationship, but my boyfriend has since found out about a few other encounters I had with the other man, which I didn't disclose at the time. Now he says he can't be with me because I wasn't honest about all the details. I still love him and want to get back together. Should I try to win him back or move on?

Hello, I'm a 20-year-old new mother and I've been dealing with what I believe is depression and severe anxiety since I was 12. I've tried various depression medications and medications to help me sleep, but nothing has worked. I stopped taking all medication when I was 17 and started self-medicating for about 2 years before stopping completely on my own. Then I found out I was pregnant and went back on depression medication because I didn't want to continue that lifestyle. However, I don't think depression is my main issue. I experience manic episodes and it's unpredictable whether I'll be high or low on any given day or hour. It's frustrating because when I'm feeling good, I know a low will follow. My anxiety is also very intense, even when I'm trying to sleep. I experience pounding heart, shaky vision, chest pain, and a lump in my throat. It also gets worse when I'm going somewhere new or around a lot of people, often leading to diarrhea. I'm currently the sole caregiver for my 8-week-old son and I can't wait until July 15th to see my doctor. I want to know your opinion on my condition and how I can get help sooner.

My son-in-law has been diagnosed with Cyclic Vomiting Syndrome, and recently his symptoms have worsened after a period of remission. My daughter and him live about two hours away from me. I've noticed that my daughter seems more stressed and distant from the family. I've asked her if there are any other problems besides the vomiting disorder, but she denies it. During my visit last weekend, I was asked to stay at a motel. However, my daughter came to visit me early one morning and revealed the truth. Her husband has been diagnosed with bipolar disorder, specifically rapid cycling, and he's been experiencing psychotic episodes, hallucinations, and blackouts. He has become irritable and verbally abusive towards my daughter. He has forbidden her from telling anyone about his condition, causing her to have panic attacks that her counselor has identified as PTSD. Additionally, he suffers from paranoia and extremely low self-esteem. Although he hasn't been physically violent yet, my daughter believes he's come close to it at one point. They have two daughters, aged 6 and 12, and my daughter has had to explain the situation to the older one. My son-in-law is receiving treatment, but the medication that seemed to help him had adverse effects on his liver, and he has difficulty keeping medication down due to his vomiting disorder. I've suspected his hostile behavior for over a year now. Last year, he got upset with me and walked out of the house, only for me to discover later that my car had been keyed. I also know that he owns multiple guns. My daughter has asked me not to tell anyone about their situation. I'm concerned about the safety of my daughter and granddaughters. What should I do to handle this situation?

Growing up, I was fortunate to have a loving and supportive family. I have two parents who cared deeply for me, and we were a family of six, with three older siblings and a younger brother who is now fourteen. My father was not only my parent but also my best friend and hero. We shared many memorable moments together and have a close bond. Even now, as an adult and married, I am grateful for the wonderful childhood I had.

It sounds like you had a privileged upbringing and achieved success in various areas of your life. However, you have always felt a sense of disconnection from others, even though you had interactions with nice people. Your parents have mentioned that you preferred playing alone as a child, which seems to indicate a long-standing discomfort with others and the world around you. Can you tell me more about how this feeling of unease manifests in your life?

This past year, 2011, has been incredibly overwhelming for me. As a junior in college, I had to juggle my demanding academic workload with preparing for the medical school graduate examination. On top of that, I had challenging science-based courses like Biochemistry and Physics II. From January to May, my stress levels were through the roof, and I was really looking forward to the relief that would come at the end of the spring semester. I managed to do well in all my classes, and I had a plan in place to take the MCAT, submit my med school applications, and then enjoy my summer abroad. Unfortunately, that plan never became a reality.

About a year ago, I made the difficult decision to leave my abusive boyfriend. It was a challenging time for me because he had control over my finances and took every penny I had. I had no other option but to seek refuge in a domestic violence shelter.
My brother has been hospitalized for 3 months for having schizophrenia and no treatment has been successful.

I've noticed some changes in my mom's behavior lately, and it's been causing me a lot of worry. We used to have a close relationship, but she's been keeping things secretive, which is unusual. I stumbled upon her Facebook messages and saw that she's been in contact with one of her old boyfriends from high school. Some of the messages made me feel really upset and there were even some with a slightly sexual tone. She even has a picture of him in her wallet and referred to him as her boyfriend. My dad, who is a truck driver, is usually only home on weekends. I don't want to disrupt our family, but I'm feeling overwhelmed and even having thoughts of self-harm. I really need guidance on what to do.

Over the past few months, I have been experiencing a rollercoaster of emotions. Last night, I felt a surge of anxiety and nervousness. This led to a sense of depression and rumination about things that should make me happy, but somehow don't. I feel conflicted about living with my parents, as I yearn for independence but question my stability to live on my own. Similarly, I feel a sense of sadness about being in a relationship with Terry, despite loving him deeply. Additionally, I feel lonely and sad about not having any friends, yet I lack the motivation to do anything about it. I became worried about my own safety, but I tried my best to push those negative thoughts away. I long for the day when these struggles become a distant memory and I can focus on normal, everyday concerns. I want to worry about trivial things like fashion and rent, rather than constantly questioning my own sanity. It's disheartening to compare myself to the strong person I used to be, and now I find myself anxious about going to sleep at night, when sleep used to bring me joy. The unsettling feeling in my stomach is always followed by intrusive thoughts. How can I stop this cycle? I've seen a therapist who prescribed Lorazepam, but I didn't like the side effects and want to conquer this naturally. While I have made some progress over the past few months, these episodes still come out of nowhere, leaving me feeling sick, scared, and worried that I may harm myself or never fully recover. Please, I need advice on how to make this go away permanently.

I am feeling extremely frustrated and overwhelmed with a challenging situation. My 11-year-old child has been diagnosed with Asperger's syndrome, and I have noticed that they only have one close friend. This friendship has been going on for about 4 years now.

I am a 22-year-old woman who has been dealing with mental health issues for most of my life. I was diagnosed with depression at a young age, and although I still experience episodes of depression, I have been managing it with therapy and medication. Lately, I've been experiencing internal auditory hallucinations, where I hear loud thoughts with distinct voices. Sometimes these voices are lighthearted, but other times they criticize me or repeat negative words. I've also been having strange fears at night, like worrying about seeing deceased individuals or being chased by ghosts. I have a family history of mental illness and psychosis, which concerns me. My psychiatrist thinks it might be anxiety or OCD, but I'm worried it could be the beginning of schizophrenia. I'm currently seeing a therapist and taking Celexa and Seroquel for my depression and the voices. I appreciate any insights you can provide. Thank you for your time.

Since starting high school, I've been feeling like I don't have any real friends. I have a lot of friends at school, but I never hang out with any of them except for one. However, she has other friends too and can't always spend time with me. I feel like a loser if I'm home alone on the weekends. This whole friend issue is making me feel insecure and like there's something wrong with me. I just want a few close friends who genuinely like me and want to hang out with me. Why is that so difficult? I just want to have fun and make good memories in high school, but without friends, it's hard to imagine. I know I should look forward to the future, but I'm really impatient and I want close friends now. I want to feel popular and accepted. The fact that making friends seems so easy for some people at my school makes me feel even worse about myself. Is all of this normal? Am I the only one feeling this way? I'm worried that high school is going to be terrible. Please help me. I just want to be happy and have friends.

Patient: I've been struggling with racing thoughts that are consuming my soul and causing extreme fear. I feel like I'm in desperate need of help and don't know what to do anymore. I've been experiencing difficulty sleeping, with episodes of insomnia lasting up to 7 days. I also feel like people are talking about me and wanting to harm me, saying cruel things and passing judgment. I have trouble focusing and understanding others at times. Additionally, I have disturbing memories of someone touching me, which is causing me distress. My psychiatrist is concerned about my experiences, including hearing strange things and having unusual visions. I feel lost and confused about my own identity, as well as the identities of others.

I have been seeing therapists who have helped me identify symptoms of bipolar I disorder. However, I am unsure if it's possible to have bipolar I without ever having received treatment or experiencing any negative consequences. Despite my manic episodes fueling a high-pressure career, I have been able to self-monitor and control my tendencies to overwhelm others with my activity and talkativeness. I haven't had a depressive episode since 1991, and even though my first one almost led to a psychotic break, I managed to get through it without any intervention. My family also claims they have never had any issues with my behavior.

I recently discovered that the man I was in a long-distance relationship with for 2 years is actually a new senior pastor at a church and is also married. I found this out by doing some online research. When I confronted him about it, he told me that he has been separated from his wife for almost 4 years, despite being married for 20. He claims that the opportunity to become a pastor came unexpectedly in January and he believes it is a calling from God, which has led him to reconcile with his wife.

I’m 15 years old, and I have two older sisters. Lately, we've been experiencing a lot of frustration with our mom. It seems like our relationship with her is different from what I see with other kids and their parents. She tends to yell at us from across the house, even for small things like picking up something that fell near her. She gets angry quickly if we don't respond fast enough or say no to her. When we try to have important conversations, she doesn't listen and just starts yelling. For example, my oldest sister was talking to her about college expenses, and my mom went off yelling and swearing at her. Her outbursts often happen on days when we clean together. She blames us for doing something wrong and sometimes even becomes physically aggressive. It's usually me that she targets. Afterwards, she acts like nothing happened. She also believes that we're ungrateful for what she does for us, even though we try to express our gratitude. Could her behavior be due to stress or is there something else going on?

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for about a year and a half. We met at work and have been spending a lot of time together. Overall, our relationship is positive and balanced. We bring out the best in each other and support one another. We do have occasional arguments, usually around once a month, but we are able to resolve them fairly easily.

I have been going through a lot of negative experiences lately. I used to be a down-to-earth and fun person, but I feel like everything has changed. I only have one best friend, but I don't want to burden her with my problems. When I'm around a lot of people, I get really nervous and start sweating. I feel dizzy and unable to be myself. Lately, I've been quiet and declining invitations to hang out with my friends, choosing to stay at home instead. I feel this emptiness inside me every day, and my mind races with excessive thoughts. I struggle to focus and keep busy with work, but I often feel paranoid. I believe people talk negatively about me behind my back or make fun of me. I think I have low self-esteem and confidence. There have been moments where I've considered suicide, but I haven't acted on it because I know it wouldn't solve anything. I just want to understand what's happening to me so I can regain control of my life. This isn't how I used to be, and it feels like everything has turned upside down. It's been a year since my last relationship, and recent events with my friends have made it difficult for me to trust anyone. I apologize for my poor grammar.

I have a brother who often becomes extremely depressed when he sees his peers from school who are in relationships and have social groups. He struggles with making friends and has some social concerns. He is a junior in high school and I am his younger brother. I feel responsible for watching over him and ensuring his well-being. However, he is resistant to having calm conversations and tends to engage in arguments, making it challenging to communicate with him.

I recently discovered that my boyfriend of 2 years has been lying about his entire identity. I found letters addressed to him with a different surname than the one he had told me. I also saw his driver's license, which had a different year of birth than what he had told me. Additionally, I realized that I have only met two of his family members and no friends. I even found a separate Facebook account of his with his real full name, which he doesn't know I know about. I also discovered that he has a brother he never mentioned. It's really difficult for me to process all of this because he claims to love me and wants to be with me forever. I had been so open and honest with him, and all he did was lie. I can't stop wondering if he would ever come clean or if there are more secrets I haven't uncovered. I still have strong feelings for him, but now I question if I can trust anyone if the person I trusted the most turned out to be a complete fraud.

I have been struggling with depression and anxiety for most of my life due to a history of abuse. From the age of 5, when my father passed away, until I was 12, I suffered abuse from my mother and stepfather. Eventually, my stepfather sold me to his dealer, but I managed to escape in 2001. Currently, I am seeing a psychiatrist who prescribed medication for my depression. However, I am finding it difficult to find someone who can help me cope with the lingering effects of being treated as a possession rather than a person. How can I find a therapist who can understand and support me?

I have been in a relationship with my ex-boyfriend for 7 years. We met in high school and he made promises to always love and protect me. I understand that people can't always keep those promises, but I'm feeling confused about everything. I put off going to college so we could be together, but neither of us ended up graduating. We moved back to our hometown and rented a room from my parents, which has been difficult. He seems to be struggling with depression.

I am a 19-year-old mother. I have a 2-year-old daughter and I am currently 4 months pregnant. I am in a relationship with the father of my unborn child. Initially, he promised that we would live together and have a great life. However, he keeps making excuses about when I can tell his parents about the pregnancy. I am unable to share this news with my own parents because they have threatened to kick me out. My dad is always yelling at me and telling me to leave whenever he gets upset. Unfortunately, I don't have anyone else to turn to. I don't have a job, I'm not in school, and I don't have a car or a driver's license. I have been trying to improve my situation, but I haven't received any help. I'm becoming more and more upset because what was supposed to be a happy moment is turning into a nightmare. I cry every day because I sometimes feel like having this baby is the worst thing I could have done, even though it's not the baby's fault. I really need some advice on what to do.

I have been in a tumultuous relationship with my husband for several years. In the first year, I discovered that he had lied to me about his criminal background and was cheating on me. We decided to work through it and move forward. However, he continued to lie and steal, which ultimately led to him serving a year in prison. Despite these challenges, we chose to stay together because we had a son. Over time, our relationship has improved and my husband has become a supportive stay-at-home dad. He has truly become my best friend.

I've been struggling with these feelings for a while now, and I haven't been able to address them. Initially, I brushed them off as mere insecurities or a passing phase, like the fleeting thoughts we have as teenagers. However, I'm now twenty-years old, and these feelings are persisting and causing confusion in my life, even impacting others.

I've been seeing a psychiatrist for almost two years now. I've tried to bring up this issue, but every time I try, I start to panic and can't speak. I'm wondering if this could be a sign of social anxiety. Or is it something that everyone experiences on a daily basis? Also, when I say I don't like it, I mean that I actively avoid any situations that trigger it.

I've been feeling overwhelmed lately. At home, there is a lot of stress and my relationship with two of my siblings is really strained. School is also a source of anxiety for me. I'm scared to go and even think about it because I feel so confused and the workload feels overwhelming. On top of that, I have AP exams and school exams coming up and I feel completely lost. My social life is also suffering and I'm struggling to sleep, getting only about five hours a night.

I've been feeling really down lately. About three months ago, I went through a breakup with someone I was really in love with. He started losing interest in me and eventually ended things. It really hurt when he blocked me on social media. Since then, I've been crying a lot and finding it hard to enjoy things. I isolate myself in my room and feel worthless. I've also been struggling with my eating and sometimes make myself sick. I just want to be happy again.

I've been struggling with intense anger and find myself living in a fantasy world that I've created. I'm currently in therapy for social phobia, but I'm too scared to talk to my therapist about this. Ever since I was very young, my fantasy worlds have been filled with violence and madness, and I spend hours each day immersed in them. I don't have any real friends and I often feel disconnected from others. I also have this belief that I'm psychic, and it freaks people out. Another issue is my anger, which gets triggered by seemingly small things. For example, when someone takes my usual lunch seat, I get so enraged that I hurt myself. I've even had thoughts of starting a fire at school. I feel like no one understands what I'm going through. Can you help me?

Patient: I recently discovered that my boyfriend has been engaging in inappropriate behavior online, such as sending explicit pictures and messages to other women. He claims it was just a game to him and that he never intended to meet them in person. He has apologized and made some changes, like changing his phone number and deleting his profile on the website. However, I'm worried that he has a deeper issue and won't be able to stop this behavior. I love him, but I'm not sure if I can trust him again. Can you offer any advice?

Throughout high school, I had a clear vision of what I wanted to achieve in life, and I've worked hard to pursue my goals. My mother, who comes from a traditional Cuban background, wanted me to stay home for college, so I commuted to a local university instead of attending an Ivy League school. However, at the age of 20, I decided to move on campus to have the college experience I felt I was missing out on. This decision deeply hurt my mother, and she has been expressing her sadness and anger about it ever since. Despite my academic achievements and acceptance into a top graduate school, she continues to make me feel guilty and says she wants to die because her life didn't turn out the way she had hoped. This constant conflict has left me feeling miserable and unsure of what to do.

Over the past 11 years, I have had a complex relationship with my sister-in-law. Initially, we were close friends who eventually became family when I married her brother. However, after becoming in-laws, our relationship has become strained. It feels like there is an unspoken competition between us, where we constantly try to outdo each other. Recently, she has betrayed my trust by going behind my back, which has led to a fallout between us and has left me feeling very sad. I find it difficult to communicate with her because she tends to avoid discussing issues. I am afraid to confront her face to face because of her anger. We have had ongoing problems for a long time, and I'm starting to feel like it's becoming too much effort and that perhaps we are incompatible. Is this a common experience with sister-in-laws? I have tried to make amends recently, but she still seems determined to hold onto her anger. Should I just let it go? It's disheartening that things have to be this way.

My mother has been struggling with depression for over 35 years. It started with postpartum depression after she had her first child in 1972. Unfortunately, back then there wasn't as much awareness or understanding about it, so it went untreated for about 20 years. While I can't recall the exact time she was diagnosed, she has tried various treatments, including different medications. Eventually, she was also diagnosed with bipolar disorder, and she has gone through a multitude of medications for that as well. It seems like nothing is working, and she expresses feelings of wishing she were dead in front of everyone. She isolates herself and constantly expresses her unhappiness. I've been encouraging her to seek a second opinion, but there aren't many advanced psychiatrists in our area. They tend to rely heavily on medication, which I don't believe is the only solution. I'm feeling lost and unsure of what to do or how to convince her to seek alternative options with me.

When I was 12 years old, I experienced depression which later developed into paranoia. The thoughts I had during that time were extremely frightening and seemed life-threatening. They felt rational and logical, even though I knew deep down they weren't realistic. The paranoia became overwhelming, and I suffered silently without seeking help. Although I don't remember everything that happened during that time, I do have flashbacks reminiscent of PTSD. Eventually, the paranoia subsided, but I noticed a significant decline in my IQ and academic performance. My social life also changed, as I found it difficult to experience emotions. For the past four years, I have been dealing with most of the symptoms associated with PTSD. Recently, I began experiencing mild paranoia again, but it is more manageable this time. I've noticed a slight improvement in my IQ, although it still lags behind what is considered normal. I have seen doctors since I was 16, but none of them have diagnosed me with PTSD. They have suggested that it might be schizophrenia instead. I tried taking medication, but it wasn't very helpful, so I lost hope and stopped taking it for a year. However, I recently came across an article about PTSD, and it made me wonder if that might be the correct diagnosis. I would like to know if I am right or if it is indeed schizophrenia.

I've been experiencing some distressing thoughts and emotions lately, and I'm not sure if it's depression or something else. Although I haven't been formally diagnosed, these feelings have been getting stronger recently. I try to distract myself by playing video games or watching movies, but it seems to make things worse. I hear negative thoughts in my head, like I'm a loser, lazy, and questioning my purpose in life. It's affecting my self-worth and my relationship with my girlfriend. I'm currently unemployed, but I'm actively looking for a job and planning to go back to school soon. However, when I try to engage in activities, these overwhelming thoughts bombard me, especially about my relationship. I feel lost and in need of help. Can you please offer any guidance or assistance?

Patient: Hello, I've been feeling uncertain about my social interactions for quite some time now. Throughout my life, I've struggled to connect with others and form romantic relationships. With my 29th birthday approaching, the fact that I've never had a girlfriend is causing me some concern.

Hello. I have a history of depression from January 2010 to January 2011, and I believe I may still be experiencing symptoms. Since I stopped counseling, it has been challenging to navigate my emotions and understand what I'm going through. Now that I am starting sessions with a new counselor, I'm unsure of how and when to disclose my struggles with my sexuality. It feels incredibly personal, and I'm not sure how to approach the topic or open up about it. Can you offer any guidance on this?

I am concerned about my partner's behavior. We have been together for almost 6 months, and he has a history of excessive drinking and aggression. Recently, he confessed to hearing constant voices in his head and experiencing a sense of deja vu. He uses alcohol to numb the voices, but his anxiety medication hasn't helped. I'm not sure if this is schizophrenia or another mental illness. He has seen a psychiatrist in the past for anxiety. Can you please provide some guidance on what I should do and how I can help?

Since I was a child, I have experienced feelings of not being good enough and facing situations where I had to handle things on my own or endure being berated and ignored by my father. I was diagnosed with Bipolar I at 17, but it took until I was 44 to receive the correct diagnosis and treatment after multiple hospitalizations. Over the years, I have gained about 100 lbs since college and now have Type II insulin dependent diabetes. Aside from the health issues, I believe that my weight serves as a protective barrier from the unresolved emotions I still carry as an adult. However, I am unsure how to address this issue with my therapist. Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) has not been effective for me, and these feelings are preventing me from fully enjoying my accomplishments. Do you have any suggestions?

It sounds like you are going through a complex and challenging situation with your stepson, daughter-in-law, and granddaughters. It must be difficult to navigate all the changes and emotions involved. How are you feeling about all of this?

For the past 15 years, my mom has struggled with alcohol addiction. During that time, I took on the responsibility of caring for my autistic brother and younger sister from the age of 8 to 16. When I started rebelling and expressing my desire to have a life of my own, my mother kicked me out. I immediately sought help from Family & Children's Services to have my brother and sister removed from her care. Now, at 22 years old, my brother and sister have finally been removed after multiple cases were filed. However, my mother's drinking has been escalating over the past year. I recently got engaged, but my mother is ignoring my attempts to reach out to her. I'm torn between trying to repair our relationship or accepting that it may involve emotional abuse. What should I do?

I have been dating this guy for 5 months, and unlike previous relationships, we didn't have a honeymoon period. He seems to value personal time a lot, while I prefer to be close to my partner. As a result, we've been distant from the start, and he believes it's important to take things slow and have personal space.

I met this girl at an open party in my house about 8 months ago, and we've seen each other frequently at university since then. We started dating after she stayed over at another party in February. However, she struggles with being affectionate with me unless she's drunk. She recently shared with me that she has depression and is on medication for it.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for six years. Recently, I expressed my desire to move out because I feel like I have been dedicating all of my time and energy to him and neglecting myself. He is disabled and unemployed, so when I come home, I feel pressured to give him my undivided attention or he becomes upset. He struggles with alcohol and pain pill addiction, which worsens his behavior in the evenings. Whenever I go out with friends or attend night classes, he becomes sad and upset, claiming to be lonely. He tells me that he gave up his friends for me, although the reality is that his friends are drug addicts and I had to make a choice between them or our relationship. I often feel obligated to stay home and keep him company to prevent him from feeling lonely. We have very different personalities - there is an eight-year age gap between us, he is a momma's boy, and I come from divorced parents who live far away. I have been working since I was 15 and I am currently in college, while he never finished high school and sporadically worked before becoming disabled. I love being around people and traveling, but he struggles with social anxiety. Initially, I thought that my love and support would help him become more outgoing and motivated to engage with the world, but instead, I find myself becoming more closed off and isolated. Despite some improvements after I expressed my desire to leave, I am still uncertain about whether I should stay or go. I don't trust that things will truly get better, considering how bad they have become. However, I am afraid to leave and I can't bear to see him hurt. I have dedicated almost all of my twenties to making this relationship work, and I am constantly feeling sad. I am experiencing physical symptoms like hair loss and a lack of motivation to go out or be around others. I'm feeling lost and don't know what to do. I feel like I'm losing my sanity.

When I was 11 years old, I experienced a traumatic event where I was allegedly molested by my stepfather. I disclosed this to a teacher, which led to a trial. The stress and depression caused my mother to become overwhelmed, resulting in a suicide attempt. During this time, I was diagnosed with Dissociative Identity Disorder (DID). Eventually, I changed my story and cleared my stepfather of any wrongdoing. At the age of 13, I was admitted to an in-patient hospital following a suicide attempt and was later diagnosed with Bipolar 1. After completing a 4-month outpatient program, I moved to Atlanta with my father due to the recommendation of professionals who believed it would be beneficial for me to be away from my stepfather.

I've been noticing some confusing behavior from a coworker. He seems shy and passive at work, often keeping to himself. However, he excels in math and computer knowledge. He used to watch me from a distance without making a move, but after I approached him, he made an effort to improve his appearance. I also noticed that he tends to have conversations with older coworkers rather than people his own age. It's all a bit puzzling to me.

My son is 3.5 years old and his father is coming to visit him after being absent for 2 years. I'm feeling unsure about how to handle this situation. When I first met my ex-husband, everything seemed perfect and he was a loving husband and father. However, we moved to another country and eventually returned to our native country after I became pregnant again and my ex-husband didn't want the baby. We are now divorced and he has since remarried. He hasn't visited our son in Serbia since we returned, but recently he reached out to inform me that he wants to visit our son for two weeks and spend as much time with him as possible, including sleepovers. I'm worried about how my son will react and what the consequences of this visit might be. I want to do what's best for my son, so I'm seeking advice on how often they should see each other during those two weeks and whether I should be present for their first meeting and subsequent visits. My son will be almost 4 years old when the visit takes place, and I don't know if his father will visit him again in the future.

My boyfriend has been struggling with severe anxiety and depression for some time now. He has been seeking help from two different healthcare professionals - a therapist for talk therapy and another doctor who specializes in medication management. Unfortunately, none of the medications he has tried so far have been effective in alleviating his symptoms. He has been prescribed various medications for depression, mood stabilization, anxiety, sleep, and antipsychotics. Recently, during his therapy session with the doctor who manages his medication, they discussed his depression and anger following the tragic murder of a family friend. According to him, the doctor advised him to "hold it in." I was taken aback by this suggestion. It seems counterproductive to ask someone with severe depression and anxiety to suppress their emotions, which can ultimately lead to a buildup of emotional distress. Am I wrong in thinking this?

I'm a 21-year-old individual who has been in a relationship with a 29-year-old who used to struggle with cocaine addiction. We've been together for six months, and I made it clear from the beginning that I would not tolerate drug use in my life. However, I recently caught him in a lie about trying to obtain drugs. I'm in denial about the situation and worried about how this might impact my trust in him and relationships with other women.

I'm a sixteen-year-old girl who lost my dad when I was twelve. He was an amazing father and we had a great relationship. I've been feeling really confused about my current relationship with my boyfriend. We started dating because he was sweet and liked me a lot. But lately, I've noticed some warning signs. He gets easily frustrated and agitated, and he becomes possessive and controlling. He demands my social media passwords and restricts me from talking to or being friends with boys. He even threatened to harm himself if I didn't cut ties with my best friend. I've also started mimicking his behavior, feeling jealous and becoming increasingly isolated. I've even resorted to self-harm and thoughts of running away or hurting myself. I feel so lonely and confused, and I just want someone to talk to who can help me.

I have been struggling with severe depression for the past 30 years. I have tried numerous medications and combinations as listed in the PDR, and I have been on medication for over two decades. I have also seen multiple therapists and psychiatrists, undergone ECT, and been hospitalized several times. I have tried various alternative therapies such as bi-lateral stimulation, energy tapping, aromatherapy, exercise, relaxation techniques, and yoga. Unfortunately, I can't afford the expensive treatments like Transcranial Stimulation, Vagus Nerve Stimulation, or newer brain surgeries as they are considered experimental. I experience daily bouts of hysteria due to the overwhelming frustration and pain of my depression and anxiety. I often find myself crying out for help, feeling exhausted and desperate. I have even had multiple suicide attempts. I feel completely worn out, crushed, and trapped in this never-ending pain. I am desperate for relief and even contemplating a peaceful end. It feels like reaching out for help is like throwing a message in a bottle. What should I do?

I have been experiencing feelings of inadequacy and impostor syndrome in various areas of my life. This includes my job, friendships, and even as a parent. I constantly worry that I don't belong and that others will discover I am a fraud. These feelings have been present for a few years, but I only recently became aware of them. I remember feeling this way during college, but I attributed it to not liking my major. Strangely, I also struggle to feel a connection with my own child, despite knowing I gave birth to her. I'm terrified that if I open up about this, someone will take her away. I'm currently being treated for depression, but keeping everything bottled up feels overwhelming. Can you help me understand what's happening?

Patient's statement (rewritten): I have been experiencing difficulties in my current relationship due to my jealousy and trust issues with my boyfriend. We have been together for about a year and a half. My past relationships have made it challenging for me to trust men, as I have been convinced that all men cheat. I am constantly afraid of getting hurt and find myself assuming that my boyfriend will cheat on me. I become jealous when he accepts female friends on his Facebook page, and when he goes out with friends, I worry that he might be seeing another woman. I even check his phone bill account to see if he has been talking to any girls, and although I haven't found any evidence of that, I still struggle to trust him. This lack of trust and jealousy leads me to become angry and yell at him. I also have low self-esteem and constantly feel like I am not attractive enough for him, despite him telling me otherwise. I question his love for me and often accuse him of lying. These issues have caused numerous arguments, and I fear that I might lose him if I don't address them. I am seeking guidance on how to stop this destructive behavior and salvage my relationship.

Patient: I feel stuck and overwhelmed. I'm 24 years old and I don't have any significant work experience. I had to leave college because I couldn't afford it, so now I'm living with my mother. I've struggled with my weight since I was young and I was constantly teased in school. It got so bad that I started making excuses to avoid going to school, which affected my grades and prevented me from qualifying for scholarships. On top of all that, I've been dealing with suicidal thoughts since I was 12, but my best friend thinks I'm just joking because I use sarcasm a lot. My family doesn't believe in seeking help and they expect me to just pray and tough it out because life is hard.

About 4 years ago, my mom left an abusive husband and started dating a man who has a son. This son is only a few months younger than me. Since we first met, we had a connection and unintentionally developed romantic feelings for each other. We both have trust and abandonment issues, but he knows how to comfort me without even knowing about my struggles. We bring out the best in each other, although we have had some problems. Our relationship has grown over the years, and I know for certain that I'm in love and have no interest in anyone else. We've talked about our feelings, and he says he loves me too. We've been in a steady relationship since January, but no one else knows about it except us. We've told our friends that we are in relationships, just not with each other.

I have been in a complicated relationship with my boyfriend for many years. We have been living together for two years, but our relationship has been on and off for a total of nine years. During one of our breaks, I got married to someone else, but still maintained a connection with my ex-boyfriend. However, after only one week of marriage, my husband was deployed and I ended up getting back together with my ex-boyfriend while still legally married. When my husband returned, I asked for a divorce and moved in with my ex-boyfriend. We have been together ever since, but now he doesn't want to marry me. He says it's because he can't forget our complicated past and believes it's too late for us to work things out, even though we have been living together for two years. It has only been a week since I moved out, but he continues to text me, expressing that he misses me and wants me back. However, he also insists that we can't be together and that it's too late. I am feeling confused and unsure about what to do.

Recently, I started therapy to address some issues in my life. It's a new experience for me to have someone listen and understand me. My therapist has been really attentive, but now I'm finding myself attracted to him and thinking about him in a sexual way during our sessions. I know it's not appropriate and won't act on it because he's my therapist and married. However, it's affecting my ability to focus during therapy. I don't want to lose him as my therapist but I also don't know how to handle these feelings. I have bipolar disorder, but I'm aware that being attracted to a therapist is not uncommon. Can you provide some guidance on how to navigate this situation?

Hello, I am an undergraduate student who is currently in my final year of studies. I have been experiencing a lot of emotional turmoil lately. A few years ago, my fiancé cheated on me, which led me into a state of depression. This year, I also had a falling out with my best friend, and I have been feeling a lot of guilt about it. On top of that, I have been dealing with frequent physical illnesses, specifically urinary infections, for the past two years. This has resulted in me constantly taking medications. I have always had a weak memory and needed to revise my studies frequently, but recently, I have been experiencing severe forgetfulness. I find myself daydreaming a lot and my mind feels overwhelmed with thoughts. When it comes to my coursework, I struggle to concentrate and often find myself getting distracted by the internet or phone calls. It feels like I am trying to avoid doing my work. I try to force myself to concentrate, but it leads to intense headaches. Sometimes, it feels like there's a huge basketball bouncing inside my head. However, I don't experience these symptoms when I am reading a novel or just relaxing. Since I am studying independently, I spend most of my time at home. I feel quite lonely. I want to study, but I find it difficult to concentrate due to the pain in my head and constant daydreaming. I feel lazy, lethargic, and often depressed because of the overwhelming thoughts in my mind. I also have difficulty controlling my talking, often resorting to singing to myself. I feel like a volcano ready to explode. My temper is short, and I snap at people easily. Minor issues can upset me to the point of crying, which seems to be a release for my pent-up emotions. The only time I feel at peace is when I am sleeping. Do you think it would be beneficial for me to visit a psychiatrist? Or is this just me being lazy and avoiding work? I'm feeling desperate and in need of help.

Counselor: Thank you for sharing your experiences and feelings with me. It takes a lot of courage to talk about what you've been through. Based on what you've described, it sounds like you are experiencing symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) related to the abuse you endured in your past relationship. Flashbacks and intrusive memories are common symptoms of PTSD. It's understandable that these experiences have been distressing for you.

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for 1 year and 2 months. I genuinely love him and believe he loves me too. However, he tends to get easily upset over small things and stays mad for a long time, despite my efforts to make him happy. Sometimes, it's because of something I did, but it can be anything really. He never admits he's mad, he just says he's frustrated. However, his frustration often involves yelling and cursing, which feels like anger to me. Even when he's not mad at me, we end up arguing because I can sense that something is bothering him, but he won't communicate it clearly. He tells me to drop it when I ask, but I struggle to know when it's truly nothing or if he wants me to persist. I want to be with him, but the frequent arguments and his quick temper make it difficult. I feel like I have to constantly tread carefully around him to avoid making things worse. I'm at a loss and would really appreciate your guidance. Thank you.

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for four years, but over a year ago, I discovered that he was exchanging intimate emails with his ex-girlfriend. He denied sleeping with her and got angry at me for reading his emails. Now, whenever he goes back to his home state where she lives, I become incredibly paranoid. Recently, he had an appointment that got rescheduled, and when I called him, he seemed distracted and kept getting off the phone. I feel like he's cheating on me, but I don't know why I feel this way. I'm considering telling him that I'll never trust him again, but I'm not sure if that's the right decision. I love him, but he's never said those words to me in the four years we've been together.

I have been in a relationship for almost 5 months now with someone I’ve known previously for about a year and a half. The relationship itself has been going great and I really think I am in love, however lately, I am feeling completely devoid of my libido. I am attracted to my partner but the attraction is not translating into sexual desire anymore. This has been a pretty recent thing (2 weeks or so) but it has been almost impossible for me to even have sex because I practically physically reject it. There are stress factors in my life right now, but I’ve been stressed before and its never had this drastic effect on me physically. I’m trying to figure out if I’m losing sexual desire for my partner as we get more and more comfortable together or if it's just something with me (which I feel is more likely because until recently I’ve always been crazy attracted to him). I still enjoy spending time with him, but I really want to get the sex back, it was a great part of our relationship and something I personally enjoyed.

Growing up, I had a loving family with parents who had a strong marriage. However, my mother has cyclothymic disorder, which means she experiences fluctuations in mood. She can be very loving, but she also had a tendency to yell a lot. As an only child, I had to learn to be self-reliant and strong. Now, in my relationships, I find myself becoming emotionally exhausted. I think it's because I'm always committed to persevering through challenges and I tend to attract partners who drain me emotionally.

"Well. Where do I start. I’m 16 and live in New Zealand. I know I have an anxiety disorder of some form. I also know I’m extremely likely to have depression. But sometimes I’m hyper, which is why I keep thinking I might have bipolar. My symptoms all up are panic attacks, lack of appetite, generally depressed and upset, really irregular sleep patterns, low self-esteem, self-harm (does that count as a symptom?), and sometimes I’m extremely over excited and hyper and can’t focus on anything. Being a teenager, could this be just because of that? I really don’t know if they’re mood swings from being my age or from bipolar. Absolutely nothing has happened in my life to make me this way. I have good parents, a comfortable life, I go to a good school with amazing friends.. yet I hate it all. At one stage I was in counseling, but it didn’t work out. I’d be prepared to go back if I was brave enough to ask my parents.. Please help, I need the advice."

Hello, I'm really concerned about my younger sister. Yesterday, her boyfriend tragically took his own life after she ended their relationship. She's only 19 and he was 26. They were together for two years, and during that time, she tried to break up with him multiple times but he would threaten to harm himself. We believed he was just emotionally manipulating her, but there may have been instances where he even assaulted her. Eventually, she found the courage to end things, and we were relieved. However, now his family blames her and she blames herself, even though we know it's not her fault. I'm here because I want to know how I can support her through this difficult time. Any tips or advice would be greatly appreciated. Thank you.

I am feeling overwhelmed and don't know what to do. I have been struggling with my emotions for the past three years, and it's becoming harder to handle. I come from a difficult background, with unstable living arrangements and limited financial resources. Two years ago, I attempted suicide and was hospitalized. I suspect that I've been dealing with depression for a while and need a proper diagnosis. However, I can't afford professional help. What should I do?

I've been feeling depressed and anxious for a while now. It seems like no one understands why, even though I have everything I need in life. I have a good amount of money, a loving family, and I'm studying at a prestigious college. But deep down, I struggle with confidence and have a history of being bullied. College has been especially challenging, as I can't seem to make friends and my mental health is deteriorating. I'm losing weight, feeling exhausted, and having suicidal thoughts. I don't have anyone to talk to about this, and it's taking a toll on me. I want to change, but I don't know where to start.

I am a 27-year-old woman who is feeling troubled by my boyfriend's past relationship. Before we started dating, he was in a long-term relationship with a girl for 4 years and they were sexually active. Unfortunately, their relationship ended when she cheated on him and became pregnant with someone else while they were in a long-distance relationship.

I'm feeling really conflicted about my boyfriend and my mom. My mom is against our relationship, even though she hasn't even met him. We've been together for about 6 months and my parents disapproved at first because he is white and I am Korean. After a lot of fighting, they reluctantly accepted our interracial relationship. But now, my mom wants me to break up with him because he doesn't have a college degree and comes from a different family background. She wants me to date someone with a similar education level and family background. I've tried explaining that his lack of a degree doesn't define him and that he is financially stable, but she doesn't seem to understand.

I've been through a lot in the past few years and I feel like I should seek professional help, but I'm hesitant. To give you some background, I lost two friends in separate incidents where they were hit by cars while walking. My parents divorced in 2008, remarried in 2009, and then divorced again in 2011. Now, they're getting back together and I feel caught in the middle. I've been financially supporting both of them and recently got laid off from my job. I'm on the verge of losing everything I've worked for and I have to settle for a low-paying job just to make ends meet. Let me explain the recent problems I've been facing.

I've been struggling with chronic procrastination lately. It's not just a regular "I'll do it later" kind of thing. I feel like I can't accomplish anything unless I'm under pressure. I also experience anxiety and a fear of failure, which makes it even harder to start and complete tasks.

Since I was 13 years old, I have been experiencing troubling symptoms. I often wake up in the middle of the night drenched in sweat, unable to fall back asleep. I also have periods of time during the day that I cannot remember, as if hours have gone missing. When I drive, I sometimes end up at a destination without any recollection of how I got there. Additionally, I have recurring nightmares of being chased by someone, and upon waking up, I occasionally see their shadow in my doorway. I have memories of traumatic events from my childhood, but the details are hazy. The person from my dreams reassures me when I ask about it, but I'm not sure if they are the same person who chases me. Throughout the day, I hear whispers and occasionally the person from my dreams calls my name, snapping me out of a trance-like state. I also experience migraines about twice a month and rely on high doses of Aleve to manage them. I also have smaller, sharper headaches during the day, but I can't recall when they go away. I recently had a CT scan that came back normal, but I feel like I'm losing my mind. I have been sleep deprived for years, often getting only about 10 hours of sleep a week. Sometimes, I stay awake for so long that I collapse and lose consciousness. A few weeks ago, I woke up on the street. I know something is wrong, and it's only getting worse. I'm feeling confused.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for ten months. Around seven months into our relationship, I experienced a traumatic event where my drink was spiked and I was sexually assaulted. It has been three months since then, and overall, I have been coping better than my boyfriend. Initially, I was really struggling and felt like a mess. However, I sought help from the GUM clinic and received advice and counseling, which significantly improved my understanding and well-being. The only challenge I'm currently facing is feeling incredibly anxious when I go out in the evening with my friends. I notice difficulty breathing, and I believe it's because I associate nightclubs and drinking with what happened to me.

Patient: I am a 30-year-old woman who has been in a relationship with my fiancé for a year and a half. We have been living together for 8 months and got engaged last June. However, I am struggling with trusting him due to past experiences. I was previously married for 2 years, but my ex-husband cheated on me, which ended our marriage. My fiancé hasn't given me any reason not to trust him, but his poor communication skills and lack of reassurance make it difficult for me. Whenever I try to discuss my concerns, he shuts down and we end up fighting. This leaves me feeling unsure about his feelings and intentions. Additionally, his moodiness makes the relationship feel unstable. I find myself obsessing over his emails and texts, constantly worrying about who he talks to and what he does online. I don't give him much alone time because I fear he might do something wrong. I need help with these trust issues. Thank you.

I've been feeling really down lately and it's making me question myself. I've been experiencing extreme fatigue for the past few months, constantly craving sleep and thinking about napping. When I'm not thinking about sleeping, I feel like everything in my life is going wrong, except for my husband. I've been crying easily, dealing with stomach issues, and losing interest in things I used to enjoy. I suspect it might be mild depression, but then I doubt myself and think I'm just overreacting due to stress from my job situation. Should I see a doctor or am I overreacting?

I've been struggling with these overwhelming emotions and it's really taking a toll on me. I feel scared to reach out for help because I'm worried about the possible consequences, like being sent to a mental institution or being locked away. Can you please guide me on how to seek help without these fears coming true?

I've been struggling to communicate my wants and desires to my loved ones, and it's causing issues in my relationship with my significant other. My family tends to ignore problems, so I've never really learned how to express myself. This leads me to say things that don't truly bother me, making the situation worse. At the end of arguments, I feel alone and hurt because I haven't been able to express my true wants. How can I learn to express myself without feeling like I'm hurting myself?
