About 7 weeks ago, my wife underwent a full hysterectomy due to severe abdominal pain. Everything seemed to be going well until almost 2 weeks ago when she started experiencing intense emotions and talking about her past and family. Initially, I attributed this to her surgery and offered comfort. However, things escalated when she became convinced that our neighbor, who is also her best friend, wanted her to report her husband for child abuse. This belief started to consume her thoughts and affected her ability to function properly. We had a conversation with her friend to address her concerns, which seemed to help for a few days. However, on Tuesday, she called me from the base, claiming that our neighbor's husband had harmed our children. She was taken to the hospital and has been there for 4 days now, with doctors still trying to determine what is wrong with her. I'm at a loss as to what could have caused this sudden change in her behavior. I miss my wife so much.

Throughout my life, I have struggled with performance anxiety, social anxiety, and manic-depression to some extent. Despite these challenges, I have always possessed intelligence and talent, which allowed me to excel academically in high school and attend a prestigious university. However, my time at university was marked by unhappiness, and I almost dropped out even though my grades were good. At one point, I received treatment for anxiety related to a prescription drug, which temporarily made me feel happy, outgoing, and popular. However, it also caused manic episodes and sexual dysfunction. During this period, I had numerous job offers but was too afraid to accept them, so I decided to start my own dot-com business. Unfortunately, once I stopped the treatment, my anxiety and depression resurfaced, and my business did not thrive as expected. Eventually, it failed, and for the past 15 years, I have been working alone for one of our former clients. While it has provided a decent income in a low-stress environment, working from home has been isolating and lonely.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for the past three years and things have been really challenging. Initially, we were happy and in love, but once we moved in together and started discussing a more serious commitment, things took a turn for the worse. He started mentally and physically abusing me, which made me feel trapped because we were living together and I still had conflicting feelings of affection and love for him. Eventually, in October, he told me he wanted to break up, even though we were still living together. Since then, I have been trying to create distance and protect myself from further hurt.

I have had a challenging upbringing due to my diagnosed conditions of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD), and being transgender. This has led to constant conflicts between myself and my parents, resulting in my placement in an institution at the age of ten. Unfortunately, during my time there, I experienced various forms of abuse, including physical, emotional, and sexual. The trauma has left me with deep trust issues, making it difficult for me to confide in adults. This cycle of problems persisted even after I returned home, leading to another period of separation when I was seventeen. It was not until I reached the age of 25 that I began to feel any sense of love in my life.

Patient's statement (rewritten): I've been struggling with making friends for as long as I can remember. Whenever someone tries to talk to me, I become overwhelmed with anxiety, worrying about how they perceive me. This often leads me to come across as uninterested or even snobby. I constantly think that people are talking negatively about me behind my back, and it causes me to panic. At school, I find myself obsessing over whether I smell bad or if my makeup is smeared, thinking that others are judging me. I also struggle to show emotions, especially when I'm anxious, and I avoid opening up to people because it makes me feel vulnerable. While my anxiety has improved over the years, I still experience intense paranoia. I constantly think that people view me as a loser, and I can't leave the house without wearing makeup because I'm terrified of what others might think of me.

About ten months ago, I started dating my now-ex-girlfriend. It took a couple of months for me to develop strong feelings for her, even though it wasn't love at first sight. She did disclose to me early on that she has bipolar disorder, but it turned out to be more severe than she initially conveyed. Despite that, she treated me incredibly well and made me feel like I was on top of the world for the first three months.

I have been dating this guy for about three months now. In the beginning of our relationship, everything was perfect and I trusted him whole-heartedly. Up until recently I’ve been very suspicious and my trust just keeps going down. I started to lose trust when finding a text message in his phone from someone calling him “babe” on Valentines Day. He said it was nothing like that, and I asked to see the rest of the messages from that person but he said no because he thought that would change the dynamics of our relationship and that I am supposed to just trust him, so I let it go. Ever since that occasion it’s been so hard for me to trust him like I did in the beginning. He’s constantly texting some person in his phone and I’m 99% sure it is a female, which does not bother me. But what does bother me is that for some reason I have this gut instinct that this female he is constantly texting is someone he is involved with. When I sit and ponder on that idea I think to myself, “He doesn’t even have time to spend with other women, he’s always so busy.” But I almost feel like I’m convincing myself because I just have this feeling inside. On top of all of this my mother and a few of my close friends don’t really trust this guy or particularly care for him too which makes it even harder for me as well. I’m wondering how you feel about this situation? Should I end this relationship before I get hurt or wait it out and see if it can really become as good as I thought it could?

About a year ago, I made a mistake and had an affair with someone. I ended things and have had no contact with that person since then. I've been trying my best to show my girlfriend that I am completely faithful now. However, she constantly accuses me of being unfaithful, even on a daily basis. It's getting to the point where I'm considering ending the relationship.

I recently received some distressing news about my sister. She attempted to take her own life and has been expressing feelings of depression and dissatisfaction with her life. I've been trying to support her as best I can, but it's challenging because we live in different countries. Unfortunately, our other family members who are closer to her don't seem to understand her needs and have been unsupportive, even saying hurtful things. I find their response to be harsh and unhelpful.

Lately, I've noticed that I've been having frequent arguments with my parents, and it's been making me increasingly angry. Most of these arguments revolve around my behavior towards my siblings and what my parents perceive as disrespect. It's difficult for me to control my reactions when my parents are yelling at me, and I feel like they don't respect me when they're in my face like that. The main issue we argue about is my younger brother, who tends to bother me. Today, he touched me, which I absolutely hate, so I slapped him on the arm. Unfortunately, my dad witnessed it and got angry with me, which just made me more frustrated. My mom also scolded me when she got home, but she didn't seem to understand how I felt. To avoid these confrontations, I've been isolating myself from my family by sleeping all day and neglecting my schoolwork and eating habits. But no matter what I do, these arguments keep happening. Is there a way to make my parents understand me? How can I handle my 7-year-old brother? Should I continue ignoring them? I'm really in need of help, and I want to stress that this is not just teenage drama. I've even harmed myself after some of these arguments. Please, I'm begging for assistance.

When I was younger, I had a natural aversion to eating meat, but I still enjoyed the taste. However, things changed for me in 6th grade when I started experiencing depression and thoughts of suicide. It was a time of transition as I was about to enter junior high, and I also struggled with insomnia. During this period, I made the decision to become a vegetarian and developed anorexic tendencies. Initially, I wasn't completely vegan and still consumed hotdogs, hamburgers, chicken nuggets, bacon, and top ramen soup. It wasn't until seventh grade that I fully embraced a vegetarian lifestyle, but I continued to face challenges. It wasn't until eighth grade that I made a positive change and became very strict about my food choices, avoiding additives, meat, and striving for overall health.

My boyfriend and I have been together for a little under 4 years. When we first started the relationship, I tried to be upfront and honest about my struggle with emotional connection and affection. Despite caring deeply for him, I realized that I needed to address some unresolved issues from my past and sought therapy. Unfortunately, delving into those memories has been overwhelming and has brought up a flood of emotions.

I have been in love with one guy for the past 8 years. We also had a 3-year long distance relationship. But during that time, I met another guy and fell in love with him. We ended things after a couple of months because he is married. However, even after 2 years, I still have lingering feelings for him. He has expressed his love multiple times and is even willing to leave his wife. I am torn between these two men and unsure of what to do. I don't want to hurt my future husband and our families, but I also feel like I may have a better life with the other man. I know this sounds selfish, but I am truly torn apart. Can you please help me?
My fiance and I had a seemingly perfect relationship for 7 years. We were always happy, never argued, and everyone around us saw us as the ideal couple. Life felt like a fairytale for both of us.

Over the past few months, I've experienced some significant challenges in my relationship. After getting engaged, I took out a loan to buy my boyfriend a truck, but then we discovered he had something in collection when we tried to get a mortgage. I suggested taking a line of credit in my name to pay off the collection so that we could eventually buy a home and get married. However, since my boyfriend left for a course, our communication has been limited, and he hasn't been responsible with the truck payments. I recently discovered an email he sent to another woman, and when I confronted him about it, he became angry and ended our engagement. I'm unsure about his intentions and whether his actions were due to his drinking or if he had an affair. I made him co-sign a loan with his parents to buy the truck from me, but I worry about his commitment to making the line of credit payments. I'm considering taking legal action if necessary.

I'm a 25-year-old male and I've been struggling with starting tasks and getting my life on track. It takes me a long time to write even a simple sentence, and I find it difficult to initiate job applications, establish writing routines, and form relationships with women. It's like I'm constantly stuck and unable to make progress.

Patient: I recently became engaged and moved in with my fiance. His mother used to have a key to his apartment for convenience, but now she is letting herself in unannounced on a daily basis, even when I am in the shower. I am a private person and find this intrusive, especially since she is loud and checks in on my fiance while he sleeps during the day. I don't want to offend my fiance or his mother, but I'm feeling uncomfortable. Please help!

I'm feeling really down because I'm 15 years old and it seems like my dad treats my brother better than me. Every time my brother goes to see him, he gets a lot of money, usually £30 or more, and he even got an Xbox Kinect. When I go to see my dad, I only get £5 and I feel like he never buys me anything. On my birthday, all I got was a small ornament. I don't want to sound ungrateful, but it feels unfair that my brother gets treated differently. It's like favoritism.

Patient: I've been experiencing a number of concerning symptoms lately and I'm really hoping you can help me. Sometimes I hear whistling when no one is around, and I've seen a man in my closet. I also see people moving around in mirrors, even though there's no one there. At night, I see black dots floating in the air. On top of that, I have strange thoughts and struggle to determine if my memories are real or not. My mood swings are intense - I can go from extreme happiness and outgoing behavior to depression, paranoia, and shyness within a couple of hours. I constantly feel like people are talking about me, and I've even had suicidal thoughts. I've tried talking to my family, but they haven't been very receptive. Can you please help me?

I have been married for 15 years. Over time, I feel like I have grown a lot personally, but unfortunately, my spouse hasn't seemed to grow alongside me. He consistently avoids addressing any issues that arise between us, demonstrating a certain level of immaturity. It's frustrating because he never takes responsibility for his part in any problem, always placing the blame solely on me. We attempted counseling twice, but unfortunately, it didn't go well. He ended up arguing with the counselor, which led her to feel unable to effectively communicate with him.

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for six months, and he has never given me any reason to doubt his trustworthiness. He has always been honest and affectionate towards me, constantly expressing his love and care. However, I find it difficult to trust him and experience intense separation anxiety when we are apart. I have a strong desire to control his actions, who he spends time with, where he goes, and what he does, even if I'm not involved. I recognize that this is unhealthy and it's starting to negatively impact our relationship.

I'm a 13-year-old and I have a twin sister. We constantly fight and it's starting to make me feel really lonely. My sister and my mom both have people they talk to all the time, like my sister's boyfriend, but I don't have anyone like that. I hardly even talk to my friends anymore. I'm not sure if it's because we're different or if it's something else, but I know that we need help. Can you please help me?

I've been struggling with self-harm since 8th grade, mainly cutting and scratching myself when I get angry. It seems to happen most often when my mom yells at me for what she says is attitude, but I don't understand why she sees it that way. It's led me to question my worth and contemplate suicide at times. I've tried to stop cutting before, but I always end up starting again. I also struggle with intense anger and have harmful thoughts. My mom doesn't think anything is wrong with me, but I disagree. I've seen two counselors in the past, but they didn't assess me for depression or any other issues. I feel lost and hope you can help me.

I've been dating my partner for about a year now, and I've been struggling with his mom. It feels like she has the exact same personality as a girl I knew back in college, and that relationship caused me a lot of emotional distress. I tried my best to tolerate that girl for five long years to avoid conflict, but I can't do the same with my boyfriend's mom. Whenever I see her, I feel this intense anger and frustration, like I want to lash out at her.

Lately, I've been experiencing intense anxiety and mood swings that seem to be triggered by external stimuli. It's really affecting my daily life and I find myself constantly reliving past events. Thank you for taking the time to listen to me. I want to make sure I provide you with all the necessary information, so please feel free to ask anything if you need more details.

I have been feeling a deep conflict within myself for as long as I can remember. It has become increasingly difficult to ignore. I'm a 17-year-old high school student, and while everyone around me is focused on college and finding their passions, I feel like I lack a sense of identity and genuine interests. This is causing problems with my social interactions because I struggle to connect with others. I find myself feeling apathetic towards everything, from current events to my relationships with friends and family. Although I am outwardly successful and involved in various activities, none of them truly interest me. I only continue with them to meet expectations and get into college. I feel disconnected from others and lack emotional connections. Even if someone close to me were to pass away, I fear that my concern would be solely focused on how it impacts my own convenience. I don't have any particular academic, athletic, or artistic interests either, despite having been exposed to various activities. The only things I enjoy doing are those that help me escape from my own thoughts and consciousness, such as playing games or reading books. However, even my appreciation for these activities feels superficial and lacking depth.

Three days ago, I discovered that a year ago my husband sexually abused my daughter. I am feeling overwhelmed and torn because I love both my daughter and my husband. To protect my daughter, I have taken precautions like putting locks on her door and bathroom, and ensuring she is never left alone with him. I confronted my husband about the allegations, but he denies them and claims he loves our child and would never harm her. I want to believe him, but I also cannot ignore my daughter's words. I am wondering if our family can be saved and if therapy could help us. I don't want to be a bad mother, but I also don't want to lose my family.

I have been married for less than a year to a wife I truly adore. We have had many ups and downs this year. However, she is subject to raging anger directed towards me. Any time that we try to resolve an issue, she blows up uses the F-word, tells me she doesn’t care about me, and doesn’t want to be in the same room with me. We are talking screaming here. Three therapists have told me that she is being irrational and suggested the possibility of emotional abuse. I have not been perfect, but I always own up to my mistakes and apologize. All I want to do is resolve an issue, and she wants to ignore it. If I try to force things she reacts (according to my therapists) WAY over the top. They have also said that she stonewalls me. My family is suggesting that I give up on the relationship, but I am not ready for that.

Over the past few years, I've noticed a significant change in my emotional experience. I no longer feel the same range of emotions as before - anger, happiness, joy, and even sadness seem to have faded away. Activities that used to bring me pleasure now only serve to distract me. I don't experience the typical highs and lows of teenage life - everything just feels flat with occasional dips. The world around me feels surreal, like a dream, and I often find myself withdrawing from it. My mind is constantly racing, making it difficult to concentrate and even to fall asleep at times.

I have been diagnosed with Major Depressive Disorder and I am struggling to function properly. Despite going to work, I feel like my depression is resistant to medication. I have tried various medications for depression and bipolar, including Abilify, but none have been effective. I have been seeing a respected therapist for eight years, but I feel stuck and have decided to change therapists as a last resort. I've seen multiple psychiatrists who have told me that this may be as good as it gets and I have to find a way to cope or transcend my depression. I'm exhausted from this daily struggle and occasionally have thoughts of suicide, but I would never hurt my children. I'm considering Electroconvulsive Therapy (ECT), but I'm afraid of the potential cognitive and memory loss. I also have learning disabilities and ADD, so I don't want to worsen these conditions. I'm aware that my depression could be contributing to or worsening my learning disabilities and ADD. It feels like I'm stuck in a never-ending cycle with this. How safe and effective is ECT?

I've been struggling with my emotions lately. It's hard for me to put my thoughts into words, so I'll just list out how I've been feeling. First, I've been feeling a constant sense of emptiness. It's like I don't feel anything anymore, even in situations that should elicit a strong emotional response. Second, I've become extremely irritable. I get angry and annoyed at the slightest things, even when someone asks me a simple favor. Third, I've been questioning the purpose of my life. While I'm not suicidal, I often find myself wondering why I continue living and have to actively come up with reasons to keep going. Fourth, I've noticed that I don't see people as individuals anymore. I view everyone as just another mammal, which ties back to my previous point. Fifth, I want to reach out for help, but I'm afraid of being judged and laughed at by my parents or anyone else. Sixth, I've lost interest in trying to form relationships with girls. While I'm still attracted to them, I find that the effort required to pursue them feels unbalanced. Seventh, I've been observing people's actions and reasoning in relationships, and it feels like everyone is lacking in some way. Eighth, I have a habit of biting my fingers, not just the nails but the skin around it. I did some research and think I might have over-focused ADHD based on the symptoms. Ninth, I've been using weed to cope. It's not an addiction, but it's the only thing that brings me some happiness. When I'm high, my racing thoughts calm down and I can function more normally. Lastly, I tend to get stuck on negative thoughts and experiences. For example, if I call a friend and they don't answer, I immediately assume they're ignoring me and spiral into depression until I hear back from them. I'm sure there's more going on, but it took me a long time just to write down these 10 points. I would really appreciate some advice. Thank you - Lost Teenager.

Last year, I made a mistake that caused a major rift between me and my closest friends. They not only betrayed my trust but also spread negative rumors about me online and even enlisted their boyfriends and their friends to do the same. As a result, I started spending a lot of time with my boyfriend and his friends. However, now that they have all gone off to college, I feel stuck in high school.

I've noticed that I have this strong desire to be dominated by my husband, specifically through spanking as a form of punishment. It's not something I saw in my parents' relationship, but it's something I've felt and needed since I got married. After the spanking, there's no sexual activity; it's purely a disciplinary session and we move on. I wouldn't necessarily label it as a fetish.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for over 3 years now, but for the past 2 years, we haven't been truly happy. We go through a cycle of breaking up and getting back together repeatedly. We fight almost every day, and he constantly lies to me and fails to provide the love and support I need. I find myself having to ask him to show me love and appreciation, which should come naturally in a relationship.

I am a 21-year-old female college student. I've been drinking since I was a freshman in high school, and it has become a big part of my identity. People know me as "The plastic bottle princess" because I drink cheap vodka and can outdrink most people. I often find myself in drinking contests and people I've never met before recognize me because of my drunken escapades.

I am experiencing some confusion regarding the amnesia aspect of Dissociative Identity Disorder (DID). I have noticed that I have different individuals living within me, but unlike what I understand about DID, we all have awareness of each other. While we don't always communicate, there are occasions when we do interact and share information. For example, I may provide comfort to the sad inner child, or the vigilant one might share their impressions of someone. Interestingly, I don't experience memory loss when another personality is in control of the body. Instead, it feels like a shift in awareness and I adopt a different way of thinking, feeling, and behaving. It's particularly noticeable when I feel threatened or insulted, as a stronger persona steps forward. I don't completely disappear, but rather my awareness seems to switch into someone with a distinct perspective.

Over the past four years, I have been prescribed various anti-depressants and have always had access to anti-anxiety medication. However, I have decided not to take any anti-depressants this year as I didn't find them effective. I am currently in the midst of completing my master's thesis, but I am struggling to focus and take action. To cope, I often find solace in fantasy and science fiction films and novels, as they provide a temporary escape from reality.

I've been in a relationship with my girlfriend for three years, and recently she told me that she has herpes after experiencing a breakout. Throughout our time together, she has shared various stories about her past that seem unbelievable, like being raped in college and being manipulated in a psych ward. She has also mentioned being in a BDSM relationship, having multiple jobs, and going through a difficult divorce. Recently, she accused me of being abusive and threatening towards her, which I strongly deny. I suspect she may have a mental disorder because she lies frequently and her stories constantly change. I've decided to cut off all contact with her because I fear she may be setting me up. How can I protect myself from someone like her?

Two weeks ago, I was sitting on the couch watching TV when suddenly I started feeling detached from reality. My whole living room felt like a picture, and I had a panic attack. Since then, I've been feeling fake and unreal, and it hasn't gone away. I'm worried that I might be schizophrenic and that everything is crazy. I can't get an appointment with mental health until next week, and I don't know what to do in the meantime. I've been pacing around my house, feeling out of breath and shaky all day. The panic won't go away, and I've been experiencing chest pain. Time seems to be flying by, and although I remember what I've done, it feels like it was all fake and didn't actually happen. I'm terrified.

Over the past two years, I have noticed a significant change in my grandson's personality. He used to be loving and caring, but now he seems unsociable and uncaring. He lacks remorse and only seems to show care when things are going his way. He often appears distant and detached when he is just sitting around. Whenever someone tries to talk to him, he cuts them off and already knows the answer. I believe he is depressed. I have tried to get him help, but since he is twenty years old, he needs to agree before I can make an appointment with a doctor. Now, the big problem is that my little dog went missing on February 1st. I am extremely upset about it. However, when I told my grandson, he said it's just a dog and that I should get another one. Two weeks later, his mother's dog passed away. He claimed it just fell over dead and didn't think it was a big deal.

I find myself in a complex situation. I have developed strong feelings for a woman who is married. She initiated the relationship, and what was meant to be a harmless first date ended up with us sleeping together. Over time, we have become close friends and share everything with each other. Her three children have also grown fond of me. She claims to no longer be in love with her husband, but still has some feelings for him despite his wrongdoings. She compliments me, saying I am amazing, sweet, and better at certain things than her husband, such as being there for her and her children, providing emotional support, and being a great listener.

During my first year at university, I had to make a difficult decision. Despite having high grades in high school, financial constraints prevented me from pursuing my desired field of study in medicine. Now, I am studying pharm.d, but I constantly face questions and pity from others who wonder why I didn't choose medicine. I am considering switching my major to dentistry because it is still a prestigious field and would allow me to escape the judgment of others. However, I am torn because I am actually more interested in the practical aspects of dentistry. I am concerned about losing a semester and falling behind. I feel unsure about what I truly want to do. I apologize for any language mistakes as English is not my native language.

My fiancé and I have been together for almost 3 years now. We have a daughter and a home together. About two months ago, we decided to take a break from our relationship. It was a difficult time for me as my fiancé started partying every night and neglected our daughter. I felt heartbroken and confused because he had always been a great dad and partner. We rarely fought and I thought we were happy.

My wife and I have been married for 4 years now. We actually met just 6 months before tying the knot. Before we got married, my wife was a virgin, but I had previous sexual experience. Despite that, our relationship is going really well and we love each other deeply. We rarely have any problems, and when we do, we make sure to resolve them before going to bed at night.

It felt like I was finally making progress in overcoming my OCD and anorexia. I had managed to control common symptoms like checking switches, washing my hands excessively, and hoarding. My thoughts were becoming more manageable. But then, a few days ago, I experienced a severe panic attack and it feels like all my progress has been undone.

I've been in a relationship with my boyfriend for the past two years. Unfortunately, he has displayed a consistent lack of trust towards me, despite my faithfulness. He accuses me of various things on a daily basis and goes as far as calling me derogatory names. Additionally, he has even resorted to physical violence in the past. On top of all this, he constantly believes I'm checking out other men whenever we're out together. Although I don't suspect him of cheating, I have stumbled upon suspicious numbers on different occasions.

I have been in a pattern of toxic relationships where I have encountered lying, cheating, and betrayal. As a result, I decided to take a break from dating for the past two years. Recently, I met someone I truly love, but I find myself projecting my past experiences onto him. I accuse him of things without any evidence, causing him to break up with me multiple times. I always beg for him to take me back. I have also been dishonest and cheated on him twice, although he is aware of me talking to someone else but doesn't know about the two instances of infidelity.

My sister has been going through a difficult time lately. She has been self-diagnosing herself and using that as a way to manipulate situations to her advantage. She recently started seeing a therapist, but it seems like she's using the therapist's words to further manipulate others.

Over the past 5-6 years, I've been struggling to form and maintain friendships. This issue has worsened since the recent deaths of two of my grandparents. Additionally, I've been having difficulty focusing in class, even before my grandparents passed away. Whether it's in school or while playing video games, my mind tends to wander and my attention drifts away.

Patient: I was wondering if mild paranoia is a common characteristic of depressive disorders? I was diagnosed with depression and I’m taking an SSRI for it, which has helped quite a bit, although I wouldn’t say that I’m “cured.” I also had some pretty severe hypochondria-related anxiety that started about nine months ago and lasted for about three months. The anxiety is no longer problematic–I still have hypochondriacal thoughts occasionally, but I can manage them and I know that they’re irrational and part of my depression.

My husband and I have been married for nearly 9 years, but we've known each other for 11 years. On the surface, we appear to be the perfect couple, enjoying adventure, travel, cooking, and being deeply in love. However, behind closed doors, we're facing a different reality. Over the past 10 years, we've been dealing with the challenges of my husband's father who suffered a stroke and now has cancer. We've been providing support to my in-laws during these difficult times.

My partner and I have been in a committed relationship for five years now. We were sexually active with each other for about three years prior to officially dating. Initially, my partner had a really strong sex drive, but over time it has significantly decreased. Currently, we only have sex about 1-2 times a month.

I've always been really focused on my academics and it seems like that's all people see about me. But lately, I've been noticing some troubling behavior in myself that I think might be signs of Borderline Personality Disorder. These behaviors have been happening more frequently and getting more intense over the past year.

Lately, I've been experiencing intense feelings of jealousy in my current relationship. This is a new experience for me, as I have never felt this way in previous relationships. In the past, there were certain situations that triggered a slight pang of jealousy, like when one of my ex-boyfriends stayed at a female friend's house in France for holidays. However, I was able to manage those feelings by reminding myself of the importance of trust in a relationship.

I'm a 15-year-old and I've been struggling with disturbing thoughts and attractions towards young girls between the ages of 6 to 8. These thoughts make me feel guilty and I worry about whether this will go away as I get older. I even find myself having fantasies about taking advantage of their innocence. It's also concerning that I don't find older women sexually attractive unless they have a more childlike appearance. Even my friend's sister who is in 8th grade is someone I feel attracted to. I hope you can offer some guidance on this matter.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for the past two years. We are both 23 years old and live in Serbia. Everything seemed fine; we didn't argue, had a great sexual life, and communicated well. However, lately, I've noticed some changes in his behavior that concern me. I think he may need help.

I have been in a relationship with my boyfriend for four years, and we have been living together for three of those years. However, there was an incident six months into our relationship that has been bothering me. One night, I found him parked in his workplace parking lot with another woman at 3am. He had told me that he was going to a friend's house, but when he didn't come home and wouldn't answer his phone, I became worried.
